FX01-001.name: House Blackthorn
FX01-001.title: Lord of Foxhurst
FX01-001.arms: a black thorn tree on silver

military.office: Lords of the Foxhurst levy
military.unit: the Blackthorn Lances, 40 riders and 300 levy bills
military.ties: Their levy marched into the forest edge in 1079 and lost a third of its men to arrows from the trees, and the Crown Host has not trusted a Blackthorn order since.

FX01-001.power: The barony of Foxhurst: charcoal villages, a timber mill on the forest road and half the woodland it held before 1080.
FX01-001.history: Harald the Founder made the Blackthorns lords of Foxhurst in 962 for cutting the forest road to the Oak Line. For a century they grew rich on charcoal and timber floated down to Kingsmere. In May 1078 Lord Oswy Blackthorn sent his loggers across the Oak Line to fell about 300 old oaks for Emperor Conrad's Cold Bay fleet. The elves warned three times, then burned three camps in one September night and killed 140 loggers. At Rinael on 7 May 1080 the empire paid 20,000 silver marks and handed Oswy over to the elves, and half his forest went to the Crown Foresters.
FX01-001.reputation: Pitied in Foxhurst and mocked at court as the house the emperor gave to the trees.

members.role: Head of the family; Lady of Foxhurst
members.note: She was eighteen when she watched her father ride into the forest at Rinael between two elven wardens, and she has not cut a living oak since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Foxhurst levy
members.note: He walks the marker stones at night with a war bow, hoping to catch an elven watcher alone.

members.role: Hawise's uncle; steward of the charcoal villages
members.note: He sells oak to Greyhaven factors through a cousin, and some of it was cut on the wrong side of the stones.

members.role: Younger daughter; novice at the Oath Hall of Bellcote
members.note: She writes letters to a grandfather everyone else calls dead and leaves them at the Oak Line stones.

famousDead: Ordered the oak-cutting of 1078 and was handed to the elves at Rinael; no one has seen him since
FX01-001.secret: In 1101 a packet in an elven hand reached Hawise with her father's signet inside. Oswy lives in the Evenwood, made to plant one oak for every one he cut.
hooks: An elven watcher offers to return Oswy Blackthorn alive in exchange for whoever burned an Oak Line marker near Foxhurst last winter.
The Crown Foresters are close to tracing Uncle Merrick's Greyhaven oak to stumps beyond the stones.

FX01-002.name: House Carrow
FX01-002.title: Lord of Carrness
FX01-002.words: What the Plough Takes, It Keeps

military.office: Captains of the Carrness Prickers
military.unit: the Carrow Prickers, 120 light riders of the March Prickers
military.ties: Every Carrow son rides two summers along the Gordush with the March Prickers before he may marry.

FX01-002.power: About 3,000 acres of steppe farmland around Carrness taken from half-orc holders after 1053, worked by licensed half-orc tenants at double rent.
FX01-002.history: Thurstan Carrow was a Harrowsett squire who stood behind the wagons at Hartgate in 1051. When the License Law of 1053 stripped the half-orcs of the march of their land, Lord Edgar Harrow gave him the farms around Carrness, and Emperor Conrad confirmed him lord in 1056. The Carrows held their timber fort when Durgash Blood-Fist burned six others in 1068, and lost their eldest son at the Gashmar Fords in 1070. In April 1103 Tarn Halfblood's riders burned the Carrow granary on their way to Hazelhollow, and Lord Brand Carrow hanged four of his own tenants for it on no proof.
FX01-002.reputation: The March Hawks call them steady men; the half-orcs of the march call them the Barn-Takers.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Carrness
members.note: He keeps the four nooses from 1103 hanging in his gatehouse as a warning, and his tenants walk around the gate.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Carrow Prickers
members.note: He means to ride first over the Gordush with Lord Garrick after May Fair and come home with Tarn's head.

members.role: Brand's daughter
members.note: She teaches tenants' children their letters in the tithe barn and secretly carries their parents' marks for Oswin Gordale's petition.

members.role: Dowager; widow of the first lord's son
members.note: She remembers the half-orc family who owned the hall before 1053 and still calls the best bedchamber by their name.

famousDead: Fought at Hartgate and founded the house on the License Law acres
FX01-002.secret: The half-orc holders of Carrness had a lord's license sealed in 1040, before the law; a Harrow clerk burned it so the land could be taken.
hooks: Oswin Gordale's petition names the Carrow acres first, and Linnet's hand is on it.
A half-orc rider from across the Gordush asks for the old hall back in his grandmother's name.

FX01-003.name: House Holloway
FX01-003.title: Knight-Banneret of Rosemarch
FX01-003.arms: three silver keys on night green

military.office: Couriers of the Night School
military.unit: the Rosemarch riders, 60 men who carry the Ravenscar cipher between Northmoor and Kingsmere
military.ties: Holloway riders carry every sealed bag of the empire's spy service, and two Holloway sons ride with the Night Riders in each generation.

FX01-003.power: The manor and market town of Rosemarch, and the trust of the Ravenscars, whose heirs are half Holloway.
FX01-003.history: The Holloways were forest knights of Rosemarch long before the Ravenscars had a name, and swore to them when Hakon gave Maud the Owl the Oak Line Shires. In 1068 Sir Wystan Holloway married Ysolde Ravenscar and took her name, so Corbin and Isa Ravenscar are Holloway by blood. The family has carried the cipher bags between Northmoor and the treasury at Kingsmere ever since. Wystan died of a winter fever in late 1089, a few weeks before King Bjorn of Northreach was poisoned at the winter court. His brother Ingram has run Rosemarch quietly since and asks nothing of his sister-in-law.
FX01-003.reputation: Discreet, reliable and a little frightening, like the house they serve.

members.role: Head of the family; Knight-Banneret of Rosemarch
members.note: He keeps his dead brother's letters in an iron box under the chapel floor and reads one every year on the day Wystan died.

members.role: Heir; cipher clerk at the Kingsmere treasury
members.note: She can read the Ravenscar ledger cipher faster than anyone but Lady Ysolde, which is why she is never allowed to leave Kingsmere alone.

members.role: Younger son; deserter from the Night Riders
members.note: He rode at Fenny Ford in May 1103, heard the children screaming in the barn, and has hidden in his father's hunting lodge ever since.

members.role: Ingram's wife; keeper of Rosemarch
members.note: She sends Hamo bread every week and tells the Northmoor riders he is in the Sunlands.

famousDead: Married Ysolde Ravenscar in 1068 and took her name; father of Corbin and Isa
FX01-003.secret: Wystan's last letters say he had learned of a cook being placed in the palace kitchen and begged Ysolde to stop it; he fell ill a week later.
hooks: Night Riders come to Rosemarch asking after a deserter named Hamo.
A stranger offers Ingram proof of how his brother really died, for the iron box.

FX01-004.name: House Erneholt
FX01-004.title: Viscount of the Eagle March and Castellan of Eagleburg
FX01-004.arms: a white eagle displayed on black, an iron bar beneath

military.office: Castellans of Eagleburg
military.unit: the Eagleburg garrison, 2,000 men, and the Erneholt Hearth Lances, 150 riders
military.ties: The garrison at the end of the Iron Road has been under an Erneholt since Lord Oswin held its walls against Harald Ironside for six months.

FX01-004.power: The walls of Eagleburg, the right to weigh every Irondeep bar at the Iron Road's end, and the only noble children on the plain who learn the dwarves' trade-tongue in the cradle.
FX01-004.history: The Erneholts were the lords of Eagleburg when the Iron Road from Irondeep first met the grain carts of the eastern plain. Lord Oswin Erneholt held the town against Harald Ironside from August 949 until his grain ran out in February 950, and Harald spared him because his dealers were the only men who could talk to the dwarves. In September 951 the Iron Road Compact was sealed in Oswin's hall, and in 968 his granddaughter Aelfled married the future Emperor Hakon, so every Ironside since carries Erneholt blood. The house lost its kingship of the east but kept the walls and the weigh-house. After the Northreach Rising it stood surety to the Deepeye court for the 24,000 hold-marks of iron the empire took on credit.
FX01-004.reputation: Old, rich and too clever with the dwarves, say the western lords; the only people who keep the Iron Road open, say the merchants.

members.role: Head of the family; Viscount of the Eagle March
members.note: He signed the surety for the emperor's iron debt himself, and he has not slept well since the dwarves' first reminder came in 1100.

members.role: Heir; envoy on the Iron Road
members.note: She spent four winters at the Irondeep gate and argues with dwarf factors in their own tongue without raising her voice.

members.role: Hesketh's sister; the family's pledge at Irondeep
members.note: She has lived in the dwarf halls since 1094 as the living pledge for the debt, and her letters home grow shorter every year.

members.role: Younger son; hundredman of the Kingsmere Crossbows
members.note: He wants a war on the Gordush so he can earn a name the dwarves did not give him.

famousDead: Held Eagleburg against Harald for six months and sealed the Iron Road Compact in his hall
Married Hakon the Oathkeeper in 968; mother of his elder sons
FX01-004.secret: Hesketh pledged the family's own walls and weigh-house as surety for the empire's iron debt; if the crown does not pay by 1108, Eagleburg's tolls belong to Irondeep.
hooks: A Deepeye clerk arrives at Eagleburg to count what the empire owes, and asks to see Gerda first.
The emperor wants Eagleburg's tolls for the war; the Erneholts cannot say why they are already promised.

FX01-005.name: House Kelswick
FX01-005.title: Warden of the Glenwash Crossings
FX01-005.arms: three white waves under a black ferry bell, on dark teal

military.office: Wardens of the Glenwash crossings
military.unit: the Ferry Wardens, 80 men and six war-barges
military.ties: Kelswick barges carried the Glenwash levy over the river in both Horde Wars, and Jarl Sigurd will not cross water without a Kelswick at the steering oar.

FX01-005.power: The ferry rights and salmon weirs of the lower Glenwash, held of the Greymane jarls.
FX01-005.history: The Kelswicks were ferry-thanes of the Greymanes when Grim Greymane's heirs still ruled the Glenwash as kings in all but name. They lost a ferry and half their men when Harald broke the truce at the fords in 945, and swore to his Greymane wife for want of anyone else. In April 1009 a Kelswick ferry, overloaded in the spring flood, turned over in the Glenwash; six men swam ashore and Prince Sigmund Ironside sank at once. The emperor spared the family, but the hall-singers sang Wulfgar's prophecy on the Kelswick quay that summer. Since 1093 the Kelswicks have quietly lent Jarl Sigurd their net lofts for things the Oath Hall must not see.
FX01-005.reputation: Every boatman on the Glenwash trusts them; every Ironside courtier crosses himself on their barges.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Glenwash Crossings
members.note: He has been told he must steer Prince Harald's barge over the Glenwash on the wedding progress, and has asked for the river to be roped.

members.role: Heir; marine officer of the Cold Bay squadron
members.note: She serves under Ingrid Greymane and knows about her captain's Coldhaven betrothal.

members.role: Garth's brother; keeper of the net lofts
members.note: The Free Hall priestess hidden at Easterham sleeps in his loft, and he sings the old lays to her at night.

members.role: Dowager; grandmother of the house
members.note: Her grandfather was one of the six who swam ashore in 1009, and she alone remembers what he said about the prince.

famousDead: Swam ashore from the ferry that drowned Prince Sigmund in 1009
FX01-005.secret: Aelfric told his family that the prince never kicked once but went down like an anvil; the Kelswicks know what the Ironside bones are and have never said it aloud.
hooks: Prince Harald's wedding progress must cross the Glenwash on a Kelswick barge.
The Oath Hall's men search the Easterham net lofts for a hidden priestess.

FX01-006.name: House Oxlade
FX01-006.title: Lord of the Yew Gate
FX01-006.arms: a gold chevron between three ox-yokes, on blue

military.office: Captains of the Yewmarch levy
military.unit: the Oxlade spears, 400 levy men
military.ties: They lead a sixth of the Fairrush levy and send their younger sons to the Hide-Knights who winter at Yewmarch.

FX01-006.power: Twelve villages on the Yewmarch road and the keeping of the Fairrush river toll-posts above the city.
FX01-006.history: The Oxlades were stewards of Oswald Fairrush when he was passed over for the crown in 927, and they followed him to Yewmarch when the river tolls became his price. In 951 an Oxlade mason, Hamo, worked in the Yewmarch chapel the same month the Fairrush lords swore on the iron ring that Osbert's silver crown had been melted. The house has kept the Fairrush toll-posts ever since and votes as the Fairrushes vote in the Oath Moot. In 1093 Lord Edmund Oxlade stood beside Lady Audra when the Moot forced the tax vote that ended the Northreach Rising.
FX01-006.reputation: Plain, slow and as loyal to Yewmarch as the river is to the sea.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Yew Gate
members.note: He will vote down the war tax again this spring, and he has told the Ravenscar owls so to their faces.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She hopes to marry Aldhelm Fairrush and bring the Oxlades into the old royal blood.

members.role: Younger son; squire in the Iron Guard
members.note: He loves the emperor's knights more than his father's lady, and he talks too much in the Iron Ring inn.

members.role: Dowager; Edmund's mother
members.note: She has told only one person in seventy years which stone of the chapel wall is hollow, and he is dead.

famousDead: Mason of the Yewmarch chapel in the year the Fairrush crown was sworn melted
FX01-006.secret: Old Isobel knows which stone of the Yewmarch chapel wall hides Osbert's silver crown, because an Oxlade laid it there in 951.
hooks: Cuthbert boasts in his cups that his family knows a royal secret, and an owl is listening.
Isobel is dying and wants to pass the secret to one grandchild only.

FX01-007.name: House Ambersley
FX01-007.title: Lord of Amberwick and Warden of the Amber Strand
FX01-007.arms: a gold sun rising over a blue sea

military.office: Wardens of the Amber Strand
military.unit: the Strand Watch, 60 riders, and 200 levy spears owed to Elderstone
military.ties: Their riders patrol the Amber Coast against smugglers, and their levy reinforces the Elderstone garrison in war.

FX01-007.power: Gathering rights on 40 km of the Amber Coast and a share of every storm's harvest.
FX01-007.history: The Ambersleys were beach-reeves for the Fairrush kings and were made lords of Amberwick by Harald the Founder's son in 980. By law every piece of amber from the Cold Bay shore must be sold on Amber Row in Kingsmere through the Amber Guild, and the Ambersleys have fought that law in the Oath Moot for a hundred years. In the Long Winter of 1011 the Strand froze for four months and Amberwick ate its horses. Since the Guild began to court Frostholm's giants in 1104, the Ambersleys fear the crown will care more for tin than for amber.
FX01-007.reputation: Rich, sea-tanned and thought to be a little dishonest, which they are.

members.role: Head of the family; Lady of Amberwick
members.note: She can price a lump of amber by holding it to her cheek, and she has never once paid the Guild's full tenth.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Strand Watch
members.note: He catches smugglers in earnest and does not yet know which ones his mother pays.

members.role: Younger son; apprentice carver on Amber Row
members.note: He was placed with a Guild carver to learn the trade and report what the Guild pays for raw stone.

members.role: Elfa's aunt; mistress of the beach gangs
members.note: She walks the tideline at dawn after every storm with a staff, and no gatherer dares pocket a piece in front of her.

famousDead: Gathered the great amber storm-harvest of 1004 and paid for Amberwick's walls with it
FX01-007.secret: A third of the Strand's amber goes down the coast in smugglers' boats past the Guild, and Elfa splits the profit with the very smugglers Osmund hunts.
hooks: Osmund arrests a smuggler who swears Lady Elfa is his partner.
The Amber Guild demands an audit of the Strand's gathering books before Return Day.

FX01-008.name: House Ormsby
FX01-008.title: Knight of the Swanvale Chase and Master of the Imperial Hunt
FX01-008.arms: a red stag at gaze on white

military.office: Masters of the Imperial Hunt
military.unit: twenty mounted huntsmen and the Swanvale kennels
military.ties: Ormsby huntsmen guide the Hide-Knights who winter at Swanvale and scout for the Crown Host when it marches through the Kingsmere Woods.

FX01-008.power: A manor in the Kingsmere Woods, the keeping of the imperial hounds and the emperor's ear on every hunting day.
FX01-008.history: Hakon the Oathkeeper knighted the first Ormsby in 993 for a boar killed under his horse, and the family has run the imperial hunt since. On 9 February 1081 Emperor Conrad rode onto the Fairrush ice while hunting with Ormsby hounds and went through it. The court gave out that he had died of a winter fever, and Lady Ysolde Ravenscar pensioned the two huntsmen at Swanvale who had seen it. Both were Ormsby men. Emperor Aldwin has hunted with the family every winter since but never once on the river side of the woods.
FX01-008.reputation: Good riders, poor knights and suspiciously well paid for both.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Imperial Hunt
members.note: He was a hundred paces behind Conrad on the ice, and he has never told even his wife what the emperor shouted as he went down.

members.role: Heir; huntsman of the kennels
members.note: He thinks the family pension comes from the emperor's love of hounds.

members.role: Halvard's daughter; falconer
members.note: She found a silver hunting horn in her father's chest with the imperial ring cut into it and river weed still in its bell.

FX01-008.secret: Halvard pulled Conrad's horn from the ice hole in 1081 and kept it. Lady Ysolde thinks it was lost in the river.
hooks: Elfa shows the horn to a friend at the Horsefair.
One of the pensioned Swanvale huntsmen is dying and wants a hall-priest to hear him.

FX01-009.name: House Quarrender
FX01-009.title: Lord of Brookcliff

military.office: Lords of the Brookcliff levy
military.unit: the Brookcliff levy, 450 spears and 30 lances, and a company of quarrymen-sappers
military.ties: Quarrender masons follow the Imperial Engine Corps to every siege to dress stone shot and mend walls.

FX01-009.power: The quarries of Quarrygate and Quarryness, which have built most of the stone forts of the Gordush.
FX01-009.history: The Quarrenders were master quarrymen raised to lords by Hakon in the year of the Iron Reform, when the Oath Hall needed stone and votes. Their stone built the walls of Crossmarch that held against 14,000 orcs in 1048 and the two towers that carried the counterweight engines in 1073. The crown paid for neither in full. Lord Aldred Quarrender sits in the Oath Moot and is courted by both sides of the war-tax quarrel.
FX01-009.reputation: Dusty, hard-bargaining and owed more by the crown than any house their size.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Brookcliff
members.note: He has promised his Moot vote to both Marshal Stane and Lady Audra, and means to sell it to whoever pays the stone debt first.

members.role: Heir; master of the Quarrygate works
members.note: She can split a block along the grain with one blow and hates her father's double dealing.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He owes the Quay Dogs 300 marks from dice in a frozen warehouse and has been offered a way to pay it with a quarry key.

members.role: Grandfather
members.note: He cut the stone for Crossmarch's towers in 1073 and still keeps the unpaid bill framed above his bed.

famousDead: Master quarryman raised to lord in 1002 to build the new Oath Hall steps
FX01-009.secret: The crown owes the Quarrenders 6,000 marks for the stone of Crossmarch, and Aldred has sold his Moot vote twice over to collect it.
hooks: Both Stane and Lady Audra learn on the same day that Aldred promised his vote to the other.
The Quay Dogs ask Kettil to leave the Quarrygate store-house unlocked on a moonless night to clear his debt.

FX01-010.name: House Reedholm
FX01-010.title: Lady of the Briarbrook Fens
FX01-010.arms: a silver eel bent in a ring, on reed green
FX01-010.power: Eel weirs, salt pans and the only dry causeway through the Briarbrook fens to the coast.
FX01-010.history: The Reedholms were fen-thanes of the Greymanes' old hall-lands, and Harald gave them to the crown when he took the Glenwash in 947. They have kept the eel weirs and salt pans of Briarbrook since and send their rents to Kingsmere. When Hakon made himself head of the Seven Halls in 1002, the Reedholm hall-priest refused the iron-ring oath and was drowned on the Drowning Steps, and the family learned to keep its faith in the reeds. In the Long Winter the fens fed Kingsmere with salt eels when the barges stood frozen.
FX01-010.reputation: Quiet fen folk with webbed feet and long memories, say the plains lords.

members.role: Head of the family; Lady of the Briarbrook Fens
members.note: She knows every safe path through the fens in fog and has guided four Free Hall priests to the coast since 1089.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He has told a Kingsmere friend that strangers sleep in the eel-smokers' huts.

members.role: Sunniva's husband; fen physician
members.note: He sets bones for half the fen villages and takes payment in eels.

members.role: Sunniva's aunt; hall-singer
members.note: She sings the old Greymane hall-lays at night in a reed hall the Oath Hall does not know exists.

famousDead: Refused the iron-ring oath of the Iron Reform and was drowned on the Drowning Steps
FX01-010.secret: A Free Hall meets in the Briarbrook reeds, and the Reedholms run a boat-road for Free Hall priests between Easterham and Northreach.
hooks: Aelfric's careless word brings Oath Hall men into the fens.
A Northreach priest arrives in the reeds carrying a letter for Jarl Sigurd from Ragna of the Stones.

FX01-011.name: the Fordham family
FX01-011.title: Sergeant of the Gordush Ford

military.office: Hereditary Sergeants of the Stake-Men at the Gordush Ford
military.unit: a company of the Gordush Stake-Men, 100 crossbowmen under Fordham sergeants
military.ties: Every Fordham son plants his first stake at the ford where Gunnar Harrow died, and the Stake-Men do not drill on that day.

FX01-011.power: Thirty acres of Gordush holding, a sergeant's warrant from the Harrows and the respect of every Stake-Man on the line.
FX01-011.history: In September 1049 Gunnar Harrow held the Gordush ford with 300 house-men for an hour so Emperor Conrad could escape the Bend. Wat Fordham, a twenty-year-old crossbowman, was one of a handful who lived, and he dragged Gunnar's body out of the water. In 1052 the Harrows gave him a holding by the ford and a sergeant's warrant for his line. Fordhams held the Crossmarch walls in 1073 and have drilled under every Master of the Stake Yard since. In 1103 one Fordham son went over the river to Tarn Halfblood.
FX01-011.reputation: The best sergeants on the Gordush, and the proudest.

members.role: Founder; last living man of Gunnar Harrow's 300
members.note: He is half blind and still walks to the ford every September with a stake on his shoulder.

members.role: Head of the family; sergeant of the ford
members.note: He drills under Captain Hilda Rook at the Stake Yard and can plant a stake line faster than any man alive.

members.role: Heir; hundredman of the Stake-Men
members.note: He wants a captain's warrant, and Lord Garrick's war is the fastest way to one.

members.role: Younger son; deserter
members.note: He crossed the Gordush in 1103 with a half-orc girl from Hazelhollow and now rides with Tarn Halfblood's men.

FX01-011.secret: Ranulf has had two letters from Dunstan across the river, and has burned neither.
hooks: When Lord Garrick crosses after May Fair, the Fordhams may meet their own son on the far bank.
Old Wat wants to be buried at the ford, on the Horde side of it.

FX01-012.name: House Thornley
FX01-012.title: Castellan of Thornstone and Dunwatch
FX01-012.arms: a white castle on dark grey

military.office: Castellans of the Crown Wall at Thornstone and Dunwatch
military.unit: the Wall Crossbows, 1,500, and the Wall Riders of the western forts
military.ties: Thornleys have commanded the old Solen forts since Harald took them in 956, and Marshal Stane counts the Crown Wall as theirs.

FX01-012.power: Command of the western forts of the Crown Wall and the Amber Road tolls at Thornstone.
FX01-012.history: When Harald marched south in 956 and took 22 old Solen forts from the herders living in them, he gave the western ones to Sir Hamo Thornley, a captain who had stormed Eagleburg's breach. The Thornleys have kept them since, beside the Harrows' old fort of Dunwatch. They know every cistern and stair of the Crown Wall, built by Solen engineers five centuries before. In 1101 the castellan's son broke up a floor at Dunwatch to mend a drain and found what lies under it.
FX01-012.reputation: Hard, careful wall-men who never leave their forts and never lose them.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Thornstone
members.note: He ordered the Dunwatch floor sealed with lime the same night and has not let a stranger into the undercroft since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Wall Riders
members.note: He rides the wall road between the forts in all weathers and knows every herder's son by name.

members.role: Godric's eldest son, passed over
members.note: He is the one who lifted the floor, and since then he drinks and talks about the bones.

members.role: Godric's daughter; keeper of the cisterns
members.note: She has mapped every Solen water-channel under the wall and believes some of them run under the range.

famousDead: Stormed the Eagleburg breach and was given the western Crown Wall forts in 956
FX01-012.secret: The floors of the Crown Wall forts are laid over the bones of orc captives the Solen buried there; if the Horde ever learns it, the wall becomes a blood-cause.
hooks: Wendel tells the story of the bones to a half-orc drover in a Thornstone alehouse.
A Horde envoy passing to Kingsmere asks to sleep one night in Dunwatch's undercroft.

FX01-013.name: House Ringmere
FX01-013.title: Bearer of the Iron Ring Banner
FX01-013.arms: a gold crown above a silver lance, on crimson

military.office: Hereditary Standard-Bearers of the Iron Guard
military.unit: the Banner Lance of the Iron Guard, 12 knights
military.ties: A Ringmere has carried the iron ring banner in every battle since Harald's crowning, and three have died holding it upright.

FX01-013.power: Galemere Tower and its 20 hearths, and the honour of riding at the emperor's right hand in war.
FX01-013.history: Sir Ulf Ringmere carried the iron ring banner before Harald Ironside at his crowning on Return Day 951, and his line has carried it since. At the Gordush Bend in September 1049 the banner-bearer Sir Aldric Ringmere was cut down in the river and the banner was lost for an hour before Emperor Conrad rode home under it. A Ringmere carried it at Hartgate in 1051 and at the Gashmar Fords in 1070. The family is poor in land and rich in scars.
FX01-013.reputation: The bravest fools in the Iron Guard.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Galemere Tower
members.note: He carried the banner at the Gashmar Fords with an orc spear through his thigh and never let it dip.

members.role: Heir; Bearer of the Iron Ring Banner
members.note: He rides with Prince Harald's hundred and has no son to take the banner after him.

members.role: Ivo's only child
members.note: She rides at the quintain every morning and means to carry the banner herself, whatever the Iron Guard says.

famousDead: Carried the iron ring banner at Harald's crowning in 951
Died holding the banner in the river at the Gordush Bend
FX01-013.secret: The banner lost at the Gordush Bend was never found; the one Conrad rode home under was sewn that night, and the true banner hangs in a war-captain's tent at Gashmar.
hooks: A half-orc trader offers to sell Sir Ivo a scrap of old crimson silk with an iron ring on it.
Wynn enters the Lance Yard trials in her dead uncle's armour.

FX01-014.name: House Wardlaw
FX01-014.title: Castellan of Frosthollow and Keeper of the Thirty-One Stones
FX01-014.arms: a white mountain on blue, a black stone at its foot

military.office: Castellans of Frosthollow and Keepers of the Watershed Stones
military.unit: the Watershed garrison, 600 of the 2,500 men of the forts and Brightmoor
military.ties: Since the burning of Brightmoor the Wardlaws have sworn to hold the watershed until a Winterborn pays for it.

FX01-014.power: Frosthollow Castle and the watch-forts along the 31 border stones set in 952.
FX01-014.history: Sir Brand Wardlaw helped set the 31 stones of the Peace of the Stones along the Stagflow watershed in June 952, and his family was given Frosthollow to keep them. For 138 years the stones meant trade, and the Wardlaws grew lazy on rye carts. On 19 January 1092 Eirik of Northreach led 800 men over the frozen Glenwash mouth and burned the grain stores at Brightmoor while Sir Thurstan Wardlaw slept two hours away. He was stripped of his command and his daughter Gerda has held the watershed since.
FX01-014.reputation: The house that slept through Brightmoor, and has not slept since.

members.role: Head of the family in name; disgraced castellan of Brightmoor
members.note: He still wears the black arm-band he put on the morning the barns burned.

members.role: Heir; Castellan of Frosthollow
members.note: She walks the stones every new moon and has set bells on the ice of the Glenwash mouth.

members.role: Younger son; quartermaster of the watch-forts
members.note: He sells the forts' spare rye over the stones to Stagflow farmers and has a Northreach wife nobody at Frosthollow knows about.

famousDead: Set the 31 stones of 952 with the Northreach envoys
FX01-014.secret: Kettil's wife is a granddaughter of the Greymane exiles of the Stagflow, and he crosses the stones to see her twice a month.
hooks: Gerda's bells ring on a winter night, and the tracks lead to her own brother.
Northreach's Stone-Watch accuses Frosthollow of moving the ninth stone a hundred paces north.

FX01-015.name: the Winchcombe family
FX01-015.title: Master of the Imperial Engine Yard

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Imperial Engine Corps
military.unit: the Imperial Engine Corps, 1,000 men, with two crews at Crossmarch
military.ties: No engine of the empire is raised without a Winchcombe measuring its throw, and Marshal Stane wants them at the Gashmar Fords by July.

FX01-015.power: The engine yard at Kingsmere, the drawings of every counterweight engine in the empire and the Marshal's trust.
FX01-015.history: The Winchcombes were carpenters who built the timber scaffolds for the new Oath Hall steps in 1002 and stayed on as the crown's engine-wrights. In 1073 Master Hamo Winchcombe raised two counterweight engines on Crossmarch's towers and broke a seven-week Horde siege in an afternoon. Emperor Conrad made the mastery of the engine yard hereditary for it. The family has built for the Crown Host ever since and keeps its drawings in a locked chest under the yard.
FX01-015.reputation: Clever, sour craftsmen who count stones while knights count glory.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Engine Yard
members.note: He broke the siege of Crossmarch with two engines and has never let anyone forget it.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Crossmarch engine crews
members.note: He keeps the Crossmarch engines oiled through the winter and sleeps beside them in war.

members.role: Hamo's daughter; draughtswoman
members.note: She has drawn an engine that could throw stone across the Gordush from the north bank, and her father says it cannot work.

members.role: Apprentice; Ingram's son
members.note: A Varennan factor has bought him three dinners and asked about his aunt's drawings.

FX01-015.secret: Beatrix's great engine works; she has built a small one in secret and it throws twice as far as her father's.
hooks: Perrin is caught copying his aunt's drawings for a Varennan buyer.
Marshal Stane asks for an engine that can reach the far bank of the Gordush before July.

FX01-016.name: the Saltash family
FX01-016.title: Mistress of the Saltash Barges
FX01-016.power: Forty grain barges on the Fairrush and the rye contract that feeds a third of Northreach.
FX01-016.history: Osric Saltash was a Yewmarch grain-factor who held full barns when the Fairrush froze in the Long Winter of 1011. He sold his rye in the spring of 1012 at ten times its price and bought barges with the silver. His heirs carried rye down to Cold Bay and on to Wolfhaven under the Peace of the Stones, and the Northreach Rising nearly ruined them. They pay the Fairrush river tolls without complaint and lend to Lady Audra's cause.
FX01-016.reputation: Rich, warm-hearted to their friends and remembered by the Kingsmere poor for 1012.

members.role: Head of the family; Mistress of the Saltash Barges
members.note: She keeps two sets of grain books, one for the Fairrush toll-men and one for herself.

members.role: Heir; barge-master
members.note: He knows every lock-keeper on the Fairrush and drinks with all of them.

members.role: Edith's brother; factor at Wolfhaven
members.note: He has lived on the Cold Coast for twenty years and thinks of Northreach as home.

members.role: Edith's daughter
members.note: She married a Coldhaven sealer against her mother's will and was cut out of the books.

famousDead: Sold hoarded rye at ten times its price after the Long Winter and founded the barge trade
FX01-016.secret: Osric hid grain while Kingsmere starved in 1011, and Lady Maud Ravenscar's grain carts were filled from stores the crown forced him to open.
hooks: A war with Northreach would rot a season of Saltash rye on the quays.
A Kingsmere hall-singer has made a song about the Saltash barns of 1011.

FX01-017.name: the Daggett family
FX01-017.title: Weigh-Master of the Eagleburg Iron Hall
FX01-017.arms: an iron bar between two black hammers, on rust orange
FX01-017.power: The brokerage of Irondeep bars at Eagleburg and a seat at the table of the Iron Road Company.
FX01-017.history: The first Daggett was a carter who drove the first loads of bar iron down the Iron Road after the Compact of 951. His sons learned the dwarves' trade-hand signs and set up as brokers between the Deepeye factors and the plains smiths. For 150 years they have weighed iron at Eagleburg under the Erneholt castellans and resented them. Since the Rising left the empire in debt to Irondeep, the dwarves weigh more carefully and the Daggetts earn less.
FX01-017.reputation: Sharp, tight-fisted and indispensable on the Iron Road.

members.role: Head of the family; Weigh-Master
members.note: He wants the Erneholts' weigh-house and would lend the dwarves the rope to hang them.

members.role: Heir; broker to the Deepeye factors
members.note: She signs with the dwarves faster than she speaks and is ashamed of her family's scales.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He packs crates for the Iron Road Company that leave no mark in any book.

members.role: Ulric's mother
members.note: She learned hand-signs from dwarf carters as a girl and still swears at them in it.

FX01-017.secret: The Daggett scales at Eagleburg read light for the dwarves, as the Tin Reeves' balance does for the giants, and a Deepeye clerk has begun to check them.
hooks: Hesketh's crate of 200 unrecorded crossbows is stolen on the Kingsmere quays.
A Deepeye weigh-clerk asks Anwen to swear on her family's scales.

FX01-018.name: the Pennick family
FX01-018.title: Master of the Bell-Founders of Bell Ward
FX01-018.power: The bell pits of Bell Ward and the right to cast every bell and bronze fitting for the Oath Hall and the Crown Host.
FX01-018.history: Wulf Pennick cast the great bell of the Oath Hall when Edmund the Waller rebuilt it in stone in 843, and his family has run the bell-founders of Bell Ward since. They cast harness bronze for the Iron Guard and pulleys for the engine yard. In the Long Winter of 1011 the great bell cracked in the frost and was recast in eight days. The Pennicks drink at the Hunter's Mead with the soldiers and never eat horse.
FX01-018.reputation: Loud, proud and deaf in one ear each.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Bell-Founders
members.note: He hears the Oath Hall bell every hour and winces at the fourth stroke.

members.role: Heir; bell-tuner
members.note: She tunes bells by ear and says the great bell has a flaw that will split it.

members.role: Younger son; bronze-caster for the engine yard
members.note: He fights soldiers in the Hunter's Mead for pleasure and the Winchcombes for money.

famousDead: Cast the great bell of the Oath Hall in 843
FX01-018.secret: The great bell recast in 1012 was poured too fast and has a hollow in its lip; the Pennicks know it will crack one day under a hard ringing.
hooks: The Oath Hall bell must ring for a full hour on the wedding day, 21 June.
Ranulf and the Winchcombes quarrel over who owes whom for a bronze winch.

FX01-019.name: the Ringwold line
FX01-019.title: Keeper of the Drowning Steps
FX01-019.arms: a white hand holding an iron ring, on dark blue
FX01-019.words: The Sea King Keeps What We Give
FX01-019.power: The keeping of the Drowning Steps below the Oath Hall and the roll of everyone given to the river since 951.
FX01-019.history: When Harald made drowning the punishment for traitors, he needed hall-priests to bind them to the iron ring and sing them to the Sea King. The Ringwolds have done it since 951, from father to child, on the stone stairs below the Oath Hall. They swore to the emperor as head of the Halls in 1002 without a murmur. They also keep the roll of every drowning, which Hakon never thought to take into his own keeping.
FX01-019.reputation: Feared, avoided at feasts and never short of a seat in the Oath Hall.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Drowning Steps
members.note: He has bound eleven men to the ring and remembers every one of their last words.

members.role: Heir; singer of the oath-lays
members.note: She sings the dawn oath-lays in the Oath Hall and has the best voice in Kingsmere.

members.role: Wulfric's elder son; outlawed
members.note: He read the old drowning roll, turned Free Hall and fled to Easterham, and his father must drown him if he is caught.

members.role: Sunniva's daughter
members.note: She reads the old rolls in the vault for fun and has found her uncle's marks in the margins.

famousDead: First Keeper of the Drowning Steps under Harald the Founder
FX01-019.secret: The drowning roll shows two Easterham men drowned on Harald's word in 946 for speaking of the Glenwash truce, with no crime written beside their names.
hooks: Aelfric Ringwold is taken at Easterham and brought to the Steps, where his father must bind him.
Ragna of the Stones writes to ask whether the Ringwolds keep a roll for 946.

FX01-020.name: the Tansy family
FX01-020.title: Bonesetter to the Hide-Knights
FX01-020.arms: a yellow tansy flower on green
FX01-020.power: The trust of every knight who has fallen from a horse, and a bone-house at Goldburg where the Lance Yard sends its broken men.
FX01-020.history: The Tansys were herb-wives of the Goldburg forest who learned to set bones for the woodcutters. In 1009 young Elfa Tansy set the leg of a Hide-Knight so well that Hakon's marshal took her family into the crown's service. For three generations they have set the bones of the Crown Host and of the imperial family. They have noticed things about Ironside bones that no other physician has been close enough to see.

members.role: Head of the family; Bonesetter to the Hide-Knights
members.note: He set Prince Harald's collarbone in 1094 and has told no one why he needed two men to lift the boy's arm.

members.role: Heir; physician of the Lance Yard
members.note: She treats Sir Roland Ashby's old wounds and is a little in love with him.

members.role: Hesketh's grandson; student
members.note: He has written a treatise on heavy bones and plans to show it to scholars in the south.

members.role: Hesketh's wife; herb-wife
members.note: She grows every herb of her great-grandmother's garden and sells poppy to nobody.

famousDead: Set a Hide-Knight's shattered leg in 1009 and brought the family into the crown's service
FX01-020.secret: The Tansys know the Ironside bones are dense as iron and that the dynasty sinks in water.
hooks: Oswy's treatise on heavy bones goes missing on the road south.
The Ravenscar owls ask Hesketh to examine a drowned man fished from the Fairrush.

FX01-021.name: the Coltsworth family
FX01-021.title: Stud-Master of the Millrun
FX01-021.arms: a white horse courant on green

military.office: Masters of the Millrun Stud Guard
military.unit: the Millrun Stud Guard, 1,500 light horse
military.ties: Every destrier of the Iron Guard is foaled under a Coltsworth eye, and their sons captain the riders who guard the crown studs.

FX01-021.power: The keeping of the crown studs of the Millrun, about 200 brood mares of the best war-horse line in the north.
FX01-021.history: Ada Coltsworth was stud-groom to one of the southern plains lords who fell at the Millrun in June 938. She brought his mares to Harald the next morning, and he kept her to run them when the Millrun studs became crown land. Her line has bred the destriers of the Iron Guard and the Hide-Knights since. They sell at the Horsefair of Kingsmere every Thursday and count the Ironsides, horse-breeders themselves once, as kin of the trade.
FX01-021.reputation: They love horses more than people, and the horses know it.

members.role: Head of the family; Stud-Master of the Millrun
members.note: He can tell a colt's temper by the way it stands in the rain.

members.role: Heir; judge of destriers at the Horsefair
members.note: Every lord who buys a war-horse at the Horsefair waits for her nod.

members.role: Younger son; captain in the Stud Guard
members.note: He hunts horse thieves along the Millrun and has hanged two.

members.role: Aldred's cousin; dealer
members.note: He sold six crown mares to a Nine Winds buyer and reported them dead of colic.

famousDead: Brought her dead lord's mares to Harald after the Millrun in 938
FX01-021.secret: Garth's six mares were Ironfoot stock, the best line in the studs, and the Nine Winds now breed them.
hooks: Quay Dog thieves sell a crown-branded mare at the Horsefair under Elswyth's nose.
A Nine Winds envoy rides into Kingsmere on an Ironfoot mare.

FX01-022.name: the Underwood family
FX01-022.title: Chief Verderer of the Foxhurst March

military.office: Foresters of the Crown on the Foxhurst march
military.unit: 120 of the 1,800 Crown Foresters
military.ties: Underwood foresters scout the Oak Line for the Crown Host and were the only Aldmark men who came home whole from the forest edge in 1079.

FX01-022.power: A forester's warrant over half the old Blackthorn woods and a quiet understanding with the elven watchers.
FX01-022.history: The Underwoods were charcoal-burners who carried grain to the Oak Line villages by night beside Maud Ravenscar in the Long Winter, and Hakon made them foresters for it in 1012. In 1078 Hamo Underwood carried the elves' three warnings to Lord Oswy Blackthorn, who laughed at him. After Rinael the Ravenscar wardens gave the Underwoods half of Oswy's forest to keep. They know where every marker stone stands and never cross one.
FX01-022.reputation: Half-wild folk who talk to trees, say the Foxhurst townsmen, and the trees answer.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief Verderer
members.note: He carried the elves' warnings to Lord Oswy in 1078 and was told to go back to his charcoal.

members.role: Heir; forester
members.note: She has learned forty words of elvish from the edge-folk and uses them on the watchers.

members.role: Hamo's daughter; living beyond the stones
members.note: She married a licensed edge-folk man of the Evenwood and lives on the elven side under their law.

FX01-022.secret: For twenty years the Underwoods have taken elven silver to warn the Evenwood whenever Aldmark loggers or soldiers move near the stones.
hooks: Ivo Blackthorn swears to hang the forester who betrayed his grandfather.
Wynn sends word that the elves are watching a Ravenscar man who meets them at new moon.

FX01-023.name: the Gullick family
FX01-023.title: Master of the Copperton Yard
FX01-023.arms: a black anchor on white over blue
FX01-023.power: The cog yard under Copperton Tower, where most of the Cold Bay squadron's cogs were built, and four cogs of their own.
FX01-023.history: Thurstan Gullick the Elder built river barges at Copperton until Conrad wanted a fleet. From 1035 the yard built cogs for the crown, first in plains oak, then in Greyhaven oak after the elves closed the Oak Line in 1080. Gullick cogs carried supplies for the failed blockade of Wolfhaven in 1092, and two of them burned with the Greyhaven galleys. The family wants Aldmark to sail its own tin from Frostholm and break Northreach's trade.
FX01-023.reputation: Good shipwrights, bad losers, eager for a sea war.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Copperton Yard
members.note: He lost two cogs and a son in the blockade of 1092 and wants Wolfhaven to pay.

members.role: Heir; master shipwright
members.note: She is building a cog with a sternpost rudder from drawings her father bought from a Greyhaven drunk.

members.role: Younger son; cog captain
members.note: He wants to captain the Amber Guild's tin cog to Frostholm and does not fear Northreach's longships.

famousDead: Burned with his cog off Wolfhaven in the blockade of 1092
FX01-023.secret: Svala's rudder drawings were stolen from the Greyhaven royal yard, and the Tidewells would call it theft by an ally.
hooks: Master Tova Brand offers Brand Gullick command of her tin cog to Skarfell.
A Greyhaven shipwright visits Copperton and recognises his own drawings.

FX01-024.name: the Hallams
FX01-024.title: Master of the Quay Dogs
FX01-024.arms: a dog's head scratched on a barge hook
FX01-024.power: The Quay Dogs, about 40 bargemen, porters and river-watch men who pilfer cargo, fence stolen horses and run dice on the Kingsmere quays.
FX01-024.history: Wat Hallam's father was a bargeman crushed between two barges in 1059, and the Fairrush quays gave his widow nothing. Her sons began by pilfering grain sacks and grew into the Quay Dogs, the gang that runs the Kingsmere waterfront after dark. They drink at the Barge and Bell, fence horses through the Horsefair and run dice in the frozen warehouses each winter. The river watch takes a cut, and Lady Ysolde's owls take what Wat hears.
FX01-024.reputation: Thieves who keep their word, which on the quays is the same as honest.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Quay Dogs
members.note: He sells what he hears to the Ravenscar owls and has let two of his own crew hang to keep it quiet.

members.role: Heir; runs the dice
members.note: She holds the IOUs of half a dozen young lords, including a Quarrender.

members.role: Wat's son; river watchman
members.note: He walks the quays with a lantern and hook for the city and tells his father which warehouses are unguarded.

members.role: Wat's mother; fence of horses
members.note: She can change a crown brand on a mare's hip in an evening.

FX01-024.secret: Wat has been an informer for Lady Ysolde since 1094, and two Quay Dogs hanged for thefts he named.
hooks: The Quay Dogs steal a crate from the Iron Road Company House and find 200 crossbows packed for the Gordush.
A hanged man's brother learns who informed on him.

FX01-025.name: the kin of Fenny Ford
FX01-025.title: Grandmother of Fenny Ford
FX01-025.arms: a red flame chalked on a barn door
FX01-025.power: Kin in every half-orc village of the Southern March and riders across the Gordush with Tarn Halfblood.
FX01-025.history: The kin of Fenny Ford were half-orc farmers of the Southern March who held their land by blood-price custom long before Aldmark drew the Gordush line. The License Law of 1053 took their fields, and the Harrows' men gave them to strangers. In April 1103 some of their young men rode with Tarn Halfblood when he burned the tax barns at Hazelhollow and Copperham. In May the Ravenscar Night Riders, acting on an informer's guess, burned an innocent family of the kin in their barn at Fenny Ford.
FX01-025.reputation: Rebels and barn-burners to the marcher lords; martyrs to every half-orc of the march.

members.role: Head of the kin; grandmother of Fenny Ford
members.note: She lost a son, his wife and three grandchildren in the Fenny Ford barn, and she knows who named them.

members.role: Durra's grandson; rider with Tarn Halfblood
members.note: He crossed the Gordush in 1103 and comes back on moonless nights to see his grandmother.

members.role: Licensed smith of Hazelhollow
members.note: He keeps his license paper sewn into his shirt and his head down, and shoes the Hayward horses.

members.role: Survivor of Fenny Ford
members.note: She hid in the well while the barn burned and has not spoken since.

famousDead: Burned in his barn with his family by Night Riders on a false report
FX01-025.secret: Durra knows the informer who sent the Night Riders to Fenny Ford was the License Reeve's younger son, paid five marks for a name.
hooks: Oswin Gordale asks the kin to keep the peace until his petition is heard at Kingsmere.
Ulric brings a Horde rider to Hazelhollow on a moonless night.

FX01-026.name: the Hayward family
FX01-026.title: License Reeve of the Southern March
FX01-026.power: The license rolls of the Southern March: no half-orc may own land or bear arms without a Hayward signature under the Harrow seal.
FX01-026.history: Sewald Hayward's father was a Harrow clerk who drew up the first license rolls when the law of 1053 came in. The family has kept them ever since and grown fat on fees, gifts and the land of those who could not pay. Their rolls decided which farms the marcher lords took between 1053 and 1063. In April 1103 Tarn Halfblood burned the Harrow tax barns at Hazelhollow and Copperham, and the Hayward copies of the rolls burned with them.
FX01-026.reputation: Every half-orc in the march spits at the name; every marcher lord needs them.

members.role: Head of the family; License Reeve
members.note: He is rewriting the burned rolls from memory, and his memory is kind to his friends.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the license rolls
members.note: She has noticed that her father's new rolls list fewer licenses than the old ones did.

members.role: Younger son; license rider
members.note: He gave the Night Riders a name at Fenny Ford for five marks, and he hears the barn in his sleep.

FX01-026.secret: Thurstan Hayward was the informer whose false report sent the Night Riders to burn the family at Fenny Ford.
hooks: Edith finds a licensed family missing from her father's new rolls, and their farm already promised to a Carrow.
Durra of Fenny Ford sends Thurstan a burnt stick wrapped in a five-mark note.

FX02-001.name: House Lantieri
FX02-001.title: Lord of the Sea Gate, by Solen honor
FX02-001.arms: a white sea-tower on the dark blue of the old court

military.office: Honorary Captains of the Sea Gate
military.unit: a household of 30 men and the right to stand the first watch on the Sea Gate at Return Day
military.ties: Lantieri sons have served as officers of the Bay Marines since the See was founded, though the house has had no real command since 759.

FX02-001.power: A stone house in the Blue Ward, olive groves outside the Clarente Gate worth about 2,000 suns a year, an old name and a relic nobody has seen.
FX02-001.history: The Lantieri held the Sea Gate of Solenne for the emperors from 418, when Brother Aldo Corvane died and the Crown branch's last captains passed their posts to their clients. On Ash Night 759, when General Marcus Vell opened the Lantern Gate, Captain Ottavio Lantieri held the Sea Gate until dawn and then fought his way up to the palace. He found the emperor already dead in his bedchamber, not on the stairs, and picked a gilt spur off the floor. He was killed in the sack the next day. His widow kept the spur, and the house has kept it and its hatred of the Vells ever since. Under the See the Lantieri became poor gentlefolk of the Blue Ward and loyal clients of House Corvane, and in 1105 they would follow Lady Aurelia's restoration anywhere.
FX02-001.reputation: Proud, poor, punctilious; the Blue Ward's best manners and its oldest grudge.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Sea Gate
members.note: He crosses the street rather than share a pavement with Matthias Vell.

members.role: Heiress; lady-in-waiting to Lady Aurelia Corvane
members.note: She carries messages between Lady Aurelia and the Luminaries whose debts the Corvanes bought.

members.role: Son; lieutenant of the Bay Marines
members.note: He has challenged a Vell cousin twice, and twice his captain has stopped it.

members.role: His aunt; keeper of the house relic
members.note: She sleeps with the gilt spur in a box under her bed and has never shown it to a priest.

famousDead: Held the Sea Gate on Ash Night and found the emperor dead in his bedchamber.
FX02-001.secret: The Lantieri keep a gilt spur of the Knights of the Sun picked up in Constantine IX's bedchamber on Ash Night, proof that the Temple's own knights killed him.
hooks: Joined with the Vell letter, the spur could break the See's founding story.
Valerio's duel with a Vell finally happens.
Lady Aurelia asks for the spur as the price of a place at her son's court.

FX02-002.name: House Palenzi
FX02-002.title: Knight of Palena Ford
FX02-002.arms: a black ram on a silver ford, on red

military.office: Knights of Lorina Castle
military.unit: 3 lances and 60 men in the Lorina Castle garrison
military.ties: Palenzi knights have served the Brennus lords in Lorina Castle for 400 years, and the present heir is Lady Petra Brennus's second in the galley squadron.

FX02-002.power: Sheep walks and a mill at Palena Ford, about 900 suns a year, and three lances in the Brennus service.
FX02-002.history: The Palenzi were sheep lords of the Palena Ford when Theodoric I lost to Maximus under Lorina's walls in 657, and they were knighted by the Brennus lords the next year for holding the ford. They have served Lorina ever since. When Cato Brennus married Donata of Palena in 1069, a Palenzi cousin of the wool family, the house became the Brennus kin as well as their knights. Donata died in the Harbor Pox of 1077, and the Palenzi raised her daughter Petra to row and ride with their own boys. The heir sails with Petra now. He knows she has promised Varenna twelve of the See's galleys without the High Luminary's leave.
FX02-002.reputation: Plain, sheep-smelling knights of the east, as loyal to Lorina as their dogs are to them.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Palena Ford
members.note: He still calls Lord Cato 'cousin' in public, which nobody else in Lorina would dare.

members.role: Heir; second captain of the Lorina squadron
members.note: He grew up beside Petra Brennus and will sail where she points, even to Varenna.

members.role: Daughter; named for the late Lady of Lorina
members.note: She runs the wool sales and knows the Lorina shepherds who opened the Mirona pit.

members.role: Younger son; squire at Lorina Castle
members.note: He has carried a sealed packet to a Varennan cog captain twice and wants to know what was in it.

famousDead: Held Palena Ford for Lorina in 657; first knight of the house.
FX02-002.secret: The Palenzi heir has helped Petra Brennus promise twelve of the See's galleys to Varenna without the High Luminary's leave.
hooks: Remo opens one of the packets meant for Varenna.
The Treasurer asks why the Lorina galleys are fitting out in winter.
Donata's shepherds know where more of the Mirona dead are buried.

FX02-003.name: House Sestani
FX02-003.title: Lord of Dorura, by Solen honor
FX02-003.arms: a gold olive tree on green, a silver coin in its branches
FX02-003.power: About 3,000 acres of olive and wine land in the Dorata vale, about 7,000 suns a year, and the private debts of two Luminaries.
FX02-003.history: The Sestani were oil merchants of Dorata under the emperors and kept their counting rooms through the Hungry Years by lending to the See's tenants. When the Harbor Pox of 1077 killed the last of the Dorata Corvanes, their olive farms came up for lease, and in 1079 Tullio Sestani outbid Lady Aurelia's agents with Ostran money. The High Luminary gave him the honorary style of Lord of Dorura with the lease. The Corvanes have called them thieves of the Stone's land ever since. In 1105 the Sestani hold the debts of two Luminaries, and they are selling those votes to Treasurer Dorn while the Corvanes sell four to whoever will crown a Corvane.
FX02-003.reputation: New money with an old title; the Blue Ward sneers, and then borrows.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Dorura
members.note: He keeps the two Luminaries' notes in an Ostran strong-box and has told Treasurer Dorn the price.

members.role: Heiress
members.note: She wants her son married to a Corvane girl and the feud ended by a cradle.

members.role: Son; oil factor at Ostra
members.note: He banks with House Lunetti and hears every rumour of the Temple's accounts.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She can see colours that her tutor cannot, and the family has started to wonder whose blood that is.

famousDead: Lent the See's tenants seed corn after the Black Cough at a quarter interest and doubled the house fortune.
FX02-003.secret: Livia Sestani's mother was a Dorata Corvane's mistress, and the granddaughter may have the Sunborn eyes.
hooks: The Sestani votes decide the High Luminary's chair if Dorn is short.
Lucia's eyes would make her a Corvane claimant.
Lady Aurelia's agents look for a reason to break the Dorura lease.

FX02-004.name: House Valcorso
FX02-004.title: Knight of Clarente Tower
FX02-004.arms: a silver hawk on a black square keep, on blue

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of Clarente Tower
military.unit: the Clarente Tower garrison, 120 crossbowmen and coast-tower men
military.ties: The house keeps Clarente Tower over the Sun Road for the See and sends a son to the Knights of the Sun in every generation.

FX02-004.power: Clarente Tower and its 120 men, a knight's manor of salt-pan and wheat land on the Clarente plain, and the ear of Keeper Marius Quill.
FX02-004.history: In September 757 a Varennan scout named Nerio Valcorso saw Constantine IX's sally come out at Clarente and raised the alarm that let Lucan's cavalry catch it in the open. When the See was founded, Benedict the First kept him as keeper of the square tower over the Sun Road, and the house has kept it since. The Valcorsos turned from Varennans into the See's most loyal knights. A Valcorso son has taken the Noon vows in every generation, and the present keeper's brother is a Needle-Keeper. Their neighbours the Merels hold the old granary, and in 1105 the Valcorsos are Keeper Quill's men on the plain, watching the beams.
FX02-004.reputation: Watchful, devout and humourless; the Clarente salt-workers say a Valcorso can see a smuggler's lantern from the tower in fog.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Clarente Tower
members.note: Keeper Quill has told him that if the Merel beams leave the granary, they must burn on the road.

members.role: His brother; Needle-Keeper
members.note: He sits beside Brother Lucan Serra in the Needle Court and reports his every word to Keeper Quill.

members.role: Heiress; married to a Merel cousin
members.note: She pities Sir Tobias's motherless children and has warned him that the tower watches the granary road.

members.role: Son; Knight of the Sun at Noon Hall
members.note: He has been named to ride north in March with the Silverbough envoy.

famousDead: Raised the alarm at Clarente in 757; first keeper of the tower.
FX02-004.secret: The keeper has orders from Keeper Quill to burn the Clarente beams on the road if Sir Tobias tries to move them.
hooks: A night cart leaves the Clarente granary.
Elisa must choose between her father's orders and her husband's kin.
Sir Ugo rides north with a sword meant for theft.

FX02-005.name: House Orvieni
FX02-005.title: Banneret of the Mirona Hills
FX02-005.arms: a black crow on a burning wheat sheaf, on gold

military.office: Bannerets of the Mirona hills levy
military.unit: the Orvieni banner, 18 lances and the Mirona tenant spears
military.ties: The house leads the Sworn Tenant Spears of the Mirona hills and works hand in glove with the Mirona Hill Scouts against the Ashen.

FX02-005.power: Temple leases over thirty poor hill villages around Mirona, the hill levy and the low justice of the hills.
FX02-005.history: The Orvieni were granted the Mirona leases by Odo I the Chronicler in 812 to keep order in the poor hills where the granary fire of 3 BR is remembered every November. Their arms show the crow on the burning sheaf, and their words say who watches the bread. In August 1094, when 31 pilgrims were murdered on the Mirona road while their escort commander slept drunk at an inn, the banneret's court tried two Mirona shepherds and hanged them on the See's orders. Everyone in the hills knows they were innocent. Since 1099 the half-elf Isaria Vale has preached to the house's tenants, and in 1103 Lorina shepherds opened a pit of hanged men outside Mirona's old wall. The hills are restless, and the banneret is afraid.
FX02-005.reputation: The See's hangmen in the hills; the tenants bow and then spit behind the hedge.

members.role: Head of the house; Banneret of the Mirona Hills
members.note: He signed the shepherds' death warrant in 1094 and has slept with a lamp lit ever since.

members.role: Heiress
members.note: She leads the hunts for the Ashen herself and believes every word the See teaches.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She slips out at night to hear Isaria Vale preach and has given her the family's spare blankets.

members.role: Son; clerk of the banneret's court
members.note: He wrote down the shepherds' trial and kept a copy that names who ordered the verdict.

FX02-005.secret: The court clerk's copy of the 1094 trial shows the See ordered two innocent shepherds hanged to cover a drunken knight's failure.
hooks: Ottavia hunts the preacher her sister shelters.
The hanged shepherds' families want the trial record.
A Mirona November vigil turns into a riot.

FX02-006.name: House Ascellani
FX02-006.title: Knight of Ascello
FX02-006.arms: a white cross pattée on a red sun, on gold

military.office: Patrons of the Ascello chapter of the Knights of the Sun
military.unit: the Ascello chapter house, 40 knight-brothers and sergeants
military.ties: An Ascellani son has taken the Noon vows in every generation since 781, and the chapter house of Ascello stands on the family's land.

FX02-006.power: A knight's manor at Ascello beside the Lavino estates, a chapter house of the Knights of the Sun on its land, and the friendship of the Vells.
FX02-006.history: When Tavian I ruled that Temple tenants owe forty days, he needed knights to lead them, and he gave the manor at Ascello beside the Lavino estates to Sir Benno Ascellani in 781. Benno gave the land under his chapel to the Knights of the Sun, and a chapter house has stood there since. The Ascellani have given a son to the vows in every generation. They are the Vells' neighbours, and the Vells' wine goes to market on Ascellani carts. In 1105 the head's younger brother is commander of the Ascello chapter, a vowed Knight of the Sun, and has a wife and two children hidden in a farmhouse three valleys away.
FX02-006.reputation: Devout country knights who give the Temple sons and the Vells company; sound people, the Brunentia market says.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Ascello
members.note: He thinks his brother's secret is the worst thing a family could hide, and he hides it.

members.role: His brother; Knight of the Sun, commander of the Ascello chapter
members.note: He rides to his wife's farmhouse on the chapter's business days and back before vespers.

members.role: Heiress
members.note: She is betrothed to a Vell cousin and has read the Vell chapel's inventory, which lists a lead tube under the altar.

members.role: Sir Garin's son, raised as a shepherd's boy
members.note: He has the family's face and does not know why the knight brings him sweets.

famousDead: Given Ascello in 781; gave the chapter house its land.
FX02-006.secret: Sir Garin Ascellani, a vowed Knight of the Sun, has a wife and two children, which would cost him his vows and the house its chapter.
hooks: A Noon Hall inspector visits Ascello.
Treasurer Dorn reviews the old leases, the Vells' and the Ascellani's.
Nino sees his father in mail and follows him home.

FX02-007.name: the Quadrelli family
FX02-007.title: Sergeant-Major of the Crossbow Yard of Dorata
FX02-007.arms: a black crossbow bolt pointing upward on silver, three red bars below

military.office: Hereditary Sergeant-Majors of the Crossbow Yard of Dorata
military.unit: the Dorata Crossbows, 4,000 men, and the Yard's armoury
military.ties: A Quadrelli has drilled every Dorata crossbowman since Odo I founded the Yard in 811, and the family keeps the armoury tallies.

FX02-007.power: The sergeant-majorship of the Crossbow Yard, its armoury keys and tallies, and the loyalty of two centuries of Dorata shooters.
FX02-007.history: On 1 April 811 Odo I the Chronicler founded the Crossbow Yard of Dorata so that paid crossbowmen, not town militia, would man the Valerian Wall. He hired a Tessarian-trained sergeant, Bruno Quadrelli, to drill them. Bruno's sons and grandsons have drilled the Yard since, and the Quadrelli count every bow, bolt and windlass in its armoury. The Dorata Crossbows man the Valerian Wall in war and the coast towers in peace. In 1105 the Yard's captain, Hugo Varr, signs away 'surplus' crossbows to a Palella smuggler, and the Quadrelli tallies show 600 bows gone where no wall needed them.
FX02-007.reputation: The best shooting instructors in the Sunlands; Varenna's Terrace School copies their windlass drill.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant-Major of the Crossbow Yard
members.note: He has found 600 bows missing from his tallies and has not decided whom to tell.

members.role: Daughter; armourer of the Yard
members.note: She makes the Yard's windlasses and stamps every one with her mark, which is how the missing bows could be traced.

members.role: Heir; file-sergeant on the Valerian Wall
members.note: Captain Varr pays him extra to sign the surplus forms, and he signs.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He can already span a light crossbow and shoots crows off the Yard wall.

famousDead: First drill-sergeant of the Crossbow Yard.
FX02-007.secret: The family's tallies prove that Captain Hugo Varr is selling the See's crossbows, and the heir has signed the papers.
hooks: A Blackreef raider is taken with a Dorata windlass bearing Serena's mark.
Bruno must choose between his son and his tally.
Lady Petra Brennus wants Dorata crossbowmen for her galleys.

FX02-008.name: the Clavieri family
FX02-008.title: Key-Sergeant of the Lantern Guard
FX02-008.arms: three gold keys on white, a black lantern above

military.office: Hereditary Key-Sergeants of the Lantern Guard
military.unit: the gate and door wards of the Lantern Guard, about 200 men
military.ties: Since the See was founded a Clavieri sergeant has kept the keys of the Lantern Gate, the Needle Court and the archive doors, and every Lantern Guard recruit swears his oath before one.

FX02-008.power: The key-ward of the Lantern Gate and the archive, a tied house on Needle Hill, and the trust of every High Luminary since Benedict.
FX02-008.history: After Marcus Vell opened the Lantern Gate in 759, Benedict the First wanted keys kept by a man who owed his bread to the Temple alone. He chose Pello Clavieri, a sergeant of the old wall guard who had refused Vell's order to stand aside and had been beaten for it. The Clavieri have kept the keys of the gate and the archive since, in a house on Needle Hill. They sign for every key that leaves the ward. In 1104 Captain Leandro Fosca took the archive key on his own authority and returned it the same night, and the key-sergeant wrote it in the book. In November the copyist Amadeo Rusk was seen leaving the archive with it.
FX02-008.reputation: Grim, upright and incorruptible; the only men in the Lantern Guard the Pilgrims' Quarter cannot bribe.

members.role: Head of the family; Key-Sergeant of the Lantern Guard
members.note: His key-book records Captain Fosca taking the archive key, and Fosca has twice asked to 'check' the book.

members.role: His wife
members.note: She bakes for the Needle-Keepers and hears their quarrels across the kitchen door.

members.role: Heir; ward-sergeant at the Lantern Gate
members.note: He knows the Brass Badge men pay the gate clerks and has named two of them to his captain, who did nothing.

members.role: Daughter; sun-sister novice at the Saltings hospital
members.note: She nursed a feverish salt smuggler who carried letters from the Mirona hills.

famousDead: Refused Marcus Vell on Ash Night; first key-sergeant.
FX02-008.secret: The key-book shows Captain Leandro Fosca took the archive key the night the physician's tablets were copied.
hooks: Fosca tries to steal or burn the key-book.
Keeper Quill asks the key-sergeant who else has borrowed keys.
Teodoro is offered a Brass Badge bribe he cannot refuse.

FX02-009.name: the Vialardi family
FX02-009.title: Post-Master of the Sun Road Riders
FX02-009.arms: a running white horse on a gold road, on green

military.office: Hereditary Post-Masters of the Sun Road Riders
military.unit: the Sun Road Riders of the Brunentia stages, about 400 light horse
military.ties: Vialardi riders keep the posts every fifteen kilometres on the Sun Road and the pilgrim roads, and every relay rider of the See learns the road from them.

FX02-009.power: Eleven post stations between Solenne and Brunentia, their remounts and grooms, and the fastest news in the See.
FX02-009.history: After the Wind riders raided the Ostran coast in 893, Aurelius I wanted word of any danger on the Sun Road in a day, and in 896 he gave the posts to Fabio Vialardi, a Lorina horse dealer. The family has kept them since. A Vialardi rider brought word of the Black Cough at Morhaven to Solenne in 916, two days before the ships. In August 1094 the family's riders were the relay for the pilgrim escort on the Mirona road, and the rider sent to wake Sir Garin Solis found him drunk at the inn and rode on without raising him. Thirty-one pilgrims died. The family has never said so, and the rider has been drinking himself to death since.
FX02-009.reputation: Fast, cheerful and well informed; any secret on the Sun Road reaches a Vialardi stable within the week.

members.role: Head of the family; Post-Master of the Sun Road Riders
members.note: He reads every sealed letter that he can open and close again, and has done so for thirty years.

members.role: Heir; the rider of August 1094
members.note: He did not wake the drunk knight, and he drinks now so that he will not dream of the Mirona road.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the Ambina post
members.note: She runs the busiest post on the road and wants her brother passed over.

members.role: Grandson; stable boy
members.note: He rode a dispatch alone at eleven when the rider was sick, and the family is proud and frightened.

famousDead: Lorina horse dealer; first post-master of the Sun Road.
FX02-009.secret: A Vialardi rider found Sir Garin Solis drunk on the night of the Mirona road massacre and did not wake him.
hooks: A sealed letter from the dying High Luminary's physician passes through a Vialardi post.
Enzo's confession would shame the Master of Noon Hall.
Flavia asks her father to name her heir.

FX02-010.name: the Mangano family
FX02-010.title: Master of the Wall Engines
FX02-010.arms: a black wheel and a throwing arm on red

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Wall Engines of the Valerian Wall
military.unit: the Wall Engine Crews, 600 men in the towers of the Valerian Wall and Lorina Castle
military.ties: The Manganos have kept the stone-throwers and great crossbows of the Valerian Wall since it was built, and every engine crew in the See learns from their drawings.

FX02-010.power: The engine-house in the Valerian Wall's tower, its drawings and timbers, 600 crewmen, and knowledge of the old tunnels under the wall.
FX02-010.history: The Manganos built the engines for Valerian II's wall between 628 and 636 and stayed to keep them. They served the emperors, then the See, and are older in Solenne than the Temple's rule. On Ash Night 759 the Mangano crews were in the towers of the Lantern Gate when Marcus Vell opened it below them, and the family has always said they were ordered not to shoot. The engines have not thrown a stone in anger since. In 1105 the master has read of a new counterweight engine built inside Tessar in 1065 and has begged the Treasurer for timber to build one.
FX02-010.reputation: Proud old engineers who talk to their machines; the city calls them the wall's grandfathers.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Wall Engines
members.note: He has drawn a counterweight engine from a traveller's description and needs 2,000 suns to build it.

members.role: Daughter; the family's draughtswoman
members.note: She keeps the old tunnel maps of the wall, which show a passage under the Needle Court nobody uses.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Lantern Gate towers
members.note: He wants war just once, to see what his engines can do.

members.role: Dowager
members.note: Her grandmother told her what the tower crews saw on Ash Night, and she tells it differently to every priest.

famousDead: Built the engines of the Valerian Wall.
FX02-010.secret: The family's tunnel maps show an old passage that runs under the Needle Court to the archive.
hooks: Someone asks to borrow the tunnel maps.
The Treasurer refuses the counterweight engine, and an Ostran banker offers to pay.
Orsino's crews fire on a smuggler's boat in the Saltings.

FX02-011.name: the Collardi of Mirona
FX02-011.title: Sergeant of the Mirona Hill Scouts
FX02-011.arms: a grey hound on brown; the scouts' mark

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Mirona Hill Scouts
military.unit: a hundred of the Mirona Hill Scouts, 800 in all
military.ties: Collardi shepherd-sons have tracked raiders, smugglers and Ashen heretics across the Mirona hills for the See since the scouts were raised.

FX02-011.power: Free shepherd land in the hills, the scouts' sergeant post, and knowledge of every goat path from Mirona to the coast.
FX02-011.history: The Collardi were free shepherds of the Mirona hills who guided the See's soldiers against bandits, and when the Mirona Hill Scouts were raised in 951, their head was made a sergeant. Since then a Collardi has led a hundred of the scouts. In 1094 the scouts were sent after the killers of the 31 pilgrims and found nothing, and the See hanged two shepherds instead, one of them a Collardi cousin. The family has hunted the Ashen for the See ever since, with less heart each year. In 1105 the sergeant's own wife goes to hear Isaria Vale.
FX02-011.reputation: The best trackers in the See, hard and silent; shepherds call them dogs of the Temple.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Mirona Hill Scouts
members.note: He knows where Isaria Vale sleeps every night and has not told the banneret.

members.role: His wife
members.note: She brings Isaria cheese and listens to her sermons on the poor.

members.role: Heir; scout
members.note: His hanged cousin was his closest friend, and he knows the name of the Lorina knight who slept.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She found a Solenne-made buckle in the hills before the Brennus shepherds found the pit.

famousDead: Collardi cousin hanged for the Mirona road murders he did not commit.
FX02-011.secret: The scout-sergeant knows where Isaria Vale sleeps and lets the See's hunts miss her.
hooks: Remo goes after Sir Garin Solis.
The banneret orders the Collardi to bring in the preacher.
Brina's buckle matches the Mirona pit dead.

FX02-012.name: the Campanari family
FX02-012.title: Keeper of the Noon Bell
FX02-012.arms: a gold bell on white, a black needle beside it
FX02-012.power: The founding and ringing of the Temple's bells, the bell foundry below Needle Hill, and the right to ring noon for the whole city.
FX02-012.history: Tavian I the Builder hired the bell-founder Ottone Campanari to cast the Temple's first bronze noon bell in 785, and the family has rung noon in Solenne since. Campanari men cast; Campanari women ring, and the Needle-Keepers' water clock tells them when. When Clement IV rebuilt the Temple, the family cast its great bell in 1082, the biggest in the west. The bell cracked inside in its first winter. The founder patched it with a bronze band hidden in the bell-frame, and only the family knows. If the bell fails on Return Day before 200,000 pilgrims, the city will read it as the Light's judgment on a dying High Luminary.
FX02-012.reputation: The city's timekeepers; deafened, devout and very proud of their bell.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Noon Bell
members.note: He is almost deaf and listens to the great bell with his hand on the frame.

members.role: His daughter; Mistress of the Ringers
members.note: She rings noon by the water clock and has noticed the bell's note going flat.

members.role: Heir; master founder
members.note: He wants to recast the great bell quietly before Return Day and needs 4,000 suns of bronze.

members.role: Granddaughter; apprentice ringer
members.note: She climbs the bell-frame and has seen the hidden band.

famousDead: Cast the first noon bell of the Temple in 785.
FX02-012.secret: The great bell of 1082 cracked inside in its first winter and is held together by a hidden bronze band.
hooks: The bell's note goes flat before Return Day.
Matteo needs 4,000 suns of bronze in secret.
Lucia tells a Needle-Keeper what she saw.

FX02-013.name: the Lucenti family
FX02-013.title: Luminary of Lorina
FX02-013.arms: a gold lamp on blue, twelve gold rays around it
FX02-013.power: Wheat farms around Ferona held of the Temple, a Luminary's seat held in most generations, and one vote in the Needle Court that may decide the chair.
FX02-013.history: The Lucenti were farmers of the Mireria plain who gave a clever son to the Temple under Odo I the Chronicler. He became a Luminary, and since priests do not marry, he raised his nephew for the Temple in turn.
