The family has kept that chain for three centuries: uncles in the Temple and brothers at home raising the next nephew. It has given the See nine Luminaries and never a High Luminary. In 1105 Luminary Benedetto Lucenti holds the seat of Lorina and is the only man in the Needle Court whom both the Treasurer's party and the Keepers can stand. He says he does not want the chair, which everyone takes as proof that he does.
FX02-013.reputation: A country family of quiet priests; everyone underestimates them, which has worked for three hundred years.

members.role: Luminary of Lorina; the family's priest
members.note: He has refused to count votes, and both parties are counting him.

members.role: His brother; head of the lay household
members.note: He farms Temple wheat at Ferona and thinks his brother would be miserable in the chair.

members.role: Nephew; deacon at Lorina
members.note: He has secretly promised his uncle's vote to Treasurer Dorn without asking him.

members.role: Niece; sun-sister
members.note: She served beside Isaria Vale before the Mother was refused, and still writes to her.

famousDead: First Luminary of the family; secretary to Odo I the Chronicler.
FX02-013.secret: The nephew has sold his uncle's vote to the Treasurer without his uncle's knowledge.
hooks: If the chair deadlocks, Benedetto is the compromise.
Serena carries letters for Isaria Vale.
Lady Aurelia Corvane offers her four votes to make Benedetto High Luminary, for a price.

FX02-014.name: the Acquesi of Acquesca
FX02-014.title: Sacristan of the Sun Temple of Acquesca
FX02-014.arms: a gold sun over blue water, on white
FX02-014.power: The sacristy of the Sun Temple of Acquesca and its spring, the pilgrims' offerings, and a relic that draws 20,000 pilgrims a year.
FX02-014.history: The Sun Temple of Acquesca stands over a spring where pilgrims on the way to Solenne have washed since Solen times. In 761 the See gave its sacristy to the lay family that had swept it for a century, and the Acquesi have kept the lamp, the spring and the relic since. The relic is a strip of the ash-grey cloth said to have covered the Crowning Stone at Corvan's crowning. In the Black Cough of 916 the spring was blamed for the sickness, and the family was nearly driven out. In 1105 the sacristan has a son who copied the relic's provenance from the archive in his novice years and found that the cloth was bought from a Lorina weaver in 812.
FX02-014.reputation: Gentle shrine-keepers whose spring water heals, or so the pilgrims say.

members.role: Head of the family; Sacristan of Acquesca
members.note: He knows the cloth is not holy and believes the pilgrims are healed anyway.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the spring
members.note: She bathes the sick pilgrims herself and has cured more fevers than the Temple physicians.

members.role: Son; scrivener of the Needle Court
members.note: He found the 812 receipt for the relic and has not burned it.

members.role: Daughter; heiress of the sacristy
members.note: She sells spring water in sealed flasks at five pence each and wants to sell it in Ostra.

famousDead: Kept the spring open through the Black Cough.
FX02-014.secret: The relic of Acquesca was bought from a Lorina weaver in 812, and a son of the house has found the receipt.
hooks: Brother Enzo's receipt falls into the Open Light's hands.
Tessa's water trade draws a rival shrine's anger.
A pilgrim is not healed, and his lord wants his money back.

FX02-015.name: the Massari family
FX02-015.title: Steward of the Temple farms of the Fields of Corvan
FX02-015.arms: a gold wheat ear on green, a white key across it
FX02-015.power: The stewardship of about 400 Temple tenant farms on the Fields of Corvan, the rent rolls, and the right to call the tenant spears for their forty days.
FX02-015.history: When Odo II the Rebuilder cut tenant rents by a quarter in 924 to bring farmers back after the Black Cough, he needed stewards who would settle new families on emptied farms. Ruggero Massari, a tenant who had kept his own farm through the plague, was given the stewardship of the Fields of Corvan. His heirs have run them since. The Massari are tenants themselves in law and masters in practice: they set the rents, call the forty days and judge the boundary disputes. When the Treasurer raised rents to fund Queen Livia's loans, the Massari collected them and kept the tenants quiet. Now some of the tenants are listening to Isaria Vale, and the steward's rolls show more empty farms each year.
FX02-015.reputation: Fair-minded for stewards, the tenants say, which is not saying much.

members.role: Head of the family; Steward of the Fields of Corvan
members.note: He has written to the Treasurer three times that the rents will empty the fields, and been answered once.

members.role: His wife; midwife of the estates
members.note: She has delivered half the tenants' children and knows which ones go to the preacher.

members.role: Heir; captain of the tenant spears
members.note: He drills the tenant spears and fears the day he is told to march them against their own neighbours.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She has copied out Isaria Vale's sermon on the tenant's tithe and passes it from hand to hand.

famousDead: Resettled the plague-emptied Fields of Corvan for Odo II.
FX02-015.secret: The steward has quietly let 60 tenant families pay half rent since 1102 and covered the shortfall from his own savings.
hooks: The Treasurer's auditors arrive at Ferona.
Elisa's copied sermons are found in a tenant's house.
Garin is ordered to march the tenant spears into the Mirona hills.

FX02-016.name: the Scrinari family
FX02-016.title: Keeper of the Imperial Letter-Chests
FX02-016.arms: a black chest bound in gold, on white
FX02-016.power: The lay keepership of the imperial letter-chests in the See's archive, the chest index, and a narrow house on the Scriveners' Steps.
FX02-016.history: When Benedict took the imperial palace in 760, the emperor's clerks were dead or fled, and the Temple needed someone who could read the chancery's chest marks. Tito Scrinari, a junior palace clerk who had hidden in the archive through the sack, was kept on. His family has kept the index of the imperial letter-chests since. The Needle-Keepers hold the archive keys; the Scrinari know which chest holds what. They know where Justinian IV's hidden order of November 602 lies, the order that would clear Admiral Gaius Merel. Sir Tobias Merel has offered the keeper a share of the lost Merel estates to fetch it.
FX02-016.reputation: Dusty, forgettable clerks; the most dangerous memory in Solenne after the Keepers' own.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Imperial Letter-Chests
members.note: He can find any letter of the emperors in a quarter of an hour and has never read one he was not told to.

members.role: Daughter; binder of the archive's books
members.note: She rebinds the Dim Chronicle's quires and has read every page twice.

members.role: Heir; clerk of the index
members.note: He has taken Sir Tobias Merel's offer and chosen a night.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He plays among the chests and has found a loose stone behind chest ninety-one.

famousDead: Palace clerk who hid in the archive through the sack and became its first lay keeper.
FX02-016.secret: The heir has agreed to fetch Justinian IV's November Order for Sir Tobias Merel in return for a share of the lost Merel lands.
hooks: Fausto's night in the archive goes wrong.
Nerio's loose stone hides something older than the chests.
Keeper Quill asks the family to lose a chest.

FX02-017.name: the Codani family
FX02-017.title: Advocate of the Lay Court of Clarente
FX02-017.arms: an open silver book on purple, a black sword across it
FX02-017.power: Four generations of practice in the Solen Code, a school of twenty clerks at Venella, and the cases of every lay folk who fall out with the Temple courts.
FX02-017.history: The Codani have pleaded under the Solen Code in the See's lay courts since 873, the year the first Needle Heresy trial taught them that some cases must never reach a Temple court. They specialise in the quarrels between lay and Temple justice: whether a priest's debt is a lay matter, whether a tenant's theft is the Temple's to judge. They won the Merels a stay of their granary lease in 1099 and lost a dozen cases against the Treasury since. In 1105 the Codani are preparing the lay defence of the Vell lease against the Treasurer's review, and a Codani notary has been asked to witness a sealed document in a lead tube.
FX02-017.reputation: Clever, argumentative and always on the lay side; the Temple's courts call them the Code's wolves.

members.role: Head of the family; Advocate of the Lay Court
members.note: He has never lost a case about a lease and is preparing the Vells' as his last.

members.role: Daughter; notary
members.note: Matthias Vell has asked her to witness a letter she may not read.

members.role: Heir; advocate
members.note: He wants a place in the Treasurer's service and argues the Temple's side at dinner to tease his father.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She can recite the Twelve Books' Temple Clause and argues it with priests in the street.

famousDead: Founded the practice after the first Needle Heresy trial.
hooks: Livia witnesses the Vell letter and learns what it says.
Remo is offered a Treasury post to throw the Vell case.
A tenant asks the Codani to defend him against a heresy charge.

FX02-018.name: the Pansali family
FX02-018.title: Master of the Clarente Pans
FX02-018.arms: three white salt cones on blue
FX02-018.power: The Temple's salt-tax farm on the Clarente pans, about 900 salt-workers, and warehouses at Venella harbour.
FX02-018.history: In 952 Tavian III farmed out the salt tax of the Clarente pans to the highest bidder, and the salt merchant Bruno Pansali won it. His family has bid and won every renewal since. They pay the Treasury a fixed sum and keep what they collect above it, and they sell salt fish to Lorina and the pilgrims' cook-shops. The salt-workers of the pans are poor, and some of their salt goes out by night to the Saltings without the tax. The Pansali make a show of hunting the smugglers. In truth they sell them untaxed salt at a fifth off and take a share of the profit.
FX02-018.reputation: Rich, respectable salt merchants; the salt-workers say the Pansali's tax is the only thing heavier than their sacks.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Clarente Pans
members.note: He dines with the Treasurer's clerks every quarter day and sells salt to the smugglers every new moon.

members.role: Heiress; keeper of the warehouses
members.note: She keeps two sets of weights and knows exactly which to use for whom.

members.role: Son; salt-tax collector
members.note: He truly hunts smugglers and does not know his father sells to them.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She pays for the salt-workers' children to learn letters at the Temple school.

famousDead: Won the first salt-tax farm of the Clarente pans in 952.
FX02-018.secret: The salt-farmers sell untaxed salt to the Saltings smugglers they are paid to hunt.
hooks: Leandro catches a smuggler boat carrying Pansali sacks.
The salt farm comes up for renewal in 1106.
Clarente Tower's keeper suspects the Pansali weights.

FX02-019.name: the Frumenti family
FX02-019.title: Grain Factor to the Treasury
FX02-019.arms: a gold sheaf on red between two black ships
FX02-019.power: The Treasury's contract to buy Tamari wheat through Lucerna, granaries at Lorina and Solenne harbour, and credit with House Lunetti.
FX02-019.history: When Odo II bought Tamari wheat through Lucerna by the shipload after the Black Cough, he used a Lorina grain dealer, Aldo Frumenti, to haggle with the Lucernan weighers. The Frumenti have bought the See's bread ever since. They know that the See lives on Lucerna's grain ships and that the Bassans know it too. In 1105 Lady Giulia Bassan is holding back the spring grain ships to force a higher price, and the Treasurer needs cheap bread before the Luminaries vote. The Frumenti are caught between: their granaries are a third full, and they have quietly bought Varennan wheat from Calena at the old price to cover the gap.
FX02-019.reputation: Hard bargainers who keep the See fed; when bread rises, the Saltings curse the Frumenti first.

members.role: Head of the family; Grain Factor to the Treasury
members.note: He has counted the Lorina granaries every morning since Giulia Bassan stopped the ships.

members.role: Heiress; factor at Lucerna
members.note: She sits in the Staple's weigh-house and has caught the weights running heavy.

members.role: Son; ship's purser
members.note: He is bringing Calena wheat down the coast in a hired cog without the Lucernan Staple's seal.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She remembers the bread riot of 1062 and keeps a store of her own under the house.

famousDead: Bought the See's Tamari wheat for Odo II after the Black Cough.
FX02-019.secret: Nella Frumenti has proof that the Lucerna Staple's weights run heavy by one in a hundred.
hooks: Cosimo's unsealed wheat cog is stopped by Lucernan galleys.
Nella's proof could break the Bassan grain squeeze.
A bread riot in Solenne before the vote.

FX02-020.name: the Dorelli family
FX02-020.title: Master Gilder of the Temple
FX02-020.arms: a gold hammer on a black anvil, on white
FX02-020.words: Thin as Breath, True as Noon
FX02-020.power: The Temple's gold-leaf and window-glass contracts, a workshop of forty beaters and glaziers below Needle Hill, and a name rebuilt from disgrace.
FX02-020.history: In 931 the Warden Aurea Corvane saw that the gold on the Needle's cap had been replaced with brass under a skin of gold, and the Temple goldsmith who had sold the gold was hanged. His widow took back her own name, Dorelli, and kept his workshop and his apprentices. In 932 she asked to gild the new cap herself for nothing, and the Temple let her. Her family has gilded the Temple's panels since and made the coloured glass for Clement IV's windows. Every year a Corvane woman inspects their gold and glass with her Sunborn eyes, and every year the family hates it. The Dorellis know they are the goldsmith's blood; the Corvanes have never let them forget it.
FX02-020.reputation: The finest gilders in the west, honest to the point of mania; nobody mentions 931 to their faces.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Gilder of the Temple
members.note: She was named for the woman who hanged her ancestor, as a family penance, and has never forgiven her mother for it.

members.role: Heir; master glazier
members.note: He made the blue of the New Temple's great window and wants to make a glass a Corvane cannot judge.

members.role: Daughter; the black sheep
members.note: She has been selling gilders' gossip about Lady Aurelia's pawned jewels to the Treasurer's men.

members.role: Aurea's husband; beater
members.note: He beats gold leaf so thin that he can read a letter through it.

famousDead: The hanged goldsmith's widow, who regilded the Needle's cap for nothing in 932.
FX02-020.secret: A Dorelli daughter has learned that Lady Aurelia's jewels lie pawned with House Lunetti and is selling the news to the Treasurer.
hooks: The yearly Corvane inspection falls in the week of the vote.
Matteo's new glass fools a Sunborn eye.
Clara's informing is discovered by the Lantieri.

FX02-021.name: the Sardi of Lorina
FX02-021.title: Net-master of the Lorina Steps
FX02-021.arms: a silver fish on a net, a sign painted on their boats
FX02-021.words: The Sea Gives, the Sea Takes
FX02-021.power: Three fishing boats, a smoke-house on the Lorina steps, and blood kinship with the dying High Luminary.
FX02-021.history: The Sardi have fished out of Lorina for as long as anyone remembers. A Sardi boy born in about 1031 went to the Temple school, then to the priesthood, took a new name at his ordination and rose to be Luminary of Morhaven. In August 1088 he was elected High Luminary as Severin III. His family stayed fishermen. He sent them money for a new boat and his blessing, and nothing else. Now that he is dying, every party in the Needle Court has remembered that the High Luminary has a sister and nephews on the Lorina steps, and the family's smoke-house is full of polite visitors.
FX02-021.reputation: Plain fisherfolk whose brother sits on the Needle's chair; Lorina is proud of them and a little afraid for them.

members.role: Head of the family; the High Luminary's sister
members.note: She has not seen her brother in seventeen years and wants only to sit by his bed.

members.role: Her son; net-master
members.note: A Corvane lady and a Treasury clerk have both offered him a house in Solenne this month.

members.role: Her daughter; smoke-house keeper
members.note: She thinks every visitor wants something and charges them for the fish.

members.role: Grandson; novice at the Lorina Temple school
members.note: Born the year his great-uncle was elected, he has been promised a Luminary's patronage by three men already.

FX02-021.secret: Severin III wrote to his sister in 1103 that he regrets the hanging of the Mirona shepherds, and she still has the letter.
hooks: Each party wants Marta at the deathbed to carry Severin's last words.
Pello is offered a fast road in the Temple for his family's loyalty.
The letter about the Mirona shepherds surfaces.

FX02-022.name: the Paludani, the Saltings runners
FX02-022.title: Mother of the Saltings
FX02-022.arms: a white crab scratched on a black oar; their mark
FX02-022.power: Twenty flat boats, a dozen salt-pan workers in their pay, safe houses in the Saltings ward of Solenne, and a share in the Brass Badge men's takings.
FX02-022.history: When the Clarente salt tax was farmed out in 952, the poorest pan families of the marsh shore began to run salt by night to the Saltings ward of Solenne, where the poor cannot pay the tax. The Paludani were the boldest of them, and by 1000 they ran the trade. They know every channel in the marshes between Clarente and the city. Their women run safe houses in the Saltings, where the sun-sisters' hospital asks no questions. Since the 1090s they have worked with Nico of the Saltings and his Brass Badge men, carrying forged pilgrim receipts out of the city as well as salt in. In 1105 they also carry letters for the preacher of the Mirona hills.
FX02-022.reputation: Marsh rats to the watch, saints to the Saltings poor; nobody in the ward has paid the full price for salt in fifty years.

members.role: Head of the family; Mother of the Saltings
members.note: She feeds every widow in the Saltings and has had two informers drowned in the marsh.

members.role: Her son; boat captain
members.note: He knows the channels by smell and has outrun the Bay Marines' boats eleven times.

members.role: Her daughter; safe-house keeper in the Saltings
members.note: She hides the feverish courier from the Mirona hills under the sun-sisters' noses.

members.role: Grandson; runner
members.note: He carried Isaria Vale's cipher packets to a Lantern Gate inn without knowing what they were.

famousDead: Made the Paludani masters of the marsh trade.
FX02-022.secret: The clan carries the Open Light's cipher letters between the Mirona hills and Solenne, which the Keepers would call heresy.
hooks: A packet carried by Remo is opened by the Lantern Guard.
The Pansali master is about to sell them out to save himself.
The Brass Badge men want the Paludani to carry forged relics to Ostra.

FX03-001.name: House Norvalle
FX03-001.title: Viscount of Casteria
FX03-001.arms: a black ram's head over a silver wheat sheaf, on russet
FX03-001.words: Slow to Rise, Hard to Move

military.office: Lords of the Casteria levy
military.unit: the Norvalle Banner, 40 lances, with 1,200 Casteria Hundredmen in war
military.ties: A Norvalle has led the left of every royal host since Aurora, and the Lord Marshal wants their 1,200 men for the Stagley stroke.

FX03-001.power: About sixty villages of sheep and wheat in the Casteria hills, some 18,000 suns a year, and the largest lay vote in the Great Council below the great houses.
FX03-001.history: The Norvalles farmed the Orsano emperors' taxes in the Casteria hills and opened their granaries to Galen the Bold before the battle at Aurora in 743. After the Treaty of the Needle Galen made Aldo Norvalle lord of the hills. Lord Ugo Norvalle died on the olive terraces of the Coast Road in 896 with 300 of his hundredmen. When the Black Cough emptied the hills after 916 the house turned its wheat to sheep and sold fleeces to the Palella weavers, which made it rich and, since the spinning wheel, dependent on House Calvane's prices. In 1049 Lotario Norvalle kept the hills quiet while Cesare Montaro marched on Venina, and Queen Lucilla made him viscount. In 1105 the queen and the Lord Marshal both court the viscount for the regency council, and he has promised neither.
FX03-001.reputation: Solid, slow and rich in sheep; the hill lords look to Casteria before they choose a side.

members.role: Head of the house; Viscount of Casteria
members.note: He got letters from the queen and the Lord Marshal in the same week and answered both with a wheel of cheese.

members.role: Viscountess; born a Melitane of Castella
members.note: She wants her son on the regency council and calls her husband's patience cowardice at table.

members.role: Heir; knight of the Crown Knights of the Forty Days
members.note: He has sworn himself to the War Party in the Laughing Captain and not told his father.

members.role: Second son; wool buyer at Crowbrook; the black sheep
members.note: He buys Ashmere fleeces across the border, and a runaway spinner from Camia slept two nights in his lodgings in December.

members.role: Daughter; novice of the sun-sisters at Varenna
members.note: She nursed in the Lion Hall infirmary in November and saw who was carried in.

famousDead: Opened the Casteria granaries to Galen the Bold in 743 and was made lord of the hills.
Held the hills for Queen Lucilla in 1049 and was made viscount.
FX03-001.secret: Fausto Norvalle sheltered Sabina of Camia at Crowbrook and took 50 suns from an Ashmere agent for the introduction.
hooks: The queen and the Lord Marshal both want the viscount's 1,200 men before the king dies.
Fausto will sell the spinner's hiding place to whoever pays first.
House Calvane cuts the fleece price by a fifth in spring 1105.

FX03-002.name: House Ruvessa
FX03-002.title: Baron of Norona
FX03-002.arms: a red boar on gold, a blue wave below

military.office: Captains of the Norona shore levy
military.unit: the Ruvessa lances, 12 knights, 300 crossbowmen and two war galleys of the Lion Fleet
military.ties: Ruvessa sons have captained Lion Fleet galleys since the Corsair War, and the house is the loudest voice for the Strait League in the Great Council.

FX03-002.power: The barony of Norona, its tuna traps and olive terraces, about 7,000 suns a year, and two galleys built at the house's own cost.
FX03-002.history: Pello Ruvessa was a knight of the Norona coast who sailed with Roderic the Lionheart to Felano in 894 and was made baron for it. The house grew on tuna and oil and paid for its own galleys. In June 1052 two Ruvessa galleys chased the pirates into the shoals of the Strait of Hael and were wrecked, and the baron's two eldest sons drowned. The next year Lord Arrigo Ruvessa lost a third galley to the fire rafts at Gull Isle under Cesare Montaro. The house has paid the dragon toll on every cask of oil since 1056 and hates Blackreef as a family duty. It also hates the Pavicini of Rocca Pavice, whose men stripped a Ruvessa wreck in 1079 and kept the cargo by wreck right.
FX03-002.reputation: Loud, brave, salt-stained and short of money; nobody wants to sit beside a Ruvessa when the dragon toll comes up.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Norona
members.note: He keeps the burned stern-post from Gull Isle in his hall and makes guests touch it.

members.role: Heir; captain of the galley Norona's Boar
members.note: Admiral Castellan's most trusted galley captain, he has sworn to sink a Blackreef ship before his father dies.

members.role: Daughter; crossbow sergeant of the Lion Marines
members.note: She ran away from a marriage contract at seventeen and enlisted under Captain Marta Rema under her mother's name.

members.role: Baroness; runs the tuna traps and the books
members.note: She knows the house has two years of money left and has quietly asked the Lucerna insurers for a loan.

famousDead: Sailed with the Lionheart to Felano in 894; first baron.
Drowned with their galleys in the shoals of the Strait.
FX03-002.secret: The baroness is negotiating a loan with a Lucernan sea-insurance house that takes its share of the dragon toll she hates.
hooks: Leandro wants a share in the 20 galleys Castellan asks of Lucerna.
A Pavicini cousin proposes to marry Mirella and end the wreck feud.
The house cannot pay for its galleys past 1106.

FX03-003.name: House Pavicini
FX03-003.title: Lord of Rocca Pavice
FX03-003.arms: a green oak growing from a grey rock, on white

military.office: Keepers of the Pavice beacons
military.unit: 8 lances and 60 coast-watchmen at the castle and three headland beacons
military.ties: Their three beacons are part of the Coast Watch, and Pavice oak has keeled half the galleys of the Lion Fleet.

FX03-003.power: The castle of Rocca Pavice on its sea rock, the oak forest behind it that feeds the royal shipyards, and the right of wreck on twelve kilometres of coast.
FX03-003.history: When Lothar I founded the royal shipyards in 783 he needed oak that Sylvaran would never sell, and the forest behind the sea rock of Pavice had it. He gave the forest and the rock to Dario Pavicini, his master forester, on condition that the house send 200 trunks to the yards each year. The Pavicini have sent them ever since, and they built the castle out of the profits. In the Corsair War they doubled the felling, and in 1052 Queen Lucilla's envoy came back from Sylvaran with nothing but otter tales, which made Pavice oak worth its weight in silver. The house also holds the old right of wreck, and in 1079 its men stripped a stranded Ruvessa cog, which began a feud. In 1105 Admiral Castellan wants 400 trunks for 40 new galleys, and the forest has perhaps 300 good ones left.
FX03-003.reputation: Rich in timber and tight with it; seamen say a Pavicini would strip his own brother's wreck.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Rocca Pavice
members.note: He has counted every good oak in the forest himself and will not tell the Admiral the number.

members.role: Dowager; his mother
members.note: In the lean years after the Corsair War she sold oak through Tibata fishermen to buyers who did not ask where it went.

members.role: Heir; forester and beacon captain
members.note: He found Blackreef felling marks on stumps his grandmother sold and has not decided what to do.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She is meant to marry a Ruvessa to end the feud and has met none of them.

famousDead: Lothar I's master forester; given the forest and the rock in 783.
FX03-003.secret: The dowager sold Pavice oak in the 1060s through Tibata middlemen to Sabran shipwrights who build for Blackreef.
hooks: The Admiral demands 400 trunks the forest does not have.
Renzo could expose his grandmother's oak sales to the Coast Watch.
A Ruvessa match is proposed to end the wreck feud.

FX03-004.name: House Melitane
FX03-004.title: Baron of the Melith Shore
FX03-004.arms: a silver pike swimming, on lake green

military.office: Captains of the Lakes banner
military.unit: the Melitane banner, 20 lances, and a company of the Castella Long Spears by custom
military.ties: Since Donella Melitane of the Norossa branch married Cesare Montaro in 1049, Melitane sons have ridden as aides to the Montaro generals.

FX03-004.power: Wheat land and fisheries on the shore of Lake Melith between Castella and Norossa, about 9,000 suns a year, and blood kinship with the Lord Marshal.
FX03-004.history: The Melitanes were lake lords of the Northern Lakes when the Treaty of the Needle gave the country to Galen the Bold. Roderic the Lionheart knighted their head at his crowning in 861 and made him baron of the Melith shore. The house served the Long Valdanes of Castella as neighbours and huntsmen for two centuries, but married none of their daughters under the Rule of the Long Blood. In 1049 Donella of the Norossa branch married Cesare Montaro the year he crushed the Serafins, and her children are the Lord Marshal Dario and General Ottavia. The Melitanes became the Montaros' kin in the north and the War Party's best recruiters there. In 1105 the baron has borrowed against two harvests to fit out his lances for the Stagley stroke.
FX03-004.reputation: The Lord Marshal's uncles; proud of it, and sometimes too sure the Montaros will pay their debts.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of the Melith Shore; cousin of the Lord Marshal
members.note: He has spent the dowries of both his daughters on horses for the Stagley stroke.

members.role: Heiress; widow of a Crown knight
members.note: She runs the lands while her father plays at war and keeps the real accounts in her own hand.

members.role: Son; aide to General Vittor Montaro at Ardata
members.note: He sends home the Crown Road army's camp gossip in letters his sister reads first.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She has noticed that General Ottavia's letters to the family stopped mentioning her brother in 1104.

famousDead: Wife of Cesare Montaro; mother of the Lord Marshal and General Ottavia.
FX03-004.secret: Orsino has borrowed 9,000 suns against the Lakes harvests, and if the Stagley stroke is called off the house cannot pay.
hooks: If the king dies, Orsino will bring his lances to Varenna for his cousin.
Serena suspects Ottavia is working against her brother.
The lenders want the Melith fisheries as security.

FX03-005.name: House Sanvaro
FX03-005.title: Banneret of the Aurora Ditch
FX03-005.arms: a gold chevron over three black stakes, on green

military.office: Bannerets of the Crown Knights of the Forty Days
military.unit: the Sanvaro banner, 20 lances owing forty days a year
military.ties: They hold their land for forty days in the saddle and have answered every muster since Galen the Bold, but their overlords are the Serafins, who oppose the war.

FX03-005.power: Five villages on the old battlefield of Aurora, about 1,500 suns a year, and twenty lances that owe service to both the crown and the Serafins.
FX03-005.history: Matteo Sanvaro was the sergeant who laid out the ditch and stakes at Aurora on 17 June 743, where Galen's crossbowmen broke the imperial knights. Galen gave him the fields he had dug. The house has held them as bannerets ever since and buries its dead on the line of the old ditch. In 968 it passed with the Aurora lands under the lords of Venina, and a Sanvaro rode with Guido Serafin in 1049 and was among the 60 hanged. Lady Clara Serafin's late husband Matteo Serafin of Aurora was godfather to the present banneret's heir. In 1105 the crown has called the Sanvaro lances to Dorium for the Stagley stroke, while their liege leads the party that wants no war.
FX03-005.reputation: Poor, stubborn and brave; every Varennan schoolboy knows the name from the ditch song, and nobody knows they are still alive.

members.role: Head of the house; Banneret of the Aurora Ditch
members.note: His father was hanged by Cesare Montaro, and the crown now orders him to serve under the hangman's son.

members.role: Heir; godson of the late Matteo Serafin
members.note: He carries Lady Clara's money to the tithe strikers and would rather go to prison than to Dorium.

members.role: Daughter; wife of a Montaro captain
members.note: She married into the Laughing Company against her father's wish and has not been home since.

members.role: Younger son; squire
members.note: He wants to ride to Stagley whatever his brother says.

famousDead: Dug the ditch and planted the stakes at Aurora in 743.
Rode with Guido Serafin and was hanged with the sixty.
FX03-005.secret: The heir carries Lady Clara Serafin's coin to the tithe strike leader, which would cost the house its land if the Temple's courts learned of it.
hooks: The banneret must choose between the royal muster and his liege's wishes.
Cassia's husband is sent to fetch the Sanvaro lances by force.
A ploughman turns up a Solen standard in the old ditch.

FX03-006.name: House Ombrane
FX03-006.title: Baron of Vicula
FX03-006.arms: a black mason's hammer on white, a green border
FX03-006.power: The barony of Vicula in the Venina hills and a third share of the Vicula marble quarry, about 6,000 suns a year, and a loud voice among the Tithe Resisters.
FX03-006.history: The Ombranes were quarry foremen under the Serafins who cut marble for the Valerian Wall. When the Treaty of the Needle gave the Venina hills to Varenna, the Serafins rewarded them with the barony of Vicula and a share of the quarry. They have followed Venina ever since. In 1049 the Ombranes rode with Guido Serafin's rising and, alone among the hill barons, lost no man to Cesare Montaro's rope. The hill folk called it luck. Today Baron Aldo Ombrane is the loudest Tithe Resister in the Great Council after Lady Clara herself, and his tenants are among Agnese's forty villages.
FX03-006.reputation: Hard-handed stone barons, fierce against the Temple; their luck in 1049 is talked of quietly in Venina taverns.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Vicula
members.note: He shouts loudest against the tithe because he knows what his father did in 1049.

members.role: Baroness; keeper of the quarry accounts
members.note: She found her father-in-law's letter to Cesare Montaro in the quarry office and burned it, but not before her son read it.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He knows his grandfather sold the 1049 rising to Montaro and cannot look Agnese of Venina in the face.

members.role: Daughter; married to a Serafin cousin
members.note: She is Lady Clara's closest companion and knows nothing.

famousDead: Rode in the rising of 1049 and came home with all his men.
FX03-006.secret: In May 1049 Baron Guido Ombrane told Cesare Montaro where the Serafin men would gather, and that is why no Ombrane hanged.
hooks: Agnese of Venina's grandfather was one of the sixty; if the truth comes out, the strike turns on Vicula.
The heir may confess to Lady Clara.
A Montaro captain hints that he has kept a copy of the old letter.

FX03-007.name: House Gravessa
FX03-007.title: Baron of the Upper Montessa
FX03-007.arms: a black bear standing on white snow, a red sky above

military.office: Keepers of the second tower of Albora Watch
military.unit: 80 house men and the tower's 40 pass spears
military.ties: Gravessa men hold the middle tower of Albora Watch for the Wardens of the Crown Road, and their sons serve as file-leaders in the Crown Road Pass Spears.

FX03-007.power: The high valleys below the Montessa Pass, summer pastures, a silver-lead mine that barely pays, and the middle tower of Albora Watch.
FX03-007.history: Bruno Gravessa was a captain of the pass forts beside Bertran Ardane the Elder, and when Ardane was made Warden of the Crown Road in 826, he was given the upper Montessa valleys as his vassal the next year. The Gravessas have held the middle tower of Albora Watch ever since and close it every November when the snow comes. They fought Crown foothill bandits for two centuries and orc raiders in the bad winters. When Lord Bertran rebuilt the towers in 1090 the Gravessas paid a third of the cost and got nothing back. Since 1099 the baron's toll-clerks have watched the Iron Road Company's wagons roll past untaxed and kept a careful tally. The bandit Remo Casti robs Ardane's toll wagons on Gravessa roads, and the Ardanes blame the Gravessas for it.
FX03-007.reputation: Hard mountain men, loyal to the Wardens in public and sour about them in private.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of the Upper Montessa
members.note: He keeps a second ledger of every Aldmark wagon that has passed untaxed since 1099.

members.role: Heir; captain of the middle tower
members.note: He has twice had the bandits in sight and twice been ordered by an Ardane officer to let them go.

members.role: Baroness; keeper of the mine
members.note: She wants her husband to sell his ledger to Lady Oria Vantes for a royal charter on the mine.

members.role: Younger son; page at Ardata
members.note: He serves at Lord Bertran's table and hears the Aldmark visitors talk.

famousDead: Pass-fort captain; first baron of the upper Montessa.
FX03-007.secret: The baron's second ledger proves that the Warden of the Crown Road lets Aldmark wagons pass untaxed for a private cut.
hooks: Lady Oria Vantes would pay well for the Gravessa ledger.
Remo is ordered to let the bandits pass a third time.
The snow closes the pass early with an Aldmark caravan caught at the tower.

FX03-008.name: House Tarvelli
FX03-008.title: Baron of Taria
FX03-008.arms: a gold sun over a red vine, on white
FX03-008.power: Vineyards and olive presses around Taria, about 11,000 suns a year, Temple leases held cheap, and a Tarvelli uncle among the Luminaries in most generations.
FX03-008.history: When Galen II tried to tax the Temple's estates in 803 and backed down in the Tithe Truce, the knight Ottone Tarvelli was the one baron who had spoken for the Temple in council. In 805 the Luminary of Varenna leased him Temple vineyards at Taria at a low rent, and the crown, wanting peace with the Temple, made him baron. The house has served the Temple since and given it a Luminary in most generations, uncle to nephew, since priests do not marry. Its wine goes to the Temple's tables in Varenna and Solenne. In 1105 the baron's brother is Luminary Brandi's deputy for the Temple's rents in the western hills, and the house is the Tithe Resisters' favourite target.
FX03-008.reputation: The Temple's barons: well fed, well connected and hated by every lord who pays the tithe.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Taria
members.note: He pays a fixed rent of 760 silver for vineyards worth ten times that, and smiles when anyone says so.

members.role: Luminary's deputy for the western rents; the baron's elder brother
members.note: He hopes to be Luminary of Varenna when Ottone Brandi rises, and Brandi hopes to rise to Solenne's chair.

members.role: Heiress
members.note: She reads her uncle's letters and has found the old Temple deeds of Taria dated 746.

members.role: Younger son; promised to the Temple
members.note: He is meant to take orders at twenty-five and spends his allowance at dice in Varenna.

famousDead: Spoke for the Temple before Galen II and was made baron.
FX03-008.secret: The Temple's Taria deeds are dated 746 and paid in coin meant for the imperial army, the very proof the Tithe Resisters seek.
hooks: Fiora could hand the 746 deeds to Lady Clara Serafin.
Enzo's gambling debts are bought by a Tithe Resister.
Ilario's rise depends on who takes the High Luminary's chair.

FX03-009.name: House Caliani
FX03-009.title: Baron of Calena

military.office: Captains of the Calena hundreds
military.unit: the Caliani lances, 15 knights, and the Calena hundreds in war
military.ties: A Caliani commanded the camp that was caught asleep on the Brightwash in 1014, and every Caliani since has wanted the chance to wash it out.

FX03-009.power: Wheat land around Calena and three granaries on the road to the Palella, about 8,000 suns a year.
FX03-009.history: The Calianis were granary-keepers of Calena who survived the Dry Year of 367, when the Lucerna Staple sold the west's grain to Solenne. They swore to Galen the Bold's son Lothar I and were made barons in 776. On the Brightwash in May 1014 Baron Fausto Caliani commanded the watch of the Varennan camp, and Queen Elsbeth's men came out of the dark onto 8,000 sleeping soldiers. He died in the rout, and the house took its owl and its words to shame the memory. The Calianis have kept their granaries full ever since and still sell to the crown below the Lucernan price. In 1105 the baron has begged the Lord Marshal for a place in the van of the Stagley stroke.
FX03-009.reputation: Watchful to the point of madness; their sentries are the best in the realm and their jokes the worst.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Calena
members.note: He has not slept a whole night in a camp in thirty years and does not intend to start at Stagley.

members.role: Heir; quartermaster of the Crown Road army
members.note: He has worked out that the barge supply for 46,000 men runs out a week before Stagley could fall.

members.role: Daughter; married into a Lucernan grain house
members.note: Her husband's house buys Calena wheat cheap and sells it dear to Solenne, and her father does not know.

members.role: Dowager
members.note: She still keeps the list of the Caliani men who died on the Brightwash and reads it every May.

famousDead: Commanded the watch at the Brightwash and died in the rout.
FX03-009.secret: The heir has told no one that the Stagley barge supply is a week short, because his father would call him a coward for it.
hooks: The baron wants the van at Stagley to wash out 1014.
Cosimo's sums could stop the war if anyone hears them.
Elisa's Lucernan husband offers to buy the whole Calena harvest early.

FX03-010.name: House Aldoreni
FX03-010.title: Baron of Lunium
FX03-010.arms: a red wolf's head on grey

military.office: Lords of the Lunium march levy
military.unit: 10 lances and 200 hill crossbowmen
military.ties: Aldoreni sons ride with the Albano Hill Riders on the Ashland March, and their hill crossbowmen guard the wells against Hael Hounds.

FX03-010.power: Dry hill farms and sheep walks of the Lunium hills toward the Ashland March, about 3,000 suns a year in good years.
FX03-010.history: Roderic the Lionheart gave the Lunium hills to his knight Galeazzo Aldoreni in 868 to hold the road toward the Ashlands. The land was poor and the house stayed poor. In the hungry years of 1091 and 1092 the baron raised his rents, and in 1093 his tenants marched to Albano and seized its granary with the rebels there, until General Vittor Montaro took the town back. The crown fined the house half its income for five years. When Roderic III planned new farms in the Ashlands, the Aldoreni hoped to be made lords of them, but Hael Hounds tore apart the surveyors in April 1099 and the plan died. The house now owes the crown its fine and owes its tenants their trust.
FX03-010.reputation: Disgraced hill lords who could not feed their own people; the March riders like them better than the court does.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Lunium
members.note: He blames the 1093 rising on Albano agitators and has never once blamed his rents.

members.role: Heir; rider of the Albano Hill Riders
members.note: He hunts Hael Hounds for sport and wears a collar of their teeth.

members.role: Daughter; married to a tenant's son
members.note: She married the man who led the tenants to Albano, and her father has not spoken her name since.

members.role: Grandson; Marta's boy
members.note: He is the only grandchild, and the baron cannot decide whether to make him heir.

famousDead: Knight of the Lionheart; first baron of Lunium.
FX03-010.secret: Marta's husband still meets the old Albano rebels, and some of them want another rising if the king dies.
hooks: The crown's fine falls due again in 1105.
Leandro offers to guide a new Ashland survey.
The baron must choose an heir: a reckless son or a rebel's child.

FX03-011.name: the Sabrini family
FX03-011.title: Bearer of the Lion Banner
FX03-011.arms: a gold lance flying a blue pennon, on red

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of the Lion Banner
military.unit: the banner guard of the Lion Guard, 24 knights
military.ties: A Sabrini has carried the royal banner beside the king in every host since the Coast Road, and the family's sons are raised in the Lion Hall.

FX03-011.power: The office of the Lion Banner, a house below Lion Hill and a royal pension of 400 suns a year, and the trust of every king.
FX03-011.history: On 14 April 896, among the olive terraces a day short of Morhaven, the Lionheart's standard-bearer fell to a Wind rider's arrow. The crossbow sergeant Pello Sabrini picked the banner out of the dust and held it on a terrace wall until the knights charged past him. The Lionheart knighted him on the field and made the banner his family's. Sabrinis carried it at the Brightwash in 1014, where the bearer died covering the retreat, and at Gull Isle in 1053. The house has never been rich, and every son is trained in the Lion Hall to stand where the king stands. On 18 November 1104 the bearer's son was one of the two knights in the practice yard who carried the king indoors.
FX03-011.reputation: The most trusted family in the palace, and the poorest knights at court.

members.role: Head of the family; Bearer of the Lion Banner
members.note: He has carried the banner for twenty-two years and asks every night who it will follow if the king dies.

members.role: Heir; knight of the Lion Guard
members.note: He carried the king indoors in November and has sworn silence to the king alone.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She sews the banner's repairs herself and knows every stain on it by battle.

members.role: Younger son; squire in the Lion Hall; the black sheep
members.note: He drinks in the Long Arm, owes money there, and has begun to hint that his brother knows something about the king.

famousDead: Held the Lion Banner on a terrace wall at the Coast Road in 896.
Died with the banner covering the retreat on the Brightwash.
FX03-011.secret: Lucan Sabrini carried the collapsed king indoors on 18 November 1104 and knows the Lion's heart is failing.
hooks: Tullio is about to sell what his brother saw.
If the king dies, the Lord Marshal and the queen will both demand the banner.
The banner needs new silk and the pension is a year late.

FX03-012.name: the Tessaro family
FX03-012.title: Castellan of the Montessa Gate
FX03-012.arms: a white gate with a black portcullis, on red

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of the Montessa Gate
military.unit: the Montessa Gate garrison, 400 pass spears and crossbowmen
military.ties: The first Tessaro was the sergeant who held the wall beside Ruggero Montaro in 952, and the family still sends its sons to the Laughing Company for a year before they take the gate.

FX03-012.power: The walled pass fort of the Montessa Gate, its two years of stores and its 400 men, under the Wardens of the Crown Road.
FX03-012.history: In the winter of 952 Crown foothill bandits tried the Montessa Gate on the old Solen wall, and Ruggero Montaro held it all night on a broken shin he did not feel. Beside him stood the sergeant Aldo Tessaro, who felt everything and held anyway. When the Wardens of the Crown Road needed a castellan for the gate in 954, the Montaros named him. Tessaros have held it since, under the Ardanes in law and the Montaros in heart. The family keeps the gate stocked for two years, as the citadel of Vitia is. In the dear year of 1102 the castellan quietly sold good grain from the stores at triple price.
FX03-012.reputation: Plain, tough frontier sergeants who keep a tidy fort; the Montaros call them the only Tessaros who feel the cold.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of the Montessa Gate
members.note: He filled half the gate's grain sacks with chaff in 1102 and prays nobody lays siege before harvest.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the stores
members.note: She knows what the sacks hold and has begun buying grain back sack by sack with her own dowry.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Laughing Company
members.note: Named for the Numb Montaro, he serves his year in the Company and has picked a fight with every cousin who laughs at him.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She shoots better than her brother and has been told she may not join the garrison.

famousDead: Held the Montessa Gate beside Ruggero Montaro in 952; first castellan.
FX03-012.secret: Half the Montessa Gate's siege stores are chaff; the castellan sold the grain in 1102.
hooks: An inspector of the Crown Road army is coming in spring.
Ruggero's quarrel with a Montaro cousin ends in a duel outside Ardata.
Bandits seem to know exactly how long the gate could hold.

FX03-013.name: the Arcella family
FX03-013.title: Pike-Master of the Castella Long Spears
FX03-013.arms: three black pikes points upward, on gold

military.office: Hereditary Pike-Masters of the Castella Long Spears
military.unit: the Castella Long Spears, 6,000 pikes at Castella and Norossa
military.ties: Every captain of the Long Spears for a hundred years has been an Arcella or married to one, and the Terrace School of Castella borrows their drill for the crossbows behind the pikes.

FX03-013.power: The pike-master's office, a drill field on the lake shore at Castella, and the loyalty of 6,000 pikemen who learned their trade from Arcella sergeants.
FX03-013.history: After the Black Cough the Northern Lakes had too few knights, and King Galen IV the Fair let the Castella towns raise a militia of long spears from the freed farmers. Its first drill-master was Nerio Arcella, a lake fisherman who had served in Morhaven and drilled the farmers in square blocks with eighteen-foot pikes. Galen made the post hereditary in 931. The Long Spears held the Brightwash crossing in 1014 while the camp fled, the one Varennan company that did not run. Since then the Arcellas have trained every pike-block in the north. In 1105 the Long Spears are named for the Stagley stroke, and the pike-master wants to march, though his grandson cannot be found.
FX03-013.reputation: The quiet backbone of the northern army; knights mock their mud-coloured coats and stand behind them all the same.

members.role: Head of the family; Pike-Master of the Castella Long Spears
members.note: At sixty-four he still walks the front rank of every drill, and the pikemen set their pace by his limp.

members.role: His daughter; married to the Terrace School's senior sergeant
members.note: She runs the drill field's accounts and is the real link between the pikes and Captain Monti's crossbows.

members.role: Heir; senior captain of the Long Spears
members.note: He has told the Lord Marshal that pikes on barges are pikes that cannot form.

members.role: Grandson; deserter
members.note: He left his block in October 1104 for a Palella spinner and has not been seen since.

famousDead: First drill-master of the Castella Long Spears.
Held the Brightwash crossing in 1014 while the camp fled.
FX03-013.secret: The pike-master's grandson deserted in 1104, and the family is hiding it from the Long Spears' muster rolls.
hooks: Valerio is seen with Palella smugglers near Crowbrook.
Tancred's doubts about the barge plan reach the War Party.
The Terrace School wants to merge the pike and crossbow drills under one master.

FX03-014.name: the Centani of Valia
FX03-014.title: Hundred-Captain of Valia
FX03-014.arms: a white muster stone on brown, the hundred's sign
FX03-014.words: When the Horn Blows, Valia Comes

military.office: Hundred-Captains of Valia
military.unit: the Valia hundreds, 1,200 Hundredmen at full call
military.ties: A Centani has called the Valia hundreds to the muster stone in every war since the Black Cough, and three of them died on the Brightwash.

FX03-014.power: Thirty acres of free land each for nine households, the old horn of the Valia hundreds, and the right to name the file-leaders.
FX03-014.history: After the Black Cough killed one in five of the plain, Teodor the Patient let the free farmers of Valia keep their land rent-free in return for drill and war service, and the Centani household was named to keep the muster stone and the horn in 918. Since then a Centani has blown it for every war. Three Centani sons died on the Brightwash in 1014, when the hundreds were caught in their blankets. A Centani file-leader was among the men who retook Albano with Vittor Montaro in 1093. They are free farmers, not lords, and proud of it. The family has learned that the crown means to call 10,000 Hundredmen for the Stagley stroke, at harvest time.
FX03-014.reputation: Free, plain-spoken farmer-soldiers; the knights call them clods and are glad of them in a fight.

members.role: Head of the family; Hundred-Captain of Valia
members.note: He has said in the Valia church that he will not call the hundreds before the barley is in, king or no king.

members.role: His wife
members.note: She runs the nine farms when the men are called and has buried two sons who answered the horn.

members.role: Heir; file-leader who fought at Albano
members.note: He saw the starving tenants of Albano hanged in 1093 and does not like to talk about it.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She wants to go to Varenna to learn letters, which no Centani has ever done.

famousDead: Three brothers who died with the Valia hundreds on the Brightwash.
hooks: The Stagley muster comes before the barley harvest.
A royal captain threatens to take the horn if Garin will not blow it.
Bianca runs away to Varenna.

FX03-015.name: the Faroni family
FX03-015.title: Keeper of the Tibata Strait Tower
FX03-015.arms: a gold flame atop a black tower, on blue

military.office: Keepers of the Tibata Strait Tower and captains of the Strait March Coast Watch
military.unit: the Tibata Strait Tower and 300 men of the Coast Watch
military.ties: Faroni sons serve as sergeants of the Lion Marines at Tibata, and the tower's fire is the first warning the Lion Fleet gets of a Blackreef sail.

FX03-015.power: The beacon tower over the Strait of Hael, a chain of six smaller beacons and 300 Coast Watch men.
FX03-015.history: After the Peace of Ratrock in 1056 the crown built the Tibata Strait Tower to watch for Blackreef sails, and gave it to Marco Faroni, a Lion Marine sergeant who had fought at Gull Isle. His sons kept the fire. In 1069 Blackreef raiders came into Tibata harbor and the tower lit in time. On the night of 1085 it did not, and the raiders burned the fishing fleet and the harbor sheds and left the town full of orphans. The keeper that night, the founder's eldest son, said the oil was wet; he drowned himself in 1086. The family kept the tower only because no one else wanted it, and has lit it every night since without fail.
FX03-015.reputation: A family that failed once and has paid for it every night since; Tibata fishermen spit and then trust them.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Tibata Strait Tower
members.note: He climbs to the fire at every dusk himself, though he has a dozen men to do it.

members.role: His wife; a Tibata fisherman's daughter
members.note: She lost her father in the 1085 burning and married the brother of the man blamed for it.

members.role: Heir; sergeant of the Lion Marines
members.note: He wants to be on the first galley that sails against Blackreef.

members.role: The keeper's brother; tower sergeant
members.note: He knows the oil was not wet in 1085, because he was the one who took the Blackreef silver for his brother.

famousDead: Lion Marine of Gull Isle; first keeper of the tower.
Keeper on the night of the 1085 burning; drowned himself.
FX03-015.secret: In 1085 the keeper's younger brother took Blackreef silver to let the fire die, and his elder brother took the blame and drowned himself.
hooks: A Blackreef agent comes back to Teodoro with a new offer.
Marco wants a berth on Castellan's flagship.
A Tibata orphan of 1085 swears to burn the tower.

FX03-016.name: the Ruffaldi family
FX03-016.title: Master of the Ruffaldi counting room
FX03-016.arms: a bolt of blue cloth unrolled over a silver bend, on white
FX03-016.power: Contracts to buy a fifth of the Weavers' Guild's blue cloth, counting rooms at Camia and in Bluewater, and a standing order from House Morello of Lucerna.
FX03-016.history: The Ruffaldis were cloth buyers of Camia from the reign of Teodor II the Silent, when Varenna grew rich selling wheat and cloth through Lucerna. They bought from the weaving widows of the plague years and sold to Lucernan factors. When the spinning wheel came in 1085, House Calvane tried to buy every yard the Palella made, and the Ruffaldis kept their share by paying the Brisa spinners a penny more. Since 1096 they have bought for House Morello of Lucerna and back the Loom Towns in the Great Council's lobbies. They are rich, unloved by the Calvanes and loved by the spinners. In December 1104 the house lent a boatman the money for a new boat, and the boatman has since left for the upper Palella.
FX03-016.reputation: Sharp, fair buyers who pay on the nail; Bluewater says a Ruffaldi yard is a true yard.

members.role: Head of the house
members.note: He has never bought a bolt without measuring it himself, even from Nella Brisa.

members.role: Heiress; runs the Bluewater counting room
members.note: She wants a weavers' seat in the Great Council and means to sit in it herself.

members.role: Son; factor at Lucerna
members.note: He drinks with Lady Flavia Morello's clerks and has heard the words 'Ostran front house' once too often.

members.role: Mother of the house; a Brisa cousin
members.note: She was one of the first women taught the wheel, and gave Sabina of Camia's boatman his boat.

famousDead: Bought the weaving widows' cloth after the plague years and built the Camia counting room.
FX03-016.secret: The mother of the house paid for the boat that carried Sabina of Camia up the Palella.
hooks: The Calvanes try to buy out the Ruffaldis' Morello contract.
Matteo stumbles onto the dragon-toll payments in Lucerna.
Rosalba runs for a weavers' seat in the Great Council.

FX03-017.name: the Barcanti family
FX03-017.title: Master of the Tarona Barges
FX03-017.arms: a black river barge on a silver wave, on green
FX03-017.power: About 140 Palella barges, the towpaths and mule teams from Tarona to Crowbrook, and the crown's contract to carry the Stagley stroke.
FX03-017.history: The Barcantis poled grain barges on the lower Palella for generations and had six boats when the Peace of Dorium opened the river and the Ashwater to Varennan barges in 1016. They borrowed, built, and by 1050 ran the largest barge fleet on the river from the small town of Tarona. Their barges carried Palella cloth up to Ashmere and Ashmere copper down. In 1104 the War Party's quartermasters hired every Barcanti barge for late April to carry 46,000 men to Crowbrook. The family stands to earn more in one season than in ten. Half its bargemen are married into Ashmere river families, and the old master does not trust them with the secret of the date.
FX03-017.reputation: River rats grown rich; nobody on the Palella moves a sack without a Barcanti hearing of it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Tarona Barges
members.note: He signed the War Party's contract and then lay awake wondering who in Ashmere would burn his barges.

members.role: Heiress; master of the mule teams
members.note: She knows every towpath innkeeper from Tarona to Crowbrook by name.

members.role: Son; married into an Ashmere river family
members.note: His wife's brothers keep the Crowbrook wharves, and he has told her that the barges are hired for spring.

members.role: Grandson; barge boy
members.note: He carried a runaway girl and a heavy sack upriver for Lupo Grell's men in November and was paid in silver.

famousDead: Built the barge fleet after the Peace of Dorium.
FX03-017.secret: A Barcanti boy helped carry Sabina of Camia and the wheel parts upriver, and Pello has let the war's timing slip to his Ashmere in-laws.
hooks: Ashmere spies want the date the barges leave Tarona.
Lazzaro is the only witness who knows which way the spinner went.
The crown is three months late paying the first instalment.

FX03-018.name: the Calafati family
FX03-018.title: Master Caulker of the Royal Shipwrights
FX03-018.arms: a black pitch-pot between two caulking irons, on yellow
FX03-018.power: The caulkers' and pitch-boilers' benches of the Royal Shipwrights of Varenna, about 300 men, and the only recipe for the yards' hull pitch.
FX03-018.history: When Lothar I opened the royal yards in 783 with slipways for twelve galleys, he brought caulkers from Lucerna's Arsenal, and one of them, Bastian Calafati, stayed and married a Varenna girl. His family has kept the caulking benches of the yards since. Calafati pitch, boiled from Pavice pine with a secret measure of fish oil, keeps a galley dry a season longer than any other. The family is under Master Aldo Ferran in the guild and above every other bench in pride. Since the Corsair War the yards have been half idle, and the Calafatis have taken work caulking Lucernan and Morhaven cogs. In 1105 Admiral Castellan's dream of 40 new galleys would make them rich, if anyone pays.
FX03-018.reputation: Black-handed, foul-mouthed and indispensable; no galley leaves the royal yards without a Calafati thumb on its seams.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Caulker of the Royal Shipwrights
members.note: He has refused three Lucernan offers for his pitch recipe and boasts of the fourth.

members.role: Heiress; boils the pitch
members.note: She is the only one besides her father who knows the fish-oil measure.

members.role: Son; caulker on Galley Row; the black sheep
members.note: He owes the Shears money and has been asked to bring them a barrel of the yards' pitch.

members.role: Granddaughter; apprentice
members.note: She sneaks into the galley sheds at night to watch the shipwrights.

famousDead: Arsenal caulker brought to the new royal yards in 783.
FX03-018.secret: The famous Calafati pitch was copied from the Lucerna Arsenal's own recipe, and the Arsenal has never forgiven the theft.
hooks: A Lucernan agent offers a fortune for the fish-oil measure.
Enzo's debts drag the family toward the Shears.
Forty new galleys would need 300 more caulkers.

FX03-019.name: the Guadeschi family
FX03-019.title: Master of the Blue Vats of Vitina
FX03-019.arms: a blue lily on silver, three drops below
FX03-019.power: The woad vats of Vitina, which dye about a quarter of the Palella blue cloth, and the guild secret of the double dip.
FX03-019.history: Palella blue is woad, and the woad vats of Vitina at the river mouth are older than the kingdom. In 922, when the plague widows began to work their husbands' looms, Orsola Guadeschi bought out three emptied vat-houses and found that a second dip after a day's airing gave the colour that does not fade. Her heirs kept the double dip secret and sold it as Palella blue. House Calvane buys most of their cloth and has long wanted their vats. Since the wheel tripled the yarn, the Guadeschi vats cannot keep up, and the house has hired new hands from outside the guild. One of them asked too many questions about the wheel and was found drowned in a vat in 1103.
FX03-019.reputation: Proud, blue-armed and secretive; the Calvanes need them and dislike it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Blue Vats
members.note: Her arms are blue to the elbow, and she still checks every vat's colour by the evening light.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He was the last man seen with the drowned vat hand of 1103.

members.role: Daughter; married to a Calvane factor
members.note: Her husband wants the double dip, and she has not decided whose side she is on.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He saw his uncle at the vats on the night of the drowning.

famousDead: Found the double dip that makes Palella blue fast.
FX03-019.secret: The vat hand drowned in 1103 was an Ashmere spy hunting the spinning wheel, and Remo Guadeschi killed him.
hooks: The Calvanes offer to buy the vats outright.
Young Ilario tells a priest what he saw.
Ashmere sends a second spy, this time after the double dip.

FX03-020.name: the Decimani family
FX03-020.title: Reeve of the Temple's Sixth in the Western Hills
FX03-020.arms: a gold key over ten gold coins, on white
FX03-020.words: One in Ten, and Ten Times Again
FX03-020.power: The hereditary reeveship of the Temple's estates in the western hills, a tenth of every rent they collect, and the Temple's courts behind them.
FX03-020.history: After the Tithe Truce of 803 the Luminary of Varenna needed lay men to collect the rents of the Temple's farms that paid the crown nothing. Lucio Decimani, a Pertello notary, took the western hills in 804 for a tenth of what he gathered. His heirs have held the reeveship since, uncles and nephews passing into the Temple when a son had no taste for ledgers. They grew rich, built a stone house above Pertello, and earned the hatred of every tenant. When the Temple doubled its rents in the Venina hills, the Decimanis sent the collectors in. Since 1102 Agnese of Venina's strike has shut forty villages to them, and their men have been stoned twice.
FX03-020.reputation: The most hated name in the western hills; mothers threaten children with the Decimani man.

members.role: Head of the family; Reeve of the Temple's Sixth
members.note: He has asked Luminary Brandi for Temple soldiers to break the strike and been told to wait for the chair to be filled.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the rent rolls
members.note: She knows which rolls have been padded and by how much.

members.role: Heir; collector in the Venina hills
members.note: He was stoned out of a village in 1104 and has sworn to burn its barns.

members.role: Younger son; priest of the Temple at Pertello
members.note: He secretly buries the dead of the striking villages, whom the Temple has forbidden its priests to bury.

famousDead: Pertello notary who took the western rents in 804.
FX03-020.secret: The family has padded the Temple's rent rolls by one part in eight for forty years and kept the difference.
hooks: Fabio plans to burn a striking village's barns.
Teodoro is caught burying strikers' dead.
If Lady Clara finds the padded rolls, the Temple itself may sacrifice the Decimanis.

FX03-021.name: the Cardane family
FX03-021.title: Physician of the Lion Stair
FX03-021.arms: a red heart pierced by a silver bend, on black
FX03-021.power: The office of physician to the Valdane kings, a house on Lion Hill, and a private book of every Valdane death since the Lionheart.
FX03-021.history: Master Ugo Cardane was the court physician who reached the Lionheart on the palace stair in March 902 and found him already dead. He wrote down the pulse, the colour and the height of the dead king and began a book. His heirs have been physicians to the Valdanes since, and the book has grown to eleven Valdane deaths, which a Cardane turned into the treatise that warns of the long-armed heart. The physicians warned Lothar III against marrying Lucilla to a Castella cousin in 1044 and were overruled. On 18 November 1104 Master Emilio Cardane was called to the Lion Hall and listened to the king's heart. He is the only physician who knows, and he has told no one.
FX03-021.reputation: The quietest family in the palace; courtiers watch their faces after every royal audience.

members.role: Head of the family; Physician of the Lion Stair
members.note: He has given the king a year at most and sleeps with the eleventh chapter of the treatise under his pillow.

members.role: His daughter; sun-sister and herbalist
members.note: She tends Prince Galen and has measured how far he can see: twenty paces, and less each year.

members.role: Heir; physician to the Lion Guard
members.note: General Montaro has offered him his father's office in the next reign if he tells the War Party what he knows.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He copies out the death book in a fair hand for his grandfather, and reads it.

famousDead: Reached the Lionheart on the palace stair in 902 and began the book of Valdane deaths.
Warned Lothar III against the Castella marriage of 1044.
FX03-021.secret: The physician knows the king's heart is failing, and his heir is close to selling the knowledge to the Lord Marshal.
hooks: Aldo must choose between his father and the War Party.
The queen asks Lucia whether her son will be fit to rule.
A thief breaks into the house for the book of Valdane deaths.

FX03-022.name: the Remigi family
FX03-022.title: Captain of the Tarium Squadron
FX03-022.arms: a silver oared galley on dark blue, a gold star above

military.office: Captains of the Tarium squadron of the Lion Fleet
military.unit: the Tarium squadron, 12 war galleys and 600 Lion Marines
military.ties: Remigi captains have commanded galleys of the royal yards since the second launch in 785, and the present head was Admiral Castellan's flag captain in the Corsair War.

FX03-022.power: Command of the twelve-galley Tarium squadron, a harbour house and ropewalk at Tarium, and the friendship of the Admiral of the Lion Fleet.
FX03-022.history: The second galley launched from Lothar I's yards in 785 was given to Remigio of Tarium, a Lucernan-trained master, and his sons kept the name and the command. Remigi galleys carried the Lionheart's knights to Felano in 894. In the Battle of the Strait in June 1052 the family lost two galleys in the shoals, and at Gull Isle in 1053 the present head, then a young captain, cut his galley free of a burning raft with an axe and towed out another. Admiral Nino Castellan has been his friend since. The house is the heart of the Strait League on the coast, and it does not know that its Lucernan friends are paid out of the dragon toll.
FX03-022.reputation: Seamen's seamen; when the Remigi squadron rows out, Tarium closes its shops to watch.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Tarium Squadron
members.note: At seventy-three he still takes the tiller of his flagship on Sea Opening.

members.role: Heir; captain of the galley Lion's Oar
members.note: He will sail with Castellan to Lucerna on 1 April to ask for 20 galleys.

members.role: Valerio's wife; keeper of the Tarium ropewalk
members.note: She buys Lucernan hemp and has noticed the Lucernans never seem short of Strait cargo.

members.role: Son; missing at sea
members.note: His cog vanished in the Strait in 1103, and a sailor swears he saw him alive on a Blackreef deck.

famousDead: Captain of the second galley of the royal yards; founder.
hooks: Remo may be alive on Blackreef.
Valerio sails to Lucerna and may learn of the fifth share.
Brina's hemp accounts could prove Lucerna's dealings in the Strait.

FX03-023.name: the Destrani family
FX03-023.title: Master of the Torossa Studs
FX03-023.arms: a black horse rearing, on silver

military.office: Remount-masters of the Crown Knights
military.unit: the Torossa studs, about 900 horses
military.ties: Destrani studs mount half the Crown Knights of the Forty Days and every Albano Hill Rider, and the family's sons serve as remount sergeants on campaign.

FX03-023.power: The Torossa plains studs, about 900 brood mares and stallions, and the crown's remount contract.
FX03-023.history: When Roderic the Lionheart founded the Hall of the Lion in 866 his knights needed big horses to carry long men in mail. The breeder Fausto Destrani crossed Morhaven stallions with the heavy plough mares of the Torossa plain, and the king gave him the royal studs at Torossa. Destrani horses carried the charge on the Coast Road in 896. The family also breeds the small hard ponies of the Albano Hill Riders. In 1105 the War Party has ordered 1,200 remounts for the Stagley stroke, and the studs have perhaps 800 fit to go.
FX03-023.reputation: Horse-mad, horse-rich and plain-mannered; knights flatter them for a good mount.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Torossa Studs
members.note: He knows the bloodline of every horse in the Lion Guard and has refused to sell the queen a mare.

members.role: Heiress; trainer of war horses
members.note: She rides the stallions nobody else will and wants to ride to Stagley as a remount sergeant.

members.role: Son; remount sergeant with the Albano Hill Riders
members.note: He races ponies against the Aldoreni heir for money he does not have.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She doctors horses and people alike, and the Torossa villagers prefer her to the priest.

famousDead: Bred the great horses of the Hall of the Lion.
hooks: The crown wants 1,200 remounts and there are 800.
A Lion Guard stallion dies of poison in the Torossa stables.
Orsino loses a prize stallion in a pony race.

FX03-024.name: the Selvani family
FX03-024.title: Warden of the King's Wood of Ambalia
FX03-024.arms: a green stag's head between two arrows, on gold
FX03-024.power: The wardenship of the royal forest of Ambalia, its forest court, 40 foresters and the right to hang poachers of the king's deer.
FX03-024.history: Roderic the Lionheart loved to hunt boar in the forest of Ambalia, and in 870 he made his huntsman Orso Selvani its warden. The Selvanis have kept the King's Wood since, with a forest court in the market town and 40 foresters. Roderic II hunted here a month before he fell at the Lion Fair. In the plague years poachers took half the deer and the Selvanis hanged a dozen. The present warden sent his best hunters to the Ashland March in 1099 to track the Hael Hounds that killed the king's surveyors, and two did not come back. In 1105 the woods are full of men who should not be there: deserters, smugglers and a preacher of the Ashen.
FX03-024.reputation: Hard, quiet forest folk; the Ambalia villagers fear their court and come to them when wolves take the sheep.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the King's Wood
members.note: He has not hanged a poacher in ten years and lets hungry men take rabbits.

members.role: Heiress; head forester
members.note: She tracked a Hael Hound pack for nine days in 1099 and came back with its leader's skin.

members.role: Son; forester gone missing
members.note: He has been listening to the Ashen preacher in the deep wood and did not come home at Midwinter.

members.role: Mother of the house; keeper of the forest court rolls
members.note: She writes the forest court's judgments and softens them in the copying.

famousDead: The Lionheart's huntsman; first warden of the King's Wood.
FX03-024.secret: The warden knows the Ashen preacher sheltered in his wood and has let him be, which is heresy by the Temple's law.
hooks: Lazzaro has joined the Ashen in the deep wood.
Deserters from the Long Spears hide among the oaks.
The crown asks for hunters to clear the Ashlands before new surveys.

FX03-025.name: the Tosatori, called the Shears
FX03-025.title: Master of the Shears
FX03-025.arms: a pair of open shears, scratched on a sun-coin; their mark
FX03-025.power: A ring of about 40 clippers, false money-changers and fences in Bluewater and on Galley Row, and pawnshops that take the galley crews' pay.
FX03-025.history: After the Corsair War the royal mint clipped the Varennan sun to pay the rowers, and Gerardo Tosatori, a mint clerk dismissed in 1056, saw that the crown had shown everyone how. He set up as a money-changer in Bluewater and shaved every coin that crossed his table. His sons built a ring of clippers and pawnshops, and the galley crews, paid in suns nobody else will take at face, have to change them at Shears' tables. Two Tosatoris have been hanged at the mint gate, and the family keeps both their nooses in a chest. When the Lord Treasurer secretly debased the coin in 1103, the Shears noticed within a month and bought every good old sun they could find. Their clipped suns have now reached the Lion Marines' pay chest.
FX03-025.reputation: Bluewater's open secret: everyone knows the Shears, and everyone has changed money with them.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Shears
members.note: He weighs every coin by hand and can tell a 1103 sun from an older one in the dark.

members.role: Heiress; runs the pawnshops of Galley Row
members.note: She holds the pawn tickets of half the Lion Marines and calls in debts on pay day.

members.role: Son; false money-changer in Bluewater
members.note: He changes money for the Calvane clerks, who know exactly what he is.

members.role: Granddaughter; the black sheep
members.note: She wants to be a sun-sister and has written a confession of the family's crimes she has not yet sent.

famousDead: Hanged at the mint gate for clipping.
Hanged at the mint gate; his noose is in the family chest.
FX03-025.secret: The Shears know the crown debased its own coin in 1103 and hold a sack of the old full-weight suns as proof.
hooks: The Lion Marines blame the treasury for clipped pay, and the treasury blames the Montaros.
Fiora's confession could hang her whole family.
Lord Calvane would pay to keep the Shears quiet about the 1103 coin.

FX04-001.name: the Dandin family
FX04-001.title: Captain of the Lagoon Marines
FX04-001.arms: a black boarding hook over a silver galley's bow, on red

military.office: Captains of the Lagoon Marines
military.unit: the Lagoon Marines, 2,400 citizen marines and crossbowmen
military.ties: Dandins have led Lucerna's marines since the seizure of the Tessarian ships in 1044, and every citizen drawn by lot for marine service learns their boarding drill.

FX04-001.power: Command of the Lagoon Marines, a council family's seat in the Great Council, and the loyalty of men who serve by lot and remember who brought them home.
FX04-001.history: On New Year's Day 1044, when Lucerna and Ostra seized 38 Tessarian ships in their harbours, the shipmaster Bruno Dandin led the boarding party that took the largest of them without a death. The Great Council registered his family that year, and he was given the marines. Dandins have commanded them since, under the Admirals of House Salvi. Bruno's son fought in the Corsair War and was on the galleys that held back at the Battle of the Strait in 1052, which the family has never explained. In 1104 the marine Iacopo Rizzo burned an old hulk off the Isle of Graves with a stolen jar of the Arsenal's oil, and Captain Orsola Dandin knows he did it on a dare from her own son.
FX04-001.reputation: The fighting family of a city that hates to fight; the marines adore them and the council finds them expensive.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Lagoon Marines
members.note: She is the first woman to captain the marines and keeps a Tessarian boarding axe from 1044 over her bed.

members.role: Her son; marine sergeant; the black sheep
members.note: He bet Iacopo Rizzo a gold crown that the lamp oil would not burn on water.

members.role: Her father; retired captain
members.note: He was on a galley that held back at the Battle of the Strait in 1052 and knows Admiral Doravelli's order was deliberate.

members.role: Daughter; drawn by lot for marine service
members.note: She would rather study at Chiara Benn's counting school and has asked her mother to buy her out of the lot.

famousDead: Took the largest Tessarian ship in the harbour in 1044 without a death.
FX04-001.secret: The captain's son dared the marine who burned the Arsenal's oil off the Isle of Graves, and the captain has hidden it from the Master of the Arsenal.
hooks: Ugo Brenta's jar count leads to the Dandin barracks.
Old Bruno is asked what really happened at the Strait in 1052.
Varenna's Admiral asks for Lucernan marines against Blackreef.

FX04-002.name: the Catenari family
FX04-002.title: Keeper of the Lagoon Chain
FX04-002.arms: a black chain stretched between two white towers, on blue

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the Lagoon Chain Towers
military.unit: the Lagoon Chain Towers, 400 men and the windlass crews
