military.ties: A Catenari has raised the iron chain across the lagoon mouth in every alarm since Doge Renato Salvi finished the towers, and the tower crews are drawn from their street at Pilots' Point.

FX04-002.power: The two towers at the lagoon mouth, the great windlasses and the chain, 400 men, and the right to stop any ship at night.
FX04-002.history: Doge Renato Salvi built the Lagoon Chain Towers between 866 and 883 and gave their keeping to his chain-smith, Lapo Catenari, who had forged the links. The Catenari have kept the chain since. They raised it against the Wind Empire's raiders in 893, against plague ships in 917 under the Forty-Day Law, and against the Tessarian ships in 1044, which could not run. They know every ship that enters at night, and they keep a book of it. Since 1056 the book has shown a small Blackreef-built boat entering four times a year on the quarter days, by order of the Lord of the Night Watch, never to be written down. The Catenari wrote it down anyway.
FX04-002.reputation: Iron-handed, early-rising and hard to bribe; every pilot salutes the towers going out and curses them coming in.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Lagoon Chain
members.note: He has kept the night book for thirty years and has never let the Night Watch see it.

members.role: Heiress; master of the windlass crews
members.note: She can raise the chain in the time it takes to say a prayer, and has timed it.

members.role: Son; crossbow sergeant of the south tower
members.note: A Night Watch officer has offered him 200 crowns for a look at his father's book.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She sews the night book's pages back in whenever her husband cuts one out in fear.

famousDead: Forged the lagoon chain for Doge Renato Salvi.
FX04-002.secret: The Catenari night book records every quarter-day landing of the boat that carries Blackreef's payments into the lagoon.
hooks: The Clean Ledger would give anything for the night book.
Fausto is close to selling it to the Night Watch.
A fire ship tests the chain on a moonless night.

FX04-003.name: the Tassin family
FX04-003.title: Captain of the Company of the Golden Wheel

military.office: Captains by contract of the Company of the Golden Wheel
military.unit: the Company of the Golden Wheel, 1,200 hired foot and crossbowmen
military.ties: The Tassins have held the Golden Wheel's contract for the Staple quays and the city since the Corsair War, renewed every seven years by the Small Council.

FX04-003.power: The Golden Wheel's contract, worth about 60,000 suns a year, a citizen's house bought in 1076, and 1,200 swords who answer to the family before the Republic.
FX04-003.history: Gaspar Tassin was a Free Company captain from the Free Marches who came to Lucerna with 300 men when the Corsair War began in 1051, because Lucerna paid on time. He stayed. His company grew into the Golden Wheel, which guards the Staple quays and the city because the Republic will not arm its own poor. Under the law a foreigner may buy citizenship after 25 years in the city, and Gaspar bought his in 1076, in the first year of the Harbor Pox. His son Ruggero holds the contract now. The family is rich, citizen and still foreign, and the old council families never ask a Tassin to dinner.
FX04-003.reputation: Reliable hired swords who have become Lucernans; the council trusts their contract, not their blood.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Company of the Golden Wheel
members.note: He knows the council would hand the city to whoever outbids him and keeps three months' pay in his own vault.

members.role: Founder; old captain
members.note: At seventy-nine he still drills the recruits in the Marches way and calls Lucernans fish.

members.role: Heiress; paymaster of the company
members.note: She wants a council family's son and a registered seat, and has picked out a poor Morello cousin.

members.role: Son; lieutenant
members.note: He has fallen for a salt-worker's daughter from the Lavium strike.

FX04-003.secret: The captain has been approached by an agent of Varenna about holding the Staple quays if the Lion Fleet ever comes.
hooks: The Golden Wheel's contract comes up for renewal in 1105.
Matteo's love ties the company to the Lavium strikers.
Clara's marriage bid stirs the old council houses.

FX04-004.name: House Rossa
FX04-004.title: Ship-lord of the Rossa cogs
FX04-004.arms: a red ship under a gold star, on silver
FX04-004.power: About 30 cogs on the Varenna and Palella runs, a registered seat in the Great Council, and the Calvane cloth trade through a marriage of 1071.
FX04-004.history: Andrea Rossa was a shipmaster who signed one of the first sea partnerships at the Harbor Court in April 726, sailing a rich widow's grain on her money, and married her daughter. The house has owned cogs ever since. In 1071 Livia Rossa married Piero Calvane of Dorium, and the Rossa cogs have carried Palella blue cloth to every port since, with Calvane cousins as their factors in the lagoon. They were left out of the toll share in 1056 and do not know it exists. In 1105 the head has joined Lady Flavia Morello's Clean Ledger, not from honesty but because the Calvane letters from Varenna say the Lion Fleet is building.
FX04-004.reputation: Solid, old, Varenna-friendly shipowners; the Doge's men think them harmless, which annoys them.

members.role: Head of the house; ship-lord
members.note: His late sister married the Lord Treasurer of Varenna, and the Calvane cousins still write to him every month.

members.role: Heiress; votes her late husband's shares
members.note: She sits with Lady Flavia Morello at every Clean Ledger supper and wants the next dogeship for a clean house.

members.role: Son; master of the cog Palella Rose
members.note: He saw the fire off the Isle of Graves from his deck and has told it in every tavern in Varenna.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She studies at Chiara Benn's counting school and carries her teacher's papers home in her satchel.

famousDead: Signed one of the first sea partnerships of 726.
Married Piero Calvane of Dorium in 1071.
FX04-004.secret: Chiara Benn's sums on the Ostran front house are hidden in the Rossa house, in a schoolgirl's satchel.
hooks: The Night Watch searches the house for Chiara Benn's papers.
Pietro's tavern tale reaches the Lion Fleet's admiral.
A Calvane letter warns of Varennan galleys.

FX04-005.name: the Sicurani family
FX04-005.title: Master of the Sicurani Bench
FX04-005.arms: a silver whale on dark green, a gold anchor below
FX04-005.words: We Pay When the Sea Takes
FX04-005.power: A sea-insurance bench in the Harbor Quarter that writes about a tenth of Lucerna's cargo policies, and a book of every wreck in the Middle Sea since 802.
FX04-005.history: After the Ostran Letter made bills of exchange common, Lucernan merchants began to sell promises against the sea, and the Sicurani opened one of the first insurance benches in 802. They kept a book of every wreck, storm and pirate taking reported in the Harbor Quarter, and priced their policies from it. In May 1088 the leviathan Old Ironjaw sank the cog Golden Gull west of the Strait of Hael, and the Sicurani had written her. The payment nearly broke them. They now insure only the Tamar run and leave the western approach to House Bassan's insurers. The heir wants the Bassan bounty on Old Ironjaw for himself, to win back the family's name.
FX04-005.reputation: Careful, gloomy, honest about bad news; captains say a Sicurani premium is the best weather forecast on the sea.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Sicurani Bench
members.note: He paid out the Golden Gull's 18,000 crowns in 1088 and has not written a western policy since.

members.role: Heir; would-be whale hunter
members.note: He is fitting out a cog with harpoon engines to claim the 5,000-crown bounty on Old Ironjaw.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the wreck book
members.note: From the wreck book she has worked out that ships which pay the dragon toll are almost never taken, and wonders why.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She pays the widows of the Golden Gull's crew a pension her husband does not know about.

famousDead: Opened one of the first sea-insurance benches of Lucerna in 802.
FX04-005.secret: The wreck book shows that Blackreef spares the ships of the four toll families, a pattern any clerk could read.
hooks: Tancred sails after Old Ironjaw.
Bianca's wreck pattern reaches the Clean Ledger.
House Bassan offers to buy the bench.

FX04-006.name: the Arvo family
FX04-006.title: Master of the Grain Run
FX04-006.arms: a silver wave and a black sail, on blue
FX04-006.power: Five grain cogs on the Tamar run, a quay at Pilots' Point, and the Morello connection by marriage.
FX04-006.history: The Arvo were sailors who obeyed the Forty-Day Law of 917 when others did not, anchoring forty days off the lagoon with plague-free crews while ships that broke the rule were sunk by the guard boats. Doge Ruggero Morello rewarded them with a grain contract, and they have sailed the Tamar run since. Teo Arvo, the best shipmaster of his generation, married Flavia Morello in 1084 and took her name, and when he died in 1090 she voted his ship shares in the Great Council. His brothers still sail the grain. In 1105 Lady Giulia Bassan has ordered the Tamar cogs to wait at sea before landing Solenne's grain, and the Arvo crews are eating their own cargo.
FX04-006.reputation: Honest grain sailors; the Morellos' sea arm, people say, which neither side likes to hear.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Grain Run
members.note: He has held his cogs at sea for three weeks on the Keeper's order and his crews are on half bread.

members.role: His wife; owner of two cog shares
members.note: She wants to land the grain at Solenne and let the Bassans sue.

members.role: Son; named for his dead uncle
members.note: He rows in the lagoon crew that won Sea Opening last year and drank free till Sea Closing.

members.role: Bastian's brother; pilot
members.note: He was named a pilot after his first ship, the Grey Gull, and keeps the Pilots' Oath like a priest.

famousDead: Best grain shipmaster of his day; husband of Lady Flavia Morello.
hooks: Marta Arvo lands Solenne's grain against the Keeper's order.
A plague rumour forces the Arvo cogs to anchor forty days.
Teo rows in this year's Sea Opening race.

FX04-007.name: the Agolanti family
FX04-007.title: Senior Night Pilot of the Pilots' Hall
FX04-007.arms: a silver needle on a black star, on dark blue
FX04-007.words: We Know the Way in the Dark
FX04-007.power: Four of the 90 Night Pilots of the Pilots' Hall, the oath-held secret of the floating lodestone needle, and the pilots' vote in the pay dispute of 1105.
FX04-007.history: The floating lodestone needle came to the Pilots' Hall about 850, and Ercole Agolanti was among the first pilots sworn to it, on his life. The family has given the Hall pilots in every generation since. Under the Pilots' Oath a pilot who shows the needle to an outsider is drowned, and in 1031 an Agolanti cousin was. The family steered the galleys that fed Morhaven in its siege and the convoys of the Corsair War. In 1105 the pilots will not lend their Night Pilots to Admiral Salvi's gold expedition until their pay is doubled, and the Agolanti are the hardest voices in the Hall. The heir has quietly been offered a fortune in Greyhaven to teach the needle.
FX04-007.reputation: Tight-lipped, star-wise and proud; captains pay them double and never ask how they find the lagoon in fog.

members.role: Head of the family; Senior Night Pilot
members.note: He says the Admiral may have his pilots when the Admiral's own pay is cut by half.

members.role: Heir; Night Pilot
members.note: A Greyhaven factor has offered him 3,000 crowns and a house to teach their pilots the needle.

members.role: Cosimo's wife
members.note: There are no women pilots, but she knows the needle as well as her husband from watching him.

members.role: Grandson; pilot's apprentice
members.note: His friend, another apprentice, was found drowned with a brass bowl and a needle in his pocket.

famousDead: One of the first pilots sworn to the floating needle.
Drowned under the Pilots' Oath for showing the needle to a Qadiri captain.
FX04-007.secret: The heir is weighing an offer from Greyhaven to sell the secret of the needle, a crime the family itself has punished by drowning.
hooks: The pilots' pay strike delays the gold expedition.
Ugo knows who drowned his fellow apprentice.
Cosimo sails for Greyhaven on a dark night.

FX04-008.name: the Fanari of Lucerna Light
FX04-008.title: Keeper of Lucerna Light
FX04-008.arms: a red flame atop a white tower, on black
FX04-008.power: The fire-tower on the harbour approach, its stores of oil and pitch from the Arsenal, and the sight of every ship that comes or goes.
FX04-008.history: When the Arsenal was founded in 762 the Republic built a fire-tower three kilometres out on the harbour approach, and gave it the next year to the fisherman Gino Fanari, whose boat had been the one to bring warning of a storm. The Fanari have kept Lucerna Light since. They burn oil and pitch sent by the Arsenal every month. Since 1025 some of the jars sent out to the Light have been marked 'lamp oil from the south', and the keeper's family found long ago that this oil burns on water. They have kept a few jars back, against the day the Republic forgets them.
FX04-008.reputation: Poor, odd, salt-cured tower folk; sailors throw them bread and fish as they pass.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of Lucerna Light
members.note: He has six jars of the Arsenal's secret oil hidden in the tower's cistern.

members.role: Heiress; night-keeper
members.note: She keeps a log of every ship's lights and saw the boat that comes in on quarter days.

members.role: Son; fisherman
members.note: He drinks in the Marsh Lamp and has boasted that his father has fire that burns the sea.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She keeps goats on a rock where nothing else will live.

FX04-008.secret: The light-keepers have six jars of Sabran fire-oil hidden in the tower cistern.
hooks: Remo's boast reaches the Night Watch.
The Sabran oil-master's agent asks about the Light's oil.
Tessa's ship log is wanted by the Clean Ledger.

FX04-009.name: the Bottari family
FX04-009.title: Cellar-Master of the Arsenal
FX04-009.arms: a black cask on gold, sealed with a red sun
FX04-009.power: The keys and tally of the Arsenal's cellars, the coopers of the Arsenal, and knowledge of what the lamp-oil jars hold.
FX04-009.history: The Bottari were coopers of the Arsenal from its founding. When the first 400 jars came from Sabra in 1025, entered as lamp oil from the south, Doge Giorgio Vanni needed a cellarer who would ask no questions, and he gave the cellar keys to Pietro Bottari. The family has kept the jars, sealed and counted, since. Each Master of the Arsenal is told the secret on taking office; the Bottari knew it before all of them. In 1104 a jar went missing on their watch and burned an old hulk off the Isle of Graves. Ugo Brenta is counting jars, and the cellar-master knows the count will come out one short whatever he does.
FX04-009.reputation: Plain coopers in the Arsenal's shadow; nobody thinks about them at all, which is the point.

members.role: Head of the family; Cellar-Master of the Arsenal
members.note: He has rewritten the cellar tally twice to hide the missing jar and is sure it shows.

members.role: Daughter; cooper
members.note: She makes the lead-sealed casks the jars travel in and knows their weight to the ounce.

members.role: Heir; cellar guard
members.note: He lost the cellar key for one night at dice last autumn and won it back by morning.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He plays in the cellars and has learned that the jars smell of the sea.

famousDead: First keeper of the lamp-oil cellar in 1025.
FX04-009.secret: The cellar-master has falsified the tally to hide the stolen jar, and his heir lent out the cellar key for a night.
hooks: Ugo Brenta's count comes out one short.
Whoever won Orsino's key at dice may have taken more than one jar.
Sabra's oil-master wants a name.

FX04-010.name: the Ghorvanni family
FX04-010.title: Master of the Rowers' Benches
FX04-010.arms: two crossed black oars on orange
FX04-010.power: The hiring of about 2,000 paid rowers for the Republic's galleys, a half-orc rowers' hall in the Harbor Quarter, and the bench-lists every captain needs.
FX04-010.history: Lucerna's galleys are rowed by paid free men, and many of them are half-orcs from every port of the Middle Sea. In 1047 a half-orc stroke-master named Ghor, who had rowed through the Debt War, bought a hall in the Harbor Quarter and began to hire rowers for the Arsenal by contract. His son took a Lucernan name with his citizenship, Ghorvanni, and the family has kept the bench-lists since. Their rowers pulled Lucerna's galleys through the Corsair War and the plague quarantines. In 1105 the Admiral wants rowers for a gold expedition up the Tirana, and the Ghorvanni remember that the last one sent 190 men to the Red Widow and paid their widows a month's wage.
FX04-010.reputation: Big, loud half-orcs who run a fair hall; the council needs them and will not seat them.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Rowers' Benches
members.note: He refuses to sign a single rower for the gold expedition until the widows of 1097 are paid.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the bench-lists
members.note: She is the only half-orc woman in Lucerna who keeps accounts with a zero, and Chiara Benn taught her.

members.role: Heir; stroke of the Doge's own galley
members.note: He rowed the Doge out to wed the sea last Sea Opening and was not invited to the feast.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She wants to buy a seat on the Great Council for a half-orc house and has started saving.

famousDead: Half-orc stroke-master who founded the rowers' hall.
FX04-010.secret: The rowers' hall hides Chiara Benn's lodgings, and the Night Watch has not thought to look among half-orcs.
hooks: The Admiral tries to hire rowers around the hall.
The Night Watch searches the Harbor Quarter for Chiara Benn.
Garin is insulted at the Doge's table and the benches go silent.

FX04-011.name: the Mulinari of Lavium
FX04-011.title: Master Miller of the Lavium Flats
FX04-011.arms: a white windmill on green, a gold sun in the corner
FX04-011.power: The skill of building post windmills, the milling of the nine Bassan mills on the Lavium flats, and the trust of the salt-workers.
FX04-011.history: The island has no good rivers, and in 1075 a Lavium miller named Teo Mulinari built the first post windmill on Bassan land, a whole mill that turns on a post to face the wind. The Bassans paid for eight more, and the Mulinari run them all. In 1103 Lady Giulia Bassan raised the milling toll, and the salt-workers of Lavium under Marro of Lavium struck and closed the pilots' landing for eleven days. The Mulinari mill the salt-workers' bread and sided with them quietly, milling at the old toll by night. Lady Giulia has found out. The family also knows how to build a windmill, and every lord in the Sunlands would pay to learn.
FX04-011.reputation: Clever, flour-white and stubborn; the salt-workers call them their own.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Miller; builder of the first post windmill
members.note: He is drawing a mill with sails that turn themselves to the wind and will not show anyone.

members.role: Heiress; runs the nine mills
members.note: She mills the strikers' grain at the old toll at night and has been caught.

members.role: Son; millwright
members.note: A Varennan factor has offered him a fortune to build windmills on the Palella plain.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She carries messages between the mills and Marro of Lavium's strikers.

FX04-011.secret: The millers have been milling at the old toll for the strikers in secret, and the Keeper of the Staple knows.
hooks: Lady Giulia threatens to take the mills from the family.
Fausto sails for Varenna with the windmill's secret.
The strike flares again and the pilots' landing closes.

FX04-012.name: the Pandetti family
FX04-012.title: Senior Notary of the Harbor Court
FX04-012.arms: a black quill crossed with a silver key, on red
FX04-012.power: The senior notary's bench of the Harbor Court, the keeping of the Hall of Records, and the drafting of half the sea partnerships in the city.
FX04-012.history: When Aurelian's admiral surrendered 40 galleys in the lagoon in 627, the price was Lucerna's own harbour court, and a Pandetti clerk wrote the treaty. The family has sat in the Harbor Court since. A Pandetti notary wrote down the sea partnership in April 726. The family keeps the Hall of Records, where the harbour ledgers run back to Solen times, among them the ledgers of 639 to 645 with Queen Nefira's seal on Lucerna's secret loan. In 1105 the senior notary has been asked by Lady Flavia Morello whether a court order could open the Doge's strongroom, and by the Lord of the Night Watch whether the Hall's old ledgers could quietly burn.
FX04-012.reputation: Dry, exact and irreplaceable; in Lucerna a contract is not real until a Pandetti has read it.

members.role: Head of the family; Senior Notary of the Harbor Court
members.note: He has told Lady Flavia that the law allows it and the Night Watch that the Hall is fireproof, and both were true.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the Hall of Records
members.note: She has read the Nefira ledgers and knows what Lucerna paid for Tamar's freedom.

members.role: Heir; notary to the Vanni house
members.note: He has drafted contracts for the Ostran front house and knows they are not about figs.

members.role: Granddaughter; pupil of the counting school
members.note: She sits beside the Rossa girl in Chiara Benn's school.

famousDead: Wrote the treaty of 627 that won Lucerna its harbour court.
FX04-012.secret: The heir has drafted the front house's contracts for the Vannis and knows what they hide.
hooks: A fire breaks out in the Hall of Records.
Lady Flavia asks the Harbor Court to order the strongroom opened.
Matteo is asked to testify against his own clients.

FX04-013.name: the Scogli of Tibenza
FX04-013.title: Master of the Night Coves
FX04-013.arms: a black rock in a white sea; scratched on their boat-posts
FX04-013.power: Thirty small boats, the night coves of the Tibenza shore, and the protection of the Lord of the Night Watch.
FX04-013.history: The Scogli fished the southern coves of Tibenza until 1020, when Doge Giorgio Vanni needed quiet boatmen to carry silver to the rebels of Sabra. They carried it, and since 1025 they have landed some of the Sabran jars that do not go through the Arsenal's books. They land Qadiri silk and Tamari wheat past the Staple at a quarter off, under the Vanni eye, and pay the Night Watch in return. In 1102 Scogli boats carried the front-house clerk Pio Ferro out into the lagoon on the night the Night Watch drowned him. In 1105 the old master has begun to wonder when the Vannis will decide that the Scogli know too much.
FX04-013.reputation: Every honest Tibenza fisher's cousin and every customs clerk's nightmare.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Night Coves
members.note: He rowed the boat that carried Pio Ferro out in 1102 and has not slept well since.

members.role: Heiress; keeper of the coves
members.note: She wants to cut the Vannis out and sell to Ostra's half-orc smugglers directly.

members.role: Son; boatman
members.note: He took a Varennan cog captain to safety from the Forty Days tavern one night in 1104, for pity, and the Night Watch is asking who.

members.role: Grandmother; net-mender and memory of the clan
members.note: She remembers which coves the first Sabran jars landed in, and why.

famousDead: Carried Doge Giorgio Vanni's silver to the Sabran rebels in 1020.
FX04-013.secret: The Scogli rowed the boat that carried Pio Ferro to his drowning in 1102.
hooks: The Night Watch hunts the boatman who hid the Varennan cog captain.
Sabina deals with Ostra's smugglers behind the Vannis' backs.
The Vannis decide the Scogli are a loose end.

FX05-001.name: House Kettleden
FX05-001.title: Lord of Kettleden and Keeper of the Yew Yard
FX05-001.arms: a green yew tree on gold

military.office: Keepers of the Brightkeep yew road
military.unit: the Kettleden levy, 300 rolled bowmen of the Northern Uplands and 20 knights
military.ties: Every stave that becomes a war bow passes the Kettleden tally at Brightkeep, and the King's Bowmen send a sergeant to count it with them each summer.

FX05-001.power: Kettleden Castle in the northern forests and the keeping of the Brightkeep yew yard, where the elven stave carts arrive each summer.
FX05-001.history: The Kettledens were castellans of the old lords of Brightkeep and came to the Ashfords when Hild of Brightkeep married Aldred in 771. When Queen Elsbeth sealed the Yew Compact with Eldergrove at Brightkeep in June 1012, she gave the Kettledens the keeping of the yew yard, where about 8,000 seasoned staves are counted every summer. Since 1099 the elven carts have come a quarter short, and the yard has filled the gap from other carts that do not come from the Compact. Lord Wulfric signs the tally either way.
FX05-001.reputation: Patient, forest-proud and closer to the elves than the court likes.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Kettleden
members.note: He signs the yew tally as full every year and does not ask where the extra carts were cut.

members.role: Heir; yard-mistress of the yew stores
members.note: She can tell an elven stave from a green one by the sound it makes when struck, and she has started counting both.

members.role: Younger son; rides with the yew carts
members.note: He is in love with a half-elf carter's daughter and has learned the cart roads into the Eldergrove hills.

members.role: Wulfric's wife
members.note: She was born a Valens and prays to the Sun in the castle chapel while her husband's carters pray to the Halls.

famousDead: Stood witness for the crown when the Yew Compact was sealed at Brightkeep in 1012
FX05-001.secret: One stave in four that has passed the Kettleden tally since 1099 was cut from living elven yew by Master Tamsin Yewhurst's men, against the Compact.
hooks: An elven envoy arrives at Brightkeep to inspect the yard before the summer carts.
Elfa finds the green staves and must choose between her father and the Compact.

FX05-002.name: House Ravencrest
FX05-002.title: Knight-Banneret of Ravencrest
FX05-002.arms: a black boar on white, a red border

military.office: Knights of the Stag Downs border
military.unit: the Ravencrest lances, 25 knights and 200 rolled bowmen of the Stag Downs
military.ties: Ravencrest knights and their bowmen man the outposts south of Stagley and answer to the Lord Warden of the Stag Downs.

FX05-002.power: Ravencrest Keep and eight villages on the Varennan border of the Stag Downs.
FX05-002.history: Varennan border knights burned 14 villages in the Stag Downs in 893, and the survivors of Ravencrest built a keep on the ridge the next spring. The crown made their headman a knight, and the family has watched the border since. Ravencrest held through the Varennan siege of Stagley from May to September 1013 and rode with Queen Elsbeth's night march to the Brightwash the next year. Now they hunt Ashen cultists and bow smugglers in the Downs and wait for Varenna to come again.
FX05-002.reputation: Hard border knights who hate Varenna more than they love the king.

members.role: Head of the family; Knight-Banneret of Ravencrest
members.note: He wants the Varennans to come up the Palella, and he has said so at the Moot.

members.role: Heir; knight of the border outposts
members.note: He rode with Princess Rowena's 600 bowmen against the Ashen in 1102 and would die for her.

members.role: Aldred's daughter
members.note: She slips out at night to an Ashen altar in the Downs and has been given an ash-mark on her shoulder.

members.role: Aldred's wife; keeper of the keep
members.note: She runs the keep, the villages and the granary while the men ride, and suspects her daughter.

famousDead: Raised the keep after the burning of 893 and was knighted for it
FX05-002.secret: Aelfwyn Ravencrest has sworn to the Ashen, the cult her father hunts.
hooks: Hamo leads a raid on an Ashen altar and finds his sister there.
A Varennan knight sends Sir Aldred a challenge to single combat at the border stone.

FX05-003.name: House Thistlekeep
FX05-003.title: Knight of Thistlekeep
FX05-003.arms: a silver sword through a purple thistle, on black

military.office: Knights of the Ash
military.unit: a lance of the Knights of the Ash, 4 knights and 12 riders
military.ties: Thistlekeeps have ridden with the Knights of the Ash since Elsbeth's war, and one of them always serves among the 200 knights at court.

FX05-003.power: Thistlekeep Tower, two villages and a name for jousting that is worth more than its rents.
FX05-003.history: Sir Godric Thistlekeep scouted for Queen Elsbeth on her night march to the Brightwash in May 1014 and died in the ambush when she chased too far. His son was given Thistlekeep Tower in 1015 as a widow's pension that became a knighthood. The family has never been rich and has never missed a Return Day contest. In 1103 the heir won a wager of 4,000 embers from Princess Rowena on a horse race, and was paid.
FX05-003.reputation: Poor, brave, handsome and always at court.

members.role: Head of the family; Knight of Thistlekeep
members.note: He has mortgaged the tower twice to keep his sons in harness and calls it the price of honour.

members.role: Heir; Knight of the Ash at court
members.note: He won 4,000 embers from the princess in 1103 and knows she paid him out of the arrow-tax stores.

members.role: Corbin's daughter; Knight of the Ash
members.note: She was knighted at the Return Day contest of 1101 and is the better rider of the two.

members.role: Corbin's wife
members.note: She has hidden the winnings of 1103 in the tower well to pay the mortgage.

famousDead: Scouted Elsbeth's night march and died in the ambush after the Brightwash
FX05-003.secret: The 4,000 embers Merrick won from Rowena came out of the Bowmen's arrow-tax stores, and the Thistlekeeps could ruin the princess with one word.
hooks: Chancellor Hale's men ask Sir Merrick about a wager in 1103.
A Lunetti factor comes to Thistlekeep to call in the mortgage.

FX05-004.name: House Willowmarch
FX05-004.title: Lord of Willowmarch
FX05-004.arms: a silver wave under a willow branch, on blue

military.office: Lords of the Willowmarch levy
military.unit: the Willowmarch men-at-arms, 120, and 400 rolled bowmen of the Ashwater
military.ties: Their bowmen form a fifth of the Ashwater rolls, and their keep guards the barge road below Crowbrook.

FX05-004.power: Willowmarch Keep on the lower Ashwater, its quays and a share in the Crowbrook barges.
FX05-004.history: The Willowmarchs were river lords below Crowbrook whom Aldred Ashford bought with a copper share in 772. They lost their small toll with the Varleys' chain in 1016 and turned to barging Varennan wine upriver instead. Lord Oswy married a Varennan lady in 1085 and joined Lady Isolde Varley's River Party in 1104. His son wants the Kingsmere Match and says so at dinner.
FX05-004.reputation: Smooth, rich and half Varennan, say the yeomen, and they do not mean the wife.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Willowmarch
members.note: He takes a Varennan wine factor's pension and lodges his surveyors in the boathouse.

members.role: Oswy's wife, born in Varenna
members.note: She loves Ashmere more than her husband does and fears what her brothers will do with his letters.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He wants to serve in Prince Harald's wedding escort and has quarrelled with his father in front of the servants.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She has found a map of the Palella barge landings drawn in a Varennan hand in the boathouse.

FX05-004.secret: The 'wine surveyors' who lodge at Willowmarch are Varennan engineers mapping the barge landings for the Stagley stroke.
hooks: Linnet shows the Palella map to her brother.
A Varennan barge arrives at Willowmarch carrying no wine and forty men.

FX05-005.name: House Stonebridge
FX05-005.title: Knight-Banneret of Stonebridge
FX05-005.arms: a black gate under a grey arch, on gold

military.office: Captains of the Hawkmarch Road Wardens
military.unit: 500 of the 1,500 Hawkmarch Road Wardens, holding the upper pass
military.ties: Stonebridge spearmen guard the high road over the Ash Range for House Hawkmarch, and every mule-train on it passes their gate.

FX05-005.power: Stonebridge Keep at the head of the pass road and a share of the Hawkmarch tolls.
FX05-005.history: The Stonebridges were Hawkmarch sergeants who rode against Ashmere in the rising of 976 and broke on the gate Tobin Cinderwell held. At the Pardon of Harrowbrook in 977 King Cedric made the Hawkmarchs wardens of the road, and the Hawkmarchs made the Stonebridges keepers of its upper gate. They have kept it since and grown rich on mules. Since the 1080s some of those mules have carried war bows south to Varenna.
FX05-005.reputation: Mountain knights who ask few questions at their gate.

members.role: Head of the family; Knight-Banneret of Stonebridge
members.note: He keeps Lord Ranulf's tithe ledger on the bow smuggling in his own hand and burns each page after it is paid.

members.role: Heir; captain of the upper gate
members.note: She turned back a mule-train of bows last autumn and was told by her father to forget it.

members.role: Younger son; mule-master
members.note: He leads the bow mules over the pass in snow and has a Varennan girl in every village on the far side.

famousDead: Rode in the Hawkmarch rising of 976 and was made keeper of the upper gate in 977
FX05-005.secret: Stonebridge keeps the ledger of every load of war bows carried over the pass to Varenna, and Lord Ranulf Hawkmarch's tenth is written in it.
hooks: Svala is offered a captaincy in the King's Guard if she brings the ledger to Ashmere.
An Aldmark escort demands to pass Stonebridge gate before the wedding.

FX05-006.name: House Rooksett
FX05-006.title: Lord of Rooksett and Captain of the King's Galleys
FX05-006.arms: a black raven on white over two blue waves

military.office: Captains of the King's Galleys at Alderwick
military.unit: the twelve coastal galleys, 600 rowers and 200 marine bowmen
military.ties: Since the Varennan blockade of 1014 a Rooksett has commanded the only ships the crown owns.

FX05-006.power: Rooksett and the harbour of Alderwick, and command of Ashmere's twelve galleys.
FX05-006.history: After Varenna's galleys closed the Palella from 1014 to 1015 and nearly starved the kingdom, Queen Elsbeth gave a coastal knight, Hamo of Rooksett, twelve galleys and a lordship to keep the shore. The galleys have never fought a battle. In 1086 Lord Aelfric Rooksett married Helga Hale, sister of the man who became Chancellor, and the house has backed the Kingsmere Match since. Rooksett ships also bring goods for the court from Ostra that do not pass through Varennan customs.
FX05-006.reputation: The Chancellor's in-laws, and the Chancellor's errand boys.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Rooksett
members.note: He fetches the king's poppy syrup from an Ostran apothecary in his own galley, on his brother-in-law's order.

members.role: Aelfric's wife; sister of Chancellor Edmund Hale
members.note: She writes to her brother every week and reads his replies to nobody.

members.role: Heir; galley captain
members.note: Named for his uncle, he wants a sea fight with Varenna and has twelve galleys to lose it with.

members.role: Younger daughter; lady-in-waiting to Princess Rowena
members.note: Rowena trusts her, and she has begun to wonder what is in the bottles her father brings from Ostra.

famousDead: First Captain of the King's Galleys after the blockade of 1014
FX05-006.secret: Rooksett galleys carry the poppy that keeps King Edric quiet before every council, at the Chancellor's request.
hooks: The poppy runs short and Rooksett must send a galley to Ostra past Varennan waters.
Tamsin tells Rowena where her father's bottles come from.

FX05-007.name: House Leacester
FX05-007.title: Lord of Leacester

military.office: Lords of the Leacester levy
military.unit: the Leacester mine guard, 80 men, and 250 rolled bowmen of the Brightwash
military.ties: Their miners are excused the butts in winter and owe the crown double arrows instead.

FX05-007.power: The Leacester copper mine in the Brightwash hills, held under the crown's fifth.
FX05-007.history: Godric the Copper King opened the deep galleries of the Brightwash in the 850s and gave the Leacester workings to a gallery-master who found the first great vein. His line became lords and paid the crown its fifth of copper for 250 years. The vein grew thin in the 1090s and ran out in 1098. Lord Hesketh has paid the crown's fifth every year since without a pound of his own copper.
FX05-007.reputation: An old mining house that still seems to dig as much as ever.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Leacester
members.note: He buys Varennan copper ingots in secret and has them hammered into Brightwash bars at night.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She has gone down the mine and found the deepest gallery bricked up with fresh mortar.

members.role: Hesketh's father
members.note: He swears the vein is only resting and goes down every morning with a candle and a hammer.

famousDead: Gallery-master who found the Leacester vein and was made lord
FX05-007.secret: The Leacester mine has been dead since 1098; every bar it sends to the mint is Varennan copper bought through the Chapmans.
hooks: The crown's assayer notes that Leacester copper has changed colour.
Edda breaks through the bricked gallery.

FX05-008.name: House Valens
FX05-008.title: Keeper of the Royal Chapel
FX05-008.arms: a gold eight-rayed star on white
FX05-008.power: The lay keeping of the royal chapel, its plate, its relics and its locked chest, and the ear of the Luminary.
FX05-008.history: The Valens line descends from a Temple official of the Solen Ash March who stayed when the governors fled in 741. When Edwin I built the royal chapel inside Ashmere Castle in the 820s, he made a Valens its lay keeper, and the house has kept the chapel's keys since. They speak Old Solen at table and pray to the Sun. The royal chapel holds the king's copy of every treaty, and since March 1104 one of them has a clause the Chancellor has never seen.
FX05-008.reputation: Proud Temple courtiers who look down on the Common Halls and up at the Luminary.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Royal Chapel
members.note: He has read the king's copy of the wedding contract by candle in the vestry and has told only the Luminary.

members.role: Cassian's wife
members.note: She keeps a list of every courtier who goes to the Common Hall on Moot Green.

members.role: Heir; clerk of the chapel
members.note: He wants to be Luminary of Ashmere after Silvan Aurel and studies the Sun rite for the wedding.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She sneaks out to the Sunday butts to watch a yeoman bowman shoot, and once went into the Common Hall with him.

famousDead: First lay keeper of the royal chapel under Edwin I
FX05-008.secret: Cassian has read the hidden Ashmere clause in the king's copy of the wedding contract and has told Luminary Silvan Aurel.
hooks: Princess Rowena demands the chapel chest be opened at the Spring Equinox Moot.
Junia's yeoman is beaten on the Holmside by men in Valens livery.

FX05-009.name: House Blackwall
FX05-009.title: Lady of Blackwall

military.office: Lords of the Blackwall levy
military.unit: the Blackwall levy, 300 hedge spears and 150 bowmen
military.ties: Blackwall levies march under the Saltmoor banner and pay their arrow tax in sulfur as often as in arrows.

FX05-009.power: The sulfur pits of the Blackwall downs, which sell to wool-bleachers, vintners and buyers down the Palella.
FX05-009.history: The Blackwalls were ash-farmers who found yellow stone in the fumaroles of the Saltmoor downs in the 890s and were made lords for the crown's share of it. Sulfur bleaches wool, sweetens wine casks and kills sheep-scab, and the Blackwalls grew rich without a single good field. Their workers cough and die young, and the downs around the pits smell of rotten eggs. Since 1090 a Lucernan buyer has taken most of the yield at three times the old price.
FX05-009.reputation: Rich, sickly and smelling faintly of the pit.

members.role: Head of the family; Lady of Blackwall
members.note: She sells to the Lucernan buyer and has never asked why a merchant republic needs so much sulfur.

members.role: Hilda's husband; pit-master
members.note: His lungs are burned from thirty years in the pits and he whistles when he breathes.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He wants to sell to Varenna as well and has written to a Dorium factor without his mother's leave.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She keeps a box of yellow crystals and burns them to watch the blue flame.

FX05-009.secret: Blackwall sulfur goes down the Palella to the Arsenal of Lucerna, where it is mixed into something the Lucernans keep in a cellar and never name.
hooks: Ingram's letter to Dorium is read by the Chancellor's clerk.
A pit collapse brings the Ashen preachers to the miners' huts.

FX05-010.name: the Shafter family
FX05-010.title: Hundredman of the King's Bowmen
FX05-010.arms: a white arrow on royal red

military.office: Hereditary Hundredmen of the King's Bowmen
military.unit: a hundred of the King's Bowmen in royal red
military.ties: A Shafter has led a hundred of the King's Bowmen since Queen Elsbeth made it a paid company in 1021, and every Shafter child shoots at the King's Butts at seven.

FX05-010.power: Forty acres of free ash land, a hundredman's pay and the respect of every bowman at the Red Fletch.
FX05-010.history: Wat Shafter was one of the first 1,200 bowmen Queen Elsbeth put into royal red in 1021, and he won the first Return Day silver arrow at the King's Butts in 1025. His sons and grandsons have led a hundred of the King's Bowmen ever since. They have won the silver arrow nine times. In 1104 the vintenar Perrin Hollowell beat Wulfric Shafter by a finger's width, and the family has not forgiven the wind.
FX05-010.reputation: The proudest bowmen in Ashmere, and the hardest drill-masters.

members.role: Head of the family; Hundredman of the King's Bowmen
members.note: He counted the arrow-tax stores in 1103, found them 4,000 embers short, and signed them whole because the princess asked him to.

members.role: Heir; vintenar
members.note: He lost the silver arrow to Perrin Hollowell in 1104 and practises at the butts by lantern-light.

members.role: Godric's wife; fletcher
members.note: She fletches every arrow her men shoot and can tell a goose feather from a swan's by touch.

members.role: Younger son; deserter
members.note: He ran from the Ashen riots of 1102, was caught, and lost his two drawing fingers; he fletches with his mother now.

famousDead: Won the first Return Day silver arrow at the King's Butts in 1025
FX05-010.secret: Godric signed a false count of the arrow-tax stores in 1103 to cover the princess's wager debt.
hooks: The Return Day silver arrow of 1105 is shot at Kingsmere for the wedding, and Wulfric means to win it there.
Chancellor Hale orders a recount of the arrow-tax stores.

FX05-011.name: House Wynmore
FX05-011.title: Warden of the Cinder Watch
FX05-011.arms: an orange mountain on dark brown, a gold beacon at its peak

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of the Cinder Watch
military.unit: the Cinder Watch, 300 beacon men on Mount Cinder
military.ties: The Cinder Watch is the oldest company of the crown, and a Wynmore has commanded it since the first beacons were lit.

FX05-011.power: Ashwell Tower and the beacon posts on Mount Cinder, and the trust of every farmer of the upper Ashwater.
FX05-011.history: After Mount Cinder buried 30 villages in September 776, King Aldred set lookouts on the mountain with beacon fires, and gave their command to Wyn of Wynmore, whose family had dug itself out of the ash. In the spring of 862 the Watch gave three days' warning of a smaller ashfall, the upper Ashwater was emptied in time and no one died. The yeomen have trusted the Wynmores with their lives ever since. Since 1102 the mountain has steamed more than any warden alive has seen.
FX05-011.reputation: Sober, honest watchmen who sleep with their boots on.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Cinder Watch
members.note: He reported the mountain 'quiet' last autumn because the Chancellor asked for no alarms before the wedding.

members.role: Heir; master of the upper beacons
members.note: She measures the steam vents every morning and has filled a book with numbers that frighten her.

members.role: Younger son; beacon runner
members.note: He climbed into the crater on a dare in 1103 and came back with his boots smoking.

famousDead: First Warden of the Cinder Watch, set by King Aldred after the eruption of 776
FX05-011.secret: Hamo falsified the Watch's autumn report at the Chancellor's request; Mount Cinder is waking.
hooks: Merewyn lights the warning beacon on her own authority in the week of the wedding.
Ash falls on Ashwell Tower in April and the Warden's report says it is fog.

FX05-012.name: House Galefall
FX05-012.title: Captain of the Downs Riders
FX05-012.arms: a silver spear between two red horseshoes, on green
FX05-012.words: Ride the Downs, Hold the Downs

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Downs Riders
military.unit: the Downs Riders, 1,000 light horse hunting Ashen cultists, bow smugglers and Hael Hounds
military.ties: Galefall riders have patrolled the Stag Downs since the siege of Stagley in 1013 and serve the Lord Warden as his eyes.

FX05-012.power: A manor on the Galefall Downs and command of the only mounted company in the south.
FX05-012.history: During the Varennan siege of Stagley in 1013, a shepherd's son named Ingram rode through the siege lines four times with messages and was knighted for it. His heirs were given the Downs Riders to command and have hunted the Stag Downs ever since. In April 1099 they were first to find the two Varennan surveyors killed by Hael Hounds in the Ashlands, before Sir Godwin Ashdown came for the bodies. In August 1102 they rode with Princess Rowena against the Ashen rioters.
FX05-012.reputation: Hard-riding, quick-tempered and the best trackers in Ashmere.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Downs Riders
members.note: He took a roll of maps from the dead Varennan surveyors in 1099, read them, and burned them.

members.role: Heir; rider-captain
members.note: She rode at Rowena's side in 1102 and the princess calls her by her first name.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: A Hael Hound took his calf in 1101; he limps and breeds the riders' dogs instead.

members.role: Ingram's wife
members.note: She nurses wounded riders and secretly feeds an Ashen widow and her children in the next valley.

famousDead: Rode through the Varennan siege lines four times in 1013
FX05-012.secret: The surveyors' maps of 1099 marked every well in the Stag Downs and a road for an army; Ingram burned them and never told the Warden.
hooks: A Varennan agent asks Ingram whether he still has the maps.
Linnet Tinker comes to the Galefall manor asking for Ulric.

FX05-013.name: the Wainwright family
FX05-013.title: Master of the Arrow Wains
FX05-013.arms: a brown cartwheel on pale gold

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Arrow Wains
military.unit: the Arrow Wains, 300 men and 120 wagons
military.ties: When the bowmen march, the Wainwrights march behind them with 24 arrows from every hearth of the kingdom.

FX05-013.power: The Arrow Houses of Ashmere, Stagley and Brightkeep, where the arrow tax is stored, and the wagons that carry it to war.
FX05-013.history: Queen Elsbeth fixed the arrow tax at 24 arrows a hearth and needed someone to store and carry them. Dunstan the wainwright of Brightkeep built her the first arrow wagons in 1021, and his line has run the Arrow Wains since. A full war levy needs millions of arrows, and the Wainwrights count them in sheaves of 24. Since the long peace began the Arrow Houses have filled to the rafters, and some of what was in them has been sold.
FX05-013.reputation: Dull, careful, essential men whom no bowman thanks until the arrows run out.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Arrow Wains
members.note: He sold 40,000 old arrows from the Brightkeep Arrow House to Kingsmere merchants for the Gordush line.

members.role: Heir; wagon-mistress
members.note: She can harness an eight-ox wain in the dark and knows every rut on the road to Stagley.

members.role: Younger son; fletcher of the Arrow House
members.note: He fills the empty barrels in the Brightkeep Arrow House with straw and lays one sheaf on top.

famousDead: Built the first arrow wagons for Queen Elsbeth in 1021
FX05-013.secret: A third of the barrels in the Brightkeep Arrow House are straw under a single sheaf; the arrows went to Aldmark's Gordush line for silver.
hooks: Varenna marches and the Arrow Wains are ordered to Stagley with the Brightkeep stores.
An Aldmark captain on the Gordush writes to thank the Wainwrights for their arrows.

FX05-014.name: the Sawyer family
FX05-014.title: Sergeant of the South Wall

military.office: Hereditary Sergeants of the Stagley south wall
military.unit: a company of the Stagley garrison, 100 men on the south wall
military.ties: Sawyers have kept the south wall of Stagley since their forefather sawed the timbers that shored it in the siege of 1013.

FX05-014.power: A sergeant's warrant, a house in the wall-tower and the keys to the south gate.
FX05-014.history: In the Varennan siege of 1013, a carpenter named Wat Sawyer shored a breaking stretch of Stagley's south wall with timber under fire, and the crown gave him the wall to keep. His heirs have been its sergeants since. When King Edric raised new walls at Stagley in 1100, Hamo Sawyer worked beside the mason. He saw the cheap mortar go in and was paid to keep his mouth shut, as the Warden was.
FX05-014.reputation: Plain soldier-carpenters who know every stone of Stagley.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the South Wall
members.note: He took 30 embers from the mason in 1100 and has knocked on the hollow stretch of the south wall every night since.

members.role: Heir; hundredman of the garrison
members.note: He thinks his father's wall is the strongest in Ashmere.

members.role: Hamo's daughter
members.note: She married a Varennan deserter who now works as a carter on the Dorium road.

members.role: Youngest son; apprentice carpenter
members.note: He found that a crowbar goes into the south wall mortar like a knife into cheese.

famousDead: Shored Stagley's breaking south wall under fire in 1013
FX05-014.secret: Hamo knows exactly where Stagley's south wall is hollow, and so, through his daughter's husband, may Varenna.
hooks: Varenna's Stagley stroke comes up the Palella, and the south wall must hold.
Brand tells his brother about the crowbar.

FX05-015.name: the Draper family
FX05-015.title: Master of the Wool Market
FX05-015.power: The great wool hall of the Ashmere Wool Market and the clip of a hundred upland valleys bought before it is shorn.
FX05-015.history: When Queen Elsbeth recoined the ember at full weight in 1018, Varennan and Aldmark buyers began to pay for Ashmere wool in good silver, and a carter named Leofric Draper built a wool hall on the market square with the first of it. His heirs buy the clip of the uplands before shearing and sell it north and south. They back the Kingsmere Match, because Aldmark pays for wool in silver and Varenna pays in promises. They lend money to yeomen against their fields, which the Ashwater Charter was meant to forbid.
FX05-015.reputation: Rich, sober and holding paper on half the farms of the Crown Vale.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Wool Market
members.note: He lends to yeomen through a Lunetti factor so his own name is never on the bond.

members.role: Heir; buyer of the clip
members.note: She rides the upland valleys every spring with silver in her saddlebags and a contract in her teeth.

members.role: Younger son; delegate to the Yeomen's Moot
members.note: He sits for the wool towns at the Moot and does not know how many of his fellow delegates owe his father money.

famousDead: Built the great wool hall with the first full-weight embers
FX05-015.secret: The Drapers hold, through a Lunetti factor, the debts of about 400 Crown Vale yeomen, and could call in their fields in a bad year.
hooks: A bad harvest brings Draper bailiffs to a yeoman's door, and the village halls rise.
Osmund learns his vote at the Moot was bought with his father's bonds.

FX05-016.name: the Chapman family
FX05-016.title: Mistress of the Copper Road
FX05-016.power: Two hundred ox-carts on the copper road from the Brightwash hills to the Crowbrook barges.
FX05-016.history: When Queen Elsbeth chartered the Copper Guild of Mossreach in 1030, a Saltmoor carter named Brand Chapman won the contract to carry its bars to Crowbrook. His family has carried most of Ashmere's copper since. Since the Deep Gallery flooded in October 1103 and Leacester's vein failed, the Chapman carts have also carried Varennan copper upriver at night and down again by day as Brightwash bars.
FX05-016.reputation: Honest carters, everyone says, which is why no one checks their loads.

members.role: Head of the family; Mistress of the Copper Road
members.note: She keeps the real cart tallies in her head and the false ones in her ledger.

members.role: Heir; carter-captain
members.note: He leads the night carts and thinks they carry Guild copper the Guild wants hidden from thieves.

members.role: Gudrun's brother; factor at Crowbrook
members.note: He buys the Varennan ingots off barges at Crowbrook and drinks with Lady Varley's bargemen.

members.role: Gudrun's daughter
members.note: She noticed the Varennan lion stamped on the bottom of an ingot and asked about it at supper.

FX05-016.secret: The crown's copper fifth is now partly paid in Varennan copper smuggled up the Palella by Chapman carts.
hooks: Elswyth's question is overheard by a guest at supper.
Varenna closes the Palella, and the hidden copper stops coming.

FX05-017.name: the Bowyer family
FX05-017.title: Master of the Bowyers of Brightkeep
FX05-017.power: The Bowyers' Guild of Brightkeep, which makes most of the kingdom's war bows from the elven staves.
FX05-017.history: When the Yew Compact brought the first elven staves to Brightkeep in 1012, Queen Elsbeth gathered the bowyers of the kingdom into a guild beside the yew yard. The Bowyer family has led it since. A Brightkeep war bow, seasoned for three years, draws harder than any in the west. Since the elven carts began coming short in 1099 the Guild has been short of good staves and long on orders.
FX05-017.reputation: Master craftsmen whose bows win wars, and who never let anyone forget it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Bowyers
members.note: He has passed one bow in ten from short-seasoned Aldmark yew as elven work to fill the orders.

members.role: Heir; master bowyer
members.note: She is the best bowyer in Ashmere and breaks every bow she suspects across her knee.

members.role: Younger son; stave-buyer
members.note: He buys the green Aldmark staves at Kingsmere and has them stained to look seasoned.

famousDead: First Master of the Bowyers' Guild of Brightkeep
FX05-017.secret: One bow in ten from the Guild since 1100 is short-seasoned and may break at full draw.
hooks: A bowman's bow snaps at the King's Butts on a Sunday, and he swears it was new.
Aelfwyn finds a stained stave in her own workshop.

FX05-018.name: the Collier family
FX05-018.title: Gallery-Master of the Copper Guild
FX05-018.arms: a black hammer on copper red
FX05-018.words: Down Is the Only Way Up
FX05-018.power: The gallery-mastership of the Copper Guild of Mossreach, which runs the Brightwash galleries under the crown's fifth.
FX05-018.history: The Colliers were gang-masters in the Brightwash galleries when Queen Elsbeth chartered the Copper Guild in 1030, and they have held its gallery-mastership in five of seven elections since. They dug the Deep Gallery, the richest in the kingdom. In October 1103 it flooded and drowned nine men. The Guild has hidden the loss, paid the widows to stay quiet and told the crown the gallery is resting.

members.role: Head of the family; Gallery-Master
members.note: He wrote the nine drowned men into the rolls of other galleries and pays their widows from his own purse.

members.role: Heir; gallery surveyor
members.note: She believes the Deep Gallery can be pumped out with an Aldmark engine and has written to Kingsmere about it.

members.role: Edric's nephew; miner
members.note: His brother was one of the nine, and he wants the Guild to say so in the Common Hall.

FX05-018.secret: Nine men drowned in the Deep Gallery in 1103, and the Copper Guild has hidden it from the crown.
hooks: Garth stands up at the Common Hall and names his brother.
Gerda's Aldmark engine-master arrives and asks to see the Deep Gallery.

FX05-019.name: the Chanter family
FX05-019.title: Hall-Keeper of Alderwick
FX05-019.power: The village halls of the Alderwick coast, whose keepers and singers are Chanters or were trained by one.
FX05-019.history: A hall-singer named Aldith first kept the Alderwick hall about 900, when the Black Cough had killed half the coast's priests. Her line has given the western halls their singers and keepers since. When Hall-Keeper Gudrun Ashdown walked the Crown Vale against the Edict of the Halls in 1089, the Chanters walked the coast. They carry her letters to the Free Halls of the north by way of Highland crossbow captains who come to Alderwick for contracts.
FX05-019.reputation: Beloved in the villages, distrusted at court.

members.role: Head of the family; Hall-Keeper of Alderwick
members.note: She has sworn in her hall that Alderwick will never take a priest confirmed by an emperor.

members.role: Heir; hall-singer
members.note: He carries Gudrun Ashdown's letters sewn into his harp case.

members.role: Aldith's daughter; turned to the Temple
members.note: She took the Sun to marry a court clerk and her mother has not said her name since.

famousDead: Kept the Alderwick hall through the years after the Black Cough
FX05-019.secret: The Chanters carry Gudrun Ashdown's promise that Ashmere's halls will join the Free Halls of the north, which the crown could call treason.
hooks: Osric's harp case is searched at Ashmere's gate.
Sunniva's husband asks her to find out who carries letters north.

FX05-020.name: the Marcellin family
FX05-020.title: Lay Steward of the Sun Temple of Aldminster
FX05-020.arms: a gold sun on dark red
FX05-020.power: The stewardship of the Sun Temple of Aldminster and its estates, the largest Temple holding in Ashmere.
FX05-020.history: The Marcellins came up with the Solen governors of the Ash March and kept the Sun Temple of Aldminster's lands when the empire fell. They still use Old Solen names and keep the Temple's rent rolls in Old Solen. The Ashwater Charter of 798 made thousands of yeomen free on land the Temple says was once its own. Since 1095 the Marcellins have been finding old Solen land-grants in the Temple vault, and some of them are very fresh.
FX05-020.reputation: Learned, polished and greedy for land, say the yeomen.

members.role: Head of the family; Lay Steward of Aldminster
members.note: He is suing three yeoman villages in the king's court on the strength of a Solen grant he 'found' in 1101.

members.role: Heir; sun-sister of the Temple hospital
members.note: She nurses yeomen and Temple tenants alike and is ashamed of her father's lawsuits.

members.role: Younger son; archivist
members.note: He ages new parchment with smoke and tea and writes in a Solen clerk's hand better than any living clerk.

FX05-020.secret: Benedict Marcellin forges the 'old Solen grants' the family uses to claim yeoman fields for the Temple.
hooks: A yeoman village's case against Aldminster comes before the Privy Council.
A Scrivener clerk notices the ink on a 'Solen' grant smudges.

FX05-021.name: the Scrivener family
FX05-021.title: Keeper of the Counter-Seal Register
FX05-021.arms: a black key on parchment white
FX05-021.power: The chancery rolls of Ashmere and the register of every treaty counter-sealed by a Chancellor since 977.
FX05-021.history: After the Hawkmarch rising of 976, the Privy Council made a custom that no treaty sealed by the king binds the realm without the Chancellor's counter-seal. A chancery clerk named Osric was set to keep the register of counter-seals, and his line has kept it since. Every treaty Ashmere has made since 977 is entered there in Scrivener hands. The treaty Edric signed at Kingsmere in March 1104 is entered too, but the Kingsmere copy has one more numbered clause than the Ashmere one.
FX05-021.reputation: Ink-stained, dry and the only people at court who read everything.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Counter-Seal Register
members.note: He noticed the Kingsmere copy's clause numbers skip and has told no one, because no one has asked.

members.role: Heir; clerk of the register
members.note: She knows the counter-seal custom by heart and believes it could save the kingdom if anyone dared invoke it.

members.role: Younger son; clerk in the Chancellor's office
members.note: Chancellor Hale pays him to report what the old clerks talk about.

famousDead: First Keeper of the Counter-Seal Register after 977
FX05-021.secret: The Scriveners' register proves the 1104 marriage treaty was never counter-sealed, and that Aldmark's copy has a clause Ashmere's does not.
hooks: Princess Rowena summons the Keeper of the Register before the Spring Equinox Moot.
Edmer tells the Chancellor that his father has been counting clauses.

FX05-022.name: the Woodward family
FX05-022.title: Woodward of the Chasethwaite Glens
FX05-022.power: The woodward's right over the royal chase of the Chasethwaite glens, and three generations of quiet planting.
FX05-022.history: The Woodwards were royal yew-wardens in the northern forests when Ashmere still grew its own bow staves. The Black Cough of 916 killed half the yew-cutters, and the royal yew woods were cut afterwards without replanting until they were gone about 1000. The Woodwards were left to keep deer in empty woods. Since 1040 they have been planting yew in the high Chasethwaite glens from seed, poaching the king's deer to feed the planters.
FX05-022.reputation: Poor woodsmen and suspected poachers, said to be a little mad about trees.

members.role: Head of the family; Woodward of the Glens
members.note: He has planted 3,000 yews in the high glens and will die before the first is ready to cut.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She poaches the king's deer to feed the planters and has lost one finger to the punishment already.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He wants to sell the secret of the glens to the Bowyers' Guild before the crown seizes them.

famousDead: Planted the first secret yew grove in the Chasethwaite glens in 1040
FX05-022.secret: A hidden yew wood of 3,000 young trees grows in the high Chasethwaite glens; in twenty years Ashmere could make its own bows again.
hooks: Merrick brings a Bowyer stave-buyer up the glens.
A royal forester arrests Bryony for poaching and finds a seed bag on her.

FX05-023.name: the Marrow family
FX05-023.title: Pawn-Lender of the Wool Market
FX05-023.arms: a pawn-sign of three brass balls over a skull, on dun
FX05-023.power: A pawn shop on the Wool Market, a network of poachers and carters, and a ledger of everyone in Ashmere who has needed money quietly.
FX05-023.history: Tib Marrow came up from the Stag Downs in 1060 with nothing and opened a pawn counter on the Wool Market. He buys poached venison, stolen arrows and anything else, and sells bow staves south to Crowbrook carters who take them on to Varenna. That is treason. He has never been caught because half the court owes him money and the other half buys his venison.
FX05-023.reputation: A kindly old pawn-lender, to those who do not know better.

members.role: Head of the family; pawn-lender
members.note: He has bought a Varennan crossbow from a poacher and wants to know who is arming the Downs, before someone asks him.

members.role: Tib's daughter; keeps the pawn counter
members.note: She keeps the ledger of pawned plate and knows which noble wives have sold their jewels.

members.role: Tib's grandson; stave-runner
members.note: He runs bow staves to Crowbrook carters by night and wants to go over the pass with the Stonebridge mules.

FX05-023.secret: Tib's ledger lists every lord who has pawned plate with him, Lady Isolde Varley's steward among them, and a Varennan agent has offered to buy it.
hooks: A Varennan agent offers Tib 500 embers for his ledger.
Wulf is caught with staves and offers to name the Stonebridge mule-trains to save his drawing fingers.

FX05-024.name: the Tinker family
FX05-024.title: Keeper of the Gorsedon Altar
FX05-024.arms: a red serpent on ash grey, scratched on pots they mend
FX05-024.power: The trust of the Ashen faithful of the Stag Downs and the hidden altars where they meet.
FX05-024.history: The Tinkers are wandering pot-menders of the Stag Downs, and they have been since anyone can remember. They are also keepers of the Ashen, the secret mountain faith carried by the survivors of the Kingdom of Hael, buried under ash in 13 BR. They carry messages between hidden altars and know the way into the buried towns. On Ash Night 1094 their young men stormed the royal chapel with 200 ruined ash-farmers and broke on Sir Owain Cinderwell's door.
FX05-024.reputation: Harmless tinkers, say the villages, and lock their doors anyway.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Gorsedon Altar
members.note: She tends the altar under Buried Gorsedon and has marked a Ravencrest daughter with ash.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He fought at the chapel door on Ash Night 1094 and still has Cinderwell's shield-rim scar across his face.

members.role: Elswyth's granddaughter
members.note: She loves a lame Galefall boy who breeds the riders' dogs, and wants out of the faith.

famousDead: Led the storming of the royal chapel on Ash Night 1094 and was killed at the door
FX05-024.secret: A Varennan agent has offered the Tinkers fifty crossbows to raise the Downs before the wedding.
hooks: Crossbows arrive at the Gorsedon altar on a Varennan pack-mule.
Linnet tells Ulric Galefall where the altar is.

FX05-025.name: the Reeve family
FX05-025.title: Speaker of the Aldminster Moot-men
FX05-025.arms: a gold wheat sheaf on green, a red arrow across it
FX05-025.power: Three hundred acres of free ash land, the reeveship of twelve yeoman villages and a loud voice at the Yeomen's Moot.
FX05-025.history: Thurstan the Reeve cleared 40 acres of ash on the coast hills in 798 under the Ashwater Charter, and his line has been reeves of the villages around the Sun Temple of Aldminster ever since. They have sat in the Yeomen's Moot since Elsbeth made it meet every Spring Equinox, and in 1003 a Reeve marched with the 6,000 archers who saved her crown. Their fields lie next to the Temple's, and the Temple wants them.
FX05-025.reputation: Stubborn, free and proud of it, the very picture of an Ashmere yeoman.

members.role: Head of the family; Speaker of the Aldminster Moot-men
members.note: He has taken 200 embers from Lady Isolde Varley to delay the dowry tax vote and tells his villages he votes for the realm.

members.role: Thurstan's wife
members.note: She runs the farm and the village granary and does not know about the 200 embers.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She shoots at the butts every Sunday and beats most of the men, and means to fight the Temple's lawsuit in court.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He was offered a place in the King's Bowmen and stayed home to plough.

famousDead: Cleared the family's first 40 acres under the Ashwater Charter of 798
FX05-025.secret: Thurstan Reeve has taken Varley silver to delay the dowry tax at the Yeomen's Moot.
hooks: The Marcellins' forged grant claims the Reeve fields.
At the Spring Equinox Moot Thurstan must vote, with both Lady Varley and his daughter watching.

FX06-001.name: House Mossheart
FX06-001.title: Grove Elder of Mirlas
FX06-001.arms: three silver fish in a ring around a green heart, on lake grey

military.office: Captains of the Silara shore wardens
military.unit: the Mirlas grove wardens, 120 bows
military.ties: Mossheart heirs captain the grove wardens of the western lake shore, a part of the 4,500 Grove Wardens, and answer to the Moot through their elder.

FX06-001.power: The elder's seat of Mirlas in the Moot, the lake-shore groves of western Silara and the night fishing rights that Nimrael's kin held before the Parting.
FX06-001.history: When Nimrael the Grey Veil left Mirlas in 340, her kin's nets, boats and grove seat passed to the Mosshearts, the fisher family that had worked Lake Silara beside them for six centuries. It was a Mossheart, the elder Thandrel, who carried word of Taeros's unmarked mast-oaks to the Moot in the winter of 339, and the Mistwalkers have never forgiven it. The house took the elder's seat of Mirlas in 341 and has held it since, a family of night fishers without night eyes who learned to fish by lantern where Nimrael's kin needed none. Mossheart archers stood in the Clarora fog of 296 beside the woman they later shamed, and the house still sings her name at the Greening while it refuses to sing the Parting Song. In 1052 its boatmen rowed Queen Lucilla's envoy past the three otters he reported as a serpent, and the family tells the story at every feast. The Mosshearts speak for the Deep Root in the Moot and want an heir of pure elven blood.
FX06-001.reputation: Honest, stiff and long of memory: the family that told on Nimrael, and would do it again.

members.role: Head of the house; Grove Elder of Mirlas
members.note: He sat in the Moot of 1037 when the heir question was first raised and has voted against changing the law at every sitting since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Mirlas grove wardens
members.note: She saw Queen Ithrien walk the Mirlas shore with a half-elf at Leaf Fall 1103 and has told no one, not even her father.

members.role: Younger son; night fisher
members.note: He rows across the lake at night to meet an Eldergrove trader's daughter and would marry her if a Mossheart were allowed to say the word Silverbough.

members.role: Thandrel's granddaughter; the memory of the house
members.note: At 465 she is the oldest elf in Mirlas and still sings the whole Mossheart line back to the first boat, Taeros's name included.

famousDead: Carried word of Taeros's mast-oak sale to the Moot in 339.
Led the Mirlas archers in the Clarora Mist of 296.
FX06-001.secret: Thandrel did not only report the sale: his own son floated twelve of the unmarked oaks down the Calara for Taeros and was paid in Solen silver, which still lies under the elder's hall.
hooks: Laerwen must decide whether to tell the Moot what she saw on the Mirlas shore in 1103.
Rinan wants to marry into an Eldergrove ship-house.
If the buried Solen silver is found, the family that shamed Nimrael is shamed in turn.

FX06-002.name: House Oakshadow
FX06-002.title: Grove Elder of Lirthil
FX06-002.arms: the black shadow of an oak across a silver field
FX06-002.power: The Lirthil groves and the aurochs valleys on the western slope of the Tusk Hills, a seat in the Moot, and the right to host the royal hunt, which no queen has used since 1036.
FX06-002.history: The Oakshadows have been elders of Lirthil since King Caerion gave them the seat in 390, after their founder Aerlas planted the oak ring that still shades the grove hall. For six centuries the royal hunt rode out from their hall into the Tusk Hills, and in 900 it was an Oakshadow guide who showed licensed human fur traders the last grey stag men ever saw. In October 1036 Prince Caelan rode out from the same hall, and a black aurochs bull gored him in the hills below it. The elder Thaenor had chosen the valley, the Tusk Hills Watch had not reported the bull, and each family has blamed the other for 69 years. Queen Ithrien has not hunted since and has not sat at the Oakshadow table, and the house has slowly lost its voice in the Moot. Its young want the black bull's herd killed to the last calf, which the Keepers will not allow.
FX06-002.reputation: A proud old house that lost a prince and has been apologising badly ever since.

members.role: Head of the house; Grove Elder of Lirthil
members.note: He chose the valley in 1036 and has walked it every Leaf Fall since, looking for a bull that is long dead.

members.role: Heir; hunt-master of Lirthil
members.note: He has tracked the black herd's grandsons through three winters and keeps a spear for them that the Keepers have forbidden.

members.role: Velthir's daughter
members.note: She has fallen in love with a young ranger of the Deerpath line, the one family her grandfather will not have under his oaks.

members.role: Thaenor's wife; healer of the Lirthil grove
members.note: She reached Caelan a quarter hour before Merion Softhand did and has never said what the prince told her.

famousDead: Planted the oak ring of Lirthil and took the elder's seat in 390.
FX06-002.secret: Caelan's last words to Nimeth were a message for his son at Nimthil, and the house has never delivered it.
hooks: Velthir means to kill the black herd's bull in the spring, against the Keepers' ban.
Ithrael and a Deerpath ranger want to marry across the feud.
Nimeth still holds Prince Caelan's last message for Thalion Halfleaf.

FX06-003.name: House Silverbark
FX06-003.title: Grove Elder of Eridor and Counter of Leaves
FX06-003.arms: a silver birch trunk bearing a single gold leaf, on black
FX06-003.power: Eridor, the most peopled grove-land of the hills; eleven voices of the Eridor groves that vote as the elder votes; and the old office of Counter of Leaves, which tallies every vote of the Moot.
FX06-003.history: Since 391 a Silverbark has counted the leaves at the Moot: every voice drops an oak leaf, green for yes and brown for no, into a bark basket, and the Counter tallies them before the Eldest Keeper. The office came to the family when King Caerion was confirmed and the old counters of Evenglade were found to have miscounted by three leaves. Eridor's hill groves are the most peopled in the forest, and their eleven voices have followed the Silverbark elder for seven centuries. The house stayed out of the Sea Covenant quarrel, the Border War and the heir question, and grew strong by being needed by both sides. In 1105 Queen Ithrien means to force a vote at Leaf Fall, and both the Open Leaf and the Deep Root have come to Eridor with promises. Its elder has promised nothing, which is the most dangerous thing a counter can do.
FX06-003.reputation: Careful, courteous and impossible to read: everyone wants the Silverbarks, and nobody trusts them.

members.role: Head of the house; Grove Elder of Eridor; Counter of Leaves
members.note: He has counted 412 votes of the Moot and says he has never miscounted one, which is not true.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the bark baskets
members.note: She wants the Open Leaf to win, because a half-elf king would owe the counters everything.

members.role: Sylwen's son; ranger of the Eastern Edge
members.note: He fought on the Lost March under Calithil Lightfoot and says openly that the Moot should crown the elf who saved the forest, not a boy in Silverbough.

members.role: Orrelan's great-granddaughter; a child
members.note: At twenty she has learned to drop two leaves with one hand, and her great-grandfather has seen it.

famousDead: First Counter of Leaves; recounted King Caerion's confirmation in 391.
FX06-003.secret: Orrelan miscounted the Moot vote of 1037 by two leaves so that it would end in a tie and no vote on the heir would be recorded. Only his daughter Sylwen knows.
hooks: Both factions will try to buy Eridor's eleven voices before Leaf Fall 1105.
Mirandil wants his family to back Calithil Lightfoot as heir.
If the miscount of 1037 comes out, every Moot vote the Silverbarks counted is in doubt.

FX06-004.name: House Wrenwing
FX06-004.title: Warden of the Two Roads
FX06-004.arms: a silver cart-wheel under a brown wren, on green

military.office: Wardens of the Two Roads
military.unit: the road wardens of Aravel, 160 bows
military.ties: Their wardens walk every dwarven train from the mountain foot to the edge towns and answer to the Ranger-Captain for every cart.

FX06-004.power: The two roads by which dwarven carters may reach the edge towns, the count of honey and wax at the road-stone, and the trust of Irondeep's factors, who will deal with no other elves.
FX06-004.history: When the dwarves of the Iron Mountains became a kingdom in 610, the Moot gave the Wrenwings of Aravel the keeping of the two roads by which dwarven carters may come to the edge, and no others. The family has walked every iron train since, counting the carts at the road-stone and turning back any dwarf who strays a step toward the Heartwood. Wrenwings speak Holdspeech, which no other Moot family does, and three of them have stood as witnesses when Irondeep's factors weighed iron against honey on their own scales. In the hungry winter of 1088 the elder Celdor carried sixty carts of Sylvaran honey to the Deep Gate on credit, which the Moot never approved, and Queen Brynja has not forgotten it. The house fears what Aldmark's grip on Irondeep means for the oldest trade either people keeps. If Aldmark soldiers stand in the Iron Road forts, the Wrenwings will be the first elves to see them.
FX06-004.reputation: The elves the dwarves trust, which makes the Moot trust them a little less.

members.role: Head of the house; Warden of the Two Roads
members.note: He has eaten in the Deep Halls three times, more than any elf alive, and likes dwarven ale more than he admits.

members.role: Heir; captain of the road wardens
members.note: She speaks Holdspeech with a Dunheim accent and has asked the Moot twice for leave to see Irondeep's forges, which no elf may see.

members.role: Calawen's son; road warden
members.note: He has been swapping arrowheads with a young Copperbraid carter, which no warden is supposed to do.

famousDead: First Warden of the Two Roads; set the road-stone at the mountain foot in 615.
FX06-004.secret: The sixty carts of 1088 were honey from the Keepers' store at Evenglade, taken without the Moot's leave; the Wrenwings have been paying it back in secret, a cart a year, for seventeen years.
hooks: Aldmark soldiers may soon stand in the Iron Road forts the Wrenwings' carters pass.
Calawen wants to be the first elf to see a dwarven forge.
Irondeep owes the house sixty carts of honey and may pay in iron the Moot would rather not see.

FX06-005.name: the Deerpath line
FX06-005.title: Wood-Captain of the Tusk Hills Watch
FX06-005.arms: a black aurochs bull on a green hill under a silver sky

military.office: Wood-Captains of the Tusk Hills Watch
military.unit: the Tusk Hills Watch, 280 scouts
