military.ties: Every Deerpath child is put on the hill paths at fifty, and the Watch has had a Deerpath captain for 675 years; they report to the Ranger-Captain at Rinael, not to the Lirthil elders.

FX06-005.power: Command of the 280 scouts of the Tusk Hills Watch, the hill paths over King Laewen's grave and the grass of the Horde, and the count of every aurochs herd in the western valleys.
FX06-005.history: The Deerpaths have watched the Tusk Hills since 430, when King Caerion set a standing watch on the holy hills where King Laewen lies and where the grass of the orc clans begins. They count the aurochs herds, turn back orc herders who stray under the trees and keep the Peace of the Grass Line, which their songs say an ancestor carried to the clan-mothers in 1350 BR. In October 1036 Prince Caelan rode into the black bull's valley from the Oakshadow hall, and the Watch's captain Faenor Deerpath gave up his command the next spring and died on the hills in 1041. The family has never accepted that the fault was theirs, and it has not spoken to the Oakshadows since. In 1104 the Watch reported more orc riders on the grass below the hills than in any year since the Second Horde War, and nobody at Evenglade has answered.
FX06-005.reputation: Quiet, hard and patient, the best hill scouts in the forest and the worst guests at a feast.

members.role: Head of the line; Wood-Captain of the Tusk Hills Watch
members.note: He took the command his father laid down in 1037 and has never once let the Watch count a herd without walking the valley himself.

members.role: Heir; second of the Watch
members.note: She speaks enough of the orc tongue to trade salt with the herd-mothers below the hills, which the Moot does not know.

members.role: Aerwen's son; scout of the Watch
members.note: He is in love with Ithrael Oakshadow and has met her eleven times under the oak ring her grandfather's grandfather planted.

members.role: Eravan's mother; Faenor's widow
members.note: She kept her husband's tally slate from 1036, which shows the black herd in the right valley after all, and has never shown it to anyone.

famousDead: Captain of the Watch when Prince Caelan died; gave up his command in 1037.
FX06-005.secret: Thaliel's slate proves the Watch counted the black herd in the right valley in 1036, so the prince went where he had been told not to go. Showing it would clear the family and shame the dead prince.
hooks: Orc riders are gathering on the grass below the Tusk Hills.
Ilarion and Ithrael Oakshadow want to marry across the feud.
Thaliel's tally slate could end a 69-year feud, at the cost of the prince's good name.

FX06-006.name: the Mistbrook line
FX06-006.title: First Guide of the Greenmire
FX06-006.arms: a grey marsh harrier over green reeds, on black

military.office: Guides of the Greenmire
military.unit: the Greenmire Guides, 300 scouts
military.ties: Mistbrook guides know the bog paths no map shows, and no ranger company crosses the Greenmire without one walking ahead.

FX06-006.power: The bog paths of the Greenmire, which only Mistbrook guides walk at night, the old bog-iron pits, and command of the 300 Greenmire Guides at Falessa.
FX06-006.history: Before the dwarves came the Mistbrooks dug the soft bog iron of the Greenmire, the only metal the elves had, and when dwarven knives made it worthless about 1900 BR they kept the one thing left: they knew the bog. Since 200 the family has led the Greenmire Guides, who walk the marsh paths at Falessa, carry the Moot's messages across it in a night and let anyone who follows without leave find the soft ground. In the War of the Forest Edge a Mistbrook led a Solen column into the Greenmire in 299 and came out alone. The family's trouble in 1105 is its own: the exiles called the Rootless hide in the marsh, the guides know where, and some Mistbrooks are kin to them by marriage. The yew that goes south to Ashmere moves through the Greenmire on paths only a guide could have shown.
FX06-006.reputation: Silent marsh-folk whom the rangers need and do not like.

members.role: Head of the line; First Guide of the Greenmire
members.note: He can walk from Falessa to Silande in the dark without a pole and has done it with a wounded ranger on his back.

members.role: Heir; guide-captain
members.note: She married an exile's brother before the exile, and the Rootless still call her sister.

members.role: Saelis's son; guide
members.note: He has guided four loads of yew through the marsh for the Rootless and been paid in dwarf crowns he cannot spend.

famousDead: Led a Solen column of 600 into the Greenmire in 299 and walked out alone.
FX06-006.secret: Fenaril guides the Rootless's yew loads through the Greenmire, and his mother has known since the first load in 1102.
hooks: The rangers have asked the guides to lead them to the Rootless camps.
Fenaril's dwarf crowns will ruin him if a Keeper finds them.
Calithil Lightfoot wants the yew road shut before Ashmere's wedding in June.

FX06-007.name: the Stillwood line
FX06-007.title: Master of the Fire Wardens
FX06-007.arms: a silver felling axe between two green firs, on black
FX06-007.words: Cut so it does not burn.

military.office: Masters of the Fire Wardens
military.unit: the Fire Wardens, 800 axes and water-carriers
military.ties: They cut every firebreak the Keepers mark and are the only elves allowed to carry a felling axe into the Heartwood.

FX06-007.power: Command of the 800 Fire Wardens, the only felling axes in the Heartwood, and the work of the great firebreak of Evenglade.
FX06-007.history: After the Aeravel fire of 501 King Caerion gave Ilareth Stillwood, who had led the cutters of the 6 km break that saved the southern groves, the keeping of a standing company of fire-cutters. The Stillwoods have led the Fire Wardens since. They are the forest's axemen, the only elves who may carry a felling axe into the Heartwood, and they hate fire more than any other line. In 1103 Eldest Keeper Arannel marked 40 km of firebreak around Evenglade, the largest cutting in memory, and the Stillwoods have been cutting it since with 300 hired human edge-folk hauling the deadwood. The work has made them unpopular in every grove it passes, and the family's heir has begun asking the Keepers what precedent allowed it.
FX06-007.reputation: Grim axemen who are thanked in dry summers and cursed in wet ones.

members.role: Head of the line; Master of the Fire Wardens
members.note: He has cut more living trees than any elf in Sylvaran's history and dreams of each of them.

members.role: Heir; captain of the firebreak works
members.note: She has asked Arannel three times for the precedent that allows a cutting of 40 km and been told three times that it exists.

members.role: Elisael's son; axeman of the firebreak
members.note: He drinks with the human haulers from Calandor and has a Coppice girl's ribbon tied inside his sleeve.

famousDead: Led the cutters of the 6 km firebreak that saved the southern groves in 501.
FX06-007.secret: In 1104 Elisael found an old Keeper's bark tally in a hollow oak on the firebreak line recording a great burning by the Keepers' own hand. She has hidden it and told no one.
hooks: The firebreak must be finished before the summer drought.
Elisael holds a tally that could reveal the Year of Ash Trees.
Laeros wants to marry a human hauler's daughter.

FX06-008.name: the Longshade line
FX06-008.title: Master Stand-Wright of the Edge
FX06-008.arms: a green bow strung across a tree's crown, on grey

military.office: Stand-Wrights of the Edge
military.unit: the tree-stand posts of the Rangers of the Edge, 600 bows
military.ties: Every hidden stand over every road that crosses the Oak Line was built or rebuilt by a Longshade, and only the family and the Ranger-Captain hold the full list.

FX06-008.power: The knowledge of every hidden tree stand along 1,900 km of the Oak Line, and the 600 rangers trained to man them.
FX06-008.history: The Longshades built the first hidden stands over the roads into the forest after the Treaty of the Oak Line in 302: platforms of living branches 12 m up that a man walking beneath cannot see. They have built and moved them since, and every stand-ranger of the Edge is trained in the family's yard at Erilas. Through the night of 23 September 1078 and the Lost March of 1079 the stands were the rangers' great weapon, and Aldmark found not one. The family's head keeps the only full list outside Rinael Hall, cut in a code of notches on a staff. In 1105 the Ranger-Captain's watchers fear that the list has been sold to Aldmark's spymistress, and the Longshades have been ordered to move a third of the stands before spring.
FX06-008.reputation: Craftsmen of the invisible; nobody knows their work, which is how they like it.

members.role: Head of the line; Master Stand-Wright of the Edge
members.note: He can find a stand he built 200 years ago in the dark by the feel of the bark.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the notch-staff
members.note: She keeps the notch-staff on her body day and night and has not slept in a bed since 1103.

members.role: Liriel's nephew; once a stand-ranger
members.note: He left the Edge in 1099 after a quarrel and now guides human hunters at Foxhurst, and he knows where a hundred stands are.

members.role: Liriel's daughter
members.note: At seventeen she has already found three stands her own mother did not know.

famousDead: Built the first hidden stand over the Clarora road in 303.
FX06-008.secret: Elthas sold the positions of nine stands to an Aldmark hunter in 1103 for a pouch of silver and has not told his family which nine.
hooks: A third of the Edge stands must be moved before spring.
Elthas must decide whether to confess the nine stands he sold.
The notch-staff is the most valuable object in the forest to Aldmark's spies.

FX06-009.name: the Thrushsong line
FX06-009.title: Keeper of the Seed-Store at Thalandor
FX06-009.arms: a gold bell hung from an oak bough, on green
FX06-009.power: The seed-store of the First Oak at Thalandor, the only nursery of saplings grown from its acorns, and the respect owed to an old Keeper line in the Moot.
FX06-009.history: The Thrushsongs have been Grove Keepers since before the count, and since the Fifth Oak was planted in 94 they have kept the seed-store at Thalandor, where acorns from each year's mast of the First Oak are sown in a hidden nursery against the day it falls. Every First Oak has been grown from the acorns of the one before, and the Thrushsongs keep the saplings that would be planted. The Fifth Oak is now about 1,010 years old, older than the Second or the Fourth when they fell. Since 1101 the store's saplings have died in their second year of a black rot in the root, and the head of the line has told only the Eldest Keeper. The family sings the Thrush Song at every planting, a song older than the Leaf Records, and believes the forest burns not when the last Oakborn dies but when the last acorn fails.
FX06-009.reputation: Gentle, devout and frightening when roused; the Keepers who keep the Keepers' tree.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Seed-Store
members.note: She has sown 1,011 years of acorns, counting back through her mothers, and has lost the last four years' saplings to a rot she cannot name.

members.role: Heir; Keeper of the Thalandor groves
members.note: He believes the rot came in on human haulers' boots from the firebreak and wants every edge-folk license burned.

members.role: Saerion's daughter; novice Keeper
members.note: She has secretly carried three healthy saplings to Naeris Seedfall's garden, where they thrive, and does not know why.

famousDead: Sang the Thrush Song at the planting of the Fifth Oak in 94.
FX06-009.secret: The seed-store has had no living sapling of the First Oak's line since 1101. If the Fifth Oak falls this year, there is nothing at Thalandor to plant.
hooks: The First Oak's saplings are dying and the Moot does not know.
Saerion wants the human edge-folk sent out of the forest.
Vaelis's saplings live in a commoner's garden, and that garden may hold the forest's future.

FX06-010.name: the Elmwhisper line
FX06-010.title: Keeper of the Second Copy
FX06-010.arms: a silver key on an elm leaf, on brown
FX06-010.power: The second copy of the Leaf Records, kept in the dry limestone caves of Syleron, and the right to copy each year's leaves from the Chronicler at Evenglade.
FX06-010.history: Queen Elunwe began the Leaf Records about 3800 BR, and the Keepers soon ordered a second copy kept far from Evenglade in case of fire. In 94, after the Fourth Oak fell, the copy was moved to the dry limestone caves of Syleron and given to the Elmwhispers, who have made it since, copying each year's leaves from the Chronicler's bark sheets onto their own. In 1063 their copy of the Grove Count was the one Faelwen the Chronicler checked before she answered the Needle-Keeper Serra. The family copies everything, including the entries the Moot never hears read, and its caves hold the Year of Ash Trees as the Keepers first wrote it. Since 1104 a half-elf trader from Eldergrove has come to Syleron twice asking to see the Grove Count, with Eldergrove silver in his pack.
FX06-010.reputation: Ink-stained, shy and scrupulous; the forest's memory, and its spare one.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Second Copy
members.note: He was born the year Ithrien was crowned and has copied every year of her reign in the same brown ink.

members.role: Heir; copyist
members.note: She has read the Year of Ash Trees entry and believes the Moot should hear it before it allows another cutting.

members.role: Eriwen's son; apprentice copyist
members.note: He took a gift of Eldergrove paper from the half-elf trader and has shown him the cave door.

famousDead: Copied the Keepers' first account of the Year of Ash Trees in 1410 BR.
FX06-010.secret: The second copy holds the Year of Ash Trees in full, copied before the Keepers wrote the false version they read to the Moot.
hooks: An Eldergrove trader wants the Grove Count and will pay well for it.
Eriwen wants the Year of Ash Trees read to the Moot before the firebreak is finished.
Caerdil has shown a stranger the cave door.

FX06-011.name: the Barkwright line
FX06-011.title: Master Boatwright of Rineron
FX06-011.arms: a brown mallet over a sewn bark boat, on river blue
FX06-011.power: The boat sheds of Rineron, which build nearly every one of the forest's 200 river boats, and the trust of the Calara and Silara Boatmen.
FX06-011.history: The Barkwrights have built the bark and plank boats of the Calara since the Moot let the river elves carry goods by water, and nearly every one of the forest's 200 boats came from their sheds at Rineron. Their boats are sewn with spruce root and sealed with pitch, and they carry rangers, honey and the Moot's messengers down the river and across Lake Silara. In 340 half the family walked down the Calara behind Nimrael, and the half that stayed swore never to build a keel that could cross the sea. The oath has held for 765 years. In 1098 the eldest son, Faerion, left for Nimthil, and he now lays keels in an Eldergrove yard.
FX06-011.reputation: Good craftsmen and better grudge-keepers; every boatman of the Calara owes them a boat.

members.role: Head of the line; Master Boatwright of Rineron
members.note: He has built 140 boats and named every one after a tree that fell.

members.role: Eldest son; shipwright at Nimthil
members.note: He sends his father a carved keel-peg every Leaf Fall, and his father burns it.

members.role: Daughter; heir to the sheds
members.note: She is building a boat in the back shed with a keel two hands deeper than her father's oath allows.

famousDead: Refused to follow Nimrael in 340 and swore the family's oath against sea keels.
FX06-011.secret: The oath was sworn after Vaeros lost the first shipwright's place to Tarael Greywave, not for the Covenant's sake, and the old sheds still hold the plans Vaeros drew for a sea keel.
hooks: Ilarwen's deep-keeled boat will break the family oath when it floats.
Faerion has asked his father to send Rineron spruce root to Eldergrove's yards.
The Calara boatmen will need forty new boats if Aldmark comes.

FX06-012.name: the Beechlight line
FX06-012.title: Warden of the Grey Stags
FX06-012.arms: a grey stag with antlers spread wide under a beech, on gold
FX06-012.words: One a year, and no more.
FX06-012.power: The keeping and count of the grey stags, the right to bring the Moot its one stag a year under King Thalorn's rule, and the deep valleys of Eriavel where no one else hunts.
FX06-012.history: Since 410 the Beechlights have kept the grey stags of the Evenwood, the giant deer with antlers wider than a man is tall that King Thalorn ruled the Moot could take only once a year. Each Greening the family brings one stag's antlers to Evenglade, and each Leaf Fall it gives the Moot a count. Humans have not seen a grey stag since 900, and most of the Known World believes them gone. The Beechlights say there are sixty in the deep valleys of Eriavel and Lirthil, and the Moot has never sent anyone to count behind them. Keepers who ask to see the herd are led in circles for a week and sent home happy.
FX06-012.reputation: Shy, gentle folk who know the deep valleys better than anyone and never invite company.

members.role: Head of the line; Warden of the Grey Stags
members.note: He has brought the same three sets of antlers to Evenglade in turn for fifty years, and nobody has noticed.

members.role: Heir; stag-tracker
members.note: She knows each of the last stags by name and has stood within a hand of the old bull called Thalorn's Crown.

members.role: Aelora's son
members.note: He wants to bring a living calf to the Moot so the forest will believe, and does not understand why his grandfather forbids it.

famousDead: Raised an orphaned grey stag calf in the Eriavel hall in 650.
FX06-012.secret: There are nine grey stags left, not sixty, and the Beechlights have taken none for the Moot since 1052. The antlers at every Greening are old ones from the family's store.
hooks: A Keeper is coming to count the grey stags herself.
Elandil plans to bring a living calf to Evenglade.
An Aldmark lord has offered a fortune for grey stag antlers at the Rinael edge-fair.

FX06-013.name: the Rootless of the Greenmire
FX06-013.title: Eldest of the Rootless
FX06-013.arms: no arms; they mark their caches with a cut root burned into bark
FX06-013.power: About forty exiles on the marsh islands of the Greenmire, a yew road south to human buyers, and the silence of guides who are their kin.
FX06-013.history: Cutting a living tree without a Keeper's mark costs an elf a hundred years of exile and the name of the line, and since 1013 the exiles who would not leave the forest have gathered in the Greenmire marsh of Silande. Their founder, a yew-cutter of Lirith called Saeros, cut twelve yews for a dwarven bowyer in a hungry year and refused to go. About forty exiles and their children live on the marsh islands on eels and stolen honey, and the guides of the Greenmire pretend not to see them. Since 1102 they have cut yew in the dry hills above the marsh and floated the staves south to human buyers on the Ashmere road. The rangers could clear them out in a season if the Moot gave the word, and the Moot has taken three years to discuss it.
FX06-013.reputation: To the Moot, a shame; to the edge-folk, the only elves who will trade without a Keeper watching.

members.role: Head of the exiles; once a yew-cutter of Lirith
members.note: He has eight years of his hundred left and says he will cut yew until the last day of them.

members.role: His daughter, born in exile
members.note: She has never had a line name and has never stood on dry ground in the Heartwood, and she wants both.

members.role: An exile of 1060
members.note: He lit a cooking fire in the deep forest in a dry August and burned two acres, and the Rootless are the only people who will eat with him.

FX06-013.secret: Their yew goes south through the Greenmire on paths a Mistbrook guide shows them, and the buyer at the other end is an agent of Ashmere's bowyers.
hooks: The rangers may be ordered to clear the Greenmire.
Sennara wants a line name and would trade her father's yew road for one.
Saeros's exile ends in 1113, and the Keepers have not decided whether his name comes back.

FX06-014.name: the Coppice family
FX06-014.title: Master of the Calandor License
FX06-014.arms: a brown hand holding a bundle of sticks bound in green, on buff
FX06-014.power: The Moot's license for the 300 human haulers of the Evenglade firebreak, a leased clearing at Calandor, and the goodwill of the Fire Wardens.
FX06-014.history: The Coppices came to the forest edge at Calandor in 925, when Queen Ithrien reopened the edge after the Black Cough and licensed a few human families to gather deadwood and carry loads the elves would not. Humans may not own land in Sylvaran, so the family has leased the same clearing from the Calandor grove for 180 years and renewed its license every decade at the Moot's pleasure. In 1103 Eldest Keeper Arannel's firebreak made them rich by edge-folk standards: the Coppices hold the license for the 300 human haulers who drag the deadwood out of the 40 km cut, and they are paid in grain, honey and salt. They speak Sylvari well and Northfolk at home, and three generations have buried their dead outside the Oak Line. In 1105 their license comes before the Moot for renewal, and the Thrushsong Keepers want every human license burned.
FX06-014.reputation: Hard-working edge-folk whom the elves rely on and will not let stay after dark.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Calandor License
members.note: He has hauled for elves for forty years and is still not allowed under the trees after dark.

members.role: Heir; tally-keeper of the haulers
members.note: She keeps the haulers' tallies in Sylvari script, which no elf taught her, and the Fire Wardens quietly use her figures.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: She has given a ribbon to a young elf of the Fire Wardens and does not know that a half-elf child could never own land in Sylvaran.

members.role: Wulfric's elder brother; the black sheep
members.note: He was caught snaring a hare under the trees in 1070, lost his license and now lives across the line at Foxhurst, selling forest gossip to Aldmark buyers.

famousDead: Won the first deadwood license at Calandor in 925.
FX06-014.secret: Osmund sells what his brother hears at the firebreak to an Aldmark spy at Foxhurst, and Wulfric has taken a share of the silver.
hooks: The Moot will rule on the human licenses in 1105.
Tamsin and a Stillwood axeman are in love, and their child would own nothing.
Osmund wants to come home and will pay with a secret.

FX07-001.name: House Brightkeel
FX07-001.title: Ship-lord of Nimion
FX07-001.arms: a gold anchor under three silver stars, on sea green

military.office: Captains of three longships of the queen's fleet
military.unit: three longships, 180 Sea-Archers
military.ties: Every Brightkeel heir captains a longship for the Fleet-Warden for ten years before taking a cog.

FX07-001.power: Six trading cogs out of Nimion, three longship crews owed to the fleet, and the Nimion herring and slate trade to Greyhaven.
FX07-001.history: The Brightkeels have built and sailed cogs out of Nimion since 560, when Queen Ilvara the Elder let a second ship-house open on the coast so the realm would not hang on one family's hulls. Every Brightkeel ship carries a strip of bright copper along its keel, a trick learned from the dwarven masons who raised the Nimthil towers in 620, and the house has lost fewer ships to worm than any other. They have always been second to the Greywaves: second to carry masts, second to carry grain, second at court. In 1098 three Greywave cogs went down near the Strait of Hael, and the house has watched Tavor Greywave borrow from Ostra with something close to joy. In 1105 the Brightkeel head is quietly asking an Ostran factor what House Lunetti would take for its note on nine Greywave cogs.
FX07-001.reputation: Able, rich and jealous: the ship-house that has been second for five hundred years and is tired of it.

members.role: Head of the house; Ship-lord of Nimion
members.note: He has never forgiven Queen Lithiel for giving the grain right to her father's house, and he says so to anyone who has had two cups.

members.role: Heir; captain of the longship Copper Fir
members.note: She rowed through the gale of 1089 beside Elandor the Steady and is the only Brightkeel the Greywaves respect.

members.role: Younger son; factor at Ostra
members.note: He carries his father's offer for the Lunetti note and has run up debts of his own in the Ostran dice halls.

famousDead: First ship-lord of Nimion; died fighting the noon raiders at Ithira.
FX07-001.secret: Caeros has agreed to carry the Temple's envoy north in March on a Brightkeel cog, for Temple gold, and has not told the queen who the passengers are.
hooks: If the Lunetti note is sold to Brightkeel, nine Greywave cogs change houses.
Aelira must choose between her father's bargain and her oath to the fleet.
Navarel's Ostran debts make him easy to buy.

FX07-002.name: House Stormleaf
FX07-002.title: Grove Elder of Mirandor
FX07-002.arms: a grey bend like a gust of wind across a silver leaf, on dark green
FX07-002.power: The hill groves of Mirandor, a voice on the Council of the Grey Veil, and the leadership of the Return to the Root among the grove elders.
FX07-002.history: The Stormleafs walked down the Calara with Nimrael in 340 and took the hill groves of Mirandor, where there was no sea to see and no fir worth a keel. For 765 years they have been the realm's inland conscience, a family of hazel and walnut planters who sing the Parting Song with dry eyes. They opposed the first yew sale to Ashmere in 776, the grave-keels and the mast trade, and lost every vote. When Nerys the Sea Keeper founded the Return to the Root in 1081, after Aldmark's loggers crossed the Oak Line, the Stormleaf elder was the first to stand beside her. In 1105 Nerys means to refuse the Keeper's mark to the Yew Ridges, and Mirandor's voice on the council is the one she is counting on.
FX07-002.reputation: Earnest, plain-living and tiresome; right more often than the council likes to admit.

members.role: Head of the house; Grove Elder of Mirandor
members.note: He has wanted to see the First Oak for 285 years and has never been allowed past the Oak Line's edge towns.

members.role: Heir; voice of Mirandor on the council
members.note: She has argued against the Yew Compact at every council since 1012 and lost each time by one voice.

members.role: Coriel's son; the one who went back
members.note: He left for Sylvaran in 1081, was refused a birth tree by the Keepers of Evenglade and now lives as a guest at Mirlas, which no Stormleaf will speak of.

famousDead: Keeper who walked with Nimrael and wept at the first grave-keel in 470.
FX07-002.secret: Taldris writes to his mother from Mirlas, and the Mosshearts of Sylvaran have offered the Stormleafs a seat in the Moot if they bring Mirandor's groves back under the Oak Line.
hooks: Mirandor's voice may decide whether the Yew Ridges get the Keeper's mark.
The Mosshearts of Sylvaran have offered the house a way home.
Taldris wants a birth tree he can never have.

FX07-003.name: House Heronshore
FX07-003.title: Warden of the West Strand
FX07-003.arms: three silver waves under a green fir, on blue

military.office: Wardens of the West Strand
military.unit: 40 forest wardens beside the West Strand Watch
military.ties: The house's wardens guide the 200 of the West Strand Watch through the forest and answer to its captain in war.

FX07-003.power: The fir forests of the West Strand, the finest keel timber on the Elder Coast, and the yearly count of every stump cut there.
FX07-003.history: Queen Aerdis gave the West Strand to Saelor Heronshore about 450, when the chart-makers found that its tall straight firs made the best keels on the coast. The house keeps the forest, walks the Sea Keepers through it at every marking and counts the stumps each autumn. For six centuries a West Strand keel has been the mark of a good ship. In 1101 smugglers were found cutting unmarked fir on the strand, and Ilvara Mistwalker's night landing burned their camp while the Heronshore wardens slept a day's walk away. The council has asked how the cutters worked a whole season unseen, and the house has no good answer.
FX07-003.reputation: Old forest lords who have started to look tired, or bought.

members.role: Head of the house; Warden of the West Strand
members.note: He has counted the strand's stumps every autumn for 180 years, and since 1099 his count has been wrong on purpose.

members.role: Heir; forest warden
members.note: She found the smugglers' saw-pits in the spring of 1101 and was told by her father to wait.

members.role: Iselor's grandson
members.note: He carries the house's silver to a money-changer in Ithira and has started skimming it.

famousDead: First Warden of the West Strand.
FX07-003.secret: Since 1099 Iselor has let Saltleaf-hired cutters take unmarked fir from the strand for Brannoc's yard and taken their silver for it. When the Driftleafs began cutting the same groves without paying, he sold their camp to the Night Rangers.
hooks: Taelis must decide whether to tell the council what her father did.
The council has ordered a new count of the West Strand stumps.
The smugglers burned in 1101 want the name of whoever sold them.

FX07-004.name: House Moonwake
FX07-004.title: Grove Elder of Falavel
FX07-004.arms: a silver crescent moon over a white wake, on deep blue
FX07-004.power: The hill groves of Falavel, the oldest half-elf grove seat in the realm, and the loyalty of the half-elf families of the fjord towns who see the house as theirs.
FX07-004.history: When Queen Serewen made every child of the Veil a citizen in 344, one of the first so counted was a fisher's son of the coast villages named Orael Moonwake. His descendants have married elves and humans in every generation and have farmed the hill groves of Falavel since 590, when Queen Ilvara the Elder made a Moonwake an elder, the first half-elf to hold a grove seat. The family is proud, poor and very old by half-elf reckoning: eleven generations against the two or three of an elven house. It has always held that the Half-Elf Speaker's seat on the council should go to a landholding line, not a merchant one. Since Corin Saltleaf took the seat in 1090, the Moonwakes have voted against him on everything.
FX07-004.reputation: The half-elves' old nobility, prickly about their dignity and short of silver.

members.role: Head of the house; Grove Elder of Falavel
members.note: At 93 she looks fifty and has outlived the patience of two elven husbands.

members.role: Heir; her son by an elven sealer
members.note: He wants the Half-Elf Speaker's seat and has been counting the half-elf votes of the fjord towns since 1101.

members.role: Raelan's daughter; pupil of the Dusk School
members.note: She was taken into the Dusk School last winter, and her family does not know why the Mistwalkers chose her.

famousDead: One of the first half-elves counted a citizen under Serewen's law of 344.
FX07-004.secret: Orael was not a fisher's son but the child of a Mistwalker kinsman of Queen Serewen and a human net-maker, and the house keeps a grey veil-pin that proves it. Selwen's eyes shine in lamplight.
hooks: Raelan means to take the Half-Elf Speaker's seat from Corin Saltleaf.
Selwen may carry the Mistwalker night sight, and the lamp test would show it.
The veil-pin, if real, makes the Moonwakes kin to the queen.

FX07-005.name: House Longwake
FX07-005.title: Captain of the Grey Gull
FX07-005.arms: a black longship under a grey gull, on white

military.office: Hereditary captains of the longship Grey Gull
military.unit: the Grey Gull's crew, 60 Sea-Archers
military.ties: A Longwake has captained the same longship's crew since the Forty Ships were launched in 350, through eleven hulls, and the Sea-Archers' Yard counts the crew as the family's own.

FX07-005.power: The captaincy of the Grey Gull and the loyalty of its 60 archers, most of them sons and daughters of the crew before.
FX07-005.history: When Tarael Greywave launched the Forty Ships in 350, the ninth was given to Faelor Longwake and his 60 archers, and a Longwake has captained that crew since. The ship has been rebuilt eleven times and always called the Grey Gull; its keels have been cut from the graves of its captains, so the family says it sails on its own dead. Longwake crews fought the noon raiders off Ithira in 611 and shot pirates off the West Strand in 1031. In the October gale of 1089 the Grey Gull was the crippled ship Elandor kept rowing and bailing until it was towed home, and the family owes him a debt it has never been able to pay. The captain's heir has never fought well from a deck, and the crew knows it.
FX07-005.reputation: Proud deck-archers with a ship full of ghosts and an heir nobody wants.

members.role: Head of the house; Captain of the Grey Gull
members.note: He has stood on the Grey Gull's deck for 160 years and walks on land like a man on a pitching ship.

members.role: Heir; first archer of the Grey Gull
members.note: He shot well at the butts for a century and froze on the deck the one time a pirate came alongside, in 1088.

members.role: Calor's niece; deck-archer
members.note: She is the best deck-archer the crew has had in a century, and the crew would rather follow her than her uncle.

famousDead: First captain of the Grey Gull, the ninth of the Forty Ships.
FX07-005.secret: Calor froze on deck in 1088 and a crewman died for it; Aeldor told the Fleet-Warden the man fell.
hooks: The crew may refuse to sail under Calor at Sea Opening.
Ysael wants a captaincy that has never passed to a niece.
The family owes Elandor the Steady a ship's worth of lives.

FX07-006.name: House Mistsail
FX07-006.title: Second of the Mistwood Night Rangers
FX07-006.arms: a silver owl over a grey mist, on dark green

military.office: Hereditary seconds of the Mistwood Night Rangers
military.unit: the day watch of the Mistwood Night Rangers, 120 of the 500
military.ties: The Mistsails keep the day watch, the stores and the roads of the Mistwood for the Mistwalker ranger kin who lead the Night Rangers in the dark.

FX07-006.power: The day watch of the Mistwood roads, the ranger stores of Aerdor and the trust of three generations of Mistwalker captains.
FX07-006.history: Queen Aerdis founded Aerdor in 431 in the valleys where mist lies every morning, and she gave the day keeping of its rangers to Tamrel Mistsail, who had fought in the Clarora fog of 296. The Mistwalker ranger kin lead the Night Rangers in the dark; the Mistsails run everything else, the stores, the road posts and the watch while the carriers sleep through the glare. In 702 a Mistsail married a woman of the Mistwalker ranger kin, and since then about one Mistsail child in five has been born with eyes that shine in lamplight, though never as well as a true carrier. The family escorts every courier on the Mistwood road, and on 9 April 1067 a Mistsail rode beside Taeron Windward when he shot the Temple agent below Aerdor. In 1105 the Temple's knight is coming, and the road will be watched by day as well as night.
FX07-006.reputation: Tireless, close-mouthed and indispensable; the rangers' day hands.

members.role: Head of the house; Second of the Mistwood Night Rangers
members.note: He has served three Mistwalker captains and outlived two, and he runs the Mistwood while they sleep.

members.role: Heir; rider of the Mistwood road
members.note: She rode beside Taeron Windward on 9 April 1067 and saw the Temple agent's hands, and they were empty.

members.role: Lisael's son; ranger
members.note: His eyes shine in lamplight, and he has hidden from his family that he sees nearly as well as a true Mistwalker.

famousDead: First second of the Mistwood rangers; fought in the Clarora fog of 296.
FX07-006.secret: Ithmar's night sight is nearly as good as a carrier's, and under the Mistwalkers' own lamp test he might be counted kin to the royal line.
hooks: Sir Aimon Rastell lands in March and the Mistwood road must be watched day and night.
Lisael knows the man Taeron killed in 1067 was unarmed.
Ithmar's eyes could make him a pawn in the royal line's quarrels.

FX07-007.name: House Tidemark
FX07-007.title: Keeper of the Nimthil Chain
FX07-007.arms: a black chain between two grey towers, on white
FX07-007.words: Up at dusk, down at dawn.

military.office: Keepers of the Nimthil Chain
military.unit: the chain towers and harbor watch of Nimthil, 500 men
military.ties: They raise and drop the floating chain across the Calara's mouth and hold the only two stone forts in the realm.

FX07-007.power: Command of the Nimthil chain, its two stone towers and the 500 of the harbor watch: nothing enters Eldergrove's harbor at night without a Tidemark's leave.
FX07-007.history: Queen Ilvara the Elder raised the floating chain across the Calara's mouth between 614 and 620, after the noon raid on Ithira, and gave its keeping to Naelor Tidemark, whose two sons had died on the Ithira quay. The Tidemarks have kept it since, raising it at dusk, dropping it at dawn and mending its timber floats every spring. Their two towers are the only stone forts in Eldergrove, cut by 80 dwarven masons from Irondeep, and the family has kept a mason's mallet over the tower door for 485 years. In 918 a Tidemark shut the chain on the Greyhaven cog that brought the Black Cough and set it burning on Queen Lithiel's order, with its crew aboard. The family has never been sure the last of them were dead.
FX07-007.reputation: Dour, dependable and slightly feared: the hands on the harbor's throat.

members.role: Head of the house; Keeper of the Nimthil Chain
members.note: He has raised the chain about 88,000 times and can tell from the creak of the floats what the river did in the night.

members.role: Heir; master of the floats
members.note: She wants the chain replaced with iron from Irondeep, and her father calls it the first step to a human harbor.

members.role: Isolwen's son; tower watchman
members.note: He drops the chain an hour early for a smugglers' boat and takes a share of the yew money.

famousDead: First Keeper of the Chain; lost two sons in the noon raid of 611.
Shut the chain on the plague cog of 918 and set it burning.
FX07-007.secret: Falan drops the chain early for a smugglers' boat before dawn for a share of yew money, and the smugglers are the Driftleafs.
hooks: Isolwen wants an iron chain from Irondeep.
Falan's dawn smuggling will be seen sooner or later.
A Greyhaven sailor claims his grandfather escaped the burning plague cog of 918.

FX07-008.name: House Swiftsail
FX07-008.title: Master Pilot of Nimion
FX07-008.arms: a silver star over a grey sail, on sea blue
FX07-008.words: Watch the water, not the needle.
FX07-008.power: The sealskin charts of the Elder Coast and the West Drift, and the skill of piloting that every ship-house buys and no one else can sell.
FX07-008.history: The Swiftsails drew the first sealskin charts of the Elder Coast for Queen Aerdis about 400, and they have piloted Eldergrove's ships along the West Drift since. They know the coast from the North Fjords to the Strait of Hael by its smell, its birds and the color of its water, and they sell nothing they know. Greywave pilots use the lodestone needle; the Swiftsails have refused it for sixty years and say a pilot who trusts a needle stops watching the sea. The star-reader Istavel's wish to teach the needle to every captain has made them his loudest enemies on the Nimthil quay. In 1098 a Swiftsail pilot refused to take three Greywave cogs south past the Strait of Hael, and all three were lost under a Greywave pilot with a needle.
FX07-008.reputation: Superb pilots, insufferable company and right about the Strait of Hael.

members.role: Head of the house; Master Pilot of Nimion
members.note: He has piloted 900 voyages and lost two ships, and he names both every night.

members.role: Heir; chart-keeper
members.note: She refused the Greywave run of 1098 and has been called a coward on the Nimthil quay ever since.

members.role: Merith's daughter; apprentice pilot
members.note: She has secretly learned the needle from Istavel and thinks her family is wrong.

famousDead: Drew the first sealskin chart of the Elder Coast.
FX07-008.secret: The Swiftsail charts mark a safe passage past Old Ironjaw's waters through the shoals east of the Strait of Hael, and they have shown it to no one, not even the queen.
hooks: Merith knows a passage that would have saved the Greywave cogs.
Velith wants to sail with a needle.
House Lunetti of Ostra would pay a fortune for the Swiftsail charts.

FX07-009.name: House Seafern
FX07-009.title: Keeper of the Grave-Firs
FX07-009.arms: a silver skull under a green fern, on sea grey
FX07-009.power: The burial rolls of the captains' hills and the mark that allows a grave-fir to become a keel; no grave-keel is lawful without a Seafern beside the Sea Keeper.
FX07-009.history: Since Queen Aerdis allowed the first grave-keel in 470, a Seafern has walked the captains' burial hills with the Sea Keeper and marked the firs whose wood may become a keel. The family keeps the burial rolls: which captain lies under which tree, and which tree has gone to sea in which ship. Sylvaran's Keepers call the custom robbing the dead, and the Seaferns have borne that insult for six centuries. They say a grave-keel is the dead captain's last voyage and the highest honor the coast can give. Since 1088 several Greywave keels have been cut from trees the Seafern rolls give no name to, and the family has noticed.
FX07-009.reputation: Solemn grave-keepers whom sailors thank and Sylvaran despises.

members.role: Head of the house; Keeper of the Grave-Firs
members.note: She has marked 212 grave-firs in 300 years and can say under which captain each one stood.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the burial rolls
members.note: He has found four Greywave keels with no grave in the rolls and wants to tell the Sea Keeper.

members.role: Saelan's daughter
members.note: She is betrothed to a Greywave nephew, and the match depends on her father keeping quiet.

famousDead: Marked the first grave-keel, for Oren Greywave's crew, in 470.
FX07-009.secret: Caelith marked two grave-firs for Greywave keels in 1090 without checking the rolls, and one of the two graves is empty.
hooks: Saelan wants to tell the Sea Keeper about the nameless Greywave keels.
Naelis's betrothal to a Greywave hangs on her father's silence.
An empty grave on the captains' hill means a captain who did not die where the rolls say.

FX07-010.name: House Spraywood
FX07-010.title: Mistress of the Ithira Rope-Walk
FX07-010.arms: a white chevron of twisted rope, on grey
FX07-010.power: The 300 m rope-walk and the sailcloth sheds of Ithira, about 120 workers, and the contracts that rig half the realm's cogs.
FX07-010.history: The Spraywoods have spun rope and woven sailcloth at Ithira since 625, when the town rebuilt its sheds after the noon raid and Queen Ilvara the Elder wanted sails made on the coast instead of bought from humans. Their rope-walk is 300 m long, the longest building in Eldergrove, and their nettle-and-flax sailcloth is grey, light and smells of seal oil. About 120 workers walk the rope for them, half of them human hired hands who may not own a share of the sheds. Since the herring failed in 1101 the Herring and Seal Hall cannot pay for nets, and the Spraywoods have been paid in promises. The family's head has begun selling cloth to Saltleaf's cogs at a loss to keep the walk turning.
FX07-010.reputation: Generous employers and sharp bargainers; half the fjord eats from their rope-walk.

members.role: Head of the house; Mistress of the Ithira Rope-Walk
members.note: She walks the rope every morning beside the newest apprentice and has walked it about 70,000 times.

members.role: Heir; her half-elf daughter by a human rigger
members.note: As a citizen she can own the sheds, and she wants to give the human walkers ship-shares as Corin Saltleaf proposes.

members.role: Ithwen's human husband; foreman of the walk
members.note: He is a docker's son from Greyhaven who took his wife's house name, and the elves of the quay still call him the hired man.

famousDead: Built the 300 m rope-walk at Ithira in 625.
FX07-010.secret: Raelwen has woven forty sails on credit for Corin Saltleaf's new cogs, and she knows their keels are of smuggled fir.
hooks: The Herring Hall owes the Spraywoods a year of nets.
Ithwen wants the human walkers to own shares.
If Saltleaf falls, the Spraywoods fall with it.

FX07-011.name: House Driftleaf
FX07-011.title: Head of the Driftleaf boats
FX07-011.arms: no arms; a dead leaf on black water, cut into the sterns of their boats
FX07-011.words: The tide takes what it likes.
FX07-011.power: Six night boats, hidden coves on the Fenandor coast, a yew road from the Greenmire to Ashmere's buyers and friends among the human dockers of Nimthil.
FX07-011.history: The Driftleafs were a small ship-house of Fenandor until 1061, when their head was caught selling twenty unmarked fir masts to a Greyhaven captain and the council exiled him for fifty years and took the house's two cogs. His kin kept his name and his trade. They cut unmarked fir in the West Strand at night, float it to hidden coves and sell it to any shipwright who does not ask, and since 1102 they have carried Sylvaran yew from the Greenmire down the coast to Ashmere's buyers. In 1101 Ilvara Mistwalker's night landing burned their camp on the strand and killed four of them. The family believes someone sold them to the Veil, and it means to find out who.
FX07-011.reputation: Smugglers with a ship-house's pride and a grudge against the crown.

members.role: Head of the family; exiled in 1061
members.note: His exile ends in 1111, and he has sworn he will come home a ship-lord again.

members.role: His daughter; captain of the night boats
members.note: She lost her husband in the burning of 1101 and keeps a list of everyone who knew where the camp was.

members.role: Calira's human second; a docker of Nimthil
members.note: He loads Driftleaf fir onto foreign cogs under the harbor watch's nose and takes a third.

members.role: Calira's daughter
members.note: She is 25, has never lived anywhere but a boat and dreams of the Dusk School.

famousDead: Calira's husband; killed when the Night Rangers burned the strand camp.
FX07-011.secret: Their yew runs past the Nimthil chain before dawn because a Tidemark grandson drops it early for them.
hooks: Calira wants the name of whoever betrayed the strand camp in 1101.
Elvar's exile ends in 1111 and he wants his cogs back.
Ashmere's bowyers pay for every yew stave the Driftleafs land.

FX08-001.name: House Bearwall
FX08-001.title: Thane of the Bearwall Hills
FX08-001.arms: a black bear standing on white

military.office: Thanes of the Bearwall muster
military.unit: the Bearwall hird, 60 axemen, and 900 men of the Stagflow levy
military.ties: Bearwall men held the left of the ambush line in the Stagflow fog in 1091 and still drink to it every 26 May.

FX08-001.power: Forest farms and hill pastures of the Bearwall Hills, a district longship, and a seat in Jarl Halvard's hall.
FX08-001.history: The Bearwalls were forest thanes who swore to Eirik in 812 with the Staggs and sat in the first Thing of 815. They have followed the Staggs since, in the regency of 917 and in the taking-in of the Greymane exiles in 947. On 26 May 1091 Thane Brand Bearwall's men held the left of the ambush line at the Stagflow fords, and when the fog lifted they stripped the Aldmark dead. Among the spoil was a leather dispatch case that the thane has never shown his jarl.
FX08-001.reputation: Slow, solid, loyal hill-men who fight like bears once roused.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of the Bearwall Hills
members.note: He keeps the Aldmark dispatch case from the Stagflow under his bed and reads it when he cannot sleep.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She runs the hill farms better than her father and wants a seat at the Ring when he dies.

members.role: Younger son; Ice Walker of the Ski Yard
members.note: He crossed the Glenwash ice with the king in 1092 and has not been paid for it since.

members.role: Brand's wife
members.note: She lost a brother at the Stagflow and lays out a cup for him at every feast.

famousDead: Swore to Eirik Winterborn in 812 and sat at the first Thing of 815
FX08-001.secret: The Stagflow dispatch case holds Marshal Stane's letters naming two Aldmark agents in Saltbridge, one of them a Bearwall cousin.
hooks: Jarl Halvard hears that Brand kept spoil from the Stagflow.
The Bearwall cousin named in the letters asks Tova to marry him.

FX08-002.name: House Emberfall
FX08-002.title: Thane of the Emberfall Forges
FX08-002.arms: a black anvil on ember red

military.office: Armourers of the Stagflow muster
military.unit: the Emberfall levy, 600 men, and forty smiths who march with the hird
military.ties: Emberfall forges make the axe-heads and mail of the King's Hird, and their smiths mend the Stagg hird in the field.

FX08-002.power: The bog-iron workings of the Emberfall forest and the forges that turn them into axes.
FX08-002.history: The Emberfalls dug bog iron from the Stagflow mosses before there was a king and were made thanes when Bjorn I the Shipwright needed iron for his Ship Levy. Bog iron is soft, and since Sigvald's reign the kingdom has bought more and more iron from Irondeep through Kingsmere, which gives Aldmark a hand on its throat. In the Rising the Emberfall forges ran day and night. In 1092 they also received 2,000 crossbow bolts from an Irondeep captain who should never have sold them.
FX08-002.reputation: Sooty, hard-working and richer than their mud deserves.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of the Emberfall Forges
members.note: He has re-stamped Irondeep bolts with the Emberfall mark twice now, and the second time the dwarf captain asked for more silver.

members.role: Heir; master smith
members.note: She forges the King's Hird axes herself and refuses to put her mark on dwarf steel.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He carries the family's quiet cargoes between Saltbridge and the Irondeep captain's men at Kingsmere.

famousDead: Forged the iron for Bjorn I's first Ship Levy longships
FX08-002.secret: Emberfall buys Irondeep crossbow bolts in secret, against the dwarves' own law, and passes them off as Stagflow iron.
hooks: An Irondeep envoy at Kingsmere demands the name of the captain who sold bolts north.
Runa finds dwarf steel in the Hird's new axe-heads.

FX08-003.name: House Dunpool
FX08-003.title: Thane of Dunpool and Taster to the King
FX08-003.arms: a white cross on slate blue

military.office: King's thanes of the Dunpool muster
military.unit: the Dunpool levy, 500 men, and a crew of the King's Hird
military.ties: A Dunpool son has served in the King's Hird as the king's taster since Eirik II, and the post carries a hirdman's rank.

FX08-003.power: The Dunpool river farms on the Carrburg Chase and an old office at the king's table.
FX08-003.history: Eirik II the Tall made a Dunpool his taster after a winter fever killed half his hall, and the family has tasted the Winterborns' food ever since. On 6 January 1090 the taster Geir Dunpool sat at the foot of the table in Kingsmere when King Bjorn III ate. He has said ever since that Hirdmaster Kettil Frost, then guard captain, sent him away to fetch more ale before the fish came. Bjorn died after that feast, and the Dunpools have hated Kettil Frost in silence since.
FX08-003.reputation: A house that lost its honour at a feast, or had it stolen.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of Dunpool
members.note: He has joined Bjorn's Avengers and sends money to Jarl Halvard's men in Ostra.

members.role: Heir; the king's taster in 1090
members.note: He was sent from the table for ale on the night King Bjorn was poisoned, and he will swear to it at the Thing.

members.role: Geir's daughter
members.note: She has been taught to taste for poison since she was five.

members.role: Ulf's wife
members.note: She tells her husband to wait for the Thing, and does not believe he will.

FX08-003.secret: Geir Dunpool believes Kettil Frost sent him from the king's table on purpose, and the Dunpools mean to say so when the cook is brought to the spring Thing.
hooks: Jarl Halvard brings the cook to the spring Thing, and Geir is called to speak.
Kettil Frost offers the Dunpools a seat in the Hird Hall for their silence.

FX08-004.name: House Meadfall
FX08-004.title: Thane of Meadfall
FX08-004.arms: a gold star on sea green

military.office: Thanes of the Meadfall muster
military.unit: the Meadfall levy, 700 men, and a district longship
military.ties: Meadfall sends its longship to the king's call and fed the army in 1091 with Jarl Asta's stockfish.

FX08-004.power: The amber beaches of the Meadfall river mouth and a share of the Coldwater amber trade.
FX08-004.history: The Meadfalls gathered amber beside the Coldwaters after the great storm of 824 and became their thanes when Torvald made Sven Coldwater jarl about 905. They grew rich with every storm and belong to Jarl Asta's Amber Traders, who want peace and trade with Kingsmere. In autumn 1103 Thane Leif Meadfall rowed a cloaked visitor from a Kingsmere cog to Asta's hall at night and rowed him back before dawn.
FX08-004.reputation: Amber-rich, soft-spoken and never far from the jarl's ear.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of Meadfall
members.note: He rowed the Ravenscar envoy to Jarl Asta's hall in 1103 and knows what was promised.

members.role: Heir; amber-sorter
members.note: She grades amber by its smell when burned and runs the family's Kingsmere sales.

members.role: Younger son; hirdman of Jarl Asta
members.note: He is Stagg-minded and loud about Bjorn's Avengers, which his father hates.

FX08-004.secret: Thane Leif carried Lady Ysolde Ravenscar's envoy to Jarl Asta in 1103 and witnessed her promise to keep Coldhaven's ships out of any war.
hooks: Sven learns what his father did in 1103 and must choose between his house and his king.
The Tallburgs offer the Meadfalls silence for a share of the amber beaches.

FX08-005.name: House Tallburg
FX08-005.title: Thane of Tallburg Tower
FX08-005.arms: a silver tower on dark blue

military.office: Keepers of Tallburg Tower
military.unit: the Tallburg tower guard, 80 men, and the crew of one of Coldhaven's five longships
military.ties: Tallburg crews fought beside Kettil Frost's longships when they burned the Greyhaven galleys off Wolfhaven in 1092.

FX08-005.power: Tallburg Tower on the headland above Coldhaven's approaches and the fishing villages under it.
FX08-005.history: Bjorn I the Shipwright built Tallburg Tower to watch Coldhaven's sea road and gave it to a captain of his Ship Levy. The Tallburgs became thanes under the Coldwaters but have always looked to Wolfhaven first. In the Rising their longship burned beside Kettil Frost's when the Greyhaven blockade broke in August 1092. Thane Hrafn Tallburg joined Bjorn's Avengers at Jarl Halvard's winter feast of 1093.
FX08-005.reputation: The king's men in the amber jarl's country.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of Tallburg Tower
members.note: He watches Jarl Asta's hall from his tower and writes what he sees to Jarl Halvard.

members.role: Heir; longship captain
members.note: She steered the Tallburg longship into the Greyhaven galleys' fire in 1092 and lost her eyebrows.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He is apprenticed to the Lawspeaker's school and loves the old verses.

famousDead: Burned with the Greyhaven galleys off Wolfhaven in August 1092
FX08-005.secret: Hrafn has seen the Ravenscar envoy's cog anchored off Coldhaven twice since 1103 and has told Jarl Halvard, but not the king.
hooks: Jarl Asta asks Hrafn to give up his tower to a Coldwater castellan.
Yrsa sees the envoy's cog a third time and means to burn it.

FX08-006.name: House Castlebarrow
FX08-006.title: Thane of the Flintwall Capes

military.office: Keepers of Flintwall Tower
military.unit: the Flintwall garrison, 120 men, and a crew of walrus-hunters
military.ties: The thanes of Flintwall keep the tower that guards the eastern approaches to Wolfhaven and raise its beacon for the king's ebb-ships.

FX08-006.power: Flintwall Tower, the wreck-right of the tundra capes east of Wolfhaven and the walrus beaches beyond.
FX08-006.history: The Castlebarrows came out of the east about 860 as walrus-hunters and offered their oath to Bjorn I for the tundra capes no one else wanted. They have kept Flintwall Tower and the wreck-right of the capes since. In 812 the old harbour thanes of Wolfhaven, the Hafgrims, had fled east to the walrus capes when Eirik took the town and were never heard of again. The Castlebarrows say they never met any Hafgrims there.
FX08-006.reputation: Grim, isolated capes-folk who know the ice better than their neighbours.

members.role: Head of the family; Thane of the Flintwall Capes
members.note: He keeps a carved Hafgrim drinking horn in a chest under the tower and drinks from it alone on Lantern Night.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She hunts walrus on the floe edge in winter and has killed a white bear with a spear.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He has heard his father's stories of the Hafgrim harbour and thinks Wolfhaven should be theirs.

famousDead: Last harbour thane of Wolfhaven, who fled east in 812; the Castlebarrows never name him
FX08-006.secret: The Castlebarrows are the Hafgrims under another name, the harbour thanes Eirik Winterborn drove out of Wolfhaven in 812.
hooks: Toke boasts at the Ice Crossing that his blood once ruled Wolfhaven.
A Free Hall keeper finds an old blood-price roll naming a Hafgrim heir at Flintwall.

FX08-007.name: the Axeholm family
FX08-007.title: Crew-Leader of the King's Hird
FX08-007.arms: a white axe on night blue

military.office: Hereditary crew-leaders of the King's Hird
military.unit: a crew of forty of the King's Hird, 600 sworn axemen in mail
military.ties: An Axeholm has stood in the king's shield-wall since Eirik's crossing of 812, and three stood behind Bjorn III at Kingsmere and could not save him.

FX08-007.power: A crew-leader's seat in the Hird Hall of Wolfhaven, a steading on the Barrens, and the right to sleep at the king's door.
FX08-007.history: Orm Axeholm was one of the 340 men who followed Eirik across the frozen bay in January 812, and one of the first through Wolfhaven's gate. Every generation since has given the King's Hird a crew-leader. Axeholm women have served as royal nurses through the long winters, feeding Winterborn babies every three hours against the fits of the frost blood. Three Axeholms were in Bjorn III's guard at the Kingsmere feast of 1090, and they serve Hirdmaster Kettil Frost now.
FX08-007.reputation: The king's own axes, with no politics but the king.

members.role: Head of the family; crew-leader of the King's Hird
members.note: He stood behind Bjorn III at Kingsmere and has never forgiven himself, or wondered aloud about his captain.

members.role: Orm's wife; royal nurse
members.note: She nursed Prince Bjorn through every winter of his childhood and knows his hands go white in the cold like anyone's.

members.role: Heir; hirdman
members.note: He guards Prince Bjorn and would take an axe for him without thinking.

members.role: Orm's daughter
members.note: She wants to be the first woman in the King's Hird and has asked Svala Snowstride for a place in the Ski Yard instead.

famousDead: Crossed the ice with Eirik in 812 and was among the first through Wolfhaven's gate
FX08-007.secret: Hild Axeholm knows Prince Bjorn lacks the frost blood, and the family has sworn to carry it to the grave.
hooks: The Dunpools accuse Kettil Frost before the Thing, and the Axeholms must choose between their captain and the truth.
A winter ice-fishing feast where the prince is expected to hold bare iron like his grandfather.

FX08-008.name: the Frostmyre family
FX08-008.title: Ski-Captain of the Saltbridge Yard
FX08-008.arms: a white bend on ice blue

military.office: Hereditary ski-captains of the Ice Walkers
military.unit: a company of 200 Ice Walkers of the Saltbridge Ski Yard
military.ties: Frostmyres have walked the winter ice for every Winterborn since the crossing of 812, and they train the Ice Walkers' new blood at Svala Snowstride's yard.

FX08-008.power: A moss-farm on the Stagflow, their skis, and the respect of every man who has crossed the winter ice.
FX08-008.history: Eleven Frostmyres crossed Cold Bay with Eirik in January 812, and four went through the ice. The survivors were given a moss-farm and the duty of leading the king's winter walkers. They crossed the frozen Glenwash mouth with Eirik III on 19 January 1092 and burned the grain stores at Brightmoor. Like all the Ice Walkers they have not been fully paid since that winter.
FX08-008.reputation: The hardest men in Northreach, and the poorest for it.

members.role: Head of the family; ski-captain
members.note: He led the walkers into Brightmoor in 1092 and gave the order he will not speak of.

members.role: Heir; Ice Walker
members.note: She is the fastest skier at the Saltbridge yard and is organising the walkers to march on Wolfhaven for their back pay.

members.role: Rane's wife; keeper of the moss-farm
members.note: She has fed the farm on credit for twelve years and the Emberfalls hold the note.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He carves skis for children and wants nothing to do with war.

famousDead: Went through the ice on Eirik's crossing of 812, one of the forty-one lost
FX08-008.secret: At Brightmoor in 1092 Rane's walkers burned the store-sheds with six surrendered Aldmark grain-guards locked inside, and the king never asked.
hooks: Sigrid leads 300 unpaid Ice Walkers to the king's hall on Lantern Night.
A Wardlaw comes north under truce asking how his kinsman died at Brightmoor.

FX08-009.name: the Cairnside family
FX08-009.title: Warden of the Thirty-One Stones
FX08-009.arms: a grey standing stone on pale green

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of the Stone-Watch
military.unit: a hundred of the 600 Stone-Watch scouts along the watershed
military.ties: The Stone-Watch has walked the 31 stones since 952, and a Cairnside has led it from Jarl Stagg's land since the stones were set.

FX08-009.power: A watch-steading below the fifteenth stone and knowledge of every path across the watershed.
FX08-009.history: When Emperor Harald and King Bjorn II set 31 stones a day's walk apart along the Stagflow watershed in 952, a Stagg huntsman named Ulf Cairnside walked beside the stone-setters, and his family has walked the stones ever since. Their scouts watched Aldmark's 12,000 march toward Saltbridge in May 1091 and sent word that set the ambush in the Stagflow fog. In the war winter of 1092 one of the stones moved.
FX08-009.reputation: Quiet watchers who know every sheep track between the two kingdoms.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Stones
members.note: She moved the ninth stone a hundred paces south in the winter of 1092 so the good spring would lie on Northreach's side.

members.role: Heir; scout
members.note: He has seen a Frosthollow quartermaster cross the stones at night and followed him to a Stagflow farm.

members.role: Thora's husband; hunter
members.note: He hunts deer on both sides of the stones and has never asked which side he is on.

famousDead: Walked beside the stone-setters of 952 and founded the Stone-Watch
FX08-009.secret: It was Thora Cairnside who moved the ninth border stone south in 1092, and the Stone-Watch's complaint against Frosthollow is a cover.
hooks: Aldmark's Frosthollow castellan demands the ninth stone be measured before witnesses.
Ulf must decide whether to report the Frosthollow quartermaster or use him.

FX08-010.name: the Beaconwold family
FX08-010.title: Keeper of the Amber Capes Beacons
FX08-010.arms: an orange flame on dark slate

military.office: Hereditary keepers of the Coast Watch beacons of the Amber Capes
military.unit: 120 beacon men of the 600-strong Coast Watch
military.ties: Beaconwold fires called the longships out against the Greyhaven blockade of 1092, and every headland of the capes has a Beaconwold watcher.

FX08-010.power: The beacon posts of the Amber Capes and the stipend of the Coast Watch.
FX08-010.history: When Bjorn I made his Ship Levy in 856, he set beacon posts on the headlands to call the crews, and gave the Amber Capes posts to a fisher family of Beaconwold. They have kept the fires since, in fog, ice and storm. In August 1092 their beacons called the longships out against the Greyhaven blockade off Wolfhaven. A beacon can also be left dark, and on the capes a wreck is worth a year's stipend.
FX08-010.reputation: Watchful, weather-beaten folk whom sailors bless and wreckers court.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Beacons
members.note: He has kept the fires for thirty years and would hang a keeper who let one go dark.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the outer headland
members.note: He takes Gull silver to let the outer beacon die on foggy nights.

members.role: Sven's daughter; beacon runner
members.note: She found a stripped cog on the rocks below her brother's headland and the beacon cold above it.

FX08-010.secret: Hakon Beaconwold leaves the outer headland dark for the Gull wreckers, and a Kingsmere cog full of tin died there last autumn.
hooks: Thyra tells her father about the cold beacon.
Reeve Oddny Tinmark sends men to ask why her stamped tin is turning up in the Gulls' net loft.

FX08-011.name: the Ebbtide line
FX08-011.title: Captain of the King's Ebb-Ships
FX08-011.arms: a black longship on pale blue

military.office: Captains of the king's eight ebb-ships
military.unit: 8 longships and 320 men who raid on the falling tide
military.ties: The ebb-ships are the king's own raiders, and an Ebbtide has steered the lead ship since Bjorn I the Shipwright built the first of them.

FX08-011.power: Command of the king's eight ebb-ships and a boathouse on the Wolfhaven strand.
FX08-011.history: Bjorn I the Shipwright chose the best pilot of the Cold Coast to lead his first fast longships, and the man took the name of the tide he sailed on. His line has captained the king's ebb-ships since, raiding on the falling tide and gone before the flood. In 1092 Steinar Ebbtide's ships helped burn the Greyhaven galleys off Wolfhaven. Since then the ebb-ships have had little war and some quiet trade.
FX08-011.reputation: The best seamen of the Cold Coast, and the least careful about whose cargo they carry.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the King's Ebb-Ships
members.note: He runs Hrimfell tusks for the Coldwaters in the closed season, and Drevna's whalers have marked his sail.

members.role: Heir; steersman
members.note: She can bring a longship into Wolfhaven in fog by the sound of the waves on the harbour wall.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He wants to seize the next Kingsmere cog that comes near the Frostholm coast, with or without orders.

members.role: Steinar's mother
members.note: She remembers every tide table of the Cold Coast and was a pilot before her husband was.

famousDead: First captain of Bjorn I's fast longships
FX08-011.secret: Steinar uses the king's ebb-ships to carry Hrimfell tusks for the Coldwaters' unicorn trade.
hooks: Reeve Oddny orders the ebb-ships to seize any Kingsmere cog near Frostholm.
A Drevna whaler rams an ebb-ship in summer fog.

FX08-012.name: the Skerry family
FX08-012.title: Master of the Skerry Cogs
FX08-012.arms: a gold anchor on deep blue
FX08-012.power: Three of the kingdom's fifteen cogs, hired each summer to the Tin Reeves for the Skarfell run.
FX08-012.history: When Sigvald the Lawful bought two Greyhaven cogs with sternpost rudders in 1035, a Coldhaven skipper named Asgeir Skerry learned to sail them, and his family has owned and sailed cogs on the tin run ever since. A laden cog carries as much tin as eight longships, and the Skerrys grew rich on the Tin Reeves' summer fleet. Last summer a Kingsmere cog loaded tin at Ragvik on Frostholm, and the Skerrys know who carried the tin to it.
FX08-012.reputation: Prosperous cog-folk who do the Tin Reeves' heavy lifting and resent it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Skerry Cogs
members.note: He carried forty bars of giant tin to a Kingsmere cog at Ragvik for Master Tova Brand's agent and was paid in Aldmark marks.

members.role: Heir; cog skipper
members.note: She sails the Tin Reeves' fleet to Skarfell and has learned a few words of the giants' slow trade-talk.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He drinks with Kingsmere sailors in Coldhaven and talks about freedom of trade.

famousDead: First Northreach skipper to master a sternpost-rudder cog
FX08-012.secret: It was a Skerry cog that carried tin to the Kingsmere cog at Ragvik, breaking the Tin Compact for Aldmark silver.
hooks: Reeve Oddny Tinmark hunts the skipper who sold tin at Ragvik.
Dagny hears the giants complain about the Tin Reeves' balance.

FX08-013.name: the Rackham family
FX08-013.title: Master of the Coldhaven Fish Racks
FX08-013.arms: a silver fish on blue-grey, over a gold rack
FX08-013.power: The great stockfish racks of Coldhaven, a seat in the Coldhaven Amber and Fish Guild and the rye trade from Kingsmere.
FX08-013.history: In the Hungry Spring of 974 the herring failed and Northreach could not pay for Kingsmere rye. A fish-drier named Torvald Rackham had a warehouse of stockfish that kept, and he traded it for rye the next year at a price that made him rich. His heirs have dried, salted and sold the coast's cod ever since and buy most of the rye that comes back. They fed Eirik's army in 1091 beside Jarl Asta, and they want peace with Kingsmere more than anyone.
FX08-013.reputation: They smell of fish and silver, and they never go hungry.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Fish Racks
members.note: He keeps a warehouse of old Kingsmere rye and sells it to the poor at double price every hungry spring.

members.role: Heir; rye-buyer at Kingsmere
members.note: She spends half the year in Kingsmere and is courted by a Saltash barge-master.

members.role: Younger son; Free Hall singer
members.note: He gives away rye from his father's warehouse to the hall's poor and is beaten for it.

famousDead: Traded hoarded stockfish for rye after the Hungry Spring of 974
FX08-013.secret: The Rackhams hold back rye each winter to raise the spring price, and Jarl Asta takes a share.
hooks: A hungry spring and an empty hall: the Free Hall keepers march on the Rackham warehouse.
War with Aldmark would cut off the Rackham rye, and Ingrid's suitor.

FX08-014.name: the Keelby family
FX08-014.title: Master Shipwright of Saltbridge
FX08-014.power: The longship sheds of Saltbridge, which build or mend most of the kingdom's 48 longships under the Ship Levy.
FX08-014.history: When Bjorn I ordered every district to keep a longship and a crew of 40 in 856, the jarls needed shipwrights, and a Stagflow boatbuilder named Keel of Keelby built the first six. His line has built the kingdom's longships since in the oak sheds of Saltbridge. Each plank is sworn on the Oathfather's name as it is fastened. Since Aldmark lost its ship oak at the Oak Line in 1080, Kingsmere buyers have offered the Keelbys good silver for seasoned Stagflow oak.
FX08-014.reputation: Master craftsmen, proud of every ship and quick to quarrel over any one of them.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Shipwright
members.note: He sold a stack of seasoned levy oak to a Coldhaven middleman who sold it on to an Aldmark yard.

members.role: Heir; master of the sheds
members.note: She is building the first Northreach longship with a sternpost rudder and the old men call it a sin.

members.role: Younger son; ship's carpenter
members.note: He sails with the Ebbtide ships to mend them at sea.

famousDead: Built the first six longships of the Ship Levy
FX08-014.secret: Hrolf Keelby sold seasoned oak meant for the Ship Levy to an Aldmark cog yard through a Coldhaven middleman.
hooks: Jarl Halvard's new longship is laid down and there is not enough seasoned oak.
Sigrun's rudder longship is launched before the Thing.

FX08-015.name: the Glenmouth kin
FX08-015.title: Hall-Keeper of Blytheham
FX08-015.arms: a white cross on dark blue
FX08-015.power: The Free Hall of Blytheham among the Greymane exiles of the Stagflow, and descent from the man who carried the Glenwash truce record north.
FX08-015.history: In February 946 Wulfgar, hall-keeper of Easterham, fled to Wolfhaven with a copy of the Oath Hall record proving Harald Ironside had broken his truce with Jarl Ulf Greymane. About 200 Greymane men followed him and settled on the Stagflow, and Wulfgar's children became their hall-keepers at Blytheham. The record itself lies under the Sea King's stones at Wolfhaven, kept by Ragna of the Stones, a cousin of the kin. The Glenmouth kin have refused every Aldmark claim on the halls since, and sent their sons to the Rising.
FX08-015.reputation: Fierce Free Hall keepers who remember the Glenwash as if it were last year.

members.role: Head of the kin; Hall-Keeper of Blytheham
members.note: Named for his forefather, he has the Glenwash truce words by heart and recites them at every Lantern Night.

members.role: Heir; hall-singer
members.note: She has carried letters through the Briarbrook fens to Easterham twice and met Jarl Sigurd Greymane once.

members.role: Wulfgar's son; hirdman of Jarl Halvard
members.note: He fought at the Stagflow beside Halvard's sons and carried one of them off the field.

famousDead: Fled to Wolfhaven in 946 with the copy of the Glenwash truce record
FX08-015.secret: Wulfgar made two copies in 946; the second lies in the roof beam of the Blytheham hall, and the kin have never told even Ragna.
hooks: Ragna of the Stones means to show Jarl Sigurd the record; if hers is lost, only the Blytheham copy is left.
Ravenscar agents ask questions in Blytheham about old roof beams.

FX08-016.name: the Lawholt family
FX08-016.title: Law-Rememberer of Saltbridge
FX08-016.arms: a brown owl on pale gold
FX08-016.power: Descent from the first Lawspeaker, a seat among the law apprentices, and the trust of the old thanes.
FX08-016.history: Thorgrim of Saltbridge was the first Lawspeaker, named at Eirik's first Thing in 815, and he learned the law from the thanes' own customs. His heirs took the name Lawholt and carried the verses in their heads for two centuries. When Sigvald let the Lawspeaker train apprentices, the Lawholts expected the seat to come back to them, and it never has. Now Lawspeaker Einar Greyhand is losing the verses, and his pupil Ivar Longmemory has been writing them on parchment, which the Lawholts call a betrayal of Eirik's wish.
FX08-016.reputation: Proud keepers of the old way, bitter that the old way passed them by.

members.role: Head of the family; Law-Rememberer of Saltbridge
members.note: He can recite the whole law in two days without a pause and wants the Lawspeaker's seat when Einar fails.

members.role: Heir; law apprentice
members.note: She stole Ivar Longmemory's parchment leaves from his loft to burn them, and has not had the heart to.

members.role: Hallgrim's son
members.note: He secretly agrees with Ivar that the law must be written before it dies.

famousDead: First Lawspeaker of Northreach, named at the Thing of 815
FX08-016.secret: Thora Lawholt has Ivar Longmemory's missing parchment leaves of the written law hidden in her chest.
hooks: An Aldmark buyer offers Thora silver for the written law.
Einar finds his sister's hidden leaves and reads them.

FX08-017.name: the Sealness family
FX08-017.title: Headman of the Sealness Ice Camps
FX08-017.arms: a grey harpoon on dark blue-black
FX08-017.power: The seal grounds of the Amber Capes ice and the winter camps on the floe edge.
FX08-017.history: The Sealness folk have followed the seals onto the ice of the Amber Capes every winter since before the kingdom, living in camps on the floe from December to April. They swore to Eirik in 812 because his father had been a sealer-chief like them. The crown takes a share of every seal catch, as the Hafgrims did before it. In 1104 Sealness men found a Kingsmere cog anchored in a hidden cove of the capes, waiting.
FX08-017.reputation: Tough, poor and closer to the seals than to the jarl.

members.role: Head of the family; headman of the ice camps
members.note: He took the Kingsmere captain's silver in 1104 to say nothing about the hidden cove.

members.role: Heir; harpooner
members.note: She has killed more seals than any man in the camps and is courted by a Rackham son she despises.

members.role: Bodvar's son
members.note: He rowed out to the Kingsmere cog for a dare and came back with an Aldmark knife.

FX08-017.secret: A Kingsmere cog waits in a hidden cove of the Amber Capes to load smuggled tin, and Bodvar has been paid to keep quiet about it.
hooks: Kalf shows his Aldmark knife in a Coldhaven alehouse.
The ice breaks early and the camp drifts toward the hidden cove.

FX08-018.name: the Gull kin
FX08-018.title: Keeper of the Net Loft
FX08-018.arms: a gull's foot cut into a net float
FX08-018.power: A net loft on the Wolfhaven Boathouse Strand, a dozen boats, and friends on every dark headland.
FX08-018.history: The Gulls were strand-folk of Wolfhaven who lived from what the sea threw up. By Northreach law a wreck belongs to the crown, and stripping one is theft paid back twice. Hakon Gull's father learned to help the sea along. Now Hakon keeps a net loft on the Boathouse Strand, buys wreck goods and runs short tin bars to Coldhaven boats.
FX08-018.reputation: Strand rats and wreckers, says the town, and buys from them anyway.

members.role: Head of the kin; keeper of the net loft
members.note: He has a stranded cog's worth of tin bars with Oddny Tinmark's own stamp hidden under his nets.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She is a clerk at the Tin Wharf warehouses, and her father's short bars come from her shears.

members.role: Hakon's son; boatman
members.note: He rows out to stranded ships before the crown's men and is the first aboard.

members.role: Hakon's mother
members.note: She mends nets on the strand and hears everything said in the Ice Crossing hall.

FX08-018.secret: Bodil Gull shaves tin from stamped bars in the Tin Reeves' warehouse, and the Gulls recast the shavings into short bars sold at Coldhaven.
hooks: A stranded cog on the capes carries Kingsmere tin with Oddny's own stamp, and the Gulls get to it first.
Reeve Oddny's men search the net lofts of the Boathouse Strand.

FX09-001.name: the Hall of Ragvik
FX09-001.title: Eldest of Ragvik
FX09-001.arms: a white boat-keel on grey water

military.office: Eldest of Ragvik
military.unit: three hall pairs, 6 giants, beside the Helstad pairs
military.ties: Ragvik's few pairs fight beside Helstad's under the Pair-Yard's rule, and its coves give the levy most of its boatmen.

FX09-001.power: The south-coast coves between Skarfell and Helstad, about 280 giants and 1,500 tribute-fisherfolk, and a vote at the Thing that has always gone to Skarfell.
FX09-001.history: Ragvik is the smallest of the five old halls, about 280 giants on the south coast between Skarfell and Helstad, and its coves hold more tribute-folk boats than any other shore.
