In 797 Cold Coast thanes came with six ships to take its tin, and Helstad's pairs broke them on Ragvik beach; the hall has leaned on its neighbors' giants ever since. The Mothers' chant says Skarvi the Small's father's mother came from Ragvik, and Lore-Chanter Sva believes the small-giant trait lay hidden in Ragvik's women before it showed in him. Eldest Gunnvor keeps the hall out of the Thing's quarrels and votes with Skarfell. In August 1104 Chieftain Skarvi let a Kingsmere cog load 200 bars of tin at Ragvik by night, and the hall's human headman stood on the beach and counted them.
FX09-001.reputation: A quiet hall of fisher-giants that the island forgets until something happens in its coves.

members.role: Eldest of Ragvik
members.note: She has kept her hall out of every quarrel at the Thing for forty years, and now the quarrel has come to her beach.

members.role: Heir; her son
members.note: He stood on the cliff above the cove on the night of the Kingsmere cog and has not decided what he saw.

members.role: Eyolf's daughter
members.note: At 22 she stands a small giant's height and can stoop through a tribute-folk door, and Sva has asked to measure her.

famousDead: Mother of Skarvi the Small's father in the chant; the small-giant trait may have come through her.
FX09-001.secret: Eyolf saw the Kingsmere cog loaded and saw Arni the Quick pay the human headman, and Ragvik's silence has a price it has not yet named.
hooks: Ragvik's vote and silence matter at the Thing of 1106.
Fjola may carry the Skarfell trait.
The Northreach Tin Reeve would pay well for what Eyolf saw.

FX09-002.name: the Watch-Hall of Haldvang
FX09-002.title: Eldest of Haldvang
FX09-002.arms: a grey stone tower over white surf

military.office: Keepers of the south-west beacon
military.unit: 20 watch-hall men and two hall pairs
military.ties: Haldvang's pairs throw stones at boats from the cliffs, and its beacon calls Helstad's pairs to the shore.

FX09-002.power: A stone watch-hall on the south-west cliffs, its beacon and its pairs, and the duty under the Tin Compact to stop runaway boats.
FX09-002.history: Haldvang is a stone watch-hall on Frostholm's south-west coast, built in 799 after the Thanes' Raid because the coast there has too little timber for a hall and stone does not burn. Two Helstad households moved in to watch the sea toward the Cold Coast, and their descendants, about 70 giants, still keep it with a few hundred tribute-folk fishers below. For two centuries Haldvang watched for raiders. Since the Tin Compact of 1002 it has watched for runaways' boats instead, because the compact obliges the halls to stop them, and the hall's giants do not like the work. In 1102 Hauk of Helstad stood the shore watch and let a smuggler's boat with four runaway families pass; Eldest Stig suspects it and has said nothing.
FX09-002.reputation: Dour cliff-watchers with a reputation, lately, for poor eyesight.

members.role: Eldest of Haldvang
members.note: He has decided that a giant who saw nothing cannot be asked what he saw.

members.role: Heir; beacon-keeper
members.note: She lights the beacon on Thing nights and would like to light it for every Northreach patrol boat too, so the runaways can hide.

members.role: Hrefna's son; youngest giant of the watch
members.note: He is the only giant born at Haldvang in thirty years, and the hall treats him like something that might break.

famousDead: First eldest of the watch-hall built in 799.
FX09-002.secret: Stig has let three runaway boats pass since 1102 by sending the watch-pair to the wrong headland, and the Northreach Tin Reeve has begun to wonder why Haldvang never sees anything.
hooks: The compact obliges Haldvang to stop runaways it would rather help.
Torgrim is the hall's only young giant.
A Northreach patrol may land to watch the watch-hall.

FX09-003.name: the Watch-Hall of Lindholm
FX09-003.title: Eldest of Lindholm
FX09-003.arms: a white beacon flame on slate grey

military.office: Keepers of the fair beacon
military.unit: 20 watch-hall men and the Lindholm runners
military.ties: Lindholm's small runners carry warning to the chieftain and serve with the Skarfell Runners in war.

FX09-003.power: The headland watch-hall east of Ragvik, the fair beacon that opens the tin fair, and small runners who reach Skarfell faster than any giant can walk.
FX09-003.history: Lindholm is the second stone watch-hall of the south coast, built in 799 on a headland east of Ragvik and given to a Skarfell household. Its 70 giants include several small Skarfell runners, who carry word to the chieftain at a run. It is Lindholm's beacon that tells Skarfell the first Northreach sail of summer is in sight and the tin fair may open. In August 1104 Lindholm's watch saw the Kingsmere cog that loaded tin at Ragvik by night and was told by the chieftain's son Arni to forget it. Eldest Yngvild is loyal to the Skarfells and will vote for Skarvi in 1106, but she has begun to ask why a chieftain who keeps the compact needs to be obeyed in the dark.
FX09-003.reputation: Loyal Skarfell kin on a windy headland, the island's eyes on the sea.

members.role: Eldest of Lindholm
members.note: She has lit the fair beacon 63 summers running and now wonders whose ships she is lighting it for.

members.role: Heir; a small runner
members.note: Small for a giant, he can run the 30 km to Skarfell in three hours, and he has carried words the chieftain did not want written down.

members.role: Isolf's daughter, a child
members.note: At thirteen she is already as tall as her father and will never be a runner, and the hall does not know what that means.

famousDead: First eldest of Lindholm, a Skarfell woman given the headland in 799.
FX09-003.secret: Isolf carried a message from Arni the Quick to the Kingsmere cog's captain in August 1104, and he knows the price agreed for the next load.
hooks: Yngvild's doubts could cost Skarvi a vote.
Isolf knows the price of the next secret load.
The first Northreach sail of 1105 will bring the Tin Reeve's questions.

FX09-004.name: the Ormhamar household
FX09-004.title: Pair-Leader of Ormhamar
FX09-004.arms: two grey hammers back to back, on white
FX09-004.words: Back to back, or not at all.

military.office: Hereditary pair-leaders of Helstad
military.unit: three of Helstad's hall pairs, 6 giants
military.ties: Ormhamar giants have fought in the Helstad pairs since two of them broke the thanes' shield wall at Ragvik in 797, and many of the Pair-Yard's champions have come from the household.

FX09-004.power: Three of Helstad's fighting pairs, a name every pair-fighter on the island knows, and the Ormhamar stead below Helstad Hall.
FX09-004.history: Two pairs of Helstad giants broke the Cold Coast thanes' shield wall on Ragvik beach in July 797 and sank two ships with thrown stones, and both pairs came from the household that farms the Ormhamar stead below Helstad Hall. The household has given the halls fighting pairs ever since, partners matched young and bound for life. Thrand the Broad learned beside Ormhamar giants at the Pair-Yard of Skarfell, and the household's young train there each winter. Frostholm has had no war since 797, so the household fights at the fair, against walrus and bear, and in the Pair-Yard's matches. In 1105 its head has lost his pair-partner to fever and fights alone, which a pair-fighter should never do.
FX09-004.reputation: The island's warriors in a land with no war, proud of a beach fight three centuries old.

members.role: Head of the household; pair-leader
members.note: His partner Asgerd died of fever in 1103, and he still stands with an empty space at his back.

members.role: Heir; pair-fighter
members.note: Her pair-partner is Hauk of Helstad, and she is the only giant who knows where he goes at night.

members.role: Kolgrim's son; at the Pair-Yard
members.note: At seventeen he has not been matched, and Thrand the Broad says he fights like a giant who wants to fight alone.

famousDead: Led the pairs that broke the thanes' shield wall at Ragvik in 797.
FX09-004.secret: Valdis keeps Hauk's night visits to the Miners' Moot secret, and if Eldest Ketil learns, both may be cast out of the hall.
hooks: Kolgrim fights alone and may die of it.
Valdis is bound to a giant who sits with the tribute-folk.
The Pair-Yard needs new champions before the Thing of 1106.

FX09-005.name: the Spearwick family
FX09-005.title: Sergeant of the Skarfell Hall Spearmen
FX09-005.arms: a grey spear between two black giant's hands, on white

military.office: Sergeants of the Skarfell Hall Spearmen
military.unit: 25 tribute-folk spearmen of Skarfell Hall
military.ties: Spearwick men have guarded the giants' knees with spears since the halls first put tribute-folk at their flanks, and they lead the 25 Hall Spearmen of Skarfell.

FX09-005.power: Command of Skarfell Hall's 25 human spearmen, the giants' trust, and a cottage at Koldal with a spear over the door.
FX09-005.history: Giants fight back to back, and what kills a giant is a man with a knife at the back of the knee, so the halls have always put human spearmen at their flanks. Since the Thanes' Raid the Spearwicks of Koldal, tin-diggers by birth, have led Skarfell Hall's spearmen. They stood at Thrand the Broad's flanks when drunk Northreach sailors rioted at the fair in 1088, and a Spearwick took a knife meant for his partner Gerd. The family is proud of its giants and bound to them by the Oath of the Six Winters like every tribute-folk family. In 1105 the Miners' Moot is asking the tribute-folk to strike the summer fair, and the Spearwicks would be the ones ordered to break the strike.
FX09-005.reputation: The giants' own humans: brave, loyal and caught in the middle.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Skarfell Hall Spearmen
members.note: He took the knife meant for Gerd of Helstad in 1088 and has a scar from ear to collarbone to show for it.

members.role: Hesketh's wife
members.note: Two of her brothers died in the Torvik pit collapse of 1071, and she wants the right to leave the island.

members.role: Heir; spearman
members.note: He has been to three meetings of the Miners' Moot and has not told his father.

members.role: Hesketh's daughter; nurse at Skarfell Hall
members.note: She nursed a sick giant child through the winter of 1104 and is the only human the child will let near her.

famousDead: First sergeant of the Skarfell spearmen after the Thanes' Raid.
FX09-005.secret: Edric goes to the Miners' Moot and has promised Colm Ashby that the Skarfell spearmen will not break a strike.
hooks: If the Miners' Moot strikes the fair, the Spearwicks must choose.
Gerda is trusted by a giant child.
Maren wants to leave the island.

FX09-006.name: the Kolfell household
FX09-006.title: Herd-Master of Kolfell
FX09-006.arms: a brown bull mammoth under a white star, on green
FX09-006.power: The herding of Haugberg's Thunder Mammoths, which haul every great timber on the island, and the teams no other household can drive.
FX09-006.history: The 900 Thunder Mammoths of Frostholm haul every great timber on the island, and the household of Kolfell has herded them for Haugberg for as long as the chant names its herders. Kolfell giants name each calf and count it like a child, and they can turn a team of twelve with their voices. In 1085 Kolfell teams hauled the roof timbers for Skarfell Hall, a favour Eldest Bergthor has reminded the halls of at every Thing since. In 1080 Northreach traders saw the mammoths at work and were laughed at when they told it at home, which the household still finds funny. In 1105 the herd's lead cow is old and her calves are few, and the household fears the herd is shrinking the way the giants are.
FX09-006.reputation: Gentle giants among giants, happier with mammoths than with anyone at the Thing.

members.role: Head of the household; Herd-Master of Kolfell
members.note: He can name all 900 mammoths and knows which ones hate each other.

members.role: Heir; driver of the timber teams
members.note: She drove the team that hauled Skarfell Hall's roof-tree in 1085, the youngest driver ever trusted with it.

members.role: Bergdis's son
members.note: At fifteen he has made friends with a Northreach trader's boy who wants to buy a mammoth calf for the King of Northreach.

famousDead: Drove the mammoths that hauled Torvik Hall's great beams after the storm of 951.
FX09-006.secret: Bergthor has asked the household to drive the mammoths to the Thingvold in 1106 to show Haugberg's strength, and Haugstein has quietly promised a calf to Kingsmere's Amber Guild as a gift.
hooks: The mammoth herd is shrinking.
Bergthor wants the mammoths at the Thing of 1106.
A Northreach boy wants to buy a calf.

FX09-007.name: the Skalholm household
FX09-007.title: Keeper of the Ice Shrine of Dagberg
FX09-007.arms: a white whale's tail under a blue arch of ice, on grey
FX09-007.power: The Ice Shrine of Dagberg, the leading of the Whale Thanking on the south coast, and the blessing of the dead before they are given to the sea.
FX09-007.history: The Ice Shrine of Dagberg is a cave of blue ice in the hills above Skarfell where the halls say the Mother Under the Ice can hear her children, and the household of Skalholm has kept it as long as the chant remembers. Skalholm giants lead the Whale Thanking when a whale strands on the south coast, cut the first flesh and give the Mother her share back to the sea. They keep the whale-bone arch at the shrine's mouth and bless the halls' dead before they are given to the sea from the capes. The household is small, seven giants, and has had no child in forty years. Its eldest has begun to teach the rites to a tribute-folk girl, which no keeper has ever done.
FX09-007.reputation: Holy, kindly and few; the island loves them and does not visit.

members.role: Head of the household; Keeper of the Ice Shrine of Dagberg
members.note: She has led 31 Whale Thankings and is teaching the rites to a human girl because there is no giant child to teach.

members.role: Heir; whale-cutter
members.note: He thinks giving the rites to a human is the end of the halls and has told the Lore-Chanter so.

members.role: Thorgunn's human pupil, of Koldal
members.note: At fourteen she knows the Whale Thanking by heart and sings it better than Hvalmund.

famousDead: Kept the shrine through hungry winters and gave her own share of the Whale Thanking to the tribute-folk.
FX09-007.secret: Thorgunn has decided that if no giant child is born to Skalholm, the shrine will pass to Linnet, and she has told no hall.
hooks: A human girl may become keeper of a giant shrine.
The next stranded whale will show who leads the Thanking.
Hvalmund wants the Lore-Chanter to stop it.

FX09-008.name: the Tinwash family
FX09-008.title: Clerk of the Skarfell fair
FX09-008.arms: three grey tin bars on white, painted on their door
FX09-008.power: The clerkship of the Skarfell tin fair under the Northreach Tin Reeves, wages in Northreach silver, and a hidden book of true weights.
FX09-008.history: Since the Tin Compact of 1002 the Northreach Tin Reeves have kept the weights and tallies of the Skarfell fair, and since 1003 the Tinwash family of Koldal has done their counting. The Tinwashes are tribute-folk who learned Northfolk letters from the traders and became the Reeves' clerks, the only islanders paid in Northreach silver. They weigh every bar the halls sell, write every tally and know to the ounce how much grain comes back. They also know that the Reeves' weights have been light by one part in twelve since 1050, because they were told to use them. When Colm Ashby showed the halls his tallies, the Tinwashes said nothing, and the island has not decided whether they are cheats or prisoners.
FX09-008.reputation: Clever, careful and distrusted by everyone, including the people who pay them.

members.role: Head of the family; Clerk of the Skarfell fair
members.note: He has used the light weights for forty summers and keeps the true figures in a second book under his floor.

members.role: Heir; under-clerk
members.note: She gave Colm Ashby a copy of one season's true tally in 1099, and her father thinks it was a stranger.

members.role: Ingram's son
members.note: He wants to go to Wolfhaven as a Reeve's clerk, which no tribute-folk may do without his hall's leave.

famousDead: First islander to keep the Reeves' tallies, from 1003.
FX09-008.secret: Ingram's second book holds the true weights of fifty-five years of tin, enough to prove Northreach owes the halls a fortune.
hooks: The second book could break the Tin Compact.
Elswyth has already given away one tally.
Wendel wants to leave the island.

FX09-009.name: the Oilcroft family
FX09-009.title: Master of the Heldal try-pots
FX09-009.arms: a black try-pot over white waves, on buff
FX09-009.words: Nothing of the whale is wasted.
FX09-009.power: The try-pots of the western coves, the whale and seal oil sold at the summer fair, and the trust of Helstad Hall.
FX09-009.history: When a whale strands on Helstad's shore, the giants thank the Mother and the Oilcrofts boil it. The family has rendered whale and seal oil in the western coves since the Six Winters, when the halls fed the stranded tin-diggers on whale fat and the diggers learned to make lamp oil from the rest. Their try-pots stand on the beach below Heldal, and their oil goes to Eldergrove's longships and Northreach's lamps at the summer fair. Helstad has always lived closest to its humans, and Oilcroft women have nursed Helstad giant children through fevers for generations. The family's head is the richest of the tribute-folk and still may not leave the island.
FX09-009.reputation: Smoky, prosperous and kind; the human family Helstad calls its own.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Heldal try-pots
members.note: He sells oil to Eldergrove captains who pay him in silver he hides from the Tin Reeve.

members.role: Heir; nurse of Helstad Hall
members.note: Her mother nursed Hauk of Helstad through the fever that nearly killed him, and he calls Aldith sister.

members.role: Godric's son
members.note: He wants to sail on an Eldergrove longship, and a captain has offered to take him if he can get off the island.

FX09-009.secret: Godric has hidden 400 suns of Eldergrove silver under the try-pots, enough to buy passage off the island for his whole family.
hooks: Godric's hidden silver is a crime under the compact.
Cuthbert wants to run away to sea.
A whale stranding will bring the whole hall to the beach.

FX09-010.name: the Gullstrand family
FX09-010.title: Boat-master of the Ragvik coves
FX09-010.arms: no arms; a gull's foot cut into a boat's thwart
FX09-010.power: Three skin-covered boats in the Ragvik coves, the moonless-night route to the Amber Capes, and the gratitude of sixty runaways.
FX09-010.history: The Tin Compact closes Frostholm to runaways, and since 1002 the coves of Ragvik have been where the island's rules are broken. The Gullstrands are a fisher family of the Ragvik coves who row tin, ivory and runaways across to the Amber Capes in skin-covered boats on moonless nights. They were at it before Yrsa Blackpenny, the famous smuggler, and they resent that the tavern songs are about her. Since 1102 the shore watch has let more boats pass than it stops, and the Gullstrands have grown bold. In 1105 the Miners' Moot wants them to carry a letter to Kingsmere, and the family has never carried anything that could hang it so high.
FX09-010.reputation: Brave night-rowers to the tribute-folk; thieves and oath-breakers to the Reeves.

members.role: Head of the family; boat-master of the Ragvik coves
members.note: He has rowed 61 runaways to the Amber Capes and lost two to the sea.

members.role: Heir; his daughter
members.note: She has made a friend of a small Lindholm runner who warns her when the watch looks her way.

members.role: Brand's brother
members.note: He talks about the family's sailings to the Tin Reeve's men when he drinks, and Brand has started to suspect.

famousDead: Brand's mother; drowned rowing a runaway family to the Amber Capes.
FX09-010.secret: Oswy sells the family's sailings to the Tin Reeve's men, and two of the runaway families caught in 1099 were his betrayal.
hooks: The Miners' Moot wants a letter carried to Kingsmere.
Oswy is selling his own family.
Yrsa Blackpenny is a rival for every moonless night.

FX10-001.name: Clan Ironroot
FX10-001.title: Thane of Vardal
FX10-001.arms: a black root twisted through three iron bars, on grey

military.office: Thanes of Vardal and captains of its hold-ward
military.unit: the Vardal hold-ward, 600 at levy
military.ties: Ironroot sons serve their thirty years in the Deep Gate Wardens, and the clan raises the largest single levy of the Deep Halls.

FX10-001.power: The old Vardal galleries, now a quarter of the Deep Halls; a thane's seat on the Council of Masters; and the largest clan levy in the hold.
FX10-001.history: Vardal was the first hall the dwarves of Stonehold cut in the Iron Mountains about 1900 BR, and the Ironroots were its hall-masters for 2,500 years before Korrin Deepeye was born. In 610 the clan was the last of the fourteen to accept Korrin's offer of a share of the great seam, and it took the title of thane as its price. The Ironroots have sat on the Council of Masters since and have never quite forgiven the Deepeyes for being younger. Their old gallery walls are still carved with the names of hall-masters who sent tithes to the First Hall before Irondeep had a king. In 1105 the thane has carved his name under Korrin Deepeye's petition to set Queen Brynja aside, the first great clan to do so.
FX10-001.reputation: Old, proud and touchy about it; the clan that reminds the Deepeyes who was here first.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of Vardal
members.note: He carved his name under Korrin's petition and told the queen to her face that he did it.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Vardal hold-ward
members.note: She thinks her father has bet the clan on a prince who will forget who stood with him.

members.role: Bergljot's son; journeyman of the Deep Gate Wardens
members.note: He drills under Harrek Stonejaw and has seen the Gate-Warden slip out to the carters' camp at night.

members.role: Ragnvald's uncle; old hall-master
members.note: At 225 he is the oldest dwarf in Irondeep and remembers the last lamellar train going down the valley in 911.

famousDead: Last hall-master of Vardal; accepted Korrin's seam in 610 and took the first thane's ring.
FX10-001.secret: Asbjorn walked beside the last lamellar train of 911 and has told his nephew everything; the Ironroots mean to use Bodvar's secret if Korrin's petition fails.
hooks: The Founding of 3 March may make or break the clan's bet on Korrin.
Hjalti knows where the Gate-Warden goes at night.
Old Asbjorn could testify to the arms sales of 896 to 911.

FX10-002.name: Clan Silverseam
FX10-002.title: Thane of the Contract Crews
FX10-002.arms: a silver seam running through a green hill, on black
FX10-002.power: Leadership of the 8,400 Irondeep dwarves who work the Highland League's silver mines for a fifth of the silver, and a thane's seat on the Council for them.
FX10-002.history: The Silverseams were deep miners of the Ore Shelf until 1060, when Queen Brynja sent the first contract crews to the Highland League's silver mines and Thorgils Silverseam led the first 900 down the road to Amberhurst. The crews take a fifth of every ounce they raise, and 8,400 Irondeep dwarves work the League's mines in 1105, the largest body of dwarves living outside a hold. The clan's head carries the title of thane for them and sits on the Council for miners who have not seen the Deep Halls in years. In 1104 a Silverseam crew driving a drainage tunnel under Redford found the richest silver vein the League has known. Silver flows home to the clan, and so do questions about what crews who live among humans are teaching them.
FX10-002.reputation: Rich, worldly and a little foreign; the Council calls them the League's dwarves.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of the Contract Crews
members.note: He has spent more of his life under Highland hills than under his own, and his Holdspeech has a League accent.

members.role: Heir; master of the Redford crew
members.note: She found the Redford vein and has sent home only half of what it gave.

members.role: Halla's son; crew miner
members.note: He has married a human woman at Amberhurst in a League temple, and their child will be a stonebairn barred from every hold.

FX10-002.secret: Halla keeps half the Redford silver in a League strongroom under a human name, against the day the crews are called home.
hooks: The Redford vein makes the clan rich and the League hungry.
Vigfus's stonebairn child is due in spring.
Orsa Flintmark suspects the crews have taught the League more than mining.

FX10-003.name: Clan Orehand
FX10-003.title: Thane of the Othdal Landings
FX10-003.arms: a black weigh-beam over a blue river, on a grey and blue chequy field
FX10-003.power: The river landings below Othdal where the Iron Road meets the Eagleburg barges, the landing fee on every bar, and the trust of Aldmark's barge-masters.
FX10-003.history: The Orehands were hall-masters of the lowest of the fourteen halls, and in 951 King Arnulf gave them the keeping of the river landings below Othdal, where the Iron Road meets the barges for Eagleburg. For 150 years every bar of iron Aldmark has bought has crossed an Orehand weigh-beam, and the clan has grown rich on the landing fee. The landings lie in sight of Aldmark's Bramton Keep, and the Orehands know Aldmark's captains better than any dwarf living. In the hungry winter of 1088 the thane arranged the grain barges that fed the hold, and the queen raised him to a thane's seat for it. In December 1104 he carried Queen Brynja's sealed letter down to the landings himself.
FX10-003.reputation: Smooth, rich and too comfortable with humans, say the clans who never leave the mountain.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of the Othdal Landings
members.note: He carried the queen's letter of December 1104 and weighed its seal in his hand like an ingot.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the weigh-beam
members.note: She has learned that Aldmark's barge-masters short the weight by one bar in forty, and has said nothing because her father takes a share.

members.role: Gudmund's younger son
members.note: He drinks with the Bramton Keep garrison and has started to think the hold would be safer as Aldmark's friend than as Aldmark's creditor.

members.role: Jorunn's daughter; weigh-clerk
members.note: She is in love with a Slatebrow crossbowman of the middle fort, whose clan despises hers.

famousDead: First keeper of the landings; built the weigh-beam in 951.
FX10-003.secret: Gudmund takes a share of the bar in forty that the barge-masters steal with false weights, and the handover of the lower fort will make him richer still.
hooks: Four hundred Aldmark soldiers come to the lower fort on 1 March, beside the Orehand landings.
Jorunn knows about the false weights.
Bard is a ready tool for Aldmark.

FX10-004.name: Clan Slatebrow
FX10-004.title: Castellan of the Middle Fort
FX10-004.arms: a black crossbow bolt point down on grey slate, a red border

military.office: Castellans of the Middle Fort of the Iron Road
military.unit: the Storgrund crossbows, 140 of the Iron Road Guard
military.ties: A Slatebrow has held the middle fort at Storgrund since the road was built in 951, under the Captain of the Iron Road guard, and every Slatebrow child learns the windlass before the runes.

FX10-004.power: The middle fort at Storgrund, 140 crossbows of the Iron Road Guard, and the halfway point of every iron train between the Deep Gate and the river.
FX10-004.history: When King Arnulf built the Iron Road in 951 he put three forts on it, and the middle one at Storgrund went to Thurid Slatebrow, a crossbow sergeant who had shot wolves off the iron trains for forty years. Her clan has held it since: 140 crossbows in a stone tower over the road, halfway between the Deep Gate and the river. Slatebrows have fought road thieves and Pinewild outlaws, and in 1094 a Slatebrow cousin died beside Harrek Stonejaw killing robbers at the upper fort. They are Captain Torsten Grimhelm's most trusted crossbows and know about the bolts he sold Northreach's hird in 1091, because they packed them. In 1105 they will not hand the road to Aldmark, whatever the queen has signed.
FX10-004.reputation: Hard, loyal fort-dwarves who would sooner shoot than bargain.

members.role: Head of the clan; Castellan of the Middle Fort
members.note: He has held Storgrund for sixty years and has told Captain Grimhelm he will shoot the first Aldmark soldier who climbs past the lower fort.

members.role: Heir; windlass-sergeant
members.note: She packed the 2,000 bolts that went to Northreach's hird in 1091 and has kept the tally stick.

members.role: Valka's son; crossbowman
members.note: He is in love with Dagrun Orehand, whose clan is about to welcome Aldmark to the lower fort.

famousDead: First Castellan of the Middle Fort (951).
Died beside Harrek Stonejaw fighting road thieves at the upper fort.
FX10-004.secret: Valka keeps the tally stick of the 2,000 bolts sold to Northreach in 1091; it could bring the Judgment of the First Hall down on Irondeep.
hooks: Steinar may refuse the queen's order to let Aldmark troops up the road.
Valka's tally stick is wanted by the Law-Carver and by Stonehold.
Ospak loves a daughter of the clan his grandfather despises.

FX10-005.name: Clan Duskdelve
FX10-005.title: Captain of the Night Trains
FX10-005.arms: a gold lantern flame on black

military.office: Captains of the Night Train escort
military.unit: the Night Train escort, 100 heavy foot
military.ties: Duskdelves have walked beside the royal iron trains by night since Queen Gunnhild began the dusk trade with Kingsmere, because a Deepeye cannot bear the sun and the trains must move in the dark.

FX10-005.power: The escort of every royal iron train, a century of the Deepeyes' trust, and two centuries of a secret sung in a walking song.
FX10-005.history: Queen Gunnhild's iron trains went down to Kingsmere by night because a Deepeye could not bear the sun, and from 790 the Duskdelves walked beside them in breastplates with war-picks. The clan has escorted every royal train since: three centuries of mules, shuttered lanterns and frost on the Ore Shelf road. From 896 to 911 Duskdelve sergeants walked beside the trains that carried 14,000 sets of lamellar to the Wind Empire's dealers, and they were sworn to silence on poured metal. The clan has kept the oath for two centuries and taught each new captain a walking song that counts the loads of every one of those nights. In 1105 the trains carry less each month, and the escort's captain has started to wonder whom the oath protects.
FX10-005.reputation: Night-walkers, close-mouthed and loyal to the crown past the point of sense.

members.role: Head of the clan; Captain of the Night Trains
members.note: He can sing the walking song of 896 to 911 load by load, and he has never sung it above a whisper.

members.role: Heir; train sergeant
members.note: She has noticed that the trains since 1100 carry fewer bars than the tallies say.

members.role: Finna's son; recruit of the escort
members.note: He has been offered a place in a Northreach smith's hall by a carter who knows too much about him.

famousDead: Walked the last lamellar train down the valley in 911 and died that winter.
FX10-005.secret: The walking song counts every load of lamellar sold to the Wind Empire, night by night, and the Law-Carver would give a great deal to hear it.
hooks: Finna has found bars missing from the night trains.
Orsa Flintmark wants the walking song.
Atli is being courted by a stranger from the carters' camp.

FX10-006.name: Clan Steelbrow
FX10-006.title: Warden of the Ore Shelf
FX10-006.arms: a black eagle on a grey crag, on white
FX10-006.words: Under the sky, for the rock.

military.office: Wardens of the Ore Shelf
military.unit: the Ore Shelf Watch, 100 scouts
military.ties: They watch the open pits and quarries above the Deep Halls, and since Aldmark's Iron Road Company began prospecting east of the Shelf they have been the hold's eyes on the hills.

FX10-006.power: The Ore Shelf Watch, the only dwarves of Irondeep who live under the sky, and the knowledge of every human who has climbed above the Deep Halls.
FX10-006.history: Since Queen Gunnhild swore in 744 that no Deepeye would ever sell raw ore, the Steelbrows have watched the Ore Shelf to see that none leaves it. Their hundred scouts walk the open pits and limestone quarries above the Deep Halls in every weather, and they spend more of their lives under the sky than any other dwarves of Irondeep. Since 1100 they have watched the Iron Road Company's prospectors dig test shafts in the hills east of the Shelf. In October 1104 a Steelbrow scout saw Sapper-Master Vigdis Coalbrow's crew open the sluice that flooded the company's shaft, and three human miners drowned. The clan has reported it to no one, and Vigdis knows the scout's name.
FX10-006.reputation: Weathered, honest and odd; dwarves who like the wind.

members.role: Head of the clan; Warden of the Ore Shelf
members.note: He once stood on the Shelf in a blizzard for three days to watch one human prospector, and was proved right.

members.role: Heir; scout-captain
members.note: She wants her father to report the drowned shaft to the Law-Carver, and he will not.

members.role: Scout; the one who saw
members.note: He watched Vigdis Coalbrow's crew open the sluice and has had a Coalbrow sapper at his elbow in every ale-hall since.

famousDead: First Warden of the Ore Shelf (744).
FX10-006.secret: A Steelbrow scout saw the Coalbrow sappers flood the Aldmark shaft in October 1104, and the clan's silence is the only thing between Vigdis Coalbrow and exile.
hooks: Sindri's word could exile the Sapper-Master.
Aldmark is looking for whoever drowned its miners.
The prospectors will be back east of the Shelf in spring.

FX10-007.name: Clan Copperbraid
FX10-007.title: Factor of the Rinael Trade
FX10-007.arms: a copper sun over a gold honeycomb, on green
FX10-007.power: The honey-for-iron trade with Sylvaran at the forest edge, the oldest trade either people keeps, and the carts and carters who run it every summer.
FX10-007.history: Copperbraids have weighed iron against honey at the forest edge since before Irondeep had a king, and the clan says an ancestor held the scales when King Faeron of Sylvaran agreed the trade. Every summer their carters take knives, axe-heads and nails down the two roads the Moot allows, and every autumn they bring back honey, wax and furs on the same carts. The trade is small beside the Iron Road but it is the oldest either people keeps, and the clan is proud that no elf has ever accused a Copperbraid scale. Since Aldmark began to pay late the clan has sided with Trade-Warden Ulla Stonecount's Open Road, which wants more buyers and fewer masters. In 1105 it wants a second market: elven honey sold on to Northreach, which pays in silver.
FX10-007.reputation: The friendliest traders in the mountains, and the only dwarves elves will drink with.

members.role: Head of the clan; Factor of the Rinael Trade
members.note: He has dealt with three generations of Wrenwings and speaks Sylvari badly but sincerely.

members.role: Heir; master of the honey carts
members.note: She has been selling honey on to Northreach for two years under the Open Road's rules and the Council's nose.

members.role: Gudny's son; carter
members.note: He swaps arrowheads with a young elf of the road wardens, a friendship his grandfather pretends not to see.

famousDead: Held the scales at Rinael when King Faeron of Sylvaran agreed the honey-for-iron trade.
FX10-007.secret: The honey Gudny sells to Northreach goes on to Wolfhaven's hird as mead money, and Ulla Stonecount takes a tenth of it for her Open Road.
hooks: Irondeep still owes the Wrenwings for sixty carts of honey from 1088, and the debt sits in the Copperbraid books.
Gudny's Northreach trade could anger Aldmark.
Geir's friendship with an elf breaks no law yet.

FX10-008.name: Clan Mallethand
FX10-008.title: Master of the Wire Hall
FX10-008.arms: a silver mallet over a ring of mail, on black
FX10-008.power: The Wire Hall and its draw-plates, a quarter of Irondeep's finished mail, and the oldest wire-drawing secret in the Westland.
FX10-008.history: Irondeep's mail is famous because its rings are drawn, not hammered, and the Mallethands have drawn the wire since 690, pulling hot iron through ever smaller holes in a hardened plate until it is fine enough to weave. The draw-plates are the clan's treasure and its secret: each hole was punched and polished by a master, and a good plate is handed down for four generations. A quarter of the hold's finished mail is Mallethand mail, and Aldmark's knights have worn it since 951. The trade has made the clan proud and careful, and it watched with horror in 1103 when a Brightanvil journeyman showed a human smith a trip-hammer. In 1105 the clan's own best journeyman has been asking where the old plates are kept.
FX10-008.reputation: Masters of fine work who trust no one, least of all their apprentices.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Wire Hall
members.note: He sleeps with the clan's oldest draw-plate under his pillow, which is uncomfortable, and he does it anyway.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the draw-benches
members.note: She wants to draw steel wire for crossbow strings, which no dwarf has done, and her father says it cannot be done.

members.role: Journeyman of the Wire Hall
members.note: He is Eyvind Coldforge's drinking companion and has begun to say that keeping secrets is a crime.

famousDead: Punched the first draw-plate of Irondeep in 690.
FX10-008.secret: Egil has copied the holes of the clan's second draw-plate onto a lead sheet and hidden it in the carters' camp.
hooks: Egil may be the next journeyman to leak a dwarven secret.
Oddbjorg's steel wire could change every crossbow in the world.
Aldmark wants more mail on credit, and the clan wants payment first.

FX10-009.name: Clan Runecut
FX10-009.title: Warden of the Ancestor Vaults
FX10-009.arms: a grey cross of chisel and lamp, on black
FX10-009.power: The ancestor vaults under the Deep Halls, the name-stones of every dwarf who has died in Irondeep, and the vault rolls that settle every claim of kinship.
FX10-009.history: The dead go into the rock, the first law says, and since Korrin's first hall the Runecuts have cut the tombs and the names. Each dwarf is sealed into the ancestor vaults under the Deep Halls with the name-stone carved at thirty, and when the Law-Carver exiles a dwarf, a Runecut grinds that name out of the vault so the dead will not know him. The clan ground out the furnace-seller's name in 1060 at Orsa Flintmark's order. It keeps the vault rolls, which are also the hold's genealogies, and every claim of kinship in Irondeep ends with a Runecut reading a wall. In 1105 the vaults are nearly full, and the clan has quietly begun cutting a new gallery under the old Vardal hall without the Council's leave.
FX10-009.reputation: Grave, dusty and incorruptible; the clan every dwarf will meet in the end.

members.role: Head of the clan; Warden of the Ancestor Vaults
members.note: He ground out the name of 1060 himself and has had a stone-dust cough ever since.

members.role: Heir; reader of the walls
members.note: She has found a name-stone in the deepest vault that was ground out and carved again, and the name is Deepeye.

members.role: Steinunn's son; tomb-cutter
members.note: He is cutting the new gallery under Vardal and has broken into a cave pool the old miners walled off.

famousDead: Cut King Korrin Deepeye's tomb in 715 and was paid with his first ingot.
FX10-009.secret: A Deepeye name in the deepest vault was ground out once and carved again, and the vault roll says it was King Bodvar's.
hooks: Ingolf has broken into a walled-off cave pool, which the law of 780 forbids.
Steinunn's re-carved name could reopen Bodvar's crime.
The vaults are full and the Council has not been told.

FX10-010.name: Clan Seamfinder
FX10-010.title: Master Assayer of Irondeep
FX10-010.arms: a black seam in bend across a white field, a red flame above
FX10-010.power: The office of Master Assayer, every survey of the rock under the Deep Halls, and the queen's private trust.
FX10-010.history: Korrin Deepeye found the great seam with sixty test pits and a fire-test of every ore, and the Seamfinders were the assayers who tested it for him from 599 to 609. The clan has assayed every seam of Irondeep since, judging iron by the color of its fire, the ring of its bloom and the weight of its ash. Its surveyors know the shape of the rock under the Deep Halls better than any map. In 1101 the clan finished a survey of Korrin's great seam, and its head has shown it only to the queen. The seam that has fed Irondeep for 495 years has about forty years of good ore left.
FX10-010.reputation: Quiet, exact and slightly sad; the clan that knows how much is left.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master Assayer of Irondeep
members.note: He has tasted ore from every gallery in the hold and can tell Dunheim iron from Vardal iron with his tongue.

members.role: Heir; surveyor of the deep galleries
members.note: She made the survey of 1101 and wants the Council told, because forty years is not long for a dwarf.

members.role: Dalla's son; prospector
members.note: He walked east of the Ore Shelf in 1103 and found what Aldmark's prospectors are looking for, and he has not said where.

famousDead: Fire-tested Korrin's sixty pits from 599 to 609.
FX10-010.secret: Korrin's great seam has about forty years of good ore left, and only the queen and the Seamfinders know. Gunnar knows where the next one lies, east of the Shelf, under ground Aldmark is prospecting.
hooks: The survey of 1101 could change every vote on the Council.
Gunnar's new seam lies where Aldmark is digging.
The queen may silence the clan to keep the hold calm.

FX10-011.name: the Ruddock family
FX10-011.title: Yard-boss of the carters' camp
FX10-011.arms: no arms; a nail bent into a hook, scratched on their carts
FX10-011.power: The night trade of the carters' camp outside the Deep Gate: a dozen carts with false bottoms, buyers in the Pinewild and Northreach, and the loyalty of stonebairn children no hold will take.
FX10-011.history: About 5,000 humans live in the carters' camp outside the Deep Gate, hauling iron down the valleys for wages, and since the 1060s the Ruddocks have run what the camp does after dark. They began as honest carters and turned to buying whatever slips out of the hold: a pocket of nails, a broken mail shirt, a journeyman's pouch of offcuts, sold on to Pinewild outlaws and Northreach smiths. The boss's grandfather rushed the carters' gate with the Pinewild outlaws in 1041 and died under Harrek Stonejaw's spear. The family also shelters stonebairn children, half-dwarf and barred from the halls, and puts them to work. In 1105 the Ruddocks hold a lead sheet with the holes of a Mallethand draw-plate on it and have a Northreach buyer who wants it.
FX10-011.reputation: Every carter owes them something, and every Gate Warden knows their faces.

members.role: Yard-boss of the carters' camp
members.note: He has never been inside the Deep Gate and knows more about what goes on there than most thanes.

members.role: His wife; fence
members.note: She keeps the stolen iron in the false bottoms of honest carts and the accounts in her head.

members.role: Garth's brother; carter
members.note: He has been courting a young Duskdelve of the night escort with the offer of a place in a Northreach smithy.

members.role: Their foster son, a stonebairn
members.note: His father was a dwarf of the Wire Hall he has never met, and he is strong enough to bend a horseshoe.

famousDead: Garth's grandfather; died rushing the carters' gate with the Pinewild outlaws.
FX10-011.secret: They hold a lead copy of a Mallethand draw-plate, and Tofi, the Gate-Warden's stonebairn son, drinks at their fire.
hooks: A Northreach buyer is coming for the draw-plate copy.
Brand wants to know his dwarf father.
The Gate Wardens may sweep the camp after the Founding.

FX11-001.name: The Redmare line
FX11-001.title: Chief of the Ughgar camps
FX11-001.arms: a red mare rearing on black horse-hide, a small ochre hand at her hoof
FX11-001.words: Ask the herd, not the hide.

military.office: Lance-captains of the Redhand war-band at Ughgar
military.unit: the Ughgar Six Hundred, lance and bow on Magak horses
military.ties: Their 600 riders are the Redhand war-band's summer guard on the Ughgar grass, and they would ride first if the Old Clans took the staff by force.

FX11-001.power: About 22,000 horses on the Ughgar river grass and 600 standing riders, the second herd of the Magak clans after the Redhands' own.
FX11-001.history: The Redmares are the oldest of the Magak kin-bands that moved onto the Ughgar river grass when Gorzak Redhand swore to Gorath for it in 1036. Their founder Hrogash broke a red mare that had killed two riders and led the first Magak herds east past the Gorur wells on her. Like the Redhands they pass the chiefship from uncle to sister's son, and every new chief swears at Gorza's mound on the Gulgar Tooth. They lost 140 riders in the feud of the Krugak wells and paid a ninth of the 900 horses of 1086, and every Redmare child can recite the Goroth kin who took them. Since 1102 Redmare mares have made up most of the 600 horses Gorm the Trader drove over the Gordush to Aldmark's Millrun breeders. In 1105 the Redmares count clans for Skarn Redhand's bid at the Great Ride.
FX11-001.reputation: Rich, touchy and loud at every Great Ride; the Goroth clans call them 'the Khan's grooms' for what their ancestors did in 875.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Ughgar camps
members.note: Keeps the Aldmark silver in a pit under his winter tent and sleeps on top of it.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Redmare kin; Ozrak's sister
members.note: Her son is the heir by custom, and she has already chosen his first wife.

members.role: Heir by the sister's-son custom; rider of the Ughgar Six Hundred
members.note: Rides at Hurn Firebrand's side whenever he can and dreams of the first wave.

members.role: Grazha's daughter; herd-girl of the Ughgar remounts
members.note: Meets a rider of the Goroth well-keepers at the summer camps, the kin her uncle has sworn to hate.

members.role: Ozrak's wife; keeper of the line's tally of horses
members.note: Counts every horse Gorm buys and knows the line has sold more than Skarn thinks.

famousDead: Broke the red mare and led the Magak herds onto the Ughgar grass in 1036; died at the Gordush Bend.
Chief of the camps who rode away from Durgash with the Redhands in 1058 and came back after Kyzai.
FX11-001.secret: In 1103 Ozrak paid a braid-girl of the Grey Mothers 40 suns to tell him what the old Redhand hide shows; she told him about the small knife in its corner, and he has told no one, not even Skarn.
hooks: Ishka wants to marry a rider of the Goroth kin who killed her great-uncle in the Krugak feud.
The braid-girl who took Redmare silver is asking for more, and the Grey Mothers are asking who paid her.
Gorm's Aldmark buyers want 300 more Redmare mares before May Fair.

FX11-002.name: The Ashbrow line
FX11-002.title: Clan-Mother of the Glenwash-edge kin-bands
FX11-002.arms: a grey thumb-smear of ash across a dun hide, over three white ford-stones
FX11-002.words: We burned our dead. We remember where.

military.office: Night-raiders of the Gashmar fords
military.unit: the Ashbrow hundred, 140 riders of the Gashmar war-band
military.ties: They ride in Garnak Stonehoof's 3,600 on the lower Gordush, and their young riders cross the fords each spring to count the fires of the Aldmark forts.

FX11-002.power: Four kin-bands, about 3,800 people and 5,000 horses on the hay bottoms of the Glenwash edge, and the trust of the Stonehoof war-captain.
FX11-002.history: The Ashbrows were a Gashmar kin-band of no name until the Gashmar Fords on 17 June 1070, when Conrad's heavy horse broke the line and about 3,000 orcs died. Mother Druka's mother smeared her brow with the ash of the Gashmar pyres and would not wash it off for a year, and the kin has carried the name since. The kin adopts captives and runaways more than any other on the fords, and in 1094 it took in an Aldmark spearman who had deserted Crossmarch after his lord hanged his half-orc wife under the License Law. Since the autumn of 1103 the Ashbrows have fed about 150 of Tarn Halfblood's guests from their own herds under the Law of the Fire. Their hay is short, their horses thin, and they want the war before their winter stores run out.
FX11-002.reputation: Poor, hard and generous; the kin that never turns a stranger from its fire, and never forgets a dead rider.

members.role: Head of the line; Clan-Mother of the Glenwash-edge kin-bands
members.note: Still wears a grey ash mark on each Return Day and makes her grandchildren wear it too.

members.role: Druka's brother; captain of the Ashbrow hundred
members.note: Has crossed the Gordush by night 30 times and counted every Aldmark fire on a knotted thong.

members.role: Adopted son of the kin; former Aldmark spearman of Crossmarch
members.note: A human with filed-down orc manners who knows every stake at the Crossmarch fords, because he drove some of them.

members.role: Druka's daughter and heir
members.note: Keeps the guest-tally of every Halfblood fed at Ashbrow fires and means to send the bill to the war-chief.

members.role: Druka's youngest son; rider of the hundred
members.note: Came home in November smelling of pitch and has not looked his mother in the eye since.

famousDead: Smeared her brow with the pyre ash of the Gashmar Fords in 1070 and gave the kin its name.
FX11-002.secret: Thokk rode with Hurn Firebrand when the Gashmar ferry was burned in November 1104, the burning blamed on Tarn's Halfbloods whom his own mother feeds.
hooks: Garnak Stonehoof asks for Edric to guide his riders over the fords before May Fair, against the war-chief's order.
A Halfblood rider learns who really burned the ferry.
The Ashbrow hay runs out in March and Mother Shura will not open the Urgol stores to Tarn's guests.

FX11-003.name: The Owlmask drummers
FX11-003.title: Keeper of the Great Drum of the Drum Lodge
FX11-003.arms: an eagle-owl's face painted on a drum-skin, on storm grey
FX11-003.power: The hereditary keeping of the Great Drum and 120 of the Drum Lodge's 400 drummers, a herd of about 4,000 horses and a seat in the Drum Council that confirms war-chiefs.
FX11-003.history: The Owlmasks have drummed at the Drum Stones since the clans rode back with Old Mother Shagra on 21 June 923. They make the lodge's drums from mare-hide and keep the signal beats that turn a relay wave in the middle of a charge. Their greatest shaman, Oruk Owl-Mask, was the young drummer who wore the eagle-owl mask at the Drum Stones in 1024 when Gorath rode the Thunder Horse, and he trained Harkun the Drum-Master before he died at the lodge in March 1079. The line's herd grew in his lifetime from almost nothing to the 4,000 horses it grazes now in the hill gardens of Rushzag. The family drums for whoever the Grey Mothers name, and says it has no side in the quarrel of the staff. In truth half the young drummers want Tarn Halfblood confirmed and the other half want Skarn.
FX11-003.reputation: Holy, half-deaf and well fed; the clans fear the Owlmasks' drums more than their opinions.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Great Drum; member of the Drum Council
members.note: Oruk's grandson, who has never asked Harkun what the old man whispered on his deathbed, because he is afraid he knows.

members.role: Mogash's wife; mare-hide drum-maker
members.note: Stretches every war-drum of the Horde herself and can tell a bad skin by its smell.

members.role: Heir; first drummer of the Drum Stones lodge
members.note: Believes in the Thunder Horse with all his heart and would drum Vrag into the grave for it.

members.role: Mogash's daughter; apprentice shaman
members.note: Found a tally of 200 horses scratched inside Oruk's old mask and asked her father what it means.

famousDead: As a young drummer wore the eagle-owl mask at the Drum Stones in 1024; later taught Harkun the Drum-Master.
Beat the turn-signal for the reserve at the Gashmar Fords until an Aldmark bolt took him.
FX11-003.secret: The Owlmask herd grew from 200 horses that Gorath's kin paid Oruk Owl-Mask for wearing the mask while they drove a wild herd past the stones in 1024.
hooks: Zurka shows the scratched tally to a Tusk drummer at the Great Ride.
The Drum Council splits, and Mogash's vote decides whether Tarn is confirmed.
Harkun asks Rakh to drum the war-chief's heir at a Great Ride where Vrag may not survive the heat.

FX11-004.name: The Thirdwave line
FX11-004.title: Captain of the Third Wave of Gorath's Hearth Guard
FX11-004.arms: three white lightning strokes, the third the longest, on black hide

military.office: Hereditary captains of the third relay wave of Gorath's Hearth Guard
military.unit: the Third Wave, 300 copper-tusked riders of the Hearth Guard
military.ties: Every Thirdwave son caps his tusks with copper at 16 and rides in the Hearth Guard that guards the war-chief and breaks the enemy line in three waves.

FX11-004.power: The captaincy of 300 riders of the Hearth Guard, a share of the hearth's plunder and about 2,500 horses in the Urgol hearth herd under the lightning brand.
FX11-004.history: When Gorath founded the Horde at Urgol in 1041 he split his best riders into three relay waves, and gave the third to Ugrash, an Urgol rider who had ridden beside him at Vrakoth in 1028. The third wave comes in when the first two have spent their ten minutes and the enemy thinks it has won. The Thirdwaves have finished Gorath's charges at the Gordush Bend, at the Gashmar Fords and at the Shagnak wells in 1096. They have never held the first wave, which goes to the boldest rider of each generation, now Grask Firstwave. They resent it in silence and drink about it in public. Since 1102 they have seen the war-chief faint twice behind their horse lines and said nothing.
FX11-004.reputation: Steady, loyal and second to no one but the first two waves, which is what eats them.

members.role: Head of the line; Captain of the Third Wave
members.note: Found Vrag fainted behind the horse lines at the Coldbarrow Bridge and swore his riders to silence on the spot.

members.role: Barg's wife; keeper of the Third Wave's remount string
members.note: Changes 900 horses for 300 riders in a fight and has never lost a remount line.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Third Wave
members.note: Has challenged Grask Firstwave to wrestle for the first wave at the next Great Ride.

members.role: Barg's daughter; rider of the Third Wave
members.note: Rode her first charge at the Well of Buroth and saw the war-chief fall white-faced from his horse.

famousDead: First captain of the third wave; died at Hartgate when the stakes held.
Brought the third wave in at the Gashmar Fords and died covering the retreat.
FX11-004.secret: The Thirdwaves know the war-chief has fainted twice after the fury, and Barg has promised Mother Ugra his riders will carry Vrag off any field before the clans see it.
hooks: Gokh wrestles Grask Firstwave for the first wave at the Great Ride of 21 June.
A Redhand rider offers Barg the first wave if the Old Clans take the staff.
Vrag falls again in a charge, and only the Third Wave is close enough to hide it.

FX11-005.name: The Ladderhand line
FX11-005.title: Ladder-Master of the Graknak Ladder Foot
FX11-005.arms: a black ladder leaning on a broken timber wall, on bread brown

military.office: Hereditary ladder-masters of the Graknak Ladder Foot
military.unit: the Ladderhand company, 200 half-orc ladder-men of the Graknak Ladder Foot
military.ties: They build, carry and climb the ladders of the Horde's only siege troops, and every war-chief since Durgash has asked for them by name.

FX11-005.power: The ladder-yard of Graknak, the skill of night escalade that no other kin of the Horde has, and about 1,200 half-orc and adopted kin who winter at the Kagdush gardens.
FX11-005.history: On 4 May 1072 Durgash's ladder parties went over the flood-softened river wall of Graknak by night, with Mogra Ladderfoot first over. The second ladder was carried by Hazga, a half-orc woman of the Upper Gordush who had fled the License Law, and she lost both hands to an axe at the top of it. Her kin took the name Ladderhand for her, and Ushkar the Grey gave them the ladder-yard and a winter ground at the Kagdush gardens. Half the line are half-orcs and adopted humans from across the river, and they break bread before meat as the Upper Gordush clans do. Since 1103 Aldmark's Ravenscar riders have mapped their camps by night. They are the only orcs who have trained for a siege of Crossmarch, and they know it would cost them half their kin.
FX11-005.reputation: Bread-eaters and wall-climbers; mocked by the horse clans until the war-chief needs a wall taken.

members.role: Head of the line; Ladder-Master of the Graknak Ladder Foot
members.note: Hazga's son, half-orc, who measures every wall he sees by the number of rungs it would need.

members.role: Hazrak's wife; adopted daughter of the kin, born in Aldmark
members.note: Bakes the bread of the ladder-yard and has a brother who is a reeve of House Harrow.

members.role: Heir; first climber of the Ladderhand company
members.note: Climbed the old Graknak wall blindfold for a bet and has been looking for a real one ever since.

members.role: Hazrak's daughter; ladder-wright
members.note: Has drawn a folding ladder with iron hooks from a picture an Aldmark smuggler sold her.

famousDead: Carried the second ladder over the Graknak wall in 1072 and lost both hands at the top of it.
FX11-005.secret: Bertha writes to her brother, a reeve of House Harrow, every spring through Jessa Crane's smugglers, and her letters have told Aldmark more than she knows.
hooks: The war-chief asks for ladders against the Crossmarch stake yard before May Fair.
Bertha's brother crosses the river asking for her.
Gruzha's iron-hooked ladder needs Aldmark iron that only smugglers can bring.

FX11-006.name: The Coldbarrow line
FX11-006.title: Keeper of the Nagdur Stockade
FX11-006.arms: a white salt-block under a grey crescent, crossed by a red spear

military.office: Keepers of the Nagdur Stockade and captains of the Coldbarrow watch
military.unit: the Nagdur watch, 400 light riders of the Salt Edge war-band
military.ties: They hold the earth stockade that faces the Nine Winds across the salt flats and ride with the Salt Edge war-band of 2,200 at the Shagnak wells and the Coldbarrow Bridge.

FX11-006.power: The Nagdur stockade and its well, 400 standing riders, and the salt-and-horse trade that crosses the Nine Winds border under their eyes.
FX11-006.history: The Coldbarrows were a Salt Edge kin-band of salt-cutters until September 1096, when 900 Nine Winds raiders struck the Shagnak wells and the kin held the stockade at Nagdur for two days until the Hearth Guard broke them. Ushkar the Grey made their chief Keeper of the Stockade. They give every guest a block of salt before food, and they have traded with Salt Wind riders across the flats for as long as there have been flats. In 1103 Salt Wind riders slept at a Coldbarrow camp the night before they were blamed for three mares stolen from the war-chief's hearth herd. The Urgol clan rode against the kin that autumn, and six orcs died before Mother Ugra stopped the feud. The Coldbarrows still guard the war-chief's border while his hearth clan wants their blood.
FX11-006.reputation: Border folk who smell of salt and sell to both sides; brave on the wall, slippery at the fire.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Nagdur Stockade
members.note: Held the stockade gate for two days in 1096 with a salt-pick when his spear broke.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Coldbarrow kin; Ulbag's sister
members.note: Feeds Salt Wind traders in one tent and Hearth Guard riders in the next and keeps them from meeting.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Nagdur watch
members.note: Lost his younger brother in the Urgol feud of 1103 and wants the hearth clan to pay.

members.role: Ghora's daughter; salt-cutter of the Guldur works
members.note: Saw a cousin ride in at dawn with three lightning-branded mares in the spring of 1103.

famousDead: Cut salt for 40 winters and gave the kin its first stockade-well.
FX11-006.secret: The kin know that the three hearth mares were stolen by Ruk Nightrein, a cousin by marriage, and let the Salt Wind take the blame and their own sons die for it.
hooks: Bugra is ready to tell the war-chief who really stole his mares.
Drak plans a blood-revenge on an Urgol rider at the Great Ride.
Salt Wind riders ask to shelter at Nagdur again, with Nine Winds horses to trade.

FX11-007.name: The Wolftail line
FX11-007.title: Bearer of the Wolf Lance of the Urgash Hills
FX11-007.arms: a grey wolf's tail tied to a lance-head, on dun felt
FX11-007.words: Where the tail goes, the pack goes.

military.office: Hereditary bearers of the Wolf Lance, standard of the Wolf war-band
military.unit: the lance-file of the Wolf war-band, 1,400 hill riders of the Urgash Hills
military.ties: The Wolf Lance goes where the war-captain goes, and no Wolf rider turns back while it stands.

FX11-007.power: The keeping of the Wolf Lance, the summer camps at the Grakzag springs where half the western clans send their families, and the long songs of the Wolf clans.
FX11-007.history: The Wolf clans swore to Gorath in 1029 after he beat them at Vrakoth, and their war-captain gave the wolf-tailed lance to Garzag, the rider who had carried it off the field instead of dropping it. His line has carried it since. The lance has gone into every Horde war with the wolf's tail renewed at each Winter Count. The Wolftails host the summer camps at the Grakzag springs, sing the forty winters of Sunland bread at every Winter Count, and are cousins of the Grey Mothers through the marriage of 935. Their young riders listen to Hurn Firebrand, who says the 11,000 orc bones under the Crown Wall are a blood grievance. The bearer's own son has sworn to carry the lance against the Crown Wall forts.
FX11-007.reputation: Singers and hill-fighters who know every old grievance by heart; slow to start a war and slower to stop one.

members.role: Head of the line; Bearer of the Wolf Lance
members.note: Has carried the lance in eleven fights and never once lowered it.

members.role: Vorg's wife; song-keeper of the Grakzag summer camps
members.note: Sings the road-gift song longer than anyone alive and adds a verse every year.

members.role: Heir; rider of the lance-file
members.note: Has sworn on the lance to carry it against the Crown Wall forts, which no bearer may swear without the war-captain.

members.role: Vorg's daughter; scout of the Urgash Hills
members.note: Has found a broken Solen milestone in the hills with words on it no one at Grakzag can read.

famousDead: Carried the Wolf Lance off the field of Vrakoth in 1028 and was given it to keep.
FX11-007.secret: Zagrun took his oath on the lance before Hurn Firebrand and 30 young Wolf riders, and if the war-captain hears of it the line loses the lance.
hooks: Hurn Firebrand asks the Wolftails to carry the lance to the Crown Wall bones.
Nazga's Solen stone may be a marker of the old road-gift track.
The war-captain of the Wolf clans dies and the lance must choose a side at the Great Ride.

FX11-008.name: The Mareborn line
FX11-008.title: Herd-Master of the Goroth Remounts
FX11-008.arms: three running horses, white on red-brown felt, a foal beneath them
FX11-008.power: About 15,000 Goroth mares and the breeding of most of the 1,500 remounts the war-chief's hearth takes from the Goroth grass each year.
FX11-008.history: The Mareborns take their name from Yazga, a Goroth herd-girl born in a mare's birthing-pit in the ice winter of 1027. She grew up to breed the war-chief's remounts on the Goroth grass for Gorath and Durgash, from the year Gorath married Yelsha of Goroth in 1046. Under Goroth custom every foal is shown to the herd-master and no mare is sold outside the Horde, and the Mareborns keep both rules more strictly than anyone. Ice sealed their grass in January 1085 and they lost a third of their horses; Ushkar's hay saved the rest, and they have been the Line of Gorath's men ever since. They work under Grenna Wildmane, the Goroth herd-master, and they share her refusal to sell a mare to Gorm the Trader or Skarn Redhand. Since December 1104 a strangling cough has spread through a fifth of the Goroth herds, and the Mareborns have helped hide it.
FX11-008.reputation: Horse-proud and closed-mouthed; the best eye for a foal on the Grass Sea.

members.role: Head of the line; Herd-Master of the Goroth Remounts
members.note: Granddaughter and namesake of the herd-girl born in the pit, and still sleeps in the foaling camp every spring.

members.role: Yazga's husband; horse-archer of the Goroth war-band
members.note: Drives the herd screen in battle and can make 400 loose horses look like a war-band.

members.role: Heir; foaling-mistress
members.note: Has burned 300 coughing foals in secret and dreams about them.

members.role: Yazga's son; remount driver to Urgol
members.note: Has been offered 40 suns a mare by Gorm's men and has not said no.

famousDead: Born in a mare's birthing-pit in the ice winter of 1027; bred the war-chief's remounts for 26 years.
FX11-008.secret: The Mareborns have hidden the strangling cough in the Goroth remount herds since December 1104, and some of the coughing horses have already gone to the Hearth Guard at Urgol.
hooks: The cough breaks out in the Hearth Guard's string before the Great Ride.
Dagrak sells Goroth mares to Gorm's buyers, breaking the custom of the clans.
A Redhand rider offers to keep quiet about the cough for 300 mares.

FX11-009.name: The Snowpass drovers
FX11-009.title: Drove-Master of the Skardush road
FX11-009.arms: a white peak over a led horse, on slate grey
FX11-009.power: Drove-rights over the Crown foothill paths, about 300 drove horses a summer to the Highland League at Redford, and a share in the trade of Gorm the Trader's Horse-Traders.
FX11-009.history: From about 1060 the Skardush clans drove Horde horses over the pass in summer to the Highland League, and the Snowpass kin were the first to make a living of it. Their founder Grokh led 60 horses over the pass in 1061 and came back with iron, wool and a Highland wife. They winter under the Ughdur ring-fort among the mountain firs and drive from May until the snow closes the pass in November. The Highland and orc herders share the high meadows by a custom older than any treaty, and the Snowpass kin speak the Highland tongue as well as their own. Since 1092 they have driven under Gorm the Trader's mark. The Highland League has never signed a treaty with the Horde, and the Snowpass kin like it that way: no treaty, no tolls.
FX11-009.reputation: Half-Highland in their manners and wholly orc in their prices; trusted on both sides of the pass, loved on neither.

members.role: Head of the line; Drove-Master of the Skardush road
members.note: Can price a horse by its hooves and a Highlander by his boots.

members.role: Grask's wife; Highland-born keeper of the drove accounts
members.note: Keeps the only written accounts in the Horde, in Highland letters no orc can read.

members.role: Heir; lead drover
members.note: Brought a drove over the pass in a September blizzard and lost only three horses.

members.role: Grask's son; apprentice at Redford
members.note: Spends his summers at Redford and his money on Highland ale and Highland girls.

famousDead: Drove the first 60 horses over the Skardush Pass in 1061 and came back with a Highland wife.
FX11-009.secret: Since 1100 the Snowpass kin have carried Highland crossbows back over the pass in the drove packs and sold them to the Upper Gordush clans.
hooks: A Highland reeve asks the kin to carry a letter to the war-chief.
The crossbows in the drove packs are found at the pass watch.
Tolgar wants to marry at Redford and stay.

FX11-010.name: The Knotmothers of Zugmar
FX11-010.title: Frame-Mother of the Zugmar felting grounds
FX11-010.arms: a rolled felt tied with three red knots, on undyed white
FX11-010.power: Twelve felting frames at Urgol and the Zugmar soaking pools, and the making of the boiled-leather and felt armor that the Hearth Guard wears.
FX11-010.history: The Knotmothers came to Urgol from the Goroth clans when Gorath called felting kin to cover the Great Camp's tents in 1041. By 1060 they had become a kin-band of their own, led by women who own the frames and teach their knots only to their daughters. In the White Death of 1067 they cut up their own best felts to wrap the war-chief's mares against the ice, and the war-chief's hearth gave them twelve frames for it. They make felt armor stiffened in mare's-milk glue, the best on the Grass Sea, and every Hearth Guard coat carries their knot-mark. They follow Mother Rasha of the felt clans, who is holding back the felt tithe to Vrag's hearth. The Knotmothers have rolled their own tithe anyway and hidden it in the Zugmar pools.
FX11-010.reputation: Proud women of the frames who never ride to war and never let anyone forget who keeps the war-bands warm.

members.role: Head of the kin; Frame-Mother of Zugmar
members.note: Has a knot for every winter she has lived and teaches none of them to men.

members.role: Heir; armor-felter of the Hearth Guard
members.note: Has made 400 felt coats for the Hearth Guard and knows the measure of every rider in it.

members.role: Shugra's husband; carter of the felt tithe
members.note: Drove the hidden tithe to the Zugmar pools without knowing what was in the bales.

members.role: Bolka's granddaughter; frame-girl
members.note: Wants to ride with Tarn's Halfbloods under the two-horse saddle-cloths she helped roll.

famousDead: Cut her own best felts to wrap the war-chief's mares in the White Death of 1067.
FX11-010.secret: Bolka has rolled the full felt tithe and hidden it in the Zugmar pools, so that the Knotmothers can give it to whoever wins the staff and be first in the new war-chief's favor.
hooks: Mother Rasha learns the Knotmothers have a hidden tithe.
The Hearth Guard needs new coats before May Fair, and only the Knotmothers can make them in time.
Uzga runs off to the Halfbloods' camp at Gashmar.

FX11-011.name: The Moonless kin
FX11-011.title: Chief of the Moonless riders
FX11-011.arms: no arms: a black hoofprint burned into a white salt-block is left where they have stolen
FX11-011.words: Laughed at if caught, sung if not.
FX11-011.power: Forty riders who know every well and salt-crust of the eastern flats, about 1,500 stolen horses a year, and buyers on both sides of the Nine Winds border.
FX11-011.history: The Moonless kin began in 1079 as a band of Salt Edge youths who stole Nine Winds horses across the flats on nights without a moon, which the Salt Edge clans count half a sport. They never stopped, and by 1090 they were stealing from orc clans as well and selling the horses back to their owners' neighbors at the Yagrak caravanserai. Among the Salt Edge clans a caught thief is laughed at and an uncaught one is sung, and the Moonless kin have a great many songs. They have twice been paid to lose a horse race at the Great Ride and once to steal a Redhand chief's stallion for a Goroth wedding. Their riders have stolen from the khan's yam stations and from the war-chief's own herd. Some of them rode with Ruk Nightrein in the spring of 1103.
FX11-011.reputation: Thieves with songs; every clan curses them and every clan has bought from them.

members.role: Chief of the Moonless riders
members.note: Has been caught four times, laughed at four times, and has stolen the laughers' horses each time after.

members.role: Hrak's wife; seller of stolen horses at Yagrak
members.note: Can change a brand with a hot knife so well the owner buys the horse back gladly.

members.role: Hrak's son; rider of the Moonless
members.note: Took a yam horse with a silver tablet still in its saddle-bag and has not dared sell either.

members.role: Hrak's daughter; lookout
members.note: Watches the Nine Winds yams by night and counts their horses better than the keepers do.

famousDead: Founder who stole a Nine Winds chief's white stallion from inside his own camp ring.
FX11-011.secret: Ghor holds a Nine Winds silver tablet that commands any yam station, and the Moonless kin are deciding whether to sell it to the Horde, the Tusk Clans or the khan's enemies.
hooks: A Nine Winds rider comes looking for the stolen silver tablet.
Someone pays the Moonless to steal a horse from the Hearth Guard before the Great Ride.
Hrak offers to name the thief of the war-chief's mares for a price.

FX11-012.name: The Saltpick kin
FX11-012.title: Mother of the Rushbad salt pans
FX11-012.arms: a white salt-pick crossed with a horse-whip, on brown
FX11-012.power: The cutting rights to the Rushbad salt pans and about 1,000 people who cut, cart and sell salt to every clan and to the Aldmark smugglers of the Gordush.
FX11-012.history: The Saltpicks came back to the Salt Sea shore when the Wind garrisons fell, and by 925 they were cutting salt at Rushbad as their grandmothers had before the Wind riders came. They have cut it for the clans ever since and carted it on oxen and camels along the Rushoth road. In the Battle of the Salt Shore of 1041 they watched from the pans while the Reed Wind and the Morning Wind stood still, and their grandmothers were the first to ask why. They have shared the grass's edge with those two tribes since and take a little salt-price of their own from them. Salt is never short, but grass is, and the Saltpicks have lost half their horses in the last three dry autumns. Their young ride with the Salt Edge war-band because it pays in horses.
FX11-012.reputation: Poor, cheerful and white to the elbows; nobody's enemy, nobody's ally.

members.role: Head of the kin; Mother of the Rushbad salt pans
members.note: Has never left the salt coast and says the Salt Sea is the only war-chief she obeys.

members.role: Heir; salt-carter of the Rushoth road
members.note: Knows every Aldmark smuggler on the Gordush by the salt he buys.

members.role: Orza's daughter; rider of the Salt Edge war-band
members.note: Rode at the Well of Buroth and came back with a Nine Winds bow and no horse.

members.role: Orza's youngest son; salt-boy
members.note: Named for nobody in particular, he says, and is tired of the jokes.

FX11-012.secret: Orza's grandmother knotted a copy of the Salt Shore bargain into a salt-cutters' tally cord in 1041, and it still hangs in the kin's pan-house.
hooks: A Reed Wind herder offers silver for the old salt tally cord.
Three dry autumns have left the kin too few horses for the Great Ride.
Aldmark's reeves stop buying salt across the Gordush.

FX11-013.name: The Goatpath line
FX11-013.title: Chief of the Lugruk kin-bands
FX11-013.arms: a goat's head over a date palm, gold on dusty green

military.office: Captains of the Lugruk hill-path foot
military.unit: about 200 hill foot of the Nagoth hill-path band
military.ties: They hold the southern hill paths with spear and sling for the Nagoth band and send riders north only when the full levy is called.

FX11-013.power: Date gardens at the Rushzag springs worked by thralls and half-orcs, about 30,000 goats and sheep, and the wool trade to the Ostran and Morhaven market towns.
FX11-013.history: The Goatpaths are chiefs of nine Nagoth kin-bands who joined Gorath late, in 1038, and fought little in the Horde Wars, which were fought far to the north. Their founder Bazga gave Gorath 400 goats and no horses and was mocked for it at the Great Ride; her line has been called date-eaters ever since. They sell wool, felt and goat-hair rope at Camina and Verica for oil, wine and grain, and in the Harbor Pox of 1076 to 1078 they closed their camps to the coast and lost almost nobody. Strangers sleep in their camps only after a cup of mare's milk. In 1105 the Goatpath mothers want no war in the north, because when the Gordush is closed the Horde's grain comes from the coast and the Ostran merchants raise the price. Their chief has a debt in Ostra that the war would make worse.
FX11-013.reputation: Rich in goats, poor in horses, and smarter traders than the northern clans want to admit.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Lugruk kin-bands
members.note: Speaks the Ostran trade tongue better than her own clan-mothers would like.

members.role: Mursha's husband; captain of the Lugruk hill foot
members.note: Can hold a goat path against a hundred riders, which is why nobody tries.

members.role: Heir; wool-trader at Camina
members.note: Has an Ostran merchant for a lover and a better price than any other trader of the south.

members.role: Mursha's son; rider of the full levy
members.note: Hates being called a date-eater and has sworn to ride north with the Hearth Guard.

famousDead: Gave Gorath 400 goats and no horses in 1038 and was laughed at; her line still is.
FX11-013.secret: Mursha owes an Ostran front house 3,000 suns for grain bought in the thin autumn of 1104, and the house has asked to be paid in news of the Horde's war plans.
hooks: The Ostran house wants the date of the war-chief's spring ride.
Barzug runs north to join the Hearth Guard against his mother's word.
The coast raises the grain price again and the southern clan-mothers threaten to stop the wool.

FX11-014.name: The Reedboat line
FX11-014.title: Keeper of the Great Ride grounds
FX11-014.arms: a drum and a silver fish on blue-grey felt

military.office: Axe-captains of the Drum Stones guard
military.unit: about 300 axe-riders of the Vrakoth lake war-band
military.ties: When the Drum Stones are threatened the Reedboats get off their horses and fight among the stones with axes, as their kin did in 476 and 879.

FX11-014.power: The keeping of the Great Ride grounds and the feast, reed-boat fisheries on Lake Vrakuk and about 6,000 horses that may not graze within sight of the Stones.
FX11-014.history: The Reedboats are a Vrakoth lake kin-band who fish Lake Vrakuk from reed boats, a rare thing among orcs. When Old Mother Shagra led the clans back to the Drum Stones in 923 their chief laid out the Great Ride course, and the line has kept the grounds and fed the feast ever since. Their grandmothers fought at the stones on foot in 879, and the line's songs still name the 200 who died there. Gorath married Drazka of the lake clans in 1029 and Vrag married Dushka of them in 1093, so the Reedboats count themselves grandparents of the war-chief's line and expect to be treated so. Their girls race the Great Ride course on foot the day before the riders. In 1105 they must lay out a Great Ride where the staff may change hands, and both sides have asked them where the Redhand tents will stand.
FX11-014.reputation: Fish-eaters with long memories; the clans laugh at their boats and fear their axes.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Great Ride grounds
members.note: Paces out the Ride course each spring with a knotted cord his great-grandmother made.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Reedboat kin; cousin of Mother Dushka
members.note: Tells everyone that the war-chief's sons are half Vrakoth and should be raised by the lake.
