members.role: Heir; axe-captain of the Stones guard
members.note: Has never fought a battle and drills every day among the stones as if one were coming tomorrow.

members.role: Vrasha's daughter; fisher and foot-racer
members.note: Won the girls' Ride-course race three times and wants to race the riders on foot.

famousDead: Laid out the Great Ride course on the clans' return in 923.
FX11-014.secret: Vrasha has promised Mother Ugra's rivals in the Grey Council that if Vrag dies, the lake clans will ask for his eldest son to be raised at Vrakoth, not at Urgol.
hooks: Both Redhands and the Hearth Guard want the tent-places closest to the Stones.
Vrag's eldest son Gorr is sent to the lake for the summer.
Azka races the Great Ride on foot and the shamans must rule on it.

FX11-015.name: The Peakwatch line
FX11-015.title: Captain of the Ughdur Ring and the signal fires
FX11-015.arms: a red flame on a white peak, over grey

military.office: Hereditary captains of the Ughdur ring-fort and the Crown foothill signal fires
military.unit: the Ughdur watch, 300 riders and scouts of the Skardush war-band
military.ties: Their chain of fires can bring the Skardush war-band to the passes in a night, and they have kept watch on the Highland towers for every war-chief since Gorath.

FX11-015.power: The Ughdur ring-fort among the mountain firs, nine signal hills of the Crown foothills and the war-chief's trust on the southern border.
FX11-015.history: When Gorath founded the Horde in 1041 the Skardush clans gave him a line of signal fires along the Crown foothills, and he gave the watch to Rurga, a Skardush scout whose grandson had married into Brakk's kin. The Peakwatches have kept the Ughdur ring-fort and its nine fires since, watching the Highland League's stone tower at the mouth of the pass and the elven tree line beyond Greycloak Gorge. They pray at the Mare shrines on the peaks and leave mare's milk on the snow at Storm Coming. Their fires have been lit in earnest only four times, the last in 1088 when Highland riders chased horse thieves into the foothills. They share the high meadows with Highland herders by an old unwritten custom and have friends among them. Their great worry is the elves, who have watched the tree line in silence for two thousand years.
FX11-015.reputation: Quiet mountain folk, more at home with Highland herders than with Urgol courtiers.

members.role: Head of the line; Captain of the Ughdur Ring
members.note: Can tell a Highland herder from a Highland soldier at two kilometers by the way he walks.

members.role: Yagra's husband; fire-master of the nine signal hills
members.note: Keeps the nine fire-stacks dry through a whole winter and counts that his greatest deed.

members.role: Heir; scout of the Greycloak Gorge
members.note: Has met an elf in the gorge three times and has told no one what she said.

members.role: Yagra's daughter; Mare-shrine girl
members.note: Leaves milk on the snow at the shrine of Vrakur every morning, not only at Storm Coming.

famousDead: First captain of the Ughdur fires, given the watch by Gorath in 1041.
FX11-015.secret: Gholl has carried messages between an elven watcher of the tree line and Tollo Quietfoot of the Longwind runners, and does not know what the messages say.
hooks: The signal fires are lit, and nobody at Ughdur lit them.
An elf asks Gholl to carry something heavier than a message.
Highland riders chase smugglers into the foothills and the old custom is tested.

FX11-016.name: The Wellkeeper line of Krugak
FX11-016.title: Chief of the Krugak wells
FX11-016.arms: a white well-mouth between three running horses, on red-brown

military.office: Captains of the Goroth horse-archers at the wells
military.unit: about 250 horse-archers of the Goroth war-band
military.ties: They shoot in the Goroth war-band's screen and guard the Krugak wells that the Horde's eastern relays water at.

FX11-016.power: The Krugak wells and the winter grass around them, about 9,000 horses, and the 900 horses of the 1086 blood-price, now grown to 1,400.
FX11-016.history: The Wellkeepers are the Goroth kin-band that holds the Krugak wells, and their line begins in blood. In August 1012 their riders killed Durr One-Ear, a Vrakoth-born rider of the Urgol clan, in a feud over the wells, and his son Gorath, 14, rode into the fight bare-armed and killed three of them. Gorath forgave the kin when he married Yelsha of Goroth in 1046, and Durgash married Kazra of Goroth after him, so the Wellkeepers are Vrag's mother's people as well as his grandfather's killers. From 1082 to 1086 they fought the Redhand clans over the same wells, and Mother Ugra won them 900 horses in blood-price. The Long Flight of 876 is sung at every Winter Count, three summers of it, and the Wellkeepers never forget that the Redhands knelt to the Khan while they fled. They breed horse-archers and keep the old rule: no mare sold outside the Horde.
FX11-016.reputation: Stiff-necked and well-watered; the Goroth kin with the best wells and the oldest grudge.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Krugak wells
members.note: Shot three Redhand riders at the wells in 1084 and still keeps their arrows in his tent.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Wellkeeper kin
members.note: Sat beside Mother Ugra through the whole Krugak judgment and learned what law can win.

members.role: Heir; horse-archer of the Goroth screen
members.note: Meets a Redmare girl at the summer camps and has given her his father's second-best bow.

members.role: Azgrash's daughter; well-keeper
members.note: Knows which of the 40 Krugak wells go bad in a dry year and keeps the list in her head.

famousDead: Led the riders who killed Durr One-Ear at the wells; died there by the hand of the boy Gorath.
Married Gorath in 1046 and bound the Wellkeepers to his line; mother of Nurga.
FX11-016.secret: The hide of 1012 says Gorath's father Durr struck first at the wells, and the Wellkeepers have their own hide that says he was drunk and they had sworn him peace.
hooks: Toksh and Ishka of the Redmares want to marry, and both kins would rather go to war.
A dry spring and three bad wells bring the Redhands back to the Krugak grass.
Vrag visits his mother's kin and asks what really happened in 1012.

FX11-017.name: The Breadbreakers of Graknak
FX11-017.title: Chief of the Gnarzag kin-bands
FX11-017.arms: a broken round loaf over a plough-share, gold on green

military.office: Captains of the Gnarzag river riders
military.unit: about 400 riders and 150 half-orc foot of the Upper Gordush riders
military.ties: They guard the upper fords and the Graknak grain store for the war-chief, and their half-orc foot stand with the Ladder Foot at need.

FX11-017.power: Ploughed river fields on the Gnarzag worked by kin and thralls, a share of the Graknak grain store, and about 6,000 people, a third of them half-orcs and adopted humans.
FX11-017.history: When the Treaty of Crossmarch gave the Horde the upper Gordush in 1074, Ushkar the Grey settled kin from Gashmar, Urgol and Vrakoth on the old Aldmark fields, and gave the Gnarzag bottoms to Turga, a Gashmar clan-mother who had once been an Aldmark captive and knew how to plough. Her kin are the only orcs who eat bread every day, and they break it before meat at every fire. Through the 1080s and 1090s they took in half-orc families pushed out of Aldmark's march by the License Law, and in 1099 they raised an adopted human to lead a kin-band, after the custom of seven winters. In the autumn of 1104 about 60 of their half-orc riders went to winter beside Tarn's Halfbloods at Gashmar. Garrick Harrow's reeves count every family that crosses the river to them. If Aldmark crosses the river in May, the Breadbreakers' fields are the first it will burn.
FX11-017.reputation: Farmers with tusks, laughed at by the horse clans and envied every hungry winter.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Gnarzag kin-bands
members.note: Granddaughter of the founder, and the only chief in the Horde who can tell rye from barley in the field.

members.role: Adopted kin-band leader; born in Aldmark's southern march
members.note: Crossed the Gordush in 1092 with a plough on his back and was raised to lead a kin-band after seven winters.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Gnarzag riders
members.note: Half-orc, and the first of the line to be both a better rider and a better ploughman than her mother.

members.role: Turga's son; rider among Tarn's Halfbloods
members.note: Wears Tarn's two-horse sign and believes the rider of two peoples will end the License Law by summer.

famousDead: A freed Aldmark captive who taught the Upper Gordush clans to plough after 1074.
FX11-017.secret: Hal still has a brother in Copperham who sends him the dates Aldmark's reeves will ride, in exchange for Graknak grain sold across the river.
hooks: Aldmark crosses the river and the Breadbreakers' fields burn first.
Brukka rides east with Tarn if Vrag sends him away.
A reeve of House Harrow offers the kin their old Aldmark fields back if they hand over the Halfbloods.

FX11-018.name: The Crescent line
FX11-018.title: Chief of the Guldur kin-bands
FX11-018.arms: a white crescent moon over a salt-block, on deep blue

military.office: Captains of the Salt Edge night riders
military.unit: about 350 light riders of the Salt Edge war-band
military.ties: They strike at Nine Winds wells by night and vanish into the salt flats, and their riders make up the Salt Edge war-band's best raiders.

FX11-018.power: The Guldur saltworks, the palm springs of Vrakhul, about 8,000 horses and a marriage tie to the Redhand chief's wife.
FX11-018.history: The Crescents led the Salt Edge kin-bands that fought on their own grass at the Battle of the Salt Shore in September 1041, and their chief took the crescent for the moonlit night before it. Durgash Blood-Fist's first wife Ulza was a Crescent daughter, and his raid on Kyzai in 1061 passed through their camps and left them rich. In 1085 Skarn Redhand married Mother Olka of the Salt Edge clans, a Crescent cousin, and the line has stood with the Old Clans since. They cut salt at Guldur, trade it to Aldmark's smugglers, and steal Nine Winds horses as half a sport. In 1096 and again in 1102 and 1103 Nine Winds raiders came through their grass to Shagnak and the Coldbarrow Bridge. The Crescents tell Skarn that Vrag's victories there were won by Salt Edge blood and Hearth Guard boasting.
FX11-018.reputation: Night raiders with good salt and bad manners; Skarn Redhand's friends on the eastern edge.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Guldur kin-bands
members.note: Has promised Skarn 800 Salt Edge riders at the Great Ride, which is twice what he has.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Crescent kin; cousin of Mother Olka
members.note: Visits her cousin at Magak every autumn and comes back knowing how Skarn counts.

members.role: Heir; captain of the night riders
members.note: Took a Nine Winds chief's horn at the Coldbarrow Bridge and wears it at his belt.

members.role: Ulgash's daughter; salt-trader at Guldur
members.note: Sells salt to Aldmark smugglers and charges them double when they ask about the war.

famousDead: First wife of Durgash Blood-Fist; mother of Hrakka the Red and Uzgar; died in the White Death.
FX11-018.secret: Relka, Durgash's daughter by a Crescent mother, married back into the kin, and her grandson has the blood fury; Hesha hides his fits so the Old Clans can raise a claimant of Gorath's own blood if they need one.
hooks: Skarn asks to see the Crescents' 800 riders before the Great Ride.
Relka's grandson shakes white after a fight at the Great Ride, and the Grey Mothers see it.
Nine Winds raiders strike Guldur and the Hearth Guard comes late.

FX11-019.name: The Hidepainters of Urgol
FX11-019.title: Elder Painter of the Winter-Count Hides
FX11-019.arms: a brush and a grey braid crossed over a pale painted hide
FX11-019.power: The craft of mixing ochre, soot and mare's-blood paints, the repainting of about 1,400 old clan hides in the Grey Mothers' tents, and the eyes that have seen every one of them.
FX11-019.history: When Mother Arga took the old hides of every sworn clan into the Grey Mothers' tents at Urgol in 1041, she needed hands to keep them, and she took a Goroth kin of hide-painters into the camp to repaint the fading pictures. The Hidepainters have done it since, under the Mothers' eye, and have sent their daughters to learn the law as braid-girls. In 1070 one of their girls, Hulga, was set to repaint the Urgol clan's hide and fled east the same month, and the family was not allowed into the tents for three winters after. She is said to have died among the Tusk Clans, and her daughter is the drummer and scholar Ashka Drumtongue. The Hidepainters have been back in the tents since 1073, painting more carefully than anyone alive. In 1105 the old pictures they repaint are the most dangerous things in the Horde.
FX11-019.reputation: Ink-fingered and quiet; the clans trust them with their hides and fear what they have seen.

members.role: Head of the kin; Elder Painter of the Winter-Count Hides
members.note: Hulga's younger sister, who paints the Urgol hide herself so no other girl has to see it.

members.role: Heir; braid-girl of the Grey Mothers
members.note: Has learned 200 winters of law by heart and noticed that some pictures were painted over twice.

members.role: Ghela's son; paint-grinder
members.note: Drinks with Redhand riders at the Great Ride and talks too much about paint.

members.role: Ghela's granddaughter; hide-girl
members.note: Has a letter from a Tusk drummer who says she is her cousin.

famousDead: Braid-girl who saw a picture on the Urgol hide in 1070 and fled to the Tusk Clans.
FX11-019.secret: Ghela knows exactly what her sister saw on the Urgol hide for 1024, and has painted it smaller every time she repaints it.
hooks: Ashka Drumtongue writes to her cousins asking to see the Urgol hide.
Ormag sells a sketch of a Redhand hide to a Redmare rider.
Mother Ugra asks the Hidepainters to make a true copy of the hide for 476 for the Great Ride.

FX12-001.name: The Saltgate clan of the Red Wind
FX12-001.title: Captain of the Torkul salt forts
FX12-001.arms: a red gate in a white salt wall, on salt white

military.office: Hereditary captains of the old Solen salt forts at Torkul
military.unit: the Torkul salt-fort garrison, 400 riders and wall-guards
military.ties: They hold the only stone walls the Red Wind owns, and they guard the salt pans and the toll on caviar and fish that passes Torkul.

FX12-001.power: The garrison of the Torkul forts, the counting of the salt and fish toll, and about 3,000 horses penned in the old Solen courtyards.
FX12-001.history: When Berek gave the Red Wind Torkul and the salt forts in the Compact of 925, the chief gave the walls to a salt-worker's son named Arslan who had held them for Temur, and the Saltgates have held them since. They pen horses in Solen courtyards and keep salt in Solen cellars, and they still find Solen coins in the mortar. Temur was murdered in his tent at Torkul by his own guard captain in January 920, and the Saltgates sing 'The Captain's Herd' at every wedding like all the Red Wind, louder than most. The forts' captain sits at Yesun's council and counts the salt toll that pays his riders. In November 1104 Yesun's champion Jarak found the guard captain's grave near Torkul. The Saltgates guard the place now, and they have not been told why.
FX12-001.reputation: Wall-folk among riders, proud of their stones and touchy about the oil money the Red Wind never gets.

members.role: Head of the clan; Captain of the Torkul salt forts
members.note: Has walked every wall of Torkul each dawn for 25 years and can name every crack.

members.role: Temir's wife; keeper of the salt toll
members.note: Knows to the last fish how much the Red Wind earns and how much the khan earns from oil, and says both numbers at every feast.

members.role: Heir; captain of the grave-watch
members.note: Guards a small mound near Torkul for Yesun and has started digging at it by night.

members.role: Temir's daughter; salt-fort archer
members.note: Is promised to a Grey Wind rider of the Silver Tablet Guard, which half the Red Wind calls treason.

famousDead: Held the Torkul forts for Temur and was given them by Berek in 925.
Captain of the forts who sheltered the paid raiders of 1079 for one night and never asked who paid them.
FX12-001.secret: In 1079 the Saltgate captain sheltered the raiders who took the fire-oil caravans, on Kutlu's word, and the clan has kept the horse-brand of one of the stolen camels in its strongroom.
hooks: Erbol digs into the guard captain's grave and finds a silver tablet with a khan's seal.
Juldyz's marriage to a Grey Wind guardsman is called off by her own tribe.
Yesun asks the forts to hold Kharsan envoys as hostages if the Horse Feast goes wrong.

FX12-002.name: The Cordkeepers of Kultau
FX12-002.title: Shaman of the Reed Wind
FX12-002.arms: a blue knotted cord coiled around a reed, on silver
FX12-002.power: The shaman's tent of the Reed Wind, which no outsider enters, the blessing of the sturgeon season, and the cords that bind the tribe's oaths.
FX12-002.history: The Cordkeepers have been the shamans of the Reed Wind since Ulagan was raised khan at Kultau in 870, when their first shaman tied the tribe's oath-cord to him. They bless the first sturgeon of spring, read the ice on the Salt Sea and keep the knotted cords of every oath the tribe has sworn. Their tent is never entered by outsiders, and the Reed Wind takes this as faith. In August 1041 the shaman of the day watched chief Mergen and the chief of the Morning Wind knot a treaty cord with Gorath's envoys, and took it into the tent. It has been there since. Each new shaman learns its meaning on the day the old one dies.
FX12-002.reputation: Quiet, holy and very rich in sturgeon; the most private shamans on the steppe.

members.role: Head of the line; Shaman of the Reed Wind
members.note: Learned the cord's meaning in 1085 and has slept in front of it every night since.

members.role: Heir; shaman's apprentice and ice-reader
members.note: Does not yet know what is in the cord bundle and has started asking.

members.role: Altyn's daughter; sturgeon-blesser of the fishing camps
members.note: Is loved in every fishing camp of the north shore and trusted with every secret but the one in her mother's tent.

members.role: Altyn's husband; keeper of the caviar cellars' oaths
members.note: Has never asked his wife a single question in 35 years of marriage.

famousDead: Took the treaty cord of 1041 into the shaman's tent.
FX12-002.secret: The knotted treaty cord of 1041 lies in the Cordkeepers' tent, and Altyn has twice been asked by Tolui of the Reed Wind to burn it and twice refused, because a shaman may not untie an oath.
hooks: Yesun's men try to enter the shaman's tent at the Horse Feast.
Altyn falls ill and Aibar must learn what the cord means.
Tolui orders the cord burned, and the shaman refuses her chief.

FX12-003.name: The Ringcloser clan of the Grey Wind
FX12-003.title: Flag-Master of the Ring Hunt of Kyztai
FX12-003.arms: a grey ring of arrows around a white flag, on grey

military.office: Hereditary flag-masters and horn-masters of the Ring Hunt of Kyztai
military.unit: the flag-riders of the Ring Hunt, 120 riders who signal thousands
military.ties: Their flags and horns move thousands of riders in the winter Ring Hunt, which is the Nine Winds' army drill, and they ride at the heir's side when he leads it.

FX12-003.power: The flags, horns and signal-calls of the Ring Hunt, which no one else knows in full, and about 4,000 horses on the Sartobe grass.
FX12-003.history: The Ring Hunt of Kyztai is older than the Compact, but the flags are not. In 952 a Grey Wind rider named Kyran worked out a code of seven flags and twelve horn-calls that let a hunt-master close a ring of 5,000 riders on the game without a single shout, and the chief made the code his family's charge. The Ringclosers have kept it since, from father to daughter or son, and they teach the calls to every rider who joins the hunt. Serik Kharsan has led the Ring Hunt each winter, with the Ringcloser flag-master at his side. The Ring Hunt is how the Nine Winds learn to fight as one. If the heir falls, the Ringclosers fear the hunt falls apart with the khanate.
FX12-003.reputation: The best signalers on the steppe, and the most certain the Grey Wind is the steppe's spine.

members.role: Head of the clan; Flag-Master of the Ring Hunt
members.note: Can close a ring of 8,000 riders with one arm and a horn, and once did it in a snowstorm.

members.role: Kyran's wife; horn-maker
members.note: Makes the ram's-horn trumpets of the hunt and tunes each to a different call.

members.role: Heir; flag-rider at Serik's side
members.note: Saw the heir limp after the hunt of 1104 and saw him bind a bloody foot behind his tent.

members.role: Kyran's daughter; horn-caller
members.note: Has made a thirteenth horn-call of her own and wants it in the hunt.

famousDead: Made the seven flags and twelve horn-calls of the Ring Hunt in 952.
FX12-003.secret: Bulat has seen the heir's foot sore that will not heal, the khan's sickness come early, and the clan has decided to tell no one.
hooks: Serik cannot ride the Ring Hunt this winter, and someone must lead it in his place.
Aigul's thirteenth call is heard in a real battle.
A Red Wind rider offers silver for the flag code.

FX12-004.name: The Tally-Knot clan of the Grey Wind
FX12-004.title: Chief Knotter of the Khatun's Tallies
FX12-004.arms: a grey cord with five knots across a white well-mouth
FX12-004.power: The knotting of the horse tax, the oil money and the tribes' herd counts into the tallies that Khatun Sorga keeps, and the eyes that see every one.
FX12-004.history: The Grey Wind has kept tallies since the Solen princess Galla taught its chiefs to count in the 430s, and the Tally-Knots are the best of its counters. When Sorga of the Grey Wind married Ozbek in 1068, she brought a Tally-Knot widow to Kharsa to keep her own accounts, and the family has knotted the khan's tallies since Sorga took the tent-chest in 1079. They knot the one-in-thirty horse tax of every tribe, the tenth of the channel fairs and, since 1103, the Tessarian silver of the oil. They read the monthly yam tallies to the khatun. Since the summer of 1104 the khan has not been able to read a cord, and the Tally-Knots have read every one to Sorga alone.
FX12-004.reputation: Dry, exact and loyal to the khatun; feared by every chief who has ever under-counted a herd.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief Knotter of the Khatun's Tallies
members.note: Has knotted every horse of the khan's tax for 26 years and never let anyone else touch the oil cord.

members.role: Heir; knotter of the yam tallies
members.note: Found that the Sea Wind's horse count does not match the channel fair's, by about 600 a year.

members.role: Erke's daughter; reader to the khatun
members.note: Reads the cords aloud in Sorga's tent and pretends the khan is listening.

members.role: Nurlan's son; knot-boy
members.note: Plays with old cords from the chest and has knotted himself a toy horse out of one that smells of age.

famousDead: Came to Kharsa with Khatun Sorga in 1068 and knotted the khan's first tally.
FX12-004.secret: The Tally-Knots know that Khatun Sorga has governed in Ozbek's name since the summer of 1104, and that the oil cord counts 30 jars a year to Tessaria.
hooks: Nurlan's count of the missing Sea Wind horses reaches the kurultai.
Toktar's toy horse is knotted from one of the cords of 912.
Yesun offers Ainur a husband and a herd for one night with the oil cord.

FX12-005.name: The Keepers of the Otbash Yam
FX12-005.title: Keeper of the Otbash Yam
FX12-005.arms: a silver tablet on a blue cord over a running horse, on white
FX12-005.power: The Otbash yam station on the north road, its 60 horses, its stabling and beds, and the right to stop any rider who does not carry a silver tablet.
FX12-005.history: The Otbash station was one of the first yams that Khatun Saran set up, in 874, a year after Kharsa's. Its first keeper was trained at Kharsa by Bayan the Keeper himself, and the family has kept it for eight generations under the Keepers of the Kharsa Yam. Every rider who changes horses at Otbash is knotted into the cords with the day and the road. In 915 the Black Cough rode the yam roads, and the Otbash keepers lost six of their people. Chagan the Postmaster rebuilt the station in 1096 and added 20 horses. In the autumn of 1104 three riders with no tablet were given fresh horses at Otbash on the word of a half-orc archer of the Salt Wind, and they rode west toward the Horde.
FX12-005.reputation: Plain, reliable people who never sleep a full night; the khan's roads would stop without families like them.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Otbash Yam
members.note: Has changed horses for 40,000 riders and remembers the face of every one who carried a silver tablet.

members.role: Japar's wife; keeper of the station cords
members.note: Knotted the three tabletless riders of 1104 into the cord exactly as she knots every rider.

members.role: Heir; yam courier
members.note: Rode the news of Coreria from Morhaven to Kharsa in five days with Kulan's riders and wants to join the Yam Riders for good.

members.role: Japar's daughter; stable-mistress
members.note: Gave the three riders the horses herself because the half-orc archer asked her nicely.

famousDead: Trained by Bayan the Keeper; first keeper of the Otbash yam.
FX12-005.secret: The station cords show three riders given yam horses without a tablet in the autumn of 1104, a crime under the yam law, and the riders were seeking the Horde's rider of two peoples.
hooks: Chagan the Postmaster comes to inspect the Otbash cords.
Bota's half-orc archer comes back with more riders who want horses.
A Black Wind band raids the Otbash horse pens.

FX12-006.name: The Tablet-Bearer clan of the Blue Wind
FX12-006.title: Hundred-Captain of the Silver Tablet Guard
FX12-006.arms: a silver tablet under a blue horsetail standard, on white felt

military.office: Hereditary hundred-captains of the Silver Tablet Guard
military.unit: two hundreds of the Silver Tablet Guard, 200 picked horse-archers
military.ties: Every Tablet-Bearer son rides in the khan's guard of 2,000, each rider carrying the silver tablet that commands any yam.

FX12-006.power: Two hundreds of the Silver Tablet Guard, the right to carry a khan's tablet, and a hearth beside the khan's own at Kharsa.
FX12-006.history: When Berek made the Tent Law in 926, he also chose 500 Blue Wind riders to guard his tent and gave each a silver tablet that commands any yam, and a rider named Burkit was among the first. His line has held two hundreds of the guard since, and its sons are raised at the Kharsa Arrow Field. They rode beside Tulgar at the Salt Shore in 1041, when two tribes stood still, and lost 60 riders guarding the khan's body back to Kharsa. They rode for Ozbek when he rebuilt the house's power after 1079. Their hundreds stand at the khan's tent door, so they see who goes in and who comes out. They have seen the khatun answering letters for a khan who sits in the dark.
FX12-006.reputation: Proud, loyal and close to the khan's ear; the western tribes call them the Kharsan's dogs.

members.role: Head of the clan; Hundred-Captain of the Silver Tablet Guard
members.note: Has stood at the khan's tent door for 30 years and knows the khan's step from anyone else's, and that it has changed.

members.role: Burkit's wife; armorer of the guard's lamellar
members.note: Laces the guard's lamellar coats and has sewn a silver tablet into each of her sons' collars.

members.role: Heir; hundred-leader of the guard at Kyztai
members.note: Rides with Serik's 800 at the Kyztai ring-hunt camp and means to be Commander of the Guard when Serik is khan.

members.role: Burkit's daughter; archer of the Arrow Field
members.note: Shot second at the Horse Feast of 1104 behind Dorin Swiftarrow and wants a place in the guard, where no woman has stood since Saran's day.

famousDead: One of the first 500 tablet-riders chosen by Berek in 926.
Carried Khan Tulgar's body from the Salt Shore with 60 dead around him.
FX12-006.secret: Burkit's men have seen Khatun Sorga sign letters in the khan's name with the khan's own seal while he sat in the dark, and have sworn among themselves to say nothing until the Horse Feast.
hooks: Altynai asks the khan for a place in the guard at the Horse Feast.
A western chief demands to see the khan without the khatun present, and the Tablet-Bearers hold the door.
Daulet is offered the guard's command by Yesun if Serik is not raised.

FX12-007.name: The Pot-Thrower clan of the Grey Wind
FX12-007.title: Pot-Master of the Keepers of the Seeps
FX12-007.arms: a black pot spilling red flame, on grey
FX12-007.words: We do not speak of the place.

military.office: Hereditary pot-masters of the Keepers of the Seeps
military.unit: the pot-throwers, 120 riders of the 1,000 Keepers of the Seeps
military.ties: They guard the khan's seeps and jar stores near Kyzai and throw the fire-oil pots in war, and every one of them has sworn the Keepers' death oath.

FX12-007.power: The making and throwing of the fire-pots, a place in the Seep Stockade, and the khan's silver for their silence.
FX12-007.history: When Khan Toghrul founded the Keepers of the Seeps in 1052, after Blackreef showed the world that fire-oil could be bought elsewhere, he took 500 hearth-tribe riders and a Grey Wind potter named Askar who knew how to seal oil in clay so it would burst and burn. Askar's line has made and thrown the pots since. In 1081 the old jar store at Kyzai burned with nine Keepers inside, three of them Pot-Throwers. In 1085 Ozbek moved the jars behind the Seep Stockade and made every Keeper swear a death oath never to speak of the place. The Pot-Throwers swore first. They winter among the Salt Wind, who resent them on their land. This winter one of their own sons is among the two Keepers who have deserted.
FX12-007.reputation: Silent, scorched and feared; the Salt Wind will not share a fire with them.

members.role: Head of the clan; Pot-Master of the Keepers of the Seeps
members.note: Has burn scars from wrist to shoulder and has never once said the word 'seep' aloud.

members.role: Askar's wife; clay-mistress of the pot kilns
members.note: Fires 2,000 pots a year in a kiln behind the stockade and counts every shard.

members.role: Heir; pot-thrower of the Keepers
members.note: Hunts his own brother on Bolor's order and prays he does not find him.

members.role: Askar's younger son; deserter of the Keepers
members.note: Fled the stockade in November with a jar record and the death oath on his head.

famousDead: First pot-master of the Keepers; burned with the jar store at Kyzai in 1081.
FX12-007.secret: Ulanbek, one of the two Keepers who deserted, carries a page of the jar record that shows 30 jars a year going south, and the Pot-Throwers are hiding where he went.
hooks: Ulanbek sends word that he will sell the jar record to the Red Wind.
Karabek finds his brother in a Black Wind camp.
The Salt Wind demands the Keepers leave its grazing.

FX12-008.name: The Ringwall clan of the Dust Wind
FX12-008.title: Warden of the Murdash Ring
FX12-008.arms: a brown ring-wall around a white water-drop, on dun
FX12-008.words: Water for the guest, arrows for the raider.

military.office: Hereditary wardens of the Murdash ring-fort
military.unit: the Murdash garrison, 300 camel riders and archers
military.ties: They hold the khan's southern ring-fort against Horde raiders and guard the camel road south toward Morhaven.

FX12-008.power: The Murdash ring-fort and its well, 300 riders, and the watch over every caravan that leaves Bekar for the south.
FX12-008.history: After the Salt Shore in 1041, Khan Toghrul manned two ring-forts against the Horde, Ulanabad in the north and Murdash in the south, and gave Murdash to a Dust Wind camel-chief named Sapar who had lost two sons at the Salt Shore. His line has held it since. The Ringwalls keep the Path of the Well: the Dry Month in August, Well Day on 14 March, and water never refused to a traveler, even an orc. They also keep the old sky cairn at Akai tied with blue cloth, as many Dust Wind families who hold both faiths do. Since 1103 the khan's secret fire-oil caravans have passed the Murdash well on their way to Morhaven, and the Ringwalls have escorted them without being told what the jars hold. This spring 200 Dust Wind riders and 40 Keepers will take 30 jars south, and the Ringwall heir rides with them.
FX12-008.reputation: Hospitable to a fault and stubborn as their camels; the khan's most trusted Well folk.

members.role: Head of the clan; Warden of the Murdash Ring
members.note: Once gave water to a lost Horde raider at the Murdash well and shot him the next morning when he tried to steal a camel.

members.role: Sapar's wife; Well-Keeper's daughter from Bekar
members.note: Judges the garrison's quarrels by the Path of the Well, and nobody appeals.

members.role: Heir; captain of the oil-caravan escort
members.note: Has smelled the jars and knows it is not lamp oil.

members.role: Sapar's daughter; camel-archer
members.note: Wants to see Morhaven and has asked to ride with the caravan disguised as a driver.

famousDead: First warden of Murdash; lost two sons at the Salt Shore.
FX12-008.secret: Baisal opened a jar on the road in 1104, saw fire-oil, and told his mother, who has told her father the Well-Keeper of Bekar.
hooks: The oil caravan is ambushed on the road south.
The Well-Keeper of Bekar asks Idris of the Sea Wind what he should do with what he knows.
Saule rides with the caravan in disguise.

FX12-009.name: The Nine-Horses clan of the Blue Wind
FX12-009.title: Herd Lord of the Ilklun pastures
FX12-009.arms: nine white horses' heads in a ring, on blue
FX12-009.words: Count the herd, not the riders.
FX12-009.power: About 14,000 horses on the Ilklun and Burgol summer grass, the second herd of the Blue Wind after the khan's own, and a fixed place among the sellers at the Yarbek channel fair.
FX12-009.history: The Nine-Horses clan grew rich under Burun the Horse-Rich, who reigned from 968 and sold a third of his 30,000 horses west; its founder Tolubai drove nine of the khan's horses to Yarbek and came home with nine bags of Greyhaven silver. The clan has bred for the channel fair since, and Greyhaven buyers ask for its horses by name. It gives the khan one horse in thirty like any other family, and gives him sons for the guard like any Blue Wind family. The White Death of 1067 killed half its herd, and the clan rebuilt by buying Horde mares through Salt Edge thieves, which no one says aloud. Since 1080 it has sold through Kaidu Horsemaster's Horse Road. The head is the richest herd lord of the hearth tribes and wants a chief's place in the kurultai.
FX12-009.reputation: Horse-rich and silver-proud; the khan's best taxpayers and his loudest complainers.

members.role: Head of the clan; Herd Lord of the Ilklun pastures
members.note: Owns more horses than three western clans together and has never forgotten a single one he lost.

members.role: Tolubai's wife; mistress of the summer camps
members.note: Feeds the khan's tax-takers so well they forget to count.

members.role: Heir; horse-seller at the Yarbek fair
members.note: Can sell a lame horse to a Greyhaven buyer and be thanked for it.

members.role: Tolubai's daughter; rider of the Yam Riders
members.note: Rides under Kulan of the Blue Wind and knows that her captain is carrying a child she will not name the father of.

members.role: Tolubai's youngest son; keeper of the family hearth
members.note: By Blue Wind custom the youngest son keeps the hearth, and he intends to keep it lying down.

famousDead: Sold nine of Burun's horses at Yarbek for nine bags of silver and founded the clan's fortune.
FX12-009.secret: The clan rebuilt its herd after 1067 with Horde mares bought from Salt Edge orc thieves, and about a third of its horses carry blood bought from the khan's enemies.
hooks: Tolubai asks the khan for a chief's place in the kurultai, and the chiefs laugh.
Aruna is asked by Kulan to carry a message she should not carry.
A Horde rider comes asking for the price of his clan's stolen mares.

FX12-010.name: The Dawn-Drover clan of the Morning Wind
FX12-010.title: Master of the Yarbek drove road
FX12-010.arms: a gold sun over a line of running horses, on grey
FX12-010.power: The droving of most of the Morning Wind's horses to the khan's channel fair at Yarbek, about 300 drovers, and the November drive of the tribe's spare herds west.
FX12-010.history: After the Compact of 925 left the Yarbek fair to the khan, the Morning Wind grew rich by driving horses to it, and the Dawn-Drovers were the first family of that trade. They sing the drovers' songs of the Yarbek road and sell no horse before the dawn blessing on the shore. Every November since 1041 they have driven the Morning Wind's spare herds, about 30,000 sheep and 4,000 horses, west to winter north of Kultau on Horde grass under Reed Wind herders. The drovers are told it is a grazing bargain with the Reed Wind. The family's head knows more, because his grandfather drove the first herd in the autumn of 1041, a month after the Salt Shore. The drive is the most visible secret on the steppe, and no one has yet asked the right question.
FX12-010.reputation: Cheerful, loud and always on the road; good company at a fire and better at a horse fair.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Yarbek drove road
members.note: Sings the drovers' songs louder than anyone, especially when someone asks about the November drive.

members.role: Bori's wife; tally-keeper of the drove
members.note: Pays the grass price to the Horde's herders herself and calls it the Reed Wind's share.

members.role: Heir; lead drover of the November drive
members.note: Saw a Horde clan-mother count his father's horses north of Kultau and wants to know why.

members.role: Bori's daughter; horse-blesser at Yarbek
members.note: Leads the dawn blessing at the fair and is courted by a Greyhaven cog master's son.

famousDead: Drove the first Morning Wind herd west to Horde grass in the autumn of 1041.
FX12-010.secret: The Dawn-Drovers have paid the Horde's Keeper of the Grass a share of the grass price every autumn since 1090, and Bori knows it is the price of the Salt Shore.
hooks: Jangir asks the wrong person about the Horde clan-mother at the Horse Feast.
Horde raiders strike the November drive by mistake.
A Greyhaven cog master offers to buy the whole drove at Yarbek.

FX12-011.name: The Kularyk clan of the Morning Wind
FX12-011.title: Chief of the Kularyk clan
FX12-011.arms: a white salt-pan under a gold rising sun, on grey water
FX12-011.words: Salt and boats, boats and salt.

military.office: Captains of the Ozlun boatmen and the Kularyk hundreds
military.unit: about 300 horse-archers and 20 oared boats of the Morning Wind hundreds
military.ties: They lead the Morning Wind's boatmen on the channel shore, and in 1041 their riders sat on the right wing at the Salt Shore and never moved.

FX12-011.power: The Kularyk saltworks, the boatyards of Ozlun, about 8,000 horses and a seat at the chief's council of the Morning Wind.
FX12-011.history: The Kularyks were the boatwrights who built the Khan's 300 channel boats at Yarbek in 882, which Osric the Diver burned, and they have built boats on the Ozlun shore ever since. In 884 they helped load 70,000 horses onto Greyhaven cogs for the crossing of the Narrows. Since 925 they have also worked the Kularyk saltworks, and the salt and the boats have made them the richest clan of the Morning Wind after the chief's own. In 1041 their chief commanded the Morning Wind's right wing at the Salt Shore and held it still on his chief's order while the Salt Wind died. The clan has told itself for 60 years that it was a wise retreat. Altan's daughter Naran is Serik's wife, and the Kularyks have staked everything on her husband's raising.
FX12-011.reputation: Rich, shore-wise and close to the heir; the western tribes call them 'the right wing that never moved'.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Kularyk clan
members.note: Grandson of the captain of the right wing, and has never let a Salt Wind man drink at his fire.

members.role: Aktai's wife; mistress of the saltworks
members.note: Runs 400 salt-workers and sells the salt to Greyhaven cogs for twice what the Red Wind gets.

members.role: Heir; boat-captain of Ozlun
members.note: Rows the heir's wife Naran across the bay when she visits home, and she tells him things.

members.role: Aktai's daughter; lady-in-waiting to Naran at Kharsa
members.note: Knows that the khan's son has a lover in the Yam Riders, and that the lover is with child.

famousDead: Built the Khan's channel boats at Yarbek in 882.
Held the Morning Wind's right wing still at the Salt Shore on his chief's order.
FX12-011.secret: Kumis has told her father that Kulan of the Blue Wind carries Serik's child, and Aktai is deciding whether to tell Naran or the khatun first.
hooks: Kumis's secret reaches Naran before the Horse Feast.
Salt Wind riders demand blood-price for the right wing of 1041.
Greyhaven cogs bring an offer to build ships for the khan at Ozlun.

FX12-012.name: The Tide-Reader clan of the Sea Wind
FX12-012.title: Master of the Altsa landings
FX12-012.arms: a white horse swimming between green waves, on dark green
FX12-012.words: The Narrows are ours at slack water.
FX12-012.power: Twelve oared boats and two small cogs at the Altsa landings, the tide-lore of the Grey Channel Narrows, and the ferrying of horses to Sunland and Morhaven buyers.
FX12-012.history: In May 884 the Wind Empire's riders crossed the Narrows from Erkent in Greyhaven ships, and the Sea Wind boatmen who guided the cogs through the tides became the Tide-Readers. They have run boats and landings on the channel shore since, and they know the slack water of the Narrows better than any Greyhaven pilot. They took the Path of the Well with their chief in 978 and bless their horses with water, not milk. Since 1100 they have carried about 600 Sea Wind horses a year across the channel to Oskan Bay at Santora without the khan's tenth. Their boats come back with silver for the new Well shrine at Erkent and Sunland cloth for themselves. The khan's tally-keepers have started counting horses that leave the shore.
FX12-012.reputation: Sea-folk among riders, half Sunland in their dress; the best boatmen of the steppe and the worst liars.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Altsa landings
members.note: Has crossed the Narrows 900 times and drowned twice, he says, and been sent back by the Well both times.

members.role: Salim's wife; keeper of the landing tallies
members.note: Keeps two tallies of the horses that cross, one for the khan and one for the Well, and hates it.

members.role: Heir; cog-master of the Santora run
members.note: Sails the Santora run in a Sunland cog he won at dice and has a wife in each port, his mother suspects.

members.role: Salim's daughter; tide-reader
members.note: Can read the Narrows' tides by the color of the water and wants to sail past them.

famousDead: Guided the Greyhaven cogs through the Narrows in 884.
FX12-012.secret: The Tide-Readers carry the Sea Wind's 600 untaxed horses a year to Santora, and Jarkyn also carries letters between Idris and his cousin Oskan Bay that the khan would hang them for.
hooks: The khan's tally-keepers send a rider to count horses at the Altsa landings.
A storm catches Jarkyn's cog in the Narrows with 80 untaxed horses aboard.
Ulbike is offered a place on a Greyhaven ship bound for the Middle Sea.

FX12-013.name: The Cairn-Binders of Sibtu
FX12-013.title: Keeper of the Sky Cairn of Sibtu
FX12-013.arms: a stone cairn tied with a blue cloth, under an open sky
FX12-013.power: The Sky Cairn of Sibtu near Kharsa, the reading of omen bones at the Horse Feast beside the chief shaman, and the blessing of every khan since Ulagan.
FX12-013.history: When Ulagan built his tent-city at Kharsa in 871, a Blue Wind shaman tied the first blue cloth to the old stone cairn at Sibtu and blessed the camp under the Eternal Blue. Her line has kept the cairn since and has read the omen bones beside the chief shaman at every Horse Feast. The Cairn-Binders crack a sheep's shoulder-blade in the fire and read the lines, and the kurultai listens. At the Horse Feast of 1104 the omen bone cracked across the khan's line. Chief Shaman Ilga of the Blue, on Khatun Sorga's order, read it as a long road. The Cairn-Binders' head stood beside her and said nothing, and has not slept well since.
FX12-013.reputation: Holy, proud and close to the khan's house; the western tribes say their bones crack the way Kharsa wants.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Sky Cairn of Sibtu
members.note: Saw the bone crack across the khan's line and knows what it meant, because she has read 40 bones before it.

members.role: Heir; bone-reader of the Horse Feast
members.note: Thinks the bones should crack the way the kurultai needs, and has told the khatun so.

members.role: Zhanar's daughter; healer of the cairn camp
members.note: Has been asked by a guard captain about sores that will not heal, and guesses whose foot it is.

members.role: Orazbek's son; cairn-boy
members.note: Ties blue cloths to the cairn every morning and talks to the sky as if it answers.

famousDead: Tied the first blue cloth to the Sibtu cairn when Kharsa was founded.
FX12-013.secret: Zhanar believes the omen bone of 1104 foretold the khan's death within the year, and that Ilga lied about it on the khatun's order.
hooks: At the Horse Feast of 1105 the Cairn-Binders read the bone, and the khatun has told Orazbek what it must say.
Yesun asks Zhanar, in front of the kurultai, what the bone of 1104 really showed.
A Well-Keeper asks to stand beside the cairn at the Horse Feast.

FX12-014.name: The Stone-Ring clan of the Black Wind
FX12-014.title: Chief of the Stone-Ring riders
FX12-014.arms: no arms: a ring of black pebbles left in a stolen horse's empty stall
FX12-014.words: The hills feed no one. We feed ourselves.
FX12-014.power: About 60 riders who know every dry wadi from Kyzdash to the camel road, hidden pens in the hills, and buyers at every channel fair.
FX12-014.history: The Stone-Rings come from the poorest camps of the Black Wind, the families whose herds Berek burned at Kyzdash on 30 August 914. Their grass took a generation to come back, and the clan never waited for it. Among the Black Wind a boy's first stolen horse is feasted and a caught thief is disowned, and the Stone-Rings have a great many feasts and very few disownings. They drive other men's herds, steal from the channel fairs and the yam stations, and sell at the fairs of the Dust Wind. Two of their riders rode with Sartak of the Black Wind in the raid on the fire-oil caravans in 1079, and one of them still remembers the trail to the seeps. They bury their dead on hilltops in a ring of stones, and the ring has grown this year.
FX12-014.reputation: Thieves, drovers and hill-riders; hated by every hearth tribe and quietly hired by most.

members.role: Chief of the Stone-Ring riders
members.note: Rode with Sartak in 1079, saw the seeps by moonlight, and has never told anyone the way.

members.role: Shokan's sister; horse-seller at the Bekar fair
members.note: Has sold the khan's own yam horses back to the yam keepers twice.

members.role: Shokan's son; raider
members.note: Is sheltering a deserter of the Keepers of the Seeps in the clan's hill pens for a share of whatever he sells.

members.role: Karlygash's daughter; lookout
members.note: Wants to join the khan's Arrow Field, which no Black Wind girl has ever done.

famousDead: Branded for horse theft at Kyzdash in the same year as Sartak and hanged the year after.
FX12-014.secret: Shokan knows the trail to the seeps as well as Sartak does, and Sartak means to sell it to a Greyhaven cog master; the Stone-Rings mean to sell it first.
hooks: A Greyhaven cog master comes to Bekar asking for a guide to the salt flats.
The Keepers of the Seeps track their deserter to the Stone-Ring pens.
Aiym rides to the Kharsa Arrow Field to shoot.

FX12-015.name: The Camel-Mother clan of the Dust Wind
FX12-015.title: Chief of the Turlun camel camps
FX12-015.arms: a brown camel under a white water-drop, a calf at her side, on dun

military.office: Captains of the Dust Wind camel riders
military.unit: about 300 of the 1,000 Dust Wind camel riders
military.ties: They guard the camel road south and ride escort for the khan's caravans, the oil caravans among them.

FX12-015.power: About 6,000 camels at the Turlun camps, the hiring of drivers and guards to every caravan that passes Bekar, and the road south toward Morhaven.
FX12-015.history: The Camel-Mothers began in 895, when their founder led the camel strings that carried fire-oil 600 km to the Wind Empire's siege of Morhaven, and came home with more camels than she had taken. The clan has bred camels and guided caravans on the southern road since. It took the Path of the Well from Qadiri camel-drivers of the Bekar road in the 990s and keeps the Dry Month and Well Day, but its old women still tie blue cloth on the sky cairn at Akai. Since 1103 the khan's secret oil caravans have gone south through Bekar, and Camel-Mother drivers lead the camels without being told what the jars hold. Their chief follows Faris of the Dust Wind, whose vote, like Idris's, is for sale to whoever gives the Well a seat. The Camel-Mothers would sell theirs for less.
FX12-015.reputation: Patient, rich and close-mouthed; the best caravan-folk of the steppe, and the most pious.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Turlun camel camps
members.note: Has never refused water to anyone, and once gave it to a Horde raider who had killed her cousin.

members.role: Raushan's husband; caravan master of the southern road
members.note: Has led 60 caravans to Morhaven and knows the price of every innkeeper on the road.

members.role: Heir; camel-rider captain
members.note: Will lead the drivers of this spring's oil caravan and has been told only that the jars are worth more than his life.

members.role: Raushan's daughter; Well-girl of Bekar
members.note: Wants the Well to have its seat at the Horse Feast and believes the khan will give it if asked nicely.

famousDead: Led the oil camel strings to the siege of Morhaven in 895.
FX12-015.secret: Zaid has guessed what the khan's jars hold, and has sent a quiet word to a Morhaven innkeeper who sells such news to the Dawn Church.
hooks: The Dawn Church learns what crosses Morhaven in Dust Wind camel packs.
Faris of the Dust Wind asks the clan how it will vote at the Horse Feast.
A Black Wind band raids the oil caravan on the road south.

FX12-016.name: The Two-Hearth clan of the Salt Wind
FX12-016.title: Chief of the Ulanai shore camps
FX12-016.arms: a white salt-crust circle with two fires inside it, on brown
FX12-016.words: The oil is under our grass.

military.office: Captains of the Salt Wind boatmen and hundreds
military.unit: about 300 horse-archers and boatmen of the Salt Wind hundreds
military.ties: Their oared boats carry fire-oil pots in war under the Keepers' orders, and their riders died in thousands at the Salt Shore.

FX12-016.power: The Ulanai shore camps, about 5,000 horses, salt-fishing boats, and a voice among the four western tribes.
FX12-016.history: The Two-Hearths are a Salt Wind clan of the Ulanai shore, half orc and half human for so long that no one counts any more. They light two hearths in every tent, one for the Eternal Blue and one for the orc Storm and Mare, and raise half-orc and human children alike. Their boats carried the fire-oil pots that burned the Solen barges at Kyzai in 425, and their camels carried oil to the siege of Morhaven. They lost about 400 riders at the Salt Shore in 1041, while two other tribes stood still on the wings. Since 1052 the khan's Keepers of the Seeps have camped on their grazing, and since 1085 they may not ride within sight of the stockade. The oil under their grass makes the khan rich, and the Two-Hearths have never had a jar of it.
FX12-016.reputation: Proud half-orc shore folk who remember every grievance of the Salt Shore and the seeps; hard friends, harder enemies.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Ulanai shore camps
members.note: Half-orc, broad as a door, and has never forgiven the Morning Wind for the right wing of 1041.

members.role: Uzak's wife; salt-fisher mother of the camps
members.note: Keeps both hearths lit and gives salt to the Salt Sea spirits before every fishing season.

members.role: Heir; boat-captain of the fire-pot boats
members.note: Has rowed the Keepers' pots in drills and says the Salt Wind should keep a few.

members.role: Uzak's daughter; quiver-sister of Tamsa
members.note: Shoots beside Tamsa of the Salt Wind and believes, as Tamsa does, in the rider of two peoples.

famousDead: Died at the Salt Shore with 400 of the clan while the wings stood still.
FX12-016.secret: Yerlan and his boatmen have kept back four fire-oil pots from the Keepers' drills over three years, and they are buried under the clan's winter hearth.
hooks: The Keepers count their pots and come four short.
Kulpash rides west with Tamsa to see the Horde's rider of two peoples.
If the Salt Shore secret comes out, the Two-Hearths will want blood from the Morning Wind.

FX12-017.name: The Well-Water clan of the Sea Wind
FX12-017.title: Chief of the Arskent clan
FX12-017.arms: a white horse's head drinking from a blue well, on green

military.office: Captains of the Arskent hundreds
military.unit: about 300 horse-archers of the Sea Wind hundreds
military.ties: They ride in the Sea Wind's 1,200 at Erkent and guard the channel shore against Horde raiders and Greyhaven smugglers alike.

FX12-017.power: The Arskent pastures, about 7,000 horses, the horse and felt trade to Sunland merchants, and the guardianship of the Turai Mounds.
FX12-017.history: The Well-Waters were the first clan of the Sea Wind to follow chief Nasr onto the Path of the Well in 978, and they gave the first Well-Keeper his tent at Erkent. They bless their horses with water, keep the Dry Month in August and judge their quarrels before a Well-Keeper. They have married daughters into Sunland horse-dealing families for a century, and their grandchildren speak Qadiri as well as the Rider tongue. Their pastures hold the Turai Mounds, where the Wind Empire buried its lords, and the clan has guarded them since 884. They lost the vote for a Well-Keeper at the Horse Feast of 1096 six to three. This year they mean to win it, by whatever vote Yesun or the khan will trade.
FX12-017.reputation: Pious, polished and half-Sunland; the steppe's most foreign clan and proud of it.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Arskent clan
members.note: Speaks for the Well in every council of the Sea Wind and was the loudest voice in 1096.

members.role: Hamza's wife; daughter of a Santora horse-dealer
members.note: Writes to her Santora cousins every month and knows the price of a horse in four cities.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Arskent hundreds
members.note: Has dug into a Turai mound by night and found lamellar of dwarven make.

members.role: Hamza's daughter; student of a Well-Keeper
members.note: Wants to be the first woman Well-Keeper of the steppe, which the Path does not forbid and nobody has tried.

famousDead: First of the clan to take the Path of the Well, beside chief Nasr in 978.
FX12-017.secret: Kairat has taken Irondeep lamellar from a Turai grave-mound and sold two coats to a Santora dealer, robbing the Wind Empire's dead.
hooks: A Santora dealer asks for more dwarven lamellar.
Yesun offers the Well a seat for the Well-Waters' vote.
Yasmin asks the Well-Keeper of Erkent to teach her the judging.

FX12-018.name: The Burgol clan of the Blue Wind
FX12-018.title: Chief of the Burgol clan
FX12-018.arms: a blue horsetail on a silver crossbar over a grey wolf's head, on white
FX12-018.words: We gave the khan his sons.

military.office: Captains of the Blue Wind hundreds of the north
military.unit: about 600 horse-archers of the Blue Wind hundreds
military.ties: They lead the northern hundreds of the khan's own tribe and give more sons to the Silver Tablet Guard than any other Blue Wind clan.

FX12-018.power: The Burgol and Ilklun summer grass north of Kharsa, about 11,000 horses, 600 riders, and the old loyalty of Khan Toghrul's men.
FX12-018.history: When Ulagan destroyed the Yarbek in 871 and split their men among the tribes, the Burgol clan of the Blue Wind took the Yarbek herds of the north and became the largest clan of the khan's own tribe. It has given the khan sons for his guard and horses for his tax ever since. Its chiefs rode with Toghrul the Watchful for 38 years, and when the chiefs forced Toghrul out in 1079 the Burgol chief was the only one who did not vote. Toghrul died at Ersgol in 1086 among his daughters' households, and the Burgol chief carried his bier. The clan serves Ozbek and has never trusted him. Its chief's mother was one of Toghrul's daughters, and some of the clan's old men say the Burgol blood has a better claim than Ozbek's.
FX12-018.reputation: The khan's own tribe's proudest clan, loyal to the house and cool to the man.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Burgol clan
members.note: Grandson of Toghrul through his mother, and has never once spoken the khan's name without a pause before it.

members.role: Kenes's wife; mistress of the Burgol camps
members.note: Is a Grey Wind woman and a cousin of the khatun, and writes to her every month.

members.role: Heir; captain of the northern hundreds
members.note: Has the lean frame of the Kharsan blood and has started to count which chiefs would vote for him.

members.role: Kenes's daughter; widow of a Silver Tablet guardsman
members.note: Her husband died at the Coldbarrow Bridge in 1102 and she blames the khan, who sent the guard too far.

famousDead: Burgol chief who alone did not vote to force Toghrul out in 1079 and carried his bier at Ersgol.
FX12-018.secret: Kenes's mother was Toghrul's daughter, and under the Tent Law her son should have been raised Kharsan at Ersgol; her husband took her home to Burgol in the White Death winter and the house let it pass, so Arman carries the lean-blood, and a Red Wind envoy has already asked whether the Burgol would take the khanship if the Kharsan line failed.
hooks: Yesun offers Arman the khanship if the cords of 912 break the Kharsan claim.
Arman shows the first signs of the Kharsan sickness.
The khatun learns from her cousin Gulim what the Red Wind envoy asked.

FX12-019.name: The Dry-Wells clan of the Grey Wind
FX12-019.title: Chief of the Akar clan
FX12-019.arms: a grey arrow standing in a dry white well-mouth, on grey
FX12-019.words: The wells were dry. The Solen were not.

military.office: Captains of the Grey Wind hundreds of Akar
military.unit: about 400 horse-archers of the Grey Wind hundreds
military.ties: They ride in the Grey Wind's 1,600 at Kyztai and in the Ring Hunt, and many of their sons serve in the Keepers of the Seeps.

FX12-019.power: The Akar pastures and the Field of the Dry Wells, about 8,000 horses, and the right to speak first after the chief in the Grey Wind's council.
FX12-019.history: The Dry-Wells clan claims descent from the riders who drew a Solen army of 12,000 to its death at the Dry Wells near Kyztai in 428 under Toghan Swift-Arrow. The clan guards the battlefield still, with its rusted Solen helmets in a cairn. Its chiefs have sat at the Grey Wind's council since there was a council, and its daughters have married Kharsan sons-in-tent and gone to live at Kharsa under the Tent Law. It backed Ulagan in 870 and Berek in 913, and its sons fill the Grey Wind's hundreds and the Keepers of the Seeps. In the Ring Hunt of 1104 its chief saw the heir's horse falter and the heir hide a limp. If the Hearth Tribes fall, the Grey Wind falls, and the Dry-Wells clan falls first.
FX12-019.reputation: Old, upright and dull, by its own boast; the Grey Wind's memory and its backbone.

members.role: Head of the clan; Chief of the Akar clan
members.note: Can recite every chief of the clan back to 428 and every one of their horses.

members.role: Ersain's wife; keeper of the Dry Wells cairn
members.note: Polishes the Solen helmets on the cairn every spring and gives them names.

members.role: Heir; rider of the Keepers of the Seeps
members.note: Shares a name with the Grey Wind chief and gets his letters by mistake twice a year.

members.role: Ersain's daughter; wife of a Kharsan son-in-tent
members.note: Lives at Kharsa under the Tent Law, and her children will be raised Kharsan whatever she wants.

famousDead: Rode with Toghan Swift-Arrow at the Dry Wells in 428.
FX12-019.secret: Moldir has told her father that the khatun keeps a second set of cords in her chest that she reads at night, and that one bundle is so old the cord is black.
hooks: Yesun's searchers come to Kharsa looking for old cords, and Moldir knows where they are.
Bars receives a letter meant for the Grey Wind chief.
A Solen scholar asks to dig at the Field of the Dry Wells.

FX13-001.name: Clan Cairnhold
FX13-001.title: Elder of Clan Cairnhold

military.office: Captains of Highcastle and its cisterns
military.unit: the Highcastle garrison, 1,200 men, under Captain Anselm Cairnhold
military.ties: A Cairnhold has commanded the garrison of Highcastle in most generations since First Speaker Ivo Cairnhold died at Redford in 470.

FX13-001.power: Summer pastures above Highwold, the captaincy of Highcastle's garrison and a marriage tie to the First Speaker's own kin.
FX13-001.history: The Cairnholds marched with Bran Greycloak against the Solen weigh-house at Amberhurst in 330 and have sat on the Council of Valleys since. First Speaker Ivo Cairnhold refused Urzag Redhand's grain bargain in 469 and died when the Old Horde burned Redford the next spring; Egil Cairnhold died First Speaker in the Rash Fever of 598. Bard Cairnhold married Helga Stonefoot and took her name, and was killed in the high valleys in 1088. The clan's cousin Liss is the chart-maker every southern explorer wants to hire.
FX13-001.reputation: Old, steady herders who have given the League two First Speakers and a hundred captains.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of Highwold
members.note: He backed Helga by the one vote that made her First Speaker and has never asked her what killed his cousin.

members.role: Captain of Highcastle and its cisterns
members.note: He knows every rock-cut tank under Highcastle and could hold the town through a winter on them.

members.role: Brother of the late Bard Stonefoot
members.note: He found his brother's body in 1088 in a valley he was not supposed to enter, and it was burned and clawed, not crushed.

members.role: Heir; herder of the high pastures
members.note: She runs the summer herds to 3,000 m and has seen white shapes over the Stonefoot valleys that are too big for eagles.

famousDead: First Speaker who refused Urzag Redhand's grain bargain and died at Redford
Married Helga Stonefoot; died in the high valleys, said to be an avalanche
FX13-001.secret: Orm Cairnhold knows Bard was killed by something with claws in the closed valleys, and the clan has kept silent for Helga's sake.
hooks: A Varennan beast-catcher asks Ylva about the white shapes above Highcastle.
Orm decides it is time the Council knew how his brother died.

FX13-002.name: Clan Bearley
FX13-002.title: Elder of Clan Bearley
FX13-002.power: The cattle runs of the Bearfold plain and a vote in the Bearfold valley council.
FX13-002.history: The Bearleys have grazed cattle on the Bearfold plain since before the Old Horde burned Redford in 455. Their herds and the Redfords' share the same passes, and the two clans have fought over strays for six centuries. They settle it on the wall-run at Highcastle when they cannot settle it with sticks. Since 1100 the Redford herds have lost more cattle to 'orc raiders' than in any year since 799.
FX13-002.reputation: Good herders, bad neighbours, and never short of a bull.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of Bearley
members.note: He buys cattle from the Blackrigg kin with the Redford brand cut out and asks no questions.

members.role: Heir; wall-run champion
members.note: She has won two wall-runs against Redford champions and wants a third against a Stonefoot.

members.role: Younger son; herders' slinger
members.note: He can knock a wolf off a ledge at a hundred paces with a sling stone.

famousDead: Won the cattle quarrel of 801 against Redford on the wall-run
FX13-002.secret: The Bearley elders buy Redford cattle rustled by the Blackrigg kin and sell them south as their own.
hooks: A Redford herder finds a cut brand on a Bearley bull at the Bearfold market.
Two valleys quarrel over a herd, and the wall-run is set for a day of ice.

FX13-003.name: the Corradin kin
FX13-003.title: Elder of the Corradin Smelters
FX13-003.arms: a red flame over a silver ingot, on black
FX13-003.power: The smelting furnaces below the Amberhurst galleries, where League silver ore becomes ingots.
FX13-003.history: In May 719 about 30,000 hungry peasants of the Holy Coast walked north into the highlands, and First Speaker Hild Stonefoot put them to work in the silver and iron mines for their food. The Corradins were among them, and they still keep their Old Solen names. They became smelters under the Silverveins and have run the Whitfield furnaces for three centuries. Since the Irondeep crews doubled the silver in 1060, more ore has passed through Corradin hands than ever.
FX13-003.reputation: Hard-working Flightfolk who still pray in Old Solen and marry their own.

members.role: Head of the kin; Elder of the Smelters
members.note: He skims a thread of silver from every ingot, as his grandmother did, and lets Gerda Silvervein blame the dwarves.

members.role: Heir; furnace-mistress
members.note: She keeps the furnace books and has noticed that the slag weighs more than it should.

members.role: Younger son; Greycloak crossbowman
members.note: He serves abroad with the companies and sends his pay home to buy his family out of the furnaces.

members.role: Clemens's mother
members.note: She keeps a Holy Coast deed to a farm her family lost in 719 and prays over it every Return Day.

famousDead: Led his family north in the Upland Flight of 719
FX13-003.secret: The Corradins have skimmed silver from the League's ore for generations; the loss Gerda Silvervein blames on the dwarf crews is theirs.
hooks: Gerda Silvervein sends a dwarf assayer to weigh the Whitfield slag.
Tavia must choose between her father and the Silver Chest.

FX13-004.name: Clan Deepstead
FX13-004.title: Elder of the Deepstead Galleries
FX13-004.arms: a black chevron over a silver vein, on slate
FX13-004.power: The Deepstead galleries and the miners of the Highwold valleys.
FX13-004.history: The Deepsteads learned to dig deep beside Solen engineers and kept their own galleries at Deepstead when the empire's tax-men left. In April 1060 First Speaker Ylva Stonefoot brought Irondeep dwarf crews into the deep silver for a fifth of what they raised, and the Deepsteads lost the deepest work to them. The League's silver doubled and the Deepsteads' pride halved. In autumn 1104 Deepstead miners following the dwarves' tunnels saw what the dwarves had found under Redford.
FX13-004.reputation: Proud, bitter miners who hate the dwarf crews and say so.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of the Galleries
members.note: He is driving a gallery from his own side toward the new Redford vein and has told no one.

members.role: Heir; gallery foreman
members.note: He fought a dwarf crewman in a tunnel in 1103 and lost two teeth.

members.role: Thurstan's daughter
members.note: She learned figures from a dwarf tally-keeper and is secretly friends with him.

famousDead: Opened the Deepstead galleries after the Solen engineers left
FX13-004.secret: Clan Deepstead knows of the rich new silver vein under Redford, which even the Redfords do not know of, and is tunnelling toward it.
hooks: The Deepstead gallery breaks into a dwarf tunnel.
Aldith's dwarf friend warns her the crews have told their queen first.

FX13-005.name: Clan Blytheton
FX13-005.title: Speaker of the Whitfield Valley
FX13-005.power: The Whitfield valley's seat on the Council of Valleys, held by election but almost always by a Blytheton.
FX13-005.history: The Blythetons rebuilt the Whitfield villages after the Old Horde burned the southern valleys in 470 and have spoken for Whitfield on the Council ever since. They have never produced a First Speaker and have always backed one. For thirty years they voted with Hugo Redford, and in July 1099 they voted for his son Tomas and lost by one. The Redford Men need a third of the Council to force a new election, and the Blythetons are one of their surest votes.
FX13-005.reputation: Practical, well-fed and always on the side that is winning, they hope.

members.role: Head of the clan; Speaker of Whitfield
members.note: He took 300 highland silver from Aldmark's agent through Tomas Redford to vote for the crossbow contract.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She thinks the League should never sell crossbows to the emperor who claimed its halls, and she says so in the valley hall.

members.role: Younger son; clerk to Speaker Redford
members.note: He carries messages between the Redford Men and has read some of them.

FX13-005.secret: Speaker Hamo Blytheton has taken Aldmark silver through Tomas Redford for his vote in March.
hooks: Wynn stands against her father for the Whitfield seat.
Osric carries a letter that names the price of every Redford vote.

FX13-006.name: Clan Foxby
FX13-006.title: Captain of Redford Tower and the Skardush Watch

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Skardush watch
military.unit: the Skardush watch, 1,000 men of Redford Tower
military.ties: A Foxby has kept the beacon of Redford Tower since it was raised in 800, and no orc raid has surprised Redford since.

FX13-006.power: Command of Redford Tower's garrison and the beacon that warns the League of the Horde.
FX13-006.history: After the orc raid of 799, the Redford clan raised a 22 m stone tower with a beacon over the valley road, and gave its keeping to the Foxbys of Bearfold, herders who had caught the raiders in the pass on their way home. First Speaker Brodd Foxby died of the Black Cough in 916. The Foxbys have watched the Horde-held Skardush Pass for three centuries and lit the beacon eleven times. In the autumn of 1104 Captain Brenna Foxby saw riders on the Skardush who were not herders.
FX13-006.reputation: The eyes of the League on the Horde road.

members.role: Head of the clan; Captain of Redford Tower
members.note: She saw Horde scouts on the Skardush with a half-orc among them and was told by Speaker Redford to say nothing until after the vote.

members.role: Heir; tower crossbowman
members.note: Named for the First Speaker, he wants to scout the far side of the pass himself.

members.role: Brenna's husband; beacon-keeper
members.note: He has laid the beacon fire fresh every morning for twenty years.

famousDead: First Speaker who died of the Black Cough in 916
FX13-006.secret: Brenna has seen Tarn Halfblood scouting the Skardush with Horde riders and has kept it from the Council on Speaker Redford's order.
hooks: The beacon must be lit, or not, on the night of the Council's vote.
Brodd crosses the Skardush alone and does not come back.

FX13-007.name: Clan Kestrelside
FX13-007.title: Hire-Captain of the Kestrelside Banners
FX13-007.arms: a black crossbow on pale blue

military.office: Hire-captains of the Greycloak Companies
military.unit: the Kestrelside banners, 800 heavy crossbowmen on winter contract at Dorium in Varenna
military.ties: Kestrelside captains have led League companies abroad since Asa Greycloak made the contracts a League office, and a fifth of their pay goes to the Silver Chest.

FX13-007.power: Kestrelside Castle in the hills above Highcastle and a standing contract with the crown of Varenna.
FX13-007.history: When First Speaker Asa Greycloak made the crossbow companies a League office between 952 and 968, the Kestrelsides were among the first hire-captains, and they have sold crossbows abroad ever since. They held the stakes at Hartgate for Aldmark in 1051 beside the Greycloaks. For three generations their banners have wintered in Varenna under contract to the Valdane kings. Their 800 men are due home in April with the other companies abroad.
FX13-007.reputation: The richest hire-captains after the Greycloaks, and the most Varennan.

members.role: Head of the clan; hire-captain at Dorium
members.note: He signed a Varennan contract with a clause that binds his banners to march up the Palella if called before April.

members.role: Heir; banner-captain
members.note: She commands 200 at Dorium and has heard the Varennan generals talk about barges.

members.role: Younger son; serving in Ashmere
members.note: He serves in a company hired by Ashmere at Stagley, the very town his father may be sent against.

famousDead: One of the first hire-captains under Asa Greycloak's contract law
FX13-007.secret: The Kestrelside contract binds 800 League crossbowmen to fight for Varenna against Ashmere if the Stagley stroke comes before April.
hooks: Varenna calls the Kestrelside banners to the barges at Dorium in late March.
Father and son may face each other across Stagley's walls.

FX13-008.name: Clan Scree
FX13-008.title: Master of the Gorge Cribs
FX13-008.arms: three grey bars like stacked timber, on brown

military.office: Hereditary masters of the rock-crews of the Greycloak Gorge
military.unit: 200 of the 400 Ridge School rock-crews, who keep the stone cribs of the Greycloak Gorge and the Redford road
military.ties: A Scree cut the first rope in the Greycloak Gorge in 331, and the rock-crews still drill under Ada Stonefoot's Ridge School to cut them again.

FX13-008.power: The keeping of the rock cribs above the Greycloak Gorge, the League's oldest defence.
FX13-008.history: On 12 July 331 about 1,500 highlanders cut the ropes holding back rocks stacked behind timber cribs above a gorge below Highcastle, and about 1,100 Solen soldiers died under them. The Screes built those cribs and cut the first rope. They have rebuilt them every generation since, and the gorge has eaten every army that tried the road. The timber must be renewed every twenty years, and the last renewal was paid for in 1084.
FX13-008.reputation: Rope-and-timber men, proud of a gorge full of old bones.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Gorge Cribs
members.note: He spent the timber silver of 1100 on his daughter's wedding and patched the cribs with rope.

members.role: Heir; rock-crew captain
members.note: She climbed the cribs last autumn and found half the timbers soft enough to push a thumb into.

members.role: Hesta's son
members.note: He plays in the gorge among the Solen bones and has a helmet with a hole in it.

famousDead: Built the cribs and cut the first rope in the Greycloak Gorge in 331
FX13-008.secret: The cribs above the Greycloak Gorge have rotted; if they were cut tomorrow, only half the rock would fall.
hooks: The Council orders a drill-cutting of one crib on Charter Day.
Hesta asks the Silver Chest for timber money, and Gerda Silvervein asks where the last payment went.

FX13-009.name: Clan Coldencombe
FX13-009.title: Keeper of the Highwold Towers
FX13-009.arms: a white castle on dark slate

military.office: Hereditary keepers of the Highwold valley towers
military.unit: 400 men of the valley pass garrisons in eight towers and cisterns
military.ties: Coldencombe keepers man eight of the League's thirty valley towers and keep their cisterns full against siege.

FX13-009.power: Coldencombe Castle and the towers and cisterns of the Highwold passes, with their mule tolls.
FX13-009.history: The Coldencombes stood in Alda the Pike-Mother's hedge at Amberhurst on 4 July 471, when 4,000 highlanders broke six waves of the Old Horde, and the League gave them the Highwold towers to keep. Their towers sit on the mule roads and take a small toll from every beast. They have guarded the passes through two orc ages without a siege. Lately the toll has grown fat on travellers who should not be there.
FX13-009.reputation: Dependable tower-keepers, a little too fond of the toll box.

members.role: Head of the clan; Keeper of the Highwold Towers
members.note: He let two Aldmark 'surveyors' through his towers for a purse and suspects they were Ravenscar men.

members.role: Heir; tower captain
members.note: She turned back a smuggler's mule-train last month and was told by her father to let it pass next time.

members.role: Younger son; cistern-keeper
members.note: He knows a dry cistern tunnel that runs under the tower walls to the far side of the pass.

famousDead: Stood in the pike hedge at Amberhurst in 471
FX13-009.secret: Wulfric Coldencombe sells passage through the Highwold towers to smugglers and spies, Aldmark's among them.
hooks: A Ravenscar agent shows up at Highcastle with a Coldencombe toll token.
Brand's dry tunnel becomes the smugglers' favourite road.

FX13-010.name: Clan Tiller
FX13-010.title: Master of the Tiller-Makers of Highcastle
FX13-010.power: The tiller and spanner workshops of Highcastle, which make the stocks and spanning levers for the League's heavy crossbows.
FX13-010.history: The Tillers have made crossbow stocks and spanning gear in Highcastle since the companies began working abroad. The Crossbow-Makers of Roseham make the bows; the Tillers make everything that holds and spans them. In 1062 a Tiller watched a dwarf crewman at Amberhurst span a steel bow with a lever that doubled its punch. The family has quietly been making copies since.
FX13-010.reputation: Clever joiners who argue with the Roseham makers about who really wins the League's wars.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Tiller-Makers
members.note: He has sold forty copied dwarf spanning levers to Northreach for the Ice Walkers.

members.role: Heir; master joiner
members.note: She wants to sell the lever openly and let the Roseham makers choke on it.

members.role: Younger son; Greycloak crossbowman
members.note: He carries one of his father's levers abroad and every captain wants to buy it.

FX13-010.secret: The Tillers copy a dwarven steel-bow lever that Irondeep law forbids anyone outside Irondeep to make.
hooks: An Irondeep crew-master sees Ulf's lever at the Bolt and Bracer.
Ivo Stringer of Roseham offers to buy the Tillers out.

FX13-011.name: Clan Rennick
FX13-011.title: Master of the Whitfield Caves
FX13-011.power: The cheese caves of Whitfield, whose great wheels sell in the Sunland markets for silver.
FX13-011.history: The Rennicks have aged cheese in the caves above Whitfield since the Broken Crowns, when the League sold to every side. A Whitfield wheel aged three years is carried down by mule to the Sunlands and sold at a price per pound close to silver. In 1050 the Rennicks broke into an old Solen silver gallery behind their deepest cave and found it the perfect cold for cheese. They never registered it with the Silver Chest.
FX13-011.reputation: Rich, round and smelling of their caves; everyone's favourite guests.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Caves
members.note: He lets the Scarth kin store goods among his wheels for rent in silver.
