members.role: Heir; cave-mistress
members.note: She has found a thread of silver ore in the wall of the old gallery where the best wheels age.

members.role: Hesketh's daughter; mule-driver to the Sunlands
members.note: She drives the cheese down to the Sunland fairs and knows every inn on the road.

famousDead: Broke into the old Solen gallery behind the caves in 1050
FX13-011.secret: The Rennicks age their best cheese in an unregistered Solen silver gallery with ore still in the walls, and hide smugglers' goods among the wheels.
hooks: A Silver Chest surveyor asks to see the back of the deepest cave.
A wheel of cheese bound for the Sunlands is found full of smuggled drake feathers.

FX13-012.name: Clan Packstone
FX13-012.title: Master of the Mule Gate
FX13-012.arms: a gold wheat sheaf on dark green
FX13-012.words: Up With Bread, Down With Silver
FX13-012.power: The great mule-trains that carry Sunland grain up to Highcastle and silver down, and the Mule Gate Inn.
FX13-012.history: When the League stopped paying the Solen tribute in 756 and grew rich in silver and poor in grain, someone had to carry bread up the mountain. The Packstones began with twenty mules in 761 and now run three hundred. They keep the Mule Gate Inn inside Highcastle's gate, where guides are hired at one silver a day. Grain is carried up, so bread in Highcastle costs half again the plains price, and the Packstones decide the half.
FX13-012.reputation: Indispensable, rich and blamed for every loaf.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Mule Gate
members.note: She holds back Sunland grain in her Roseham barns each spring until the Silver Chest pays her price.

members.role: Heir; train-master
members.note: He has led trains over the passes in blizzards and lost only one mule, which he still mourns.

members.role: Dagny's daughter; keeper of the Mule Gate Inn
members.note: She rents rooms to every stranger in Highcastle and knows which one is a Varennan beast-catcher.

famousDead: Led the first Packstone mule-train up to Highcastle in 761
FX13-012.secret: The Packstones hoard grain each spring to force up Highcastle's bread price, and Gerda Silvervein's Chest has paid it for three bad years.
hooks: A bad harvest in the Sunlands and a hungry Highcastle: the Packstone barns at Roseham are full.
Liss Cairnhold's charts are stolen from her room at the Mule Gate Inn.

FX13-013.name: Clan Hornby
FX13-013.title: Master of the Hornby Studs
FX13-013.arms: a dark red horse on tan
FX13-013.power: The mule studs of the Bearfold plain, which breed most of the League's pack mules.
FX13-013.history: The Hornbys bred cattle on the Bearfold plain until the League's silver trade began to need mules, and from 760 they bred donkey stallions to valley mares. A Hornby mule can carry 100 kg over a 3,000 m pass in snow. They sell to the Packstones, the Greycloak companies and anyone who pays. Some of those buyers come over the Skardush.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Studs
members.note: He sells mules to Horde traders at the foot of the Skardush, though the League has signed nothing with the Horde.

members.role: Heir; breeder
members.note: She can turn a breech foal and sits up all night with any mare in trouble.

members.role: Younger son; drover
members.note: He drives the mules to the Skardush meeting-place and has made friends with an orc drover his own age.

FX13-013.secret: The Hornbys sell pack mules to Horde traders over the Skardush, and some of them carry the Horde's supplies on the Gordush.
hooks: Brenna Foxby's watch catches Kettil coming back from the Skardush.
Aldmark's agent learns that Horde baggage trains walk on Hornby mules.

FX13-014.name: Clan Greydale
FX13-014.title: Hall-Keeper of Greydale
FX13-014.power: The Free Hall of Greydale, chosen by its valley for eleven generations, and the trust of the Highwold herders.
FX13-014.history: The Greydale valley has chosen its hall-keeper from the same family since the 560s, when the Twelve Books banned other faiths in the cities but the Charter kept the highland halls open. The Greydales stood with the Free Hall of Amberhurst when the League refused the Iron Reform in 1003 and again when Aldwin claimed its priests in 1089. They preach against the Aldmark contract in every Highwold village. Their own son serves in a Greycloak company.
FX13-014.reputation: Fierce Free Hall keepers who love the League more than its silver.

members.role: Head of the clan; Hall-Keeper of Greydale
members.note: She preaches that a crossbow sold to the emperor is a bolt in the back of the Free Halls.

members.role: Hilde's son; Greycloak crossbowman
members.note: His company is already listed in Ulric Greycloak's private promise to Aldmark for the Gordush.

members.role: Heir; hall-singer
members.note: She carries Hall-Keeper Aelfric of Amberhurst's Northreach silver to the valley halls that will vote no.

famousDead: Spoke for the Highwold halls when the League refused the Iron Reform in 1003
FX13-014.secret: Hilde Greydale preaches against the Aldmark contract while her own son's company is already promised to it, and the Greydales pass Northreach silver to the valley halls.
hooks: Aelfric's company is ordered to march for the Gordush the day after the vote.
Ulric Greycloak's men catch Ingrid with Northreach silver.

FX13-015.name: Clan Lorne
FX13-015.title: Reader of the Charter of Highcastle
FX13-015.arms: a broken white crown on dark blue
FX13-015.power: The reading of the Charter on Charter Day, the drafting of every hire contract, and the League's only copy of the Charter in Old Solen besides the original.
FX13-015.history: In 761 the Council answered High Luminary Benedict's claim to the Highland tribute by reading the Charter aloud, and the clerk who read it was a Lorne. Every Charter Day since, a Lorne has read the clause that no outside king may tax the League. Since Asa Greycloak's time the Lornes have also drafted the hire contracts in Old Solen. They know the Charter better than any living person, including its faded parts.
FX13-015.reputation: Dry, exact and quietly the most powerful clerks in the League.

members.role: Head of the clan; Reader of the Charter
members.note: He has read a faded clause under the Charter's seal that no one has read aloud since 612.

members.role: Heir; drafter of hire contracts
members.note: She drafted the Aldmark contract the Council will vote on and slipped in a clause that ends it after one season.

members.role: Younger son; clerk at Ostra
members.note: He keeps the League's contracts at the Ostran banks and drinks with Aldmark clerks.

famousDead: Read the Charter to answer the Holy See's tribute claim in 761
FX13-015.secret: A faded clause of the Charter owes 1,500 soldiers to 'the emperor' whenever he goes to war; an Aldmark lawyer could argue the Emperor of Aldmark inherits it.
hooks: Perrin lets slip to an Aldmark clerk that the Charter has a forgotten clause.
Ulric Greycloak finds the one-season clause in his contract the night before the vote.

FX13-016.name: Clan Hawkhallow
FX13-016.title: Elder of the Hawkhallow Cragsmen
FX13-016.arms: a black eagle on pale stone
FX13-016.power: The right to take eagle eggs, chamois and wild honey from the cliffs of the Highwold, and ropes that no one else can climb.
FX13-016.history: The Hawkhallows were cragsmen like the first Stonefoots, gathering eagle eggs and honey from cliffs no one else would climb. When Hild Stonefoot stood on Mount Roktar in 702 and her kin rose to lead the League, the Hawkhallows stayed on their ropes. Since Siv Stonefoot closed two high valleys to outside hunters in the 870s, the Hawkhallows have been barred from the best cliffs in the range. They have never stopped wondering why.
FX13-016.reputation: Wild cliff-folk, poor, proud and jealous of the Stonefoots.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of the Cragsmen
members.note: He has hated the Stonefoots since Helga beat him on the Redford cliff in 1063, when they were both children.

members.role: Heir; cragswoman
members.note: She can climb any wall in the League and has twice been turned back by Cliff Runners at the edge of the closed valleys.

members.role: Siri's son
members.note: He saw a white egg the size of a man's head on a ledge above Highcastle and told a stranger at Roseham.

famousDead: Climbed beside Hild Stonefoot on the lower slopes of Mount Roktar in 702
FX13-016.secret: Young Arn Hawkhallow has seen a Snow Drake's egg and told a Varennan beast-catcher at Roseham where.
hooks: The Varennan beast-catcher hires Siri to climb to the ledge.
Ada Stonefoot's Cliff Runners come to Hawkhallow asking what the boy saw.

FX13-017.name: the Scarth kin
FX13-017.title: Head of the Scarth Pass-Runners
FX13-017.arms: a black raven on grey-blue, cut on a mule's harness
FX13-017.power: Forty mule-men and guides who carry anything over any pass for a mule's fee, and a safe house in the Whitfield cheese caves.
FX13-017.history: The Scarths were guides who lost their herds in the Black Cough of 916 and turned to carrying what other people would not. They have smuggled silver past the Silver Chest's tolls, Sunland wine past the valley towers and runaway soldiers out of the League for two centuries. They drink at the gate of Highcastle and work with anyone. Since 1100 their best trade has been Greycloak deserters.
FX13-017.reputation: Every valley hates them, and every valley uses them.

members.role: Head of the kin; pass-runner
members.note: He guides Greycloak deserters to Varenna, where a Varennan captain pays a bounty for every trained crossbowman.

members.role: Heir; mule-mistress
members.note: She runs the mules through the Coldencombe tunnel and pays the toll in silver and gossip.

members.role: Garr's son
members.note: He has carried a sealed box for a Varennan beast-catcher and was told never to open it.

FX13-017.secret: The Scarths sell Greycloak deserters to a Varennan captain for a bounty, and some of those men now stand in Varenna's ranks.
hooks: A deserter the Scarths sold south turns up as a Varennan sergeant on the Stagley road.
The Varennan beast-catcher's sealed box starts to warm.

FX13-018.name: the Blackrigg kin
FX13-018.title: Head of the Blackrigg Rustlers
FX13-018.arms: a black boar scratched on a shepherd's crook
FX13-018.words: Four for One, If They Catch Us
FX13-018.power: A dozen hard herders, hidden folds in the Blackrigg heights and buyers who ask no questions.
FX13-018.history: The Blackriggs were herders exiled from the Redford valley in 1040 after a cattle quarrel ended in a killing. By League law a rustler pays fourfold and is exiled for a second theft, and the Blackriggs have been exiles ever since. They live in hidden folds on the Blackrigg heights between Bearfold and Redford. Since 1100 they have taken more Redford cattle than in any year since the orc raid of 799, and blamed the orcs.
FX13-018.reputation: Cattle thieves and cut-brands, the plain truth of it.

members.role: Head of the kin
members.note: Her father was the man exiled in 1040, and she takes Redford cattle as payment for a debt she says is never settled.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He cuts the Redford brand off a cow's hip in the time it takes to say it.

members.role: Ragna's daughter
members.note: She wants to go back to Redford and herd honestly, and has asked a Foxby boy to speak for her.

famousDead: Exiled from Redford after the killing of 1040
FX13-018.secret: The 'orc raids' that have cost Redford its cattle since 1100 are Blackrigg work, sold on through the Bearley elders.
hooks: Speaker Tomas Redford uses the orc raids to argue for crossbows on the Skardush.
Aud Blackrigg offers to name the buyers if her kin is pardoned.

FX14-001.name: House Hardacre
FX14-001.title: Reeve-Lord of Highwell
FX14-001.arms: a black gate between two golden ears of barley, on russet

military.office: Keepers of the Highwell road to the Bellbridge Pass
military.unit: the Highwell Companies, 900 men of the Shire Heavy Foot
military.ties: Every spring a Hardacre carts the Rift Watch's bread and bolts up the Highwell road, and the Watch has never gone hungry while one held the town.

FX14-001.power: The crown rents of Highwell, a walled city of the inland forest, and the toll-post on the only cart road up to the Bellbridge Pass.
FX14-001.history: The Hardacres were reeves before they were lords. In 830, when King Godwin raised the Rift Watch to hold the Bellbridge and Falconhaven passes, a Highwell reeve named Aldred Hardacre fed the new spearmen through their first winter out of his own barns, and in 842 the crown made the reeveship of Highwell hereditary in his line. Since then the house has collected the king's rents in Highwell, held its middle court and kept the road the Rift Watch eats from. In the War of the Channel it sent 600 foot to the coast, and two Hardacre sons died on the decks off Beaconstone in 1008. The earthquake of 1098 cracked the Falconhaven wall and threw down half of the Hardacre hall, and the house has been rebuilding both ever since.
FX14-001.reputation: Solid, slow and honest in the old way, and lately a little too fond of good cut stone.

members.role: Head of the house; Reeve-Lord of Highwell
members.note: He has asked the king three times for the post of Marshal of the Rift and been answered three times with the one hand-sign that means 'wait'.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Highwell Companies
members.note: She marched her companies up to the Falconhaven works in October and stayed to haul stone beside them, which Marshal Isobel Crane noticed.

members.role: Younger son; steward of the Highwell rents
members.note: The cut stone that keeps vanishing from the Falconhaven works is going into his father's new hall, and Ivo signed the carters' tallies himself.

members.role: Dowager; widow of the old Reeve-Lord
members.note: She has read the hand-signs of three kings and still opens the court letters before her son does.

famousDead: Fed the new Rift Watch through the winter of 830 and won the hereditary reeveship of Highwell.
FX14-001.secret: Since the autumn of 1104 Ivo Hardacre has carted the crown's cut stone from the Falconhaven works to rebuild the family hall, robbing the very wall Isobel Crane swore would be finished by April.
hooks: Marshal Isobel Crane pays someone to follow the stone carts out of Falconhaven.
Rowena wants the Marshal of the Rift's post before her father dies asking for it.
A Redley factor offers to buy the Highwell road toll outright.

FX14-002.name: House Sedgecombe
FX14-002.title: Lord of Sedgecombe
FX14-002.arms: three black furrows on gold, a red sickle above

military.office: Bannermen of the Redley levy
military.unit: the Sedgecombe levy, 400 spears and 20 lances
military.ties: Sedgecombe spears march under the Redley sheaves whenever the plain is called out, and a Sedgecombe son has served in the Redley Guard for six generations.

FX14-002.power: Twenty-two villages of bound tenants on the edge of the Redley Plain, and a mill on every stream.
FX14-002.history: The Sedgecombes have held their fields under House Redley since 803, when a Redley lord gave his loyal steward the manors west of Briarhollow. They grow rye and barley for Redley's ships and owe the great house 400 spears and their harvest at Redley's price. They did well out of Tamar's hungry year of 1088, when Lord Godric Redley sold grain abroad at three times the price, and spent the silver on a stone hall. In 1097 Redley's stewards hanged a serf at Redley's gate, and since then Sedgecombe tenants have been slipping away into the Wrendale forest to join Ned Thornby's outlaws. Lord Perrin Sedgecombe has hanged two runaways of his own and lost eleven more.
FX14-002.reputation: Hard landlords who take their orders from Redley and their manners from his stewards.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Sedgecombe
members.note: He has slept with a loaded crossbow by the bed since the Spring Equinox rumors reached his villages.

members.role: Elder daughter and heir
members.note: She has carried bread to the forest edge every new moon since 1103, and one of Thornby's men carries her letters back.

members.role: Son; squire in the Redley Guard
members.note: He means to be the man who brings Ned Thornby's head to Redley's gate.

members.role: Grandmother
members.note: She was born a tenant's daughter on these very fields and has never let her son forget it.

famousDead: Lost two cargoes of the house's barley with Redley's grain fleets in the War of the Channel and paid Redley back over thirty years.
FX14-002.secret: The heir Tamsin feeds Ned Thornby's outlaws and has told them which Sedgecombe villages will run at the Spring Equinox.
hooks: Two hundred bound tenants plan to run on the Spring Equinox.
Ranulf hunts outlaws in the forest and finds his sister's letters on one of them.
Lord Godric Redley demands that the house double its grain shipments for the dragon year.

FX14-003.name: House Kestrelby
FX14-003.title: Lord of Hawkcester; Master of the King's Mews
FX14-003.arms: a silver kestrel stooping on blue, within a gold border
FX14-003.power: The market town of Hawkcester with its tide mills and salt pans, and the king's mews on the downs above it.
FX14-003.history: King Edric II gave Hawkcester to his falconer Wynn Kestrelby in 931, after a season in which the king's hawks took more herons than any lord's. The family has kept the royal mews there ever since and sends a cast of falcons to the khan of the Nine Winds every year with the horse-grain ships, a gift written into the Horse Road Compact. Hawkcester grew on salt pans and tide mills, and the Kestrelbys grew with it. Baron Hamo Kestrelby drowned when the earthquake of 1098 broke the mill dam, and his widow Clemence has ruled the town for their son since. She has fought the Redley factors over the salt price for six years.
FX14-003.reputation: Proud as their birds, generous hosts, and very touchy about the salt.

members.role: Head of the family; holds Hawkcester for her son
members.note: She broke the Redley salt ring in 1101 by selling her pans' salt straight to the Drevnan envoys' ships, and Godric Redley has not forgiven it.

members.role: Heir; Baron of Hawkcester in name
members.note: He is training a grey gyrfalcon that the khan's envoy covets, and plans to carry it to Yarbek himself against his mother's word.

members.role: Uncle; Master of the King's Mews
members.note: He has flown hawks for two kings and can read the deaf king's sign for 'let go' from across a field.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She goes to Lady Linnet's household as a maid of honor in spring, if Lady Linnet is still in Greyhaven by then.

famousDead: Falconer of Edric II; granted Hawkcester in 931.
FX14-003.secret: Baron Hamo did not drown by chance: Kestrelby stewards had been undercutting the mill dam for years to dig new salt pans, and Clemence paid the millers' widows to blame the earthquake.
hooks: The khan's envoy offers 300 horses for Merrick's gyrfalcon.
Redley factors buy up Hawkcester's salt carts on the road before they reach the quay.
A miller's widow wants more silver for her silence.

FX14-004.name: House Tarnholt
FX14-004.title: Lord of the Tarn Mines
FX14-004.arms: a silver mountain over a black tarn, on dark blue
FX14-004.power: Iron and silver workings in the Silverdale hills, a smelting town of 3,000, and the right to sell iron to the crown's arsenal.
FX14-004.history: The Tarnholts dug silver for the Solen mints before there was a kingdom. King Leofric made Bertram Tarnholt a baron in 867 for silver that paid the galley crews in a bad toll year. The house has sold Silverdale iron to the arsenal and the yards ever since, and silver from Osric the Diver's ferry years paid for its first stone smelting hall. The upper seams are thin now. Since 1099 the crown has bought dwarven iron from Irondeep in secret, and it comes ashore at a Silverdale creek and leaves the Tarnholt smelters stamped as Silverdale iron, so that Aldmark and the dwarves' other buyers never know.
FX14-004.reputation: Rich, close-mouthed hill lords who never invite anyone underground.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Tarnholt
members.note: He has not been down his own mine in twenty years and knows to the ounce what comes out of it.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the smelters
members.note: She can tell an Irondeep bar from a Silverdale bar by the note it rings on the anvil.

members.role: Younger son; reeve of the mine guard
members.note: He loses at dice in the Silverdale taverns and talks about the dwarf boats when he loses.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: At four she has already lost a tooth in a fall in the old adit and still will not keep out of it.

famousDead: Paid the galley crews with Tarnholt silver in a bad toll year and was made baron in 867.
FX14-004.secret: Tarnholt smelters restamp secret Irondeep iron as Silverdale iron for the crown, and Hesketh's dice debts are owed to a man who sells news across the channel.
hooks: A dwarf boat founders off Silverdale with iron bars aboard and a Toll-House galley nearby.
Hamo Keel offers Aldith a share of his own dwarven iron contract if she will undercut her father.
Hesketh's creditor wants a map of the landing creek in place of coin.

FX14-005.name: House Brackenridge
FX14-005.title: Knight of Brackenridge; Warden of the Wren Foresters
FX14-005.arms: a green oak leaf on silver, crossed by a brown bend

military.office: Wardens of the Wren Foresters
military.unit: the Wren Foresters, 800 scouts of the Wrendale woods
military.ties: Brackenridge foresters scout for the land host whenever it moves through the forest shires, and they mark every royal ship oak with the crown's axe.

FX14-005.power: Three forest manors and the wardenship of House Wren's foresters, who decide which oaks are felled.
FX14-005.history: The Brackenridges were Wren foresters raised to knighthood in 1012, after Wulf Brackenridge led the Wrendale bowmen home through the woods at the end of the War of the Channel. They mark the oaks, count the fellings and hunt timber thieves for the Wrens. When Lady Elinor Wren began selling oak to Aldmark in 1080, Sir Garrick Brackenridge chose the trees, and the house has lived comfortably on her commission since. In 1102 Garrick's second son Kettil went to Sevany in Velgrad as a timber factor, and the oak he sells there goes to the Channel-Master's galley yards. The family tells the neighbors Kettil is in Aldmark.
FX14-005.reputation: Quiet woodsmen who know every tree in Wrendale, and lately a family that changes the subject.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Brackenridge, Warden of the Wren Foresters
members.note: He would cut off his own hand for Lady Elinor and suspects that is roughly what she has asked of his son.

members.role: Heir; captain of foresters
members.note: He does not know where his brother really is, and he has begun to ask.

members.role: Second son; House Wren's timber factor at Sevany
members.note: He has watched old hulls being tarred in a Sevany creek and wonders who they are meant for.

members.role: Daughter; forester
members.note: The best shot in the Wren Foresters, she has twice let Thornby's outlaws go rather than shoot a hungry man.

famousDead: Led the Wrendale bowmen home through the forest in 1010 and won the knighthood.
FX14-005.secret: Kettil Brackenridge is House Wren's agent at Sevany, selling ship oak to the Velgradan yards that are fitting the fire rafts.
hooks: Kettil writes home that he has seen something in a creek below Mount Dobava.
Aelfric finds a Sevany tally in his father's chest.
One of Ned Thornby's men asks Nessa for a favor, in return for the letter Thornby holds.

FX14-006.name: House Merrow
FX14-006.title: Banneret of the Smokewell March
FX14-006.arms: a red flame on yellow, under a black chief

military.office: Wardens of the Smokewell pits
military.unit: the Merrow banner, 20 lances, with the 800-man garrison of Wrenreach and the sulfur pits
military.ties: The sulfur that fills the fleet's pitch-pots comes down the mountain under Merrow guard, and a Merrow banner has landed with the Admiral's shore parties since 884.

FX14-006.power: The sulfur pits of Smokewell, worked by hired diggers, and a crown contract for pitch-pot sulfur.
FX14-006.history: Osric the Diver gave Ingram Merrow the Smokewell sulfur pits in 884, out of the Khan's ferry silver, to keep the fleet in pitch. The Merrows have dug the mountain's yellow ground ever since, and their diggers cough themselves to death by fifty. In 1071 Merrow diggers were on the slopes when Smokewell vented the black cloud that the city saw as a dragon, and the old banneret made them swear on the iron ring to say nothing of what they saw. The digger Hob Yellowhand works a Merrow pit. In the autumn of 1104 Velgradan buyers came across the channel short of sulfur, and the Merrow steward sold them forty cartloads at double the crown price, with the young banneret's leave.
FX14-006.reputation: Hard, yellow-handed march lords, rich in a bad smell and poor in friends.

members.role: Head of the house; Banneret of the Smokewell March
members.note: He sold the sulfur to Velgrad thinking it was for dye, and has since worked out what Velgrad wants with pitch.

members.role: His mother; keeper of the pit rolls
members.note: She knows the dragon of 1071 was smoke, because her husband made the diggers swear it, and she keeps the oath roll in her chest.

members.role: Brother; captain of the pit guard
members.note: He wants to tell the Admiral about the Velgradan buyers and is afraid of hanging his own brother.

members.role: Brand's daughter
members.note: She coughs in the pit smoke like the diggers' children do, and her father has begun to look at the mountain differently.

famousDead: Given the Smokewell pits by Osric the Diver in 884.
FX14-006.secret: The Merrows sold forty cartloads of Smokewell sulfur to Velgradan buyers in autumn 1104, and the old banneret's oath roll proves the house has known since 1071 that the dragon was the mountain's smoke.
hooks: Hob Yellowhand wants his share of the Velgradan silver.
Osmund rides for Greyhaven to confess to the Admiral.
Hall-Keeper Wulfric Grey asks, very politely, to see the oath roll of 1071.

FX14-007.name: House Ravelstow
FX14-007.title: Knight of Ravelstow; Owner of the Ravelstow Cogs
FX14-007.arms: a gold anchor between two silver waves, on deep blue

military.office: Masters of the pressed cogs of Silverdale
military.unit: eleven cogs pressed into the fleet in war, with 400 seamen
military.ties: Ravelstow cogs carried the bread for the Wolfhaven blockade in 1092 and will carry it again, at the crown's price and not a penny less.

FX14-007.power: Eleven cogs on the Silverdale iron run and the Horse Road grain trade, and a knight's manor that came with a bride.
FX14-007.history: The Ravelstows were cog-masters of Silverdale who carried iron and horse-grain for a century before anyone called them sir. In 1079 Roland Ravelstow married Edda, last daughter of the old Saltmarsh knights of the Silverdale shore, and by Greyhaven's custom that ship-owners may marry into the peerage freely, her manor and her knighthood passed to their line. Ravelstow cogs fed the Wolfhaven blockade in 1092, and two of them burned on the night Northreach longships came out on the ebb. The crown still owes the house 8,000 suns for those ships. The old shield families of the coast call them tide-knights and borrow from them all the same.
FX14-007.reputation: New money in old armor; good payers and very hard bargainers.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Ravelstow
members.note: He carries the crown's note for the two burned cogs in his doublet and shows it to any lord who will look.

members.role: His wife; last of the Saltmarsh knights
members.note: She brought the knighthood in her dowry and reminds her husband of it in every quarrel.

members.role: Heir; master of the cog Silver Hind
members.note: Admiral Brightwater has asked him to bring a cog behind the chain in July, and he has not told his father.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She is promised to Hesketh Tarnholt and in love with a pilot's son.

famousDead: Built the family's first three cogs out of the iron run's profits.
FX14-007.secret: Two Ravelstow cogs carried Silverdale iron to Lucerna in 1103 under false papers to dodge the toll, and the Toll-House clerk who passed them is paid every quarter.
hooks: The crown offers to pay the 8,000 suns in toll remissions instead of coin.
Aelfwyn means to run off with her pilot.
Brightwater wants three Ravelstow cogs behind the chain from the first of July.

FX14-008.name: House Lowmoor
FX14-008.title: Lord of Lowmoor
FX14-008.arms: a gold bell on green, above a silver base
FX14-008.power: Fourteen villages on the eastern rim of the Redley Plain and the grain road down to Highwell market.
FX14-008.history: In 896 Ingram Lowmoor rang the plain's bells to bring the harvest in ahead of a rider raid that never came, and House Redley made him a baron for the grain he saved. The house has been Redley's man on the eastern plain ever since and sits with it in the peace party: its grain goes out by sea, and every channel war costs it a harvest. In 1006 Lord Ulric Lowmoor stood beside Edwin Redley against King Edmund's doubled toll and lost his seat at the Tide Council for it. The present lord married Godric Redley's younger sister in 1080. The Lowmoors quarrel with the Hardacres of Highwell over the road toll every market day.
FX14-008.reputation: Comfortable, careful grain lords; Redley's shadow on the plain.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Lowmoor
members.note: He has never ridden to war and hopes to die without having to start.

members.role: His wife; born a Redley, Lord Godric's sister
members.note: She copies her brother's letters before they go to the ship, because she does not trust him to remember who wrote what.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He swore on the iron ring on Oathfather's Day to serve the king first, and has begun to wonder what his uncle writes to Velgrad.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She dances with Ivo Hardacre at every Highwell feast, to her father's horror.

famousDead: Rang the harvest in ahead of the riders in 896 and was made baron.
FX14-008.secret: Lady Oddny keeps copies of every letter Godric Redley has sent to Borek Marten of Velgrad since 1103.
hooks: Thurstan finds his mother's copies.
The Hardacres raise the Highwell road toll on grain carts.
A Velgradan fur buyer arrives in Highwell asking for Lady Oddny by name.

FX14-009.name: House Coldridge
FX14-009.title: Knight of Coldridge; banner-knight of the Tide Knights
FX14-009.arms: a silver chevron between three silver horseshoes, on black

military.office: Hereditary banner-knights of the Tide Knights
military.unit: the Coldridge banner, 25 lances of the Tide Knights
military.ties: A Coldridge has led a banner of the Tide Knights at every royal muster since Cedric II, and Coldridge children sit a steppe horse before they can walk.

FX14-009.power: A knight's manor in the Briarhollow forest, a stud of 40 steppe-bred destriers, and a banner of the Tide Knights.
FX14-009.history: Cedric II knighted Wendel Coldridge in 941 for riding down a Rift outlaw band on one of the first steppe horses the Horse Road brought in. The Coldridges have served in the Tide Knights, Greyhaven's 3,000 heavy horse, ever since, and they have little else: a manor of 300 souls and a stable worth more than the house. Greyhaven fights its wars at sea, and a knight of the Tide Knights can go a lifetime without a charge. Sir Edric Coldridge went ashore with the landing party at Wolfhaven in 1092 and came home without his sword hand. His daughter rides at the head of his banner in his place.
FX14-009.reputation: Poor, brave and horse-mad, with more pride than pasture.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Coldridge
members.note: He lost his sword hand to a Northreach axe on the Wolfhaven beach and has had a lance-rest strapped to the stump.

members.role: Heir; banner-knight of the Tide Knights
members.note: She leads her father's 25 lances, wants one real charge before she dies, and fears she will spend her life escorting tax carts.

members.role: Son; horse-breaker
members.note: He buys the family's colts from the Marrowbys on credit the family does not have.

members.role: Edric's wife; keeper of the stud book
members.note: Her stud book reaches back to the first Horse Road mares of 925, and she would save it from a fire before the silver.

famousDead: Rode down a Rift outlaw band on a steppe horse in 941 and was knighted for it.
FX14-009.secret: The Coldridge stud book is partly false: half the 'pure Horse Road' destriers they sell to other knights were bred from forest mares.
hooks: Ingrid is offered a place in Aldmark's Iron Guard and must choose between her father's banner and a real war.
The Marrowbys call in Corbin's debt.
A buyer finds out what a 'pure' Coldridge horse really is.

FX14-010.name: House Oakenshaw
FX14-010.title: Lord of Oakenshaw; Keeper of the King's Oak Rows
FX14-010.arms: a green tree with golden roots on silver, under a red crown
FX14-010.power: The crown's planted oak rows on the coast behind Deepwatch, where the king's own ship timber grows, and seven villages of foresters and sawyers.
FX14-010.history: King Leofric grew tired of buying his galley timber at Wrendale prices, so in 873 he planted his own oak rows on the coast behind Deepwatch and gave their keeping, with a barony, to a sawyer's son named Osmund Oakenshaw. The first rows were cut for Edmund the Toll-Doubler's war fleet in 1006, and the second planting stands ready in 1105. Every crown galley that is not Wren oak is Oakenshaw oak, and the two houses have hated each other for two centuries. The Oakenshaws want the crown to cut the second planting now, before the Wrens' Aldmark contracts take all the yards' business. In 1104 their foresters found fresh Wren axe-marks on twelve crown oaks.
FX14-010.reputation: Patient tree-lords with long memories and a short temper for anything that grows in Wrendale.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Oakenshaw
members.note: He walks the oak rows every morning and has named the oldest tree after his grandfather.

members.role: Heir; the house's voice at court
members.note: She is at court pressing Admiral Brightwater for a new galley order, and Hamo Keel calls her the only lord in Greyhaven who can price timber.

members.role: Younger son; chief forester
members.note: He caught a Wren sawyer in the rows last autumn and broke both his hands.

members.role: Grandmother
members.note: She planted the second rows as a girl in 1040 and means to live to see them cut.

famousDead: First Keeper of the King's Oak Rows.
FX14-010.secret: In the hungry year of 1088 the Oakenshaws sold a hundred crown oaks privately to the Brookhurst yards and wrote them down as storm-fall.
hooks: Wren axe-marks on crown oaks: a theft, or a warning?
Brightwater asks whether the second planting can be cut this spring.
The broken-handed sawyer's kin swear that Dunstan will pay.

FX14-011.name: House Chainley
FX14-011.title: Windlass-Master of the Chain Towers
FX14-011.arms: a black wheel with a silver chain looped through it, on sea green

military.office: Hereditary Windlass-Masters of the Greyhaven chain towers
military.unit: the windlass crews of the Chain Guard, 240 men in the two towers
military.ties: The harbor chain has not been raised once in 333 years without a Chainley at the windlass, and most captains of the Chain Guard learned their trade under one.

FX14-011.power: The windlasses of the two chain towers, a knight's stipend from the Toll-House, and the knowledge of exactly how fast the chain can rise.
FX14-011.history: When Prince Aldred raised the chain towers in 772, a smith named Edric Chainley forged the windlass gears and stayed on to work them, and the Chain-Maker knighted him for raising the chain in a gale before a Velgradan raider could slip in. A Chainley has stood at the windlass ever since. The house's sons serve as sergeants and captains in the Chain Guard, 3,000 marines, and its children learn to grease the gears before they learn to read. In July 1105 the Chain Guard means to raise the chain at every dusk. Sir Hamo Chainley says the old gears will not stand it, and the Captain of the Chain Guard, Hugo Stannard, will not hear it.
FX14-011.reputation: Greasy-handed knights whom nobody in Greyhaven will hear a word against.

members.role: Head of the house; Windlass-Master of the Chain Towers
members.note: He has asked the Toll-House for new gears every year since 1098 and been told every year to wait until the dragon year is over.

members.role: Heir; sergeant of the north tower crew
members.note: She can raise the chain with a crew of thirty in the time it takes to sing the Diver's Lay, and has done it for a bet.

members.role: Son; file-leader in the Chain Guard
members.note: He drinks at the Tapper's House and has heard Wat Eelby's story about the hulls.

members.role: Hamo's sister; keeper of the gear rolls
members.note: She has written down every crack in every gear since 1072.

famousDead: Forged the first windlass and raised the chain in a gale in 772.
FX14-011.secret: The great gear of the south tower cracked in the earthquake of 1098; the Chainleys patched it in secret, and it may not survive a month of raising the chain every dusk.
hooks: The south gear groans on the first dusk of July.
Perrin wants to buy Wat Eelby's story before the Admiral's man does.
A Toll-House clerk offers new gears in return for a favor.

FX14-012.name: House Gullstone
FX14-012.title: Castellan of Deepwatch and Warden of the Channel Towers
FX14-012.arms: a grey tower on a black rock above white waves, on blue-grey

military.office: Castellans of Deepwatch and Wardens of the Channel Towers
military.unit: the Deepwatch garrison and the 72 channel watch towers, 2,160 men at 30 to a tower
military.ties: Every fire that tells Greyhaven a fleet is coming is lit by a man who answers to a Gullstone.

FX14-012.power: The castle of Deepwatch and the command of the 72 watch towers strung along the channel shore.
FX14-012.history: Velgradan galleys slipped along the shore unseen in 1008, and when the War of the Channel ended King Edmund built Deepwatch and a chain of watch towers along the coast. In 1010 he gave the castle to Aldred Gullstone, the tower sergeant who had lit the warning fire at Beaconstone before the battle. The Gullstones have kept the towers since, thirty men to a tower and a fire laid ready in each. Their men saw the black column of 1071 from three towers and wrote down three different things. In 1105 the towers are the eyes of the whole kingdom, and the castellan has orders to light the fleet fire the moment anything burns on the water in July.
FX14-012.reputation: Sharp-eyed, sleepless and dutiful; the coast trusts their fires more than its priests.

members.role: Head of the house; Castellan of Deepwatch
members.note: He rides to a different tower every night and once hanged a tower sergeant for sleeping.

members.role: Heir; captain of the southern towers
members.note: Her towers face Mount Dobava across the channel, and she has seen lights in the creek below it twice since October.

members.role: Son; sergeant at Beaconstone
members.note: He signals love verses by tower flag to a girl at the next tower, which the whole coast can read.

members.role: Halvard's wife; keeper of the tower rolls
members.note: She keeps the three accounts of 1071 in one chest and believes the one that says 'smoke'.

famousDead: Lit the warning fire at Beaconstone in 1008 and became the first castellan of Deepwatch.
FX14-012.secret: Maren Gullstone has reported the lights below Mount Dobava, and Admiral Brightwater sent back word to say nothing to anyone and keep watching.
hooks: A tower fire is lit by mistake in July and the whole coast arms.
Emeric's flag verses are being read by a Velgradan spy, who has learned the code.
Maren rows across the channel to see the creek for herself.

FX14-013.name: the Scarrows of Bellbridge
FX14-013.title: Sergeant-Warden of the Bellbridge Barricade
FX14-013.arms: a black spear across a grey crag, on red

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Rift Watch at the Bellbridge Pass
military.unit: the Bellbridge barricade, 900 spearmen of the Rift Watch
military.ties: Since Godwin raised the Rift Watch in 830 there has always been a Scarrow sergeant on the Bellbridge barricade, and every Scarrow child carries a first spear up the pass at fifteen.

FX14-013.power: A franklin's farm below the pass, the sergeants' room at the Bellbridge barricade, and the trust of every Marshal of the Rift.
FX14-013.history: The first Scarrow was a shepherd who showed King Godwin's captains the goat path round the Bellbridge narrows in 830, so that they could block it. His sons enlisted in the new Rift Watch, and the family has filled its sergeants' ranks for 275 years without rising higher or wanting to. Scarrows held the barricade against the outlaw bands of the 830s and against the steppe raiders who tried the pass in the Wind years. They have never had to hold it against an army. The earthquake of 1098 opened a cleft in the rock above the barricade, and old Sergeant Brand Scarrow says it makes a second goat path that no map shows.
FX14-013.reputation: Hard as the pass, plain-spoken, and the best spear-sergeants in the kingdom.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant-Warden of the Bellbridge Barricade
members.note: He has walked the pass every day for forty years and found the new cleft in the rock himself.

members.role: Heir; sergeant of the second line
members.note: He wants the new path walled before spring and cannot get masons, because every mason in the kingdom is at Falconhaven.

members.role: Daughter; file-leader in the Rift Watch
members.note: The first Scarrow woman on the barricade, she climbs the new cleft at night to see where it comes out.

members.role: Youngest son
members.note: He hates heights, wants to be a clerk in Highwell, and has not dared to tell his father.

famousDead: Showed King Godwin's captains the goat path round the Bellbridge narrows in 830.
FX14-013.secret: In the winter of 1103 Brand Scarrow let a band of smugglers through the new cleft for a purse of silver, before he understood that he had shown them a road.
hooks: Audra finds where the new cleft comes out.
The smugglers come back with heavier loads and more men.
Sewald runs away to Highwell.

FX14-014.name: House Fanhope
FX14-014.title: Bearer of the Diver Banner
FX14-014.arms: a silver open hand on sea green, within a gold border

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of the Diver Banner on the king's galley
military.unit: the banner guard of the royal galley, 40 marines
military.ties: Wherever the royal galley goes the Diver Banner flies from its stern in a Fanhope's hands, and the whole fleet steers by it in battle.

FX14-014.power: A knight's manor on the Wrenreach shore, a crown stipend, and the right to stand at the king's side in every sea fight.
FX14-014.history: On the night of 19 July 882, while Osric the Diver was under the Khan's chain at Yarbek, a marine named Cuthbert Fanhope held the king's banner upright on the lead galley under the arrows until the chain came free. Osric knighted him on the deck. Since then a Fanhope has carried the Diver Banner, a silver diver on sea green, on the stern of the king's galley in every sea fight. Sir Oswy Fanhope held it off Beaconstone in 1008 with an arrow through his thigh. The house has no great wealth and wants none, but its head stands next to the king and reads the divers' hand-signs better than most councillors.
FX14-014.reputation: Loyal to the point of folly, and the kingdom's favorite knights at any feast.

members.role: Head of the house; Bearer of the Diver Banner
members.note: He reads the king's hand-signs at a glance and has noticed that Lady Linnet does not always say what her father signs.

members.role: Heir; banner guard
members.note: Prince Tristan wants him at his side on the galleys in July, which would mean leaving the king's banner.

members.role: Daughter; marine of the Chain Guard
members.note: She is the best crossbow shot in the Chain Guard and keeps a list of the officers she has outshot.

members.role: Aldred's son
members.note: At five he sleeps with a toy banner and salutes the galleys from the shore.

famousDead: Held the king's banner on the lead galley at Yarbek in 882.
Held the Diver Banner off Beaconstone in 1008 with an arrow through his thigh.
FX14-014.secret: Sir Cuthbert has seen Lady Linnet change her father's words in council at least four times and has told no one, not even the king.
hooks: The king asks Cuthbert, by hand-sign, what Linnet really said in council last week.
Aldred must choose between the prince and the banner.
A Velgradan agent offers silver for the royal galley's battle signals.

FX14-015.name: the Tarrants
FX14-015.title: Captain of the Brookhurst Boarders
FX14-015.arms: a black boarding axe on orange

military.office: Hereditary captains in the Brookhurst Boarders
military.unit: the Brookhurst Boarders, 2,000 marines
military.ties: Tarrant men have led the first wave over an enemy rail in every sea fight since 1008, and the Boarders' axe-drill is still called the Tarrant drill.

FX14-015.power: Captaincies in the Brookhurst Boarders, a squire's farm outside Hawkcester, and a name every marine knows.
FX14-015.history: Sewald Tarrant led the boarding party that took a Velgradan galley off Beaconstone in 1008, and when the war ended in 1010 King Edmund made him a squire and a captain of the new Brookhurst Boarders. The Tarrants have served in the Boarders since; they teach the axe-drill to every recruit and lose a man or two in every generation. Ivo Tarrant lost eighty boarders at Wolfhaven in 1092, when Northreach longships came out on the ebb and burned two galleys. In 1105 the Boarders are quartered at the Brookhurst yards. Captain Ingram Tarrant wants a fight with Sevany to win back the name Wolfhaven cost his father.
FX14-015.reputation: Loud, scarred and dangerous to drink with; nobody you would rather have on your deck.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Brookhurst Boarders
members.note: He has asked Brightwater for the first boarding wave in any fight with Sevany and will not take no.

members.role: Daughter; file-leader of the Boarders
members.note: She won the Boarders' rope-climb three years running and broke a sergeant's nose for saying a woman could not.

members.role: Old captain; Ingram's father
members.note: He drinks to each of his eighty Wolfhaven dead by name on the anniversary, and it takes all night.

members.role: Younger son; said to have drowned
members.note: He jumped ship at Lucerna in 1103, and his father tells everyone he drowned.

famousDead: Took a Velgradan galley by boarding off Beaconstone in 1008; first Tarrant captain of the Boarders.
FX14-015.secret: Corwin Tarrant did not drown: he deserted at Lucerna and now rows for the Blackreef corsairs, and he has written home asking for money.
hooks: Ingram gets his first wave, if the fire rafts come.
A letter arrives from Blackreef in the dead son's hand.
Helga is offered a sergeant's post in the Chain Guard, away from her father's shadow.

FX14-016.name: the Seldons
FX14-016.title: Senior Diver of the Diving School
FX14-016.arms: a sign: a white wave over a black knife, painted on the family boat

military.office: Diver-sergeants of the Tide Divers
military.unit: the Tide Divers, 240 marines of the Diving School
military.ties: Seldons have taught half the Tide Divers to hold their breath and every one of them to cut a cable by feel in black water.

FX14-016.power: Places in the Diving School, a harbor boat, and the trust of Diver-Master Ness Tidewell.
FX14-016.history: The Seldons were wreck and oyster divers of Greyhaven harbor who joined the divers' boats in 919, after Osric the Diver's death. They have no Tidewell lungs, only hard training: a Seldon child swims the harbor before it walks well. They dive on the harbor chain, the fouled anchors and the galleys' hulls, and when a royal child makes the ring dive a Seldon waits at the bottom of the ring line. In 1092 Seldon divers cut the cables of the Northreach fire rafts off Wolfhaven beside Ness Tidewell, and one of them did not come up. The family is deaf in one ear by forty and dead by sixty, and in 1105 it will follow the Diver-Master wherever she dives.
FX14-016.reputation: Half-deaf, salt-stained and fearless; the harbor's own family.

members.role: Head of the family; senior diver of the Diving School
members.note: She is deaf in both ears now and teaches the young divers with her hands, the way the king speaks.

members.role: Heir; diver-sergeant
members.note: He cut two raft cables at Wolfhaven at eighteen and lost his left eardrum doing it.

members.role: Daughter; apprentice diver
members.note: She has already dived deeper than her brother and wants to go down off Smokewell with the Diver-Master.

members.role: Grandfather; retired diver
members.note: He went down to the harbor chain beside Osric III in the winter dive of 1084 and came up; the king did not.

famousDead: Drowned cutting a Northreach fire-raft cable off Wolfhaven.
FX14-016.secret: On the winter dive of 1084 old Ordgar saw that the chain had been fouled with new rope, not by a wreck, and he has never said whom he suspects of tying it.
hooks: Ness Tidewell asks for Seldons on her dive off Smokewell.
Ordgar finally talks about the rope.
A stranger offers silver for a diver who could cut the harbor chain at night.

FX14-017.name: the Lodemans
FX14-017.title: Senior Pilot of the Pilots' Guild
FX14-017.arms: a gold star over a black needle, on blue
FX14-017.power: Four sworn pilots in the Pilots' Guild, the channel's shoals in their heads, and a share in the secret of the floating lodestone needle.
FX14-017.history: The Lodemans took one of the first seven-year oaths of the Pilots' Guild about 870 and have taken the fleet and the great cogs through the Grey Channel's fogs ever since. In the 1040s Ansel Lodeman was one of the pilots who learned the floating lodestone needle from the Lucernans, and the family has kept the secret as Guild law demands: a pilot who shows the needle to an outsider is drowned. They expected the Guild's mastership in 1089 and lost it to Garth Ferris by one vote. In 1104 a Lodeman nephew who had gambled away his pay was seen drinking with Velgradan sailors at the Tapper's House, and the family has not let him out of its sight since.
FX14-017.reputation: Proud, secretive, indispensable, and still sour about the mastership.

members.role: Head of the family; senior pilot
members.note: He lost the Guild's mastership by one vote and knows exactly who cast it.

members.role: His wife; chart-maker
members.note: Her charts are the best in the city, and by Guild law she may draw them but never pilot by them.

members.role: Heir; sworn pilot
members.note: He is in love with Aelfwyn Ravelstow, who is promised to a mine lord's son.

members.role: Nephew; apprentice pilot
members.note: He owes 200 suns at dice, and a Velgradan sailor has offered to pay it for one look at the needle.

famousDead: Learned the floating needle from the Lucernan pilots in the 1040s.
FX14-017.secret: Alric Lodeman has already shown a Velgradan sailor the needle's box, though not the needle, and by Guild law the whole family could be cast out for not drowning him.
hooks: The Guild hears rumors about Alric and sends for the family.
Selwyn and Aelfwyn plan to run off on a Lodeman-piloted cog.
Garth Ferris falls ill and the mastership opens again.

FX14-018.name: the Brinewolds
FX14-018.title: Master of the Brinewold Cogs
FX14-018.arms: a black cog under full sail, on green-grey
FX14-018.power: Seven timber cogs that carry Wrendale oak to Aldmark's Cold Bay yards, and a long contract with the Timber Guild.
FX14-018.history: Hesketh Brinewold built his first cog in 1032 to carry Wren chestnut to the Brookhurst yards, and the family grew with the Wrens' timber trade. When Lady Elinor signed the Aldmark oak contract in 1080, the Brinewolds won the carrying, and their seven cogs now make the Cold Bay run eight times a year. Two of those runs a year go somewhere else. Since 1102 one Brinewold cog has sailed twice a year to Sevany with oak that the bills call 'chestnut for cooperage'. The captain is the head's own daughter, and she knows exactly whose yards she unloads at.
FX14-018.reputation: Steady timber haulers with a good name in Aldmark and a few too many friends at Sevany.

members.role: Head of the family; master of the cogs
members.note: He tells himself the Sevany oak is Lady Elinor's sin and not his.

members.role: Heir; captain of the cog Wrenwing
members.note: She has unloaded oak at Sevany beside hulls being tarred for something that is not fishing.

members.role: Son; factor at Cold Bay in Aldmark
members.note: Aldmark's yard-masters trust him, and he has no idea what his sister carries.

members.role: Grandmother
members.note: She sailed the Cold Bay run with her husband until she was sixty and still curses the channel tides by name.

famousDead: Built the first Brinewold cog in 1032.
FX14-018.secret: The Brinewolds carry Wren oak to Velgrad's galley yards at Sevany twice a year under false bills.
hooks: A Toll-House clerk notices that the Wrenwing's bills do not match her draft.
Ragna is offered triple to carry pitch back from Sevany.
Tostig hears about the Sevany runs in an Aldmark tavern.

FX14-019.name: the Hempstalls
FX14-019.title: Master of the Ropers of the Galley Strand
FX14-019.arms: a brown knotted rope laid bend-wise, on gold
FX14-019.power: Three ropewalks on the Galley Strand and the mastership of the Ropers, who make every galley cable and the hawsers that float the harbor chain.
FX14-019.history: The Hempstalls have twisted rope on the Galley Strand since 948, when Osmund Hempstall bought the first long ropewalk from the fleet. Every cable on every royal galley and the hawsers that float the harbor chain come off their walks, and the Master of the Ropers has stood with the Shipwrights at every fleet muster since. In 1096 the rope merchant Merrick Fenn opened a store beside their walks, undercut them for a season and then left for Sevany, and the Hempstalls have hated him ever since without knowing he is the Admiral's spy. The house is now three walks, sixty ropers and a feud. The master's younger brother keeps a fourth walk at Brookhurst and sells to the Keels at a price the Guild forbids.
FX14-019.reputation: Honest makers of the best rope in the channel, and quarrelsome among themselves.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Ropers
members.note: He tests every fleet cable with his own hands and once rejected a whole season's hemp from Wrendale.

members.role: Brother; master of the Brookhurst walk
members.note: He sells cheap to Hamo Keel against Guild rules and says Osmund is welcome to come and stop him.

members.role: Osmund's daughter and heir
members.note: She has noticed that Merrick Fenn's store sold more pitch than rope, and to sailors with Velgradan accents.

members.role: Beorn's daughter
members.note: She works the walk with her cousin Asa and carries messages between the two feuding brothers.

famousDead: Bought the first ropewalk on the Galley Strand in 948.
FX14-019.secret: Beorn Hempstall's cheap cables for the Keels are laid from short hemp; one parted in a gale in 1103 and a cog was lost, and everyone blamed the weather.
hooks: A galley's cable parts on a July night.
Asa follows Merrick Fenn's old pitch buyers through the Galley Strand.
The brothers' feud splits the Ropers at the spring muster.

FX14-020.name: the Marrowbys
FX14-020.title: Master of the Marrowby Paddocks
FX14-020.arms: a white horse running on brown, under a gold sun
FX14-020.power: The paddocks behind Hawkcester where steppe horses rest after the crossing, the grooms' quarter at the Horse Quay, and old friends among the Nine Winds.
FX14-020.history: Ivo Marrowby sailed with the first grain ships to the Yarbek horse fair in 925 and came home with 40 mares, and the family has dealt in steppe horses ever since. They rest the horses in their paddocks behind Hawkcester after the crossing and sell them to the Tide Knights, the Horse Road Riders and the lords of the plain. Half-orc grooms came with the trade, and in 1050 Wendel Marrowby married a half-orc groom's daughter, so the younger branch has small tusks and the older branch pretends not to notice. They speak the Wind Rider tongue at home. In 1105 the Nine Winds' envoys have asked to see the old ferry rolls of 884, and the Marrowbys are the men they ask to arrange things.
FX14-020.reputation: Shrewd, open-handed horse-copers who know every khan's cousin by name.

members.role: Head of the family; master of the paddocks
members.note: He has eaten horse-milk cheese with three khans and says the third was the stingiest.

members.role: Half-orc cousin; head groom of the Horse Quay
members.note: She runs ninety half-orc grooms and can calm a stallion that has crossed the channel in a storm.

members.role: Heir; buyer at Yarbek
members.note: He spends half the year at Yarbek and carries a sealed request from the khan's envoy to the king's archive.

members.role: Brenna's daughter
members.note: At ten she rides any horse in the paddocks bareback, better than the squires who come to buy.

famousDead: Brought the first 40 steppe mares home from Yarbek in 925.
FX14-020.secret: Harek Marrowby has taken the Nine Winds envoy's silver to get a copy of the ferry accounts of 884 to 890 out of the king's archive.
hooks: Harek asks the archive keeper Clemence Varrow for a favor.
A shipment of horses comes ashore with steppe fever.
Corbin Coldridge's debt falls due and the Coldridges cannot pay.

FX14-021.name: the Tallowbys
FX14-021.title: Second Counter of the Toll-House
FX14-021.arms: a silver key on black, under a gold pair of scales
FX14-021.power: Three desks in the Toll-House, the second count-book, and a memory of every ship that has paid since 764.
FX14-021.history: A Tallowby clerk counted the first channel toll on Sea Opening 764, and the family has kept a desk in the Toll-House for 341 years. They keep the second count-book, which checks the first. In 1088 the head of the family expected the Toll-Mistress's chair and lost it to Beatrix Hollin, a toll clerk's daughter like himself. Since 1094 the second book has disagreed with the first by about 6,000 a year on Velgrad's half of the through-toll, and old Edwin Tallowby has said nothing, because his son's place depends on it. His granddaughter has noticed.
FX14-021.reputation: Dry, careful, slightly bitter clerks who know more about the kingdom's money than its lords do.

members.role: Head of the family; Second Counter of the Toll-House
members.note: He has known for eleven years that the Toll-Mistress shaves Velgrad's half, and keeps the proof in a book under his floor.

members.role: Son; clerk of the through-ships
members.note: He writes through-ships down as bound for Greyhaven when the Toll-Mistress tells him to, and hates himself every Oathfather's Day.

members.role: Haldor's wife
members.note: She wants her husband in the Toll-Mistress's chair and would trade the book under the floor to get him there.

members.role: Granddaughter; junior clerk
members.note: She has added up the second book against the first and wants to know why they never match.

famousDead: Counted the first channel toll on Sea Opening 764.
FX14-021.secret: Edwin Tallowby's book under the floor records eleven years of shaved tolls on Velgrad's half, entry by entry.
hooks: Mildred asks the wrong person why the two books never match.
Rothild offers the book under the floor to Godric Redley for a seat in the Toll-House.
The Channel-Master of Velgrad's buyers come looking for a Toll-House clerk with debts.

FX14-022.name: the Forgewards of Silverdale
FX14-022.title: Keeper of the Smith's Hall of Silverdale
FX14-022.arms: a black anvil under a red flame, on grey
FX14-022.power: The Smith's Hall of Silverdale, where miners and smiths swear on the iron ring, and a tithe on every smelting.
FX14-022.history: The Forgewards have kept the Smith's Hall at Silverdale since 790, a hall-priest's line passing to son or daughter's son. Miners swear on their iron ring before they go below, and the Forgewards bless every new seam. They are the only priests in the kingdom who quarrel openly with the Greys of the Sea King's Hall: they say the Smith, not the Sea King, should be first in a land that lives on iron as much as on water. In 1090 Keeper Wystan Forgeward preached that the Black Dragon was a smith's fire under the sea and no beast at all, and the Hall-Keeper at Greyhaven had him barred from the Tide Council. His daughter now keeps the hall, and the dwarven iron that lands at Silverdale has made her curious about the dwarves' own Smith.
FX14-022.reputation: Stubborn, learned hall-priests whom the miners love and the Greys call heretics.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Smith's Hall
members.note: She has drunk with the dwarf boatmen at the landing creek and learned that their Smith has another name.

members.role: Old Keeper; her father, blind
members.note: He went blind at his forge in 1100 and still preaches that the dragon is a fire under the sea.

members.role: Sigrid's husband; mine foreman
members.note: He is foreman of the deepest Tarnholt seam and knows the dwarves' bars by their weight in the hand.

members.role: Her son; hall-boy
members.note: He wants to be a smith, not a priest, and works the Tarnholt forge at night when his mother thinks he is praying.

famousDead: First keeper of the Smith's Hall at Silverdale.
FX14-022.secret: In 1090 old Wystan learned from a Merrow digger that Smokewell's smoke made the dragon of 1071, and he wrote it into the Silverdale hall-roll, which is still there.
hooks: The Greys send a priest to Silverdale to see the hall-roll.
Sigrid is asked, quietly, to bless an Irondeep landing.
Orm runs away to Brookhurst to be a smith's apprentice.

FX14-023.name: the Kittocks of Gull Point
FX14-023.title: Lantern-Mother of Gull Point
FX14-023.arms: a sign: a white crescent moon over a lantern, scratched on their doors
FX14-023.power: A fishing village of 300 on the rocks of Gull Point, false lanterns on moonless nights, and a web of cellars for wreck goods.
FX14-023.history: The Kittocks were fishers of Gull Point on the Smokewell March shore when King Wystan drowned chasing toll-runners in 812, and some of what washed up from his six galleys went into Kittock cellars. They learned that the rocks pay better than the nets. For three centuries they have hung false lanterns on stormy, moonless nights to bring cogs onto the reef, and the Channel Law has hanged eleven of them at the harbor mouth. Since 1071 they have done better than ever, because the smoke off Smokewell gives them a dragon to blame for every wreck. The present Lantern-Mother has sworn the clan to leave crown ships alone, and her grandson has already broken the oath.
FX14-023.reputation: Smiling fishers by day and corpse-robbers by night; every sailor in the channel curses Gull Point.

members.role: Head of the clan; Lantern-Mother of Gull Point
members.note: She has outlived two husbands, a hanged son and three Admirals, and knows which Merrow pit-guard takes silver.

members.role: Her son; leader of the lantern men
members.note: He wants to hang the false lanterns on the July dusk, when every eye in the kingdom will be on the water.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He wrecked a toll galley's tender in November against the Lantern-Mother's oath and kept the purse.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She pulls drowning sailors out of the surf before her uncle's men reach them, and has hidden one in the net loft since autumn.

famousDead: Hanged at the harbor mouth after the wreck of a Lucernan cog.
FX14-023.secret: The sailor hidden in Kenna's net loft is a Velgradan off one of the Sevany hulls, washed ashore in a storm, and in his fever he talks about fire.
hooks: Sigurd plans false lanterns for the July dusk.
Kenna's Velgradan sailor wakes up and wants to go home.
A Chain Guard patrol finds a crown seal in a Kittock cellar.

FX14-024.name: the Greaves of Briarhollow
FX14-024.title: Wolf-Reeve of Briarhollow
FX14-024.arms: a black bow strung with red, on green
FX14-024.power: The wolf-reeveship of the Briarhollow forest, a crown bounty on every wolf and outlaw, and forest paths no one else knows.
FX14-024.history: After the Black Cough of 917 emptied the forest villages and the wolves came into Briarhollow, Edric II made the hunter Halvard Greave his wolf-reeve in 919 and paid him a bounty for every wolf's head. The Greaves have hunted the king's forest since, wolves and boar and outlaws alike, and they lead the king's hunts when he comes inland. Their forest runs into the Wrendale woods where Ned Thornby's outlaws hide, and the crown pays them a bounty on outlaw heads too. They have not brought one in since 1098. Their own cousins were among the Redley serfs Thornby freed, and the Greaves remember that the king's forest was a refuge before it was a hunting ground.
FX14-024.reputation: Silent, wolfish forest folk whom lords hire and never invite in.

members.role: Head of the family; Wolf-Reeve of Briarhollow
members.note: He has been paid for 300 wolf heads and has never once asked for the bounty on a man.

members.role: Heir; huntress
members.note: She guides runaway serfs through the forest to Thornby's camps by paths no Redley steward knows.

members.role: Son; king's huntsman
members.note: He led the king's boar hunt in 1103 and wants a knighthood more than he wants another wolf.

members.role: Frida's daughter
members.note: At six she can name every bird in the forest by its call.

famousDead: First wolf-reeve of Briarhollow after the Black Cough.
FX14-024.secret: Frida Greave guides Ned Thornby's runaways through the king's forest, and her brother Orvar has begun to suspect.
hooks: House Redley doubles the bounty on Ned Thornby's head.
Orvar is promised a knighthood if he finds the outlaw camp.
Two hundred serfs will need a path through the forest on the Spring Equinox.

FX15-001.name: House Varelli
FX15-001.title: Lord of Lucina Vale
FX15-001.arms: a green oak with gold acorns, on white

military.office: Knights of the Edicts of Lucina Vale
military.unit: the Varelli banner, 18 lances and 400 Edict Spearmen
military.ties: Varelli knights ride with the Knights of the Edicts and lead the Lucina Vale levy whenever the Sun Road is threatened.

FX15-001.power: Wheat and olive farms of Lucina Vale, 18 lances of the Knights of the Edicts, and the mill rights on the Lucina stream.
FX15-001.history: The first Varelli was a centurion of Lucan the Grey's legion who was given Lucina land when the legion came home from Solenne in 760. The Schism Tax of 738 had already let Temple officials buy a sixth of the farms around Lucina, and Varelli and Temple fields have shared hedges and quarrels ever since. When King Ottone seized 2,000 Temple acres in 1007, the Varelli farmed them for five years; when the Temple took them back in 1012, the house lost its best wheat. Lord Orsino Varelli rides with the Knights of the Edicts and votes with the Castors against the Luminary's Sun Party. His brother is in debt to Ostran bankers to the tune of 4,000 suns.
FX15-001.reputation: Solid old wheat lords who hate the Temple's stewards more than any steppe rider.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Lucina Vale
members.note: Has walked the Temple's hedges every Return Day for forty years to see if they moved.

members.role: Heir; knight of the Edicts
members.note: Wants to sail with the Varenna contingent if the call comes.

members.role: Daughter; Temple novice at Lucina
members.note: Took the Sun's vows to spite her father and now prays for him every noon.

members.role: Brother
members.note: Owes Ostran bankers 4,000 suns and has offered them the mill rights he does not own.

famousDead: Centurion of Lucan the Grey; given Lucina land after the fall of Solenne.
FX15-001.secret: In 1062 the Varelli moved six boundary stones and have farmed 300 acres of Temple land ever since.
hooks: A Temple surveyor comes to Lucina with an old map.
Dario's creditors arrive to collect the mill.

FX15-002.name: House Calderane
FX15-002.title: Lady of Castel Ascino
FX15-002.arms: a black castle with three towers, on dun gold

military.office: Castellans of Castel Ascino
military.unit: the Ascino garrison, 30 lances and 300 crossbows
military.ties: Castel Ascino is the inland anchor of the steppe watch, and Calderane lances join the Marshal of the Steppe March every summer.

FX15-002.power: The castle of Castel Ascino on the plain road toward Santora, its market, and grazing on the plain that the Sabine horse runs covet.
FX15-002.history: King Lucan II the Marcher pushed the realm onto the steppe edge in the 820s and gave the castle on the plain to his captain Renzo Calderane in 826. In 895 Khan Ulagan's riders swept past Castel Ascino to besiege the capital, and the Calderane held it for two years on horse meat and well water. The house has quarrelled with the Sabine over the plain's grazing since the Black Cough emptied the farms after 916. Lord Ugo Calderane died in a fall in 1099, and his widow Ottavia has held the castle since. Since 1103 the night caravans of 'lamp oil' have rested in her outer bailey, and she takes a fee for the stabling.
FX15-002.reputation: Hard castle folk who never forget a siege or a debt.

members.role: Head of the house in her son's name; Lady of Castel Ascino
members.note: Charges the king's oil caravans two suns a camel for a night in her bailey and asks nothing.

members.role: Heir; Lord of Castel Ascino in name
members.note: Wants to ride with Dame Oriana's Santora Riders and has no idea what sleeps in his own bailey.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Rides with the camel strings at night for a share and has seen the jars broken open.

members.role: Dowager
members.note: Tells everyone that her grandmother ate the castle's last dog in 897.

famousDead: Held Castel Ascino against the Khan's riders from 895 to 897.
FX15-002.secret: The king's fire-oil caravans rest in Castel Ascino's outer bailey, and Lady Ottavia keeps a tally of every jar.
hooks: Dame Oriana's riders arrive at the gate on the night a caravan is inside.
Lazzaro wants to sell a jar of fire-oil himself.

FX15-003.name: House Aquilo
FX15-003.title: Knight of the Lucina Tower
FX15-003.arms: a silver hawk on a grey tower, on sky blue

military.office: Hereditary captains of the Lucina coast towers
military.unit: four towers of the Tower Watch, 56 lookouts
military.ties: Aquilo knights have captained the Lucina towers since Tancred's Tower Edict, and their daughter was mother of Dame Serena Falcone.

FX15-003.power: Four watch towers on the Lucina coast, a small knight's fief, and blood ties to the Master of the Tower of Far Eyes.
FX15-003.history: The Aquilo were given the first towers of the Lucina coast when King Tancred the Steadfast ordered a tower every 10 km in 898. They have been tower knights since, poorer and prouder than the Tower Falcones of Felano. In 1073 Nerina Aquilo married Prince Leone Falcone; she died of the Harbor Pox in 1077, and he died on the upper Tirana in 1079. Their daughter Serena, now Master of the Tower of Far Eyes, was raised at court, but she spends every summer at the Lucina tower with her uncle. Sir Vittor Aquilo has the eyes of a good lookout, if not a Falcone's, and he has watched cogs load at night.
FX15-003.reputation: Poor, upright tower knights; the Falcones' poor relations.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of the Lucina Tower
members.note: Counts the cogs that load oil at night and sends the numbers to his niece in cipher.

members.role: Dowager; Dame Serena's grandmother
members.note: Wants Serena married to a man who will make her queen, not a lookout.

members.role: Heir; tower captain
members.note: Jealous of his famous cousin and certain he could read flags as well as she does.

members.role: Daughter; lookout
members.note: Has the sharpest eyes in the family and nobody has noticed yet.

famousDead: Wife of Prince Leone Falcone and mother of Dame Serena; died of the Harbor Pox.
FX15-003.secret: Sir Vittor's tower log, sent to Dame Serena in cipher, is half of the proof of which road the oil jars came by.
hooks: A Harbor-Mistress's clerk asks to buy Sir Vittor's old logs.
Tessa reads a signal flag nobody else can see.

FX15-004.name: House Lavinari
FX15-004.title: Temple Knight of Pertena
FX15-004.arms: a gold sun with twelve rays on red

military.office: Temple knights of the Pertena grain valleys
military.unit: the Lavinari lances, 8 knights and their sergeants
military.ties: Lavinari knights hold Pertena land of the Temple's settlement of 1012 and ride with the Knights of the Edicts.

FX15-004.power: A Temple knight's fief in the Pertena grain valleys, the ear of Luminary Fabio Cresta, and a dead princess's memory.
FX15-004.history: When the Temple took back its Pertena farms in the settlement of 1012, it gave one valley to the knight who had guarded its priests through the corsair year, Ilario Lavinari, and the family has held it as Temple knights since. In 1095 Vittoria Lavinari married Prince Tancred Falcone, the greatest match the house ever made. She died in childbirth in 1097 with a stillborn son, and Tancred has not married again. Sir Leandro Lavinari now offers the prince his younger daughter Brina, and Luminary Cresta's Sun Party pushes the match. Brina does not want it.
FX15-004.reputation: Pious, ambitious and still dressed in mourning for a princess.

members.role: Head of the house; Temple Knight of Pertena
members.note: Tells the Luminary every word the prince says at his table.

members.role: Younger daughter
members.note: Is offered to a prince and in love with a Coast Road Knight.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Runs the fief, thinks his father's plans will end badly, and says nothing.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Keeps her dead daughter's room as it was on the day she married.

famousDead: Wife of Prince Tancred; died in childbirth with a stillborn son.
Guarded the Temple's priests through 1011 and was given a Pertena valley.
FX15-004.secret: Sir Leandro carries the prince's table talk to Luminary Cresta, including Tancred's anger over the oil.
hooks: Prince Tancred asks for Brina's hand in spring.
Brina plans to run away with Sir Fausto Venorri.

FX15-005.name: House Sabelli
FX15-005.title: Lord of the Felt Hills
FX15-005.arms: a gold spear with a blue streamer, on brown

military.office: Bannerets of the Santora Riders
military.unit: a company of the Santora Riders, 250 horse archers
military.ties: Every Sabelli son rides in the Santora Riders, and the house lost 31 riders in the ambush of August 1097.

FX15-005.power: Felt-hill grazing on the steppe edge, 2,000 horses, and a company of the Santora Riders.
FX15-005.history: The Sabelli were knights of the Sabine lords of Santora who settled the felt hills in 870 and, like their lords, married women of the Wind Rider tribes every other generation. They wear felt coats over mail, tie blue cloth to the cairns and shoot from the saddle. In August 1097 Dame Oriana Sabine led 120 riders into an ambush beyond Santora, and 31 of them were Sabelli. Lord Remo Sabelli's son Teodoro survived and saw the tower's warning flag go up before the charge. He has kept silent because the Sabine are the house's lords. The blinded lookout's family lives two valleys away.
FX15-005.reputation: Half-steppe riders, fierce in the saddle and loyal to the Sabine to a fault.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Felt Hills
members.note: Rode with Arnaut Sabine on the embassy to Khan Ozbek in 1080 and still drinks mare's milk at breakfast.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Santora Riders
members.note: Saw the tower flag rise before Dame Oriana charged in 1097, and knows the lookout was blinded for nothing.

members.role: Lady of the house, born of the Sea Wind tribe
members.note: Knows every horse trader of the Horse Road by his family and his lies.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Wants to ride to the Nine Winds and see the Khan's tents.

famousDead: Remo's brother; died in the ambush beyond Santora in August 1097.
FX15-005.secret: Teodoro Sabelli knows that Dame Oriana charged after the tower had warned her, and that the lookout lost his eye for her mistake.
hooks: The blinded lookout's son asks Teodoro to swear to the truth.
Oriana's March ride needs Sabelli riders.

FX15-006.name: House Torvanelli
FX15-006.title: Lord of the Beech Hills
FX15-006.arms: a black woodsman's axe on silver, a green border

military.office: Lords of the Castina Hill Javelins
military.unit: 300 of the Castina Hill Javelins, light foot against boars and bandits
military.ties: Torvanelli foresters fill a quarter of the Castina Hill Javelins and guard the iron road for the Castors.

FX15-006.power: The beech and oak woods of the Castina hills under Castor lordship, sawpits, and 300 hill javelins.
FX15-006.history: The Torvanelli armed their woodcutters beside the Castors when the Wind Riders burned Felano's harvest in 693, and they have held the Castina beech woods under the Castors since. The Solen Fleet Law stripped these hills of oak in 283, and the house has spent four centuries growing it back. The Castor chancellors set the price of Castina timber, and Felano's shipwrights call it robbery. Lord Stefano Torvanelli sells at the Castor price and quietly cuts a second load for Felano by night. His cousin Rinaldo went into the hills with bandits after a quarrel over a woman and has not come out.
FX15-006.reputation: Rough forest lords who are too useful to the Castors to be punished.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Beech Hills
members.note: Sells Castina oak to Felano shipwrights by night at twice the Castor price and half the Castor tax.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Hill Javelins
members.note: Killed a hell boar with two javelins at 19 and has hunted bandits since.

members.role: Daughter; married to a Castor mine-reeve
members.note: Warns her father whenever her husband's cousins come to count logs.

members.role: Cousin; outlaw
members.note: Leads a band of 20 in the high woods and robs only Castor carts.

famousDead: Armed his woodcutters against the Wind Riders in 693.
FX15-006.secret: Lord Stefano cuts Castina oak for Felano's shipwrights by night, cheating the Castor chancellors of their timber price.
hooks: A Castor reeve counts the stumps.
Rinaldo's band robs a cart carrying the chancery's rolls.

FX15-007.name: House Ostrani
FX15-007.title: Knight-Captain of the Lucina Border
FX15-007.arms: a red gate on white, a blue chief

military.office: Knight-Captains of the Lucina Border garrison
military.unit: the Lucina Border garrison, 1,200 men on the Sun Road toward Ostra
military.ties: The Ostrani have commanded the border garrison on the Sun Road since 931 and keep the toll gate toward the Free City.

FX15-007.power: The Lucina Border garrison of 1,200 men, the Sun Road toll gate, and cousins in the counting houses of Ostra.
FX15-007.history: The Ostrani came from an Ostran wine family that settled at Lucina after the Black Cough and married into a knight's house.
