King Tancred II made them captains of the Sun Road border in 931, and they have held it since. Half the house's cousins sit at counting benches in Ostra, and the crown's debt of 350,000 suns to the Ostran bankers has made those cousins very interested in what passes the gate. Sir Nerio Ostrani keeps the gate honestly. His wife writes to her brother in Ostra every week.
FX15-007.reputation: Half-Ostran border knights; men say their loyalty is for rent.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight-Captain of the Lucina Border
members.note: Turned back an Ostran banker's carriage in 1101 for not paying the toll, and has not been invited to Ostra since.

members.role: Lady of the house, born in Ostra
members.note: Writes to her banker brother every week about the soldiers who pass the gate.

members.role: Heir; sergeant of the border garrison
members.note: Believes Morhaven should pay its debts and wishes his mother would stop talking about them.

members.role: Daughter; clerk at an Ostran bench
members.note: Counts coin in Ostra and means never to come home.

FX15-007.secret: Lady Fiora reports every troop movement on the Sun Road to her brother, a clerk of the Ostran bank that holds the crown's debt.
hooks: The Varenna contingent marches past the Lucina gate.
Giulia sends home a ledger page that names a Morhaven lord.

FX15-008.name: House Venorri
FX15-008.title: Banneret of the Coast Road Knights
FX15-008.arms: a gold lion holding an olive branch, on dark blue
FX15-008.words: On the Road, As at Felano

military.office: Bannerets of the Coast Road Knights
military.unit: a banner of the Coast Road Knights, 22 lances
military.ties: A Venorri banner rode in the first muster of the Coast Road Knights in 1013 and will sail with the Varenna contingent if King Roderic dies.

FX15-008.power: A banner of the Coast Road Knights, a fief of olive terraces on the coast road, and the king's favor.
FX15-008.history: When King Aurelio Falcone raised the Coast Road Knights in 1013, named for the old victory of 896 among the olive terraces, he gave the first banner to Bastian Venorri, a captain who had manned the harbor chain in 1011. The house has led a banner of the Knights since. Sir Amadeo Venorri led it at the Felano alarm of 1096 when the Redsail galleys came. His son Fausto is to sail with the 600 Coast Road Knights under Sir Ruggero Castor if the Varenna pact is called. Fausto is also in love with Brina Lavinari, whom the Temple means for the prince.
FX15-008.reputation: Gallant coast knights with more courage than land.

members.role: Head of the house; Banneret of the Coast Road Knights
members.note: Rode the length of the coast road in a night in 1096 to call the Felano chain crews.

members.role: Heir; knight
members.note: Writes songs for Brina Lavinari and would fight a prince for her.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Runs the olive terraces and knows her son is about to ruin the family.

members.role: Younger son; squire
members.note: Carries his brother's letters and tells nobody, not even his mother.

famousDead: Manned the Morhaven harbor chain in 1011; first banneret of the Coast Road Knights.
FX15-008.secret: Fausto Venorri and Brina Lavinari have exchanged rings in secret before a hedge priest.
hooks: The Varenna pact is called, and Fausto must sail.
Prince Tancred learns who holds Brina's ring.

FX15-009.name: the Mironi family
FX15-009.title: Sergeant of the Deep Walls
FX15-009.arms: a black crossbow bolt on grey stone

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Heights Garrison crossbows
military.unit: the Mironi files, 120 crossbowmen of the Heights Garrison
military.ties: A Mironi has sergeanted a stretch of the Deep Walls since the stone was laid in 806, and they were on the wall through the whole siege of 895 to 897.

FX15-009.power: Command of the crossbow files on the landward wall, a house in the Mine Lanes, and four centuries of wall-craft.
FX15-009.history: When Marius the Mason finished the Deep Walls in 806, a crossbow sergeant named Pello Mironi was given the stretch above the landward gate, and his sons have held it since. They were on that wall through the Khan's siege of 895 to 897, and a Mironi sergeant shot the Khan's engineer who first brought fire-oil pots to the harbor. They drink at the Twelve Metres alehouse, marry miners' daughters and never leave the city. Sergeant Aldo Mironi knows that the 'carrion carriers' paid in 897 were his own great-great-grandfather's men, because the family tale says so.
FX15-009.reputation: Stone-faced wall sergeants; the city sleeps because they do not.

members.role: Head of the family; sergeant of the landward gate
members.note: Can put a bolt through a sentry's visor at 200 paces in the dark, and has.

members.role: Wife; miner's daughter
members.note: Brews the wall-sergeants' wine and hears all their grumbles.

members.role: Heir; file-leader
members.note: Bored on the wall; wants to sail with the Varenna contingent and see a real war.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Spans her father's crossbow when he is asleep.

famousDead: Sergeant of the landward wall in the siege; family tale says he led the carrion carriers by night.
FX15-009.secret: The family tale, told only to heirs, is that a Mironi led the men who fouled the Khan's water in 897.
hooks: The Luminary preaches the Miracle of 897 and Aldo laughs aloud.
A clerk of the chancery asks the family for its tale.

FX15-010.name: House Pellegrane
FX15-010.title: Castellan of the Horse Road Forts
FX15-010.arms: a white tower on green over a gold road

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of the six lesser forts of the Horse Road
military.unit: the Steppe March forts, about 1,000 of their 2,400 men
military.ties: Pellegrane castellans hold the forts beyond Castel Ascino for the Marshal of the Steppe March and have built four of Prince Tancred's eleven new towers.

FX15-010.power: Command of the lesser forts on the Horse Road and the trust of Prince Tancred, Marshal of the Steppe March.
FX15-010.history: After the first Horse Road compact of 930, King Tancred II built six small forts along the road and gave their keeping to Renzo Pellegrane, a sergeant who had ridden with the Sabine to the Nine Winds. The family has held them since, and they are the Marshal's men, not the Master of Horse's. Since Prince Tancred became Marshal in 1096, Pellegrane masons have built four of his eleven new towers. They watch the night caravans pass and know what is in the jars. In late 1104 a Pellegrane rider carried a letter without a seal north toward the Tessarian front.
FX15-010.reputation: Plain soldiers who would die for the prince and distrust everyone at Santora.

members.role: Head of the house; Castellan of the Horse Road Forts
members.note: Has watched the king's oil go by for two years and spits each time.

members.role: Daughter; master mason of the new towers
members.note: Built four towers in seven years and drinks with the Marshal's engineers as an equal.

members.role: Heir; rider of the forts
members.note: Carried Prince Tancred's unsigned warning across the Grey Channel in November 1104.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Begs her son to forget where he rode.

famousDead: Sergeant who rode to the Nine Winds in 930 and became first castellan of the Horse Road forts.
FX15-010.secret: Stefano Pellegrane carried Prince Tancred's unsigned warning about the 'lamp oil' to Prince Nikos Tessaran.
hooks: King Aurelio's men ask who rode north in November.
Dame Oriana wants Pellegrane riders for her March ride.

FX15-011.name: the Camparo family
FX15-011.title: Gallery-Sergeant of the Mine Hall
FX15-011.arms: a black mountain cut by a gold gallery, on iron grey

military.office: Gallery-Sergeants of the Castina Miners
military.unit: two squads of the Castina Miners, 80 counter-miners
military.ties: Camparo men fought in the Night of the Mines in 895 and have trained in the Mine Hall of Castina since it opened in 898.

FX15-011.power: Two squads of counter-miners and the oldest knowledge of the listening galleries under the Deep Walls.
FX15-011.history: Neri Camparo was one of the Castina miners who broke into the Khan's tunnel under the landward gate in November 895 and fired it. When the Castors opened the Mine Hall of Castina in 898, he was its first gallery-sergeant, and his family has kept the post since. Camparo boys learn to listen to a bowl of water on a gallery floor before they can read. They serve under Master Otto Deepgrave of the Mine Hall and keep the galleries 12 metres under the Mine Lanes. In 1088 a Camparo found an old gallery from Marius's time that runs under the Sun Temple, and the family has listened there ever since.
FX15-011.reputation: Pale, quiet tunnel folk; people are a little afraid of them.

members.role: Head of the family; gallery-sergeant
members.note: Can hear a pick at forty paces through rock and tell you if it is human.

members.role: Daughter; gallery-mapper
members.note: Listens under the Sun Temple and writes down what the priests say.

members.role: Heir; squad leader
members.note: Went up the Tirana with Master Deepgrave's bolt-thrower crews in 1079 as a boy and came back.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Sleeps in the galleries because he says the city is too loud.

famousDead: Broke into the Khan's tunnel on the Night of the Mines and fired it.
FX15-011.secret: A forgotten gallery runs under the Sun Temple, and the Camparo have listened to the Luminary's councils from it since 1088.
hooks: The Chancellor asks what the Luminary said last night.
Temple workmen dig a new crypt toward the old gallery.

FX15-012.name: the Solvani family
FX15-012.title: Tower-Captain of the Steppe Edge
FX15-012.arms: a white owl on a black tower, on blue

military.office: Tower-captains of the steppe-edge towers
military.unit: three towers of the Tower Watch on the steppe edge, 42 lookouts
military.ties: Solvani lookouts have climbed steppe towers since the first was built in 898, beside the charcoal-burner's son who founded House Falcone.

FX15-012.power: Three towers of the steppe watch and the respect of every lookout in the kingdom.
FX15-012.history: The Solvani climbed the steppe towers in the first year of Tancred's Tower Edict, and a Solvani lookout taught a charcoal-burner's boy named Piero to read flags in 935; that boy's house now wears the crown. The family has stayed in the towers, sworn to go blind rather than lie. In August 1097 Dame Oriana Sabine lost 120 riders in an ambush beyond Santora and blamed the tower. Lookout Pello Solvani lost an eye under the Falcone Edicts for a false alarm he never gave. The family has not forgotten, and the other lookouts have not either.
FX15-012.reputation: Proud, poor watchers who are owed an eye by the Sabine.

members.role: Head of the family; tower-captain, one-eyed
members.note: Lost his left eye for Dame Oriana's mistake and still reads flags at two kilometres with his right.

members.role: Wife; lookout
members.note: Took her husband's tower shift the day after the blinding and has kept it since.

members.role: Heir; lookout
members.note: Has sworn on his father's eye to make Dame Oriana confess.

members.role: Daughter; tower apprentice
members.note: Learns cipher at the Tower of Far Eyes and adores Dame Serena.

famousDead: Lookout who taught Piero the Falcon to read flags.
FX15-012.secret: Ugo Solvani has written to the Marshal, and the letter names Teodoro Sabelli as a witness.
hooks: Ugo meets Dame Oriana on the Horse Road.
A lookout's false alarm brings the whole steppe watch to arms.

FX15-013.name: the Feliciane family
FX15-013.title: Master of the Smiths of Felano
FX15-013.arms: a grey stone anvil marked with runes, on red
FX15-013.power: The Smiths' Guild of Felano, its stone anvil with the dwarf marks, and the iron trade from the Castina pits to the ships.
FX15-013.history: The smiths of Felano learned the bloomery from an exiled dwarf about 1000 BR, and their guild still keeps his stone anvil and a garbled tale of 'the Short Master'. The Feliciane have held the guild's mastership since the Broken Crowns, and they forge the nails, anchors and chain of every Felano ship. The Castor chancellors own the Castina iron and sell it at their price, and the Feliciane have fought that price for three centuries. They forged the new harbor chain after the earthquake of 1039. In 1104 a dwarf traveller offered the guild master gold to see the anvil, and he refused.
FX15-013.reputation: Proud iron-workers of Felano who think the capital lives on their sweat.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Smiths of Felano
members.note: Refused a dwarf's gold to see the anvil and now wonders why a dwarf wanted to.

members.role: Daughter; chain-smith
members.note: Forged half the links of the Felano harbor chain and can lift an anchor fluke alone.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Buys iron from the Torvanelli carts on the side and calls it guild stock.

members.role: Apprentice; grandson
members.note: Has copied the dwarf marks off the anvil onto a wax tablet.

famousDead: Forged the new harbor chain of Morhaven after the earthquake of 1039.
FX15-013.secret: The marks on the guild's stone anvil are a dwarf's name and his hold's sign, which some dwarves would pay dearly to read.
hooks: The dwarf traveller comes back with friends.
The Castors raise the iron price again.

FX15-014.name: the Verazzi family
FX15-014.title: Galley-Master of Felano
FX15-014.arms: a black anchor on white over blue waves

military.office: Galley captains of the Felano squadron
military.unit: two war galleys and 120 Galley Marines
military.ties: Verazzi captains have led galleys of the Felano squadron since the corsair year of 1011 and would carry the Varenna contingent across the Middle Sea.

FX15-014.power: Two war galleys in the crown's Felano squadron, three cogs of their own, and the best shipyard berths in Felano.
FX15-014.history: In May 1011 a Felano galley captain named Leone Verazzi rowed beside Aurelio Falcone's coast galley when the 42 corsair sails were sighted, and he was given his own galley when Aurelio was crowned. The family has captained Felano galleys since. In July 1096 they rowed out under the chain when Dame Serena sighted the Redsail galleys. Captain Flavia Verazzi hates the Blackreef pirates who burned her grandfather's ship and has argued against every toll paid to them. Her cogs need Castina oak, and she buys it by night from the Torvanelli.
FX15-014.reputation: Hard-rowing Felano sea folk who would rather sink than pay a pirate.

members.role: Head of the family; Galley-Master of Felano
members.note: Rowed out under the chain in 1096 and has wanted a war with Blackreef every year since.

members.role: Heir; galley captain
members.note: Knows the crossing to Varenna by heart and dreads making it with 4,000 men aboard.

members.role: Brother; shipwright
members.note: Builds cogs from night-cut Castina oak and asks no questions about it.

members.role: Daughter; marine
members.note: Climbed the mast of a Redsail prize at twelve and refuses to come down from anything since.

famousDead: Rowed beside Aurelio Falcone in 1011; drowned in the harbor when the 1039 earthquake struck.
FX15-014.secret: The Verazzi cogs are built of Castina oak cut illegally by night and sold below the Castor price.
hooks: The Varenna contingent must sail in nine days.
A Blackreef envoy rows into Felano under a white flag.

FX15-015.name: the Aurisane family
FX15-015.title: Master of the Horse Gate
FX15-015.arms: a running brown horse on gold, a blue cloth at its neck
FX15-015.words: Every Head Tolled, Every Head Sold
FX15-015.power: Horse runs on the plain, stables at the Horse Gate of Morhaven, and the brokerage of about a third of the horses that come down the Horse Road.
FX15-015.history: The Aurisane were grooms of the Sabine who went to the first Santora Horse Fair in 930 and stayed in the trade. They now run horses on the plain and stables at the Horse Gate of the capital, and they broker a third of the horses that come down from the Nine Winds. Half their grooms are half-orcs and steppe men. They pay the Master of Horse his twentieth and the crown its toll, and they hang no horse thieves because they buy back the horses first. This spring 400 Morhaven-bred horses are to leave their runs for Prince Andros's Dawn Lances, by Lord Arnaut Sabine's order and against the king's word to Queen Livia.
FX15-015.reputation: Rich, sharp horse-copers; nobody buys from them without a second look.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Horse Gate
members.note: Can price a horse from the sound of its hooves on stone.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Drinks fermented mare's milk with steppe traders at the Falcon's Rest and loses at dice on purpose.

members.role: Head groom; half-orc foster son
members.note: Will drive the 400 horses north and knows they are for the enemy of the king's friend.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Keeps the stud book and has noticed the 400 are written down as 'dead of colic'.

famousDead: Groom of the Sabine who brokered horses at the first Santora Horse Fair.
FX15-015.secret: The 400 horses sold to Prince Andros are written in the Aurisane stud book as dead of colic.
hooks: Prince Tancred's men inspect the runs before the horses leave.
Vittoria asks her mother where the dead horses are buried.

FX15-016.name: the Albrescane family
FX15-016.title: Steward of the Temple Farms of Lucina
FX15-016.arms: a gold bell on white with a red sun-ray border
FX15-016.power: Stewardship of the Temple's farms around Lucina, about a sixth of the land there, and the debt rolls of the Temple courts.
FX15-016.history: When Temple officials used the Schism Tax to buy the farms of Lucina in 741, they needed stewards, and the Albrescane were Lucina clerks who could read Old Solen. They have run the Temple's Lucina farms since, collected its rents and sat as clerks of the Temple courts, which in Morhaven judge all debt. King Ottone's seizure of 1007 cost them five years of rents, and they still pray for his soul with feeling. Father Nerio Albrescane is secretary to Luminary Fabio Cresta and the pen of the Sun Party. Since 1099 he has known that the chancery holds a roll that shames the Miracle of Morhaven.
FX15-016.reputation: Polite, pious and merciless with a debtor.

members.role: Head of the family; secretary to the Luminary
members.note: Drafts every sermon of the Sun Party and has read the Treasurer's clerk's letter about the carrion roll.

members.role: Sister; Steward of the Temple Farms of Lucina
members.note: Knows every hedge and boundary stone around Lucina, and that six of them have moved.

members.role: Graziella's son; clerk of the Temple debt court
members.note: Holds the debt papers of half the knights of Lucina.

members.role: Graziella's daughter; Temple novice
members.note: Sings at noon in the Lucina temple and slips notes to a Varelli son.

famousDead: Steward of the Temple's Lucina farms bought with the Schism Tax.
FX15-016.secret: Father Nerio knows the Chancellor showed the carrion roll to a Holy See clerk in 1099, and is saving it to break the Castors.
hooks: Graziella finds the moved boundary stones.
Emilio calls in a knight's debt on the eve of the Varenna muster.

FX15-017.name: the Clarenzi family
FX15-017.title: Notary of the Chancery Rolls
FX15-017.arms: a silver key over a black quill, on blue
FX15-017.power: The copying and keeping of the chancery rolls of Morhaven under the Castor chancellors, and the cipher tables of the Tower of Far Eyes.
FX15-017.history: When Marco Castor became the first Chancellor in 760, he hired a Solen notary named Valerio Clarenzi to copy the new kingdom's rolls, and the Clarenzi have copied them for 344 years. They write Old Solen, the cipher of the Tower Watch and three kinds of trade shorthand. In 1099 Notary Fabio Clarenzi copied the garrison roll of 897 for the clerk of the Holy See's Treasurer, by the Chancellor's order. His daughter teaches cipher at the Tower of Far Eyes and helps Dame Serena keep her log. The family knows more of Morhaven's secrets than any lord, and has never sold one.

members.role: Head of the family; Notary of the Chancery Rolls
members.note: Copied the carrion roll for a Holy See clerk in 1099 and kept a third copy nobody ordered.

members.role: Daughter; cipher-mistress at the Tower of Far Eyes
members.note: Helps Dame Serena encode the oil log and sees what it proves.

members.role: Heir; notary
members.note: Wants nothing but a quiet desk and is about to be offered a fortune.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Can already read his grandfather's shorthand upside down.

famousDead: First notary of the Morhaven chancery.
FX15-017.secret: Fabio Clarenzi kept a third copy of the carrion roll of 897 in his own house.
hooks: The Luminary's secretary offers Emilio a Temple post for the third copy.
Aurelia must choose between Dame Serena's log and her father's oath.

FX15-018.name: the Montessi family
FX15-018.title: Huntsman of the Castina Hills
FX15-018.arms: a black boar on green, a red spear across it
FX15-018.power: The royal hunting rights in the Castina hills, the boar bounty, and a pack of 30 boarhounds.
FX15-018.history: The Montessi have been huntsmen in the Castina hills for generations, but their office dates from 1066, when a hell boar killed King Leone's huntsman Lazzaro Montessi above Felano. The king paid a bounty on boars for ten years and gave the dead man's son his post. The family has led the royal hunts since and taken more than 300 bounties. Prince Tancred hunts with them when he cannot sleep. The head's daughter has tracked a hell boar to a den near the Dorica iron workings, where Castor men say nothing lives.
FX15-018.reputation: Scarred, cheerful hill hunters; welcome at every inn.

members.role: Head of the family; Huntsman of the Castina Hills
members.note: Took his father's post at fourteen and has killed 140 boars since, nine of them hell boars.

members.role: Daughter; tracker
members.note: Tracked a hell boar to a den by the Dorica workings where the Castor men swear nothing lives.

members.role: Heir; kennel master
members.note: Talks to his boarhounds more than to people and is happier for it.

famousDead: King Leone's huntsman, killed by a hell boar above Felano.
FX15-018.secret: The Castor reeves at Dorica have been feeding the hell boar near the workings to keep people out of a gallery.
hooks: Prince Tancred wants a night hunt.
Nella finds something in the Dorica den that is not a boar's.

FX15-019.name: the Fosso family
FX15-019.title: Captain of the Lantern Lads
FX15-019.arms: a red flame in a black lantern (chalked on doors they protect)
FX15-019.power: The Lantern Lads, about 50 dockers of the Harbor Town who unload what others will not touch, and a cellar under the harbor temple.
FX15-019.history: The Fosso were dockers of Morhaven harbor who lost their licences when the Harbor Pox emptied the quays in 1078. They kept working anyway, by night, and their crew became the Lantern Lads. They unload what the harbor clerks cannot see: Ostran wine past the tolls, horses with blurred brands, and since 1103 the 'lamp oil' jars that the king's own clerks pretend not to see. They take a share and keep their mouths shut. Old Mother Fosso has three rules: never steal from a sailor, never talk to a priest, never open the jars.
FX15-019.reputation: Harbor rats with a code; the watch takes their coin and leaves them alone.

members.role: Head of the clan; called Mother Fosso
members.note: Has three rules and has buried two men who broke them.

members.role: Son; captain of the Lantern Lads
members.note: Opened one jar in 1104, smelled it, and knows it is not lamp oil.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: Wants to sell what her uncle smelled to whoever pays most.

members.role: Son; horse-brand blurrer
members.note: Can turn any brand into any other with a hot iron and a damp rag.

FX15-019.secret: Remo Fosso broke open a 'lamp oil' jar and knows it is the Khan's fire-oil.
hooks: Bianca offers to sell a jar to a Tessarian spy.
A horse at the Horse Gate turns out to be stolen from the Sabine runs.

FX15-020.name: the Vitrano family
FX15-020.title: Master of the Steppe Trade
FX15-020.arms: a red chevron over three green olives, on white
FX15-020.words: Grain for Gold, Oil for Peace
FX15-020.power: Warehouses at the Horse Gate, camel strings on the Horse Road, and the oil, wine and grain trade with the Horde's Nagoth clans.
FX15-020.history: Old Pello Vitrano began selling olive oil and wine to steppe traders at the Horse Gate in 1049, and his son took the trade further: since the 1080s the Vitrano have sold oil, wine and grain to the Nagoth clans of the Horde, with the king's leave and his tax. They ship 300 cartloads a year up the Horse Road and bring back hides, salt and silver. Master Tullio Vitrano's natural son by an orc trader's daughter manages the Nagoth end and is the only man of the house the orcs trust. The house keeps no oil of its own in the night caravans, but it lends its camels.
FX15-020.reputation: Rich traders who deal with orcs; the Sun Party calls them traitors.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Steppe Trade
members.note: Has sold grain to orcs for twenty years and never once been robbed by one.

members.role: Natural son; factor among the Nagoth clans
members.note: Half-orc, half-Vitrano, and the only one who knows what the Horde says about Morhaven.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Pretends her husband's orc son does not exist and hates that she needs him.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Lends his father's camels to the night caravans and pockets the hire.

famousDead: Began the steppe trade at the Horse Gate in 1049.
FX15-020.secret: Dario Vitrano hires the family's camels to the king's fire-oil caravans without his father's knowledge.
hooks: A Nagoth chief asks Gorza why Morhaven sells fire to Tessar.
The Sun Party preaches against orc-traders on Return Day.

FX16-001.name: House Ardolani
FX16-001.title: Lord of Castel Ardola
FX16-001.arms: a silver castle on a green hill, a purple sky above

military.office: Castellans of Castel Ardola
military.unit: 80 house crossbowmen and the Castel Ardola garrison
military.ties: The Ardolani hold their castle on the Sabena road by contract with the Twelve and send their sons to the Purple Company for a year to learn how hired men think.

FX16-001.power: Castel Ardola above the Sabena road, olive hills worth about 6,000 suns a year, and a contract with the Twelve renewed every ten years.
FX16-001.history: In July 893, when 8,000 Wind riders burned Camina and the villages around Sabena, the olive farmer Bruno Ardolani held his walled farm on the hill with forty tenants and two crossbows. Ilaria the Ledger bought the hill from the Twelve's account and gave it back to him with a castle contract, which is how Ostra makes lords. Castel Ardola has been an Ardolani fort ever since, held by contract, not by blood right, and the contract has been renewed eleven times. The house married into the Aventi-Lunetti of Calora in 1060. In 1105 the lord wants his contract made hereditary before the Sabena Commons march, and the First Banker has not answered his letter.
FX16-001.reputation: Ostra's nearest thing to country lords; the Twelve find them useful and slightly comical.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Castel Ardola
members.note: He reads his castle contract every New Year's Day and is terrified of the renewal clause.

members.role: Lady of Ardola; born an Aventi-Lunetti of Calora
members.note: She is a Lunetti cousin without the memory and has never forgiven the family for testing her at five.

members.role: Heir; serving his year in the Purple Company
members.note: He has heard his sergeant say the company's pay chest is pledged to dwarves.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She gives olives to the Sabena dyers' children at the castle gate and has met Mora Purplehand.

famousDead: Held his hill against the Wind riders in 893 and was given the castle contract.
FX16-001.secret: Lady Camilla has written to Adriano Carrano offering the castle's support if he will make the contract hereditary when he wins.
hooks: The castle contract is up for renewal in 1106.
The Sabena Commons march passes under the castle walls.
Matteo learns how few men the Purple Company really has.

FX16-002.name: House Belurni
FX16-002.title: Knight of Belurno
FX16-002.arms: a gold sun over a black plough, on white

military.office: Knights of the Temple's Ostran estates
military.unit: 4 lances and the Belurno tenant spears
military.ties: Belurni sons have ridden with the Knights of the Sun's Ostran chapters as lay escorts for three centuries, and the house leads the Temple tenants' levy around Belurno.

FX16-002.power: A knight's manor at Belurno held of the Temple, about 800 suns a year, and the stewardship of 40 Temple farms bought in the Schism Tax years.
FX16-002.history: In 746 a Temple official used Schism Tax money to buy the farms around Belurno, and he placed a knight's family to hold them for the Temple: the Belurni. Their deed is dated 746 and has never been shown to anyone. When Ostra bought its freedom in 758, the Temple's farms stayed the Temple's, and the Belurni have held them since as the Temple's knights inside a city of bankers. They are the Temple Party's only sword in the Ostran countryside. In 1105 Luminary Paolo Treve uses their manor for meetings he does not want held on Tower Hill.
FX16-002.reputation: Pious country knights in a city that worships ledgers; the bankers call them the Temple's scarecrows.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of Belurno
members.note: He lends his hall to Luminary Treve and does not ask what is discussed there.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the Temple farm rolls
members.note: She has read the 746 deed and knows exactly whose coin bought Belurno.

members.role: Heir; lay escort of the Knights of the Sun
members.note: He wants to ride to Tessar with the Noon knights if Treasurer Dorn wins the chair.

members.role: Daughter; pupil at the Ledger School
members.note: She studies bookkeeping on Luminary Treve's money and reports what she sees in the school's books.

famousDead: Placed at Belurno in 746 to hold the Temple's farms.
FX16-002.secret: The Belurno deed of 746 shows the Temple bought its Ostran farms with coin meant for the imperial army.
hooks: Luminary Treve's meetings at Belurno are watched by Lunetti men.
Elisa finds something in the Ledger School's books.
Fabio rides for Tessar.

FX16-003.name: the Brennock family
FX16-003.title: Captain of the Sabena Citadel
FX16-003.arms: a black crossbow on a grey mountain, on white

military.office: Captains by contract of the Sabena Citadel
military.unit: the Citadel Crossbows, 1,600 Highland crossbowmen and garrison men
military.ties: The Brennocks came down from the Highland valleys with their crossbows when the citadel was begun in 1084, and every captain of its walls since has been one of them.

FX16-003.power: Command of the Sabena Citadel and its 1,600 crossbows, paid monthly by the Twelve, and the Highland valleys' habit of sending sons where a Brennock pays.
FX16-003.history: When the Twelve began the Sabena Citadel in 1084 after the dyers' riots, they wanted crossbowmen who had no cousins in Sabena. Rolf Brennock, a Highland crossbow captain, brought 400 men down from the valleys and built the garrison around them. His daughter Ulla took the citadel in 1099. The Brennocks are paid on the first of every month in good Ostran silver and have never mutinied. They are the same Highland stock as Captain Gerolt Marr of the Purple Company, and the two companies drink together. In 1105 the Sabena Commons may march at the Purple Fair, and Lorin the Lamplighter wants the citadel itself.
FX16-003.reputation: Foreign, sober and paid; Sabena hates the citadel and grudgingly respects the woman who holds it.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Sabena Citadel
members.note: She has told the Twelve she will hold the citadel against any march but will not shoot into a bread crowd.

members.role: Her father; founder of the garrison
members.note: He still walks the walls each evening and calls the dyers 'the purple sheep'.

members.role: Ulla's daughter; crossbow sergeant
members.note: She has been meeting a lamplighter's boy from Sabena on the citadel steps.

members.role: Ulla's son; born in Sabena
members.note: He speaks Sabena dock cant better than Highland speech and is not sure which side he is on.

FX16-003.secret: Edda Brennock's sweetheart is one of Lorin the Lamplighter's men, sent to learn the citadel's gates.
hooks: The Purple Fair march reaches the citadel's walls.
Edda is asked to leave a postern unbarred.
The citadel's pay is late for the first time in twenty years.

FX16-004.name: the Cavaroni family
FX16-004.title: Captain of the Calora Lances
FX16-004.arms: a running gold horse on red, a silver lance across

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Calora Lances
military.unit: the Calora Lances, 1,200 medium horse at Calora Castle
military.ties: The Calora Lances are Ostra's only horse, and a Cavaroni has led them on the Sun Road west since they were raised after the Wind raid of 893.

FX16-004.power: Command of the Calora Lances, a horse farm in the Calora hills, and the Sun Road west to the Holy See's border.
FX16-004.history: After the Wind riders burned the villages around Sabena in 893, Ilaria the Ledger decided the city needed horsemen of its own to watch the Sun Road. In 897 she hired Taddeo Cavaroni, a Morhaven horse-sergeant who had fought the Khan, to raise the Calora Lances. The family has led them since, under contract renewed by every First Banker. The lances escort Temple coin and Lunetti couriers on the Sun Road and chase bandits in the Calora hills. They have not fought a battle in two centuries and are proud of it. In 1105 the Lances escort the secret Tessarian envoys between the border and Ledger Street, and the captain knows their faces.
FX16-004.reputation: Ostra's only cavalry, dashing and underemployed; the Sun Road inns know them well.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Calora Lances
members.note: He has escorted both Tessarian envoys to Ledger Street and swears he has never seen either.

members.role: Heiress; master of the horse farm
members.note: She breeds the Lances' remounts and rides patrols in her brother's place when he is drunk.

members.role: Son; lieutenant of the Lances; the black sheep
members.note: He has lost money at dice to a Velgrad merchant who asks a great deal about the envoys' route.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She keeps the family's contract copies in a chest no banker has seen.

famousDead: Raised the Calora Lances for Ilaria the Ledger in 897.
FX16-004.secret: The captain's son has let slip the Tessarian envoys' road to a Velgrad agent over dice.
hooks: Bandits ambush an envoy party on the Sun Road.
Fiora wants the captaincy over her brother.
The Lances are ordered to escort the fourth gold expedition's silver.

FX16-005.name: the Murati family
FX16-005.title: Warden of the Sea Walls and the Harbor Chain
FX16-005.arms: a white wall of three courses on blue, a gold chain below

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of the Sea Walls and the Harbor Chain
military.unit: the Sea Walls and harbor chain garrison, 1,200 men and engineers
military.ties: A Murati mason rebuilt the harbour mole with the Harbor Wardens in 697, and the family has kept the walls and chain for the city since, raising it in 1044 against the Tessarian ships.

FX16-005.power: The wardenship of the Sea Walls and harbor chain, 1,200 men, the masons' lodge of the harbour, and the oldest office in the city.
FX16-005.history: When the earthquake of 9 February 697 threw down Ostra's harbour mole, the Harbor Wardens hired the mason Pietro Murati to rebuild it, and he stayed to keep it. The Murati raised the Sea Walls after it and forged the harbour chain. Their wardenship is older than the Charter of the Twelve and older than Ostra's freedom. On New Year's Day 1044 a Murati raised the chain on Isabetta Lunetti's word and trapped the Tessarian ships in port. The family is proud and not rich, and it knows every crack in the walls. In 1105 the warden has found that the mole the Aventi built in 697 is settling, and it would cost 40,000 suns to save.
FX16-005.reputation: Stone-dusted, plain and proud; the oldest family in Ostra that never became rich.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Sea Walls
members.note: He has measured the mole's settling for six years and the Twelve have laughed at his figures.

members.role: Heiress; master mason
members.note: She dives under the mole herself to look at the footings.

members.role: Son; captain of the chain crews
members.note: He keeps the chain greased and knows the night chests of the dragon-toll money come in under it.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She was on the walls in 1044 and still tells the story of the trapped ships to every child on the street.

famousDead: Rebuilt the harbour mole after the earthquake of 697.
Raised the harbor chain against the Tessarian ships in 1044.
FX16-005.secret: The harbour mole is settling and could fall in a hard earthquake; the Twelve have ignored the warden's figures.
hooks: An earthquake shakes the harbour.
Bruno is paid to look away when a night chest lands.
The Twelve refuse 40,000 suns for the mole.

FX16-006.name: the Scudieri family
FX16-006.title: Sergeant of the Vault Door
FX16-006.arms: a silver round buckler on purple, a black key in its boss

military.office: Hereditary Sergeants of the Vault Door in the Exchange Guard
military.unit: the vault watch of the Exchange Guard, 60 men
military.ties: Since the Temple's coin came to the Lunetti vault in 951, a Scudieri sergeant has stood at its door, and every Scudieri boy trains at Buckler Hall before he is ten.

FX16-006.power: The night and day watch on the Lunetti vault door, 60 picked men, and the trust of the house that holds the Temple's coin.
FX16-006.history: On New Year's Day 951 the Temple's coin moved to House Lunetti's vault at Ostra, and the Lunettis needed men for its door who could be trusted with gold they would never own. They chose the Scudieri, buckler-men of Buckler Lane who had guarded the Exchange benches. A Scudieri has stood at the vault door since. They do not go into the vault and do not want to. The present sergeant trained under Master Rico Ambro at Buckler Hall and is his best pupil. He has noticed that the strong-room clerk Fausto Renn leaves late on nights when the First Banker's study lamp is out.
FX16-006.reputation: Silent, buckler-armed and incorruptible; Ledger Street jokes that the Scudieri are part of the door.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Vault Door
members.note: He has written down Fausto Renn's late nights and does not know whom to hand the list to.

members.role: His wife
members.note: She keeps a knife in her sleeve because her husband's job has made her expect visitors.

members.role: Heir; buckler-man of the vault watch
members.note: Fausto Renn has befriended him and bought him wine three times this winter.

members.role: Daughter; Buckler Hall pupil
members.note: Master Ambro says she has the quickest hands in the hall.

famousDead: First sergeant of the vault door in 951.
FX16-006.secret: The sergeant's list of Fausto Renn's late nights would expose the leak from the First Banker's study.
hooks: Tullio is asked by his new friend to swap a watch on Lantern Night.
Orso must decide whether to take his list to Beatrice Lunetti.
Rosa is challenged to a street bout by a Carrano boy.

FX16-007.name: House Fosco
FX16-007.title: Master of the Fosco Ship-Brokers
FX16-007.arms: a black ship with a broken mast, on gold
FX16-007.power: A ship-broking bench in the harbour, a dozen old captains' loyalty, and the memory of a seat on the Twelve held for 304 years.
FX16-007.history: The Fosco were one of the twelve houses that paid Lucan the Grey in 758 and swore the Charter of the Twelve. They were shippers on the Neck road trade for three centuries. In 1062 the Neck road closed in the Tessarian civil war, the house could not pay its bills, and the Twelve gave its seat to the dyers of House Pell, who owed House Lunetti 30,000 suns. The Fosco have broked other men's ships ever since. They hate the Pells for the seat and the Lunettis for giving it away. In 1105 the head has joined Adriano Carrano's creditors, and a Fosco grandson works as a clerk in the Pell dye-houses.
FX16-007.reputation: Proud bankrupts with old manners; the harbour likes them, the Exchange pities them.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Ship-Brokers
members.note: He was twenty-five when his father's bench was broken and has waited forty-three years.

members.role: Heiress; ship-broker
members.note: She makes the bench pay and thinks her father's revenge will ruin them twice.

members.role: Grandson; clerk in the Pell dye-houses
members.note: He has copied the guild's 1083 pay books, which show the dyers were paid in debased coin on purpose.

members.role: Ottone's sister
members.note: She kept the family chapel's seat-cushion from the Twelve's chamber and sits on it every Sunday.

famousDead: One of the twelve who paid Lucan the Grey in 758.
Head of the house when its seat was taken; died the year it fell.
FX16-007.secret: A Fosco grandson holds copies of the Dyers' Guild pay books proving the 1083 debasement was deliberate.
hooks: The pay books could fire the Sabena Commons before the Purple Fair.
Carrano promises the Fosco a seat if Lunetti falls.
Aurelia is offered a Pell marriage to end the feud.

FX16-008.name: House Orsatti
FX16-008.title: Master of the Orsatti Bench
FX16-008.arms: a silver bear holding a gold coin, on purple
FX16-008.power: One of the 24 benches of the Exchange Hall, about 300,000 suns in coin and loans, and the loans of the Temple Party's lords.
FX16-008.history: Andrea Orsatti took one of the first benches of the Exchange Hall in 849, beside Benedetto Lunetti. His heirs never stood for the first seat and never failed, which in Ostra is a kind of glory. The Orsatti bench lends to Temple estates, to Varennan barons and to pilgrims' inns, at modest interest and long terms. Since 1084 it has lent Queen Livia's officers small sums against the Temple's word. The house is the money behind Luminary Paolo Treve's Temple Party, and in 1105 it fears that a quiet partition of the Neck would leave its Livian paper worthless.
FX16-008.reputation: Old, steady, dull and devout; the bench that never broke.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Orsatti Bench
members.note: He has heard of the Neck drafts from Luminary Treve and is quietly calling in his Livian loans.

members.role: Heiress; banker
members.note: She was Beatrice Lunetti's schoolmate at the Ledger School and envies her memory more than her wealth.

members.role: Son; factor at Solenne
members.note: He handles the Temple Treasury's small accounts and likes Treasurer Dorn's clerks.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She was tested for the Lunetti memory at five as a joke, and passed a little too well.

famousDead: Took one of the first benches of the Exchange Hall in 849.
FX16-008.secret: The Orsatti grandmother was a Lunetti ward who left the house under the Ledger Contract, and her great-granddaughter may have the memory.
hooks: Calling in the Livian loans warns the market that something is up.
House Lunetti claims young Lucia under the Ledger Contract.
Fausto is asked to carry Temple gold to Tessar.

FX16-009.name: the Rocchetti family
FX16-009.title: Master of the Alum Warehouses
FX16-009.arms: a white crystal mountain on red
FX16-009.power: The import of almost all the alum the murex dyers need to fix their colour, warehouses at Miressa and Felena, and contracts with Qadiri mine-owners.
FX16-009.history: Purple does not hold without alum, and Ostra has none of its own. In 912, two years after Ubaldo Pell set the Felena vats to one recipe, a Miressa shipper named Lapo Rocchetti signed a contract with a Qadiri mine-owner for all his alum. The family has sold alum to the dyers since, and the Pells have tried three times to break their hold. Every dyer in Ostra pays the Rocchetti before he pays himself. In 1083 the family raised its price in the same month the Leontine crashed, and some in Sabena blame them for the riots as much as the guild. In 1105 the head has quietly stopped one shipment, to see what the Pells will offer.
FX16-009.reputation: The dyers' bitter necessity; every vat on the Murex Shore is a little bit Rocchetti.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Alum Warehouses
members.note: He has held back one alum cargo at Novice to make Oddo Pell come to him.

members.role: Heiress; factor at Qadira
members.note: She speaks Qadiri and has been offered the mine-owner's son.

members.role: Son; warehouse master at Miressa
members.note: He beats warehouse men who steal alum and sells what he takes from them.

members.role: Mother of the house
members.note: She gave the dyers' burial club its first purse in 1084, before Mora Purplehand made it the Commons.

famousDead: Signed the first Qadiri alum contract in 912.
FX16-009.secret: The mother of the house still gives money to the Sabena Commons, which her husband would see as treason to trade.
hooks: The withheld alum cargo stops the Felena vats before the Purple Fair.
Ilaria's Qadiri marriage would bind the alum for a generation.
The Commons name the Rocchetti alongside the guild.

FX16-010.name: the Murici of Miressa
FX16-010.title: Head-Diver of the Miressa Beds
FX16-010.arms: a purple murex shell on white; painted on their boats
FX16-010.power: The diving rights of the Miressa murex beds, about 300 divers and gatherers, and the guild's need for every shell they bring up.
FX16-010.history: The murex shells for Ostra's purple come up from the sea floor off Felena and Miressa, gathered by divers who hold their breath for the length of a prayer. The Murici have led the Miressa divers since Ubaldo Pell joined the dye sheds under one guild in 910. The Pells pay by the basket. In 1083 the guild paid them in Leontines that lost half their worth that autumn, while selling the cloth for Ostran suns, and two Murici divers drowned going down in winter to make up the shortfall. The family joined the Sabena Commons the next year. In 1105 the head-diver's daughter carries messages between Miressa and Mora Purplehand.
FX16-010.reputation: Purple-handed, deep-lunged and poor; the dye towns say a Murici can stay under longer than a fish.

members.role: Head of the family; Head-Diver of the Miressa Beds
members.note: His lungs are going and he will not stop diving.

members.role: Daughter; runner for the Sabena Commons
members.note: Her two brothers drowned in the winter of 1083 and she has sworn the guild will pay.

members.role: Son; diver
members.note: He wants only to dive, marry and be left alone.

members.role: Mother of the house; gatherer
members.note: She sorts the shells on the beach by colour and can tell a good catch by smell.

famousDead: Divers who drowned in the winter of 1083 trying to make up their debased pay.
FX16-010.secret: The divers have hidden a store of raw murex shells to sell to dyers outside the guild, which the Pells would call theft.
hooks: Tessa carries the Commons' march orders to Miressa.
The Pells cut the basket price again.
A stranger asks to buy shells outside the guild.

FX16-011.name: the Saggiatori family
FX16-011.title: Master Assayer of the Exchange
FX16-011.arms: a gold balance over a black touchstone, on silver
FX16-011.power: The assaying of coin and bullion for the Exchange, the touchstones and scales of the assay-house, and the trust of every bench.
FX16-011.history: In 1005 Emperor Nikandros cut the silver in the Leontine by a quarter, and within a year Bernardo Carrano's weighers found it. The chief weigher was Rinaldo Saggiatori, and after that every bench in the Exchange wanted his scales. His family has assayed for the Exchange since. In 1043 a Saggiatori stood beside Isabetta Lunetti when she cut open the Tessarian gold bars and found lead, and weighed the halves for the record. The family is honest by trade and has hanged nobody. In 1105 the master has been shown a Leontine die so perfect that he could not tell it from the mint's, and he knows who cut it.
FX16-011.reputation: The Exchange's conscience; a Saggiatori stamp on a bar is worth more than the bar's own seal.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Assayer of the Exchange
members.note: He has seen Lazzaro Fenn's false Leontine die and cannot decide whether reporting it would start a war.

members.role: Heiress; assayer
members.note: She keeps the weights of the 46 lead bars in her own hand and has been asked by Carrano's lawyers to testify.

members.role: Son; the black sheep
members.note: He has been trading touchstone secrets to the Hold Bank's factor for silver.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He can already tell copper from silver by the ring.

famousDead: Chief weigher who found the debased Leontine in 1005.
Weighed the cut lead bars for Isabetta Lunetti in 1043.
FX16-011.secret: The master assayer knows a forger has cut perfect dies for Queen Livia's own Leontine and has told no one.
hooks: Carrano's lawyers call Chiara to testify about the lead bars.
Matteo is caught selling assay secrets to the Hold Bank.
A false Leontine shipment reaches the Exchange.

FX16-012.name: the Venn family
FX16-012.title: Admiral of Ostra
FX16-012.arms: a silver anchor between two gold moons, on dark blue
FX16-012.words: Paid to Sail, Proud to Return

military.office: Admirals of Ostra by contract
military.unit: 30 war galleys and 2,400 Galley Marines
military.ties: Venn admirals have commanded Ostra's galleys since the seizure of the Tessarian ships in 1044, and the marines are recruited from their own Novice coast.

FX16-012.power: The admiral's contract, the 30 galleys and 2,400 marines, and a fishing and shipbuilding town at Novice where half the men have rowed for a Venn.
FX16-012.history: Ostra had galleys before 1044 but no admiral it trusted. When Isabetta Lunetti called in the Tessarian loans, she gave the galleys to Corrado Venn, a Novice shipmaster, to seize the Tessarian ships in the harbour, and he took eleven of them without loss. The Twelve made the post his by contract, and Venns have held it since. They patrolled the coast through the Corsair War without ever fighting Blackreef, because Ostra's doctrine is never to fight when it can pay. The present admiral knows that some of the night chests that come into the harbour carry the dragon-toll money, and he has been told by the First Banker not to know.
FX16-012.reputation: Competent sailors in a city that would rather not use them; the marines love them, the Exchange counts their cost.

members.role: Head of the family; Admiral of Ostra
members.note: He has orders to keep the galleys in harbour all of 1105 and sails them out once a month to keep the rowers' arms.

members.role: Heir; captain of the galley Lunetti's Moon
members.note: He wants to command the fleet for the fourth gold expedition up the Tirana.

members.role: Daughter; shipwright at Novice
members.note: She builds the galleys and wants to build one fast enough to catch a Blackreef raider.

members.role: Bartolo's brother; marine captain; the black sheep
members.note: He lets the half-orc smugglers land the night chests past the chain for a fee.

famousDead: Took eleven Tessarian ships in Ostra harbour in 1044.
FX16-012.secret: The admiral's brother is paid to let the dragon-toll night chests land past the harbour chain.
hooks: Corrado wants the gold expedition fleet.
Nino is seen at a night landing.
Varenna asks Ostra for galleys against Blackreef.

FX16-013.name: the Ferrante family
FX16-013.title: Master of the Ferrante Ships
FX16-013.arms: a black iron anchor-ring on red, two silver waves
FX16-013.power: About 20 ships out of Sabena, warehouses on the Sabena quays, and the First Banker's late wife's blood in the Keeper of the Ledgers.
FX16-013.history: The Ferrante have shipped out of Sabena since Ilaria the Ledger married a Sabena ship-master who took her name, and the Ferrante, his cousins, got the Lunetti cargoes. In 1077 Cosimo Lunetti married Isotta Ferrante, and their daughter Beatrice is the Keeper of the Ledgers. Isotta died in 1085, and the Ferrante have been Lunetti kin without Lunetti love since. They are a Sabena house: their dockers live in the streets that rioted in 1083 and march with the Commons. In 1105 the head is caught between his granddaughter's house on Ledger Street and his own dockers at the Purple Fair.
FX16-013.reputation: Sabena's richest shippers and its least trusted; the dockers call them half-Lunetti, the Exchange calls them half-Sabena.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Ferrante Ships
members.note: He is Beatrice Lunetti's grandfather and has never once been invited to Ledger Street for supper.

members.role: Heir; Isotta's brother
members.note: He has taken Adriano Carrano's money for the Commons' cudgels and told himself it was a loan.

members.role: Rinaldo's wife; dockmaster
members.note: She runs the Ferrante quays and marched with the dyers' widows in 1083.

members.role: Rinaldo's son
members.note: He adores his cousin Beatrice and writes to her every week.

famousDead: Wife of Cosimo Lunetti and mother of Beatrice.
FX16-013.secret: The heir has passed Carrano's money to the Sabena Commons for the cudgels of the Purple Fair march.
hooks: Beatrice Lunetti learns her uncle pays for the march.
The Ferrante dockers strike on the eve of the Purple Fair.
Bastian is used to carry a message onto Ledger Street.

FX16-014.name: the Libranti family
FX16-014.title: Reader of the Fled Debtors
FX16-014.arms: a black open book on silver, a red seal upon it
FX16-014.power: The notary's register of bills of exchange in the Exchange Hall, the list of fled debtors, and the duty of reading it in every church on New Year's Day.
FX16-014.history: When the Exchange Hall opened in 849, the Charter of the Exchange required every bill and every bankruptcy to be written in a register, and Corrado Libranti was its first notary. His family has kept the register since. On New Year's Day a Libranti reads the names of fled debtors in the city's churches, so that no one may lend to them or shelter them. They read Guido Carrano's bench into the register in 1047 and Adriano Carrano into the Debtors' Tower in 1084. The family knows who owes what in Ostra better than anyone but the Lunettis. In 1105 the reader has been bribed to leave one name off the list, and has.
FX16-014.reputation: The most feared voice in Ostra on New Year's Day; the rest of the year, quiet clerks.

members.role: Head of the family; Reader of the Fled Debtors
members.note: He has read the list in every church for thirty-one years and never left a name off until this one.

members.role: Heiress; keeper of the register
members.note: She noticed the missing name and has not asked her father why.

members.role: Son; notary to the Purple Company
members.note: He wrote the note that pledged the Purple Company's contract to the Hold Bank.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She practises reading the debtors' list in a booming voice.

famousDead: First notary of the Exchange register in 849.
FX16-014.secret: The Reader left the name of a fled debtor off the New Year's list for a bribe; the debtor is a Ferrante cousin hiding with the Commons.
hooks: Teodora corrects the register and the missing name is read late.
Leandro knows exactly what the Hold Bank holds on the Purple Company.
A debtor begs to be read off the list.

FX16-015.name: the Segugi family
FX16-015.title: Master of the Debt-Hounds of Sabena
FX16-015.arms: a black hound running on purple, a silver chain in its jaws
FX16-015.power: A kennel of tracking hounds, twenty hunters, and the banks' commissions for every fled debtor brought back to Ostra.
FX16-015.history: After Ilaria the Ledger's will of 911 bound her house to forget nothing, the banks wanted men who would bring back the debtors who ran. In 912 the Sabena huntsman Bruno Segugi began to hire out himself and his hounds to the benches, and his family has hunted men for the banks since. A Segugi brought back a Carrano clerk from Madara in 1084 and a Varennan baron's son from the Crown foothills in 1099. Their hounds are famous; their manners are not. They work beside the great Debt-Hound Lupo Varga and envy him. In 1105 the Lunettis have hired them to watch the roads out of Sabena before the Purple Fair.
FX16-015.reputation: Hated in Sabena, feared on every road; nobody runs from an Ostran debt with a Segugi on his scent.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Debt-Hounds
members.note: He has brought back 140 debtors and remembers every one of their faces.

members.role: Heiress; kennel-master
members.note: She breeds the hounds and lets a debtor go if he has children with him.

members.role: Son; hunter
members.note: He wants to steal Lupo Varga's Madara commission and has gone east without leave.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She names every puppy after a debtor her grandfather caught.

famousDead: Sabena huntsman who first hired his hounds to the benches.
FX16-015.secret: The kennel-master has let at least a dozen debtors with children escape and reported the trail cold.
hooks: Remo turns up in Madara where Jory Flint is kept.
The Lunettis order the Segugi to watch the Commons' leaders.
A fled debtor's child asks Orsola for help.

FX16-016.name: the Ambessi family
FX16-016.title: Warden of the Sun Temple of Ambessa
FX16-016.arms: a gold sun with twelve rays on dark blue, a white tower beneath
FX16-016.power: The wardenship of the Sun Temple of Ambessa, the stewardship of the Temple's farms on the Ostran coast, and the rents that go to Solenne.
FX16-016.history: When Ostra bought its freedom in 758, the Temple kept every acre it had bought in the Schism Tax years, a sixth of the city's farmland. In 760 the See named the Ambessi, a family of lay clerks at the Sun Temple of Ambessa, to steward those farms and send the rents home. They have done so since. Ambessi sons become priests and Ambessi daughters sun-sisters, and the house is the Temple's eyes in the countryside as Luminary Treve is its voice on Tower Hill. The Twelve tolerate them because the rents are banked with House Lunetti. In 1105 the warden has been told by Treve to count every Temple farm in case the See needs to sell them.
FX16-016.reputation: The Temple's land-agents; country folk find them fair, the bankers find them in the way.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Sun Temple of Ambessa
members.note: He has been ordered to count farms the See may sell, and fears it means the Livian war is lost.

members.role: Daughter; sun-sister of the Ambessa hospital
members.note: She nursed the dyers in 1083 and still sends medicine to Sabena.

members.role: Heir; rent-steward
members.note: He wants to buy the best Temple farms himself if they are sold.

members.role: Son; priest at Novice
members.note: He reads the fled debtors' list at Novice church each New Year's Day and hates doing it.

famousDead: Named steward of the Temple's Ostran farms in 760.
FX16-016.secret: The heir is borrowing from House Orsatti to buy the Temple's best farms in secret if the See sells them.
hooks: The See orders the Ostran farms valued for sale.
Clara's medicine for Sabena is used to hide letters.
Tenants hear their farms may be sold to bankers.

FX16-017.name: the Gravesca kin
FX16-017.title: Mother of the Gravesca Paths
FX16-017.arms: a purple handprint on a grey stone; their sign
FX16-017.power: Mule paths through the Gravesca hills to the Holy See, sixty mules, safe barns in the hill villages, and a market for stolen purple in Solenne.
FX16-017.history: Only the Twelve and Temple envoys may wear Ostran purple, and the purple tax pays half the city. Purple stolen from the Felena and Miressa vats is worth its weight in silver in Solenne, where priests' tailors ask no questions. When the Fosco ships stopped in 1062, some of their out-of-work drivers took to the Gravesca hills with mules and stolen cloth, and a Miressa widow named Ornella organised them. Her family runs the paths still. They carry stolen purple and untaxed Isle wine west and bring back Temple salt and forged pilgrim badges. In 1105 they also carry raw murex shells from the Miressa divers to dyers outside the guild.
FX16-017.reputation: Hill smugglers with purple hands; the dye towns shelter them, the guild hangs them when it can.

members.role: Head of the family; Mother of the Gravesca Paths
members.note: She knows every hill shepherd by name and pays each of them a cheese a month.

members.role: Her son; mule-master
members.note: He has outrun the Calora Lances three times on paths their horses cannot climb.

members.role: Her daughter; fence in Solenne
members.note: She sells purple to the tailors who dress the Luminaries, and one of them is a candidate for the chair.

members.role: Grandson; mule boy
members.note: He found a dead Lunetti courier on a hill path in December and kept the satchel.

famousDead: Fosco carter who took the first stolen purple over the Gravesca hills.
FX16-017.secret: A Gravesca boy holds the satchel of a Lunetti courier found dead on a hill path in December.
hooks: The dead courier's satchel holds a letter about the Neck talks.
The Pells send men into the hills after the shell trade.
A Luminary's purple robe is traced back to the Gravesca paths.

FX17-001.name: House Lutfi
FX17-001.title: Lord of the Hazifa Hills
FX17-001.arms: a white bull on green hills, under a blue water-jar

military.office: Lords of the Hazifa levy
military.unit: about 3,500 Hazifa levy spears and 200 horse
military.ties: The Lutfi raise the largest levy of the eastern hills and have sent a son to the Guard of the Water Jar in every generation.

FX17-001.power: The cattle and hay country of the Hazifa hills, about 60 villages, a seat in the Divan and the hay contracts of the Emirs' Horse.
FX17-001.history: Sultan Idris I gave the Hazifa hills to his cousin's steward Lutf in 838, when the eastern hill chiefs submitted, and the Lutfi have grazed cattle there since. They are the richest lords of the east and the dullest, and they like it that way. They sat out the war of 1020–1025 by sending hay instead of men, which the West March has never forgiven. In the Divan the present lord sits with the Sea Traders, because a war on Sabra would take his sons and his hay. His mother was a Zahiri cousin of Yasesh, and he is the Sultan's second cousin, which makes him useful to everyone and trusted by no one.
FX17-001.reputation: Rich, slow, sensible cattle lords; the Bahesh Party calls them the hay-sellers.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Hazifa Hills
members.note: Votes for peace in the Divan and sells hay to whoever wins.

members.role: His wife, of the Cousins of Yasesh
members.note: Visits the Sultan's sickroom weekly and reports to Grand Vizier Omar what she sees.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Guard of the Water Jar
members.note: Serves under Crown Prince Samir and has seen the prince wince when he thinks no one is looking.

members.role: Second son
members.note: Has joined the Bahesh Party against his father and drinks with Nabil Tarsi's officers.

famousDead: Received the Hazifa hills from Idris I in 838.
FX17-001.secret: Ziyad knows Crown Prince Samir has the stones, and Rawiya has already told the Grand Vizier.
hooks: Hisham rides west to join the Sabun column without his father's leave.
The Admiral demands 2,000 loads of hay for the fleet's march.
Rawiya is asked by the Crown Prince's men what she tells the Vizier.

FX17-002.name: House Jebeli
FX17-002.title: Chief of the Tabir Valleys
FX17-002.arms: a grey mountain with a white sling-stone above it, on red

military.office: Hereditary captains of the Sunwall hill javelins
military.unit: about 600 Sunwall hill javelins and slingers of the Tabir valleys
military.ties: The Jebeli lead the hill javelins and slingers of the Sunwall valleys, and no Qadiri column has crossed their passes without a Jebeli guide.

FX17-002.power: Goat terraces and copper diggings in three high valleys under Fort Tabir, and the loyalty of the hill clans who sling stones better than any crossbowman.
FX17-002.history: The Jebeli are the oldest family in this book: hill chiefs of the Sunwall who fought beside Prince Idris against the Solen from 258 to 262 and submitted with him at Qadira. They say they never truly surrendered and kept their slings. Their men fought in the Sabun Pass beside Hazir's Riders in 593, and the emirs and sultans have left them their valleys in return for their javelins. Fort Tabir was built on their land in the Solen chain of fourteen forts, and the family has held its outer walls under every master since. They are poor, proud and illiterate by choice, and they despise the coast men who read.
FX17-002.reputation: Wild hill chiefs with the oldest name in Qadir, brave and quick to take offense.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of the Tabir Valleys
members.note: Can knock a hawk from the air with a sling and cannot read his own grant.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Keeps the goats, the copper tally and the peace between her husband and everyone else.

members.role: Heir; captain of the hill javelins
members.note: Knows the wyvern cliffs of the Sabun and has guided the Wardens twice.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Ran away to a well-school in Qadira to learn to read; her father has not decided whether to bring her back or be proud.

famousDead: Hill chief who fought the Solen beside Prince Idris until 262.
Guided the Sultan's army through the Sunwall in the Salt War years.
FX17-002.secret: The Jebeli have dug copper in their valleys for a century without paying the Sultan's share, and sell it to Clan Sulaya.
hooks: A Qasimi mine-captain finds the Jebeli diggings.
Najma refuses to come home from the well-school.
The Admiral's Sabun column needs Jebeli guides through the wyvern cliffs.

FX17-003.name: House Najmi
FX17-003.title: Warden of the Crown Gardens of Yasesh
FX17-003.arms: a gold star above a green date palm, on white
FX17-003.words: We count the stars and the dates.
FX17-003.power: Wardenship of the crown's date and barley gardens east of Qadira, a share of the winter grain that feeds the city, and the gardens' water-books.
FX17-003.history: Najm the Star-Counter was the astronomer who told Samir I when to sow, and in 815 the new Sultan made him warden of the crown gardens of Yasesh. His line has run them since, under the eye of the Zahiri cousins of Yasesh, who own them. The Najmi set the sowing and harvest days, keep the water-books of the gardens and send barley to Qadira in winter. They have married Zahiri cousins twice and are counted almost kin. In the Hungry Year of 1088, when Tamari wheat failed, the Najmi gardens fed Qadira through the spring, and the warden of the day was given a gold cup by Zahir III. The present warden is careful with the water and careless with his sons.
FX17-003.reputation: Learned garden-wardens, half court astronomers, half farmers, close to the royal cousins.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Crown Gardens
members.note: Has kept a record of every star-rising over Yasesh since 1068.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the water-books
members.note: Has found that the Admiral's shipyards draw garden water the books do not show.

members.role: Son; officer of the fleet
members.note: Joined the new fleet against his father's wishes and serves on a green-timber galley.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Plays the lute in the harbor houses and has fallen in with a Sabran broker's daughter.

famousDead: Astronomer of Samir I; first warden of the Yasesh gardens.
FX17-003.secret: Idris passes the dates of fleet water-loading at Yasesh to a Sabran broker's daughter, thinking it is pillow talk.
hooks: Rashad's galley is one of the twelve that leak.
Asila's water-books reach the Keeper of the Purse.
Rafiq the Quiet's men start watching the Najmi house.

FX17-004.name: House Nahiri
FX17-004.title: Lord of Lost Basir (signs as Lord of the Bahesh Fields)
FX17-004.arms: a black river-line under a red sword, on white
FX17-004.words: We will drink the Bahesh again.

military.office: Captains of the West March levy
military.unit: about 500 West March levy spears and 60 horse
military.ties: Nahiri sons ride in the Emirs' Horse under the Tarsi, and the family has lost a man in every fight with Sabra since 1022.

FX17-004.power: A few hundred acres of goat and gum land at Ashah, a levy of exiles' sons, and a deed to Bahesh fields Sabra has held for 80 years.
FX17-004.history: Nahir, a captain under Ghazi Tarsi, took the Bahesh mouth in 848 and received irrigated fields beside the Tarsi on the lower Bahesh. The house lived well for 175 years. In 1024 the Hazimi changed sides and let Sabran riders into the Basir fields, and the Nahiri lost their land and their eldest son in the same week. They followed Anas Tarsi to the West March in 1025 and live now on poor land at Ashah, keeping their deeds in a cedar box. They hate House Hazimi above Sabra itself. Every Nahiri boy swears at twelve, as the Tarsi do, to sign no title but the one they lost.
FX17-004.reputation: Bitter exiles who talk about Basir at every meal and fight like men with nothing to lose.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Lost Basir
members.note: Has borrowed 3,000 suns from the Water Endowment against the Basir fields, as his lord did.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Sells gum to Sabran brokers through a Yasiri boatman and keeps the family alive on it.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Emirs' Horse at Mirad
members.note: Wants to be first through the Sabun Pass and first into the Basir fields.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Was promised to a Tarsi cousin and is in love with a Lutfi son of the peace party.

famousDead: Took the Bahesh mouth with Ghazi Tarsi in 848.
Eldest son; killed defending the Basir date gardens.
FX17-004.secret: Hanan's gum trade is with Sabra itself, through a Hazimi broker, the house her husband hates most.
hooks: Kamal is offered the van of the Sabun column.
Lina elopes with Hisham Lutfi.
The Endowment calls in the Basir loan if the war is declared against the Book.

FX17-005.name: House Qasrani
FX17-005.title: Lord of the Upper Saman Races
FX17-005.arms: a white water-wheel on blue, a bend of silver
FX17-005.power: The first water rights of the upper Saman streams, which every mill below must buy from them in the dry months, and a fortified house above the valley.
FX17-005.history: The Qasrani built the stone races of the upper Saman for Sultan Zahir the Thirstless and received first water there in 812, long before there was paper. When the mills came about 880, every mill family found it had to buy summer water from the Qasrani. The family has been fighting the mill families ever since, in the Well-Keepers' courts, at the races with knives, and once, in 1047, with a dam that the Keepers ordered torn down. The Saman's water rights are the most fought-over in the realm, and most of the cases have a Qasrani name on them. The present lord is a lawyer by temper, and his daughter is said to have the best water-law in Qadir after the Keeper himself.
FX17-005.reputation: Rich, litigious water-lords; the mill families call them the leeches of the Saman.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Upper Saman Races
members.note: Has 14 cases before the Well-Keepers and has won 11.

members.role: Heir; water-lawyer
members.note: Studied under a Keeper of the House of Water and argues against her own father when he is wrong.

members.role: Son; race-master
members.note: Cut a mill-boy at the races in 1103 and paid the blood-price in water.

members.role: The lord's sister; widow of a mill master
members.note: Married into the Kutubi mill family and has never been trusted by either side.

famousDead: Built the upper Saman races for Zahir the Thirstless.
FX17-005.secret: Suad Qasrani has learned the pulp-making from her late husband's mill and has told her brother everything; the Qasrani could build a mill of their own.
hooks: The summer water price for the mills is due, and Hakim doubles it.
Tahira is asked to judge a case against her own family.
The Master of Doors learns that a non-mill family knows the craft.

FX17-006.name: House Karami
FX17-006.title: Lord of the Olive Terraces of the Basim Road
FX17-006.arms: a silver olive branch on copper red
FX17-006.words: Oil for the lamp, copper for the pan.

military.office: Captains of the Basim mule-train guard
military.unit: the Karami mule-guard, 120 crossbowmen with the Qasimi copper trains
military.ties: Karami crossbowmen guard the Qasimi copper trains from Basim to the coast and over the Sabun Pass.

FX17-006.power: Olive terraces and two presses on the Basim road, and the guard-contract of the Qasimi mule trains.
FX17-006.history: Karam was a mule-driver of the Basim mines who saved a copper train from Sunwall bandits in 902, and the Qasimi emirs gave his son a terrace and a press. The Karami have pressed oil and guarded copper ever since, and their crossbowmen walk beside every Qasimi mule train. Since 1088 those trains have gone over the Sabun Pass to Sabran brokers, and since 1101 Nabil Tarsi has taken one load in ten to let them pass. The Karami know what the trains carry, and since 1102 they have also known about the sealed letters the mule-drivers carry for a Sabran broker. They are copper men and peace men, and they have chosen not to ask.
FX17-006.reputation: Dependable caravan guards and olive-pressers, close-mouthed about their masters' business.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Olive Terraces
members.note: Has walked the Sabun road 60 times and knows every Tarsi toll-man by name.

members.role: His wife; mistress of the presses
members.note: Sells oil to the House of Water for its lamps and hears the Keepers' gossip.

members.role: Heir; captain of the mule-guard
members.note: Opened one of the sealed letters in 1104, read a nurse's report on the Sultan's health, and resealed it badly.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Wants to be a well-house healer and practices on the mules.

famousDead: Saved a Qasimi copper train from bandits in 902.
FX17-006.secret: Amin Karami has read one of the Sultan's nurse's reports going to Sabra and knows Sabra has a spy in the sickroom.
hooks: The Sabran broker notices his seal was broken.
Amin must decide whether to take what he knows to Rafiq the Quiet.
Nabil Tarsi demands two loads in ten.

FX17-007.name: House Zuhri
FX17-007.title: Keeper of the Nahin Cisterns
FX17-007.arms: a blue water-drop in a white cistern-arch, on black

military.office: Keepers of the Sabun road cisterns
military.unit: about 150 cistern guards of the Nahin road
military.ties: The Zuhri keep the walled cisterns that water every column going up to the Sabun Pass Fort.

FX17-007.power: Four walled cisterns on the road to the Sabun Pass and the right to water or refuse every caravan and column.
FX17-007.history: Jalal II walled the cisterns of the Sabun road after the disaster of 1022, when Qadiri soldiers died of thirst in the pass, and in 1033 he gave them to Zuhr, a cistern-mason who had survived the march down on stolen water. The family has kept them since and guards them with the fierceness of men who remember thirst. Every column for the Sabun Pass Fort waters at a Zuhri cistern. The Book forbids refusing water to the thirsty, but it says nothing about the price of storing it, and the Zuhri charge caravans for 'keeping'. Since 1095 Sabran caravans coming the other way have paid well and asked no questions.
FX17-007.reputation: Hard cistern-keepers who never refuse a drink and never forget a debt.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Nahin Cisterns
members.note: Has the cistern levels of the last 30 summers in his head.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Charges Sabran caravans for 'keeping' and lets them water at night.

members.role: Son; cistern guard
members.note: Wants to serve with the Wardens of the Sabun at the pass fort.

famousDead: Survived the Sabun march of 1022 and walled the road's cisterns for Jalal II.
FX17-007.secret: Dunya waters Sabran caravans at night for silver, and one of them carried Sabran scouts in 1104.
hooks: The Sabun column will need every drop of the four cisterns in April.
A Sabran caravan-master asks Dunya for the cistern levels.
A cistern is found fouled, and the Book says the man who did it dies.

FX17-008.name: House Saqri
FX17-008.title: Captain of the Jar Gate
FX17-008.arms: a white hawk on a green water-jar, on gold

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Jar Gate in the Guard of the Water Jar
military.unit: the Jar Gate company of the Guard of the Water Jar, 200 heavy foot
military.ties: A Saqri rode with Zahir the Thirstless across the Burning Waste in 790, and a Saqri has guarded the Sultan's door ever since.

FX17-008.power: The captaincy of the palace gate company, a house by the Jar Palace and the Sultan's trust.
FX17-008.history: Saqr was one of the 600 camel riders who crossed the Burning Waste with Zahir the Thirstless in January 790, and one of the few who lived to tell it. Zahir made him keeper of his door, and the Saqri have commanded the gate company of the Guard of the Water Jar since. They have stood at the door of fourteen sultans and seen most of them die of the stones. In 973, when the Keepers unmade Idris II's galley law, the Saqri captain refused the Sultan's order to close the House of Water, and Idris thanked him for it later. The present captain stands every night outside the room where Zahir IV lies sick.
FX17-008.reputation: The Sultan's doorkeepers, incorruptible and slightly frightening.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Jar Gate
members.note: Tastes the Sultan's water himself, distrusting the horn cup.

members.role: Heir; lieutenant of the Jar Gate
members.note: Guards the Crown Prince and has sworn to say nothing of what he sees.

members.role: Jamil's wife; of a nurse's family
members.note: Is friendly with the Sultan's nurse Dalia and has told her more than she should about the night watches.

members.role: Jamil's son; page in the Guard
members.note: Runs messages between the sickroom and the Divan.

famousDead: Crossed the Burning Waste with Zahir in 790.
Refused Idris II's order to close the House of Water in 973.
FX17-008.secret: The family has a letter of Saqr of the Crossing that says the guide of 790 was a Sandfolk rider who was paid, not a sign of the Giver.
hooks: Thabit finds the nurse Dalia at the door at an hour she should not be.
The Crown Prince asks Jamil to fetch a stone-cutter in secret.
The founder's letter is stolen from the family chest.

FX17-009.name: House Haddadi
FX17-009.title: Sergeant of the Pass Fort Cistern
FX17-009.arms: a black anvil under a white crossbow, on grey

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Wardens of the Sabun
military.unit: a company of the Wardens of the Sabun at the Sabun Pass Fort, about 100 spears and crossbows
military.ties: Haddadi men have kept the walled cistern of the Sabun Pass Fort since it was built and serve as smiths and sergeants of the Wardens.
