FX17-009.power: The smithy and the cistern-keys of the Sabun Pass Fort, and four generations of sergeants in the Wardens.
FX17-009.history: The first Haddadi was a smith of the column ambushed in the Sabun Pass in October 1022, who walked down the mountain behind Prince Jalal and buried two brothers on the way. When Jalal II built the Sabun Pass Fort around its walled cistern at 2,598 metres, he made the smith keeper of its forge and its cistern-keys. His sons and grandsons have served in the Wardens of the Sabun since, mending crossbows, shoeing mules and guarding the water. They serve the Tarsi now, and they know Nabil Tarsi's mule-tenth from the Qasimi copper trains goes through their gate. They are the sort of men who will hold a fort to the last because they know what thirst is.
FX17-009.reputation: Grim, steady pass soldiers whom every Warden trusts with his life and his water.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Pass Fort Cistern
members.note: Has wintered at 2,600 metres for 30 years and says the cold is kinder than the coast.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the fort's stores
members.note: Counts every water-skin in the fort and knows exactly how many days 1,000 men can last.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Wardens
members.note: Fought off a wyvern on the cliffs in 1103 and wears its claw.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Works the bellows and has made her own small crossbow.

famousDead: Survived the Sabun ambush of 1022; first keeper of the pass fort forge.
FX17-009.secret: Rashad keeps a private tally of Nabil Tarsi's unreported mule-tenth, in case the Warden ever turns on his men.
hooks: The column of 1105 asks the pass fort for more water than it holds.
A Qasimi mule-driver offers Rashad money to forget a train.
Hamid is chosen to scout the Sabran side of the pass.

FX17-010.name: House Ramli
FX17-010.title: Captain of the Miruma Marines
FX17-010.arms: a red boarding-axe over a blue wave, on white

military.office: Hereditary marine captains of the Sea Keep Marines at Miruma
military.unit: the Miruma half of the Sea Keep Marines, 1,200 marines
military.ties: Ramli sons are trained at the School of the Sea Keep and have fought on every Qadiri galley since the first fleet of Jalal I.

FX17-010.power: A marine captaincy at Miruma, a house by the galley slips and the loyalty of men who learned to fight from Ramli fathers.
FX17-010.history: A Ramli marine sailed in Jalal I's first fleet of twenty galleys, and the family has served the galleys since. Six Ramli drowned with Jalal I off Miruma in 874. In August 1024 the head of the house burned with his galley under the harbor towers of Sabra, and his son swam ashore into a Sabran prison and was sent home in 1025 without his hands' skin. The family has carried the memory of the Night of Fire for 80 years and wants to go back. The present captain trains marines at Miruma under Faris Bahri's school; neither man has ever seen fire-oil burn. His grandmother has, and she says not to go.
FX17-010.reputation: Hard-drinking, hard-fighting marine captains who mean to burn Sabra and fear fire at sea in their dreams.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Miruma Marines
members.note: Has trained 3,000 marines to board and none to fight fire.

members.role: His grandmother
members.note: Saw the galleys burn from a Sabran prison window in 1024 and dressed her husband's burned hands.

members.role: Heir; lieutenant of marines
members.note: Has been picked for the first galley through the Strait if the fleet sails.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Experiments with wet hides and vinegar against fire in the slipway sheds.

famousDead: Burned with his galley on the Night of Fire.
Swam ashore in 1024, was held in Sabra and came home scarred.
FX17-010.secret: Widad Ramli knows the burning stuff of 1024 was boiled oil; she saw the jars, and nobody in the family has ever asked her.
hooks: Hala's fire-screens are tested on a leaking galley.
Widad asks to see the Admiral before the fleet sails.
Nizar's galley is one of the twelve of green timber.

FX17-011.name: House Talawi
FX17-011.title: Castellan of Faluz Tower and Watch-Captain of the East Shore
FX17-011.arms: a white tower with a flame on top, on dark blue

military.office: Castellans of Faluz Tower and captains of the East Shore watch
military.unit: Faluz Tower garrison and the East Shore coast watch, about 400 men and nine beacon towers
military.ties: The Talawi keep the beacon chain of the East Shore and report every Yasiri boat to the Master of Doors.

FX17-011.power: Faluz Tower, the nine beacons of the East Shore, the customs of Yasir and the right to stop any boat between Qadir and the Sand Clan harbors.
FX17-011.history: After Qadiri galleys sank a Blackreef toll boat off the East Shore in 1056, Sultan Samir III built a chain of beacons along the coast and gave Faluz Tower to Tamim Talawi, the galley captain who had done it. The Talawi have watched the East Shore since. Their real enemy is not Blackreef but the Sand Clan smugglers of Yasira and Janiya, who carry dates, paper and people past Qadir's customs. Every month the Talawi seize a Yasiri boat, and every month two more get through. In October 1104 the castellan's own beacon was dark on the night a smuggler carried two runaway paper journeymen east; he says the oil ran out.
FX17-011.reputation: Zealous coast-watchers with a habit of missing the boats that matter.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Faluz Tower
members.note: His beacon was dark on the October night of 1104, and he has blamed a dead lamp-boy.

members.role: His wife; customs-keeper of Yasir
members.note: Has seized 40 Yasiri boats and released none, which makes her the most hated woman on the East Shore.

members.role: Heir; captain of the beacon chain
members.note: Believes his father's story about the lamp-boy.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Meets a Yasiri fisherman's son on the beach below the tower.

famousDead: Sank the Blackreef toll boat off the East Shore in 1056.
FX17-011.secret: Nabil Talawi is paid by Clan Yasiri to keep certain beacons dark, the same arrangement the pilots of Miruma have.
hooks: Rafiq the Quiet's agent asks why the beacon was dark in October.
Zahra seizes a boat carrying a Sand Clan chief's son.
Nisrin is caught on the beach with a smuggler's boy.

FX17-012.name: House Jamali
FX17-012.title: Master of the West March Caravans
FX17-012.arms: a gold camel on red under a white star
FX17-012.power: Camel trains, warehouses at Ashah and Mirad, and old friendships with the brokers of Sabra and the Gold Houses of Zanara.
FX17-012.history: The Jamali grew rich on the Gold Road after the Salt and Gold Pact of 918, carrying Zanari gold from the Bahesh mouth over the Sabun Pass to Qadira. The loss of Sabra in 1025 broke their road, and they moved to Ashah with the West March exiles. For 80 years they have kept trading with Sabra anyway, through Sand Clan guides and over the Sabun Pass, because a caravan merchant must. Their camels carry Qadiri paper and copper south and Sabran dates and Zanari gold north. They lend to the Tarsi, buy from the Hazimi and are cursed by both. A war on Sabra would end them, and they know it.
FX17-012.reputation: Merchants who trade with the enemy and lend to the patriots, and survive both.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the West March Caravans
members.note: Has lent Emir Bashir 6,000 suns and sold Faisal the Broker 6,000 suns of paper the same year.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the sealed notes
members.note: Moves silver by the Endowment's inn-notes and never carries a coin.

members.role: Heir; caravan-master
members.note: Has crossed the Red Waste five times with Adib guides and speaks Sandfolk.

members.role: Daughter; married into a Sabran broker family
members.note: Lives in Sabra and writes home in a code her mother taught her.

famousDead: Founded the house on the Gold Road after 918.
FX17-012.secret: Jumana Jamali's letters home carry Sabran news to the Master of Doors, and Sabran news to her mother's friends in the Divan, at two prices.
hooks: The war closes the Sabun road and a Jamali caravan is trapped in Sabra.
Faisal the Broker asks Jumana to carry a message north.
Bashir Tarsi cannot repay the 6,000 suns.

FX17-013.name: House Kutubi
FX17-013.title: Master of the Kutubi Mill
FX17-013.arms: a white sheet hanging from a black wire screen, on sky blue
FX17-013.power: One of the 32 paper mills on the Saman streams, a watermark of their own and a vote in the Guild of the Mills.
FX17-013.history: The Kutubi were neighbors of the Warraqi on the Saman streams and among the first mill families given the charter of Sultan Rashad about 884. Like every mill family they married cousins and kept the craft inside, and they wear the master's brass stamp on a cord. They have always come second to the Warraqi in the guild and minded it. In the Hungry Year of 1088 they bought Tamari rags cheaply through Rasha the Ragwoman and grew rich enough to want the Master's chair. Since the two Warraqi journeymen vanished in September 1104, the Kutubi have quietly told the other mill families that Hamid the Papermaker cannot keep his own house in order.
FX17-013.reputation: Second family of the mills, skilled, cousin-married and hungry for the first place.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Kutubi Mill
members.note: Shares a name and a street with Hamid the Papermaker and has hated him for both since boyhood.

members.role: His wife and cousin
members.note: Sorts rags by feel faster than any woman on the Saman.

members.role: Heir; vat-master
members.note: Was a friend of the vanished journeymen and has kept a letter Adil left for him.

members.role: Second son; journeyman
members.note: Owes money in the harbor and has been approached by a Lucernan in a blue coat.

famousDead: One of the first mill masters under Rashad's charter.
Died of the Harbor Pox at the mill.
FX17-013.secret: Badr Kutubi has sold the Lucernan a description of the wire screens, and the Master of Doors does not yet know it.
hooks: Yusuf's letter from Adil says where the journeymen meant to go.
Rafiq the Quiet questions every mill journeyman with debts.
The guild votes on a new Master if Hamid the Papermaker falls.

FX17-014.name: House Mirahi
FX17-014.title: Harbor-Pilot of Miruma
FX17-014.arms: a white lantern on a black chain, over a blue wave
FX17-014.words: We know where the rocks are.
FX17-014.power: A seat in the Brotherhood of Pilots of Miruma, the right to bring ships into Miruma harbor, and the harbor lamps.
FX17-014.history: The Mirahi say their ancestors were among the fishermen who chained sixty boats across the harbor mouth of Qadira every night in the siege of 601–604. A Mirahi boat was in the chain on the last night, and the family took the pilot's oath at Miruma in 603. They have brought ships into Miruma ever since and kept its lamps. Mirahi pilots took the first Qadiri galleys out in 860 and watched six of them sink in 874. They sit in the Brotherhood of Pilots under Salim the Pilot and are his rivals for its mastership. Since 1101 they have been paid by Clan Yasiri to keep the harbor lamps dark on certain nights.
FX17-014.reputation: Old pilot family, proud of their oath and a little too fond of Yasiri silver.

members.role: Head of the family; Harbor-Pilot of Miruma
members.note: Can bring a galley into Miruma on a moonless night by the sound of the surf.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the harbor lamps
members.note: Decides which lamps go dark and takes the Yasiri silver herself.

members.role: Heir; pilot of the war fleet
members.note: Pilots the Admiral's flagship and does not know what his mother does at night.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Swims out to the moored galleys at night and has counted the leaking ones.

famousDead: Held a boat in the harbor chain of Qadira in 604.
FX17-014.secret: Rihab Mirahi keeps Miruma's lamps dark for Yasiri smugglers, and in December 1104 two Yasiri boats lent to Sabra scouted the harbor under that darkness.
hooks: Wasim must pilot the fleet out of a harbor his mother has sold.
Manar tells a stranger which galleys leak.
Salim the Pilot wants the Mirahi out of the Brotherhood.

FX17-015.name: House Abadi
FX17-015.title: Stone-Cutter to the Sultan
FX17-015.arms: a silver knife over a blue water-jar, on white
FX17-015.power: The hereditary office of physician and stone-cutter to the house of Zahiri, a well-house hospital by Qadira and a library of medical books on Qadiri paper.
FX17-015.history: Abad the Physician cut a stone from Samir I in 836 and the Sultan lived two more years; Idris I made the office hereditary in 838. Since then the Abadi have attended every Zahiri sultan, and they know the Thirstless blood better than anyone: it kills with the stones, most often in the fifties. They cut the stone of Rashad the Papermaker, who lived to 59 and did not carry the blood, and they failed with Zahir III in 1092. The family keeps a book of every Zahiri stone since 815, which is the most dangerous book in Qadira. Zahir IV has refused the knife since November and drinks from his horn cup instead.
FX17-015.reputation: The Sultan's physicians, learned and grave, who know things about the royal house nobody else does.

members.role: Head of the family; Stone-Cutter to the Sultan
members.note: Has asked the Sultan eleven times to let him cut, and been refused eleven times.

members.role: Heir; physician of the well-house hospital
members.note: Has examined the Crown Prince in secret and knows he has the stones.

members.role: Son; physician to the fleet
members.note: Has seen the burns on old marines and thinks the fleet is sailing to its death.

members.role: Hadiya's daughter
members.note: Reads the stone-book when nobody is looking.

famousDead: Cut a stone from Samir I in 836; first hereditary stone-cutter.
FX17-015.secret: The Abadi stone-book records every Zahiri sultan's stones and shows the Crown Prince is following his grandfather's course; Hadiya has promised the prince to say nothing.
hooks: The Sultan finally asks for the knife.
Grand Vizier Omar asks to see the stone-book.
The nurse Dalia asks Hadiya how long the Sultan has.

FX17-016.name: House Tamimi
FX17-016.title: Master of the Hazifa Studs
FX17-016.arms: a black horse's head on gold

military.office: Remount-masters of the Emirs' Horse
military.unit: the Hazifa studs, about 900 horses
military.ties: Tamimi horses mount most of the Emirs' Horse, and Tamimi grooms ride with it as farriers and scouts.

FX17-016.power: The studs of the Hazifa hills, hay rights from the Lutfi and the remount contracts of the Emirs' Horse.
FX17-016.history: Tamim the Horse-Trader came from the Holy Coast with northern mares in 931 and crossed them with Sunwall hill stock on Lutfi pasture. His line has bred horses for the emirs' cavalry since, and about 4,000 horses in the realm owe something to Tamimi stock. They serve the Lutfi and sell to everyone: the Guard of the Water Jar, the Tarsi, and quietly the Sabran Camel Guard, which wants horses for its officers. The family is horse-mad and quarrelsome, and its two branches have not spoken since a stallion was sold twice in 1089. Since 1100 they have also bought Tamari remounts under false brands, cheaply, from a breeder at Rashira.
FX17-016.reputation: The best horse-breeders on the coast, quarrelsome among themselves and willing to sell to anyone.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Hazifa Studs
members.note: Has not spoken to his brother since 1089 over a stallion called Long-Night.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Sells horses to Sabran officers through a Jamali caravan.

members.role: Bashir's brother; head of the rival branch
members.note: Swears Long-Night was his and wants the debt settled with a race or a knife.

members.role: Layla's son
members.note: Rides Long-Night's grandson, which both branches claim.

famousDead: Brought northern mares to Hazifa in 931.
FX17-016.secret: Layla Tamimi sells horses to the Sabran Camel Guard, which is trading with the enemy of the realm.
hooks: The Emirs' Horse needs 400 remounts by April.
The two Tamimi branches agree to settle the Long-Night quarrel by a race on Well Day.
A Sabran officer comes to Hazifa in person to collect his horses.

FX17-017.name: House Hilmi
FX17-017.title: Well-Keeper of Hazifa and Judge of the House of Water
FX17-017.arms: a black book open over a blue well, on white
FX17-017.power: A judgeship in the House of Water, the well-school and court of Hazifa, and a voice among the forty judges.
FX17-017.history: The Hilmi have sent Well-Keepers to the courts of Qadir since 652, when Hilm the Water-Judge settled a war over a Sunwall spring by the sayings of Samar. They have held one of the forty judgeships of the House of Water more often than not. In 973 a Hilmi judge voted against Idris II with Zaki Alami; in 1025 another voted for the Peace of the Bahesh. The present judge has broken with the Keeper: he holds that a war to take back the believers of Sabra from an Emir who sells fire to pirates is a just war, and he leads the judges who would vote for it. He and Yusuf Alami were boys together in the same well-school.
FX17-017.reputation: Learned, stubborn judges, honest by long habit, now split against the Keeper's own party.

members.role: Head of the family; Well-Keeper of Hazifa, Judge of the House of Water
members.note: Leads the judges who would let the Admiral's war stand on Well Day.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the Hazifa well-school
members.note: Teaches 200 girls to read and disagrees with her father in front of all of them.

members.role: Son; Well-Keeper at the Sea Keep
members.note: Hears the confessions of galley captains and knows which ships leak.

members.role: Inas's son
members.note: Can already recite the Book's water sayings by heart.

famousDead: Settled the Sunwall spring war in 652 by the sayings of Samar.
FX17-017.secret: Kamal Hilmi has taken 4,000 suns from the Bahesh Party to rebuild the Hazifa well-school, which a judge may not do.
hooks: The vote of the forty judges on Well Day may turn on one Hilmi.
Inas learns where the well-school money came from.
Thabit is asked by a frightened captain to hear a confession about green timber.

FX17-018.name: the Fadli of the Rag Market
FX17-018.title: Hook-Master of the South Gate Heaps
FX17-018.arms: a bent iron rag-hook (scratched on the walls of the heaps they hold)
FX17-018.words: Rags are paper, water is gold.
FX17-018.power: Three refuse heaps outside the south gate of Qadira, about 30 rag-pickers with hooks and knives, and a secret tap into a Saman water-race.
FX17-018.history: The Fadli were rag-pickers of Qadira's south gate when the Harbor Pox of 1076–1078 killed the gang that held the best heaps, and Fadl the Hook took them with his sons and a borrowed knife. Since then the family has held three heaps and fought the Sieve's people for the rest. Rags are paper, and the mills buy every scrap by weight. The Fadli have a second trade that could hang them: since 1095 they have tapped a Saman race under the Rag Market and sold the water to gardeners by night. Water theft is common in Qadir; fouling a cistern is death, and one of their taps runs dangerously close to one.
FX17-018.reputation: Knife-quick rag gang of the south gate, rivals of the Sieve and cheap water-sellers to the poor.

members.role: Head of the family; Hook-Master of the South Gate
members.note: Took the heaps with a borrowed knife in 1077 and has never given back the knife.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the water-tap
members.note: Sells stolen Saman water to gardeners at half the endowment price.

members.role: Son; knife of the gang
members.note: Cut one of the Sieve's people in December, and Samira has sworn he will not see Well Day.

members.role: Nadira's daughter
members.note: Learned to read from torn pages in the rag bales.

famousDead: Took the south gate heaps in the Harbor Pox years.
FX17-018.secret: The Fadli knew that the Sieve hid two mill journeymen in rag bales in September 1104, and are waiting for the best buyer for that knowledge.
hooks: Rafiq the Quiet offers the Fadli the Sieve's heaps for a name.
The water-tap seeps into a cistern, and a Well-Keeper comes asking.
Ziyad's feud with the Sieve's people turns into a war of knives in the Rag Market.

FX18-001.name: House Horeni
FX18-001.title: Overseer of the Canal of Akayn
FX18-001.arms: a gold sluice-gate over two wavy blue bars, on green
FX18-001.words: Water where the king wills it.
FX18-001.power: The headgates and sluice-books of the Canal of Akayn, which water about 40,000 acres, and a fee of one sheaf in thirty from every canal field.
FX18-001.history: Horen the Leveler laid out the canal of Akayn for Teti the Canal-Digger in 771, and the king gave his family the headgates to keep forever. For three centuries the Horeni have opened and shut the sluices by the height on their own small gauge-stair at the canal mouth, and Akayn's 40,000 acres drink when they say so. In 942 they kept the canal running for the Tessarian Exarch rather than see Akayn starve, and in the famine of 974 Akayn ate while the city nome buried its dead; the Talim priests have called them the Exarch's ditch-men ever since. In the Hungry Year of 1088 the canal ran dry for the first time in living memory, and Nakhtmose Horeni broke his own headgate to let the last of the river into the fields. Since 1098 he has written to the Vizier every spring that Abaran channels upriver are stealing the Mother's water.
FX18-001.reputation: Careful water-lords whom the farmers of Akayn trust and the Talim priests despise as collaborators.

members.role: Head of the family; Overseer of the Canal of Akayn
members.note: Broke his own headgate in 1088 and has walked with a stick since the timber fell on his leg.

members.role: Heir; Keeper of the gauge-stair
members.note: Copies every gauge reading twice, and one copy goes somewhere he will not name.

members.role: Nakhtmose's daughter; wife of a Delta Wells broker of Marira
members.note: Took the Path of the Well when she married in 1099, and her father has not said her name aloud since.

members.role: Youngest son; page in the Vizier's household
members.note: Sent to Seti the Scribe's house to learn letters and to listen.

famousDead: Laid out the canal of Akayn for Teti the Canal-Digger.
Kept the canal running for the Exarch and fed Akayn through the famine of 974.
FX18-001.secret: The Horeni gauge-stair at the canal mouth read the 1089 flood a hand and a half below 'fair', and Hornefer still keeps the reading.
hooks: The headgate of Akayn needs 8,000 suns of new stone before the flood of 1105.
Hornefer's hidden gauge copy could bring down a king if it reached the Talim priests.
Takhat asks her younger brother to carry a Delta Wells petition into the Vizier's house.

FX18-002.name: House Nebari
FX18-002.title: Lord of the Natron Weigh-House of Rashira
FX18-002.arms: a white natron sack between two red towers, on black

military.office: Captains of the Rashira posts of the Kadari Rift Guard
military.unit: the Nebari company of the Rift Guard, 300 spears and archers on the natron road
military.ties: Every Nebari son serves at least three years in the Rift Guard under a Kadari captain, and two have died on the natron road.

FX18-002.power: The natron weigh-house of Rashira, where every sack from the Burning Waste is weighed and taxed, and the terraced fields around it.
FX18-002.history: The Nebari were potters of Kadah until April 985, when Tessarian hired soldiers burned the town and Nebet the Potter carried three children out through the drains. Amenhar I rebuilt Kadah and in 991 gave her son the natron weigh-house of Rashira as reward for the family's dead. The house has served House Kadari ever since and keeps a burnt pot from the old workshop above its door. The natron comes across the Burning Waste with Tamira guides, and the Nebari know every Tamira caravan-master by name. They hate Tessaria as only Kadah families do, and they cheered when Rahotep Kadari was made General of the River.
FX18-002.reputation: Hard, honest weighers who would rather break a scale than cheat on it, and who never forget a Tessarian face.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Natron Weigh-House
members.note: Keeps a tally of the Kadah dead on the weigh-house wall and adds the name of every Tessarian he hears has died.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the weigh-books
members.note: Runs the weigh-house in fact and lends the Tamira guides water-skins on credit.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Rift Guard
members.note: Rode with Rahotep's men against grain thieves in 1088 and still dreams of the broken dykes.

members.role: Second son
members.note: Wants to cross the Burning Waste with the Tamira and see the old wells their guides whisper about.

famousDead: Carried three children out of burning Kadah through the drains in 985.
FX18-002.secret: Nebet the Potter's second husband, father of the line, was a Tessarian deserter who hid in her kiln during the massacre; the family has buried that for a century.
hooks: A Tamira guide offers to take Iymer across the Burning Waste for a share in the weigh-house.
The Yeori have moved a boundary stone on the upper terraces after the flood, and Wennakht wants the law's hundred blows.
A Tessarian letter-carrier stops at the weigh-house on the way to Kadah.

FX18-003.name: House Talimi
FX18-003.title: Lord of the Temple Fields of Talim
FX18-003.arms: a black key under a white ibis feather, on blue-green
FX18-003.words: The door was opened from inside.

military.office: Holders of the Talim temple-guard's river gate
military.unit: about 80 temple guards of the Talim river stair
military.ties: A Talimi has held the keys of the temple fort's river gate since the night of the rising in 981.

FX18-003.power: Leases of the Senmut temple estates in the Upper Nome and the keys of the river gate of the temple fort of Talim.
FX18-003.history: On a night of August 981 Senbi Talimi, a gate-keeper of the Talim temple, unbarred the river gate and let the rebels in to kill the Tessarian garrison of 400. The Senmut priests rewarded the family with leases of temple fields when Amenhar I was crowned in 989, and the Talimi have farmed for the priests and held their keys ever since. They have been servants of House Senmut for four generations, and their sons marry temple singers and scribes' daughters. They watched the Tamar temple win back the High Flood-Priesthood about 1030 and have hated the Measurers since. In 1074 Tessarian raiders burned two Talimi villages below Talim, and the family still pays a widow's bread to every house that lost a man.
FX18-003.reputation: The Senmut priests' faithful doorkeepers, proud, pious and a little too fond of reminding the king who let his ancestor in.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Temple Fields
members.note: Wears the iron key of 981 on a cord and has never let a Tamar priest touch it.

members.role: Heir; steward of the temple leases
members.note: Keeps the leases straight and her father's temper away from the Senmut.

members.role: Second son; temple scribe at Tamar
members.note: Copies tax rolls in the Measurers' archive and has quietly sold Menna's watch-captain the names of Talim's letter-carriers.

members.role: Iymerit's daughter
members.note: Sings in the temple choir and plays with the old mason's grandchildren in the temple yard.

famousDead: Unbarred the river gate of the Talim temple fort in 981.
FX18-003.secret: Djedhor, the second son, is the Measurers' informer inside the Talim household.
hooks: The dying mason at Talim lodges in a Talimi house, and someone has asked who visits him.
Iymerit suspects her brother and must decide whether to tell the Senmut.
A Tamar priest demands the key of 981 be given up to the crown's temple.

FX18-004.name: House Khaiyi
FX18-004.title: Lord of the Wells of Khaiyah
FX18-004.arms: a green date palm over a stone well-mouth, on sand-gold
FX18-004.power: The date gardens and deep wells of Khaiyah, the market where desert caravans meet the river, and the guest-house of the Tamira guides.
FX18-004.history: The Khaiyi have held the wells and date gardens of Khaiyah since Kheti II gave them to a royal cupbearer in 704. Khaiyah is where the desert touches the river, and the house has always lived by its guests: natron caravans, Sand Clan guides and, since 983, the Tamira riders who fought for Tamar at Lake Nubako and water their camels here free. The Khaiyi house chapel keeps a shelf of Old Kingdom clay tablets dug out of their own deepest well in 1031, listing wells 'cut by the masons of the king' on a road into the Waste. Nobody at Khaiyah could read them until the scholar Merit the Star-Reader passed through in 1102. The family has kept her reading to itself.
FX18-004.reputation: Generous hosts of the desert road, too friendly with Sandfolk for the taste of the Tamar temple.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Wells of Khaiyah
members.note: Speaks Sandfolk better than any lord in Tamar and owes his life to a Tamira guide.

members.role: His wife; mistress of the guest-house
members.note: Knows which caravan-master is lying before he has finished his water.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Has been promised to a Moyari son and is in love with a Tamira guide's younger brother.

members.role: Son; keeper of the chapel tablets
members.note: Has copied the well-road tablets onto papyrus and hides the copy in a water-jar.

famousDead: Dug the deepest Khaiyah well and found the Old Kingdom tablets in 1031.
FX18-004.secret: The chapel tablets name a road of Old Kingdom wells into the Red Waste, and the last of them sits where the Well of Samar is now; the Khaiyi know it was Tamari masons, not the Giver, who first cut it.
hooks: A Qadiri Well-Keeper arrives at Khaiyah asking to see the chapel.
Hormerit runs off with a Tamira caravan on the eve of her betrothal.
The Tamira chief asks the Khaiyi to stand guarantor for 40 natron loads.

FX18-005.name: House Moyari
FX18-005.title: Lord of the Granary Fields of the City Nome
FX18-005.arms: a gold wheat sheaf on a white granary dome, on blue-green
FX18-005.power: Crown fields on the east bank above Tamar, the tenancy of six royal granary domes and the ear of Princess Tiye, Overseer of the Granaries.
FX18-005.history: Moyar the Granary-Keeper counted the royal domes for Nebhet II, and in 893 the king gave his son crown fields above Tamar to feed them. The house kept the domes under the Tessarians, which the Senmut never forgave, and handed back every sack to Amenhar I in 989, which the crown never forgot. Since then a Moyari has kept the tallies of six of the great domes beside the Flood Walls. In the Hungry Year of 1088 Hapet Moyari opened two domes to the crowd at the north gate a day before the order came, and was fined and quietly thanked. In 1103 Princess Tiye sold a month's grain in secret to pay the Lucernan interest, and the Moyari tallies were the ones changed to hide it.
FX18-005.reputation: Prosperous, discreet granary lords who always seem to know the bread price a week early.

members.role: Head of the family; widow of the old lord
members.note: Opened the domes to a starving crowd in 1088 and has kept the city's goodwill since.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the dome tallies
members.note: Changed the tallies in 1103 at Princess Tiye's word and now sleeps badly.

members.role: Pahor's son; promised to Hormerit Khaiyi
members.note: Wants a commission in the King's Horse, not a desert bride.

members.role: Pahor's sister; married to a Lucernan grain factor
members.note: Lives in Well Lane among the factors and tells her brother which way Lucerna will jump.

famousDead: Counted the royal domes for Nebhet II and founded the house.
FX18-005.secret: The Moyari tallies for 1103 hide a month's grain sold to Lucerna; the domes hold three months' bread, not four.
hooks: A tally-clerk of the Granary Mice offers Pahor the true count of the domes for a price.
Rahor breaks his betrothal to Hormerit Khaiyi and starts a quarrel between two houses.
Princess Tiye asks the Moyari to change the tallies a second time.

FX18-006.name: House Yeori
FX18-006.title: Lord of the Flax Terraces of Rashira
FX18-006.arms: a blue flax flower on white linen, a chevron of brown
FX18-006.power: Irrigated flax terraces on the Rashira shoulder, retting pools, and contracts to sell raw flax to the weavers of Tamar.
FX18-006.history: When Emperor Theodoric gave Rashira back to Tamar in 664, the family of a Solen-era terrace-builder swore to Queen Nefira and kept its fields; Kheti I made them lords of the flax terraces in 668. The Yeori have grown flax for Tamari linen for four centuries, and their thread goes to the looms of Nofret the Weaver. Since the Rag Compact of 1091 even their old linen sells to Qadir, and the house has grown richer than its rank. It is a quarrelsome family: in 1088, as the river fell, a Yeori steward moved a boundary stone against the Nebari terraces, and the case has been in the Vizier's courts for sixteen years. The head of the house, a widower, has married his heir to a weaver's daughter for money, which the old lords of Rashira count a disgrace.
FX18-006.reputation: New-rich flax lords with old blood, litigious and clever with a contract.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Flax Terraces
members.note: Has spent 600 suns on lawyers to keep a boundary stone his steward moved.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Married a weaver's daughter for her dowry and has come to love her, to his own surprise.

members.role: Nebnefer's wife, of the weavers' guild
members.note: Sits on the Rag Compact's tally bench and knows exactly how many shrouds of the Hungry Year went to Qadir.

members.role: The head's younger brother
members.note: Owes 300 suns to a beer-house on the Boatmen's Quay and has pledged a terrace he does not own.

famousDead: Brought blue flax seed from the delta and doubled the house's yield.
FX18-006.secret: The Yeori steward moved the boundary stone on Iymer's order, and the old steward is still alive.
hooks: Khamer's creditor arrives to claim a terrace.
The Vizier's court calls the old steward to swear on the stone.
Sitmut is asked to falsify the Rag Compact tallies.

FX18-007.name: House Djedari
FX18-007.title: Steward of the Temple Fields of Akayn
FX18-007.arms: a black measuring rod across a gold sun, on red
FX18-007.power: Stewardship of the Flood Temple's estates around Akayn: rents, tenants and a share of every temple harvest.
FX18-007.history: The Djedari have managed the Flood Temple's lands at Akayn since 755, when a Measurer's younger son married into a family of land-scribes. They collect the temple rent after the flood-priests set the grain tax, and they have done it for every master: the Old temple, the Tessarian Exarch's clerks in 943 and the Measurers again since 1030. They are the Measurers' kin and their right hand in the canal country, and the Horeni across the canal call them 'the rod-men'. In 1089, when the priests cut the grain tax by a third to hide the poor harvest, the Djedari went on collecting the temple's rent at the full rate from their tenants. The difference, about 9,000 suns over three years, is in their own vaults.
FX18-007.reputation: Stiff temple stewards who measure everything, trusted by the Stair and hated by their tenants.

members.role: Head of the family; Steward of the Temple Fields of Akayn
members.note: Cousin of Menna the Measurer and never lets anyone forget it.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the rent-rolls
members.note: Found the double rent in her father's books last winter and has not decided what to do.

members.role: Second son; reader at the Flood Stairs
members.note: Trained as a stair-reader under Menna and believes every mark on the Stairs is holy.

members.role: Tamut's daughter
members.note: Plays with tenants' children, which her grandfather has forbidden.

famousDead: Married the Measurer's son into the family and made the stewardship hereditary.
FX18-007.secret: Since 1089 the Djedari have taken the temple rent at the full rate and pocketed the third the priests forgave, about 9,000 suns.
hooks: A tenant brings a Delta Wells preacher to read out the Djedari rent-book in the market.
Tamut must choose between her father and the Measurers' auditors.
Nebankh is chosen to re-plaster the Flood Stairs before the 1105 reading.

FX18-008.name: House Mutari
FX18-008.title: Lord of the Neck Villages below Talim
FX18-008.arms: a red spear-head over a burning village, on grey
FX18-008.words: We were here when they came.

military.office: Village captains of the Talim March
military.unit: the Mutari village spears, about 250 levy men and a beacon tower
military.ties: The Mutari hold the first beacon on the Neck road, and their levy is the first to answer when the Talim March calls.

FX18-008.power: Twelve poor villages on the Neck border below Talim, a beacon tower and a levy that has fought Tessarian raiders three times in living memory.
FX18-008.history: Amenhar I gave the border villages below Talim to Mutar, a rebel captain of 981, on the day he was crowned. The land is poor, the river narrow and the Neck road close, and the family has never been rich. In September 1074 about 600 Tessarian raiders burned five Mutari villages, killed the old lord at his beacon and carried off his wife; the Sons of the Mother caught them at the river, and Intef the Shield won his name that day. The present lord was 21 and buried his father with his own hands. The Mutari serve under the Warden of the Talim March and have never asked for more land, only for more spears.
FX18-008.reputation: Poor, brave border lords whom the Talim March counts on and the Tamar court forgets.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Neck Villages
members.note: Buried his father at the beacon in 1074 and has never learned what became of his mother.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the beacon
members.note: Lit the beacon herself in 1091 when a Tessarian patrol crossed, and was right.

members.role: Heir; file-leader in the Talim March
members.note: Wants to cross the Neck and take back his grandmother's bones.

members.role: Nakht's half-sister, born in Tessaria
members.note: Came back across the Neck in 1092 claiming to be the stolen lady's daughter; half the family believes her.

famousDead: Rebel captain of 981, first lord of the Neck villages.
Killed at his beacon by Tessarian raiders.
FX18-008.secret: Menet is not the stolen lady's daughter but a Tessarian claimant's spy; the old lady died in 1075, and Menet knows where she is buried.
hooks: Hornakht leads ten men across the Neck at night.
A letter in Tessarian hand reaches Menet at the beacon.
The Warden of the March asks the Mutari for 100 spears for a war the king has not declared.

FX18-009.name: House Nubari
FX18-009.title: Lord of the Night Bank
FX18-009.arms: a silver moon over a black pyramid, on deep blue
FX18-009.power: The west bank of Tamar: the cemetery land, the tomb-builders' village, the ground rents of every embalmer's house and the tomb-guards.
FX18-009.history: Menkar II gave the west bank of Tamar to his tomb-overseer Nubar in 830, and since then every tomb cut on the Night Bank pays the Nubari a ground rent. The house keeps the tomb-guards, licenses the embalmers' houses and sells plots above the flood line to anyone who can pay. Under the Tessarians the Exarch let the Nubari keep their rents in return for 'old ornaments', and the house sold him the grave goods of three Tamaren queens to save its land; the stripped tombs were sealed again in 989 and nobody has opened them since. Tomb robbers caught on the Night Bank are drowned, and the Nubari judge them. The family lives on the dead and dresses like the living rich.
FX18-009.reputation: Rich, gloomy landlords of the dead, polite to everyone and trusted by no one.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Night Bank
members.note: Has sat in judgment on 41 tomb robbers and drowned 38.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Wants a seat in the royal household and courts Queen Nefret's ladies with gifts of old jewelry.

members.role: Second son; captain of the tomb-guards
members.note: Takes a share from the Painters' night diggings and drowns their rivals.

members.role: Youngest daughter
members.note: Born in the Hungry Year and raised among the embalmers' children; she can wrap a body faster than her father can count the fee.

famousDead: Overseer of royal tombs, granted the Night Bank in 830.
FX18-009.secret: In 948 the Nubari sold the grave goods of three Tamaren queens to the Exarch; the sealed tombs are empty, and Nebet's 'old jewelry' comes from the last of what was kept back.
hooks: A Lucernan collector offers 2,000 suns for a queen's collar that should be in a sealed tomb.
Hori's arrangement with the Painters goes wrong and a guard is found in the river.
The king orders the tomb of Queen Wenet opened for a royal burial.

FX18-010.name: House Menkari
FX18-010.title: Lord of the Salt Marsh of Halifa
FX18-010.arms: a gold crown on a green reed bed, on white
FX18-010.power: Salt pans and reed marshes on the delta coast by Fort Halifa, a fishing village, and an old claim of blood nobody can prove or disprove.
FX18-010.history: The Menkari hold the salt marsh east of Marira and say they descend from House Sethepi, the old delta kings, through a daughter who married a marsh-lord about 860. Khaset III granted them the marsh in 870, and they have boiled salt and cut reeds there ever since. The claim was harmless while the Tamaren line was secure. Since 1101, when the king's first son died of the blood sickness and left one half-blind boy as heir, people in the delta have begun to say the Menkari name in a new tone. The present head is an old man who laughs at the talk; his grandson does not.
FX18-010.reputation: Poor marsh lords with a royal story, harmless to some and dangerous to others.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Salt Marsh
members.note: Tells everyone the only crown he wants is a dry roof.

members.role: His son; salt-master
members.note: Pays a Delta Wells broker in Marira for every sack and keeps out of politics.

members.role: Grandson and heir
members.note: Has had the Sethepi line painted on the hall wall and visits the Talim priests more than a salt lord should.

members.role: Ahmose's wife
members.note: Burns every letter her son receives from Talim before her husband sees it.

famousDead: First Menkari lord of the salt marsh; said to be grandson of the last Sethepi daughter.
FX18-010.secret: A Talim priest has shown Khamer a genealogy roll from the Senmut vault that makes his Sethepi descent plausible; the Senmut keep him as a spare king.
hooks: A delta crowd hails Khamer as 'Sethepi' at the Harvest of the Mother.
The Measurers send a watch-captain to the salt marsh.
Baket asks a stranger to carry Khamer away to Lucerna before he is killed.

FX18-011.name: House Sesheni
FX18-011.title: Bearer of the Sun-Boat Standard
FX18-011.arms: a gold sun-boat standard on a blue-green pole, on black
FX18-011.words: It does not touch the ground.

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of the Sun-Boat Standard of the Sons of the Mother
military.unit: the standard guard of the Sons of the Mother, 40 picked shields around the standard
military.ties: A Sesheni has carried the king's sun-boat standard before the Sons of the Mother in every fight since Return Day 989, and the family trains its boys in the House of the Shield from the age of nine.

FX18-011.power: The standard itself, which only a Sesheni may carry, a house beside the House of the Shield and a pension from the crown granaries.
FX18-011.history: On Return Day, 21 June 989, the starving Tessarian garrison marched out of Tamar, and a spearman named Seshen carried the sun-boat standard of Amenhar I through the gate ahead of the king. The king made the office hereditary that day, and the Sesheni have carried it since. The standard fell once, at the river below Talim in 1074, when its bearer was killed; his twelve-year-old son picked it up from the mud and carried it the rest of the fight beside Intef the Shield. That boy is the head of the family now. The Sesheni are poor and proud, and every son is trained in the tall shield and the spear wall by Intef's school.
FX18-011.reputation: The most honored common soldiers in Tamar, poor as spearmen and proud as princes.

members.role: Head of the family; Bearer of the Sun-Boat Standard
members.note: Picked the standard out of the mud at twelve beside his dead father and has carried it ever since.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Stitches the standard's linen every New Year and keeps the house on a spearman's pension.

members.role: Heir; shield-man in the Sons of the Mother
members.note: Born in the Hungry Year, raised on bread-tickets, and the fastest runner in the House of the Shield.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Trains with the boys at dawn before anyone can forbid it.

famousDead: Carried Amenhar I's standard through the gate of Tamar on Return Day 989.
Killed bearing the standard at the river below Talim.
FX18-011.secret: Senbi was not twelve but ten in 1074, and the man who truly lifted the standard was a Kadari captain who died a minute later; the family took the honor and the Kadari never claimed it.
hooks: Rahotep Kadari asks for the standard to march with ten galleys the king knows nothing about.
Wenet wants to carry the standard if her brother falls.
An old Kadari soldier remembers who lifted the standard in 1074.

FX18-012.name: House Tashiri
FX18-012.title: Captain of the Reed Stations of the Delta
FX18-012.arms: a white ibis pierced by a black arrow, on reed green
FX18-012.words: From the reeds, at the first light.

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Delta Reed Stations of the Ibis Archers
military.unit: the delta reed stations of the Ibis Archers, about 1,500 bows among the marshes of the Monuti mouths
military.ties: Tashiri archers have held the delta reed banks since the Solen landing of 642, and their boys learn the bow at the Reed School of Marira before they learn their letters.

FX18-012.power: Command of the delta reed stations, the reed-cutters' villages that feed them, and a seat at the Reed School of Marira.
FX18-012.history: The Tashiri say their first archer shot from the reed banks when Queen Nefira's men threw the Solen landing back at Marira in 642. A Tashiri captain led a company of the 2,000 Tamari archers who broke Maximus's line at Felano in 667, under the first Kadari lords, and came home with a captaincy for his line. The family has held the reed stations of the delta ever since, through the Tessarian years, when it hid its bows in the marsh, and the revolt, when it brought them out again. Hapu the Reed, master of the Reed School, was trained by a Tashiri, and the house sends him its best boys. The Tashiri are delta people and many of their archers keep the Path of the Well, which the Tamar temple notes and dislikes.
FX18-012.reputation: Quiet marsh soldiers, the best shots in the kingdom, suspected in Tamar of being half Delta Wells.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Reed Stations
members.note: Taught Hapu the Reed to shoot and still beats him at the long mark one year in three.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Marira station
members.note: Keeps the Path of the Well, as her mother did, and will not hide it for any priest.

members.role: Son; archer in the Ibis Archers
members.note: Rows contraband at night for Marira boatmen and thinks his father does not know.

members.role: Nakhtet's daughter
members.note: Has a child's bow cut from the same reed bed as her great-grandfather's.

famousDead: Led a company of Tamari archers at Felano in 667.
FX18-012.secret: The reed stations quietly let Delta Wells preachers and Qadiri money pass into the delta, and Nakhtet has met Faruq the Lamp.
hooks: The Measurers demand a Tashiri archer swear by the Mother before the Harvest of the Mother.
Djedi's night rowing brings a crate of Qadiri silver into the reed station.
Rahotep needs the delta archers for a war in the Neck.

FX18-013.name: House Wadjari
FX18-013.title: Master of the Dyke Corps
FX18-013.arms: a silver hammer breaking a brown dyke, on blue

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Dyke Corps ('the Dyke-Breakers')
military.unit: the Dyke Corps, 1,400 engineers at Tamar, Talim and the delta
military.ties: The Wadjari broke the dykes at Lake Nubako in 983 and again for Rahotep Kadari in 1088; the army does not fight on the river without them.

FX18-013.power: Command of the Dyke Corps, the corvée lists of the dyke work and the knowledge of every sluice and weak bank in the valley.
FX18-013.history: Wadjar the Dyke-Builder was a corvée foreman of Talim when Amenhar's rebels marched north in 983. At Lake Nubako he broke the dykes so the late flood covered the road, and 11,000 Tessarians fought in mud and lost. Amenhar I made him master of the king's dyke-builders, and the office has passed father to son ever since. Every man in Tamar owes a month of dyke work, and the Wadjari keep the lists and brand the dodgers. In the Hungry Year of 1088 Tjati Wadjari broke dykes on Rahotep's order to flood out the grain-thief camps, and drowned two villages that were not thieves. The army calls him 'the Dyke-Breaker' with respect; the villages call him worse.
FX18-013.reputation: Engineers who can drown an army or a village, respected by soldiers and feared by farmers.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Dyke Corps, called the Dyke-Breaker
members.note: Drowned two innocent villages in 1088 on Rahotep's order and pays their survivors' tax himself every year.

members.role: Heir; captain of the delta dyke company
members.note: Knows every bank between Tamar and the sea and where each one would break.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the corvée lists
members.note: Refuses to brand any man who missed his month in the Hungry Year.

members.role: Wadjmose's son
members.note: Swims the Monuti in flood on a dare, which no Wadjari is supposed to do.

famousDead: Broke the dykes at Lake Nubako in 983.
FX18-013.secret: Tjati knows Rahotep's 1088 order named the two drowned villages as Talim tenants who had refused the levy, not as thieves.
hooks: A survivor of the drowned villages comes to Tamar to kill the Dyke-Breaker.
Rahotep asks for a dyke company to sail with the galleys he has promised Prince Andros.
Nefira's soft corvée lists are reported to the Vizier.

FX18-014.name: House Desheri
FX18-014.title: Sergeant-Helmsman of the Crocodile Boats of Talim
FX18-014.arms: a green crocodile on a red boat, on sand

military.office: Hereditary sergeant-helmsmen of the Crocodile Boats
military.unit: four Crocodile Boats of the Talim squadron, about 50 marines and rowers
military.ties: Desheri men have steered the long, low marine boats of Talim since the squadron was formed, and they serve under Nakht the Oar.

FX18-014.power: Four boats, the right to choose the squadron's helmsmen, and a boat-shed on the Talim river stair.
FX18-014.history: The Crocodile Boats were formed after Amenhar I's death in 1017 from the river men who had closed the water around Tamar in 987, and the first helmsman of the Talim squadron was Desher the Fowler. His line has steered its boats ever since. They are low boats of 20 oars that hide in the reeds and strike at night, and the Desheri can bring one alongside a barge without a sound. They fought the Tessarian raiders below Talim in 1074 and are proud of it. The present head has served Nakht the Oar for twenty years and would follow him anywhere, which may soon be tested.
FX18-014.reputation: Hard river sergeants who drink, fight and never miss a night patrol.

members.role: Head of the family; sergeant-helmsman
members.note: Has steered Nakht the Oar's own boat since 1085 and carried a letter for him in December 1104 without reading it.

members.role: His wife; boat-shed keeper
members.note: Pitches every hull herself and knows which boats will not last the year.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of marines
members.note: Wrestles crocodile-hunters for beer on the Talim quay.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Was the boy who carried Nakht the Oar's bag down to the Tessarian boat in December.

famousDead: First helmsman of the Talim Crocodile Boats.
FX18-014.secret: The letter Hori carried in December 1104 went to a Tessarian boat; the Desheri are bound up in Rahotep's secret offer to Prince Andros.
hooks: A temple spy asks young Nakhtmose what was in the bag.
Nakht the Oar orders the Talim boats down to Marira without a royal seal.
A Desheri boat is found burned in the reeds.

FX18-015.name: House Shemari
FX18-015.title: Castellan of Fort Halifa
FX18-015.arms: a white castle on a red rock, over blue waves

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of Fort Halifa
military.unit: the Granary and Wall Watch garrison of Fort Halifa, about 400 spears and archers
military.ties: The Shemari have held the coast castle for the crown since Amenhar I built its walls, and their sons serve in the Granary and Wall Watch.

FX18-015.power: Fort Halifa and its cistern, the coast-road toll and the right to search every barge that passes the castle.
FX18-015.history: Amenhar I built Fort Halifa on the stony desert coast east of the delta in 995, to watch the sea road from the Neck, and gave it to Shemar, a captain of the siege of Tamar. The Shemari have held it since. The castle has seen no siege, but it has seen everything that moves on the coast road: Tessarian deserters, Delta Wells pilgrims bound for Qadir and smugglers with Qadiri paper. In 1061, when the Neck closed, the spice barges began to pass the castle and the toll doubled. The present castellan is an old soldier whose sons have taken up the toll-books with more zeal than the sword.
FX18-015.reputation: Dutiful castle-keepers grown comfortable on the coast toll.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Fort Halifa
members.note: Has walked the walls every night for 30 years and has never seen an enemy.

members.role: Heir; toll-master of the coast road
members.note: Takes a quiet tenth from the Qadiri paper smugglers and calls it a search fee.

members.role: Daughter; married to a Lucernan factor's agent
members.note: Carries the castle's news to Marira twice a month.

members.role: Ankhu's son; spearman in the Wall Watch
members.note: Wants to be a real soldier and is ashamed of his father's fees.

famousDead: Captain at the siege of Tamar; first castellan of Fort Halifa.
FX18-015.secret: Wenu lets the paper journeymen's smugglers and others pass for a tenth; in October 1104 he waved through a boat he was paid not to search.
hooks: Qadir's Master of Doors sends an agent to ask who passed Fort Halifa in October.
Shemu reports his own father to the old castellan.
A Tessarian galley is seen off the coast at dawn.

FX18-016.name: House Pernakhti
FX18-016.title: Warden of the Talim March
FX18-016.arms: a black wolf on a white border-stone, on blue-green

military.office: Wardens of the Talim March
military.unit: the Talim March, 5,000 spears, archers and light horse at the Fort of Talim and the Neck border
military.ties: Since 1018 the Wardens of the Talim March have come from this house more often than from any other, and every Pernakhti child is born within sound of the fort's horn.

FX18-016.power: Command of the Talim March, its fort and its border posts, and the trust of the upper-valley levy.
FX18-016.history: Pernakht was a captain of the Talim rising of 981 who held the Fort of Talim after the Peace of 989; Amenhar II made the wardenship his in 1018, and his line has held it six times in seven. The house stands between Tamar and the Neck, and it has fought Tessarian raiders, deserters and the hungry for a century. Neferhor of Talim, the present Warden, is the first woman to hold the March; her brothers died of the Hungry Year's flux, and the king gave her the March in 1090 because the soldiers would have no one else. The Pernakhti owe their rise to the Talim rising and their office to the king, and they have spent eighty years trying not to choose between the Senmut and the crown.
FX18-016.reputation: The best soldiers of the upper valley, loyal to the king and listened to in the Talim temple.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Talim March
members.note: Took the March in 1090 when her brothers died and has not lost a border post since.

members.role: Her husband; quartermaster of the March
members.note: A Talim scribe's son who keeps 5,000 men fed on barges that are always late.

members.role: Heir; captain of the March horse
members.note: Leads 200 of the King's Horse on the border and wants a war before he is thirty.

members.role: Daughter; novice of the Talim temple
members.note: Serves in the Senmut household and hears more than a novice should.

famousDead: Held the Fort of Talim after 989; first Warden of the house.
FX18-016.secret: Sitmut has told her mother that the Senmut hold proof against the king's ancestor; Neferhor has told no one and has begun to count which of her captains would follow her and not the General.
hooks: Rahotep orders the March's horse to Kadah, and Neferhor must decide whether to obey.
A Tessarian envoy crosses the Neck under truce asking for the Warden alone.
Pernakht raids across the border against orders.

FX18-017.name: House Ankhari
FX18-017.title: Factor of the Spice Barges at Khaiyah
FX18-017.arms: a red pepper-sack in a gold barge, on blue
FX18-017.words: The river carries more than grain.
FX18-017.power: Twenty spice barges, warehouses at Khaiyah and Tamar, and the trust of the Ranpuri and Keshi spice factors who pay the crown's river toll through them.
FX18-017.history: The Ankhari were barge-owners hauling dates and natron on the upper Monuti until February 1061, when the Tessarian civil war closed the Neck road and spice from the Eastern Gulf began to come up the river instead. Ankhet the Barge-Mother saw the first Keshi pepper boats tie up at Khaiyah and bought every barge she could borrow for. Within ten years the house carried a third of the spice that passed through Tamar, and the river toll on its barges paid a tenth of the crown's silver. The family has married into scribes and granary lords and is not yet noble, which it minds. If the Neck road reopens, or if Zanara's new road east reaches the Monuti, the Ankhari could lose everything in a season.
FX18-017.reputation: Quick new money of the river, generous at feasts and nervous about the future.

members.role: Head of the family; factor of the spice barges
members.note: Her mother's daughter: bought four barges on credit in the Hungry Year and paid for them in a season.

members.role: Heir; master of the Tamar warehouse
members.note: Counts every sack twice and trusts no one who arrived after 1061.

members.role: Daughter; at Marira with the Ranpuri factors
members.note: Speaks Ranpuri and has been offered marriage by a pepper factor twice her age.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Lost a full barge of cardamom at dice in 1104 and told his mother it sank.

famousDead: Bought the first barges for the spice trade in 1061.
FX18-017.secret: Hotepet has paid Tessarian agents to keep the Neck road closed since 1098.
hooks: Word comes that the Neck road may reopen in 1105.
Djedhor's cardamom barge turns up at Marira under a new name.
A Zanaran engineer asks to buy warehouse space at Khaiyah for the east road.

FX18-018.name: House Rashiri
FX18-018.title: Chief Scribe of the Corvée Rolls
FX18-018.arms: a black reed pen and a white scroll, on gold
FX18-018.power: The corvée rolls of the Vizier's office, which list every man's month of dyke work, and a school of 40 scribes' boys.
FX18-018.history: The Rashiri are royal scribes and claim the most famous marriage any scribe ever made: in 783 Ahset, daughter of King Teti's chief scribe and of this family, married the exiled Qadiri prince Zahir, and her son became Sultan Samir I. The family has served the royal pen since, and its daughters are still welcomed in Qadira as distant kin of the Zahiri. Under the Tessarians the Rashiri kept the corvée rolls in their own house and handed them to Amenhar I in 989. Seti the Scribe, Vizier of the Two Banks, learned his letters in the Rashiri school, and the family now keeps his corvée rolls. The head of the house is a mild old man; his niece runs the school and asks too many questions.
FX18-018.reputation: Learned, well-connected scribes with a Qadiri sultan in their family tree and ink on every important roll.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief Scribe of the Corvée Rolls
members.note: Taught Seti the Scribe his first letters and still corrects his grammar.

members.role: His niece; mistress of the scribes' school
members.note: Has noticed that the 1089 corvée rolls excuse half the villages of the valley for 'flood damage' in a year the priests called fair.

members.role: Djedi's son; scribe in the Qadiri trade office
members.note: Goes to Qadira twice a year and is received by the Zahiri cousins as kin.

members.role: Ipi's daughter
members.note: Reads better than boys twice her age and copies the old letters of Ahset for fun.

famousDead: Daughter of King Teti's chief scribe; married Zahir in exile and bore Sultan Samir I.
FX18-018.secret: Meritnefer Rashiri has a copy of the 1089 corvée excusals, which show the flood was low.
hooks: A Qadiri envoy asks the Rashiri to carry a private letter to the king.
Meritnefer asks a stranger to compare her rolls with a temple tax roll.
The Vizier wants the corvée rolls 'tidied' before the Harvest of the Mother.

FX18-019.name: House Senmeri
FX18-019.title: Commander of the Sea Galleys at Marira
FX18-019.arms: a blue anchor between two white oars, on sea green
FX18-019.words: The sea is wider than the river.

military.office: Commanders of the sea galleys at Marira
military.unit: Tamar's 10 sea galleys and 640 marines at Marira
military.ties: The Senmeri have commanded Tamar's few sea galleys for three generations and train their rowers with the River Marines.

FX18-019.power: Command of the ten sea galleys, a share in two grain cogs and a captain's house on the Marira harbor.
FX18-019.history: Tamar has always been a river kingdom, and its few sea galleys were built after 1017 to chase Gulf pirates from the grain lanes. Senmer the Navigator, a Marira pilot, took the first of them out in 1020, and his line has commanded them since. Paser the Helm, the present commander, has kept ten galleys afloat on a budget meant for six by hiring them out to escort Lucernan grain ships. The family sees the Middle Sea as Tamar's future and the river as its past, which makes them odd men at a river court. They are Kadari men by appointment and Marira men by blood, and they drink with the Delta Wells brokers.
FX18-019.reputation: Salt-water sailors in a river kingdom, able, unpolished and half Lucernan in their habits.

members.role: Head of the family; Commander of the Sea Galleys, called the Helm
members.note: Keeps ten galleys afloat on Lucernan escort fees the treasury pretends not to know about.

members.role: His wife; owner of two grain cogs
members.note: Carries Tamari wheat to Lucerna in her own hulls and pays the family's debts.

members.role: Heir; captain of a sea galley
members.note: Wants Tamar to build twenty galleys and fight the Blackreef toll like Qadir.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Sailed as a ship's boy in her brother's galley in 1102 with her hair cut short; the crew keeps her secret.

famousDead: First commander of Tamar's sea galleys in 1020.
FX18-019.secret: Paser's galleys escort Lucernan grain ships that carry wheat the crown has already pledged elsewhere.
hooks: Rahotep's ten promised galleys must come from somewhere, and Paser has ten.
A Blackreef toll boat demands payment from a Senmeri cog.
Hotepmut is unmasked aboard her brother's galley.

FX18-020.name: the Papyrus-Makers of the Delta
FX18-020.title: Master of the Papyrus-Makers
FX18-020.arms: a green papyrus stalk crossed with a cutting knife, on cream
FX18-020.power: The papyrus beds of the delta marshes, the drying yards, and the 2,000 sheets of the River Gift owed to Abara every year.
FX18-020.history: This family of papyrus-makers has cut the delta reeds, laid them crossways and beaten them into sheets for as long as Tamar has kept records; it took its trade name as a house name when Queen Nefira gave the papyrus beds of the delta marsh to the makers in 640. For centuries papyrus was the only writing sheet of the Southland, and Tamari kings raised its price when they pleased. Then about 880 the Qadiri began to make rag paper, and the trade has fallen ever since. Since the Rag Compact of 1091 Tamari linen rags go west to feed the Qadiri mills, and the makers call it selling the knife to the man who will cut your throat. The family still makes the 2,000 sheets of the River Gift each year and the temple's roll-papyrus, and little else.
FX18-020.reputation: Proud old craftsmen of a dying trade, bitter about Qadir and its paper.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Papyrus-Makers
members.note: Can lay a sheet so fine you can read through it, and curses Qadir before every meal.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the drying yards
members.note: Says the trade will die with her father unless they learn the Qadiri way.

members.role: Son; reed-cutter and smuggler's friend
members.note: Has heard that two Qadiri paper journeymen are hiding somewhere east of Qadir and would pay any price to bring them to the delta.

members.role: Henutnefer's daughter
members.note: Has made a sheet from old linen in a pot, by accident, and hidden it from her grandfather.

famousDead: Received the delta papyrus beds from Queen Nefira in 640.
FX18-020.secret: Henutnefer has sent a cousin to Marira to buy a Qadiri mill drawing from a Lucernan agent, and Sitnefer has already made rag paper by chance.
hooks: Nakhtmose goes looking for the runaway Qadiri journeymen at Janiya.
Abara demands the River Gift in silver, and the papyrus goes unsold.
Qadir's Master of Doors learns a Tamari family has made rag paper.

FX18-021.name: the Stair-Cutters of Tamar
FX18-021.title: Master of the Temple Masons
FX18-021.arms: a white chisel over a black stair of seven steps, on ochre
FX18-021.power: The mastership of the masons who keep the Flood Stairs, the temple walls and the Night Bank tombs in repair.
FX18-021.history: This line of masons has cut and mended the stone of the Flood Temple since the Measurers won back the High Flood-Priesthood about 1030 and wanted their own men on the Stairs. They plaster, pave, cut tomb doors and recut worn marks on the 28 steps. The masons who work on the Stairs swear an oath of silence before the High Flood-Priest, and the family's old men keep it. In the autumn of 1089 four temple masons and a boy worked one night on the Stairs; two of the masons are still alive, and one is the head of this family. He has not spoken of that night to anyone, and he receives a temple pension of 40 suns a year that no other mason gets.
FX18-021.reputation: Silent, skilled temple masons who drink alone and never talk shop.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Temple Masons
members.note: One of the two living masons of the night of 29 September 1089, and the other is dying at Talim.

members.role: Heir; stair-mason
members.note: Has noticed that one step of the Stairs is plastered thicker than the rest and has asked his father why.

members.role: Neferhotep's wife; seller of tomb plaster
members.note: Wants the temple pension doubled and has hinted as much to a temple clerk.

members.role: The boy of 1089, now a journeyman
members.note: Held the lamp that night at twelve and talks too much when he drinks on the Boatmen's Quay.

famousDead: First master of the family's temple masons.
FX18-021.secret: Hornefer helped plaster over the true flood mark of 1089 and cut the new one; his apprentice nephew Wenamun held the lamp.
hooks: Menna's watch-captain visits the family the day after Ahmose dies at Talim.
Wenamun is overheard on the Boatmen's Quay by a Delta Wells preacher.
The temple orders the Stairs re-plastered before the October reading.

FX18-022.name: House Hentari
FX18-022.title: First Singer of the Tears at Talim
FX18-022.arms: a silver harp under a blue star, on white
FX18-022.power: The singing of the Tears at the Talim temple every 15 August, a temple house and a pension as kin of the royal line.
FX18-022.history: The Hentari have sung in the Talim Flood Temple for two centuries, and they lead the Tears, the long lament sung on 15 August when the flood begins to rise. In 981 the Senmut priests proclaimed that Amenhar I was the son of a hidden prince by a temple singer of Talim, and they named the Hentari as the singer's family. The house was raised overnight: a pension, a temple house and a place at royal funerals as the king's 'mother's kin'. It has kept the honor for 124 years and four kings. The Hentari know that no daughter of theirs ever bore a prince, and they have sung the lie with the rest of the temple.
FX18-022.reputation: Honored temple singers with royal kinship, a little overdressed for priests.

members.role: Head of the family; First Singer of the Tears
members.note: Has sung the Tears for 40 years and cried at every one of them.

members.role: Her son; temple harper
members.note: Wants a seat at court as the king's kinsman and has started to believe the story.

members.role: Her daughter; singer at the royal court
members.note: Sings for Queen Nefret and is sick of lying to a woman she likes.

members.role: Rahor's son
members.note: Has found a note in the temple record that the 'royal singer' of 950 died childless.

famousDead: Named in 981 as aunt of the 'hidden singer' who bore Amenhar I.
FX18-022.secret: The Hentari never had a daughter who bore a prince; they have lived for 124 years on the Senmut forgery that made Amenhar I a king.
hooks: Ankhmeret is asked by the Queen to tell her about the singer who bore Amenhar I.
Iymer shows his grandmother the note about the childless singer.
If the Senmut fall, the Hentari fall with them.

FX18-023.name: the Crocodile-Takers of Khaiyah
FX18-023.title: Headman of the Crocodile-Takers
FX18-023.arms: a black crocodile jaw on river brown (a mark painted on their boats)
FX18-023.power: The right to hunt crocodiles on the upper Monuti, a market for hides and teeth, and the respect of every ferryman between Talim and Tamar.
FX18-023.history: The Crocodile-Takers have hunted the great crocodiles of the upper Monuti for three centuries, clearing the fords and ferry stairs for the river towns and selling hides to shield-makers. The Lords of Khaiyah gave them the hunting right in 820, and the family has served the Khaiyi since. Every adult in the family has a scar, and the head has lost two fingers. They took the beasts that ate Tessarian soldiers at the fords in 987 and are proud of it. The temple forbids killing a crocodile on a flood-day, and once in every generation a Taker breaks the rule to save a child and pays for it.
FX18-023.reputation: Scarred river hunters, fearless, poor and much in demand at every ford.

members.role: Head of the family; Headman of the Crocodile-Takers
members.note: Lost two fingers to a seven-meter beast at the Khaiyah ford and kept its skull.

members.role: His daughter; the best hide-curer on the river
members.note: Sells hides to the House of the Shield and knows Intef the Shield by name.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Killed a crocodile on a flood-day in 1103 to save a ferryman's child, and someone saw him.

members.role: Nakht's son
members.note: Has a pet baby crocodile in a jar, which is a crime of a sort nobody has named.

famousDead: Cleared the fords around Tamar in the siege of 987.
FX18-023.secret: Nakht killed a crocodile on a flood-day in 1103, which is death by temple law; the witness is a Djedari tenant.
hooks: A temple court summons Nakht for the flood-day killing.
A giant crocodile takes three men at the Talim ford, and the March wants the Takers.
A Lucernan collector wants a live crocodile for his garden.

FX18-024.name: the Painters of the Night Bank
FX18-024.title: Master of the Tomb-Painters (and of the night digging)
FX18-024.arms: a painted hand in red ochre (their mark, scratched inside the tombs they rob)
FX18-024.power: Licensed tomb-painters by day and diggers by night, with tunnels under the Night Bank, fences in Marira and a cut for the tomb-guards.
FX18-024.history: The Painters have decorated tombs on the Night Bank since the Old Kingdom, and since the Tessarian conquest of 942 they have robbed them too. In 943, when the Exarch's men stripped royal tombs for the treasury, a painter named Djedi learned which walls were hollow, and his family has dug from behind its own paintings ever since. They paint a tomb, mark a hollow wall, wait twenty years and come back. Tomb robbers caught on the Night Bank are drowned, and the family has lost a man in every generation. Since the Hungry Year of 1088 they have also worked with the Granary Mice, selling stolen grain and grave goods side by side on the Boatmen's Quay.
FX18-024.reputation: Gifted painters with a bad smell about them; everyone on the Night Bank knows and no one says.

members.role: Head of the family; master painter and master digger
members.note: Painted the tomb of Amenhar IV and knows exactly where its wall is thin.

members.role: His wife; fence in Marira
members.note: Sells old gold to Lucernan collectors as 'Solen jewelry'.

members.role: Heir; tunneler
members.note: Broke through into a queen's tomb in 1104 and found it already empty.

members.role: Daughter; apprentice painter
members.note: Paints better than her father and wants nothing to do with the night work.

famousDead: Learned in 943 which royal tomb walls were hollow.
Drowned for tomb robbery on the Night Bank.
FX18-024.secret: Hori found three royal tombs already empty in 1104: someone looted them long before the Painters, and the Nubari keep the keys.
hooks: Hori wants to sell the knowledge of the empty tombs to the highest bidder.
The Nubari tomb-guards demand a bigger cut or a drowning.
Menet is offered a royal commission that would put her in the palace.

FX18-025.name: House Iymeri
FX18-025.title: Keeper of the King's Studs at Rashira
FX18-025.arms: a white horse rearing on a red hill, on dark green
FX18-025.words: A horse in the valley is worth ten.

military.office: Remount-masters of the King's Horse
military.unit: the Rashira studs, about 600 horses and 90 grooms
military.ties: Nearly every mount of the King's Horse was foaled on Iymeri pasture, and their grooms ride as scouts with the Rift Guard.

FX18-025.power: The king's horse studs on the Rashira and Kadah pastures and the remount contracts of the King's Horse.
FX18-025.history: Tamar has always been short of horses: the valley is all field and dyke, and the old chariot horses died under Solen javelins at Kadah in 207. In 1036 Amenhar II gave the rift-shoulder pastures above Rashira to a horse-trader named Iymer who had bred desert stock with Sand Clan stallions, and asked for a royal cavalry. The family has bred the mounts of the King's Horse ever since. They buy stallions from Sandfolk breeders across the Burning Waste and are nearly as fluent in Sandfolk as in Tamari. In the Hungry Year of 1088 the army ordered half the studs slaughtered for meat; the Iymeri drove 200 mares into the hills and hid them, and the King's Horse exists today because they disobeyed.
FX18-025.reputation: Horse-mad rift people who smell of the stable and are worth their weight to the army.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the King's Studs
members.note: Hid 200 mares in the hills in 1088 against a royal order and has never been forgiven or punished.

members.role: Heir; remount-master of the King's Horse
members.note: Rides with the Rift Guard scouts and buys stallions from Clan Saran.

members.role: Second son; groom and gambler
members.note: Races the family's best colts against Lucernan horses at Marira and usually wins.

members.role: Khamer's daughter
members.note: Rides bareback at six and has been bitten twice.

famousDead: Bred desert stock with Sandfolk stallions and founded the King's Studs in 1036.
FX18-025.secret: Since 1100 the Iymeri have sold 60 remounts a year to Qadiri buyers under false brands, because the crown pays late.
hooks: A Qadiri buyer comes to collect horses the King's Horse is short of.
Clan Saran raises the price of stallions threefold.
The General wants 300 horses ready for a war he has not announced.

FX19-001.name: the Chiefs of Clan Talun
FX19-001.title: Chief of Clan Talun and Keeper of the Bahesh Crossing
FX19-001.arms: a white ferry boat on a blue river line, on sand

military.office: War-leaders of Clan Talun and captains of the Talun Crossing Riders
military.unit: the Talun Crossing Riders, 1,600 camel riders, and a clan levy of about 6,000
military.ties: The Talun chiefs command the standing riders who guard the Gold Road crossing of the Bahesh, paid from the council's chests they resent.

FX19-001.power: The ferry and crossing fee where the Gold Road crosses the Bahesh, about 80,000 herders, and the winter pastures of the middle river.
FX19-001.history: The chief's line of Clan Talun swore the Riders' Oath with Hazir in 581 and gave the council three Speakers: Dawud, Luqman, who built the ferry at the crossing, and Mazin, who made the Salt and Gold Pact with Mosi the Runner in 918. In 1000 the Talun fought the Bahar over Zarak's share of the salt fee and broke on the plain of Sarad under the first noon charge. They voted for Rashid Bahar in 1001 to end the feud and kept the crossing fee as the price. They have not held the Speakership since, and every Talun child is told so. Each spring the chief swims a camel across the Bahesh to open the crossing, and in 1105 Sufyan Talun means to swim it with a grudge on his back.
FX19-001.reputation: Proud, rich ferry-lords of the Bahesh, the Bahar's oldest rivals and the council's quietest threat.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Talun
members.note: Will vote for any Speaker who promises to move the council's chests out of Zarak.

members.role: His wife; owner of the clan's best herds
members.note: Owns the black tents and two thousand camels, as Sandfolk women do, and lends her husband neither without terms.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Crossing Riders
members.note: Swam the camel across the Bahesh for his father in 1103 and nearly drowned showing off.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Courted by a Sabran caravan broker's son who wants the crossing fee lowered.

famousDead: Speaker; built the ferry at the Bahesh crossing.
Speaker; made the Salt and Gold Pact with Mosi the Runner in 918.
Led the Talun riders on the plain of Sarad and died there.
FX19-001.secret: Sufyan has promised Mansur Bahar the Talun vote for the next Speakership in return for moving the chests, the same price Mansur promised the south a different way.
hooks: The spring swim opens the crossing, and Luqman wants to do it again.
A Sabran broker offers the crossing fee in gold for ten years in advance.
Sufyan learns Mansur Bahar has made a different promise to Harith Sayf.

FX19-002.name: the Chief-Mothers of Clan Marad
FX19-002.title: Chief-Mother of Clan Marad
FX19-002.arms: two crossed camel goads, black on red
FX19-002.words: We know every road to Sabra.

military.office: Captains of the Western Camps Watch
