military.unit: the Western Camps Watch, 1,400 camel riders on the Sabran border
military.ties: Marad riders hold the oases of the Sabran border for the council, and in 1022 they hired themselves to Sabra for the Sabun Pass ambush.

FX19-002.power: The western camps and oases on the Sabran border, about 60,000 herders, and three centuries of trade in camels and guides with Sabra.
FX19-002.history: Clan Marad gave the council its seventh Speaker, Thabit Marad, who moved the council from the Well to Zarak in 712. His death came in a feud with Clan Bahad over the western wells that left the council without a Speaker for three years and killed a tenth of the western herds; it ended in 734 with a marriage. The Marad have lived on Sabra's trade for three hundred years, and about 300 of their riders took Farid Sabrani's silver for the Sabun Pass ambush of 1022. In 1101 Chief Hilal Marad died of a scorpion sting, and his widow Hind has led the clan as chief-mother while their son grows up. In 1103 Zarani slave-takers carried about 30 children out of the border camps and sold them at Zaran as Veld-born. Hind has gone to the Well-Mother and to the Speaker, and the Speaker has done nothing.
FX19-002.reputation: Old friends of Sabra turned bitter, led by a widow nobody in the council wants to face.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief-Mother of Clan Marad
members.note: Has asked the Speaker three times for the children and is close to closing the western wells to Sabra on her own.

members.role: Heir; son of the late chief
members.note: Thirteen, and has sworn to ride to Zaran himself and bring the children home.

members.role: Hilal's uncle; captain of the Western Camps Watch
members.note: Thinks a chief-mother is a stopgap and that he should lead the clan.

members.role: Hind's sister; mother of a taken child
members.note: Has followed the slavers' tracks as far as the Nahur toll and come back with a name.

famousDead: Speaker; moved the council to Zarak in 712, killed in the Bahad feud.
Chief; died of a scorpion sting.
FX19-002.secret: Ghanim Marad led the clan's riders for Sabra in a small raid in 1099 and took Zarani silver; he may have shown the slavers the camps.
hooks: Afra's name points to a Sabran pearl master's boat.
Hilal rides west alone.
Hind asks a stranger to buy back one child at Zaran as proof.

FX19-003.name: the Bridge-Chiefs of Clan Darai
FX19-003.title: Chief of Clan Darai and Keeper of the Darai Bridge
FX19-003.arms: a white bridge arch on red

military.office: Holders of the Darai Bridge
military.unit: about 1,200 Darai riders and the bridge towers
military.ties: The Darai hold the bridge where the Salt Road crosses the river below Zahira, and lost it to a Zanaran column in 1059.

FX19-003.power: The Darai Bridge and its toll, the town of Zahira and the slopes of Mount Madul.
FX19-003.history: Clan Darai joined the Riders about 650. About 940 it built the bridge on the Salt Road below Zahira with Zanari masons paid in salt, and it has taken a toll there ever since: one silver piece for ten camels, unchanged for 164 years, which every Darai counts as honesty. A Zanaran column seized the bridge in 1059 and held it until the relief of Mirah in 1060, and the Darai have hated Zanaran soldiers since. They like Zanaran merchants well enough, and many Darai speak Zanari. The chiefs bury their dead in rings of stone on Mount Madul facing the Well of Samar. In 1105 Chief Suhayl Darai follows Harith Sayf, because the east road would skip his bridge as surely as the salt fee.
FX19-003.reputation: Honest toll-keepers of the Salt Road, Zanari-speaking and Zanaran-hating.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Darai
members.note: Has doubled the toll for Zanaran survey parties only, and says that is not changing the toll.

members.role: His wife; Zanari-speaking trader
members.note: Buys kola and cloth from Zanari merchants on the bridge and hears all their news.

members.role: Heir; captain of the bridge towers
members.note: His grandfather died retaking the bridge in 1060, and he keeps the man's broken bow on the tower.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Loves a Zanaran mason's son who comes each spring to mend the bridge.

famousDead: Built the Darai Bridge about 940 with Zanari masons paid in salt.
Died retaking the bridge in the relief of Mirah.
FX19-003.secret: The Darai have been paid by Zanara's Road-Master to let survey parties pass at night without the double toll.
hooks: A Zanaran survey party crosses the bridge at night and Badi stops it.
Nawra's Zanaran sweetheart is found with road drawings.
The bridge needs Zanari masons, and Harith Sayf forbids hiring them.

FX19-004.name: the Chiefs of Clan Qasani
FX19-004.title: Chief of Clan Qasani and Sweeper of the Well of Badifa
FX19-004.arms: a white stone well-mouth on brown
FX19-004.words: We keep the dry well clean.

military.office: War-leaders of Clan Qasani
military.unit: about 1,500 hill riders and foot archers of Qasan
military.ties: Qasani riders fought beside the Sayf outside Mirah in 1060 and lost many men.

FX19-004.power: The hill town of Qasan and its winter market, the striped-blanket weavers, and the hills west of Mirah.
FX19-004.history: Clan Qasani came into the Riders about 610 and gave the council one Speaker, Zubair Qasani, who admitted Clan Sulaya in 812. The ruined well of Badifa, one of the nine Samar and Hazir dug in 566, lies in Qasani land, and the clan keeps the dry well swept as a debt to Samar. Its riders fought beside the Sayf in the Salt War, and it borrowed from Zanara's Gold Houses to rebuild its herds; it still owes its share of the south's 40,000 suns. Since 1098 the outlaw Zayd Blackveil and his 60 riders have wintered in the hills near Qasan with the chief's knowledge, and Qasani herders feed them. If Zanara's marshal comes hunting the raiders, Qasan will be the first town he reaches.
FX19-004.reputation: Poor, pious hill folk who sweep a dry well and shelter an outlaw.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Qasani
members.note: Feeds Zayd Blackveil's band on Harith Sayf's quiet word and pretends to the council he has never seen them.

members.role: His wife; mistress of the blanket looms
members.note: Her striped blankets sell to every caravan, and half the clan's debt is paid in them.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Rides with Zayd Blackveil on raids, which his father does not know.

members.role: Daughter; sweeper of the Badifa well
members.note: Sweeps the dry well every Well Day and has found masons' marks in the old stone lining.

famousDead: Speaker 806–829; admitted Clan Sulaya to the council.
FX19-004.secret: Shabib Qasani rides with Zayd Blackveil's raiders, and Khain well-diggers died in a camp they burned in December 1104.
hooks: Clan Khain comes to Qasan demanding blood-price.
A Zanaran column is seen on the road to Qasan.
Ruwayda shows a Qadiri scholar the masons' marks in the dry well.

FX19-005.name: the Chiefs of Clan Marir
FX19-005.title: Chief of Clan Marir
FX19-005.words: Not within sight of the water.

military.office: War-leaders of Clan Marir
military.unit: about 1,800 Marir camel bowmen
military.ties: Marir bowmen fought from camelback outside Mirah in 1060 and still ride in the southern levy.

FX19-005.power: The town of Marir, its well, the Haliya Hills pastures and about 35,000 herders.
FX19-005.history: Clan Marir came into the Riders from the Haliya Hills about 640 and has always followed Clan Sayf as one of the Southern Clans. In 1098 a Marir man killed a young man of Clan Sayf, and the dead man's cousin Zayd killed him at the well of Marir, within sight of the water, which the faith forbids. The Marir demanded that Zayd be cast out, and Harith Sayf sent him into the desert without water to keep the south together. In December 1104 Marir herders saw Zayd alive in the Southern Hills with 60 riders, and Chief Amr Marir has begun to ask how an exile without water lives so well. If he learns that Harith pays him, the south splits.
FX19-005.reputation: Stiff, honor-proud hill folk who have not forgiven a killing at their well.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Marir
members.note: Has sent his best trackers after Zayd's band to find who feeds them.

members.role: His wife; mother of the man Zayd killed
members.note: Buried her son beside the well in 1098 and wants Zayd's water-skin cut in front of her.

members.role: Heir; master of the trackers
members.note: Followed Zayd's tracks to the hills above Qasan and saw Qasani herders bring them bread.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Was promised to a Sayf cousin before 1098; the betrothal has never been spoken of again.

famousDead: Brought the Haliya hill herders into the Riders about 640.
FX19-005.secret: Amr Marir has written to the Speaker offering to leave the southern bloc if Clan Bahar will give him Zayd Blackveil's head.
hooks: Najib's report reaches the Marir council: Qasan feeds Zayd.
Harith Sayf offers Amr a Sayf bride to forget the matter.
Zayd Blackveil raids Marir camels in plain sight.

FX19-006.name: the Chiefs of Clan Khaiya
FX19-006.title: Chief of Clan Khaiya and Patron of the Western Oases
FX19-006.arms: a green date palm on sand
FX19-006.power: The date gardens and water-shares of four western oases, about 30,000 client gardeners and a third of every harvest.
FX19-006.history: Clan Khaiya joined the Riders in the 620s and took the western oases of Abin, Azayn, Waduma and Zabesh, whose gardeners became its clients. Its one Speaker, Wahb Khaiya, closed the Roll of the Clans at 23 in 880, the year he died. The Black Cough came to the oases with Sabran date-buyers in 921 and killed a fifth of the gardeners, and the clan borrowed from Qadir's Water Endowment to replant, a habit it has kept. Alone among the clans the Khaiya build mud-brick houses at their oases. In the dry summer of 1104 its wells did not fail, and Chief Sahl Khaiya sold water to southern herds at a fee. The Riders' way forbids selling a drink, and Clan Hazari now calls the Khaiya 'Wells in Riders' robes'.
FX19-006.reputation: The richest and softest of the clans, mud-brick lords whom the purists call half townsmen.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Khaiya
members.note: Says he sold the use of troughs, not water, and has a Qadiri scholar's letter that agrees.

members.role: His wife; owner of the Zabesh gardens
members.note: Owns more date palms than her husband and has told him to stop selling water before Well Day.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Must answer the Hazari before the council on Well Day for his father's trough-fees.

members.role: Daughter; married to a Sabran date-buyer
members.note: Lives half the year at Sabra and brings back Sabran money and Sabran gossip.

famousDead: Speaker; closed the Roll of the Clans at 23 in 880.
FX19-006.secret: The Khaiya owe the Water Endowment 18,000 suns, and Keeper Yusuf Alami's agents have hinted that the debt could vanish if the clan votes against reading the contract of Zahir.
hooks: The Hazari demand judgment on the trough-fees at Well Day.
The Endowment calls in the Khaiya debt.
Duha brings a Sabran offer to buy the whole Zabesh harvest for oil silver.

FX19-007.name: the Saran Camel-Masters
FX19-007.title: Chief of Clan Saran and Brander of the Crescent
FX19-007.arms: a crescent of white camels on red

military.office: War-leaders of Clan Saran
military.unit: about 2,500 Saran camel riders
military.ties: Saran riders guarded the treaty tent at Zarak in 1063, and Saran camels carry half the clan levy into war.

FX19-007.power: The best riding-camel herds of the Waste, sold to Sabra, Qadir and Zanara alike, and the council's swing vote.
FX19-007.history: Clan Saran joined the Riders about 590 and gave the council two Speakers. Sulayman Saran was Speaker when a Bahar chief sold Zahir of Qadir the Burning Waste route in 790 and was never told the full terms, a slight the Saran still repeat. Jabr Saran let Clan Tamira ride for Tamar at Lake Nubako in 983 and died in the spring of 1000 with the council split. The Saran brand every camel with the crescent and name it at birth, and selling an unnamed camel is a shame. Their camels carried Mosi the Runner's envoys to Zarak in 918, and they still sell Zanara most of its riding camels. In 1105 Chief Hani Saran will back whoever promises to open the Bahar chests to the council's inspection.
FX19-007.reputation: Rich, sharp camel-breeders who sell to everyone and vote for whoever opens the chests.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of Clan Saran
members.note: Has stopped selling camels to Sabra until the Marad children come home, and doubled the price to Qadir.

members.role: His wife; mistress of the named herds
members.note: Can name every one of 3,000 crescent camels and its mother.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Wants to marry his son to a half-Saran girl of the Zahas herds in Sabra to keep the camel trade open.

members.role: Hani's sister
members.note: Keeps the clan's old tally of 790 and says it proves the Bahar chief was paid twice.

famousDead: Speaker in 790, never told the full terms of the Bahar bargain with Zahir.
Speaker; let Clan Tamira ride for Tamar in 983.
FX19-007.secret: Rawda Saran's old tally shows the Bahar chief of 790 took both Zahir's silver and a share of Qadiri water-rights the council never knew about.
hooks: The council vote on opening the chests turns on Hani Saran.
A Qadiri buyer offers triple for 400 camels before April.
Jabr's grandson's betrothal to a Sabran girl becomes a hostage question.

FX19-008.name: the Escort-Captains of Bahad
FX19-008.title: Captain of the Salt Road Escort
FX19-008.words: A red thread for every caravan.

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Salt Road Escort
military.unit: the Salt Road Escort, 4,000 camel riders between Zarak and Mirah
military.ties: This tent-line of Clan Bahad has captained the paid Salt Road Escort since Speaker Karam Bahad founded it, and its pay comes from the chests of Zarak.

FX19-008.power: Captaincy of the Salt Road Escort and its 4,000 riders, and the pay-chest that feeds half of Clan Bahad.
FX19-008.history: Karam Bahad, Speaker from 962 to 979, raised the paid Salt Road Escort to guard the caravans between Zarak and Mirah, and gave its captaincy to his brother's line. That line has held it since, and Bahad riders make up most of the escort. Bahad riders braid a red thread into their camels' halters for every caravan guarded without loss, and the captain's own halter is red from end to end. They fought outside Mirah in 1060 and are the Speaker's surest vote, because the escort's pay comes from the chests at Zarak. That pay makes them the most exposed if Zanara's east road cuts the salt fee: with no gold at Mirah there is no pay, and 4,000 idle Bahad riders would be everyone's danger.
FX19-008.reputation: Loyal, well-paid escort captains, the Speaker's own spear and the south's suspicion.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Salt Road Escort
members.note: His halter is red from end to end, and he has not lost a caravan since 1091.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the escort pay-tallies
members.note: Knows the escort's pay is two months behind and has hidden it from the riders.

members.role: Heir; captain of a camel-hundred
members.note: Wants to ride against Zanara's east-road camps himself, not leave it to an outlaw.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Braids the red threads for the whole escort and knows every rider's count.

famousDead: Speaker; founded the paid Salt Road Escort.
FX19-008.secret: The escort's pay is two months behind because Hamza Bahar's second tally cord has been skimming the chest.
hooks: The riders learn their pay is late.
Karam rides on the east-road camps without the Speaker's word.
A caravan is lost under Bahad escort for the first time in 14 years.

FX19-009.name: the Rimal of the Dark-Moon Ring
FX19-009.title: Master of the Dark-Moon Ring
FX19-009.arms: a black ring of sand on silver, a white star in the middle

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Dark-Moon Ring of the Turn
military.unit: the ring-guard of the Bahar tents at Zarak, 1,000 rotating clan riders
military.ties: Since Rashid Bahar's time the Rimal have commanded the ring of other clans' sentries that guards the sand-eyed Bahar on moonless nights.

FX19-009.power: Command of the ring-guard, the trust of the Speaker's family and the knowledge of every Bahar's weakness in the dark.
FX19-009.history: Rashid Bahar could see through noon glare and was blind on a moonless night, and so are his descendants. In 1002 he asked a night-guide of Clan Janun, Fahim Rimal, to raise a ring of sentries from other clans around the Bahar tents at the dark of the moon. The Rimal have commanded that ring since, and it has become the Turn's ring-guard of 1,000 riders. They are a small tent-line with good night eyes, and they know exactly how helpless a Speaker is at the dark of the moon. Bakr Bahar died on the Hazir River in 1062 on a moonless night outside the ring, and the Rimal of that day never forgave himself.
FX19-009.reputation: Quiet night-watchers of the Speaker's tents, trusted with a secret everyone half knows.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Dark-Moon Ring
members.note: Can walk the ring blindfolded and counts every sentry twice on a moonless night.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Sews the black veils of the ring-guard so no lamp shows them.

members.role: Heir; captain of the ring-guard
members.note: Has been offered Mansur Bahar's favor if he moves one sentry on a certain night.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Learns the stars from Adib guides and can find north on any night.

famousDead: Night-guide of Clan Janun; raised the first dark-moon ring for Rashid Bahar.
FX19-009.secret: Dhafir Rimal has been asked by someone close to Mansur Bahar to leave a gap in the ring on the dark of the moon after Well Day.
hooks: A sentry is found dead at his post on a moonless night.
Fahim learns his son has met Mansur's men.
The Speaker asks the Rimal to guard him at the Well, outside Zarak.

FX19-010.name: the Ghabra, Bearers of Hazir's Lance
FX19-010.title: Bearer of Hazir's Lance

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of Hazir's Lance in the Riders of the Well
military.unit: a camel-hundred of the Riders of the Well at the Well-court
military.ties: The Ghabra carry Hazir's lance and saddle round the Well each Well Day and lead a hundred of the Riders of the Well.

FX19-010.power: The honor of carrying Hazir's relics, a hundred of the Riders of the Well, and a tent by the Well-court.
FX19-010.history: Ghabr was Hazir the Rider's lance-bearer and was with him when he died of fever before Qadira in 603. He carried the lance and saddle back to the Well, and Nabhan Hazari made his line their keepers. Every Well Day for five centuries a Ghabra has carried Hazir's lance round the Well at the head of the Riders. They ride in the Riders of the Well under the Hazari and keep the Riders' way purer than the Hazari themselves: no fee, no Keeper, no Qadiri in the desert. Since the summer of 1104 the head's younger son has followed the prophets of the Last Well who camp at the Well's cisterns, and wants to carry the lance before a returning Well-Finder.
FX19-010.reputation: The purest of the Riders, proud keepers of the oldest relics of the clans.

members.role: Head of the family; Bearer of Hazir's Lance
members.note: Has carried the lance round the Well 38 times and wept every time.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Oils Hazir's saddle with her own hands every Well Day eve.

members.role: Heir; captain of a hundred
members.note: Wants every Qadiri Keeper thrown out of the desert by Well Day.

members.role: Younger son; follower of the Last Well
members.note: Preaches among the prophets at the cisterns that the Well-Finder will come when the last well runs dry.

famousDead: Hazir's lance-bearer; carried the relics back to the Well in 603.
FX19-010.secret: The lance carried round the Well is a copy made in 812; the true one broke in a fall in 811 and its head lies wrapped in the Ghabra tent.
hooks: Wahb wants to carry the lance before the prophets on Well Day.
A Qadiri Well-Keeper asks to see the lance-head.
The Khaiya are judged at the Well, and Muhanna wants to judge them with a lance.

FX19-011.name: the Kathib Slingers of Mirah
FX19-011.title: Captain of the Hill Towers of Mirah
FX19-011.arms: a red hill with a white tower, a sling-stone above
FX19-011.words: Five months and not a gate.

military.office: Hereditary captains of the hill towers of Mirah
military.unit: the tower companies of the Mirah garrison, about 800 slingers and archers
military.ties: A Kathib has commanded the hill towers of Mirah since the Sayf took the town, and in 1060 they held them for five months against 18,000 Zanarans.

FX19-011.power: The hill towers around Mirah, the garrison's slingers and the respect of every Sayf.
FX19-011.history: When Fahd Sayf took the hill town of Mirah about 885, he gave its towers to the Kathib, a slinging family of the Southern Hills who had climbed the walls first. They have held the towers since. In April 1060 Emperor Mosi II came with 18,000 men and 30 war elephants, and for five months the Kathib slingers broke every assault from the towers while the riders outside starved the Zanarans of water. Hazir the Blind put a Kathib in 'The Thirst of Mirah', and every child in the Waste knows the line. The family is proud and poor, because the gold that passes through Mirah goes on to Zarak.
FX19-011.reputation: The heroes of the siege of Mirah, living on a poem and a garrison wage.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Hill Towers
members.note: Was twelve on the walls in 1060 and slung the stone that killed an elephant's driver.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the tower cisterns
members.note: Keeps the tower cisterns full against a siege she is sure is coming.

members.role: Heir; captain of the north tower
members.note: Wants to close the Salt Road tomorrow and fight Zanara again.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Wins the poetry feuds at the Mirah market before any blade is drawn.

famousDead: First up the walls of Mirah about 885.
Held the north tower in the siege and died the week before the Zanarans left; named in 'The Thirst of Mirah'.
FX19-011.secret: Sakhr Kathib sold Mirah's tower plans to a Zanaran engineer in 1101 for gold to rebuild the towers, and the engineer now works on the east road.
hooks: A Zanaran engineer is seen measuring the towers.
Harith Sayf orders the towers ready for war in spring.
Yamama's poem at the market insults a Bahar captain.

FX19-012.name: the Sharaf Star-Guides of Adib
FX19-012.title: Elder of the Star-Guides of Badayn
FX19-012.arms: a white star over a black dune

military.office: Masters in the Brotherhood of Guides and leaders of the Star Guides on retainer
military.unit: about 60 Star Guides on retainer with the Escort and the Speaker
military.ties: Sharaf guides lead the army's night marches and found the relief road to Mirah in 1060.

FX19-012.power: Masterships in the Brotherhood of Guides, star-names earned in sandstorms, and the knowledge of every well from Zarak to Mirah.
FX19-012.history: The Sharaf are a tent-line of Clan Adib, the clan of guides, and have trained guides since about 640. A guide earns a star name only by leading a caravan through a sandstorm without loss, and the Sharaf have more star names than any other line. Sharaf guides led the relief riders to Mirah by night in 1060. In 1104 the Brotherhood split when its master, Khalid the Star, took Zanara's pay to survey water points for the east road and about 20 Adib guides went with him. Two Sharaf sons went; the head of the line calls it treason to the Riders and has not spoken their names since.
FX19-012.reputation: The finest guides in the Waste, now split between old oaths and Zanaran gold.

members.role: Head of the family; Elder of the Star-Guides, called Sandwise
members.note: Has brought caravans through nine sandstorms and refused Zanara's pay in person.

members.role: Elder son; surveyor for Zanara's east road
members.note: Walks the east road with Khalid the Star and says a guide guides whoever pays.

members.role: Daughter; heir in her father's eyes
members.note: Earned a star name, Greyveil, in 1102, the first Sharaf woman in a century to do it.

members.role: Younger son; with Hilal on the east road
members.note: Wants to come home and does not know how.

famousDead: First of the line; guided the council's first caravans to Zarak.
Led the relief riders to Mirah by night in 1060.
FX19-012.secret: Hilal Sharaf knows where Khalid the Star found the Red Hollow well, and that the Well-Mother has knotted it as Bahar's alone.
hooks: Harith Sayf's men hunt the guides who walk the east road.
Ghayda is asked to guide the Speaker to the Well on Well Day.
Nayif sends word he wants to come home.

FX19-013.name: the Umran Ring-Fort Keepers
FX19-013.title: Keeper of Fort Najayn
FX19-013.arms: a grey stone ring on green

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the ring-fort of Najayn
military.unit: about 150 riders and the fort's cistern for 200 people
military.ties: The Umran have kept Clan Jalai's ring-fort on the Veld border since it was built of Yasuz stone.

FX19-013.power: Fort Najayn and its cistern, the salt-for-cattle trade with the Veld villages and the fire on its tower each Well Day.
FX19-013.history: Clan Jalai joined the Riders about 850 and built ring-forts of stone against Veld raiders, the only nomads who do. In 870 the Umran, a Jalai tent-line, carried stone from the Yasuz Hills and raised Fort Najayn; they have kept it since. It holds a cistern for 200 people and their camels for a month. The Umran trade salt to the Veld villages for cattle and were trusted there until 1094, when some Jalai took Zarani silver to guide slave raiders. An Umran cousin was among them. The Veld villages now blame all Jalai, and the Umran have offered their fort and riders to Clan Marad to close the western road to Zarani slavers, whatever the Speaker says.
FX19-013.reputation: Stubborn frontier fort-keepers, ashamed of one cousin and determined to wash it out.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of Fort Najayn
members.note: Shares a name with his clan's chief and is often mistaken for him, which he allows.

members.role: His wife; salt-trader to the Veld
members.note: The one Jalai the Veld headwomen still drink with.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Has killed two Zarani riders on the Veld road and buried them without telling anyone.

members.role: Hudhayl's cousin; the guide of 1094
members.note: Took Zarani silver to guide slave raiders in 1094 and lives at the fort on sufferance.

famousDead: Carried stone from the Yasuz Hills and raised Fort Najayn about 870.
FX19-013.secret: Ubayd Umran guided the Zarani raiders in 1103 as well, the raid that took the Marad children.
hooks: Clan Marad asks for the fort's riders to close the western road.
A Veld headwoman demands Ubayd's head.
Zarani riders come to Najayn looking for their missing men.

FX19-014.name: the Ma'arid Knot-Readers
FX19-014.title: First Knotter of the Well-Mother's Register
FX19-014.arms: a white knotted cord on blue
FX19-014.power: The tying and reading of the Well-Mother's knotted register, which says which clan may water where and when.
FX19-014.history: When Layla the Knotter became Well-Mother in 1001 and moved the knotted register into the Bahar tents, she took a girl of the Ma'arid tents as her helper. The Ma'arid have tied and read the register's cords for every Well-Mother since. Each well of the Waste is a knot; each clan's watering right a color; each season a turn of the cord. The family can read the register better than the clans whose wells it records, and they are trusted because they are poor and have no herds worth watering. In November 1104 Salma Bahar had the head of the family knot the new well at Red Hollow as Bahar's alone, and tie it where only a knotter would find it.
FX19-014.reputation: Humble cord-readers of the Well-Mother's tent, who know more about water than any chief.

members.role: Head of the family; First Knotter of the Register
members.note: Tied the Red Hollow knot in November and has not slept well since.

members.role: Her son; register-reader at the troughs of Zarak
members.note: Reads out the watering order at the salt wells each dawn and stops knife fights with it.

members.role: Granddaughter; apprentice knotter
members.note: Has found a knot in the register that no one can explain, tied in Rashid Bahar's time.

famousDead: Helper of Layla the Knotter; first of the family's knotters.
FX19-014.secret: Lubaba knotted the Red Hollow well as Bahar's alone on Salma Bahar's word, against the custom that a new well belongs to the council.
hooks: The southern clans demand the register be read aloud at council.
Maysa's unexplained knot turns out to mark a hidden well in Talun land.
Someone tries to steal a cord from the register.

FX19-015.name: the Hijana Well-Cleaners
FX19-015.title: Master of the Shaft of the First Well
FX19-015.arms: a black rope down a white well, on sand
FX19-015.words: We go down so you may drink.
FX19-015.power: The right to go down the shaft of the Well of Samar and clean it, and to be chosen as Keeper of the First Well.
FX19-015.history: After the Well Truce of 604 the council chose a Keeper of the First Well from the well-cleaners who went down the shaft, and the Hijana have been among those cleaners ever since. Four Hijana have been Keeper; the present Keeper, Ayub the Deep, is a cleaner of another line who learned the shaft from a Hijana master. The family goes down on ropes, clears the sand and the fallen stone and comes up with the blessing of the Riders. At 9 metres the stone lining of the Well changes, and the Hijana have known for centuries that the lower lining is cut in a style no Sandfolk ever used. They call it the Giver's stone and do not discuss it.
FX19-015.reputation: Holy, humble well-cleaners, honored by every Rider and paid by none.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Shaft
members.note: Has been down the Well 300 times and knows every mason's mark in the lower lining.

members.role: Heir; rope-man
members.note: Wants to be Keeper after Ayub the Deep and prays at the bottom of the shaft.

members.role: Hamza's wife; water-blesser of pilgrims
members.note: Blesses the pilgrims' cups on Well Day and knows the prophets of the Last Well by name.

members.role: Hamza's daughter
members.note: Has been lowered into the shaft once in a basket and drew the marks she saw.

famousDead: Hijana Keeper of the First Well when the council moved to Zarak.
FX19-015.secret: The Hijana know the lower lining of the Well of Samar was cut by Old Kingdom masons, the same marks that show at the Well of Talai in Tamira land.
hooks: A Qadiri scholar wants to be lowered into the Well.
Afra's drawing reaches a Tamari natron trader.
The water drops a finger at the Well in spring, and the prophets say the end is near.

FX19-016.name: the Ruwah Salt-Caravan Masters
FX19-016.title: Master of the Badir Caravans
FX19-016.arms: a white salt slab on a brown camel saddle, on blue
FX19-016.power: Caravans of 400 camels on the Salt Road, troughs at the Well of Badir, and contracts with Zanaran salt-buyers at Mirah.
FX19-016.history: The Ruwah are a tent-line of Clan Janun who began carrying salt south the year after the Salt and Gold Pact of 918, when Mosi the Runner's price made the long road worth it. They water the Zanaran salt caravans at the Well of Badir and run their own trains to Mirah, four slabs to a camel and one gold weight a load under the treaty of 1063. Like every Janun well, theirs has two troughs, one for guests and one for the clan, so no guest waits. Since the three wells failed in 1104 southern herds have crowded onto Ruwah wells by the Well-Mother's order, and there have been knife fights at the troughs. The family fears the Well-Mother will give the south permanent shares in their water to buy Harith Sayf's oath.
FX19-016.reputation: Reliable salt-carriers and generous hosts, now stretched thin by other clans' thirst.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Badir Caravans
members.note: Has stopped a knife fight at his own trough three times since July.

members.role: His wife; owner of the caravan camels
members.note: Owns 900 camels and has refused to lend 200 to the southern clans.

members.role: Heir; caravan-master
members.note: Leads the trains to Mirah and has been warned by Zayd Blackveil's riders to stay off the east road.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Keeps the short-weight tally of the salt clerks at Zarak, given to her by a cutter who trusts her.

famousDead: Carried the first Janun salt south after the pact of 918.
FX19-016.secret: Mudhi Ruwah holds a cutter's tally proving the salt clerks of Zarak pass short slabs and that someone at the Salt Fort profits.
hooks: The Well-Mother orders a permanent southern share in the Badir troughs.
A cutter wants Mudhi to carry the tally to the Speaker.
Dawwas's caravan is raided on the Salt Road by riders in black veils.

FX19-017.name: the Thamad Cutters of the Northern Pans
FX19-017.title: Slab-Master of the Badara Pan
FX19-017.arms: a white cutting axe on grey
FX19-017.power: The best slab-cutting crews of the northern pans below the Sunwall, and the cutters' oath that no clan can replace them.
FX19-017.history: The Thamad are a cutting family of Clan Musuz, who have cut the 25-kilo rock-salt slabs at the northern pans of Badara since the clan joined the Riders about 600. Cutters marry cutters, and a cutter's first slab is given to the Well of Samar. The slabs pay for the whole confederation, and the cutters see little of the gold. In 1094 the cutters' share was cut to pay the Speaker's promises to the south, and since then they have cut the slabs a finger short, about 23 kilos, and sold the shavings to Clan Yasiri's smugglers. In 1105 Nasr the Cutter means to stop cutting on Well Day unless the Salt-Master pays a larger share, and the Thamad will put down their axes with him.
FX19-017.reputation: Salt-crusted cutters, poor, stubborn and the most needed people in the Waste.

members.role: Head of the family; Slab-Master of Badara
members.note: Can cut a slab true to a finger by eye, and has cut them a finger short for ten years.

members.role: His wife; shavings-seller
members.note: Sells the salt shavings to Yasiri boats at the coast under the Hazad Pass.

members.role: Heir; cutter
members.note: Wants to march on Zarak with 300 axes if the Salt-Master refuses.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Will marry a cutter, like every Thamad girl, and wishes she could marry a guide.

famousDead: Brought the Badara cutters into the Riders with Clan Musuz.
FX19-017.secret: The Thamad have sold the shavings of ten years' short slabs to Yasiri smugglers, about 4,000 suns' worth of the council's salt.
hooks: The cutters stop cutting on Well Day.
Hamza Bahar's men come to weigh the slabs at the pan.
Jassar leads the axes toward Zarak.

FX19-018.name: the Dhurwa, the Water-Thief's Line
FX19-018.title: Chief of the Dry Tents
FX19-018.arms: a broken water-skin (cut into the halters of camels they steal)
FX19-018.power: About 40 riders, a hidden well at Tamuma, stolen camels sold at Mirah and Zanaran east-road camps that pay for protection.
FX19-018.history: The Dhurwa were cast out of Clan Khain in 1063 when their ancestor, Shabib the Water-Thief, was caught selling stolen water from a council cistern in the last year of the Salt War. Exile without water should have killed them; instead they found an unmarked well at Tamuma that is in nobody's register, and they have lived there since as raiders and camel thieves. They steal camels from every clan and sell them, rebranded, at the Mirah market. Since 1103 they have sold protection to Zanara's east-road well-camps, which makes them the enemies of Zayd Blackveil, who burns those camps for Harith Sayf. Two Dhurwa riders died in a Blackveil raid in December 1104, and the family has sworn blood.
FX19-018.reputation: Outcast camel thieves who live where nobody can find water, feared by caravans and hated by the council.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief of the Dry Tents
members.note: Named for the Water-Thief and proud of it; has sworn to bring Zayd Blackveil's veil to the Zanaran camp-master.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the hidden well
members.note: Has killed a guide who came too close to the Tamuma well.

members.role: Heir; camel thief
members.note: Once stole a Noon Lance's camel from inside the Zarak camel ground and sold it back to him.

members.role: Fawwaz's daughter
members.note: Has never been inside a town and thinks every well in the world is secret.

famousDead: Cast out of Clan Khain in 1063 for selling stolen cistern water; found the Tamuma well.
FX19-018.secret: The Tamuma well is in nobody's register; if the Well-Mother knew, it would belong to the council and the Dhurwa would have nowhere to live.
hooks: Shabib offers Zanara's camp-master Zayd Blackveil's hiding place in the hills above Qasan.
A caravan guide finds the Tamuma well and must be silenced or bribed.
Fawwaz steals a camel from the Speaker's own herd.

FX20-001.name: House Owandari
FX20-001.title: Governor of Owana
FX20-001.arms: a red bull with gold horns on a black field
FX20-001.words: The herd walks behind the bull.

military.office: Governors of Owana and holders of the Owana levy
military.unit: the Owana Horn, 9,000 levy spears raised at the dry-season muster
military.ties: Every Owandari heir serves a turn as colonel in the Horn Regiments before he may sit the governor's stool.

FX20-001.power: The governorship of Owana's 1.2 million people, the cattle tenth of the Owana hills and the largest levy any governor can raise.
FX20-001.history: The Owandari were cattle chiefs of the Owana hills who held out against Mosi the Runner until the Battle of Bandi in 927. Chief Tumo Owandari swore on the Ancestor Hill on 20 March 930, and his son was taken to court as a page; the boy was one of the three who never went home. Mosi made Tumo governor in his son's place, and the house has held Owana for the emperors ever since. Owandari spears stood in the chest of the horns at the Matazi Ford in 1016, and the house lost two sons of thirst before Mirah in 1060. In the Great Arming of 1104 Governor Kibwe sent 4,000 Owana men to Marshal Juma at Atani before any other governor had answered.
FX20-001.reputation: The richest governors on the plains, loud in loyalty, and watched by everyone who remembers that loyal men also choose regents.

members.role: Head of the house; Governor of Owana
members.note: He has quietly promised Juma Kanemba the Owana levy for a regency council and calls it 'only prudence'.

members.role: Senior wife; keeper of the governor's granaries
members.note: She owns the grain she grows, as Zanari women do, and has refused her husband's order to sell it to the Atani camp at a loss.

members.role: Heir; colonel of the Owana Horn at Atani
members.note: He drills his horn by night like the Marshal's riders and wants to be first across the border.

members.role: The governor's younger brother
members.note: He lost 700 head of the family's cattle at Stones in one rainy season and now pays his debts in secrets about his brother.

members.role: Daughter; offered as a junior wife at court
members.note: Her father wants her in the Crown Prince's household; she would rather learn the 21-string harp from the Rememberers.

famousDead: Swore on the Ancestor Hill in 930 and gave a son to the court who never came home.
Led the Owana water-carriers at Mirah and died of fever in the lines.
FX20-001.secret: Kibwe has sworn privately to back Juma Kanemba as regent if the emperor dies, in return for the governorship of Atani as well as Owana.
hooks: Ndege offers to sell his brother's regency letter to the highest bidder.
The Owana levy is ordered home for the harvest just as Juma needs it.

FX20-002.name: House Anumbari
FX20-002.title: Lord of the Lotapa Pastures
FX20-002.arms: a gold sun rising over a black cow on green

military.office: Lords of the Anumba muster
military.unit: the Anumba levy, 5,000 spears and herdsmen
military.ties: Their spearmen were the ones Dembe Kanemba ran to raise in 851, and they still muster at the Tetamo ford where he fell.

FX20-002.power: The great cattle pastures of the Lotapa around Anumba, 1.35 million people, and kinship by marriage with the Runner kin of House Kanemba.
FX20-002.history: The Anumbari were the cattle lords of Anumba when Dembe Kanemba, a runner of their own town, ran 206 km in two days and a night in March 851 to raise the Anumba spearmen against an Omamba raid. Lord Kojo Anumbari answered the run, and the families married within a generation. When Mosi the Runner took the crown in 903 the Anumbari were the first lords to send cattle to feed his army, and he made them lords of the Lotapa pastures. They have given senior wives to no emperor but have married into the Runner kin at least five times, and they call the Kanemba 'our cousins from town'. The Matazi defeat of 1016 cost them 600 men, and they have hated Abara since. In 1104 they sent 8,000 head of cattle to feed the Marshal's camp at Atani.
FX20-002.reputation: Proud old cattle-folk who talk as if the empire began in their town, which in a way it did.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Lotapa Pastures
members.note: He counts his cattle every dry season himself and knows 4,000 of them by the shape of their horns.

members.role: Senior wife; born of the Runner kin
members.note: A Kanemba by birth, she ran the Runner's Round herself as a girl and guards her granddaughter like a gold store.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Runner Guard
members.note: He can run the Zanara road in four days and has twice carried messages for Sefu the Runner.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: At eight she outran every boy in Anumba, and the old women whisper about whose blood that is.

famousDead: Answered Dembe Kanemba's run of 851 and raised the Anumba spearmen.
FX20-002.secret: Zuri's father was a junior-wife son of the Kanemba line, and she was sung into the Anumbari line instead of the Kanemba one, against the Law of the Sung Line.
hooks: A Rememberer asks why the girl at Anumba runs like an emperor.
The Marshal's quartermasters have not paid for the 8,000 cattle.

FX20-003.name: House Kendawi
FX20-003.title: Lord of the Atani Marches
FX20-003.arms: a black tower on a gold hill under a red sky
FX20-003.words: The border sleeps in our beds.

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Atani Fort
military.unit: the Atani fort garrison, 1,200 spears and archers
military.ties: They held the Atani fort against the Abari raid of 956 and have kept its gate for the emperors ever since.

FX20-003.power: The fort and fields of Atani on the Abari border, and the only men who know every goat path across the Matazi watershed.
FX20-003.history: When Tano I's armies took the Eastern Uplands in 955, he gave the new fort at Atani to Captain Dumisa Kendawi, a spear captain of Anumba stock. In February 956 Abari hill-lords raided the fort, and Dumisa held the gate for a night and a day until help came; it was the first fight between Zanara and Abara. The Peace of the Matazi of 1017 left Atani Zanari, and the Kendawi have watched Tamowa across the watershed for 150 years, raiding and trading cattle with the Abari valleys in turn. In October 1104 Marshal Juma camped on their land with 12,000 spearmen and 1,600 horse to guard 11,000 road laborers, and the camp now eats the Kendawi granaries. The road would make them rich, and a war would put them first in the fire.
FX20-003.reputation: Hard border folk with Abari cousins they will not name, trusted by soldiers and suspected by courtiers.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Atani Marches
members.note: He has told the Marshal that the Abari pikes at Tamowa are 8,000, not 5,000, and no one listened.

members.role: Senior wife; keeper of the granaries
members.note: She is selling the camp her own grain at triple price and calls it the fee for having 12,000 guests.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Atani gate
members.note: He wants the war, because he thinks the Kendawi will be lords of Tamowa when it is over.

members.role: Daughter; married across the border
members.note: She eloped in 1103 with an Abari cattle-trader of the Tamowa valleys, and her letters home are read by both armies.

famousDead: Held the Atani fort gate against the Abari raid of 956.
FX20-003.secret: Makame's grandmother was Abari, and the house has always kept a cattle path open to Tamowa for its own trade, the path an army could use.
hooks: The Marshal asks the Kendawi to show his riders the secret cattle path.
Akosua sends word that the Tamowa pikes will march at the next new moon.

FX20-004.name: House Simbara
FX20-004.title: Lord of the Jitamo Hills
FX20-004.arms: a silver lion with a broken spear on blue
FX20-004.power: Millet terraces and iron furnaces in the Jitamo hills, with a million people who owe them the grain tax.
FX20-004.history: The Simbara were western hill chiefs who swore on the Ancestor Hill in 930 only because Mosi the Runner held their heir as a page. The boy, Baraka Simbara, died at court of a fever the family has always called poison, and he was one of the three page-sons who never went home. The house has served every emperor since, collected the grain tax and smelted iron for the Horn Regiments, and has never once been forgiven for its grudge or let go of it. In the Salt War it paid its levy in iron rather than men, which the court remembered. Since 1102 the Simbara furnaces have sold more spear-iron than the Horn Regiments buy, and the extra goes east.
FX20-004.reputation: Sullen, correct and dangerous, the family every emperor counts twice at the muster.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Jitamo Hills
members.note: He pours milk for the poisoned page every dry season and has never once said the emperor's name at the rite.

members.role: Daughter and heir; mistress of the furnaces
members.note: She sells the extra spear-iron to Dauda the Smith's agents for Tedana gold dust and keeps the ledger in her head.

members.role: Younger son; spear in the First Bull
members.note: He serves beside the Crown Prince's regiment and loves the boy, which his father treats as treason.

members.role: The lord's aunt; keeper of the family songs
members.note: She can sing the Simbara line back nineteen names without a breath, and the page's name loudest.

famousDead: The page who died at Mosi's court; the house's grievance.
FX20-004.secret: Since 1102 the Simbara have sold about 2,000 spearheads' worth of iron to Dauda the Smith for the Tedana night drills.
hooks: A tax clerk counts the furnaces and the iron does not add up.
Sefu is asked to spy on his own father for the Crown Prince.

FX20-005.name: House Chikwanda
FX20-005.title: Lady of Osezi
FX20-005.arms: a green serpent coiled around a gold millet stalk on white
FX20-005.power: The sorghum and millet granaries of Osezi, which feed the Horn Camps of Zanara in the dry season.
FX20-005.history: The Chikwanda were made lords of Osezi in 958 by Tano I the Builder, who needed someone to feed the new eastern garrisons, and they have been the empire's grain-keepers since. When the Salt War swallowed the army's water trains in 1060, Osezi grain kept the survivors of Mirah alive on the march home, and Mosi II gave the house the right to hold its own grain store free of the governor. For three generations the house has been run by its women, because Chikwanda men die young of the river fevers in the Osezi bottoms. Lady Ngozi has held it since 1091 and fed the Great Arming of 1104 out of her own stores.
FX20-005.reputation: Quiet, rich in grain, and ruled by widows whom no grain-buyer has ever cheated twice.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of Osezi
members.note: Widowed at 36, she has outlived two husbands and both of their brothers and buried each under the granary floor.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: She counts every sack twice and has found that the camp's quartermasters pay in dust that weighs a little light.

members.role: Son; a runner of the House of Runners
members.note: He left the granaries for the relay roads and sends his mother news from the Atani camp faster than the drums.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She has caught the river fever twice and lived both times, and her grandmother calls it a sign.

famousDead: Fed the survivors of Mirah from Osezi's stores in 1060.
FX20-005.secret: Tendai has proof that the dust the Marshal's camp pays in is shaved, and she does not know whether the Gold Houses or the Marshal did it.
hooks: The camp quartermaster demands grain on credit.
A runner son brings word that Atani will burn within the month.

FX20-006.name: House Mabundi
FX20-006.title: Lord of the Tefude Market
FX20-006.arms: a gold key crossed with a cattle-goad on dark red
FX20-006.words: Every hoof pays at the gate.
FX20-006.power: The toll and market-court of Tefude, the great cattle fair between the Mosawa lands and the capital.
FX20-006.history: In 989 Tano II the Drummer gave the toll of the Tefude cattle fair to Kibwe Mabundi, a drum-master who had built three talking-drum towers on the Tefude road. His heirs have judged the fair's quarrels and taken one cow in fifty at its gate ever since. The Well Quarter's caravans pass Tefude on the way north, and the Mabundi and the Kante have argued over the gold-dust toll since the Charter of the Well Quarter, which freed Well merchants from many fees. The house is not rich in land, but it hears every price on the plains first. Lord Kondo Mabundi doubled the gate in 1100 and has since grown fat on the army's cattle buying.
FX20-006.reputation: Toll-takers and gossips, liked by drovers for honest scales and hated by the Well Quarter for honest tolls.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Tefude Market
members.note: He weighs his guests before he feeds them, they say, and he feeds them very well.

members.role: Senior wife; judge of the women's market
members.note: She has fined her own husband twice for short measure in front of the whole fair.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He runs a Stones board behind the cattle pens and takes bets on the war.

members.role: Daughter; apprentice at the drum tower
members.note: She can read drum speech from five towers off and has heard things the family should not know.

famousDead: Built three drum towers on the Tefude road and won the fair's toll.
FX20-006.secret: Kondo takes a quiet tenth from the Well caravans' guides in return for not searching their dust bags, against the toll he is sworn to keep.
hooks: A Well caravan refuses the toll and calls on the Speaker.
Waridi hears a drum message about the emperor's hand.

FX20-007.name: House Wazimba
FX20-007.title: Lord of Old Kupa
FX20-007.arms: a black boar before a burned gate on ochre

military.office: Holders of the Omamba spear-families
military.unit: the Omamba levy, 2,000 spears
military.ties: They lost 5,000 men to Mosi's horns at the Wamaya, and their sons now serve in those same horns.

FX20-007.power: The ruined walls of Old Kupa, a few hill villages of Omamba and a name older than the empire.
FX20-007.history: The Wazimba were the chiefs of the Omamba walled town of Kupa when Mosi the Runner's 14,000 broke 18,000 Omamba spearmen at the Wamaya in November 905. Kupa was burned and never rebuilt, and Chief Nduma Wazimba knelt in its ashes in 906 to keep his life and a tenth of his lands. The house has lived beside its ruin ever since, poorer every generation, sending sons to the Horn Regiments that beat it. In 851 it was an Omamba raid that Dembe Kanemba ran to stop, and the Anumbari have never let the Wazimba forget it. Zuberi Omamba, First Spear of the Horn Regiments, is a cousin they claim, and he has never claimed them.
FX20-007.reputation: Proud and poor, quick to take offense, and the best spear-fighters of any lord's house on the plains.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Old Kupa
members.note: He still holds court in a roofless hall inside the burned walls, because his grandfathers did.

members.role: Heir; file-leader in the Horn Regiments
members.note: Named for the First Spear in hope of patronage, he has been passed over for sergeant three times.

members.role: Daughter; dug the Old Kupa ruins
members.note: She found a pit of old Omamba gold rings under the burned gate in 1104 and has told no one, since every nugget is the emperor's.

members.role: The lord's mother
members.note: She curses the Anumbari at every meal and would marry her granddaughter to a goat before an Anumbari son.

famousDead: Last free chief of Kupa; knelt in its ashes in 906.
FX20-007.secret: Asali has hidden a pit of pre-imperial gold from the Kupa ruins; under the Nugget Law the whole house could lose its hands.
hooks: A royal warden comes to survey Old Kupa for road stone.
An Anumbari son asks for Asali's hand to end the feud.

FX20-008.name: House Kalunde
FX20-008.title: Lord of the Samandi Heights
FX20-008.arms: a gold wheat sheaf on a black mountain under a red flame
FX20-008.words: Burn it once, we fill it twice.

military.office: Keepers of the Samandi granary roads
military.unit: the Samandi road guard, 600 spears
military.ties: They feed and guard the roads of the Samandi Granary Fort, from which the western garrisons watch the Sand Clans.

FX20-008.power: The mountain farms that fill the Samandi Granary Fort and the road tolls of the western passes.
FX20-008.history: When Obi the Quiet built the Samandi Granary Fort in 965 to feed the garrisons that watch the Sand Clans' hill towns, he gave the mountain farms around it to Captain Juma Kalunde, who had built its walls. The house has filled the fort's granaries for 140 years. In February 1061, in the Salt War, about 1,200 clan riders burned the Samandi granaries, and Lord Hodari Kalunde died trying to save the grain; his widow refilled them before the next rains. The Kalunde have hated the Sand Clans since, and they cheer the east road because it might free the empire from the salt price. They resent the Owandari, who were paid for grain the Kalunde gave free in 1061.
FX20-008.reputation: Stubborn mountain farmers with long memories and full barns.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of the Samandi Heights
members.note: She refilled the burned granaries in 1061 and still smells smoke whenever the dry wind blows from the north.

members.role: Son and heir; captain of the road guard
members.note: Born the year after his father burned, he has killed eleven Sand Clan riders and keeps a knot for each.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He trades with a Birayn herder boy across the line and has learned the clan speech, which his father must never know.

famousDead: Died in the burning of the Samandi granaries in 1061.
FX20-008.secret: Baraka's last raid killed a Sand Clan boy under a flag of truce, and the clans have sworn blood for it.
hooks: Sand Clan riders gather near Samandi asking for Baraka by name.
Kamau's clan friend warns of a raid on the granaries.

FX20-009.name: House Tandiri
FX20-009.title: Lord of the Lower Mosawa
FX20-009.arms: three silver fish swimming on blue waves
FX20-009.words: The river remembers, and so do we.

military.office: Captains of the Tedana vassal quota
military.unit: 1,500 of the Tedana vassal quota's 8,000 spears
military.ties: Their sons drill at the Spear School of Tandi and, since 1102, in the night drills no one is supposed to see.

FX20-009.power: Gravel bars on the lower Mosawa panned for the emperor, river villages, and the oldest lordship still sworn to the Tedana kings.
FX20-009.history: The Tandiri held the lower Mosawa for the Tedana kings of Tandi before the empire, and they stood on the walls with Sefu the Stubborn through the seven-month siege of 921. When Tandi fell, Mosi buried Sefu with honor and let the Tandiri keep their gravels under the new vassal king in 922. They have panned for the emperor and sworn to the Tedani for 180 years. Lord Chuma Tandiri's sons drill by night in the Tedana spears, and the Tandiri Rememberers stopped singing the Kanemba line in 1102 with the rest of Tandi. The house is split, because the lord's brother serves Baraka Tedani, who has sold the night drills to the Marshal.
FX20-009.reputation: The Tedani's oldest friends, as proud of losing in 921 as other houses are of winning.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Lower Mosawa
members.note: He keeps Sefu the Stubborn's broken spear-shaft over his door and swore on it to King Kato in 1102.

members.role: The lord's brother; instructor at the Spear School of Tandi
members.note: Baraka Tedani's closest man, he knows the night drills have been reported and is too afraid to tell his brother.

members.role: Heir; captain of a night company
members.note: She drills 200 spears by torchlight in a dry gravel pit and has promised them the Kanemba gold store.

members.role: The lord's grandmother's sister; a Tedana Rememberer
members.note: She sings Sefu the Stubborn as the fourteenth king, in Old Tedani, every morning.

famousDead: Fell beside Sefu the Stubborn on the palace roof of Tandi.
FX20-009.secret: Sadiki knows Baraka Tedani has betrayed the night drills to Juma Kanemba and has said nothing, to save his own neck.
hooks: Imani's night company is ordered to seize a Kanemba gold convoy.
Sadiki asks a stranger to carry a warning he cannot sign.

FX20-010.name: House Mbaruku
FX20-010.title: Spear-Lord of Jiwamo
FX20-010.arms: a white hawk stooping on a green field

military.office: Riders of the Golden Horse by hereditary place
military.unit: a lance of the Golden Horse, 12 riders
military.ties: Their founder rode down clan riders at the Hazir River in 1062 and was given land for it; every son since rides in the Golden Horse.

FX20-010.power: A small manor of Jiwamo granted for one charge, and twelve places in the Golden Horse.
FX20-010.history: Dumisa Mbaruku was a herdsman's son of Owana who rode with the Zanari horse that caught 400 Sand Clan riders at a watering place on the Hazir River in November 1062. He took the clan war banner with his own hands, and Mosi II gave him a manor at Jiwamo under the Owandari governors in 1063. The house is new and knows it. Its sons ride in the Golden Horse in quilted coats and borrowed mail, and its daughters marry up when they can. In 1104 the Great Arming doubled the Golden Horse, and the Mbaruku were given command of a new lance but not the money to mount it.
FX20-010.reputation: Hard-riding upstarts, brave, poor and in debt to every horse-dealer from Tetamba to Jiwamo.

members.role: Founder and head of the house; Spear-Lord of Jiwamo
members.note: He still has the clan banner of the Hazir River and unrolls it for every guest whether they ask or not.

members.role: Heir; lance-leader in the Golden Horse at Atani
members.note: He bought twelve horses on credit from Yohannes of the Mandi Horse School's Tamowa dealer and has not asked where they came from.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She rides her uncle's warhorse bareback at thirteen and wants a place in the Golden Horse that no girl has had.

FX20-010.secret: The Mbaruku horses at Atani were bred at Mandi in Abara and sold through a Tamowa dealer, and Kojo has paid in Golden Horse pay-dust.
hooks: The horse-dealer wants payment in news of the Golden Horse's orders.
Sanaa asks to ride in the Hazir River anniversary race.

FX20-011.name: the Mahundi family
FX20-011.title: Head-Driver of the Elephant Lines
FX20-011.arms: a grey elephant's head shown as a silver bell on red

military.office: Hereditary Head-Drivers of the Elephant Corps
military.unit: the Left Line of the elephant lines, 20 elephants and 200 men
military.ties: They caught the first 30 elephants for Kofi the Lion in 1008 and have driven the Elephant Corps under every master since, now under Tafari the Horn.

FX20-011.power: The trust of the elephants themselves: a Mahundi voice can move a beast that no other driver can.
FX20-011.history: In 1008 Kofi the Lion sent hunters into the Mosawa woods for elephants, and Juma Mahundi, a woodsman who had raised an orphaned calf, brought out 30 of them alive. Kofi founded the Elephant Corps and made Juma its first head-driver. At the Matazi Ford in March 1016 the elephants would not cross under Abari javelins, and Juma's son died trying to drive his beast into the water; the family has carried that shame for 89 years. At the Siege of Mirah in 1060 eleven of the 30 elephants died of thirst, and the Mahundi drivers gave the beasts their own water rations. In 1104 the Great Arming raised the corps to 60 elephants, and the Mahundi train every new driver.
FX20-011.reputation: Elephant-folk who smell of the lines, talk to beasts more than to men, and are never asked to dinner on the Hill.

members.role: Head of the family; Head-Driver of the Left Line
members.note: His old cow Nyota has carried him for 31 years and will not let any other man touch her ears.

members.role: Daughter and heir; the only woman driver in the corps
members.note: Tafari the Horn let her drive because no man could handle the bull Simba, and she has never let him forget it.

members.role: Son; driver
members.note: In 1102 he killed his own maddened beast with the driver's chisel and mallet and has not mounted an elephant since.

members.role: Granddaughter; calf-keeper
members.note: She sleeps in the calf pens and has named every one of the new elephants bought in 1104.

famousDead: Brought 30 elephants out of the Mosawa woods for Kofi the Lion.
Drowned at the Matazi Ford driving his beast into the water.
FX20-011.secret: Bakari knows the corps' elephants still panic at javelin volleys, and has told the Marshal they are ready.
hooks: The Marshal wants ten elephants at Atani before the rains.
Jabali is ordered back onto a beast for the coming war.

FX20-012.name: the Jiamari Spears
FX20-012.title: Colonel of the Anumba Horn
FX20-012.arms: two gold spears crossed over a black ox-hide shield on red

military.office: Hereditary Colonels of the Anumba Horn of the Horn Regiments
military.unit: the Anumba Horn, 3,000 spears of the Horn Regiments
military.ties: Their founder led the Anumba spearmen raised by Dembe Kanemba's run of 851, and they have stood in the chest of every Zanari battle line since the Wamaya.

FX20-012.power: Command of a regiment of 3,000 spears, and the right to stand in the chest of the horns, nearest the emperor.
FX20-012.history: When Dembe Kanemba ran into Anumba in March 851, it was Captain Oduya Jiamari who beat the drum and led the spearmen against the Omamba raid. The Kanemba never forgot. Under Mosi the Runner the Jiamari drilled the chest, the center of the bull's horns that holds while the young men run around the flanks, and at the Wamaya in 905 their line did not move for two hours. The house has held the Anumba Horn as hereditary colonels since 931. It lost half the regiment at the Matazi Ford in 1016 and a quarter before Mirah in 1060. In 1104 the regiment marched to Atani in the Marshal's field host.
FX20-012.reputation: The steadiest spears on the plains, slow-witted to their enemies and immovable to everyone.

members.role: Head of the family; Colonel of the Anumba Horn
members.note: At Mirah he held the line for three days with no water and still will not drink before his men.

members.role: Senior wife; keeper of the regiment's cattle
members.note: She drives 900 head behind the regiment as moving food, as Mosi the Runner taught.

members.role: Heir; captain of two village hundreds
members.note: He has told his father the Marshal's night marches will break the chest, and they have not spoken since.

members.role: Younger son; deserter
members.note: He ran from the Atani camp in December 1104 to marry a Well Quarter girl, and his name is now struck from the regiment's song.

famousDead: Led the Anumba spearmen raised by Dembe Kanemba's run.
Colonel who died of thirst at Mirah holding the chest.
FX20-012.secret: The regiment is 600 men short of its 3,000 since the Great Arming, and Wekesa draws pay for the missing names to feed the rest.
hooks: A pay-clerk counts the Anumba Horn at Atani.
Tumo begs his mother to have him sung back into the family.

FX20-013.name: House Sikamba
FX20-013.title: Warden of Datula Walls
FX20-013.arms: a gold gate in a red wall on sand

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of Datula Walls
military.unit: the Datula garrison, 800 spears and 200 archers
military.ties: They hold the desert castle that faces the Sand Clans, and their wardens escorted the army's water trains in the Salt War.

FX20-013.power: The desert castle of Datula Walls, its two deep wells and the only water on the old northern caravan line.
FX20-013.history: Mosi the Runner built Datula Walls in 919 around two deep wells, after the Salt and Gold Pact, to watch the Sand Clans he had just bought. Its first warden, Tano Sikamba, was a captain of the Kisara night run, and his heirs have kept the wells ever since. In the Salt War the Sikamba led the water trains to Mirah in 1060, and when the clan riders burned them the warden's eldest son died with the camels. The family blames Mosi II for marching beyond the grass and the court for forgetting it. Since the Treaty of the Salt Road the Sikamba have quietly traded water to Sand Clan herders for news.
FX20-013.reputation: Thirsty, patient desert soldiers who know the clans better than any man at court.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of Datula Walls
members.note: She has held the walls since her husband died in 1086 and counts the water in the cisterns every dawn.

members.role: Son and heir; captain of the archers
members.note: He knows the names of the Khain clan herders who water at Datula and pays them in salt for news of Zayd Blackveil.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She rides camels with the Khain girls and dreams of crossing the Red Waste to Qadira.

members.role: The warden's brother-in-law; old sergeant
members.note: He survived the burning of the water trains in 1060 and has not spoken a clan man's name since.

famousDead: Captain of the Kisara night run; first Warden of Datula Walls.
Died with the burning water trains before Mirah.
FX20-013.secret: Shani lets Khain clan herders water at Datula for news, and some of that news goes on to the Sand Clan council.
hooks: Zayd Blackveil's riders ask for water at the gate.
The court orders Datula's wells closed to all clan herders.

FX20-014.name: House Ngomani
FX20-014.title: Bearer of the Gold Tail
FX20-014.arms: a gold horse's tail on a black staff on red
FX20-014.words: Where the tail flies, the horse follows.

military.office: Hereditary Standard-Bearers of the Golden Horse and Wardens of Seduna Walls
military.unit: the Gold Tail troop, 300 riders of the Golden Horse
military.ties: Their founder carried the Gold Tail standard when the Golden Horse rode to Kabale in 1049, and they have carried it on every campaign since.

FX20-014.power: The Gold Tail standard, the castle of Seduna Walls and its remount pastures on the steppe.
FX20-014.history: When the slaves of the Kabale shafts rose in 1049, the Golden Horse rode from Zanara to relieve Lady Nala Kabale, and Nduma Ngomani carried its standard, the Gold Tail, at the front. Mosi II made the standard hereditary in his family and gave him Seduna Walls to breed remounts. In the Salt War Nduma's son led the charge that caught 400 clan riders at the Hazir River in 1062. The house has raised the Golden Horse's officers since and expected to command it. In 1100 the emperor gave the captaincy to Kamau Sawandi instead, and the Ngomani have not forgiven it.
FX20-014.reputation: Proud horsemen who carry the gold and resent the man who gives the orders.

members.role: Head of the family; Bearer of the Gold Tail
members.note: He led the charge at the Hazir River at sixteen and has carried the Gold Tail ever since without once letting it dip.

members.role: Senior wife; mistress of the Seduna remounts
members.note: She breeds 400 horses a year on the steppe and refuses to buy the Abari ones the Mbaruku bring in.

members.role: Heir; lance-captain of the Gold Tail troop
members.note: He has been offered the captaincy of the Golden Horse by the Marshal's men, if Kamau Sawandi should fall in the first battle.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She sews the gold threads back into the old standard each rainy season and knows every tear by its battle.

famousDead: Carried the Gold Tail to relieve Kabale in 1049.
FX20-014.secret: Sefu has agreed with the Marshal's agents that Kamau Sawandi's place will be his after the first battle, by whatever means.
hooks: Kamau Sawandi asks the Ngomani to ride in the front rank at Atani.
The Gold Tail is stolen the night before a review.

FX20-015.name: the Kalumbe drum-wardens
FX20-015.title: Keeper of the Fort Nisi Drums
FX20-015.arms: a black chevron of crossed drumsticks over a drum on yellow

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the drum towers of the Fort Nisi road, under the House of Runners
military.unit: nine drum towers and 120 drummers and relay runners
military.ties: Tano II the Drummer gave them the towers, and every order between Zanara and the eastern forts passes through their sticks.

FX20-015.power: Nine talking-drum towers on the eastern road; every short message between the capital and Atani crosses their hands.
FX20-015.history: When Tano II the Drummer set talking-drum towers between the runner posts, he gave the towers of the Fort Nisi road to Pendo Kalumbe, a drum-master who could send a sentence eight kilometres. Her heirs have kept them for 120 years under the House of Runners. In the Salt War the Kalumbe towers carried the news of the Janir caravan's destruction to Zanara in a day. Now the road to Atani runs past Fort Nisi, and the drummers hear every order the Marshal sends and every answer. In November 1104 one of them sent a message about the emperor's hand that was stopped two towers on, and the drummer who sent it has disappeared.
FX20-015.reputation: Quiet tower folk who hear everything and are paid to forget it.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Fort Nisi Drums
members.note: He has heard the message about the emperor's numb hand and knows that hearing it may kill him.

members.role: Daughter and heir; master drummer
members.note: She drums faster than anyone on the road and has started keeping a written record of every message, against the rule.

members.role: Nephew; relay runner, missing
members.note: He drummed the message about the emperor's hand on to the next tower and has not been seen since November.

famousDead: Drum-master who built the Fort Nisi towers for Tano II.
FX20-015.secret: Subira's written record of drum messages since 1103 holds the Marshal's orders, the emperor's illness and a Well Quarter cipher.
hooks: Someone offers Subira 500 suns for her record.
A body is found at the foot of the fifth tower.

FX20-016.name: the Dandara family
FX20-016.title: Sergeant of the Gold Door
FX20-016.arms: a black anvil before a gold door on white

military.office: Hereditary Sergeants of the Gold Door in the Ancestor Hill Guard
military.unit: the 40 door-guards of the imperial gold store
military.ties: Since the store was walled in 954 a Dandara has stood at its door on every day of every reign.

FX20-016.power: The keys and the door-watch of the imperial gold store on the Ancestor Hill.
FX20-016.history: When Tano I finished the walls of the Ancestor Hill and the gold store in 954, he chose a spearman named Kato Dandara to keep its door, because Kato could not count past ten and could not be tempted. The family has kept the door for 150 years, and its men marry only women of the Hill Guard. No Dandara has ever been accused of theft. But the last sergeant saw gold carried out of the store at night in 1103 to pay the Sorondo loan, more than the court admits, and the present sergeant has counted the empty shelves.
FX20-016.reputation: Honest, dull and unbribable door-keepers whom courtiers forget are in the room.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Gold Door
members.note: He has counted the gold store's shelves with a knotted string and knows the empire is poorer than the emperor says.

members.role: Wife; daughter of the Hill Guard
members.note: She begs her husband to forget the knotted string.

members.role: Heir; door-guard
members.note: He is the first Dandara who can read numbers, which frightens the family more than any war.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She is courted by a Gold House clerk who keeps asking about her father's string.

famousDead: First Sergeant of the Gold Door, chosen because he could not count.
FX20-016.secret: Kato's knotted string shows the gold store holds about a third less than the court's tallies say.
hooks: A Gold House clerk asks Abena to bring him her father's string.
Kato is offered a farm at Anumba if he retires this year.

FX20-017.name: House Mbwambo
FX20-017.title: Second Weigher of Scale Street
FX20-017.arms: a silver wheel of gold-weights on dark green
FX20-017.words: The scale is older than the house.
FX20-017.power: One of the five charters of the Gold Houses, a fortune of about 400,000 suns and agents at Sabra and Qadira.
FX20-017.history: The Mbwambo were named second of the five Gold Houses by the Charter of the Scales in 951 and have followed the Sorondo weights ever since, with growing bitterness. They made their fortune on the Gold Road after Sabra broke from Qadir in 1025 and lost a part of it in the Debt War, when Sorondo bought at the old price and sold at the new before anyone else. Since the Scale Pact of 1071 the Mbwambo have bought and sold by Sorondo weights at Sabra and Qadira. In 1102 their Sabra agent noticed that a Sorondo gold weight balanced short against an old Solen weight. Old Jelani Mbwambo has kept that Solen weight in a box ever since.
FX20-017.reputation: The second-richest scales in the world, careful, sour and always weighing the first.

members.role: Head of the house; Second Weigher of Scale Street
members.note: He keeps an honest Solen weight in a locked box and takes it out only to look at it.

members.role: Daughter and heir; mistress of the Sabra counting house
members.note: She found the short weight at Sabra and wants to test it in public before the Master of Doors of Qadir does.

members.role: Son; clerk who courts a Dandara daughter
members.note: He courts the daughter of the Sergeant of the Gold Door to learn how much gold the emperor really has.

members.role: The head's senior wife
members.note: She fears the box with the Solen weight more than any war and has hidden the key twice.

famousDead: Won the second charter of the Scales in 951.
FX20-017.secret: The Mbwambo know the Sorondo standard weight is short and are waiting for the moment the truth will ruin Sorondo but not the Gold Houses.
hooks: Asali wants a stranger to carry the Solen weight to Qadira.
Kwame Sorondo invites Jelani to dinner for the first time in twenty years.

FX20-018.name: House Kimani
FX20-018.title: Master of the Kimani Caravans
FX20-018.arms: a white tusk on a red field
FX20-018.power: Ivory and kola caravans from Tandi east to Kesh, and the only Zanari agents trusted at Monuro.
FX20-018.history: The Kimani began as kola sellers in the Tandi market and turned to ivory when the Ring Hunters began selling tusks after 1001. They carried tusks east over the Eastern Uplands to the Spice Coast, and by 1050 they kept a compound at Monuro. In 1093 a Kimani ivory caravan carried the young Imani Tembo to Kesh, where she learned the Deep Green. The house is Tedana by birth and Kanemba by interest, and it will profit from whichever road reaches the sea. Since 1104 it has financed Imani Tembo's search for a track to Monuro and watched the Road-Master's road with the other eye.
FX20-018.reputation: Long-road traders with a foot in every camp and a tusk for every purse.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Kimani Caravans
members.note: He has crossed to Kesh nine times and keeps a Keshi wife at Monuro whom his senior wife pretends not to know about.

members.role: Daughter and heir; caravan mistress
members.note: She travelled with Imani Tembo to the Leaf People in 1101 and wants the Monuro track for the Kimani alone.

members.role: Son; agent at Monuro
members.note: He drinks with Hamisi Monuri's captains and sells what they say to whoever pays in gold.

famousDead: Kola seller who sent the first Kimani tusks to the Spice Coast.
FX20-018.secret: Baraka Kimani also sells Zanari news to Faraji Keshari's agents at Monuro.
hooks: The Road-Master wants the Kimani to stop funding her sister.
A Kimani caravan comes back from the Deep Green with one survivor.

FX20-019.name: Clan Zimuka
FX20-019.title: Elder of the Zimuka Forges
FX20-019.arms: a black hammer on a red-hot iron bar, on grey
FX20-019.power: Twelve forge compounds in the Smiths' Ward and the contract for the Horn Regiments' spearheads.
FX20-019.history: The Zimuka are one of the old smith clans that came to Zanara when King Kasimu moved the court there in 781, and like all Zanari smith clans they marry only among their own. They have forged for the Horn Regiments since Mosi the Runner drilled the horns. They sit in the Society of Smiths under Dauda the Smith and have lost the Society's leadership to his clan twice. When the Great Arming doubled the army in 1104, the Zimuka took the spearhead contract, and they have learned that Dauda's forges are working on spearheads that the army never ordered, paid in Tedana gold dust.
FX20-019.reputation: Sooty, clannish and proud, the best spear-smiths in the Smiths' Ward after the clan they hate most.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of the Zimuka Forges
members.note: He lost the Society's election to Dauda by two votes in 1097 and has counted them every day since.

members.role: Daughter; mistress of the charcoal yard
members.note: She buys the clan's charcoal and noticed that Dauda's yard buys twice what his orders need.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He is in love with a girl of Dauda's clan, which would make the first marriage between the two clans in a century.

members.role: The elder's mother
members.note: She speaks to the forge-ancestors in the coals and says they are angry with Dauda.

famousDead: Forged the spearheads of the Matazi campaign.
FX20-019.secret: Kamau has written down the count of Dauda the Smith's illegal spearheads for the Tedana and means to sell the paper to the Marshal.
hooks: Sadiki asks to marry into Dauda's clan.
A Zimuka apprentice is caught with a sack of spearheads bound for Tandi.

FX20-020.name: the Sabanduri Rememberers
FX20-020.title: Chief Rememberer of the Tedana at Tandi
FX20-020.arms: a white knotted cord on indigo
FX20-020.power: The songs of the Tedana kings in Old Tedani, which no vassal king can be confirmed without.
FX20-020.history: Rememberers pass their office by training, not blood, but at Tandi the Sabanduri have trained every chief Rememberer of the Tedana since about 640, when Tedan the Gold-Fist's son made one of their line keeper of his songs. They sing the Tedana kings in Old Tedani and count Sefu the Stubborn as the fourteenth king. In 1102 the Sabanduri elder stopped singing the Kanemba line at the Tandi rites, the first time any vassal house had done so since 930.
