The family is split: the elder's son trains on the Ancestor Hill under Oduya the Long-Voiced, whose memory is failing and who has no clear successor.
FX20-020.reputation: Keepers of the oldest songs on the plains, revered at Tandi and feared on the Hill.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief Rememberer of the Tedana
members.note: He struck the Kanemba line from the Tandi rite in 1102 and says the ancestors told him to.

members.role: Son; Rememberer on the Ancestor Hill
members.note: He fills in the High Rememberer's gaps at the rites and could be named his successor, if he denies his father.

members.role: Granddaughter; apprentice
members.note: She has memorised a song her grandfather forbade: the true story of how Mosi took the crown.

famousDead: Sang Sefu the Stubborn's burial on the Ancestor Hill in 921.
FX20-020.secret: Kojo has been feeding the failing High Rememberer the words of the rites for two years, and could change a line without anyone knowing.
hooks: Kojo is offered the High Rememberer's place if he sings his father unsung.
Ama is asked to sing the forbidden song at a feast.

FX20-021.name: the Nduma physicians
FX20-021.title: Bone-Setter of the Ancestor Hill
FX20-021.arms: a white hand holding a green leaf on brown
FX20-021.words: Count the pulse, not the praise.
FX20-021.power: A century and a half of private records on the deaths of emperors, kept by the physicians who attended them.
FX20-021.history: After Tano I died of a stroke in the middle of a rite in 959, the court called a bone-setter named Kibwe Nduma, and his heirs have attended the Kanemba ever since. They bled Obi the Quiet, packed Tano II's head in wet clay and sat beside Kofi the Lion when he fell from his horse. They have kept a private book of every Kanemba death, and the book shows what no one at court says aloud: the emperors who married Runner-kin cousins on both sides died youngest. In 1104 old Makame Nduma was not called when the emperor's hand went numb, because only Sefu the Runner knew. He has guessed anyway.
FX20-021.reputation: Quiet, careful healers who never lose a patient they are allowed to see.

members.role: Head of the family; Bone-Setter of the Ancestor Hill
members.note: He saw the emperor drop a cup with his left hand in December and has said nothing to anyone.

members.role: Daughter and heir; physician to the Runner kin
members.note: She treats the junior-wife lines and believes the Senior Wife Rule is killing the emperors.

members.role: Son; physician in the Marshal's camp
members.note: He has shown Juma Kanemba pages of the family book on emperors' deaths, for a promise of the Bone-Setter's place.

famousDead: First physician of the Kanemba; attended Obi the Quiet.
FX20-021.secret: The Nduma book of Kanemba deaths predicts, by its own reckoning, that Mosi III will die within three years.
hooks: The Marshal asks for the whole family book.
Efua is called secretly to the emperor in the night.

FX20-022.name: the Wekesari Ring Hunters
FX20-022.title: Ring-Master of the Juwalo Bush
FX20-022.arms: a black arrow through a gold ring on tawny

military.office: Captains of a company of the Ring Hunters
military.unit: 200 Ring Hunters of the Juwalo bush
military.ties: They hunt lion and buffalo for the court and scout the frontiers under Tafari the Horn.

FX20-022.power: Hunting rights in the Juwalo bush, a company of 200 Ring Hunters and the trade in lion skins and ivory.
FX20-022.history: The Wekesari were bush hunters of Juwalo who rode with Kofi the Lion on his great ring hunts, in which a thousand beaters close a circle and the emperor kills what is caught inside. When Kofi founded the Elephant Corps in 1008 they caught the first beasts with the Mahundi, and Kofi gave them the Juwalo bush. In 1025 a Wekesari hunter was at Kofi's side when he died of a stroke following a wounded buffalo, and the family was blamed for the hunt. They have since scouted for the army, and in 1104 Tafari the Horn sent them to map the Matazi watershed for the Marshal.
FX20-022.reputation: Wild bush-folk who smell of smoke and lion fat and see a goat path where others see a cliff.

members.role: Head of the family; Ring-Master of the Juwalo Bush
members.note: He has killed fourteen lions and wears one claw for each on a cord he will be buried with.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: She mapped the Matazi watershed in December and walked into an Abari village by mistake; she walked out with a goat.

members.role: Son; poacher
members.note: He sells ivory from the emperor's bush to the Kimani caravans without the corps' mark.

famousDead: Was at Kofi the Lion's side when he fell after a buffalo in 1025.
FX20-022.secret: Jengo has sold about 300 tusks from the emperor's bush to the Kimani without the mark of the Elephant Corps.
hooks: A man-eating lion kills runners on the Juwalo road.
Nyokabi is asked to guide the Marshal's riders over the watershed.

FX20-023.name: the Tetambari herd-masters
FX20-023.title: Master of the Army Herds
FX20-023.arms: a white ram's horn on green grass under a gold sky
FX20-023.words: The army eats what we drive.
FX20-023.power: About 30,000 humped cattle on the Tetamba steppe and the office of driving the army's moving herds.
FX20-023.history: Mosi the Runner fed his armies by driving cattle behind them, and from 906 the Tetambari herders of the steppe drove those herds. He made their elder Master of the Army Herds, and the family has held the office through every war since. The Tetambari never eat their clan animal, the ram, though they drive cattle to slaughter by the thousand. In the Salt War their herds died of thirst behind the army at Mirah, and the house nearly went under. In 1104 the Great Arming made them rich again: they drive 20,000 head to the Atani camp and buy Abari cattle across the border to make up the numbers.
FX20-023.reputation: Rich, dusty cattle-lords who would sell beef to both armies if the drums allowed it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Army Herds
members.note: He buys Abari cattle at Tamowa through a Mandari dealer and sells them to the Marshal as Zanari beef.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: She drives the herds herself and has told her father that the Abari cattle are spies' cattle.

members.role: Son; drover at Atani
members.note: He plays Stones with Abari drovers every night and has lost a herd and won a sister's betrothal.

famousDead: First Master of the Army Herds under Mosi the Runner.
FX20-023.secret: A third of the cattle feeding the Atani camp are Abari beasts bought through House Mandari's dealers, and the Abari herders who drive them count the camp.
hooks: An Abari drover is caught counting tents.
The Marshal refuses to pay for beef he calls Abari.

FX20-024.name: the Kitwari dust-runners
FX20-024.title: Old Stick of Asilo
FX20-024.arms: a hollow walking stick, scratched on doorposts
FX20-024.power: A network of about 60 runners, panners and gate-porters who carry gold dust from the gravels to buyers below the Scale price.
FX20-024.history: The Kitwari began in 1047, when the Debt War sent the gold price up by a quarter and a panner named Kitwa learned that a hollow walking stick holds 200 grams of dust. His children built a trade on it: dust from the Tedana gravels carried in sticks and robe hems to Asilo Oasis, and sold there to Well Quarter buyers and Sand Clan traders below the Scale price. The law takes a hand for a nugget, and four Kitwari have lost theirs. The family pays the oasis watch and keeps out of the Salt Cats' trade at the capital's East Gate. Since 1103 Tedana dust has poured through Asilo, and the Kitwari have learned whose dust it is.
FX20-024.reputation: Smiling oasis folk with soft robes, heavy sticks and one-handed uncles.

members.role: Head of the clan; the Old Stick
members.note: She feeds every widow at Asilo and buys the oasis watch new sandals each rainy season.

members.role: Son; runs the stick-carriers
members.note: He lost his left hand at nineteen and has carried gold in the stump's binding ever since.

members.role: Granddaughter; buyer at the Well caravans
members.note: She can weigh dust by eye to a grain and has started buying for herself.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: At thirteen he runs the shortest sticks and tells everyone he will be an emperor's runner one day.

famousDead: Panner who first carried dust in a hollow stick.
FX20-024.secret: Ayana launders King Kato Tedani's withheld nuggets as dust through Asilo, and has kept back a tithe for herself.
hooks: A royal warden arrests Hodari with a stick full of dust.
The Salt Cats want a share of the Asilo trade.

FX20-025.name: the Nyokari canoe-masters
FX20-025.title: Master of the Upper Tedana Canoes
FX20-025.arms: a black war canoe on three blue waves on white
FX20-025.words: The river is a road with teeth.

military.office: Hereditary Masters of the Canoe Spears of the Upper Tedana
military.unit: 40 war canoes and 1,000 Canoe Spears
military.ties: Their ancestor closed the Mosawa with war canoes at the siege of Tandi in 921, and they have commanded river canoes for the emperors since.

FX20-025.power: Forty war canoes, the barge trade of the upper Tedana and the right to stop any boat on the river.
FX20-025.history: At the siege of Tandi in 921, Mosi the Runner held the Mosawa with war canoes so that no grain could reach the city, and Captain Shomari Nyokari led them. Tandi fell in October, and Mosi gave the Nyokari the canoes of the upper Tedana. The family has paddled the emperors' war canoes and gold barges since. They are hated at Tandi, where old songs still curse the canoes that starved the city. In 1104 the Great Arming ordered 20 new canoes, and the Nyokari have watched barges of grain move down the Mosawa toward Tandi at night.
FX20-025.reputation: River folk with paddle-scarred hands, loyal to the throne and unwelcome in every Tedana market.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Upper Tedana Canoes
members.note: He can paddle a war canoe up the Tedana rapids by night with no torch.

members.role: Daughter and heir; canoe captain
members.note: She has counted 40 grain barges going down to Tandi by night since October and wants to sink them.

members.role: Son; barge-master
members.note: He carries grain to Tandi at night himself and is paid in Tedana gold dust.

famousDead: Closed the Mosawa with war canoes at the siege of Tandi in 921.
FX20-025.secret: Chuma is one of the bargemen carrying grain to Tandi for King Kato's stores, against his own family's oath.
hooks: Zuri plans to sink the night barges and does not know her brother is on one.
Tandi offers the Nyokari a pardon in song if they change sides.

FX21-001.name: House Marjani
FX21-001.title: Pearl-Buyer of the League
FX21-001.arms: a white pearl in an open shell, shown as a moon, on coral red
FX21-001.power: A seat on the League council, the pearl trade of the Spice Coast and a stake of 30,000 suns in the Isle of Pearls venture.
FX21-001.history: The Marjani were pearl-divers' bosses of the Kesh harbor who bought their first council seat in 951, when Prince Hamadi Madami needed votes. They have bought and sold the League's pearls ever since, sending the best north through the Neck until it closed in 1061. In the Spice War they lost three pearl boats to the Amber fleet and swore never to forgive the Sultans. Then the peace came, and the Isle of Pearls showed them a better revenge: in 1102 Mistress Zuhura Marjani put 30,000 suns into the venture that the Sultan and Princess Laila planned. If the 20 ships do not sail on 1 April, the house loses its fortune, and Zawadi Kioyani's withheld fees are the reason they may not.
FX21-001.reputation: Bold, glittering gamblers of the council, loved by divers and distrusted by growers.

members.role: Head of the house; Pearl-Buyer of the League
members.note: She dived for pearls herself until she was twenty and still keeps her diving stone on her desk.

members.role: Son and heir; captain of a pearl boat
members.note: He has sailed to the Isle of Pearls under an Amber flag to scout it and come home with a scar and a map.

members.role: Daughter; council clerk
members.note: She is counting votes for the Prince's son on First Pepper day and selling the count to both sides.

members.role: Zuhura's husband
members.note: He married into the house and spends its money on palm wine and Amber Row dice.

famousDead: Bought the house's first council seat in 951.
FX21-001.secret: The Marjani have borrowed half their 30,000-sun stake from the same Amber house that holds the Prince's pawned harbor dues.
hooks: Zuhura asks a stranger to persuade the shipwright to release the last six hulls.
Rashidi's map of the Isle of Pearls is stolen.

FX21-002.name: House Pilipari
FX21-002.title: Master of the Upper Kioya Gardens
FX21-002.arms: a white rose on a black pepper vine, on green
FX21-002.power: Pepper and cardamom gardens of the upper Kioya hills, a council seat and the second-largest weight at the Pepper Hall.
FX21-002.history: The Pilipari were pepper growers of Kioya when the four towns swore the League in 880, and they stood with the Kioyani for the Pepper Hall. They have voted with the hill houses for two centuries and married Kioyani daughters four times. When Ranpur's Nagora pepper undercut Keshi pepper in the north after 1081, the Pilipari lost a third of their price and dug up a quarter of their vines for cardamom. They hate the Amber Isles and fear Ranpur more. In 1104 Master Kombo Pilipari began selling pepper secretly to a Ranpuri buyer at Kioya Water, the very enemy whose pepper ruined him.
FX21-002.reputation: Solid hill growers who talk of honest weight and keep two sets of sacks.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Upper Kioya Gardens
members.note: He has sold 12 tonnes of pepper to a Ranpuri buyer, the people he curses at every council.

members.role: Wife; a Kioyani cousin
members.note: She reports every Pilipari sale to her cousin Zawadi, not knowing about the Ranpuri ones.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Kioya Vine Watch
members.note: He hunts smugglers in the hills and has started to wonder where his father's night carts go.

famousDead: Swore the League oath for the Kioya growers in 880.
FX21-002.secret: Kombo Pilipari sells pepper to a Ranpuri buyer by night through Kioya Water, while the council fights Ranpur's pepper.
hooks: Nassoro's Vine Watch stops one of his father's night carts.
The Ranpuri buyer asks for cardamom seedlings, which would ruin the hills.

FX21-003.name: House Tangawi
FX21-003.title: Broker of Amber Row
FX21-003.arms: a gold key on a red and black chequer
FX21-003.power: The brokerage of Amber loans in Kesh, a share of the pawned harbor dues and the debts of half the council.
FX21-003.history: The Tangawi were ginger traders who learned the Amber tongue in the Spice War, when they ran ginger through the blockade. After the Treaty of Madamo in 1072 they set up as brokers on Amber Row, matching Keshi borrowers with Amber lenders and taking a fee from both. In 1102 Mistress Neema Tangawi brokered the 200,000 suns the League borrowed for 20 new ships, and in 1104 she arranged the pawning of the harbor dues of 1105 for 40,000 suns. The house has grown richer than any council house in thirty years. It has no seat on the council and wants one.
FX21-003.reputation: New money with Amber manners, needed by everyone and invited by no one.

members.role: Head of the house; Broker of Amber Row
members.note: She brokered the pawn of the harbor dues and kept a tenth of it for herself through a cousin in Amberport.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He courts a Monuri daughter for the council seat it would bring.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She keeps the house's ledgers and has realised her mother's cousin in Amberport does not exist.

members.role: Neema's grandfather's brother; ginger runner
members.note: He ran ginger through the 1071 blockade and still thinks of the Amber fleet as the enemy his niece now serves.

FX21-003.secret: Neema owns a tenth of the pawn on Kesh's harbor dues through a false Amber name, so she profits if the Prince cannot redeem them.
hooks: Kito the Gecko's robbery of the Amber house puts Neema's false name at risk.
Kurwa asks a stranger what to do with her mother's ledger.

FX21-004.name: House Mvuleni
FX21-004.title: Master of the Deep Green Trade
FX21-004.arms: a black tree on a green field
FX21-004.power: The iron-for-hardwood trade with the Leaf People of the Deep Green and a timber yard at Monuro.
FX21-004.history: When a Keshi explorer came home from the Deep Green in 1070, Jumanne Mvuleni, a ship's carpenter of Monuro, went back with him the next year carrying iron knives. He came home with ebony and red ironwood, and the house was made. The Mvuleni have traded iron to the Leaf People for rare woods ever since, under the protection of House Monuri, whose yards buy the best timber. Six Mvuleni have died of fever in the Deep Green. In 1102 the house supplied timber for the League's 20 new ships at Rehema's yards, and four of the hulls were built of green wood it swore was seasoned.
FX21-004.reputation: Fever-hardened forest traders who bring back the finest wood on the coast and not always the driest.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Deep Green Trade
members.note: He speaks the Leaf People's trade-signs and has had the forest fever five times.

members.role: Daughter and heir; master of the timber yard
members.note: She sold the green timber in 1102 and knows exactly which four hulls it went into.

members.role: Son; forest trader
members.note: He has lived a season among the Leaf People and wants to marry a woman of their trading village.

famousDead: Died of fever on the third Deep Green journey.
FX21-004.secret: Mwanaidi Mvuleni knowingly sold green timber for four of the League's new fighting ships, which may open their seams in the first heavy sea.
hooks: A new ship leaks on her trial run.
Uledi brings a Leaf People woman home to Monuro.

FX21-005.name: House Mnazi
FX21-005.title: Garden-Holder of Zetu
FX21-005.arms: a gold sheaf of rice on dark green
FX21-005.power: Coconut, cardamom and rice gardens around the Zetu market and the rents of its stalls.
FX21-005.history: The Mnazi were palm-garden holders around Zetu who sent their nuts and cardamom down to the coast long before the League. In 931 they bought the right to hold the Zetu market for the Kioyani, and they have collected its stall rents and judged its quarrels since. They are not rich, but every hill grower who goes to the Pepper Hall passes through Zetu and pays them a little. In the Spice War they fed the Kioya Vine Watch for nothing. The present head is old, and her three sons hate each other over who will hold the market.
FX21-005.reputation: Comfortable hill gentry who know every grower by name and every quarrel by heart.

members.role: Head of the house; Garden-Holder of Zetu
members.note: She judges the Zetu market from a chair under the oldest palm and has never been overruled.

members.role: Eldest son
members.note: He expects the market by right and has never collected a rent himself.

members.role: Second son
members.note: He does all the work and has quietly borrowed from Amber Row to buy his brothers out.

members.role: Youngest son; smuggler's friend
members.note: He drinks with the Pwanari night-carters and warns them when the Vine Watch is coming.

famousDead: Bought the Zetu market rights in 931.
FX21-005.secret: Salimu has borrowed 4,000 suns from the Tangawi brokers against the market rents, which are not yet his.
hooks: Old Bibi falls ill before naming an heir.
The Vine Watch catches Pazi with a smuggler's cart.

FX21-006.name: House Kaskazi
FX21-006.title: Holder of the Kioya Water Landing
FX21-006.arms: a black ship burning on a red flame, on gold
FX21-006.power: The landing at Kioya Water, its sheds and the pack road up into the hills.
FX21-006.history: On 15 August 1068 the Amber fleet burned 22 Kioyani ships at Kioya Water, and the boatswain Daudi Kaskazi pulled 40 men out of the burning harbor before his own boat went down. The Kioyani gave him the landing and its pack road in 1069, and his family has kept it for them since. The Kaskazi rebuilt the sheds, keep the road eight days down from the hills, and send every child to watch the water on the anniversary of the burning. They are fierce against the Amber alliance and furious at the pearl venture. In 1104 Daudi's grandson saw Kioyani pepper loaded at the landing onto a ship with an Amber mark.
FX21-006.reputation: Burn-scarred landing folk who hate the Amber Isles in their bones.

members.role: Head of the house; Holder of the Kioya Water Landing
members.note: His arms are burned to the elbow from 1068, and he will not let an Amber sailor tie up at his landing.

members.role: Daughter and heir; master of the sheds
members.note: She runs the landing's sheds and keeps the burning's dead on a carved post by the water.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He saw Zawadi Kioyani's pepper loaded onto a ship with an Amber mark in 1104, and has told only his grandfather.

FX21-006.secret: The Kaskazi know Zawadi Kioyani sold pepper to Amberport through their own landing, and Daudi has not decided whether to shame his liege.
hooks: Daudi stands up at the burning's anniversary to speak.
An Amber ship asks to shelter at Kioya Water from a storm.

FX21-007.name: House Jahazi
FX21-007.title: Captain of the Monuro Marines
FX21-007.arms: a silver grapnel shown as an anchor on dark blue

military.office: Hereditary captains of the Monuro Marines
military.unit: the Monuro Marines, 3,000 boarders and crossbowmen
military.ties: Their founder was among the first crews trained at the Sea School of Monuro in 925, and a Jahazi has led the boarders onto every enemy deck since.

FX21-007.power: Command of the Monuro Marines and the loyalty of the boarders of the Monuro squadron.
FX21-007.history: When Chande Monuri founded the Sea School of Monuro in 925 to train galley crews in ramming and night sailing, a dock-fighter named Chane Jahazi was its first master of boarders. His heirs have led the Monuro Marines for the Monuri ever since. At Tekook in 1070 three Jahazi brothers led the boarding of an Amber galley, and one came home. The house serves House Monuri first and the League second, and in 1105 that difference matters: Hamisi Monuri has offered Monuro's ships to the Amber Isles for a Monuri prince. Captain Mwanahawa Jahazi has heard of it from Baruti Monuri, and the marines are waiting for her word.
FX21-007.reputation: The hardest boarders in the Eastern Gulf, more loyal to Monuro than to the League.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Monuro Marines
members.note: She led the boarders off Madamo in 1093 and took a pirate galley with forty marines.

members.role: Her father; survivor of Tekook
members.note: The only one of three brothers to come home from Tekook, he swore never to serve beside an Amber sailor.

members.role: Son and heir; marine officer in the Pearl Squadron
members.note: He sails with Baruti Monuri's Pearl Squadron in April and does not know what his commander has betrayed.

members.role: Daughter; swimmer
members.note: She has asked to join Neema Nightwater's Night Swimmers, against her grandfather's wishes.

famousDead: First master of boarders at the Sea School of Monuro.
FX21-007.secret: Mwanahawa knows of Hamisi Monuri's letter to the Amber Grand Vizier and has not told the Prince, because her marines would follow Monuro.
hooks: The Prince asks the Monuro Marines to swear to him directly.
Old Abasi refuses to board an Amber ship for the pearl venture.

FX21-008.name: House Mwambao
FX21-008.title: Keeper of the Harbor Chain
FX21-008.arms: a silver chain between two black towers on blue
FX21-008.words: Up for friends, up for no one.

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the Harbor Towers and the Chain of Kesh
military.unit: the Harbor Tower crossbowmen of Kesh, 600 bows
military.ties: They have kept the chain between the Harbor Towers since it was forged, and they held it shut through the Amber blockade of 1071.

FX21-008.power: The windlass of the harbor chain and the crossbows of the two Harbor Towers.
FX21-008.history: The chain between the Harbor Towers of Kesh was hung in 919, when Chande Monuri walled the League's harbors, and he gave its windlass to a tower-builder named Nuru Mwambao. The family has raised and lowered it ever since. In 1071 the Amber fleet blockaded Kesh for months, and Keeper Imara Mwambao kept the chain up until an October cyclone scattered the Amber ships. The Mwambao answer to the Prince, not to any house, and they are proud of it. Since the harbor dues of 1105 were pawned, an Amber clerk sits in the tower counting ships, and the Keeper is not allowed to throw him out.
FX21-008.reputation: Stiff-necked tower folk who think the harbor belongs to them.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Harbor Chain
members.note: She held the chain through the 1071 blockade and calls the Amber clerk in her tower 'the guest who pays nothing'.

members.role: Daughter and heir; captain of the tower crossbows
members.note: She has been asked by Faraji Keshari to raise the chain on an Amber ship if the Sultan turns on the League.

members.role: Faiza's husband; smith of the chain
members.note: He has found three links worn half through and has no iron to replace them.

famousDead: Tower-builder who hung the chain in 919.
FX21-008.secret: Three links of the harbor chain are worn half through, and the Keeper has hidden it rather than admit the chain may break under a ship.
hooks: An Amber warship tries to leave harbor without paying.
Majaliwa needs 400 suns of iron the treasury does not have.

FX21-009.name: the Mrima elephant-men
FX21-009.title: Master of the Kioya Elephants
FX21-009.arms: a grey elephant shown as a black bull on green

military.office: Hereditary handlers of the Kioya Elephants
military.unit: the Kioya Elephants, 30 beasts and 200 men
military.ties: They haul hardwood in peace and stand ready at the Kioya Hill Fort as the League's only war elephants.

FX21-009.power: Thirty trained elephants at the Kioya Hill Fort, which haul the League's hardwood and could carry archers in war.
FX21-009.history: After the Monuro cyclone of 1033 the League needed timber to rebuild 40 ships, and the Kioyani bought five young elephants from Ranpur and hired a Ranpuri-trained handler, Hawa Mrima, a Keshi woman who had worked the beasts in the Ranpuri timber camps. Her family has handled the Kioya Elephants since 1034. They haul logs from the hills in peace and stand in the Kioya Hill Fort as the League's only war elephants. They have never fought a battle. The Mrima speak a handlers' tongue full of Ranpuri words, and they are the only Keshi who think kindly of Ranpur.
FX21-009.reputation: Gentle giants' keepers, half Ranpuri in speech and wholly Keshi in pride.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Kioya Elephants
members.note: Granddaughter and namesake of the first handler, she can calm a bull in must with a song.

members.role: Son and heir; head mahout
members.note: He wants the elephants sent with the pearl venture to show they can fight, which his mother forbids.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She was born the night an elephant calf was born and the two have never been apart.

famousDead: Brought the first five elephants from Ranpur in 1034.
FX21-009.secret: Hawa writes every year to a Ranpuri timber master, and her letters have told Ranpur how many elephants and how many archers the League keeps.
hooks: The council asks for elephants to haul the green hulls ashore.
A Ranpuri visitor asks to see the elephants and the fort.

FX21-010.name: House Kusini
FX21-010.title: Castellan of Fort Zubanga
FX21-010.arms: a white castle on a blue wave on black

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of Fort Zubanga
military.unit: the Fort Zubanga garrison, 500 spears and archers
military.ties: They hold the steppe-coast fort that watches the land road to Zanara and the beaches the Amber fleet once landed on.

FX21-010.power: The castle of Fort Zubanga, its beach watch and the eastern land road toward Zanara.
FX21-010.history: Fort Zubanga was rebuilt in 1072 after the Spice War, when Amber marines had landed on its beaches twice, and Prince Nuru gave it to his marine captain Taji Kusini. The house has kept it for the Keshari since and is one of the few that owes everything to them. The fort watches the coast and the eastern land road where the League quarrels with Zanara over the road east. The Kusini see Zanari traders, scouts and gold buyers pass every month. In 1104 Castellan Rukia Kusini caught a Zanari surveyor measuring the road to the fort and sent him home with his cord cut.
FX21-010.reputation: The Keshari's own watchdogs on the eastern coast, poor, loyal and lonely.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Fort Zubanga
members.note: She sent a Zanari surveyor home with his cord cut and a letter for his master in her own hand.

members.role: Husband; master of the beach watch
members.note: He was a marine at Tekook and still reads the sea every morning for Amber sails.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He wants to leave the lonely fort for the Pepper Guard at Kesh and has been offered gold by a Zanari trader to stay and watch instead.

famousDead: Marine captain given Fort Zubanga by Nuru the Boneless in 1072.
FX21-010.secret: Young Taji has taken Zanari gold to report on the League's eastern coast and road.
hooks: A Zanari column appears on the eastern road.
Rukia finds Zanari dust in her son's chest.

FX21-011.name: the Bahariya pilots
FX21-011.title: Chief Pilot of Monuro
FX21-011.arms: a white star over a blue wave
FX21-011.power: The knowledge of every reef, tide and night mark from Kesh to Madamo, taught only to Bahariya children.
FX21-011.history: The Bahariya have taught night sailing at the Sea School of Monuro since it was founded in 925, and they guided the League's galleys on every night attack in its history. In June 1069 a Bahariya pilot brought Nuru Keshari's 12 boats into Amberport by night, and they burned 12 Amber ships. The family keeps its reef marks in its head and teaches them only to its own. In 1105 the Amber Isles want Keshi pilots for the Isle of Pearls, and Sultan Iskandar's captains have asked for a Bahariya by name.
FX21-011.reputation: Quiet, weather-eyed pilots without whom the League's night fleet would be blind.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief Pilot of Monuro
members.note: He piloted Nuru's boats into Amberport in 1069 and has never told how he found the harbor in the dark.

members.role: Daughter and heir; night pilot
members.note: She is the pilot the Sultan's captains have asked for, and she has not said yes.

members.role: Son
members.note: He has drawn the Monuro reef marks on a hide for an Amber captain who paid him 800 suns.

famousDead: First master of night sailing at the Sea School of Monuro.
FX21-011.secret: Yahaya has sold a chart of the Monuro reefs to an Amber captain, the first time the Bahariya marks have left the family.
hooks: An Amber ship enters Monuro at night without a pilot.
Zawadi is ordered to pilot the pearl fleet.

FX21-012.name: House Ngalawi
FX21-012.title: Master of the Ngalawi Ships
FX21-012.arms: a white ship with red sails on dark blue
FX21-012.power: Eight merchant ships of their own, captained by family, that carry pepper north past the Amber harbors.
FX21-012.history: The Ngalawi have owned their own ships since 1001, when Taji Ngalawi bought a damaged coaster and sailed it home to the Zubanga beaches. They are free shipmasters, not bound to the Monuri or the Kioyani, and they carry pepper for whoever pays. After the Neck closed in 1061 their ships went north past the Amber harbors, paying the harbor fee when they had to. In the Spice War they fought at Tekook with two ships and lost one. In 1105 the council has asked every free shipmaster to lend a ship to the pearl venture, and the Ngalawi have refused.
FX21-012.reputation: Free-sailing shipmasters, proud of owing nothing and suspected of everything.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Ngalawi Ships
members.note: He has refused the council a ship for the pearl venture and said the League can drown without his help.

members.role: Daughter and heir; captain
members.note: She commands the house's best ship and has secretly agreed to sail it with the pearl fleet for a share of the pearls.

members.role: Son; captain
members.note: He lost a ship's cargo at dice in Amber Row and has borrowed from the Tangawi to hide it.

famousDead: Bought the first Ngalawi ship in 1001.
FX21-012.secret: Fatuma Ngalawi has promised her ship to the pearl venture behind her father's back, in return for a tenth of any pearls taken.
hooks: Salimu learns his daughter's ship is fitting out for war.
The Tangawi call in Rashidi's debt.

FX21-013.name: the Mtoni shipwrights
FX21-013.title: Master of the Mtoni Yard
FX21-013.arms: a gold hammer over a ship's keel on brown
FX21-013.power: A walled shipyard at Monuro with 120 carpenters, the second yard of the League after Rehema's.
FX21-013.history: The Mtoni came to Monuro after the cyclone of 1033 sank 40 ships in its harbor and the Monuri needed every carpenter on the coast. Old Kibibi Mtoni opened a yard inside the new sea wall in 1034, and it has built galleys and coasters for the Monuri since. In 1102 the League gave the order for 20 new ships to Rehema the Shipwright's yards, not the Mtoni, and the family has not forgiven it. They know the timber trade of Monuro well, and they know where four hulls' worth of green wood went.
FX21-013.reputation: Good shipwrights with a sore grudge, quick to say what is wrong with any ship but their own.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Mtoni Yard
members.note: She lost the League's great order to Rehema and has built only coasters since, each one better than the last.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He knows the four green hulls by sight and has told no one, waiting for one to leak.

members.role: Daughter; apprentice at Rehema's yard
members.note: She went to learn from the rival yard and admires Rehema, which her mother calls treason.

famousDead: Opened the Mtoni yard after the Monuro cyclone of 1033.
FX21-013.secret: The Mtoni know which four of the 20 new hulls are green timber and are waiting to profit from the scandal.
hooks: Mvua is asked by Rehema to find the four green hulls.
The council asks the Mtoni to inspect the new ships.

FX21-014.name: the Uzio ropewalkers
FX21-014.title: Master of the Ropewalk
FX21-014.arms: a white coil of rope shown as a wheel on red
FX21-014.power: The long ropewalk of Kesh harbor and its sailcloth looms, which rig most of the League's fighting ships.
FX21-014.history: The Uzio have spun rope and woven sailcloth on the long walk by Kesh harbor since 912, a century before the Keshari founded the Rope Hall up the hill. The two families are cousins many times over: the Rope Hall climbs the ropes the Uzio make. They rigged the League's first war galleys and every fighting ship since. In 1102 the order for 20 new ships made them busier than ever, but the treasury has not paid for the rigging. Their master has sold some of the unpaid cordage to Amber captains to keep the walk going.
FX21-014.reputation: Rough-handed harbor folk, cousins to every climber and creditor to every captain.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Ropewalk
members.note: He has rigged 60 fighting ships and has not been paid for the last 20.

members.role: Daughter and heir; mistress of the looms
members.note: She is a cousin of the Rope Hall climbers and hears every whisper of the harbor lanes.

members.role: Son; climber of the Rope Hall
members.note: He trains under Tumaini the Rope and has been asked to climb a certain Amber house roof on a moonless night.

famousDead: Laid the long ropewalk of Kesh harbor in 912.
FX21-014.secret: Hasani has sold about 2,000 suns of the League's unpaid cordage to Amber captains.
hooks: Kheri is caught on a roof in Amber Row.
An Amber ship's rigging carries the Uzio twist.

FX21-015.name: the Kisiwani shrine-keepers
FX21-015.title: Rememberer of the Fukoba Ancestor House
FX21-015.power: The Ancestor House of Fukoba and the songs of the League's founding houses.
FX21-015.history: The Kisiwani have kept the Ancestor House of Fukoba, inland from Kesh, since before the League, and their Rememberers sing the lines of the spice houses. When the four towns swore the League in April 880, a Kisiwani sang the oath. They bury the League's dead with a pinch of pepper in the mouth and speak the princes' names at every rite. The Keshari princes are sung at Fukoba too, and when Princess Laila married into the house in 1101 keeping her Well faith, the Kisiwani elder refused to sing her. In 1105 the council will vote on the infant Nuru as expected heir on First Pepper day, and the boy cannot be sung without the Kisiwani.
FX21-015.reputation: The keepers of Kesh's memory, gentle in manner and immovable on the old ways.

members.role: Head of the line; Rememberer of the Fukoba Ancestor House
members.note: She refused to sing the Amber princess in 1101 and has refused to say whether she will sing her son.

members.role: Son; Rememberer
members.note: He has been offered a seat on the council by Prince Amani if he sings the infant heir.

members.role: Granddaughter; apprentice
members.note: She has learned the founding oath of 880 by heart and found a verse in it that the Monuri would rather forget.

famousDead: Sang the oath of the League at Kesh in 880.
FX21-015.secret: Nasra has decided to sing the infant heir only if the Princess gives up the Path of the Well, and she has told no one but the Kioyani.
hooks: First Pepper day comes and the Rememberer is silent.
Rehema recites the forgotten verse at a council feast.

FX21-016.name: the Pembari clerks
FX21-016.title: Clerk of the League Council
FX21-016.arms: a black reed pen crossed with a silver key on white
FX21-016.power: The minutes, rolls and sealed votes of the League council, kept since the Pepper Hall was built.
FX21-016.history: When Seif Madami built the Pepper Hall in 884, he made a Pembari scribe clerk of the council, and the family has written its minutes ever since. They kept the roll of the vote of 1068 that made Nuru Keshari prince over Saidi Monuri, and the treaty papers of Madamo in 1072. They are not rich, but every council house owes them favors, because the Pembari decide what the minutes say a house promised. In 1105 the council will vote on First Pepper day whether the infant Nuru is expected heir. Clerk Daudi Pembari has been offered money by both the Monuri and the Keshari for the count before it is taken.
FX21-016.reputation: Ink-stained, dry-voiced clerks whose pens have more power than the houses they serve.

members.role: Head of the family; Clerk of the League Council
members.note: He has been offered 5,000 suns by the Monuri and a council seat by the Keshari for the same count.

members.role: Daughter and heir; under-clerk
members.note: She found a page missing from the 1068 minutes, the page with Saidi Monuri's last speech.

members.role: Son
members.note: He sold the missing page of 1068 to Hamisi Monuri for 300 suns and a promise.

famousDead: First clerk of the League council under Seif Madami.
FX21-016.secret: The missing page of the 1068 minutes shows that the council's vote for Nuru Keshari was miscounted by one, and Hamisi Monuri now has it.
hooks: Hamisi Monuri reads the page of 1068 aloud on First Pepper day.
Hidaya asks a stranger to recover the page.

FX21-017.name: the Kombari forest-hunters
FX21-017.title: Head Hunter of the Monuro Forest
FX21-017.arms: a red serpent on a green leaf, painted on a shield of hide
FX21-017.power: The paths and traps of the forest behind Monuro, and poisoned bamboo stakes no army likes to meet.
FX21-017.history: The Kombari are forest people of the hills behind Monuro who hunt forest hog, pangolin and snakes and sell skins and ivory at the yards. The Monuri hired them in 1040 to keep the forest roads clear and to guard the cinnamon forests the house later bought from the Madami. The Kesh hill folk fight with pit traps and poisoned bamboo stakes, and the Kombari are the best of them. They guided the Mvuleni's first journeys toward the Deep Green. In 1104 they were hired to guide the Zanari explorer Imani Tembo's party on its way toward Monuro.
FX21-017.reputation: Barefoot forest folk who leave no tracks and never sit with their backs to a door.

members.role: Head of the family; Head Hunter of the Monuro Forest
members.note: He has set pit traps on every forest road to Monuro and keeps the only map in his head.

members.role: Daughter and heir; guide
members.note: She guided Imani Tembo's party and knows how close the Zanari track is to reaching Monuro.

members.role: Son
members.note: He poaches in the Monuri cinnamon forests and sells the ivory to a Zanari caravan's agent.

FX21-017.secret: Zuhura has found that the Zanari track to Monuro needs only 60 km more cutting, and Hamisi Monuri has paid her to tell no one else.
hooks: A Zanari scout arrives at Monuro out of the forest.
The Prince's men ask the Kombari where the track runs.

FX21-018.name: the Pwanari night-carters
FX21-018.title: Old Cart of Zetu
FX21-018.arms: a cart wheel scratched in charcoal on a doorpost
FX21-018.power: About 40 carters, porters and boatmen who run pepper from the hill gardens past the Pepper Hall to waiting ships.
FX21-018.history: The Pwanari were carters ruined by the Tessar default of 1046, when the Madami could no longer pay for their carts. In 1047 they began carrying hill pepper by night down to the coast and onto Amber ships, skipping the Pepper Hall's tax of one part in ten. They work out of Zetu, where every hill road meets. They pay the Madami weigher at the Pepper Hall and the smuggler Omari pays them in turn, and the Vine Watch has caught them only twice in 58 years. In 1104 Ranpuri buyers began asking for Keshi pepper at the coast, and the Pwanari carry for them too.
FX21-018.reputation: Friendly cart folk of Zetu whom everyone knows and nobody names.

members.role: Head of the clan; the Old Cart
members.note: Born the year the default ruined her father, she has never once paid the Pepper Hall a grain.

members.role: Son; leads the night carts
members.note: He carries Pilipari pepper to a Ranpuri buyer and Kioyani pepper to an Amber one in the same week.

members.role: Granddaughter; lookout
members.note: She charms the Vine Watch at the Zetu crossroads while the carts go round the back.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He wants to climb at the Harvest Home and be a Rope Hall boy, not a carter.

famousDead: Ruined carter who began the night runs in 1047.
FX21-018.secret: The Pwanari carry pepper for both Kombo Pilipari and Zawadi Kioyani, the two loudest enemies of smuggling on the council.
hooks: The Vine Watch sets an ambush at the Zetu crossroads.
A Ranpuri buyer wants pepper seedlings carried, which means death.

FX22-001.name: House Wenzari
FX22-001.title: Lord of the Nusalo Terraces
FX22-001.arms: a blue stag on white over green terraces

military.office: Lords of the Nusalo levy in the Blue Host
military.unit: the Nusalo terrace levy, 3,000 spears
military.ties: They feed and house the Blue Host at Nusalo every odd year, when the second court withdraws there.

FX22-001.power: The terraces around Nusalo and the hospitality of the second court, which lives on their grain every other year.
FX22-001.history: The Wenzari were stewards of the old lords of Nusalo before those lords became House Asfari, and when the twins were crowned in 1012 Asfar gave the Nusalo terraces to his steward Hailu Wenzari. Since the Compact of 1053 the king who is not reigning withdraws to Nusalo with his household, and the Wenzari have fed that court every other year for half a century. They wore the blue border for Kiros and now wear it for Yonas. Yonas's court has borrowed from the Gold Houses of Zanara since 1096, and Lord Dereje Wenzari signed as witness to the loans. When Yared voided the Road Promise on New Year's morning, the Wenzari understood that the debt was now theirs as much as anyone's.
FX22-001.reputation: Gracious hosts of the second court, deep in its debts and deeper in its secrets.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Nusalo Terraces
members.note: He has fed King Yonas's court on credit for six years and keeps the tallies in a cord he will not let the Keeper of the Salt Bars see.

members.role: Wife; mistress of the Nusalo granaries
members.note: She owns the house's grain in her own name and has begun selling it to Tamari river traders for silver.

members.role: Heir; captain in the Blue Horse
members.note: He means to ride with the Blue Guard to Abara next New Year's dawn, whatever his father signs.

members.role: Daughter; lady-in-waiting at the Blue House
members.note: She was sealed in the Blue House with Yonas's papers for one night and has read the secret clause on Tamowa.

famousDead: Steward of Nusalo who received the terraces from King Asfar in 1012.
FX22-001.secret: Dereje witnessed the 60,000 suns of Gold House loans, and his own lands stand as part of the security.
hooks: A Zanari Gold House agent arrives to inspect the Nusalo terraces.
Liya is asked to recite the secret clause for a price.

FX22-002.name: House Koreti
FX22-002.title: Lord of the Balona Valley
FX22-002.arms: a green chevron over a white ox on black

military.office: Captains of the Northern Spears of Balona
military.unit: the Balona company of the Northern Spears, 1,200 men
military.ties: Their founder carried King Kaleb's banner at Zutati in 1051, and every Koreti son serves in the Northern Host under the Tsega.

FX22-002.power: The Balona valley's wheat and cattle and a company of the Northern Spears.
FX22-002.history: Gebre Koreti was a spear captain of Zutati who carried King Kaleb's banner at the Battle of Zutati in February 1051, when the Tsega pike hedge broke Kiros's center. After the Compact of 1053 Kaleb gave him the Balona valley, which had followed Kiros, and the Koreti have worn the green border ever since. They lend cattle to Yared's court and march with the Northern Host. In 1104 Lord Asrat Koreti sent 400 spears to Tamowa with Gebre Tsega. He wants the crown to stay with Yared at the next New Year, and he has said so in front of the Blue Guard's captain.
FX22-002.reputation: Green to the bone, brave and blunt, and hated in every valley that remembers Kiros.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Balona Valley
members.note: He keeps the banner of Zutati in his hall and spits when anyone wears blue past his gate.

members.role: Wife; born a Tsega cousin
members.note: She writes to Marshal Gebre Tsega every month and knows more of the Northern Host's plans than her husband.

members.role: Heir; captain at Tamowa
members.note: He commands 400 spears at Tamowa and has crossed the stream at night to count the Zanari fires.

members.role: Younger son; Blue Guard deserter
members.note: He joined Yonas's Blue Guard for love of a Nusalo girl, and his father has called him dead.

famousDead: Carried King Kaleb's banner at Zutati in 1051.
FX22-002.secret: Abeba Koreti passes the Northern Host's plans to the Tsega and also, for Zanari gold, to a pedlar who sells them on.
hooks: Ermias rides in the Blue Guard that will try to take the capital next New Year.
The Northern Host finds its plans known at Atani.

FX22-003.name: House Ketemari
FX22-003.title: Lord of the Yandi Valley
FX22-003.arms: a white horse's head on blue over a red bend

military.office: Lords of the Yandi horse in Kiros's Men
military.unit: 400 riders sworn to House Mandari
military.ties: They rode in Tesfaye Mandari's charge at Zutati in 1051 and starved before the walls of Abara with Kiros in 1052.

FX22-003.power: The Yandi valley's pastures and orchards, and 400 riders who answer to the Mandari before the crown.
FX22-003.history: The Ketemari swore to the Mandari horse-lords in 714, two years after the Mandari themselves swore to Kasa II the Rider, and they have followed the Mandari horse ever since. In the Twin War they rode for Kiros, broke on the Tsega pikes at Zutati in 1051 and starved at the siege of Abara in 1052. Since the Compact they have worn the blue border and called themselves Kiros's Men. When Prince Tekle was banished in 1090, Lord Wolde Ketemari wept in the Crown Yard and was fined 200 salt bars. The house now carries Mesfin Mandari's letters to Tekle by its own pedlars.
FX22-003.reputation: Romantic, reckless horsemen who still drink to a dead king and an exiled prince.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Yandi Valley
members.note: He rode in Kiros's guard as a boy and keeps the dead king's riding whip under his pillow.

members.role: Wife; keeper of the house's letters
members.note: She copies every letter to Tekle before it leaves, in case it is lost; the copies would hang them all.

members.role: Heir; rider in Tekle's company at Tessar
members.note: He rode to Tessar in 1100 to serve Prince Tekle under Queen Livia and writes home that the prince is coming.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She is betrothed to a Koreti cousin to make peace, and she would rather go to the Rememberers.

famousDead: Starved before the walls of Abara with King Kiros's army.
FX22-003.secret: Genet's copies of the Mandari letters to Tekle are hidden in a hive in the Yandi orchards, and they name every lord who has promised to ride.
hooks: Desta the Pedlar asks Genet to sell him the copies.
Yemane comes home in secret with a message from Tekle.

FX22-004.name: House Malkari
FX22-004.title: Lord of the Kasani Forests
FX22-004.arms: a red coffee branch with black berries on gold, shown as a tree
FX22-004.power: The wild coffee forests of Kasani and the coffee trade down the Monuti to Tamar.
FX22-004.history: The Malkari were coffee gatherers of the western forests whom Queen Hirut's son made lords of Kasani in 889 to keep the coffee trade under the crown. When Tamar became free again and the River Gift Pact of 989 opened the Monuti, Kasani coffee went downriver in sacks and came back as linen and Tamari silver. The house prospered quietly through the Twin War by selling coffee to both kings. Since 1104 the Zanari road has frightened it, because Zanari buyers at Tamowa pay more than Tamari ones, and the Malkari have been selling to both. Lady Mahlet Malkari wants peace with Zanara and says so only in her own hall.
FX22-004.reputation: Rich, quiet forest-lords who smell of roasting beans and never take a side until the price is known.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of the Kasani Forests
members.note: She brews her coffee three times for guests and reads their faces on each cup.

members.role: Heir; coffee buyer at Koyako
members.note: He has signed a contract with House Kante's agents to sell the 1105 crop in Zanari gold.

members.role: Daughter; forest-walker
members.note: She knows every coffee grove in the forest and found a path through it that the Zanari road surveyors missed.

famousDead: First lord of Kasani; sent the first coffee to Tamar after the pact.
FX22-004.secret: The Malkari have sold the whole 1105 coffee crop to House Kante of Zanara, while King Yared calls the Zanari the kingdom's enemy.
hooks: King Yared's toll-men seize Malkari coffee bound for Zanara.
Zanari scouts ask Hirut about her forest path.

FX22-005.name: House Adarashi
FX22-005.title: Warden of Fort Makale
FX22-005.arms: a white castle among green trees on black

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of Fort Makale on the Zanari border
military.unit: the Fort Makale garrison, 600 spears and 200 javelin men
military.ties: Their founder held the forest road at the Matazi Ford in 1016, and the fort guards the coffee forests the Zanari have wanted for 90 years.

FX22-005.power: The forest castle of Fort Makale, its garrison and every path through the coffee forests to the Zanari border.
FX22-005.history: At the Matazi Ford in March 1016 Kidane Adarashi held a forest path with 200 spearmen while King Asfar held the ford, and no Zanari column got round. After the Peace of the Matazi of 1017 Asfar built Fort Makale in the forest and gave it to him. The Adarashi have watched the Zanari at Atani for 88 years, trading raids with the Kendawi of the Atani Marches. In the Twin War they stayed in the fort and served neither king, which both kings remembered. In 1104 the Road Promise would have put Zanari spears on their road, and Warden Fana Adarashi refused to let the surveyors pass.
FX22-005.reputation: Forest soldiers who answer to the border first and the crown second, and never lose a path.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of Fort Makale
members.note: She turned back Nia Tembo's surveyors at spear-point in 1102 and has a Zanari measuring cord nailed over her gate.

members.role: Son and heir; captain of the forest javelins
members.note: He leads night patrols to the watershed and has twice exchanged spears with Kendawi riders.

members.role: The warden's husband's brother; old sergeant
members.note: He fought the Twin War from the fort's walls and says both kings were wrong.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She climbs the tallest trees to watch the Zanari camp fires and counts them for her uncle.

famousDead: Held the forest path at the Matazi Ford in 1016.
FX22-005.secret: The Adarashi have a blood-debt with the Kendawi of Atani: a Kendawi son died in a raid in 1098, and the Adarashi buried him in the forest and never told his family.
hooks: Zanari riders try the forest path before the rains.
A Kendawi woman arrives asking for her brother's grave.

FX22-006.name: House Werqari
FX22-006.title: Lord of the Wamazi Streams
FX22-006.words: What the stream gives, the crown counts.
FX22-006.power: The stream-gold beds of the Wamazi hills and the panners who work them for a share.
FX22-006.history: In 943, when the Tessarian column was turned back at the escarpment, a spear captain named Werq took a wound that crippled him, and Queen Mother Mulu gave him the stream-gold beds of Wamazi. His heirs have panned the streams for the crown ever since, keeping a fifth for themselves. The house paid the gold to whichever king held the crown that year, and so it survived the Twin War and grew rich after it. Since 1096 Zanari gold buyers have come up the Tamowa road offering better weights than the crown. Lord Kiros Werqari has sold to them, and his panners now ask why they work for salt bars.
FX22-006.reputation: Gold-fingered lords who pay their panners in salt and themselves in dust.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Wamazi Streams
members.note: He weighs his gold on Zanari scales because he likes the answer better.

members.role: Wife; mistress of the panners
members.note: She pays the panners fairly behind her husband's back and they would follow her anywhere.

members.role: Heir
members.note: He lost a season's gold at dice to a Zanari buyer, who asked for a map of the streams instead of payment.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She pans beside the workers and has found a nugget the size of a thumb, which she gave to the crown's tally man herself.

famousDead: Crippled turning back the Tessarians at the escarpment in 943.
FX22-006.secret: The Werqari have sold about 2,000 suns of crown gold to Zanari buyers since 1096 and entered it in the tallies as washed out by floods.
hooks: The Keeper of the Salt Bars sends a tally-clerk to Wamazi.
The Zanari buyer comes for the stream map Dawit promised.

FX22-007.name: House Dabori
FX22-007.title: Lord of the Selomba Water
FX22-007.arms: a white anchor-shaped water-gate on blue over brown earth

military.office: Lords of the Selomba archers in the Blue Host
military.unit: the Selomba company of Highveld Archers, 1,000 bows
military.ties: Their archers serve in Yonas's Blue Host under a Mekonen marshal they no longer trust.

FX22-007.power: Irrigated terraces of the Selomba valley, fed by the Loati headwater streams.
FX22-007.history: The Dabori have held the Selomba valley for the Mekonen Keepers of the Source since Seyum III restored the Kimoni line in 786. They are Mekonen vassals and have sent archers to every Mekonen muster for 300 years. In 1098 Dawit Mekonen's engineer cut a channel from a Loati headwater stream to the Mekonen terraces, and in the dry months since then the Selomba terraces have gone thirsty. Lord Lemma Dabori complained to his liege in 1100 and was told the water belonged to the Source. He has measured the stream since, and his tally shows the channel takes far more than a twentieth.
FX22-007.reputation: Loyal vassals turned bitter, with dry fields and a careful tally.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Selomba Water
members.note: He has knotted a cord for every dry-season day the stream ran low since 1098, and the cord is longer than he is.

members.role: Daughter and heir; captain of the Selomba archers
members.note: She serves under Marshal Tsion Mekonen and has refused to drink with her.

members.role: Son
members.note: He has offered the stream tally to a Tamari river trader, knowing Tamar would call the channel a dam.

famousDead: First Dabori lord, rewarded by Seyum III in 786.
FX22-007.secret: Lord Lemma's knotted tally proves the Loati channel takes about a tenth of the stream in the dry months, which Tamar could use to break the River Gift Pact.
hooks: A Tamari envoy asks to see the Selomba tally.
The Mekonen send their engineer to 'repair' the Selomba ditches.

FX22-008.name: House Lamari
FX22-008.title: Lord of the Jimba Valley
FX22-008.arms: a black owl on a green field

military.office: Lords of the Jimba javelins in the Northern Host
military.unit: 800 Highland Javelins of Jimba
military.ties: They have taught the hidden spear line, rising out of tall grass at a horn call, to the Northern Host for centuries.

FX22-008.power: The Jimba valley, the oldest lordship in the north, and the hidden-line javelin men of its hills.
FX22-008.history: The Lamari were among the lords of Zutati who restored Ayele I's son in 493 after the royal cousin Gashaw murdered his father, and the restored king gave them the Jimba valley. They are the oldest lords of the north, older than the Tsega. Their javelin men learned to lie flat in the tall grass and rise at a horn call, and the Northern Host still drills the hidden spear line the Lamari way. In the Twin War they rode for Kaleb. In 1090 Lord Tadesse Lamari's eldest son rode out with Prince Tekle, and the house has been watched by the Tsega ever since.
FX22-008.reputation: Old northern blood, sly in battle and secretive at home.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Jimba Valley
members.note: He taught Gebre Tsega the hidden line as a boy and has not been invited to Zutati since 1090.

members.role: Eldest son; in exile with Prince Tekle
members.note: He rode out with Tekle in May 1090 and is one of the prince's Tessar captains.

members.role: Daughter; heir in her brother's absence
members.note: She runs Jimba and the javelin muster and has told the Tsega she has no brother.

members.role: Grandson, son of Berhanu
members.note: He has never met his father and practices the javelin in the grass every evening.

famousDead: Helped restore Ayele I's son against Gashaw the Unsung in 493.
FX22-008.secret: Berhanu writes to his sister through the Ketemari pedlars, and Saba has promised Tekle the Jimba javelins if he comes home.
hooks: A Tsega officer arrives to count the Jimba javelin men.
Berhanu sends word he is crossing the Neck in spring.

FX22-009.name: House Zewdari
FX22-009.title: Hill-Lord of Okilo
FX22-009.arms: two silver stars side by side on red
FX22-009.power: The Okilo hill terraces and two boys who may one day be counted among the twin-born kin of the crown.
FX22-009.history: The Zewdari were raised to the Okilo hills in 1031 for keeping the Mekonen terraces through a hard drought, and they have been minor vassals of the Keepers of the Source since. In 1088 Lord Yohannes Zewdari married a Mekonen girl of the Tefera line, a cord daughter descended from Princess Hanna, without asking leave under the Cord Law. In 1090 she bore twin sons. The family has told everyone the boys are cousins' children. Under the Compact, if neither king has a twin son, the Rememberers must choose among twin-born kin of the line, and the Zewdari twins are now 15.
FX22-009.reputation: Small hill lords no one notices, which is exactly how they want it.

members.role: Head of the house; Hill-Lord of Okilo
members.note: He married a cord daughter without leave and has spent fifteen years hiding the twins it gave him.

members.role: Wife; a cord daughter of the Tefera line
members.note: She knows her sons' place on the royal cords and wants them sung.

members.role: Elder twin son
members.note: He is the elder by the length of a prayer and thinks he is a hill lord's bastard cousin.

members.role: Younger twin son
members.note: He wants to be a Rememberer, which would put him in the room where his own fate is sung.

FX22-009.secret: The Zewdari twins are children of a cord daughter, born without leave under the Cord Law; they may be twin-born kin of the royal line.
hooks: A Rememberer comes to Okilo asking about twins born in 1090.
Queen Mother Saba invites Hiwot Zewdari to court.

FX22-010.name: House Abati
FX22-010.title: Keeper of the Koyako Stair
FX22-010.arms: a white mountain over a gold stair on brown

military.office: Keepers of the escarpment path at Koyako
military.unit: 300 spears of the Koyako stair-guard
military.ties: Their founder turned back the Tessarian column at the escarpment in 943, and they guard the climb that no lowland army has passed.

FX22-010.power: The escarpment stair above Koyako and the toll on every load that climbs it.
FX22-010.history: In March 943 a Tessarian column climbing toward Koyako was turned back at the escarpment by Abari spearmen on the terraces, and their captain, Tsehai Abati, a woman, rolled the first stones. Queen Mother Mulu gave her the stair and its toll. Since the River Gift Pact the gift has passed up the Abati stair to the Keeper of the Source, and since 1063 Keshi pepper has climbed it on its way to Tamar. The house is rich on tolls and proud of a wall no enemy has crossed. In January 1105 Yared's new toll-men took over the searching of pepper loads, and the Abati lost a third of their fees in a morning.
FX22-010.reputation: Toll-keepers of the high stair, proud of 943 and furious about 1105.

members.role: Head of the house; Keeper of the Koyako Stair
members.note: Named for the woman who rolled the stones in 943, she has asked the king to remove his toll-men or remove her.

members.role: Son and heir; captain of the stair-guard
members.note: He has started charging Keshi pepper carriers a second toll that the king's men do not see.

members.role: Daughter; tally-keeper of the river gift
members.note: She counts every bushel of Tamar's gift up the stair and has found that the Keeper's men take a share before the court sees it.

famousDead: Rolled the first stones on the Tessarian column at the escarpment in 943.
FX22-010.secret: Tsion's tally shows the Mekonen take about 2,000 bushels of the river gift each year before it is counted for the courts.
hooks: King Yared's toll-men and the Abati spears come to blows on the stair.
Almaz Teferi asks to see Tsion's tally.

FX22-011.name: the Tsahari family
FX22-011.title: Sergeant of the Green Twin Guard
FX22-011.arms: a green spear between two white lines on black

military.office: Hereditary Sergeants of the Green Twin Guard
military.unit: a hundred of the Green Twin Guard, 100 men
military.ties: Since the Compact of 1053 a Tsahari has stood at King Kaleb's and then King Yared's door, and their cousins stand in the Blue Guard.

FX22-011.power: The trust of King Yared and a hundred spears inside the royal ridge.
FX22-011.history: When the Compact of 1053 split the court in two, King Kaleb raised the Green Twin Guard, and its first sergeant was Desta Tsahari, a spearman who had held the Walls of Abara through the siege of 1052. His twin brother joined Kiros's Blue Guard, and the family has served both guards ever since; the Wuhari of Nusalo are the Blue branch. The Tsahari walk the Crown Yard each New Year's dawn when the crown is handed over. In 1104 King Yared asked his marshal to keep the Green Guard in the capital next New Year and refuse the handover. Sergeant Habte Tsahari has been told to hold the Green House door against his own cousins.
FX22-011.reputation: Plain, sworn spearmen who would rather die at a door than open it wrongly.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Green Twin Guard
members.note: He has been ordered to hold the Green House door against his own Wuhari cousins next New Year's dawn.

members.role: Wife
members.note: She is a Wuhari by birth and has sworn she will stand in the Crown Yard between the two guards.

members.role: Heir; spearman of the Green Guard
members.note: His best friend since childhood is his Wuhari cousin Yonas, who will be on the other side of the yard.

famousDead: First sergeant of the Green Twin Guard; held the Walls of Abara in 1052.
FX22-011.secret: Habte has orders in Yared's own hand to kill anyone who crosses the Crown Yard without the king's word at the next New Year.
hooks: The two guards meet in the Crown Yard at dawn.
Asrat and his Wuhari cousin plan to stop the fight themselves.

FX22-012.name: the Wuhari family
FX22-012.title: File-Leader of the Blue Twin Guard
FX22-012.arms: a blue sword between two white lines on black

military.office: Hereditary File-Leaders of the Blue Twin Guard
military.unit: a hundred of the Blue Twin Guard, 100 men
military.ties: They are the Blue branch of the Tsahari, sworn to Kiros and now to Yonas, and they guard the even-year king at Nusalo.

FX22-012.power: A hundred places in King Yonas's Blue Twin Guard and the ear of its captain, Eleni Sabara.
FX22-012.history: The Wuhari descend from Gidey, twin brother of the first Tsahari sergeant, who joined Kiros's Blue Guard in 1054 because a twin, the family says, should serve the other twin. They have guarded the even-year kings at Nusalo ever since and ride to Abara each even New Year's dawn to take the crown. Eleni Sabara, captain of the Blue Guard, means to bring the whole guard to the capital at the next New Year, and the Wuhari will ride in its front rank. File-leader Dawit Wuhari knows his cousins will be holding the door.
FX22-012.reputation: The Tsahari in blue, just as stubborn and more bitter, because they have always been second.

members.role: Head of the family; File-Leader of the Blue Twin Guard
members.note: He has never forgiven the Tsahari for keeping the better house in the capital.

members.role: Heir; spearman of the Blue Guard
members.note: Named for the king, he grew up with his Tsahari cousin Asrat and has no wish to kill him.

members.role: Dawit's wife; keeper of the guard's stores
members.note: She has noticed the Blue Guard's stores are being filled for a march, not a ceremony.

members.role: The family's grandmother
members.note: Daughter of the first Tsahari sergeant's sister, she is the last who remembers both branches as one house.

famousDead: Twin of the first Tsahari sergeant; joined Kiros's Blue Guard.
FX22-012.secret: Captain Eleni Sabara has told Dawit the Blue Guard will take the capital whether or not the Rememberers hand over the crown.
hooks: Grandmother Yeshi calls both branches to a funeral feast before New Year.
Yonas is asked to carry a message to his cousin in the Green Guard.

FX22-013.name: the Feresi hedge-sergeants
FX22-013.title: Hedge-Sergeant of Londi Walls
FX22-013.arms: five white pikes upright on green

military.office: Hereditary drill-sergeants of the Tsega Pikes at Londi Walls
military.unit: the Londi Walls pike company, 600 pikes of the Tsega Pikes
military.ties: They have drilled pikemen for the Tsega Spear Yard since its founding in 790 and stood in the front rank at Zutati in 1051.

FX22-013.power: The drill-yard of Londi Walls, where northern boys learn the pike hedge.
FX22-013.history: When the Tsega founded the Spear Yard of Zutati in 790, they took a hill family called Feresi to drill the levies, because a Feresi grandfather had first made the pike hedge stand on the terraces. The family has drilled pikemen for 315 years and now keeps the pike school at Londi Walls under Kebede the Pike. At Zutati in 1051 three Feresi brothers stood in the front rank of Abebe Tsega's hedge when it broke Kiros's center, and two died. The family sends a son to every Tsega muster. In 1104 the Great Arming doubled the Tsega Pikes, and the Feresi have been drilling boys who have never seen a horse charge.
FX22-013.reputation: The hardest drill-masters in the north, who say a pikeman is made in the fourth year or never.

members.role: Head of the family; Hedge-Sergeant of Londi Walls
members.note: He survived the front rank at Zutati and says the Mandari horse sounded like a hailstorm on a roof.

members.role: Daughter; quartermaster of the pike school
members.note: She has 2,000 new pikemen and pikes for 1,400, and Gebre Tsega's quartermaster will not answer her letters.

members.role: Son and heir; sergeant at Tamowa
members.note: He drills the new boys at Tamowa and thinks half of them will run at the first elephant.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She carries a broom-handle pike in the drill-yard and the old men pretend not to see.

famousDead: Died in the front rank of the Tsega hedge at Zutati.
FX22-013.secret: Mesfin let a Mandari rider escape the field at Zutati in 1051, and that rider was Mesfin Mandari's own father; the Mandari have never forgotten the debt.
hooks: The Mandari ask the Feresi to remember Zutati.
Elephants appear in the Zanari camp at Atani.

FX22-014.name: House Ambari
FX22-014.title: Keeper of the Walls of Abara
FX22-014.arms: a grey stone wall with a black gate on gold

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the Walls of Abara
military.unit: the wall garrison of Abara, 1,600 men
military.ties: They have kept Bekele the Builder's walls since 362 and held them against Kiros through the siege of 1052.

FX22-014.power: The keys and gate-watch of the Walls of Abara, and the right to shut them on any king.
FX22-014.history: When Bekele the Builder finished the stone Walls of Abara in 362, he made his master mason Ambar keeper of their gates, and the Ambari have kept them for 743 years under four dynasties. They shut the gates on Gashaw the Unsung's men in 493, on Hawaz the Red's in 786 after he fell, and on King Kiros for six months in 1052, when both armies starved and the walls held. They serve the crown, not the king, and each New Year's dawn the keeper opens the gate for the king whose year it is. In 1105 Keeper Alemu Ambari has been asked by King Yared to keep the gates shut next New Year.
FX22-014.reputation: Grim old gate-keepers who know that a wall is only as loyal as the man holding the key.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Walls of Abara
members.note: He was a boy on the walls in 1052 and ate leather when the bread ran out.

members.role: Daughter and heir; master of the gate-watch
members.note: She says the Compact is the law and the gate opens for whoever holds the crown at dawn.

members.role: Son; stonemason
members.note: Repairing the north wall, he found a sealed shaft under the ancestor houses that is on no plan.

famousDead: Master mason of the Walls; first keeper of their gates.
Held the Walls of Abara through the siege of 1052.
FX22-014.secret: Wolde's sealed shaft leads under the walls into the Rememberers' Hall, a way in that the Ambari have kept for emergencies since 786.
hooks: King Yared orders the gates kept shut next New Year.
Someone asks Wolde about the shaft under the ancestor houses.

FX22-015.name: House Sholari
FX22-015.title: Castellan of Kokuka Walls
FX22-015.arms: a gold eagle over a black tower on white
FX22-015.words: From the wall we see the hill.

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of Kokuka Walls
military.unit: the Kokuka garrison, 1,200 spears and archers of the Northern Host
military.ties: They held the Loati fords for the Tsega in the Upland War of 1014 to 1017 and keep the castle that guards the northern road to Zutati.

FX22-015.power: The castle of Kokuka Walls, half a million people in its district and the road from the Loati fords to Zutati.
FX22-015.history: In the Upland War of 1014 to 1017 the Tsega pikes held the Loati fords while the twin kings fought at the Matazi, and their captain was Hailu Sholari. The twins built Kokuka Walls on the fords' road in 1017 and gave it to him. The Sholari have held it for the Tsega and the Northern Host for 88 years, and they hold the north's road to Zutati. In 1090 Castellan Amare Sholari let Gebre Tsega's riders through to seize Prince Tekle, and they found the road empty because Kebede the Pike had let the prince pass. Amare has suspected the Feresi of warning Kebede ever since.
FX22-015.reputation: Watchful northern castellans, close to the Tsega and closer to their own walls.

members.role: Head of the house; Castellan of Kokuka Walls
members.note: He keeps a list of everyone who used the Zutati road on the night of Tekle's escape.

members.role: Wife; keeper of the castle stores
members.note: She has two years of grain in the castle and quietly feeds the Feresi pike school when Zutati forgets.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Kokuka archers
members.note: He has been offered a place in Tekle's company by a letter that came in a honey jar.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She keeps the castle's ravens and reads the messages they carry before her father does.

famousDead: Held the Loati fords in the Upland War; first Castellan of Kokuka Walls.
FX22-015.secret: Amare's list proves Kebede the Pike let Tekle pass in 1090, and he has kept it as a weapon instead of giving it to Gebre Tsega.
hooks: Hailu answers the letter in the honey jar.
Gebre Tsega asks Amare who warned Tekle.

FX22-016.name: the Hamasi ancestor-keepers
FX22-016.title: Keeper of the Royal Ancestor Houses
FX22-016.arms: a white baobab-shaped oak on dark brown
FX22-016.power: The keys of the royal ancestor houses and the rock-cut shrines beneath them, the second holiest site of the Thousand Ancestors.
FX22-016.history: The Hamasi have swept, fed and guarded the royal ancestor houses of Abara since King Zeray II rebuilt them after the Grey Grass years, and they say their grandmothers carried milk to Abar himself. Rememberers sing the kings; the Hamasi feed them. They kept the houses through the Grey Grass years, four dynasties and the siege of 1052. They know which shrines hold which kings, including the two unsung ones whose names no one may speak. Since 1103 the Queen Mother has taken 9,000 suns from the ancestor houses' gold to pay Yonas's interest, and the Hamasi carried the gold out at night.
FX22-016.reputation: Silent, pious keepers of the dead whom even kings greet with lowered eyes.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Royal Ancestor Houses
members.note: She carried the ancestors' gold out for the Queen Mother and has fasted every seventh day since in penance.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He knows exactly how much gold is gone and has carved the count on a stone inside the house of Bekele.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She has found Gashaw the Unsung's shrine, the one no one may enter, and gone in.

famousDead: Kept the ancestor houses fed through the famine of 636 to 638.
FX22-016.secret: The Hamasi carried 9,000 suns of the ancestors' gold out of the royal ancestor houses for the Queen Mother in 1103 and 1104.
hooks: A Rememberer notices the gold offerings are thin.
Kidist comes out of the unsung king's shrine with a knotted cord.

FX22-017.name: the Kidani of Kimoni
FX22-017.title: Keeper of the Kimoni Ancestor Houses
FX22-017.arms: a gold ox-yoke drawn in ochre on the shrine door
FX22-017.power: The care of the old Kimoni kings' ancestor houses, which still receive offerings, and a story no one has proven.
FX22-017.history: When House Kimoni ended with Anbesa II in 1011, the crown gave the care of the Kimoni ancestor houses to a farming family of the Kimoni hills, the Kidani, and they have kept the old kings fed with milk and barley since. They farm poor terraces between rites and travel each rainy season to sweep the houses at Kimoni. The family has always said its grandmother served in Anbesa II's household. The Rememberers never sang a son of Anbesa's, but the Kidani elders know the name of the boy born in 1008 to a Kimoni serving woman, because he was their great-grandfather.
FX22-017.reputation: Poor, pious hill farmers who keep the old kings' houses and keep to themselves.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Kimoni Ancestor Houses
members.note: He is the grandson of Anbesa II's unsung son and has never once said so aloud.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She has heard the story from her grandmother and thinks the Kidani deserve more than a shrine broom.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He has the heavy Kimoni brow of the old kings' statues, and travellers sometimes stare.

famousDead: The unsung son of Anbesa II; lived and died a shrine-keeper.
FX22-017.secret: The Kidani descend from Anbesa II's unsung son of 1008, and so carry the blood of the Kimoni kings and of the Line of Abar.
hooks: Birtukan goes to Abara to ask the Rememberers to sing her great-grandfather.
Tekle's agents come looking for a living Kimoni.

FX22-018.name: the Gerari salt carriers
FX22-018.title: Head Carrier of Koyako
FX22-018.arms: a white cart-wheel over a salt bar on green
FX22-018.words: Up the stair, down the river.
FX22-018.power: Six hundred pack mules, the salt-bar trade of the Highveld and the carrying of Keshi pepper from the plateau down to the Monuti.
FX22-018.history: The Gerari were salt-bar carriers of Koyako for generations, small men with twenty mules. When the Tessarian Civil War shut the Neck road in 1061 and Keshi pepper began coming west over the Highveld to Koyako in 1063, the Gerari were the first to carry it down to the Tamari boats. In forty years the family grew from twenty mules to six hundred and became the richest commoners in Koyako. They pay the Abati toll on the stair and the crown's toll at the river. In January 1105 King Yared's new toll-men began searching every pepper load, and the Gerari have been asked for a bribe by the men sent to stop bribes.
FX22-018.reputation: New-rich mule-drivers who still eat with their drivers and buy their daughters silk.

members.role: Head of the house; Head Carrier of Koyako
members.note: He started with twenty mules and still knows the name of the first one.

members.role: Daughter and heir; mistress of the Keshi accounts
members.note: She speaks Keshi and Tamari and has been offered a marriage into a Kesh council house.

members.role: Son; mule-train leader
members.note: He has started hiding pepper sacks inside salt-bar loads to dodge the king's search.

FX22-018.secret: Fikru's salt loads have carried about 30 tonnes of Keshi pepper past the king's search since January.
hooks: A toll-man cuts open a salt-bar load.
Mekdes's Keshi suitor turns out to be a smuggler's son.

FX22-019.name: the Semeni grain-mothers
FX22-019.title: Elder of the Salt Market Women
FX22-019.arms: a gold barley ear on a red cloth
FX22-019.words: The king eats from our hand.
