FX22-019.power: The grain stores of the Salt Market below the north gate of Abara, which are owned by women and pass from mother to daughter.
FX22-019.history: The Salt Market of Abara is run by the women who own the city's grain, and since about 880 the eldest of them has usually been a Semeni. The house passes from mother to daughter; sons marry out. In the siege of 1052 the Semeni women sold grain to both armies at prices the songs still curse, and they made the house's fortune. Both courts buy from them, and both owe them. In 1104 Elder Tsehai Semeni refused King Yonas's court any more credit, and she has been asked by King Yared for grain to feed the Northern Host at Tamowa until the rains.
FX22-019.reputation: Hard-bargaining market women whom kings flatter and soldiers fear more than the Zanari.

members.role: Head of the house; Elder of the Salt Market Women
members.note: She has sold grain to six kings and calls them all 'the boy'.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: She wants to sell the Northern Host's grain at siege prices and has already bought up the barley of three valleys.

members.role: Son; married into House Werqari's panners
members.note: He left the house to marry, as sons do, and brings his mother news of the gold streams.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She keeps the market's tally cords at ten and already catches the weighers cheating.

famousDead: Sold grain to both armies at the siege of Abara in 1052.
FX22-019.secret: Hirut has cornered the barley of three northern valleys and plans to sell it to whichever court wins the next New Year.
hooks: King Yared demands grain on credit for Tamowa.
A Zanari agent offers to buy the whole Salt Market's stores.

FX22-020.name: the Hadari smith clan
FX22-020.title: Elder of the Balona Forges
FX22-020.words: No land, no master but the king.
FX22-020.power: The forges of Balona, which make pike-heads and spear-iron for both hosts.
FX22-020.history: In about 50 AR King Berhan I made the smith clans of Abara landless servants of the crown, forbidden to own land in return for the king's protection, and the Hadari of Balona have lived under that law for over a thousand years. They may not own a field, but no lord may touch them. They forged spearheads for both kings in the Twin War and say they have no side. Since the Great Arming of 1104 they have forged pike-heads for the Tsega and the Blue Host at once, and they sell to both by the same weight. They have noticed that Zanari spear-iron now reaches the Abari market through Tamowa, cheaper than theirs.
FX22-020.reputation: Proud, landless iron-folk who belong to the crown and to nobody else.

members.role: Head of the clan; Elder of the Balona Forges
members.note: He says a pike-head does not care which king holds it and has forged 6,000 since 1104.

members.role: Daughter; master of the bellows
members.note: She keeps the clan's iron accounts and knows which pike-heads went to which host.

members.role: Son
members.note: He wants to buy a terrace in his wife's name, breaking the law of Berhan I, and thinks no one would know.

famousDead: Forged the pike-heads of the Tsega hedge at Zutati.
FX22-020.secret: Dereje has already bought a terrace near Balona in his wife's name, which the law of Berhan I punishes by turning the whole clan out of the king's protection.
hooks: A Tsega quartermaster orders pike-heads only for the Northern Host.
A neighbor reports Dereje's terrace.

FX22-021.name: the Lemmari midwives
FX22-021.title: Midwife of the Nusalo Births
FX22-021.arms: a white open hand on blue
FX22-021.power: Two centuries of knowledge of twin births and the trust of the royal women.
FX22-021.history: The Lemmari have delivered the women of Nusalo since 921, when Lady Tsehay of Nusalo bore the first of her three pairs of twins. Twins kill mothers, and the Lemmari know more about keeping both alive than any physician in the kingdom. A Lemmari midwife delivered Kaleb and Kiros in 1029 and died of the spotted fever in 1049, before anyone asked her who came first. Her daughter has always said her mother told her, but the Lemmari keep what they hear at the birthing stool. They delivered Yared and Yonas in 1070 and attended Queen Bezawit when she died in 1099.
FX22-021.reputation: Trusted, tight-lipped healers who have seen more royal blood than any soldier.

members.role: Head of the family; Midwife of the Nusalo Births
members.note: Her mother delivered Kaleb and Kiros, and on her deathbed told her which cried first.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: She delivered Yared's daughter in 1096 and is called to every Asfari birth since.

members.role: Son; physician
members.note: He wants to write down what the women only say, which his mother forbids.

famousDead: Delivered Kaleb and Kiros in 1029; died of the spotted fever.
FX22-021.secret: Etenesh's mother told her that Kiros was born first, the same truth the knotted birth-cord holds.
hooks: Prince Tekle's men come to Nusalo looking for the old midwife's family.
Rahel is called to a secret twin birth at Okilo.

FX22-022.name: the Debari horse gentry
FX22-022.title: Horse-Master of Tezenga
FX22-022.arms: a white horse rearing on red

military.office: Remount masters of the Horsemen of the Monundi
military.unit: the Tezenga remount herds, 1,200 horses
military.ties: They breed the remounts that the Horsemen of the Monundi ride, and their sons ride in Mesfin Mandari's companies.

FX22-022.power: The horse fair of Tezenga and herds of about 1,200 highland horses.
FX22-022.history: After the Matazi Ford in 1016, where Asmar's horsemen fell on the Zanari baggage, the twin kings wanted more horses and gave the Tezenga pastures to Fikru Debari, a Mandari horse-breeder, in 1018. The family has bred highland horses for the Mandari companies ever since. It holds the horse fair at Tezenga twice a year. Since 1101 Yohannes Mandari of the Horse School has bought Debari horses and sold some on to a dealer at Tamowa, and the Debari have learned where those horses went. King Yared means to take a tenth in silver at the southern horse fairs, and the Debari will be the first to pay.
FX22-022.reputation: Horse-folk with Mandari blue on their shawls and silver in their saddlebags.

members.role: Head of the family; Horse-Master of Tezenga
members.note: He can tell a horse's dam from the way it holds its head.

members.role: Daughter and heir; mistress of the fair
members.note: She has refused to sell to the Tamowa dealer since she saw a Debari brand under a Zanari saddle.

members.role: Son; rider in the Horsemen of the Monundi
members.note: He rides with Meron the Red Cow's raiders some nights for the fun of it.

famousDead: Mandari breeder granted the Tezenga pastures in 1018.
FX22-022.secret: About a quarter of the horses the Golden Horse of Zanara bought in 1104 were Debari-bred and sold through the Tamowa dealer.
hooks: King Yared's tax-men arrive at the Tezenga fair.
A Zanari officer recognises the Debari brand on his own horse.

FX22-023.name: the Kasani forest-wardens
FX22-023.title: Warden of the Kasani Coffee Forest
FX22-023.arms: a black boar's tusk on green, cut on tree bark
FX22-023.power: Knowledge of every path, spring and leopard den in the Kasani coffee forests.
FX22-023.history: The Kasani wardens are forest folk who have walked the wild coffee groves for the Malkari lords since 891, keeping out poachers and leopards and leading the gatherers. They take their name from their place, as common Abari do. In the Matazi campaign of 1016 a Kasani warden guided Kidane Adarashi's 200 spearmen along the forest path that saved the ford. They hunt forest hog and leopard and sell skins in Abara's Tanners' Lane. In 1102 they guided the Zanari road surveyors halfway into the forest and then lost them on purpose.
FX22-023.reputation: Wild forest people, half hunters and half spirits to the coffee pickers.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Kasani Coffee Forest
members.note: He led the Zanari surveyors in circles for three days and charged them for each one.

members.role: Daughter and heir; leopard-hunter
members.note: She killed a leopard with a spear at sixteen and wears its skin at every market.

members.role: Son
members.note: A Zanari agent has offered him a sack of gold dust to map the forest path.

famousDead: Guided the spearmen who held the forest path at the Matazi Ford.
FX22-023.secret: Berhanu has already sold half the forest path to the Zanari agent and means to sell the rest after the next payment.
hooks: Zanari scouts appear on the forest path.
A man-eating leopard kills coffee pickers in the deep groves.

FX22-024.name: the Hawazi raiders
FX22-024.title: Red Elder of the Hawazi
FX22-024.arms: a red hand-print on a cattle hide
FX22-024.power: About 60 riders and herders who lift Tsega cattle from the northern pastures and drive them south through the hills.
FX22-024.history: When Tsega the Spear killed Hawaz the Red, lord of Zutati, in the royal hall in 786, Hawaz's younger sons fled south with a few riders. The Rememberers struck Hawaz from the royal song, and his line was struck from everything else. His descendants have lived in the Wamazi hills ever since as cattle raiders, lifting Tsega herds from the Zutati pastures and calling it rent on stolen land. Cattle raiding is repaid sevenfold under Abari law, and the Hawazi have never paid once. They ride with Meron the Red Cow's band when it suits them and against it when it does not.
FX22-024.reputation: Ancient cattle thieves with a grudge against the Tsega that is older than the Asfari crown.

members.role: Head of the clan; the Red Elder
members.note: Every Red Elder takes the name Hawaz and swears to sit one day in the hall at Zutati.

members.role: Daughter; leads the night raids
members.note: She lifted 300 Tsega cattle in a single night in 1103 while the Tsega were watching Tamowa.

members.role: Son
members.note: He sells the clan's stolen hides in Abara's Tanners' Lane and has been seen talking to Desta the Pedlar.

members.role: The Red Elder's mother
members.note: She sings Hawaz the Red as a true king to her grandchildren every night, which is a crime.

famousDead: Lord of Zutati who killed Seyum II and held Abara five years; the third unsung king.
FX22-024.secret: The Red Elder holds an old knotted cord from 786 that the family says proves Hawaz's line was Kimoni kin.
hooks: Gebre Tsega sends riders south while the army is away.
Tigist offers the clan's riders to Prince Tekle for a pardon.

FX23-001.name: the Hall of Torfell
FX23-001.title: Eldest of Torfell
FX23-001.arms: a white reindeer antler on grey
FX23-001.power: The eastern taiga nearest the tusk-whale grounds, a reindeer herd, about 45 old giants and a few hundred human herders, and one young giant everyone wants.
FX23-001.history: Torfell is the eastern taiga hall of the White Coast, the smallest of the hall-lands and the closest to the tusk-whale grounds, with about 45 old giants and a few hundred human reindeer herders. The Warm Winters of 762 to 768 struck it almost as hard as Ulfdal, and it has been dying for a century. Only one giant child has been born there in twenty years, Eyja, who came of age in the autumn of 1104 and spoke the herders' Eastfolk before the Hall Tongue. Mother Asta has chosen Eyja as Ulfar's bride, Eyja has written across the sea to Frostholm for another match, and Eldest Thordis needs her to stay and keep the hall's herd. If Torfell loses Eyja, it will be the next hall to die.
FX23-001.reputation: A brave, fading hall that votes with whoever feeds it, and everyone knows it.

members.role: Eldest of Torfell
members.note: She is 104 and knows that whichever way Eyja goes, the hall's last chance goes with her.

members.role: Heir; reindeer master
members.note: He shares one fire every winter with the human herders and speaks Eastfolk at home.

members.role: Ormar's wife; keeper of the Gundheim Caves
members.note: She copies the old wall paintings of the Gundheim Caves onto hides so that something of Torfell will outlast it.

famousDead: Led Torfell through the Warm Winters with thirty giants left alive.
FX23-001.secret: Thordis has promised Torfell's vote at the Thing to Brenna of Valdhall for two winters of grain, and promised it to Mother Asta for Eyja's marriage, and she cannot keep both.
hooks: Eyja's marriage will decide whether Torfell lives.
Thordis has sold one vote twice.
The tusk-whale grounds near Torfell are where a Drevnan trader wants to go.

FX23-002.name: the Hall of Lindnes
FX23-002.title: Eldest of Lindnes
FX23-002.arms: a grey stone hall on a white fell

military.office: Keepers of the western pass
military.unit: two stone-hall pairs, 4 giants
military.ties: Lindnes's two pairs are counted in the kingdom's standing army and watch the western fells for the king.

FX23-002.power: The westernmost stone border hall at about 1,640 m, toll on the few overland traders, and two fighting pairs.
FX23-002.history: Lindnes is the westernmost of the three stone border halls King Hallvard the Trader raised on the southern fells in the 830s, after the Ivory Peace barred Eastfolk trappers from the high country. It stands at about 1,640 m where no timber grows, and about 60 giants of Valdhall's kin keep it. They watch the high passes for trappers and outlaws coming north from the Lakeland and take toll from the few traders who come overland. Lindnes has fought no battle in living memory; its giants were not called to the Hrimfell Raids. In bad winters most of them go down to Valdhall's beaches and leave a single pair on the fell, and Eldest Bard votes with Brenna's Grain Party because Lindnes eats Valdhall's grain.
FX23-002.reputation: A quiet fell hall of toll-takers, loyal to the hand that feeds it.

members.role: Eldest of Lindnes
members.note: He has seen 22 eldests' names cut in the hall stones and expects the next name will be the last.

members.role: Heir; pass-keeper
members.note: She took a toll in 1104 from a Lakeland trader carrying Drevnan crossbows north and let him pass, because the toll was good.

members.role: Torunn's son; pair-fighter
members.note: His pair-partner went down to Valdhall in the hungry winter of 1103 and did not come back up.

famousDead: First eldest of Lindnes; cut the first name on the hall stones.
FX23-002.secret: Torunn let a Lakeland trader carry Drevnan crossbows north over the pass in 1104, and she does not know where they went.
hooks: Drevnan crossbows are somewhere on the White Coast.
Lindnes eats Valdhall's grain and votes as Valdhall says.
Jorund needs a new pair-partner.

FX23-003.name: the Hall of Raghaug
FX23-003.title: Eldest of Raghaug
FX23-003.arms: a grey beacon tower on a black fell

military.office: Keepers of the middle fells
military.unit: a few hall pairs and 20 human hunters
military.ties: Raghaug watches and warns for Jotunhall; its runners carry word to the king faster than any giant can walk.

FX23-003.power: The middle stone border hall above the Lakeland trappers' camps, its beacon, and the king's first warning of anything that comes up the fells.
FX23-003.history: Raghaug is the middle stone border hall, built in the 830s at about 1,620 m above the trappers' camps of the Lakeland edge, and about 70 giants of Jotunhall's kin keep it with a few dozen human hunters. For 270 years they have turned back trapping parties that climb above the tree line, feeding them, shaming them and sending them down without their furs. Raghaug saw the Drevnan settlers come north to the Whale Coast after 1085, and it was Raghaug's runners who first told King Hraldr that Dobin's whalers had killed two Frost Leviathans in 1095. Its beacon can be seen from Jotunhall's southern fells. Eldest Sigrid is loyal to the Old Blood and will vote as Mother Asta asks.
FX23-003.reputation: Stern, fair watchers of the fells, loyal to the king's line to the bone.

members.role: Eldest of Raghaug
members.note: She has turned back forty trapping parties and fed every one of them first.

members.role: Heir; watch-leader
members.note: He has counted the Drevnan trappers' camps below the fell growing every year since 1085 and thinks the truce is a slow defeat.

members.role: Human hunter; head runner of the hall
members.note: He ran the news of the leviathan kills to Jotunhall in 1095, 90 km in a day, and has never been thanked by name.

famousDead: Built Raghaug's beacon and first turned back the trappers.
FX23-003.secret: Valgard has been trading furs with a Drevnan trapper below the fell for news, and the trapper has begun asking about Jotunhall's grain.
hooks: Drevna's trappers are creeping up the fells.
Merrick wants his name cut in the hall's stones.
Sigrid's vote is Mother Asta's to command.

FX23-004.name: the Hall of Skarhamar
FX23-004.title: Eldest of Skarhamar
FX23-004.arms: a grey hammer on a white peak

military.office: Keepers of the high route
military.unit: two stone-hall pairs, 4 giants
military.ties: Skarhamar's pairs fought at Dobin under Torvald of Torholm and stand in the Walking Halls' line.

FX23-004.power: The highest giant hall of the White Coast, the high route to the Lakeland, the Sigberg Stones, and two veteran pairs.
FX23-004.history: Skarhamar is the highest giant hall of the White Coast, a stone border hall at about 1,750 m on the south-eastern fells, built in the 830s and kept by about 60 giants of Torholm's kin. Below it stand the Sigberg Stones, a Thing ring of halls that died in the Long Walk, and Skarhamar's giants clear them of snow for every Midsummer rite. The hall watches the high route between the White Coast and the Lakeland, which Drevnan trappers and traders use when Whale Sound is iced. It sent two pairs to the Hrimfell Raids, and Bjarki of Skarhamar died of crossbow wounds after the attack on Dobin harbor in 1097, the last giant Hrimfell lost in the war. His club hangs over the hall door, and Eldest Gorm wants the truce broken.
FX23-004.reputation: The angriest hall on the fells, and the one closest to the enemy.

members.role: Eldest of Skarhamar
members.note: He touches Bjarki's club every morning and says the truce is a debt to the dead.

members.role: Heir; Bjarki's pair-partner
members.note: She carried Bjarki up the fell after Dobin and has hated crossbows ever since.

members.role: Eldrid's son
members.note: At thirteen he is the youngest giant on the high fells and wants to see the Lakeland, which his mother calls the crossbow country.

famousDead: Died of crossbow wounds after the attack on Dobin, the last giant Hrimfell lost in the raids.
FX23-004.secret: Eldrid has been watching the Drevnan trappers' route on the high fell and has picked the camp where she will start a war if the Thing gives her the chance.
hooks: Skarhamar wants the truce broken.
Eldrid has chosen her target.
The Sigberg Stones must be cleared for Midsummer.

FX23-005.name: the Hookwater family
FX23-005.title: Sergeant of the Jotunhall harpooners
FX23-005.arms: a black harpoon barb on white, painted on their skin boats
FX23-005.words: Guard the knees, take the share.

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Jotunhall harpooners
military.unit: the Jotunhall harpooners, 60 of the Harpooners of the White Coast
military.ties: Hookwaters have guarded the giants' flanks since Grom the Mountain put harpooners beside his pairs, and they fought at Dobin in 1097.

FX23-005.power: Command of sixty harpooners of Jotunhall, two skin boats, and a voice among the human hunters that Arvo Sealbane listens to.
FX23-005.history: Grom the Mountain could neither run nor turn, so he put human harpooners on his flanks and taught the pairs to fight beside them, and the first harpooner he chose was a Hookwater. The family has led Jotunhall's harpooners since, sixty hunters with iron-barbed harpoons who guard the giants' knees. In August 1097 Hookwater harpooners held the giants' flanks at Dobin harbor while the pairs broke the gate, and two of them died there. At the Thing of 1098 Arvo Sealbane asked for a human seat and was refused, and the Hookwaters stood behind him. In 1105 they must decide whether to follow Arvo to Drevna's Whale Coast if the Thing refuses again, or stay beside the giants they have guarded for a century.
FX23-005.reputation: The best harpooners on the coast, with giants' blood on their hands and giants' gratitude in short supply.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Jotunhall harpooners
members.note: He held Ulfar's flank at Dobin and saw the prince's knees go on the ice the winter after.

members.role: Heir; harpooner
members.note: She has promised Arvo Sealbane that the Jotunhall harpooners will go south with him if the Thing refuses.

members.role: Sunniva's son, a child
members.note: He rode on Ulfar's shoulder at the Whale Thanking of 1104 and thinks giants are the best people in the world.

famousDead: First harpooner Grom the Mountain chose for his flank.
Thurstan's brother; killed at Dobin harbor.
FX23-005.secret: Sunniva has sworn the Jotunhall harpooners to Arvo Sealbane's bargain with Dobin without her father's knowledge.
hooks: The Thing's answer to Arvo will split the family.
Thurstan knows the truth about Ulfar's knees.
Aelfric loves the giants his mother may leave.

FX23-006.name: the Haugnes household
FX23-006.title: Pair-Leader of Haugnes
FX23-006.arms: two grey giants breaking a black gate, on white

military.office: Pair-leaders of the Torholm Shore Pairs
military.unit: three of Torholm's eight shore pairs, 6 giants
military.ties: Haugnes giants stand in Torholm's shore pairs facing Whale Sound, and they broke Dobin's harbor gate beside Torvald in 1097.

FX23-006.power: Three of Torholm's shore pairs, the barley stead nearest the stone harbor, and the loudest voices for war in the Walking Halls.
FX23-006.history: The Haugnes household farms the barley stead nearest Torholm's stone harbor and has given the hall its shore pairs since the Hunters' Rising of 412, when its giants fought beside Bolverk the Hard on the ice. In July 1096 a Haugnes pair was in the raiding party caught by Drevnan crossbows at the Torholm shore on a warm day, and they carried Hakki of Torholm's body home. In August 1097 three Haugnes pairs broke Dobin's harbor gate beside Torvald and Brodd and burned the whaling boats. The household spoke against the Truce of Dobin and lost. It trains its young on the shore every winter, facing Dobin's lights across Whale Sound.
FX23-006.reputation: Gate-breakers and grudge-keepers; heroes of the raids to some, the next war to others.

members.role: Head of the household; pair-leader
members.note: He carried Hakki of Torholm's body home from the shore in 1096 and has never let Torvald forget whose son it was.

members.role: Heir; his pair-partner
members.note: She led the shove that broke Dobin's gate and wants another gate.

members.role: Ragnvei's son
members.note: At fifteen he throws stones at Dobin's lights across the sound every night, and none of them reach.

famousDead: Fought beside Bolverk the Hard on the ice in the Hunters' Rising.
FX23-006.secret: Thorvard has seen Brodd binding Torvald's failing knee before dawn, and he wants Ragnvei to lead the shore pairs instead.
hooks: The household wants the truce broken.
Thorvard could unseat the leader of the Walking Halls.
Ragnvei wants another gate.

FX23-007.name: the Vidheim household
FX23-007.title: Keeper of the Ice Shrine of Jorhamar
FX23-007.arms: a white whale under a blue arch of ice, on grey
FX23-007.power: The Ice Shrine of Jorhamar, the leading of the Whale Thanking for the western halls, and the blessing that the unicorn trade has always needed.
FX23-007.history: The Ice Shrine of Jorhamar stands in Valdhall's land, a cave of old ice where the halls bring the first whale tooth of each spring, and the household of Vidheim has kept it since the years of the Taking-In. Vidheim giants lead the Whale Thanking for the western halls, and they hold, as all the halls do, that each whale carries an ancestor's soul. Since Valdhall began selling the spiral tusks of the small whales as unicorn horn in 1059, the household has had to bless a trade it thinks is close to selling grandmothers. Skuli of Valdhall's bargain in 1104, showing a Drevnan trader the bay where the tusk-whales calve, has turned that unease into anger. The household's eldest has told Brenna of Valdhall that the Mother will answer.
FX23-007.reputation: Devout, stern and lately dangerous; the conscience Valdhall would rather not hear.

members.role: Head of the household; Keeper of the Ice Shrine of Jorhamar
members.note: She has told Brenna of Valdhall that the Mother will answer Skuli's bargain, and she half hopes to be right.

members.role: Heir; chanter
members.note: He has learned the old chant from Grani the Rememberer and knows that Valdhall's Mothers come first in it.

members.role: Sigvald's daughter, a child
members.note: She was born the year the tusk-whales came closest to Valdhall's shore, and the household calls her whale-blessed.

famousDead: Kept the shrine through the Famine Winter of 991, when no whale stranded on the coast.
FX23-007.secret: Sigvald knows the old chant's order and means to sing it at the Thing of 1105 if Grani does not, which would shake the Law of the Mothers.
hooks: Skuli's bargain may bring Drevnan whalers to the calving bay.
Sigvald could sing the old chant at Midsummer.
The household must bless or curse the unicorn trade.

FX23-008.name: the Scrimmer family
FX23-008.title: Master of the Scrimmer shed
FX23-008.arms: a white chevron of carved ivory, on black
FX23-008.power: A carving shed beside the royal ivory workshop, Northreach buyers who trust their combs and cups, and a skill no one else on the coast has.
FX23-008.history: When King Orm founded the ivory carvers' workshop at Jotunhall in 1062, the Scrimmers were the first human family he set to work, carving walrus tusk into combs, game pieces and cups for the southern trade. Grete Tuskcutter heads the workshop in 1105, and the Scrimmers have never forgiven Orm's successors for passing them over. The family now carves in its own shed beside the workshop's and sells through Northreach traders. Since 1059 the most valuable thing on the coast has been the spiral tusk of the small whales, sold south as unicorn horn for up to 3,000 suns. In 1103 the Scrimmers learned to carve a walrus tusk into a spiral that a southern buyer cannot tell from the real thing.
FX23-008.reputation: Gifted, bitter carvers whose work is admired and whose word is not.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Scrimmer shed
members.note: He carved King Orm's game set in 1063 and still talks about it.

members.role: Heir; carver
members.note: She carved the first false spiral tusk in 1103 and is ashamed of how good it is.

members.role: Merewyn's son; apprentice
members.note: He is to carry three false tusks to a Northreach trader at the summer landing, and he does not know they are false.

FX23-008.secret: The Scrimmers carve walrus tusk into false unicorn horn, and if the south finds one, the whole White Coast trade is ruined.
hooks: A false unicorn horn is going south this summer.
Grete Tuskcutter's workshop suspects the Scrimmers.
Sewald does not know what he carries.

FX23-009.name: the Reinholt family
FX23-009.title: Herd-master of Hjalvik
FX23-009.arms: a brown reindeer bull on a white felt banner
FX23-009.power: About 1,400 reindeer at Hjalvik, the sledges that drag the king, and the best-fed human village on the White Coast.
FX23-009.history: About 2,200 humans live under Valdgard, and the Reinholts of Hjalvik have herded its reindeer since Sigvald the Woodwright's households came to the forest edge in 834 and brought their tribute-folk with them. The family's herd of about 1,400 animals pulls the hunters' sledges, feeds Valdgard in winter and drags timber down from the Eyheim Wood. Reinholt sledges dragged King Hraldr to the raids on Dobin, and the family's men have dragged the king's sledge at every Thing since. Valdgard's fields are the richest in the kingdom, and the Reinholts are as well fed as any tribute-folk on the White Coast. They have no wish to follow Arvo Sealbane south, and they have begun to quarrel with hunter families who do.
FX23-009.reputation: Comfortable, cautious herders; the hunters call them the king's sledge-dogs.

members.role: Head of the family; Herd-master of Hjalvik
members.note: He dragged King Hraldr's sledge to Dobin and back and says the king weighs more than Grom's whale.

members.role: Heir; sledge-master
members.note: She has quarrelled openly with Sunniva Hookwater over Arvo Sealbane's plan to take 400 families south.

members.role: Halvard's younger son
members.note: He is secretly going south with Arvo's families and has already sold his share of the herd.

famousDead: Led the first tribute-folk herd to Valdgard with Sigvald the Woodwright in 834.
FX23-009.secret: Dunstan has sold his share of the herd to a Drevnan buyer and means to leave with Arvo's families after Midsummer.
hooks: The hunters' exodus divides the human families.
Dunstan's secret sale will be found out at the spring count.
The king's sledge must be dragged to the Thing.

FX23-010.name: the Snowcairn family
FX23-010.title: Head of the Snowcairns
FX23-010.arms: no arms; three stones piled in a cairn, scratched on a sledge-runner
FX23-010.power: The high routes past the border halls, dog sledges, and buyers among Northreach agents and Velgrad's fur dealers.
FX23-010.history: The Ivory Peace says ivory is weighed at Valdhall and Jotunhall under one set of weights, and since 1060 the Snowcairns have made a living proving it wrong. They are descendants of Eastfolk trappers at the Valdgard forest edge who carry walrus ivory, white bear pelts and the occasional spiral tusk over the fells to Northreach agents and Velgrad's Ostmir fairs, paying no share to any hall. They know the high routes past the border halls and when each watch-pair sleeps. Under the Hunters' Law a human who takes more than his share answers to his hall, and the halls have caught two Snowcairns in 45 years. In 1105 the family is carrying something heavier than ivory: letters between Arvo Sealbane and the Drevnan lord at Dobin.
FX23-010.reputation: Fell-runners and fur-thieves to the halls; to the hunters, the only free family on the coast.

members.role: Head of the family; trapper
members.note: He has crossed below Skarhamar's watch eighty times and once shared a fire with a giant who pretended not to see him.

members.role: Heir; his daughter
members.note: She carries Arvo Sealbane's letters to Lord Kolin's man at Dobin, sewn into a fox pelt.

members.role: Hamo's brother; fur trader at the Ostmir fairs
members.note: He sells white bear pelts to Velgrad and news of the White Coast to whoever buys it.

FX23-010.secret: Hawise carries Arvo Sealbane's letters to the lord of Dobin, and if the halls learn of it the Hunters' Law could give her to the sea.
hooks: The letters to Dobin could decide where 400 families live.
Skarhamar's watch has seen tracks on the high fell.
Emeric sells White Coast news in Velgrad.

FX24-001.name: House Nakhli
FX24-001.title: Lord of the Basir Date Gardens
FX24-001.arms: a gold date palm on a green field, a black river-line beneath

military.office: Captains of the Basir Fields soldier-farmers
military.unit: about 1,000 of the Basir Fields soldier-farmers, spears in their own villages
military.ties: The Nakhli hold their gardens on condition of service, and their villagers are the spearmen who would meet a Qadiri column on the Bahesh.

FX24-001.power: The irrigated date gardens of the lower Bahesh that House Tarsi lost in 1025, about 30 villages, and the river water-shares that go with them.
FX24-001.history: The Nakhli were date-farmers who lifted Bahesh water onto Tarsi fields with swing-poles, as their fathers had for 170 years. In 1024, when Hazimi riders let the Sabrans into the Basir fields, Sahl the Gardener opened the sluices to them and showed them the Tarsi granaries. Emir Tahir gave him the abandoned Tarsi gardens in 1025, and the family has farmed them since with the old Tarsi deeds still missing from the house chest. They are the richest farmers of the emirate and the most exposed: every Qadiri war plan ends in the Basir fields. The present lord hopes for peace and drills his villagers twice a month in case.
FX24-001.reputation: Rich gardeners risen from the swing-pole, despised by the Qadiri exiles as turncoat tenants.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Basir Date Gardens
members.note: Still lifts a swing-pole at harvest to remind his sons where the land came from.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the water-shares
members.note: Argues water-shares before the Well-Keepers of Basir and wins more than she loses.

members.role: Heir; captain of the soldier-farmers
members.note: Has walked the Sabun road to the pass and back to know where the Qadiri will come.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Found an old Tarsi boundary stone in the gardens and has hidden it under her bed.

famousDead: Opened the Basir sluices to the Sabrans in 1024 and received the Tarsi gardens.
FX24-001.secret: Sahl the Gardener took the Tarsi deeds from the burning house in 1024 and buried them; the Nakhli know where, and the deeds are good in any Qadiri court.
hooks: The Qadiri column of 1105 will march straight at the Basir gardens.
A Nahiri exile comes in disguise to look at his family's old fields.
Hiba's boundary stone matches a deed someone is trying to buy.

FX24-002.name: House Sarabadi
FX24-002.title: Lord of Sarabad in the South March
FX24-002.arms: a white wheat-sheaf on brown, bound with a red cord

military.office: Holders of the Sarabad levy of the South March
military.unit: about 400 levy spears and 50 camel riders of Sarabad
military.ties: The Sarabadi feed the South March and send their younger sons to ride with the Zarani slave-riders.

FX24-002.power: The wheat and cattle country around Sarabad, the granaries of the South March and the road from Zaran to the coast.
FX24-002.history: Jafar Zarani gave the town of Sarabad to his caravan quartermaster, Rabi, two years after he became Lord of the South March in 1041. The Sarabadi have fed the march since, and their granaries carry the Zarani riders through every raid into the Western Veld. The family rides with the slavers and eats from their trade, and most of its sons have done so without thinking. The present lord's daughter, sent to Sabra for schooling, came home in 1102 a believer in Mahmud the Just's mercy and has begun teaching the captives in the Zaran pens the Book of Wells, which would make them free. Her father has not stopped her. Her cousin has noticed.
FX24-002.reputation: Solid wheat lords of the march, Zarani men to the bone, with one troublesome daughter.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Sarabad
members.note: Has fed the Zarani raids for 30 years and never once ridden on one.

members.role: His daughter
members.note: Teaches the captives in the Zaran pens to recite the Book of Wells, which may make them free under Mahmud's rulings.

members.role: Heir; nephew and adopted son
members.note: Rides with the slave-riders and has reported Lubna's teaching to Musa Zarani.

members.role: Ghalib's wife
members.note: Fears the Zarani more than the Book and begs her daughter to stop.

famousDead: Jafar Zarani's quartermaster, first lord of Sarabad.
FX24-002.secret: Some of the captives Lubna teaches are Sandfolk children from the Marad camps, and they have told her so.
hooks: Lubna asks a stranger to carry a Marad child's name to the Well-Mother.
Musa Zarani demands Ghalib choose between his daughter and his lord.
Diyab is offered the lordship of Sarabad if Lubna disappears.

FX24-003.name: House Akhdari
FX24-003.title: Lord of the Green Wadis of Sabira
FX24-003.arms: a white camel couchant in a green valley, on red

military.office: Camel captains of the Hazimi riders
military.unit: about 300 of the Hazimi camel riders of the Sabira wadis
military.ties: The Akhdari ride under the Hazimi banner and have done so since the 880s, when both families guarded the Qadiri governors' roads.

FX24-003.power: Terraced wadis and camel pastures in the hills above Sabira, and 300 riders sworn to the Hazimi.
FX24-003.history: The Akhdari were road guards with the Hazimi under the Qadiri governors, and the Hazimi gave them the green wadis of Sabira in 912. Their riders died of thirst beside the Hazimi in the Sabun Pass in 1022, and they changed sides with them in 1024. They have followed the Hazimi in everything since, including, now, the Old Allegiance. The head of the house has sworn to ride with Walid Hazimi whatever he does. His wife is a Sabrani cousin who lives, by Sabrani house law, half the year at the Emir's palace, and the family is split down the middle.
FX24-003.reputation: Old upland camel lords, loyal to the Hazimi above the Emir, quietly nostalgic for Qadir.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Green Wadis
members.note: Rode down the Sabun beside Walid Hazimi as a boy captain in 1075 and would follow him into Qadir.

members.role: His wife; of a Sabrani cousin line
members.note: Lives half the year in the Emir's palace by house law and eats salt at every meal like the rest of the blood.

members.role: Heir; rider of the Camel Guard
members.note: Serves under Nuri Hazimi in the Camel Guard and loves the Emir's son like a brother.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Raised in the palace among Sabrani cousins; she sweats in winter like them.

famousDead: Received the Sabira wadis from the Hazimi in 912.
FX24-003.secret: Hamdan Akhdari carried Walid Hazimi's November 1104 letter to the Sabun Pass himself.
hooks: Talal must choose between the Hazimi and the Emir's son.
The Emir's spies ask Areej who left Sabira in November.
Durra's sweating marks her as Sabrani blood, and a Qadiri agent wants her.

FX24-004.name: House Qatrani
FX24-004.title: Lord of the Nahur Toll
FX24-004.arms: a black barge on a blue river, a gold chain across it
FX24-004.power: The Gold Road toll at Nahur, upriver of Sabra, goat and gum land along the Bahesh, and the friendship of the Talun ferrymen.
FX24-004.history: Emir Tahir gave the toll at Nahur in 1028 to Qatran, a caravan guard who had led Sabran gold up and down the Bahesh through the war. The family takes the emirate's due on every Gold Road load that comes down the river, one dinar for twenty camels, and keeps a share. It has grown rich on the treaty of 1063 and poor in every year the Gold Road runs thin. The Qatrani deal with Clan Talun at the crossing upriver and with Clan Marad on the west bank, and they know the Sandfolk better than any other Sabran lord. Since 1103 the Marad children have soured that friendship, and Marad riders no longer drink at Nahur.
FX24-004.reputation: Shrewd toll-lords of the river, more at home with Sandfolk than at the Emir's court.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Nahur Toll
members.note: Drinks camel milk with Talun chiefs and wine with Sabran brokers on the same night.

members.role: His wife; of a Marad chief's family
members.note: Clan Marad's daughter, married to bind the west bank; her sister's son was among the children taken in 1103.

members.role: Heir; master of the toll-house
members.note: Keeps a count of every caravan and every slave coffle that passes the toll.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Rides with her mother's Marad kin in the summer camps.

famousDead: Led gold up the Bahesh in the war; first lord of the toll.
FX24-004.secret: Shadi's toll-books record a coffle of 30 children passing Nahur in 1103 with a Zarani captain, coming from the Marad side, not the Veld.
hooks: Ruba demands her husband give the toll-books to Clan Marad.
Musa Zarani's riders come to Nahur asking for the 1103 page.
Clan Marad closes the west bank to Sabran caravans.

FX24-005.name: House Hawari
FX24-005.title: Lord of Azara Harbor
FX24-005.arms: a white pearl in a black oyster, on blue
FX24-005.words: The sea gives to the patient.

military.office: Captains of the Pearl Banks watch
military.unit: the Pearl Banks watch at Azara, about 300 scouts and light foot
military.ties: The Hawari command the watch that guards the pearl banks and the coast between Azara and the Oil Shore.

FX24-005.power: The harbor and market of Azara, the harbor dues of the pearling fleet and the Pearl Banks watch.
FX24-005.history: When Emir Farid walled the Oil Shore in 1036, he needed a lord at Azara he could trust to keep the pearling town quiet next door. He chose Hawar, a pearl master who had captained a fire-boat on the Night of Fire. The Hawari have held the harbor since, between the free divers, the slave boats of the Pearl Masters and the token-guarded Oil Shore a day's walk away. They take the harbor dues and keep out of the quarrel between Mahmud the Just and Jamila Sabrani, which is getting harder every year. In November 1104 a runaway oil-slave was seen in Azara, and the Hawari watch has been told to find her and has not.
FX24-005.reputation: Careful harbor-lords who try to please everyone in a town where nobody is pleased.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of Azara Harbor
members.note: Pays the slave boats' dues and the free divers' feast with the same hand.

members.role: His wife
members.note: Treats divers with burst ears and bleeding noses, free and slave alike.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Pearl Banks watch
members.note: Has been ordered to find the runaway boiler and has decided not to look very hard.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Dives with the free-diver girls in secret and has reached seven fathoms.

famousDead: Captained a fire-boat on the Night of Fire; first lord of Azara harbor.
FX24-005.secret: The runaway boiler Salwa Ropecutter is hidden in a diver's house within sight of the Hawari harbor-tower, and Sami knows which one.
hooks: The Oil Shore Watch comes to Azara to search the divers' houses.
Lamya is caught diving and her father must punish her or bless her.
A Varennan captain offers Sami 500 suns for the runaway.

FX24-006.name: House Mahari
FX24-006.title: Lord of the Sabira Terraces, Husband-line of the Emir's House
FX24-006.arms: a gold crown over a white pearl, on dark red
FX24-006.words: Close to the fire, never in it.
FX24-006.power: Wheat and fruit terraces at Sabira, a household in the Emir's palace by marriage, and the ear of the Sabrani family.
FX24-006.history: In 1040 a Mahari wheat lord of Sabira married a daughter of Emir Farid, and by Farid's house law he moved into the palace at Sabra and his children took the Sabrani name. The Mahari kept their own name for the sons of a second marriage and their own lands at Sabira, and they have married into the Sabrani twice since. They are the Emir's kin by marriage, live at court half the year and know the house's habits: the salt at every meal, the servant with salted water at noon. The present lord's son by a Sabrani mother is counted a Sabrani; his son by a second wife is a Mahari and heir to the terraces, and the two brothers do not love each other.
FX24-006.reputation: Courtiers of the Emir's household, well dressed, well informed and never quite trusted.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Sabira Terraces
members.note: Has dined with three Emirs and knows which one drinks salted water at dawn.

members.role: Heir; son of the second wife
members.note: Resents his Sabrani half-brother and sells palace gossip to Faisal the Broker's people.

members.role: Jasim's second wife
members.note: Runs the Sabira terraces while her husband lives at court.

members.role: Raed's son
members.note: Plays with the Sabrani children in the palace and has seen what they eat.

famousDead: Married a daughter of Emir Farid in 1040 and moved into the palace.
FX24-006.secret: Raed Mahari has told a Qadiri agent that Sabrani of the blood cannot keep the Dry Month fast without salt, a weakness that could kill an Emir in a long siege.
hooks: A palace poisoning plot needs someone who knows the Sabrani salt.
Raed's half-brother learns who has been selling the household's secrets.
Jasim is asked to carry a marriage offer from Qadir.

FX24-007.name: House Fahhami
FX24-007.title: Lord of the Charcoal Hills of Nahur
FX24-007.arms: a red flame over a black hill, on sand
FX24-007.power: Thorn-scrub hills, charcoal kilns and goat herds around Nahur, and the sole contract to fuel the boiling-sheds of the Oil Fort.
FX24-007.history: When Farid built the Oil Fort in 1036, the Nafari boiling-sheds needed fuel that did not come by sea where it could be counted. In 1037 the Emir gave a charcoal-burner of Nahur, Fahham, the thorn hills and the contract to feed the sheds, and the Fahhami have sent their charcoal to Zariya in sealed sacks ever since. They have never entered the Oil Shore; their sacks are left at the token-gate. But a family that has counted sacks for 70 years knows how much fire the sheds burn, and so roughly how much oil comes out. The present lord has worked it out and has told no one, which is the wisest thing his family has ever done.
FX24-007.reputation: Sooty hill lords, rich from a contract nobody discusses.

members.role: Head of the family; Lord of the Charcoal Hills
members.note: Has worked out from 70 years of sack-counts how many jars the Oil Fort fills a year, and has burned the sum.

members.role: His wife; mistress of the kilns
members.note: Has black hands and the best kilns in the emirate.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Found his father's burned sum half-legible in the hearth and copied what he could read.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Tends the goats and talks to every traveler on the Bahesh road.

famousDead: Received the thorn hills and the Oil Fort fuel contract in 1037.
FX24-007.secret: From the sack-counts the Fahhami can reckon the Oil Fort's output, about twice what Lucerna is told it buys; Khalaf has a half-copy of the sum.
hooks: A Lucernan factor visits Nahur asking about charcoal prices.
The Oil-Master suddenly doubles the charcoal order for 1105.
Khalaf shows his copy to a friend in Sabra.

FX24-008.name: House Bandari
FX24-008.title: Castellan of Daham Tower
FX24-008.arms: a black tower with an eye of fire, on white

military.office: Hereditary Castellans of Daham Tower and watchers of the northern sea
military.unit: Daham Tower garrison, about 300 crossbowmen and a chain of signal fires
military.ties: The Bandari keep the northern lookout that warned of the Qadiri galleys in 1024, and their fires reach the harbor towers of Sabra in an hour.

FX24-008.power: Daham Tower on the northern coast, its signal-fire chain to Sabra and a small fishing harbor.
FX24-008.history: In August 1024 a fisherman named Bandar saw the 19 Qadiri galleys rounding the cape and ran a day and a night to Sabra to warn Farid Sabrani. The fire-boats were ready when the galleys anchored. Emir Tahir built Daham Tower on the cape in 1026 and gave it to Bandar's son. The Bandari have watched the northern sea since, and their signal fires can carry a warning to the harbor towers within an hour. If Qadir's fleet comes in 1105, the Bandari will see it first. The present castellan's brother sold fish to Blackreef boats for years and knows their captains, which the family keeps quiet.
FX24-008.reputation: The emirate's watchmen, honored every Night of Fire and rarely thought of in between.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Daham Tower
members.note: Named for the runner of 1024 and sleeps in the lantern room from April to September.

members.role: His brother; master of the fishing harbor
members.note: Sells fish and water to Blackreef boats and drinks with their captains.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the signal fires
members.note: Has rebuilt the fire chain with oil-soaked faggots that light in the wind.

members.role: Shadya's son
members.note: Runs the cape path every morning, timing himself against the old story.

famousDead: Ran a day and a night to warn Sabra of the Qadiri galleys in 1024.
FX24-008.secret: Ihab Bandari has carried oil jars out to Blackreef boats off the cape at night for the Emir's own agents since 1092.
hooks: Sails are seen off the cape in April, and Shadya must judge whether to light the chain.
A Qadiri spy is found among the fishermen.
A Blackreef captain asks Ihab for twice as many jars.

FX24-009.name: House Najjari
FX24-009.title: Master of the Fire-Boat Sheds
FX24-009.arms: an orange flame on a black boat, on blue

military.office: Hereditary masters of the fire-boat sheds and captains of the Fire-Boat Crews
military.unit: the fire-boat sheds of Sabra and four fire-boat crews, about 160 men
military.ties: A Najjari built and steered the boats of the Night of Fire, and every fire-boat in Sabra has come from their sheds since.

FX24-009.power: The fire-boat sheds by the harbor towers, the craft of building the small boats that carry oil pots, and four crews.
FX24-009.history: Najjar the Boatwright built the line of small boats that Farid Sabrani smeared with fire-oil on 19 August 1024, and steered the second boat himself into the Qadiri galleys. He swam back with his back on fire and lived 40 more years. The emirs have bought every fire-boat from the Najjari since, and the family's sons serve as crew captains under the heir. Tahir Sabrani learned his oil-pot work from Saad the Burnt and his boats from the Najjari, and the family loves him. The present master is old and badly scarred, and he does not want to see a second Night of Fire; his son cannot wait.
FX24-009.reputation: The heroes of the harbor, honored on the naming wall every year and paid like shipwrights the rest of it.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Fire-Boat Sheds
members.note: Lost an ear and two fingers to a pot that broke early in 1080 and builds every boat himself.

members.role: Heir; captain of four fire-boats
members.note: Has volunteered to lead Tahir's raid on Miruma through the Strait.

members.role: Zaki's wife; keeper of the shed books
members.note: Reads the names of the lost on the naming wall every Night of Fire.

members.role: Zaki's son
members.note: Swims across the harbor every morning because his great-great-grandfather did it on fire.

famousDead: Built and steered the fire-boats of the Night of Fire in 1024.
FX24-009.secret: Hashim Najjari has written to Saad the Burnt that half the new fire-boats are badly pitched and will burn their crews before they reach Miruma.
hooks: Zaki's crew is chosen for the raid on Miruma.
A Qadiri marine captain's family swears blood against the Najjari.
Saad the Burnt asks Hashim to say nothing about the bad boats.

FX24-010.name: House Jaddi
FX24-010.title: Noon-Captain of the Camel Guard
FX24-010.arms: a gold sun over a running camel, on red

military.office: Hereditary captains of a camel-hundred of the Camel Guard of the Emir
military.unit: two camel-hundreds of the Camel Guard at Hazim, about 200 lancers and archers
military.ties: A Jaddi has led a camel-hundred of the Camel Guard since Farid raised it, and every Jaddi boy trains at the Camel School of Hazim.

FX24-010.power: A captaincy in the Camel Guard, a breeding herd of noon-trained camels and the trust of the Emir's heir.
FX24-010.history: Jadd was a camel-boy of the Hazim uplands who rode beside Farid Sabrani in the Sabun Pass ambush of 1022 and carried the prince's salted water at noon. When Farid raised the Camel Guard in 1036 he gave Jadd's son a camel-hundred, and the Jaddi have commanded it since. They are trained by the Hazimi Camel School and paid by the Emir, and that has never mattered until now. The present captain knows Nuri Hazimi saw his uncle's courier leave in November 1104. He also knows that the family servant who carries the heir's salted water is his own cousin.
FX24-010.reputation: Hard noon riders, the Emir's men first and Hazim's men second, if anyone asked.

members.role: Head of the family; Noon-Captain of the Camel Guard
members.note: Has fought at noon in August 40 times and never once let the Emir's heir see him thirsty.

members.role: His wife; master of the noon herd
members.note: Breeds camels that will walk at noon in August, which takes six years to teach.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Camel Guard
members.note: Rides at Tahir Sabrani's side and wants to be at Miruma, not Hazim.

members.role: Ayham's cousin; water-bearer of the Emir's heir
members.note: Carries salted water for Tahir Sabrani at every drill and has sworn on the Book never to say why.

famousDead: Carried Farid Sabrani's salted water in the Sabun Pass in 1022.
FX24-010.secret: The Jaddi have carried the Sabrani's salted water at noon for three generations; they know the Salt-skin's weakness better than any enemy.
hooks: Nuri Hazimi asks Ayham what the Camel Guard would do if Hazim rode north.
A Qadiri agent tries to buy Hilal.
Mazin deserts the Camel Guard to join the fire-boats.

FX24-011.name: House Murjani
FX24-011.title: Captain of the Token-Gate
FX24-011.arms: a red coral branch over a black gate, on sand

military.office: Hereditary captains of the token-gate of the Oil Shore Watch
military.unit: the token-gate company of the Oil Shore Watch, about 200 guards and archers
military.ties: The Murjani have kept the only gate onto the Oil Shore since the token law of 1036, and they kill anyone who comes without the Emir's brass token.

FX24-011.power: Command of the token-gate, the right to kill strangers on the Oil Shore, and a list of every token ever issued.
FX24-011.history: Murjan the Coral-Cutter was a pearl-diver turned soldier whom Farid set at the gate of the new Oil Fort in 1036 with one order: no token, no life. His line has kept the gate since. They have killed about 30 people in 70 years, most of them lost fishermen, and they do not apologize. They keep the list of tokens issued and returned and are proud that none has been lost. In November 1104 a boiling-shed burned at Zariya, three slaves fled in the smoke, and a dead cook's token went missing in the confusion. The captain has told the Oil-Master the token was burned with its owner. He is not sure.
FX24-011.reputation: Grim gatekeepers of the Oil Shore, feared up and down the coast.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Token-Gate
members.note: Has killed nine people at the gate himself and dreams of each one.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the token list
members.note: Knows that the token list for November 1104 is one short.

members.role: Heir; lieutenant of the Watch
members.note: Was on the gate the night of the fire and let a smoke-blackened figure through.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Brings water to the slave boilers when her father is not looking.

famousDead: First captain of the token-gate under Farid.
FX24-011.secret: A token is missing from the November 1104 list, and Wasil let a smoke-blackened figure out through the gate on the night of the fire.
hooks: Rima the Water-Seller is seen with a brass token at the Pens.
The Oil-Master orders a recount of every token.
Wasil must confess or let his father take the blame.

FX24-012.name: House Dalali
FX24-012.title: Weigher of the Gold Yards
FX24-012.words: Honest weight, fair price, no questions.
FX24-012.power: Yards and scales in the Gold Yards of Sabra, advances on Gold Road caravans, and a seat among the Caravan Brokers of Sabra under Faisal the Broker.
FX24-012.history: The Dalali began weighing Tedana gold at the Bahesh mouth after the Salt and Gold Pact of 918 and set up their own scales in 921. They have weighed Zanari gold for Qadiri governors, the rebel Tahir and three Emirs since, and they lend against each spring's caravan. Since 1071 they have used the weights of the Scale Pact, set at House Sorondo's scale house in Zanara, and in 1102 the old weigher noticed that the Sorondo weights run light by about one part in fifty. He told no one but his account book. The house is close to Faisal the Broker and signs some of the 50,000 suns of caravan advances the emirate owes the Gold Houses.
FX24-012.reputation: Exact, wealthy gold-weighers with a long memory and a short temper for cheats.

members.role: Head of the family; Weigher of the Gold Yards
members.note: Can tell a short weight by the swing of the beam and found the Sorondo weights light in 1102.

members.role: Heir; master of the caravan advances
members.note: Lends against caravans that have not left Zanara yet and has never lost a sun.

members.role: Son; caravan-master on the Bahesh road
members.note: Rides with every spring caravan and knows the Talun chief's sons by name.

members.role: Rania's daughter
members.note: Plays with the brass weights and can already tell which ones are false.

famousDead: Set up the first Dalali scales in the Gold Yards in 921.
FX24-012.secret: Rafi Dalali's account book proves the Scale Pact weights run light by one part in fifty, a fraud that has cost Sabra and Qadir a fortune in gold.
hooks: A Zanaran Gold House agent offers to buy the account book.
War closes the Bahesh, and the spring caravan is paid for but cannot arrive.
Faisal the Broker asks Rania to sign a larger advance than she likes.

FX24-013.name: House Ghawasi
FX24-013.title: Rope-Chief of the Free Divers of Azara
FX24-013.arms: a white rope coiled around a blue stone (painted on their boat's prow)
FX24-013.power: Three family boats on the shallow banks, the right to name the free divers' chants, and the respect of every free diver on the gulf.
FX24-013.history: The Ghawasi have dived the banks off Azara for longer than Sabra has had a name, one family to a boat, with turtle-shell nose-clips and a knife. They name each other by depth: the head of the family is Twelve-Fathom, his son Ten-Breath. Since 1062 the slave boats of the Pearl Masters have taken the deep banks where the best pearls lie, and the free divers have been pushed onto the shallows. The Ghawasi despise the slave boats and lead the free divers' chant on the Night of Fire, when the names of the lost are read on the harbor wall. They are the heart of Mahmud the Just's support on the gulf, and they hide escaped slaves when they can.
FX24-013.reputation: Proud free divers, poor and fearless, the conscience of the pearling coast.

members.role: Head of the family; Rope-Chief, called Twelve-Fathom
members.note: Has dived to twelve fathoms on one breath and buried two brothers who tried for thirteen.

members.role: His wife; rope-tender
members.note: Hides a runaway oil-slave in her net-loft and calls her a cousin from Basir.

members.role: Heir, called Ten-Breath
members.note: Wants to cut the ropes of a slave boat at sea and free its divers.

members.role: Daughter, called Seven-Fathom
members.note: Teaches a harbor-lord's daughter to dive in secret.

famousDead: Free diver who dove the deep banks before the slave boats came.
FX24-013.secret: The runaway boiler hidden in Hayfa Ghawasi's loft knows the secret road to the seeps.
hooks: Fayez plans to cut the ropes of a Lului slave boat.
The Oil Shore Watch searches Azara for the runaway.
Mahmud the Just asks the Ghawasi to bring believing divers to the Well-house on Well Day.

FX24-014.name: House Lului
FX24-014.title: Pearl-Master of the Deep Banks
FX24-014.arms: three white pearls on dark blue
FX24-014.power: Eleven pearling boats, about 140 slave divers and a share in the Zaran pens, under the Pearl-Master Jamila Sabrani.
FX24-014.history: The Lului were free divers until 1062, when Emir Nasir wanted more pearls and House Zarani began bringing young divers from the Western Veld. Mahdi Lului bought the first three slave divers sold at Zaran and was rich within ten years. The family has dived slaves on the deep banks off Azara since, weighted with stones and lowered on ropes, and one in ten dies each season. In 1093, a bad year, Jamila Sabrani bought the boats of three ruined masters; the Lului sold her two and became her partners. They stand with the Pearl Masters against Mahmud the Just and have hidden 14 believing divers from his count.
FX24-014.reputation: Rich pearl masters, the free divers call them the Rope's partners.

members.role: Head of the family; Pearl-Master of the Deep Banks
members.note: Was a free diver until he was 12 and has never been in the water since.

members.role: His wife; keeper of the pearl books
members.note: Weighs every pearl and pays the Emir's best-of-the-week before anyone else touches the catch.

members.role: Heir; master of the slave boats
members.note: Sends a diver down again if he comes up empty.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Studies at the Well-house and has begun to ask her father how many of his divers pray.

famousDead: Bought the first slave divers sold at Zaran in 1062.
FX24-014.secret: Four of the Lului slave divers are Sandfolk children of the Marad camps, bought in 1103 knowing what they were.
hooks: Nawal brings Mahmud the Just to the Lului boat-sheds.
A slave boat's rope is cut at sea.
The Well-Mother of the Sand Clans names the Lului an enemy of the clans.

FX24-015.name: House Marsawi
FX24-015.title: Well-Keeper of Basir
FX24-015.arms: a blue well-mouth under a white book, on green
FX24-015.power: The Well-house and court of Basir, a seat among Sabra's Well-Keepers and the judging of water-shares on the lower Bahesh.
FX24-015.history: Before 1025 the Keepers of Basir answered to the House of Water in Qadira, and a Qadiri Keeper overruled them on water-shares in favor of the Tarsi. When Sabra broke away, Ishaq Marsawi, a Basir Keeper, was among those who broke from the House of Water and confirmed Tahir as Emir before the Book. His line has kept the Well-house of Basir since. The family is split by Mahmud the Just's rulings: the old Keeper holds that a slave who takes the Path after capture is still a slave, as the Pearl Masters say; his daughter, also a Keeper, sits on Mahmud's side and has freed eleven divers. Father and daughter judge in the same court on alternate days.
FX24-015.reputation: Learned Keepers of the fields, honest and divided.

members.role: Head of the family; Well-Keeper of Basir
members.note: Holds that the Book says nothing of slaves who convert after capture and so the Pearl Masters may keep them.

members.role: Heir; Well-Keeper of Basir
members.note: Has freed eleven believing divers and is Mahmud the Just's surest voice outside the capital.

members.role: Son; clerk of the Emir's water court
members.note: Writes judgments for the Emir and knows the oil is never mentioned in any of them.

members.role: Ilham's daughter
members.note: Carries water to the freed divers' camp behind the Well-house.

famousDead: Broke from the House of Water in 1025 and confirmed Tahir as Emir.
FX24-015.secret: Yaqub Marsawi has taken a gift of pearls from Jamila Sabrani's people every year since 1095.
hooks: Father and daughter must rule on the same diver on Well Day.
Ilham's freed divers are seized on the Basir road.
Muhsin is asked to draft a judgment that names the oil.

FX24-016.name: House Zaydani
FX24-016.title: Master of the Zahas Herds
FX24-016.arms: a brown camel and a white horse face to face, on green

military.office: Remount-masters of the Camel Guard
military.unit: the Zahas herds, about 3,000 camels and 400 horses
military.ties: The Zaydani raise the remounts of the Camel Guard and send herd-boys with it as camel-tenders.

FX24-016.power: The grass steppe of Zahas, its hay meadows and the remount contracts of the Camel Guard and the caravan brokers.
FX24-016.history: Zayd the Herdsman bred camels for Farid's Camel Guard on the Zahas grass from 1036, and in 1041 the Emir gave him the steppe as his own. The Zaydani have raised the emirate's riding camels since, and a few horses for officers, bought as stallions from Qadiri breeders in Hazifa. They are the one Sabran family that trades openly with the Sand Clans, buying Saran camels at the Bahesh bend. Since the Marad children were taken in 1103 the Sandfolk have raised their prices, and the herd-master has written three times to the Emir that a blood feud with the clans would leave the Camel Guard on foot within two years.
FX24-016.reputation: Steppe herders with Sandfolk friends, plain-spoken and indispensable.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Zahas Herds
members.note: Has written to the Emir three times about the Marad children and been answered once.

members.role: His wife; Sandfolk-born
members.note: Born to Clan Saran and married across the border in 1072; she still owns her own herd, as Sandfolk women do.

members.role: Heir; camel-master of the Camel Guard
members.note: Tends the Guard's camels on the Sabun road and has seen Hazimi riders gather.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Was promised to a Saran chief's grandson before 1103; the promise is now uncertain.

famousDead: Bred the first Camel Guard herds and received the Zahas steppe in 1041.
FX24-016.secret: Rabab Zaydani has passed word of the Marad children to her Saran kin, who carried it to the Well-Mother.
hooks: Clan Saran refuses to sell camels to Sabra until the Marad children come home.
Areej's betrothal to a Saran boy could buy peace or start a feud.
Hatim counts Hazimi riders gathering on the Sabun road.

FX24-017.name: House Sadafi
FX24-017.title: Uncle of the Pearl Quay
FX24-017.arms: an open shell with an eye in it (scratched on their stalls)
FX24-017.words: A quarter is better than nothing.
FX24-017.power: Two oyster-opening stalls on the Pearl Quay, the Ropewalk Brothers as their runners, and buyers on every Blackreef boat that calls at Sabra.
FX24-017.history: The Sadafi have opened oysters on the Pearl Quay for three generations and fenced stolen pearls for two. Since Dragon Night in 1051 Blackreef boats have come freely to Sabra, and the Sadafi learned their Corsair cant and sold them pearls kept back from the Emir's best-of-the-week. Today the harbor boys of the Ropewalk Brothers steal pearls from the slave boats' catch and bring them to the Sadafi stalls, where they fetch a quarter of their worth. The family has an 'uncle' in every generation, a fence with a soft voice. The present uncle also knows that Blackreef sailors pay ten times better for a full oil jar than for any pearl.
FX24-017.reputation: Oyster-openers everyone uses and nobody trusts, uncles to every harbor thief.

members.role: Head of the family; uncle of the Pearl Quay
members.note: Speaks Corsair cant with a soft voice and has never raised it.

members.role: His sister; oyster-opener
members.note: Can palm a pearl while opening a shell in front of the Emir's weigher.

members.role: Heir; runner-master of the Ropewalk Brothers
members.note: Runs the harbor boys and is trying to buy an empty oil jar with Sabra's well-mark for a Varennan.

members.role: Taghrid's daughter
members.note: Picks pockets on the Pearl Quay and has a free diver's nose-clip she stole from Twelve-Fathom himself.

famousDead: First Sadafi fence; learned Corsair cant from Blackreef sailors after 1051.
FX24-017.secret: Muhsin Sadafi is trying to sell a Varennan sailor an oil jar stamped with Sabra's well-mark, proof of the dragon that could start a war.
hooks: The Varennan sailor who wanted the jar turns up drowned in the harbor.
The Ropewalk Brothers steal from Jamila Sabrani's own boat.
The Emir's men offer the Sadafi a pardon for the name of the jar-seller.

FX25-101.name: House Chernavin
FX25-101.title: Lord of the Lords' Bench; Viscount of Belina
FX25-101.arms: an old gold crown on black, within a red border
FX25-101.words: We Were Here Before the Bear

military.office: Lords of the Belina regiment
military.unit: the Belina regiment, 1,200 war-hearth spears and 60 Bench knights
military.ties: The Belina regiment has stood in the royal host's center since Lake Ostec, and a Chernavin has always led it, though never as Lord Marshal.

FX25-101.power: The city of Belina and its rye villages, the oldest seat on the Lords' Bench, and a handful of Bench votes that follow old blood.
FX25-101.history: The Chernavins were princes of Belina when the Eastfolk princes swore to the Solen emperor at Novgrad in 440, and they sent their sons to the legions for three centuries. When Borislav Sevrin, an officer from a channel town, took the crown in 736, the Chernavins knelt last of the old princes and were given a seat on the Lords' Bench for it. They have sat on it ever since, poorer every century and prouder of a blood older than the Sevrins'. Lord Ratibor Chernavin led the Belina shield wall at Lake Ostec in 957 and claimed the victory for it; Radoslav gave the march to Ostoja Koren instead, and the house has never forgiven either of them. In 1105 the Chernavins hold no office, and they talk quietly about what the Code says of a regency: that the Bench names whom it likes.
FX25-101.reputation: Proud, poor and old-blooded, always one grievance short of rebellion.

members.role: Head of the house; Viscount of Belina
members.note: He counts the Bench votes for a regency every night and has found he needs only four more.

members.role: Heir
members.note: She has been Queen Zora's friend since girlhood and reports to her father every word Zora says about the king.

members.role: Second son; officer of the Dawn Volunteers
members.note: He serves with Anton Koren's volunteers at Coreria and writes home that the muster rolls are full of dead men's names.

members.role: Dowager
members.note: She keeps the old princes' chain of Belina in a chest and wears it at Dawn Feast though the king has asked her not to.

famousDead: Led the Belina shield wall at Lake Ostec in 957 and was passed over for the march.
FX25-101.secret: The Chernavins have promised their Bench votes to the Purse Bench in return for a seat on any regency council, and Bohuslav's letters about the dead volunteers could ruin Zoran Koren.
hooks: Bohuslav comes home on leave with a copy of the true muster roll.
The king's eyes fail him at the Bench, and Ratibor starts counting aloud.
Snezhana must choose between her friend the queen and her father.

FX25-102.name: House Yastrebin
FX25-102.title: Lord of the Lords' Bench; Warden of the Mirovo Road
FX25-102.arms: a brown eagle with spread wings on pale grey

military.office: Wardens of the Mirovo road
military.unit: the Yastrebin riders, 30 Bench knights and 400 road spears
military.ties: Yastrebin riders patrol the paved road from the Mirovo Gate down to the channel, and the gate's crossbow captains are usually Yastrebin godsons.

FX25-102.power: The barony of Mirgrad below the Mirovo Pass and the cart toll on the old Solen road down to Sevany.
FX25-102.history: Borislav II made the Yastrebins lords of Mirgrad in 811 to keep the paved road the Solen engineers had built from the Mirovo Pass to the channel. When the Black Cough came in 917 and King Ratimir closed the pass, Dobromil Yastrebin held the road shut for two years and turned back his own kin at spear-point. Every cart between Velgrad and Sevany has paid the house since. In the autumn of 1104 sledges of pitch and sulfur began to come down the road toward Sevany, sixty of them by Midwinter. The baron charged each one twice and asked no questions; his daughter has started counting them.
FX25-102.reputation: Watchful, toll-hungry road lords who know everyone's business by the weight of his cart.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Mirgrad
members.note: He has let sixty sledges of pitch and sulfur pass down his road since October and charged every one of them twice.

members.role: Heir; captain of the road post at the top of the pass
members.note: She has started keeping her own tally of the pitch sledges and has worked out that it is enough for eight ships.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He dices with the Sevany carters, who talk when they lose.

members.role: Miron's wife
members.note: She gives a tenth of the road tolls to the monastery school on Lamp Street and wants her younger son to be a priest.

famousDead: Held the Mirovo road shut through the Black Cough of 917 to 919.
FX25-102.secret: The Yastrebins know the sledges on their road carry pitch and sulfur for Sevany, and Darina keeps a tally of every one in case it is ever worth selling.
hooks: Darina's count of the pitch sledges reaches the wrong ears.
A Greyhaven spy is caught on the Mirovo road with a drawing of a sledge.
Lev loses his sister's tally book at dice.

FX25-103.name: House Vranek
FX25-103.title: Lord of Velin
FX25-103.arms: a black raven on silver-grey, a green reed in its claws

military.office: Knights of the Ostec Lances
military.unit: the Vranek lances, 120 riders of the Ostec Lances
military.ties: Vranek riders have charged with the Ostec Lances since Ostoja Koren raised them, and every Vranek heir serves two summers at the Ostmir Gate.

FX25-103.power: The barony of Velin, a stud of destriers, and a long friendship with House Koren that has turned into a long debt.
FX25-103.history: Kazimir Vranek rode beside Ostoja Koren on the marsh flank at Lake Ostec in 957, and in 960 the Korens gave him Velin to hold under them. The Vraneks have been Koren men ever since: they ride with the Ostec Lances, speak the Marchfolk speech of the border, and borrow from the Korens when the harvest fails. Lord Zdenek Vranek rode south to the Neck with Zoran Koren in 1075. His elder son fell in the storm of Doria in 1103, leading Vranek lances under Anton Koren. To pay for new horses and armor, his wife pledged half the barony to House Koren in 1101, as the Veskovs of Ostmir once did, and has not told him.
FX25-103.reputation: Brave, loyal marcher knights who have lent their swords to the Korens and their land as well.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Velin
members.note: He still calls Zoran Koren 'my captain', though Koren now holds his debts.

members.role: His wife; keeps the barony's books
members.note: She signed away half of Velin to pay for her sons' lances and has hidden the pledge in her dowry chest.

members.role: Heir; knight of the Ostec Lances in the Neck
members.note: Heir since his brother fell at Doria, he is still at Coreria with Anton Koren and wants revenge more than land.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She writes to Dana Veskov of Ostmir, the widow who defied the Korens, and admires her far too openly.

famousDead: Rode on the marsh flank at Lake Ostec in 957 beside Ostoja Koren.
Elder son; killed leading Vranek lances in the storm of Doria.
FX25-103.secret: Lady Yarina has pledged half the barony of Velin to House Koren for a loan, behind her husband's back.
hooks: Koren stewards arrive to survey the pledged villages.
Danek comes home from the Neck to a barony half sold.
Vojka rides to Ostmir to meet Dana Veskov.

FX25-104.name: House Lisovik
FX25-104.title: Knight of the North Woods; Captain of Ski-Runners
FX25-104.arms: a grey wolf running on white, over three green pines

military.office: Captains of the North Woods Ski-Runners
military.unit: a company of the North Woods Ski-Runners, 300 scouts on skis
military.ties: The ski companies that watch the North Woods are led by Lisovik knights, and every Lisovik child skis before it can walk.

FX25-104.power: Three forest manors in Dobina, a hundred trap lines, and a captaincy of the Ski-Runners.
FX25-104.history: King Bogdan knighted a trapper's son, Anton Lisovik, in 1018 for guiding the king's tax-gatherers through the North Woods in a winter when the roads had vanished. The Lisoviks hold three forest manors around Dobina and lead a company of the Ski-Runners, the 1,200 scouts of the North Woods. They live on sable as much as land, and since Borek Marten's fur house began buying from the trappers before the Tolmir clerks could, they have been in Marten's debt. In 1101 Sir Gregor Lisovik borrowed 2,000 suns from Marten to rebuild his hall after a fire, and the debt has doubled. His eldest daughter runs the trap lines and keeps the family alive.
FX25-104.reputation: Generous, poor forest knights who would give a stranger their last stove and their last pelt.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of the North Woods
members.note: He hosts any trapper at his stove and has never once collected his rents in full.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the trap lines
members.note: She has started selling sables straight to Greyhaven buyers at Droin to escape Marten's prices.

members.role: Son; captain of the ski company
members.note: He races his skiers across frozen lakes for wagers and has lost two men through the ice.

members.role: Grandmother
members.note: She cures pelts better than anyone in Dobina and swears in three tongues.

famousDead: Guided King Bogdan's tax-gatherers through the North Woods in 1018 and was knighted.
FX25-104.secret: Olesya Lisovik sells sables past the Fur Staple straight to Greyhaven buyers at Droin, which the Staple's charter calls theft.
hooks: Borek Marten's men come to Dobina to collect the debt.
A Staple inspector finds ungraded Lisovik sables at Droin.
Stas wagers the family's best sled team on a race across thin ice.

FX25-105.name: House Medvarin
FX25-105.title: Lord of the Lords' Bench; Baron of Belovo
FX25-105.arms: a gold ram before a red lamp-flame, on dark red

military.office: Patrons of the Belovo volunteers
military.unit: the Belovo company of the Dawn Volunteers, 300 men at Coreria
military.ties: Medvarin silver raised the first Belovo volunteers for Andros in 1062, and a Medvarin son has marched south in every levy since.

FX25-105.power: The barony of Belovo, its rye and its bell foundry, and the friendship of the Patriarch's Lamp Party.
FX25-105.history: Radomir Medvarin cast the great bell of the Dawn Cathedral for its consecration on Dawn Feast 772, and King Branimir made him lord of Belovo. The Medvarins still cast bells for half the churches of the realm, and they are the loudest lords of the Lamp Party, which holds that Andros's war is holy and the money for it a tithe. When Patriarch Kirill's envoys crowned Andros in 1062, Belovo sent the first company of volunteers. Lord Svetozar Medvarin calls the Lord Treasurer a traitor to the Lamp at every sitting of the Bench. In November 1104 his younger son died of camp fever at Coreria, and the volunteer rolls still list him alive and drawing pay.
FX25-105.reputation: Loud, pious bell-lords; the Lamp Party's drum.

members.role: Head of the house; Baron of Belovo
members.note: He calls Mirek Tolmir a traitor to the Lamp at every Bench sitting, and means every word.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the bell foundry
members.note: A volunteer sergeant has written to tell her that her brother died in November, while the rolls still pay his wage.

members.role: Youngest son
members.note: He means to march south in spring and take his dead brother's place in the line.

members.role: Svetozar's wife
members.note: She still sends winter furs to Coreria every autumn, addressed to the son she does not yet know is dead.

famousDead: Cast the great bell of the Dawn Cathedral for its consecration in 772 and was made lord of Belovo.
Died of camp fever with the volunteers at Coreria; still listed as living on the rolls.
FX25-105.secret: Svetozar Medvarin knows his son is one of the dead men whose pay Anton Koren draws, and keeps silent to protect the holy war.
hooks: Radka wants the truth told before the Bench, against her father.
Ilya marches south and finds his brother's name on the living roll.
The Patriarch asks the Medvarins for one more bell's worth of silver for Andros.

FX25-106.name: House Ledovan
FX25-106.title: Lord of Vyova; Keeper of the Debt Rolls
FX25-106.arms: a white wave on deep blue, a black chain across it

military.office: Keepers of the Vyova shore and the debt-rowers
