The monasteries cancel their order after a quarrel with the Patriarch.

FX26-218.name: the Ladyin boatmasters
FX26-218.sur: son or daughter of the father; the Ladyins by byname
FX26-218.title: Master of the Ladyin Barges
FX26-218.arms: a brown river barge on blue-green
FX26-218.power: Twenty Dromir barges, a seat in the Rivermen's Guild, and the winter boat-sheds of Polgrad.
FX26-218.history: The Ladyins have moved fur, wax, rye and silk down the Dromir in their barges since about 990, and they lent boats to the crown in every war. In the Tusk raid of 1065 they took the people of Polgrad's suburbs off the bank in their barges while the granaries burned. They sit in the Rivermen's Guild, which since 1100 has paid a river pirate from Korov to rob Velgradan fur barges on the Dromir, and they vote for it every year. The boatmaster's daughter is in love with one of the pirate's men.
FX26-218.reputation: Tough, cheerful river folk who know every bend of the Dromir.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Barges
members.note: He votes for the pirate's pay every year and drinks to the man's health at the Guild feast.

members.role: Heir; barge captain
members.note: She is in love with one of the Korov pirate's oarsmen and carries his messages in her cargo.

members.role: Son; barge captain
members.note: He thinks the pirate's robberies will start a war on the river and has said so in the Guild.

members.role: Grandmother
members.note: She steered the barge that took eighty people off the burning bank at Polgrad in 1065.

famousDead: Built the first Ladyin barge on the Dromir.
FX26-218.secret: The Ladyins help pay the Korov river pirate through the Rivermen's Guild, and Marina carries his messages hidden in her barge's cargo.
hooks: Velgradan crossbows on the Tolek fire on a Ladyin barge.
Marina's pirate is caught and names her.
Pyotr tries to stop the Guild's payments.

FX26-219.name: the Zvonars of the Isles
FX26-219.title: Bell-Priest of the Monastery Isles
FX26-219.arms: a silver bell on dark blue, under a small gold lamp
FX26-219.power: The bell-towers and copying rooms of the Monastery Isles, the right to ring the dawn bell for the Lake Council, and a family of married priests and copyists.
FX26-219.history: The Zvonars rang the bell of Drevna's church on the spring equinox of 734, when the Luminary of Drevna followed Bogumil into the Dawn Church, and they have been married priests and bell-ringers of the Monastery Isles ever since. They also serve the lesser Patriarch's house as copyists. In September 1066 a Zvonar copyist made the new copy of Ludmila's Code for the Lake Council, with a clause in it no council had ever voted. He died in 1090 without confessing; his son found the draft in his desk. The family serves Stefan the Grey and wants a Drevnan church free of Velgrad.
FX26-219.reputation: Learned, musical, gentle priests; the island bells everyone loves.

members.role: Head of the family; Bell-Priest of the Monastery Isles
members.note: He found his father's draft of the forged clause in 1090 and hid it in the bell-tower.

members.role: His wife; choir mistress
members.note: She leads the island choir at the Dawn Feast and has a voice that carries across the frozen lake.

members.role: Heir; copyist of the lesser Patriarch's house
members.note: He works beside Miron Velic in the law rolls and wonders why his father will not let him climb the bell-tower.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She rings the dawn bell herself when her father's hands shake, and nobody can tell the difference.

famousDead: Copied the Code for the Lake Council in 1066, with the forged clause in it.
FX26-219.secret: The draft of the forged set-aside clause, in a Zvonar hand, is hidden in the bell-tower of the Monastery Isles.
hooks: Lavro climbs the bell-tower.
Stefan the Grey asks Bohdan to burn the draft.
The Prince-Consort's men come to the isles asking for old drafts.

FX26-220.name: the Gramotins
FX26-220.title: Master of the Radov School
FX26-220.arms: a brown owl on a gold scroll, on green
FX26-220.power: The lay school of Radov, the scribing of the river towns' contracts, and the tutoring of lake lords' children.
FX26-220.history: The island monks taught the lake lords' sons to read for three centuries, and in 1012 a lay scribe named Ilya Gramotin opened a school at Radov to teach their daughters too, under the protection of House Jezeran. The Gramotins have taught and written for the river towns since: contracts, wills, debt rolls, and the letters lake lords cannot write themselves. Half the Lake Council learned its letters from a Gramotin. Their present master tutored Princess Ludmila in her girlhood and taught her the hand-signs of the Still Hall's book.
FX26-220.reputation: Patient, precise teachers who know every lord's handwriting and every lord's secrets.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Radov School
members.note: He tutored Princess Ludmila and says she is the cleverest child he ever taught, drums or no drums.

members.role: Heir; scribe of contracts
members.note: She wrote Stepan Jezeran's debt bond to the Brodar sled house and knows exactly how much it is.

members.role: Son; tutor at Brodava
members.note: He tutors Pavel Brodar's household clerks and copies their letters for anyone who pays.

members.role: Ilya's wife
members.note: She treats the schoolchildren's coughs and fevers for free.

famousDead: Opened the lay school of Radov in 1012.
FX26-220.secret: Arseni Gramotin copies the Prince-Consort's household letters and sells them, and one copy went to the Queen's Ear.
hooks: Arseni is caught copying a letter about a physician's bribe.
Princess Ludmila sends for her old tutor.
Natalya is asked to forge a second debt bond.

FX26-221.name: the Ugrakov horse-herds
FX26-221.sur: son or daughter of the father; the Ugrakovs, after the founder Ugrak
FX26-221.title: Herd-Master of the Ugava Grass
FX26-221.arms: a sign: a black horse's head on yellow, cut into their saddles
FX26-221.power: Herds of steppe horses on the grass around Ugava, riders in the half-orc light horse of the Steppe March, and kin on both sides of the grazing line.
FX26-221.history: Ugrak was a half-orc herder of the Tusk Clans who stayed on the Drevnan side of the grazing line when it was fixed at Thardush in 1066, with his Drevnan wife and forty horses. The Zoracs let his family graze the grass around Ugava Fort in return for remounts. His sons and grandsons breed steppe horses for the Drevnan army and ride in the 1,200 half-orc light horse of the Steppe March. They speak both tongues and have cousins in the Tusk camps. The Rye Shame calls them orcs; the Tusk riders call them traitors; the herd-master calls them horse-breeders.
FX26-221.reputation: Superb riders, distrusted by both peoples and needed by both.

members.role: Head of the family; Herd-Master of the Ugava Grass
members.note: He was four when his father crossed the line and he remembers the drums of the camps.

members.role: Daughter; rider of the half-orc light horse
members.note: She rides patrol on the grazing line and talks across it with a Whitehorn cousin.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He breaks colts for the Zorin Crossbows' wagons and wants a Drevnan wife, which no Drevnan father will allow.

members.role: Grandmother; Ugrak's widow
members.note: A Drevnan farmer's daughter, she married a half-orc in 1060 and has heard every insult there is.

famousDead: Half-orc herder who stayed on the Drevnan side of the grazing line in 1066.
FX26-221.secret: Gorka Ugrakov's Whitehorn cousin has told her the Tusk riders will raid in spring if the rye has not come, and that they will not touch the Ugrakov herds.
hooks: Gorka brings the Whitehorn warning to the castellan.
Rye Shame men try to drive the Ugrakovs off the grass.
Duro falls in love with a Polyanin daughter.

FX26-222.name: the Lovchin bearwards
FX26-222.title: Bearward of the Lubevo Forest
FX26-222.arms: a sign: a brown bear's paw on green, painted on their door-posts
FX26-222.power: The crown's bear-wardenship of the Lubevo forest, a bounty on bears that raid the hives, and the forest trails between the Dromir and the lakes.
FX26-222.history: After the Black Cough of 917 emptied the forest villages, the bears came out of the Lubevo woods and tore open the royal hives, and King Lubor made the hunter Medved Lovchin bearward of the forest. The Lovchins have hunted bears for the crown since, with spear and dog, and they guide travelers through the forest trails. Every Lovchin child takes a bear before marrying. The present bearward's son guides smugglers along the forest trails when the river is watched.
FX26-222.reputation: Tough, honest forest folk with scars from claws and no fear of anything on four legs.

members.role: Head of the family; Bearward of the Lubevo Forest
members.note: He has killed 41 bears and been marked by three of them.

members.role: Heir; huntress
members.note: She keeps the family's bear-dogs and raised an orphaned cub that follows her like a hound.

members.role: Son; forest guide
members.note: He guides smugglers' pack trains through the forest when the castellan's men watch the river.

members.role: Medved's wife
members.note: She sews claw wounds better than any physician in Drevna.

famousDead: First bearward of the Lubevo forest after the Black Cough.
FX26-222.secret: Stas Lovchin guides the Komar smugglers' pack trains through the forest past the Lubevo garrison.
hooks: A bear raids the royal hives at Darsky in the spring thaw.
Ksenia's tame bear is wanted for a lord's feast.
The castellan's men catch Stas with a smuggler's pack train.

FX26-223.name: the Komar clan
FX26-223.sur: son or daughter of the father; the Komars, 'the gnats', by byname
FX26-223.title: Old Gnat of the Western Lakes
FX26-223.arms: a sign: a white skull scratched on the runners of their sleds
FX26-223.power: Thirty fast sleds and boats on the Western Lakes, hiding places in the reeds on both sides of the border, and buyers in Velgrad and the Wax Market.
FX26-223.history: The Komars began smuggling across the Western Lakes the year the Peace of Polov fixed the border in 1037, running wax and honey west and Velgradan sables east by sled in winter and by boat in summer. Since Drevna raised the silk toll at Lubany in 1100 and again in 1103, they have also run silk past the staple across the ice to a Velgradan silk house's factor. The Kraina garrison hangs one of them now and then, and the Velgradan river forts shoot at them. The Old Gnat has a rule: never carry anything for a lord. His grandson has broken it.
FX26-223.reputation: Small, quick, everywhere and impossible to swat; the lake folk love them.

members.role: Head of the clan; the Old Gnat
members.note: He has crossed the frozen border more than five hundred times and never carried anything for a lord.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the sleds
members.note: She meets the Velgradan silk factor on the ice at night and haggles in two tongues.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: He carried a sealed letter across the ice for a Velgradan castellan's man in December, for a purse he did not share.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: She sells fish on the Kraina quay and counts the garrison's patrols.

famousDead: Ran the first sled of sables across the new border in the winter of 1037.
FX26-223.secret: The Komars run silk past the Lubany staple to the Shelkov house of Vyova, and Kostya has carried letters for the Velgradan castellan of Kamogda.
hooks: The Kraina garrison catches Vera on the ice with a silk bale.
Kostya's letter turns out to be a list of Krainov fish-weirs.
House Lubec offers a bounty for every Komar sled.

FX26-224.name: the Solnik salt house
FX26-224.title: Master of the Solnik Salt House
FX26-224.arms: a white cart-wheel on dark grey, crusted with salt
FX26-224.power: The Drevnan share of the Eaglespire salt trade, salt barns at Darsky, and the summer caravan to the Roof.
FX26-224.history: Ostap Solnik was one of the Drevnan merchants who sealed the Salt Letters of Eaglespire with Skyhold in 1071, buying salt, borax and sky wool from the Roof each summer and paying in silver by weight. His family has led the summer caravan up the Beaconrun valley ever since and sells Roof salt in the Darsky market. They pay the Skyhold toll in silver and the Dobnik wardens in goodwill. In 1105 Skyhold's dying abbot and its rival claimant have split the Roof, and the Solniks do not know which monastery's seal will be honored at Eaglespire this summer.
FX26-224.reputation: Sober, honest salt-traders with friends on the Roof.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Salt House
members.note: He sealed the Salt Letters at 23 and has climbed to Eaglespire thirty-three summers running.

members.role: Heir; caravan master
members.note: She speaks the Skyfolk tongue and has drunk butter tea with an abbot's steward.

members.role: Son; salt factor at Drevna
members.note: He cuts the Roof salt with Whale Coast sea salt and sells it at the Roof price.

members.role: Ostap's wife
members.note: She keeps the salt barns dry and the accounts straight.

FX26-224.secret: Taras Solnik cuts the Roof salt with cheap Whale Coast sea salt and sells it at the Roof price, and the Pchelins have found out.
hooks: The summer caravan reaches Eaglespire and finds two rival seals.
Baroness Pchelin threatens to expose Taras unless the Solniks sell their barns.
Milana is asked to carry a letter to the Red Stair claimant.

FX27-001.name: House Highpasture
FX27-001.title: Herd-Lord of the Upper Bellcrest Camps
FX27-001.arms: a white yak on a green mountain, on sky blue
FX27-001.words: Our grass grows nearest the sky.
FX27-001.power: About 4,000 yaks and the highest summer pastures of Bellcrest, which the Snowborn need for their guide camps.
FX27-001.history: The Highpasture household has grazed the highest camps above Bellcrest since before the Snowborn took their name, and in 702 the 6th Abbot made their elder a herd-lord for feeding the monks of the winter crossing's heirs. The Snowborn's boys spend their summers at 5,000 m on Highpasture grass, and the two households have married and quarreled for four centuries. When the Snowborn rose after 1061, the Highpasture rose with them as clients. Their elder knows that Pasang Snowborn gave a search monk gold in December 1104, because the monk slept in a Highpasture tent on his way down. The Highpasture have three households expecting children in 1105 too, and none of them is on Pasang's list.
FX27-001.reputation: Old, quiet herd-lords in the Snowborn's shadow, patient as yaks and as heavy to move.

members.role: Elder of the household; Herd-Lord of the Upper Bellcrest Camps
members.note: He fed the young search monk who carried Pasang's gold and asked him, gently, about his list.

members.role: Wife of the three Highpasture brothers
members.note: She runs the herd and the household, and her three husbands do what she says by long habit.

members.role: Second husband; guide in the Snowborn Guides
members.note: He went with Jigme Snowborn's party that led Emberdeep crossbowmen to Kardeep and cannot stop dreaming of the falling dragon.

members.role: Daughter; expecting a child in spring
members.note: Her grandfather has begun asking monks about omens around her tent.

famousDead: First herd-lord of the upper camps, raised by the 6th Abbot in 702.
FX27-001.secret: Tsewang means to show the next search monks omens around his granddaughter's tent, as the Snowborn did around theirs.
hooks: A ring of light appears over the Highpasture tents.
Gompo is asked to confess what happened at Kardeep.

FX27-002.name: House Saltlake
FX27-002.title: Herd-Lord of the Stillhold Lakes
FX27-002.arms: a white salt slab under a gold sun, on brown
FX27-002.power: About 6,000 yaks, the cutting rights at the Stillhold dry lakes for the monasteries, and the southern salt trail through Sunfold to Ranpur.
FX27-002.history: When the 3rd Abbot, Kunga, sent the first monastery salt caravans from the Stillhold dry lakes through Sunfold to the hill towns of Ranpur in 521, he gave the driving of them to a herder household of the lakes. The Saltlake have cut and driven the monasteries' salt and borax south ever since, trading it for the rice and cotton the Roof cannot grow. They lost half their animals in the Black Cough years when the trails were shut, and they lost an abbot's trust in 950 when Abbot Lodro went down their trail to Chanari and died of fever. The Windmane run the northern trade and the Saltlake the southern, and the two houses have despised each other for three centuries. In November 1104 Saltlake yaks carried Steward Sonam's 18 kg of gold dust down to Chanari.
FX27-002.reputation: Salt-crusted southern herd-lords, rich in rice and dangerous with a secret.

members.role: Elder of the household; Herd-Lord of the Stillhold Lakes
members.note: His yaks carried the Steward's gold south, and he knows what is coming back up the trail in the spring.

members.role: Daughter; caravan mistress of the Sunfold trail
members.note: She will lead the caravan that brings 40 Chanari blades up the trail, and has not decided whether to let it arrive.

members.role: Son; monk at Stonespire
members.note: The house's given child, he has sworn the vow never to kill and has heard rumors of the blades.

famousDead: First caravan master of the southern salt trail in 521.
FX27-002.secret: The Saltlake carried the Steward's lamp-treasury gold south to buy steel blades and will carry the blades back up in the spring hidden in rice sacks.
hooks: Phurba asks his sister to tip the blades into a gorge.
Windmane salt-smuggling comes to Saltlake ears.

FX27-003.name: House Silverfleece
FX27-003.title: Herd-Lord of the Drumhaven Valleys
FX27-003.arms: a silver ram on a dark red field
FX27-003.power: Flocks of about 15,000 sheep and goats whose fine sky wool goes north to Drevna under the Salt Letters.
FX27-003.history: The Silverfleece have bred the fine-wooled goats of the Drumhaven valleys since the 9th century, and the 8th Abbot raised them to herd-lords in 840 after Eaglespire opened to the northern caravans. Their sky wool is the softest on the Roof, and since the Salt Letters of 1071 Drevnan merchants buy it at Eaglespire each June. The house sends its wool down through the Windmane trains and pays them a fee it thinks too high. Lady Choekyi Silverfleece has been courted by Abbess Dechen's Quiet Doubters, and since 1102 she has sent wool to the eastern monasteries as well as the western.
FX27-003.reputation: Soft-spoken, well-dressed herd-lords who give to both Stairs and trust neither.

members.role: Head of the household; Lady of the Drumhaven Valleys
members.note: She married two Silverfleece brothers and outlived both, and the household calls her lady in their place.

members.role: Son and heir
members.note: He wants to drive the wool to Lubov himself and cut out the Windmane trains.

members.role: Daughter; novice at Moonstair
members.note: She serves Abbess Dechen and has carried letters to the High Wastes that she was told not to read.

famousDead: Bred the first sky-wool goats of Drumhaven; raised by the 8th Abbot.
FX27-003.secret: Metok carries Abbess Dechen's letters to Norbu of the Red Stair, and her mother knows.
hooks: Metok's letter falls into Stair Guard hands.
Sherab sets off for Lubov without the Brotherhood's leave.

FX27-004.name: House Redridge
FX27-004.title: Herd-Lord of the Quietwatch Ridges
FX27-004.arms: a red stair of seven steps on grey
FX27-004.power: About 3,000 yaks on the eastern ridges and the loyalty of the herders who feed the Red Stair.
FX27-004.history: The Redridge are herd-lords of the eastern ridges near Quietwatch, raised by the 7th Abbot in 766 to keep peace with the herders of the High Wastes edge. Like their herders, they have honored the Great Ash Dragons as sky-kings for centuries. When the eastern monasteries proclaimed Norbu in May 1062, the Redridge elder stood with them, and the house has given children and butter to the Red Stair since. It keeps the Truce of the Circuit and its herders rob pilgrims, both at once. In October 1104 Snowborn guides led Emberdeep's crossbowmen over Redridge goat paths to shoot at the sky-kings above Kardeep, and the Redridge want blood for it.
FX27-004.reputation: Proud eastern herd-lords, half monks and half rebels, who will not say the 13th Abbot's name.

members.role: Elder of the household; Herd-Lord of the Quietwatch Ridges
members.note: He was at Moonstair when monks threw stones in 1062 and still has the scar.

members.role: Wife of the Redridge brothers
members.note: She keeps the Truce on her ridges and turns back robbers who carry blades.

members.role: Son; robber on the circuit
members.note: He robs pilgrims with a sling for Norbu's barley and has sworn to kill a Snowborn guide for the dragon.

members.role: Daughter; nun of the Red Stair
members.note: She is the house's given child and tends the herders' sick at Mistpass Monastery.

famousDead: Stood with the eastern abbots when they proclaimed Norbu in 1062.
FX27-004.secret: Lobsang Redridge has sworn on the sky-kings to kill Jigme Snowborn, which would break the Truce of the Circuit.
hooks: Jigme Snowborn passes the Quietwatch ridges with a party of dwarves.
Norzom asks a stranger to stop her son.

FX27-005.name: the Stonetent household
FX27-005.title: File-Leader of the Stair Guard
FX27-005.arms: a white staff and a sling crossed on dark blue

military.office: Hereditary file-leaders of the Stair Guard at the White Stair
military.unit: a company of the Stair Guard, 200 staves and slings
military.ties: They have served in the Stair Guard since Abbot Yeshe raised it in 722, and every Stonetent son passes the test of the Hall of Still Hands.

FX27-005.power: Two hundred places in the Stair Guard and a family name every Guard recruit has heard.
FX27-005.history: When Abbot Yeshe raised the Stair Guard in 722, paid in butter and barley, a herder named Dorje of the stone tents was among its first file-leaders, and his household has served it ever since. In 767 a Stonetent guard was one of those who killed the three Moonstair robbers, and the shame of it led to the Hall of Still Hands; the family has trained there more faithfully than any other since. Every Stonetent son passes the Hall's test before he may carry a staff. In November 1104 Steward Sonam sent south for 40 Chanari blades, and the Stonetent file-leader has been told his company will carry them.
FX27-005.reputation: The model of a guard who does not kill, proud of a rule they once broke.

members.role: Elder of the household; File-Leader of the Stair Guard
members.note: He has been told his company will carry steel, and he has asked Nima of the Still Hands what a guard does then.

members.role: Wife of the Stonetent brothers
members.note: She sets the bones of every guard her husbands bind and every robber they bind too.

members.role: Son; staff-fighter
members.note: He thinks the Guard should carry blades and has said so in the Hall, where no one says it.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She can hit a butter lamp with a sling stone at 60 paces and wants to be the first woman in the Guard.

famousDead: First Stonetent file-leader of the Stair Guard in 722.
FX27-005.secret: A Stonetent guard killed one of the three Moonstair robbers in 767, and the family has paid the robbers' heirs butter every year since in secret.
hooks: The blades arrive and Tsering's company must take them.
Pasang is challenged to a staff duel by a Red Stair herder.

FX27-006.name: the Whitepass watch
FX27-006.title: Warden of the Eaglespire Tower
FX27-006.arms: a white eagle over a gate on blue

military.office: Hereditary Wardens of the Eaglespire Tower and the Beaconrun road watch
military.unit: the Eaglespire Tower and Beaconrun road watch, 200 guards
military.ties: They have kept the northern gate since Abbot Rabten opened it in 831 and shut it against the Black Cough from 916 to 921.

FX27-006.power: The Eaglespire Tower, the abbey's toll on the northern road and the gate itself.
FX27-006.history: When Abbot Rabten opened the gate at Eaglespire to the yak caravans in 831 and taxed the salt trade, he gave the tower and its toll to a pass-guard household of Eaglespire. The Whitepass have kept the gate ever since. In 916 Abbot Gendun ordered it closed against the Black Cough, and the Whitepass held it shut for five years while Skyfolk starved and Drevnan traders begged outside; no plague crossed. Since the Salt Letters of 1071 they take one load in five from every Drevnan buyer. They live beside the Windmane, who own the caravans, and they know the Windmane have smuggled salt past the tower since 1096, down a herders' path east of their own walls.
FX27-006.reputation: Strict, unbribable gate-keepers of the north, who held the plague gate and have never forgotten it.

members.role: Elder of the household; Warden of the Eaglespire Tower
members.note: He has counted the Windmane yaks out and in for ten years and the numbers have never matched.

members.role: Daughter; toll-keeper
members.note: She found the herders' path east of the tower in October and followed it alone to the Lakeland edge.

members.role: Son; road-watch captain
members.note: He takes butter from the Windmane drovers to look the other way, which his father would exile him for.

famousDead: Held the Eaglespire gate shut against the Black Cough from 916 to 921.
FX27-006.secret: Jampa Whitepass takes Windmane butter to let the smuggling trains pass, while his father and sister try to catch them.
hooks: Tsamchoe brings her proof of the smugglers' path to the Steward.
A Drevnan merchant offers silver for an early opening of the gate.

FX27-007.name: the Coldspring lay brothers
FX27-007.title: Gate-Captain of Moonstair
FX27-007.arms: a white crescent over a black gate on grey
FX27-007.words: Whoever holds the gate holds the road.

military.office: Hereditary gate-captains of the Moonstair lay garrison
military.unit: the Moonstair lay garrison, 400 guards
military.ties: Their line has kept the gate of Moonstair, the White Stair's fortress against the High Wastes, since it was walled in the 6th century.

FX27-007.power: The gate of Moonstair and the 400 lay guards who decide who passes from the High Wastes to the White Stair.
FX27-007.history: When Moonstair was walled in the 6th century as the White Stair's eastern fortress, a household of the Coldspring valley took the gate, and their lay brothers have held it for over 500 years. Their sons have been Stair Guards and robbers in turn, like all Moonstair herders. In 1062 monks of both Stairs threw stones in the courtyard below their gate, and in 1064 the Truce of the Circuit was sworn there. Abbess Dechen has promised Norbu of the Red Stair the gates of Moonstair if the White Stair holds a new search. The Coldspring captain holds the keys, and the Steward has asked him privately which way he would turn them.
FX27-007.reputation: Poor, grim gate-keepers of the east whose loyalty both Stairs claim and neither trusts.

members.role: Elder of the household; Gate-Captain of Moonstair
members.note: He holds the keys Abbess Dechen has promised to Norbu, and the Steward has asked him which way he would turn them.

members.role: Wife of the Coldspring brothers
members.note: She is one of the Quiet Doubters and believes the boy found first in 1061 was the true abbot.

members.role: Son; lay guard
members.note: His best friend robs pilgrims for the Red Stair, and he has let him through the gate twice.

famousDead: Kept the gate when the Truce of the Circuit was sworn in its courtyard.
FX27-007.secret: Gyaltsen has promised both the Steward and the Abbess to keep the gate for them, and he has not decided which promise is a lie.
hooks: Norbu's herders gather in the valley below Moonstair.
The Steward sends a new gate-captain with a letter.

FX27-008.name: the Ridgewind body-breakers
FX27-008.title: Master Body-Breaker of Drumhaven
FX27-008.arms: a black raven on a white platform, painted on a prayer flag
FX27-008.power: The sky-burial platforms of Drumhaven and the knowledge of how every person on the Roof dies.
FX27-008.history: The Ridgewind have broken the dead for the vultures on the Drumhaven platforms since the 5th century, cutting the bodies so the lammergeiers can carry them into the open sky. The work is holy and unclean at once, and the family marries only among body-breakers. They see every corpse the monasteries send, and they know a fever death from a fall or a sling stone. When the Steward called them to Skyhold in 1104 to prepare in secret for the Abbot's burial, they learned how sick Tashen is. In August 1104 they were also asked to break a robber's body from Starspire, and found it had already been hidden under a cairn.
FX27-008.reputation: Feared, avoided and needed, the family no one invites and everyone will one day meet.

members.role: Elder of the household; Master Body-Breaker of Drumhaven
members.note: He has been told to be ready to break the 13th Abbot's body and has already sharpened the knives.

members.role: Daughter; body-breaker
members.note: She can tell a sling-stone wound from a fall at a glance, and she has seen one on a Red Stair herder this winter.

members.role: Grandson; apprentice
members.note: He feeds the vultures by hand and names them, and the old men say the birds come when he calls.

famousDead: Broke the bodies of the 60 pilgrims of the Great Blizzard of 983.
FX27-008.secret: The Red Stair pays the Ridgewind in barley to send word of every death at Skyhold, and they have already told Norbu how sick the Abbot is.
hooks: A body arrives on the platform with a blade wound, on a Roof where no one carries blades.
The robber's kin ask the Ridgewind where their son's body went.

FX27-009.name: the Prayerstone copyists
FX27-009.title: Master Copyist of Stonespire
FX27-009.arms: a black key on a white stone, on saffron
FX27-009.power: The copying rooms of Stonespire, where the search records and abbots' books are copied for every monastery.
FX27-009.history: The Prayerstone are a lay household of copyists who have copied scripture in Old Sky script at Stonespire since the early 7th century, and who make the fair copies of the search records that every monastery keeps. A Prayerstone copied the record of the 1061 search, the one signed by the young monk Pema of Moonstair. The household gives one child to the monks each generation and keeps the rest at the copying tables. Master Lhazin Prayerstone was a girl of twelve when her father copied the 1061 record, and she remembers that he copied it twice and burned the first.
FX27-009.reputation: Ink-blackened, half-blind and wholly trusted, the memory of the monasteries.

members.role: Head of the household; Master Copyist of Stonespire
members.note: She remembers her father copying the 1061 search record twice and burning the first copy in the lamp.

members.role: Son; copyist
members.note: He has found in an old ledger that the first copy of 1061 used more paper than the second, by exactly one page.

members.role: Daughter; nun and search-monk's assistant
members.note: She serves Jampa of Sunfold, Master of the Search, and is listing omens for the next abbot.

famousDead: Copied the record of the 1061 search; burned the first copy.
FX27-009.secret: The first copy of the 1061 search record named a different child before it was burned, and Jigme Prayerstone has worked out that a page is missing.
hooks: Jigme asks to read the Moonstair library's copy.
Paldon is asked to write a false omen into the new search list.

FX27-010.name: House Greyyak
FX27-010.title: Master of the Yak Yards Butter Hall
FX27-010.arms: a grey yak's head on a gold field
FX27-010.power: The butter and tea trade of the Yak Yards below Skyhold, and a cousin in the Steward's chair.
FX27-010.history: The Greyyak have traded butter, tea bricks and barley in the Yak Yards below Skyhold since the long peace of the 12th Abbot. Butter is money on the Roof, and it lights every lamp in the Lamp Treasury, so the house has always sold to the monasteries. Steward Sonam is a butter trader's son of the salt treasury and a Greyyak cousin, and since he became Steward in 1089 the house has supplied the abbey's butter without competition. In 1101 House Bluewater began paying the Red Stair 40 loads of butter a year, and the Greyyak sold it to them.
FX27-010.reputation: Fat and friendly butter merchants who are suddenly the Steward's family.

members.role: Head of the house; Master of the Yak Yards Butter Hall
members.note: He shares his name with the Red Stair's claimant and jokes about it at every feast, more nervously each year.

members.role: Daughter and heir; keeper of the butter books
members.note: She knows the Lamp Treasury's butter accounts as well as the Steward does, and that they are short.

members.role: Son; trader on the Sunfold trail
members.note: He went south with the Saltlake caravan in November and has seen what the Steward's gold bought.

famousDead: Opened the Butter Hall in the Yak Yards in 990.
FX27-010.secret: The Greyyak sold the 40 loads of butter a year that House Bluewater pays to the Red Stair, and the Steward's own cousins have fed his enemies.
hooks: The Stair Guard traces Red Stair butter back to the Butter Hall.
Mingma talks too much about Chanari steel in the Butter Lamp tea house.

FX27-011.name: the Windtent weavers
FX27-011.title: Master of the Starspire Looms
FX27-011.arms: a white tent with a gold star above it on dark brown
FX27-011.power: The looms of Starspire, which weave yak-hair tents, felt and sky-wool cloth for herders and pilgrims.
FX27-011.history: The Windtent began weaving yak-hair tents for the pilgrims at Starspire soon after House Bluewater built its first inn in 930, and they have woven the circuit's tents and blankets ever since. They buy wool from every herd-lord and sell cloth to every inn, and they know every household's quarrels. When pilgrims fell by a third in 1104, the Windtent lost a third of their orders. In August 1104 a Windtent weaver saw the Bluewater warden Dorje Stonesling carry a body up the hill above Starspire at night.
FX27-011.reputation: Busy, talkative weavers who know every yarn of the circuit and spin a few of their own.

members.role: Head of the household; Master of the Starspire Looms
members.note: She has woven a tent for every herd-lord of the Roof and kept a scrap of each.

members.role: Son; weaver
members.note: He saw Dorje Stonesling carry a body up the hill in August and has drawn the cairn's place on a scrap of felt.

members.role: Daughter; dyer
members.note: She has heard her brother's story and thinks it is worth a winter's silver.

famousDead: Wove the first pilgrims' tents at Starspire.
FX27-011.secret: Samten Windtent knows where the Red Stair robber killed by the Bluewater warden lies hidden, and his sister wants to sell it.
hooks: Yangchen offers the cairn's place to the Red Stair.
Lady Lhamo Bluewater orders a strangely large tent, paid in advance.

FX27-012.name: the Bluerock robbers
FX27-012.title: Elder of the Bluerock Camp
FX27-012.arms: a blue stone in a sling, scratched on rocks along the circuit
FX27-012.power: About 30 herders and slingers who rob pilgrims on the Bluespire circuit and know every path the Stair Guard knows.
FX27-012.history: The Bluerock are a herding household of the Moonstair valleys, and one of the three robbers the Stair Guard killed on the circuit in 767 was a Bluerock. That killing led to the Hall of Still Hands, and the family has never let anyone forget it. It has robbed pilgrims on and off for three centuries, paying back threefold in butter when caught and walking the circuit in penance when caught again. Since 1062 it has robbed for the Red Stair, and the silver buys Norbu's barley. In August 1104 a Bluerock son went robbing above Starspire and never came home.
FX27-012.reputation: Hard, poor, sling-handed herders who rob as their grandfathers did and pray to the sky-kings for luck.

members.role: Elder of the household; Elder of the Bluerock Camp
members.note: His son went robbing above Starspire in August and never came home, and he has sworn to find out why.

members.role: Wife of the Bluerock brothers
members.note: She has walked the circuit twice in penance for her sons and asks every pilgrim for news of the missing one.

members.role: Son; robber
members.note: He has bought a steel knife from a Ranpuri trader, the first blade the family has ever owned.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: She sings to the sky-kings every dawn and wants to be a Red Stair nun.

famousDead: One of the three robbers killed by the Stair Guard in 767; the reason for the Hall of Still Hands.
Went robbing above Starspire in August 1104 and never came home.
FX27-012.secret: Dawa Bluerock carries a steel knife and means to use it on whoever killed his brother, Truce or no Truce.
hooks: The Bluerock learn where the cairn above Starspire lies.
The Stair Guard comes to Moonstair to collect the threefold butter.

FX28-001.name: Clan Tinbeard
FX28-001.title: Thane of Barmark Gate
FX28-001.arms: a white gate-tower in snow on blue, a tin-grey border

military.office: Thanes of Barmark Gate
military.unit: the Barmark gate company, 200 pikes and crossbows
military.ties: Tinbeard companies serve their turns in the Gate Wardens and hold the high Zardeep road for the crown from June to September.

FX28-001.power: Barmark Gate high on the Zardeep road, its snow-sheds and cairns, and the crown's pay for keeping the summer road open.
FX28-001.history: Queen Runa II built Barmark Gate high on the Zardeep road about 300 BR to mark where the dwarves' border begins, and the Tinbeards, a clan of tin miners from Nardeep, have held it since; after the Treaty of Zardeep in 615 made the high road worth a fortune, King Orm III made their head a thane. They keep the gate, the snow-sheds and the cairns of the high road, digging out the drifts each June so the summer caravans can climb to the pass. Every winter the road kills porters and mules, and the Tinbeards bury them in the rock beside the road, humans as well as dwarves, which no other clan does. Since the Nagora road opened in 1081 the caravans have fallen by a third, and Barmark lives on half of what it did. The clan's young want Kettil Ironbrow's war to win the traffic back; its head wants Ranpur to pay for the snow-sheds instead.
FX28-001.reputation: Tough, kindly road-keepers who bury strangers and quarrel with no one, until now.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of Barmark Gate
members.note: He has buried 312 porters beside the high road and knows most of their names.

members.role: Heir; captain of the gate company
members.note: She drills with Brenna Ironbrow's pikes and wants the Nagora Gate back, against her father's wishes.

members.role: Hallveig's son; snow-shed digger
members.note: He found a Tessarian courier frozen in a drift in 1103 with a sealed letter, and he has not opened it.

famousDead: First thane of Barmark Gate after the Treaty of Zardeep of 615.
FX28-001.secret: Thorgeir takes a Ranpuri merchant's silver each summer to report which caravans climb the Zardeep road, and the merchant sells the reports to the Nagora toll farm.
hooks: Hallveig wants to march with the Old Toll in spring.
Leif holds a frozen courier's sealed letter.
Ranpur's silver could make Thorgeir a traitor in the Old Toll's eyes.

FX28-002.name: Clan Gemcutter
FX28-002.title: Thane of the Sapphire Galleries
FX28-002.arms: a blue sapphire cut with eight points, on silver
FX28-002.power: The sapphire galleries under Mount Bardun, the best gem-cutters in Stonehold, and a thane's seat on the Hall Council.
FX28-002.history: King Hjalmar opened the sapphire galleries under Mount Bardun about 1150 BR and gave them to the Gemcutters, who have cut blue stones from the same rock for 2,250 years; King Hrodvar IV made their head a thane in 30. They have always been the second house of Dramhall, living beside the Goldveins' gold and rubies and marrying their daughters often enough to keep the peace. When the Hold Bank was made in 790, the Gemcutters asked for the Mastership and lost it to Rorik Goldvein by one vote of the Hall Council; the clan has kept the tally stone of that vote. The sapphire seams still run, while the Goldvein ruby seam failed in 1099. The clan's head has heard that the Master has been paying his miners from somewhere other than his own vaults.
FX28-002.reputation: Rich, polished and patient; the clan that has waited 315 years for the Bank.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of the Sapphire Galleries
members.note: He keeps the tally stone of 790 on his table and touches it before every Hall Council.

members.role: Heir; master gem-cutter
members.note: She is the best gem-cutter in Stonehold and does not care who runs the Bank, which her father finds unbearable.

members.role: Hrafnkel's nephew; clerk at the Hold Bank
members.note: He works two desks from Ragnhild Tallystone and has seen her copy a tally she should not have.

famousDead: Lost the Mastership of the Hold Bank to Rorik Goldvein by one vote in 790.
FX28-002.secret: Oddvar has seen Ragnhild Tallystone copy the tally of Orrin Goldvein's loan to his own mines, and Hrafnkel means to use it before she does.
hooks: The Gemcutters want the Mastership of the Hold Bank.
Oddvar holds a dangerous secret about a dangerous colleague.
Sigrid would rather cut stones than plot.

FX28-003.name: Clan Quarrystone
FX28-003.title: Thane of Garbek Gate
FX28-003.arms: a grey gate in a green gorge, on grey

military.office: Thanes of Garbek Gate
military.unit: the Garbek gate company, 300 pikes and crossbows
military.ties: The clan holds the southern gorge road for the crown and sends its sons to the Gate Wardens; it sent none to the Nagora War.

FX28-003.power: Garbek Gate across the southern gorge road from Ranpur, the high pastures of the Garbek Mosswoods, and the rent of the human herders who graze them.
FX28-003.history: King Bardi I built Garbek Gate across the southern gorge road about 800 BR, and the Quarrystones, who cut its stones, have held it since; King Asgrim II made their head a thane in 120. The gate looks down through the Garbek Mosswoods to Ranpur's hills, one of the gorge roads that a handful of dwarves can close, and Ranpuri traders and monsoon rain have come up it in equal measure for 1,900 years. The clan speaks Ranpuri, trades with the hill towns below and sent no company to the Nagora War, which the Old Toll has not forgiven. Its thane stands with Crown Prince Hrodgar for peace. Garbek Gate is also where Ranpur would come if it ever came, and the clan knows it.
FX28-003.reputation: Called cowards by the Old Toll and wise by the Crown Prince; they answer neither.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of Garbek Gate
members.note: He sent no pikes to Tiravi and has been called a coward by Kettil Ironbrow at every Hall Council since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the gate company
members.note: She speaks Ranpuri like a native and has a Ranpuri tea-merchant friend who tells her what the rajas' captains say.

members.role: Torunn's son
members.note: He ran off toward Tiravi in 1083 at five, was carried home by a Gate Warden and has wanted to be a soldier ever since.

famousDead: Cut the stones of Garbek Gate for King Bardi I.
FX28-003.secret: Hogni has met Ranpuri envoys at the foot of the gorge twice since 1100 to talk of a shared toll, without the king's leave.
hooks: The Old Toll calls the clan cowards.
Torunn's Ranpuri friend may be a spy for one side or both.
If Ranpur ever marches, Garbek Gate is the door.

FX28-004.name: Clan Stonebraid
FX28-004.title: Thane of the Terraces
FX28-004.arms: a gold barley-sheaf on stepped green terraces, on brown
FX28-004.power: The 4,000 barley terraces below the First Hall, the granary keys, and the labor of about 9,000 human terrace farmers.
FX28-004.history: King Brom II cut the first barley terraces below the First Hall about 2000 BR so the hold could feed half its people, and the Stonebraids have kept them since: 4,000 terraces of stone-walled barley, goat pens and yak pasture in the valley of the hot spring. The clan's head has been called Thane of the Terraces since 205 and holds the granary keys of the First Hall. Human farmers work most of the terraces now, about 9,000 of them, paid in barley and housed in villages below the gates. The terraces feed half the hold in a good year and a third in a bad one, and 1104 was bad. The thane has asked the Hall Council for silver to buy grain and been told by Orrin Goldvein that the king said no.
FX28-004.reputation: Plain, fair and unglamorous: the clan that feeds the clans that matter.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of the Terraces
members.note: He has asked the king for grain silver three times and does not believe the king ever heard the question.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the granary keys
members.note: She has counted the First Hall's barley and knows it runs out in May.

members.role: Ase's son
members.note: He wants to get past Orrin Goldvein's clerks and ask King Harvald himself.

famousDead: Cut the first terraces below the First Hall for King Brom II.
FX28-004.secret: The First Hall's barley runs out in May, and Ase has been quietly buying Ranpuri rice through the Quarrystones of Garbek Gate.
hooks: The First Hall will go hungry in May unless someone pays for grain.
Skeggi wants to reach the forgetful king.
Ranpuri rice could feed the hold and enrage the Old Toll.

FX28-005.name: Clan Shaftdelve
FX28-005.title: Sergeant of the Hall of Counter-Mines
FX28-005.arms: a black pick over a red tunnel mouth, on grey

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Hall of Counter-Mines
military.unit: a company of the Kelfast Sappers, 100 counter-miners
military.ties: Shaftdelves have dug against every mine laid under a Stonehold wall since Thargard in 611, and their sergeants serve under the Master of the Hall of Counter-Mines.

FX28-005.power: A company of the Kelfast Sappers, the best counter-miners alive, and a secret the Old Toll needs.
FX28-005.history: A Shaftdelve sapper brought down 20 m of Thargard's wall on the 38th day of the siege in 611, and the clan has been the backbone of Stonehold's counter-miners since. In 1002 Shaftdelve crews flooded two Tessarian tunnels under Kelfast with the hold's own pumps. In August 1084 they lost the third race under the Dwarf's Gate on the Nagora road, when Ranpuri miners reached the tower footing first and brought it down. After the Treaty of Tirpur the Hall Council ordered every dwarven gallery under the gate collapsed. The Shaftdelve sergeant sent to do it collapsed the mouths and left three dry galleries running under the gate, and he is still alive.
FX28-005.reputation: Dust-caked, foul-mouthed and fearless; the dwarves other dwarves send underground first.

members.role: Head of the clan; sergeant of counter-miners
members.note: He left the three galleries open in 1085 and has told only his daughter and the leader of the Old Toll.

members.role: Heir; sapper
members.note: She has walked the three galleries in the dark twice since 1100 and heard Ranpuri voices above her.

members.role: Gro's son; apprentice sapper
members.note: He talks too much in Mormund's ale-halls, and everyone knows he knows something.

famousDead: Brought down 20 m of Thargard's wall in 611.
FX28-005.secret: Three dry galleries still run under the Dwarf's Gate because Thorstein did not collapse them in 1085, and the Old Toll means to use them.
hooks: Kettil Ironbrow's spring march needs the Shaftdelve galleries.
Hauk's loose tongue could reach a Ranpuri ear.
If the Hall Council learns of the galleries, Thorstein faces the Carvers.

FX28-006.name: Clan Boltcarver
FX28-006.title: Captain of the First Hall Crossbows
FX28-006.arms: a black windlass crossbow on gold

military.office: Captains of the First Hall Crossbows
military.unit: 400 heavy crossbows of the First Hall
military.ties: The clan has held the crossbow galleries above the First Hall's gate since heavy crossbows came to the holds, and its windlasses are the heaviest in the Known World.

FX28-006.power: The crossbow galleries of the First Hall, 400 heavy crossbows, and the windlass yard that makes them.
FX28-006.history: The Boltcarvers made the first heavy windlass crossbows of Stonehold about 600, and King Orm III put a Boltcarver over the crossbow galleries of the First Hall's gate. The clan has held them since: 400 crossbows that can put a bolt through a breastplate at 150 m, cranked by windlasses each worth a year's wage. Boltcarvers were among the 40 hired crossbowmen who marched with Ostra's third gold expedition in 1097 and tore the Red Widow's wing at the upper Tirana, and two of the clan's sons were among them. One came home. The clan believes a big enough bolt can kill a dragon, and it has been building one.
FX28-006.reputation: Patient marksmen with a dragon on their minds.

members.role: Head of the clan; Captain of the First Hall Crossbows
members.note: He has not left the gate galleries for more than a night since 1060 and keeps a cot beside his windlass.

members.role: Heir; master of the windlass yard
members.note: She is building a crossbow that takes four dwarves to wind and means to shoot a dragon with it.

members.role: Gunnbjorn's son; survivor of the gold expedition of 1097
members.note: He watched the Red Widow take his brother off a rock and has asked to march with Ostra's fourth expedition to go back.

famousDead: Taken by the Red Widow on the third gold expedition.
FX28-006.secret: Alfdis has tested her dragon-bow with barbed bolt-heads bought from an Emberdeep Dragon Watch sergeant, which would look very bad while the First Hall tries Emberdeep.
hooks: Ottar wants to march with Ostra's fourth gold expedition.
Alfdis's dragon-bow needs a target.
The Old Toll wants the First Hall crossbows for its spring march.

FX28-007.name: Clan Hornhelm
FX28-007.title: Horn-Bearer of the Gate Wardens
FX28-007.arms: a black bull's horn bound in silver, on red
FX28-007.words: One for the wall, three for the door.

military.office: Horn-Bearers of the Gate Wardens
military.unit: the horn-file of the Gate Wardens, 24 horn-bearers
military.ties: A Hornhelm blows the signals of the Gate Wardens' line, and the great horn of the gate has been in the clan's hands since the siege of Thargard.

FX28-007.power: The horns of the Gate Wardens and the trust of every shield in the line, which moves when a Hornhelm blows.
FX28-007.history: The Gate Wardens fight in passages too dark and loud for shouted orders, and since the siege of Thargard in 611 the Hornhelms have carried their horns: one blast to brace, two to swap shields, three to give ground, and the long note that shuts a door. In August 1084, at the fall of the Dwarf's Gate, Shield Elder Eyvind Graywall gave the order, and a Hornhelm sounded the long note that shut the inner door on the last 40 of the rear guard. The horn-bearer was Hrefna Hornhelm, and she has not blown a horn since. The clan's other horn-bearers still serve in every company of the line. Kettil Ironbrow believes the Ranpuri killed his son behind that door, and the Hornhelms know who gave the order and who carried it.
FX28-007.reputation: Humble soldiers whose music every warden obeys without thinking.

members.role: Head of the clan; Horn-Bearer of the Gate Wardens, retired from the horn
members.note: She sounded the long note of 1084 and has not lifted a horn to her lips since.

members.role: Heir; horn-bearer of the First Hall company
members.note: He thinks his mother should tell Kettil Ironbrow the truth before someone else does.

members.role: Vestein's daughter; horn apprentice
members.note: She has learned every signal but the long note, which her grandmother will not teach.

famousDead: Blew the horn that sent the dwarves into the breach at Thargard in 611.
FX28-007.secret: Hrefna knows that Eyvind Graywall gave the order of 1084 and Brenna Ironbrow carried it, and that Kettil's son was alive behind the door when she blew.
hooks: Vestein wants the truth of 1084 told.
Kettil Ironbrow may learn who blew the horn.
Solveig wants to learn the long note.

FX28-008.name: Clan Saltvein
FX28-008.title: Master of the Kragmund Works
FX28-008.arms: a white chevron between three salt blocks, on black
FX28-008.power: The Kragmund and Bromstead saltworks, the salt trade from Morhall to the Neck, and a strongroom of silver no one talks about.
FX28-008.history: Queen Thorunn II built the Kragmund and Bromstead saltworks about 450 BR, and the Saltveins have boiled brine and cut rock salt there ever since. Salt is the one thing every porter, yak and human village below the holds must buy, and the clan sells it by the block from Morhall to the Neck. Since Orm III gave Skyhold's salt caravans free passage forever in 650, the Saltveins have had to compete with monks who pay no toll, and they have resented it for 455 years. The clan is rich, careful and much less famous than its money. In 1105 its head is lending salt and silver to the Old Toll's spring march, in return for a share of the Nagora tolls if the gate is retaken.
FX28-008.reputation: Quiet money; nobody remembers the Saltveins until they need salt or a loan.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Kragmund Works
members.note: He calls Skyhold's monks the salt-thieves and has written to the Hall Council about them every decade.

members.role: Heir; factor of the Neck trade
members.note: She has been selling salt to Ranpuri caravans on the Nagora road, which her father's Old Toll friends would call treason.

members.role: Ingrid's son; works foreman
members.note: He was badly scalded in a brine pan in 1100 and walks with a stick at 36.

FX28-008.secret: Kolbjorn backs the Old Toll's war while his daughter sells salt on the road it would close, and each keeps the other's account books.
hooks: The Old Toll's march runs on Saltvein salt and silver.
Ingrid's Nagora trade could be exposed.
Skyhold's free passage is up for argument again.

FX28-009.name: Clan Cinderbeard
FX28-009.title: Master of the Three Furnaces of Balforge
FX28-009.arms: a black anvil before red flames, on white
FX28-009.power: Three of the twelve great crucible furnaces of Balforge, above the First Hall, and a seat in the crucible guild.
FX28-009.history: The Cinderbeards were among the smiths of Balforge who first melted iron and charcoal in sealed clay crucibles about 540 BR, and since 100 the guild has given them three of its twelve great furnaces on the falls above the First Hall. No outsider has ever entered Balforge's lower halls, and Cinderbeard steel has edged the blades of kings. Since 1101 the Balforge ore has gone brittle, and the clan's ingots crack under the hammer one in four. The house of Brightforge has kept selling flawless ingots under its own mark through the same years. The Cinderbeards want to know how.
FX28-009.reputation: Superb smiths, sore losers, and lately very curious.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Three Furnaces
members.note: He has broken four of his own ingots on the anvil this winter, in a rage, to see where they crack.

members.role: Heir; crucible-mistress
members.note: She bought a Brightforge ingot under a false name and found an Emberhand rune ground off its end.

members.role: Halldora's son; journeyman
members.note: He is courting Hela Brightforge's niece for his mother's reasons and is starting to mean it.

famousDead: One of the Balforge smiths who made the first crucible steel.
FX28-009.secret: Halldora has proof that the house of Brightforge sells Emberdeep steel as Balforge steel, and if she takes it to the Eldest Carver it will be used against Emberdeep at the Founding.
hooks: Halldora holds proof that could ruin a rival and convict a sister hold.
Balforge's ore is failing and no one knows why.
Hrapp's courtship may end in love or in betrayal.

FX28-010.name: Clan Hearthward
FX28-010.title: Fire-Keeper of the First Hall
FX28-010.arms: a gold flame in a black hearth, on white
FX28-010.power: The keeping of the First Hall's fire, from which every forge of Stonehold and Irondeep is relit at the Kindling, and a place beside the Eldest Carver on the holiest night of the year.
FX28-010.history: At every Kindling on 21 December the forges of Stonehold and Irondeep are put out and relit from the fire of the First Hall, and the Hearthwards say they have fed that fire since Brom Bardun struck it in 2340 BR; the carved law has named them its keepers since King Hrodvar IV in 30. It burns in a stone hearth below the carved Law, fed with charcoal from the clan's own yards, and it has not gone out in 3,445 years. The clan carries the new fire to the gates in iron lamps for Irondeep's runners, a duty that has made it the friend of carvers and couriers in both holds. Its head stands beside the Eldest Carver at every Kindling. In 1104 he stood beside Thora Grimstone when she swore to find who taught Chanari, and he did not like what he heard.
FX28-010.reputation: Devout, gentle and tired; they have not slept a whole night in the family's memory.

members.role: Head of the clan; Fire-Keeper of the First Hall
members.note: He has fed the fire every night for 120 years and slept beside it on the coldest.

members.role: Heir; lamp-bearer
members.note: She carried the Kindling lamp to Irondeep's runners in 1104 and was handed a letter for Thora Grimstone she was told not to open.

members.role: Gudlaug's son; charcoal-burner of the hearth
members.note: He let the hearth burn low one night in 1103 while drunk, and nobody but his mother knows how low.

famousDead: Said in the clan to have carried the first coal for Brom Bardun.
FX28-010.secret: In 1103 Ivar let the First Hall's fire sink to three coals, and the clan does not know whether, by the letter of the Law, it went out.
hooks: If the fire went out in 1103, every forge relit from it since was lit wrongly.
Gudlaug carries letters between the holds and knows what is in some.
The Kindling of 1105 will be watched by every hold.

FX28-011.name: the Goatfoot kin
FX28-011.title: Eldest of the Goatfoots
FX28-011.arms: no arms; a goat's hoof scratched on a cairn stone
FX28-011.power: The high goat paths above 5,000 m around the Zardeep toll gate, a string of yaks, and buyers on both sides of the Worldspine.
FX28-011.history: The Zardeep road takes one part in ten of every load, and for as long as it has, someone has carried loads around it. The Goatfoots are the best at it: a clan of Morhall goatherds who know the high paths above 5,000 m that mules cannot climb but dwarves with yaks and stubbornness can. They carry pepper, cotton and Chanari steel past Mormund's gate in winter, when the Ironbrows think nothing moves. In 1062 the Carvers exiled their head for it, and the family moved its goats and its trade higher. Since the Nagora road cut the tolls by a third the Toll-Warden has hunted the Goatfoots harder, and they have begun selling road news to Ranpur's toll farmers as well.
FX28-011.reputation: Mad mountain smugglers whom every porter admires and every Ironbrow wants hanged.

members.role: Eldest of the kin; exiled in 1062
members.note: He has crossed the 5,600 m saddle above Mormund 140 times and lost three toes doing it.

members.role: His daughter; master of the yak trains
members.note: She sells road news to a Ranpuri toll-farmer's man at Tirpur and does not think of it as treason.

members.role: Una's son
members.note: He wants to stand in the Gate Wardens' line, which an exile's grandson may not do.

FX28-011.secret: For years the Goatfoots carried Chanari blades over the high saddle to Stonehold smiths who wanted to study them, and they know which smiths bought.
hooks: The Toll-Warden has sworn to catch Grimkell before the snow melts.
Una's road news reaches Ranpur.
Ketil wants to stand in the Gate Wardens' line.

FX28-012.name: the Mulazzi family
FX28-012.title: Master of the Garbek herds
FX28-012.arms: a black mule's head on yellow
FX28-012.power: About a third of Stonehold's mules and yaks, the high pastures below Garbek Gate leased from the Quarrystones, and debts owed by every trader on the southern road.
FX28-012.history: Stonehold moves on 3,000 mules and 1,000 yaks, and about a third of them have been bred by the Mulazzis, a family of Solen porters who came up the Garbek gorge in a hungry year about 700 and stayed. Humans may not own land in the holds, so the family rents its high pastures below Garbek Gate from Clan Quarrystone, paying in mules. Its animals carried grain to besieged Tessar for Queen Hallgerd in 708, a story the family tells and no dwarf confirms. The Mulazzis are tall, loud and indispensable, and every dwarf trader on the southern road owes them money. In 1105 the Old Toll wants 600 mules for its spring march, and the family must decide whether a war is good for business.
FX28-012.reputation: Loud, shrewd human herders whom the dwarves pretend to tolerate and could not do without.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Garbek herds
members.note: He can price a mule by its ears at fifty paces and has never lost money on a war.

members.role: Heir; drover of the yak trains
members.note: She has walked the Zardeep road twelve summers and speaks Holdspeech better than her father.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: He wants to marry a dwarf porter's daughter of the terraces, which no law forbids and every dwarf would forbid.

famousDead: Led the mule train that carried grain to besieged Tessar over the mountains in 708.
FX28-012.secret: Fausto has already sold 300 mules to Ranpur's Nagora toll farm, and the Old Toll's order would have him selling to both sides of the same war.
hooks: The Old Toll wants 600 mules by spring.
Remo's dwarven sweetheart would make him an outcast among two peoples.
Lazzaro's story of 708 points at a contract the Carvers keep secret.

FX29-001.name: Clan Coalheart
FX29-001.title: Thane of Gorhall
FX29-001.arms: a red sun of glowing coal on black, a copper border

military.office: Thanes of Gorhall and Wardens of the Hazdeep road
military.unit: the Gorhall and Hazdeep road watch, 300 crossbows and shields
military.ties: The thane commands the road watch for the Forge-Queen, and Coalheart sons serve their five-year turns in the Tharmund Gate Shields.

FX29-001.power: Gorhall hold with its copper and iron galleries, the road watch on the Hazdeep road, and empty galleries enough to house a kingdom.
FX29-001.history: Forge-King Harl opened Gorhall for copper and iron near the Hazdeep road about 590 and gave its galleries to the Coalhearts, who had carried charcoal on the exile road. Gorhall is the hold farthest from the Breath Halls and the coldest, the only one in Emberdeep that burns charcoal for warmth, and its people call the capital's dwarves soft. The Coalheart thane commands the 300 of the Gorhall and Hazdeep road watch and keeps the road east toward Skyhold's country. Since the Dragon Watch killed a young Ash Dragon in November 1104, Red Stair pilgrims on the Hazdeep road have been asking questions at Gorhall's gate. If the hold must one day leave the Breath Halls, Gorhall is cold and has room, and its thane has begun to say so.
FX29-001.reputation: Blunt, hardy frontier dwarves who think the capital has grown soft in its hot baths.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of Gorhall
members.note: He offered Gorhall's empty galleries to the Forge-Queen as a new capital, loudly, at a council she meant to keep quiet.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Hazdeep road watch
members.note: She turned back a party of Red Stair pilgrims in December who asked to see the walled gallery at Kardeep.

members.role: Kolfinna's son
members.note: He has come to believe the Red Stair, that dragons are holy, and he keeps it from his mother.

famousDead: First thane of Gorhall under Forge-King Harl.
FX29-001.secret: Hrolf knows about the Forge-Queen's escape road and means to make Gorhall, not Balmund, the end of it, whatever that costs Balmund.
hooks: The Red Stair is asking questions on the Hazdeep road.
Gorhall wants to become the new heart of Emberdeep.
Ulfljot may give the dragon secret to the pilgrims.

FX29-002.name: Clan Deepbellow
FX29-002.title: Thane of the Balmund Terraces
FX29-002.arms: a gold barley-sheaf on three green terrace steps, on brown
FX29-002.power: The barley terraces, goat pens and yak pastures of Balmund, the food of a third of the hold, and the 15,000 human farmers and porters who work them.
FX29-002.history: Forge-Queen Sif cut Balmund on the south slope about 705 so that Emberdeep could feed its own, and the Deepbellows, a clan of bellows-men from the first forges, asked for the terraces instead of the fires. They have farmed them since: barley, goats and yaks on the warm south slope, worked by about 15,000 human farmers and porters who live below the hold. In the hungry years of the 940s the terraces failed three years in four, and it was a Deepbellow thane who first went down the Tharmund road to beg rice from Ranpur. The clan never learned what the rice was paid with. In 1105 strange work-parties have been seen at night in the old silver galleries above Balmund, and the thane has been told by the works guard not to ask.
FX29-002.reputation: Generous farmer-lords, more at home with goats and porters than at court.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of the Balmund Terraces
members.note: He has seen lamps in the old silver galleries above his terraces and been told by a captain half his age that they are none of his business.

members.role: Heir; mistress of the human villages
members.note: She speaks the porters' dialect and has heard them say the mountain is going to open.

members.role: Signhild's son
members.note: He followed a night work-party into the old galleries and found a tunnel running uphill toward the Breath Halls.

famousDead: Went down to Ranpur to beg rice in the hungry years of the 940s.
FX29-002.secret: Torfi has found the Forge-Queen's escape road, and the Deepbellows have worked out what it means.
hooks: Torfi knows where the escape road runs.
The human villages below Balmund believe the mountain will open.
If the hold moves to Balmund, the Deepbellows become the most important clan in Emberdeep.

FX29-003.name: Clan Anvilborn
FX29-003.title: Thane of Stordeep
FX29-003.arms: a black anvil on red, a gold gem above

military.office: Thanes of Stordeep
military.unit: the Stordeep watch, 100 shields
military.ties: Anvilborn carriers serve in the Hammer Guard, where their arms are counted among the clan's thirty.

FX29-003.power: The gem-cutting halls of Stordeep, Hammerhand blood and carriers of the hammer arms, and the hope of the forge-masters who want an heir who keeps secrets.
FX29-003.history: When the Hammerhands married cousins to keep the hammer arms, some branches drifted from the crown, and the Anvilborns are the oldest of them: descendants of Forge-King Harl's younger son Sverri, who failed to lift the Anvil of Dagna at the Kindling of 615 when his sister Sif succeeded, and was given Stordeep's gem halls instead. They have cut Emberdeep's gems at Stordeep since, and every generation they send a child to try the anvil. None has lifted it in 490 years. In 1104 the thane's granddaughter, 40 and not yet carved, lifted a 90 kg anvil-weight above her head in the clan's own forge and held it for the count. Forge-Princess Asta wants to confess the hold's crimes, and some forge-masters would rather the crown went to a Hammerhand who would not.
FX29-003.reputation: Royal cousins with long memories, fine hands and a grudge as old as the crown.

members.role: Head of the clan; Thane of Stordeep
members.note: He tried the anvil at forty and failed by a hand's breadth, and has spent 120 years waiting for a grandchild who would not.

members.role: Heir; master gem-cutter of Stordeep
members.note: She would rather her daughter cut sapphires than fight her cousins for a crown.

members.role: Brynhild's daughter; carrier of the full hammer arms
members.note: She lifted the anvil-weight in 1104 and has been invited to the Hammer Guard's table by Rolf Hammerhand, who does not trust her.

famousDead: Harl's younger son; failed the anvil in 615 and founded the line at Stordeep.
FX29-003.secret: Sigtrygg has promised the Smith-Father's Breath that Dagrun would never confess the hold's crimes, in return for their voices if Asta is set aside.
hooks: Dagrun could lift the Anvil of Dagna at the Kindling of 1105.
The Smith-Father's Breath wants an heir who keeps secrets.
Rolf Hammerhand's failing heart may open the Hammer Guard's champion's place.

FX29-004.name: Clan Granitejaw
FX29-004.title: First Sergeant of the Tharmund Gate Shields
FX29-004.arms: a grey shield bearing a black mountain, on red

military.office: Hereditary file-sergeants of the Tharmund Gate Shields
military.unit: the Granitejaw files, 60 shields of the Tharmund Gate Shields
military.ties: Every dwarf of Emberdeep serves five-year turns in the Gate Shields, and the turns have been drilled by Granitejaw sergeants since the gate was cut.

FX29-004.power: The drill-yard of Tharmund Gate, sixty shields, and the habit of command over every dwarf who has served a turn there, which is every dwarf.
FX29-004.history: The Granitejaws have stood in Tharmund Gate since Dagna cut it about 430: a gate at 2,673 m on the one road up from the Gundgard valleys. When Forge-Queen Ragna put the Gate Shields on five-year turns, the drilling of each new turn fell to the sergeant clan that had stood in the gate longest, and that was the Granitejaws. Their sergeants have taught the shield-wall to every thane, smith and carver now living, the Forge-Princess among them. They are the Road-Warden's men and proud of it, and they watch every train that passes. In 1105 they have noticed that the gem trains going down to Ranpur weigh less at the bottom of the road than at the top.
FX29-004.reputation: The loudest voices in Emberdeep and the most honest; every dwarf remembers being shouted at by one.

members.role: Head of the clan; First Sergeant of the Gate Shields
members.note: He drilled Forge-Princess Asta in her turn of 1032 and still calls her by her file-name.

members.role: Heir; file-sergeant
members.note: She counts the gem trains at the top and the bottom of the road and has found one load in ten missing.

members.role: Thorgerd's son; in his first turn
members.note: He is serving his first five years behind a shield and wants to join the Dragon Watch instead.

famousDead: First sergeant of Tharmund Gate under Dagna.
FX29-004.secret: Thorgerd's count proves that one gem in ten goes missing between the top and bottom of the road, which points at the Road-Warden the clan has served for 600 years.
hooks: Thorgerd must decide whether to accuse the Road-Warden.
The gems pledged for the Lotus Loan are being skimmed.
Kalf wants a place in the Dragon Watch.

FX29-005.name: Clan Skybolt
FX29-005.title: Bolt-Sergeant of the Kardeep Dragon Watch
FX29-005.arms: a red dragon pierced by a black barbed bolt, on white

military.office: Bolt-sergeants of the Kardeep Dragon Watch
military.unit: the Skybolt crews, 60 heavy crossbows of the Dragon Watch
military.ties: A Skybolt crew has stood on the Kardeep heights since Forge-King Harl founded the Dragon Watch in 614, and the clan's bolt yard makes the barbed heads that tear a wing membrane.

FX29-005.power: Sixty heavy crossbows on the Kardeep heights, the bolt yard of the Dragon Watch, and a body in a walled gallery.
FX29-005.history: After the eggs of 612 Forge-King Harl founded the Kardeep Dragon Watch, and the first bolt-sergeant he named was a Skybolt who had seen Durek's party fall from the gorge road. The clan has served the Watch since, crewing the heavy crossbows above the gold mines at 4,773 m and forging the barbed bolt-heads that tear a dragon's wing. In 1074 a Skybolt crew wound the crossbow Inga Crag used to drive off the Ash Dragon over the ore train. In November 1104 another Skybolt crew shot down the young dragon above Kardeep, and the clan's sergeant walled its body into the old gallery with his own hands. The clan knows what the Red Stair would do if it learned, and it sleeps badly.
FX29-005.reputation: Sky-watchers with stiff necks and steady hands, proud of the most dangerous post in the hold.

members.role: Head of the clan; Bolt-Sergeant of the Dragon Watch
members.note: He walled the dead dragon into the old gallery in November and dreams that it is still breathing.

members.role: Heir; master of the bolt yard
members.note: She has sold barbed bolt-heads to a Stonehold crossbow captain who wants to shoot a dragon of his own.

members.role: Hildigunn's son; crossbowman
members.note: He kept a scale from the dead dragon, and a Red Stair pilgrim at Gorhall has offered him gold for it.

famousDead: First bolt-sergeant of the Dragon Watch (614).
FX29-005.secret: Grjot kept a scale from the dragon walled up in November 1104, and he has shown it to a Red Stair pilgrim.
hooks: The scale could bring the Red Stair's curse on the hold.
Hildigunn's bolt-heads have gone to Stonehold.
The dead dragon's mate still nests above Kardeep.

FX29-006.name: Clan Ventguard
FX29-006.title: Captain of the Stair Watch
FX29-006.arms: a silver key over a white plume of steam, on grey

military.office: Captains of the Stair Watch
military.unit: the stair watch of the Breath Halls, 200 of the garrison
military.ties: Since the steam burst of 1050 the Ventguards have posted the watch above every sealed gallery of the Breath Halls, and no one goes below without their key.

FX29-006.power: The keys of every sealed gallery of the Breath Halls and 200 dwarves of the garrison who guard the lower stairs.
FX29-006.history: The Ventguards were masons of the lower Breath Halls until February 1050, when a steam pocket broke into a sealed gallery and killed Forge-Queen Ragna and 23 smiths. The clan's head led the first party down after the burst, his son carried the queen's body up, and Hilde Hammerhand gave the clan the keys of every sealed gallery that year. They have kept the stair watch since: 200 dwarves posted above the lowest halls, who listen to the rock, read the sweat on the walls and turn back anyone who wants to go down. Their captains are the only dwarves outside the twelve sworn surveyors who see the lower stairs every day. They have learned to say nothing about what they see.
FX29-006.reputation: Grim, quiet guards of the hold's cellar door; children dare each other to ask them what is down there.

members.role: Head of the clan; Captain of the Stair Watch
members.note: He carried Forge-Queen Ragna's body up the stair in 1050 and has walked it every night since.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the gallery keys
members.note: She has felt the heat of the lowest stair with her own hand every day for ten years, and her figures are three degrees higher than the Carvers' stones.

members.role: Ingunn's son; watchman
members.note: He has been offered a place in the works guard of the silver seam and knows it is no silver seam.

famousDead: Led the first party down after the steam burst of 1050.
FX29-006.secret: Ingunn's own readings show the lower stair three degrees hotter than the Carvers' tally stones, and she knows the stones were cut wrong on purpose.
hooks: Ingunn holds proof that the heat tallies were falsified.
Hoskuld is being drawn into the escape road's guard.
A new vent opened on the lowest stair in December.

FX29-007.name: Clan Bellowsmouth
FX29-007.title: Master of the Bellows Hall
FX29-007.arms: a pair of red bellows blowing a gold flame, on black
FX29-007.power: The Bellows Hall, the water-driven bellows of the Breath Forges, and the secret of the newest pattern.
FX29-007.history: Emberdeep's forges breathe through bellows, and since the exile road the Bellowsmouths have built them: great leather lungs worked by hand and foot, and since 870 by the hot-spring water piped through the Breath Halls. Their water-driven bellows are the clan's secret and its pride. In 1096 a bellows-wright the clan had trained for forty years, Yrsa Windbellows, sold drawings of one to a Chanari smith, and Eldest Carver Bolli Ashgrave had her walled out in the winter snows. The Bellowsmouths spoke against her and have not been forgiven by half the forges, who say the clan taught her the trade and then threw her to the snow. The clan's head knows the drawings Yrsa sold were of the old pattern, not the new.
FX29-007.reputation: Proud craftsmen with a cold name since 1097.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master of the Bellows Hall
members.note: He spoke against his own pupil in 1097 and stood at the wall while they bricked her out.

members.role: Heir; water-bellows master
members.note: She was Yrsa's friend and still gets a letter from her each monsoon, from somewhere below the Gundgard.

members.role: Aldis's son; apprentice
members.note: He has drawn a bellows driven by steam from the vents themselves, which would be either the hold's salvation or its funeral.

famousDead: Carried the clan's bellows leathers on the exile road.
FX29-007.secret: Thorkel knew the drawings Yrsa sold were of the old bellows, worthless to Chanari, and let her be walled out anyway to keep the new pattern safe.
hooks: Aldis receives letters from an exile.
Fjalar's steam bellows could change the forges.
If Yrsa returns, she will want her name and her revenge.

FX29-008.name: the Vorcaro family
FX29-008.title: Master of the Maghelm charcoal
FX29-008.arms: a black charcoal kiln under a green fir, on gold
FX29-008.power: A third of the charcoal that feeds Emberdeep's crucibles, the timber trade of Maghelm, and the props contract for the works guard's silver seam.
FX29-008.history: The Vorcaros came up the Gundgard as porters in 812 and stayed to sell what Emberdeep does not have: wood. Maghelm is the timber and fur market below the holds, and the family's charcoal-burners in the villages of Dramshaft and Thraindor cut the fir and oak of Vorkarn Wood for the forges. The hot springs heat the halls, but crucible steel still eats charcoal, and the Vorcaros sell about a third of it. Humans may not enter the inner halls, so the family's head has never seen the forges his charcoal feeds. Since 1102 the works guard has been buying timber props by the thousand for a silver seam, and the Vorcaros have noticed that silver seams do not usually need that many.
FX29-008.reputation: Prosperous, sociable human merchants who count everything, including what the dwarves do not say.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Maghelm charcoal
members.note: He has sold charcoal to Emberdeep for 35 years and has never been allowed past Tharmund's inner door.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the props contract
members.note: She has sold 6,000 timber props to the works guard since 1102 and worked out how long a tunnel they would hold up.

members.role: Younger son; charcoal-burner at Thraindor
members.note: He drinks with the Sootfingers and has carried one of their parcels down the gorge road without asking what was in it.

famousDead: Came up the Gundgard as a porter in 812 and stayed to burn charcoal.
FX29-008.secret: Fiora has worked out from the props she sold that the works guard is cutting a tunnel about 9 km long, and she has told a Ranpuri temple-bank agent.
hooks: The props contract has made the family rich and curious.
Pello is drifting toward the Sootfingers.
The temple banks of Ranpur now know more about the escape road than the Forge-Queen thinks.

FX29-009.name: Clan Ashvault
FX29-009.title: Keeper of the Drying Halls
