FX29-009.arms: a grey vault-arch over a black bier, on white
FX29-009.power: The drying halls where every dwarf of Emberdeep lies for a year before burial, and the trust of every family that visits its dead there.
FX29-009.history: Forge-Queen Sif began the custom that outsiders find strangest: the dead of Emberdeep are laid for a year in hot, dry galleries until they dry like leather, and only then sealed in the rock. The Ashvaults have kept the drying halls since about 700, washing the dead, laying them out and leading the families who come to visit them. The drying galleries were cut on the warmest rock of the Breath Halls, and since 1050 they have grown warmer every year. In 1103 the clan moved the dead to a higher gallery without telling anyone why. The Ashvaults now dry their dead in half the time their grandparents did, and they have told only the Forge-Queen.
FX29-009.reputation: Calm, kindly keepers of the dead whom every dwarf meets twice: once as a mourner, once as a guest.

members.role: Head of the clan; Keeper of the Drying Halls
members.note: She has laid out 6,000 of the dead and sat the year beside the Forge-Queen's mother.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the upper gallery
members.note: He moved the dead uphill in 1103 and carried his own grandfather twice.

members.role: Bjorn's daughter; washer of the dead
members.note: She found a body in the old gallery in December that was on no roll: a dwarf in a works-guard coat.

famousDead: First Keeper of the Drying Halls under Forge-Queen Sif.
FX29-009.secret: Gerd found the unrecorded body of a works-guard dwarf in the old drying gallery, and the works guard has asked the clan to forget it.
hooks: The drying halls are too hot, and the dead show it.
Gerd's unrecorded body points at the secret road.
Families who visit their dead have begun to ask why they were moved.

FX29-010.name: Clan Ridgehorn
FX29-010.title: Master Hunter of Gorhall
FX29-010.arms: a black ibex horn above a green mount, on white
FX29-010.power: The high hunting grounds above Gorhall, the passes the roads do not use, and the best knowledge of the dragons' nesting ground of anyone alive.
FX29-010.history: The Ridgehorns have hunted the heights above Gorhall since the hold was cut, taking ibex, blue sheep and the snow bears that come down to the mine dumps in hard winters. They guide prospectors, carry messages over passes the roads do not use and know the warm ground above Kardeep where the dragons nest better than any dwarf alive. Kolbein Bearbane is the famous hunter of the heights; the Ridgehorns are the family that taught him and resent that he forgot it. Since the dragons came to nest above Kardeep in 1102 the clan has watched the pair through polished crystal lenses. They know the female has laid again.
FX29-010.reputation: Shy, weather-beaten hunters who would rather sleep on a ledge than in a hall.

members.role: Head of the clan; Master Hunter of Gorhall
members.note: He has watched the Kardeep dragons for three years from a rock shelf 2 km off and named both of them.

members.role: Heir; guide of the high passes
members.note: She guided a Red Stair pilgrim to a shelf above the nest in 1103 and wishes she had not.

members.role: Asny's son
members.note: He was Kolbein Bearbane's best pupil until Kolbein struck him for a missed shot, and he has not forgiven it.

FX29-010.secret: The Kardeep dragon pair has laid again since the young one was killed, and the Ridgehorns have not told the Dragon Watch.
hooks: New dragon eggs lie above the gold mines.
The Red Stair pilgrims want a guide.
Toki has a grudge against Kolbein Bearbane.

FX29-011.name: the Sootfingers of Thraindor
FX29-011.title: Head of the Sootfingers
FX29-011.arms: no arms; a black thumbprint of soot on a white rag
FX29-011.power: A gem path down the gorge that the Gate Shields do not watch, a charcoal village that keeps its mouth shut, and Ranpuri dealers who ask no questions.
FX29-011.history: Dwarves walled out of Emberdeep for crimes against the Deep Law have nowhere to go but down, and since about 1040 a few of them have come to the charcoal village of Thraindor in the Maghelm Firs. There they found human charcoal-burners with long knives and no love for the gate fee, and the two together became the Sootfingers. They carry gems down the gorge by paths the Tharmund Gate Shields do not watch, sell them to Ranpuri dealers and buy back rice and news. Their dwarves cannot go home and their humans cannot enter the halls, so they have made a home of the smoke. In 1104 they began carrying parcels for someone inside the hold, and the parcels go to Chanari.
FX29-011.reputation: Soot-black smugglers whom the Road-Warden hunts and half of Maghelm buys from.

members.role: Head of the gang; a dwarf walled out in 1061
members.note: He was exiled for striking a Carver's clerk and has sworn to strike a Carver before he dies.

members.role: His human partner; charcoal-burner of Thraindor
members.note: She runs the gem path down the gorge and has never lost a parcel or a carrier.

members.role: Brina's son
members.note: He is the fastest runner in Thraindor and carries the Chanari parcels.

FX29-011.secret: The parcels they carry to Chanari for someone inside the hold are Emberhand letters, and the Steel-Warden of Chanari answers them.
hooks: The Tharmund Gate Shields are hunting the gem path.
Someone inside the hold pays the Sootfingers to carry letters to Chanari.
Starkad wants revenge on the Carvers.

FX30-001.name: House Tirwala
FX30-001.title: Lord of the Ekapur Shore
FX30-001.arms: a gold sun over green rice terraces, on saffron
FX30-001.words: The rain comes to the patient.

military.office: Lords' Shields of the Ekapur coast
military.unit: the Tirwala Shields, 800 heavy foot and 20 elephants
military.ties: Tirwala Shields have stood in the Raja's second line in every dry-season war since the Sagar rajas.

FX30-001.power: About 300 villages of terraced rice and sugar cane in the Ekapur hills, the market tolls of three coast towns, and 800 Shields in the house's own pay.
FX30-001.history: The Tirwala were rice chiefs of the Ekapur hills when Raja Mahendra II Sagar built his 40 galleys in 706, and he paid them for teak and rowers with the title of Lord. Their dykes held in the cyclone of 1071 while the delta's broke in 40 places, and they sold rice to the crown that winter at famine prices, which Raja Devraj never forgave. Lord Bhanu Tirwala led 800 Shields at Tiravi in April 1083 and pulled them off the field before the maddened elephants reached his line. Prince Indrajit called it cowardice; the Shields call it the day Bhanu saved them. Since 1103 Bhanu's heir has drunk with Lord Kiran Ranavir and lent him rice silver against a promise of the Chief Minister's seat.
FX30-001.reputation: Rich, careful and cold; the Raja's men call them Lord Kiran's purse.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Ekapur Shore
members.note: Pulled his Shields out of the rout at Tiravi and has been called a coward at court for twenty years.

members.role: Heir; Captain of the Tirwala Shields
members.note: Lends Lord Kiran rice silver and already chooses the robes he will wear as Chief Minister.

members.role: Lady of the house; keeper of the granary books
members.note: Knows to the sack how much rice the house hid in 1071, and how many delta children died for want of it.

members.role: Younger son; novice at the Great Temple
members.note: Carries his brother's letters to temple families he is not supposed to know.

famousDead: First Lord of the Ekapur Shore; sold teak and rowers to the new Sagar fleet.
FX30-001.secret: Since 1103 the house has lent Lord Kiran Ranavir 6,000 lotus, and Yash has promised him the Tirwala Shields if the succession breaks.
hooks: If Prince Vikram fails his arsenic cup in public, the Tirwala Shields march on the palace.
A granary clerk wants silver to forget the rice hidden in 1071.

FX30-002.name: House Girvan
FX30-002.title: Lord of the Tiravi Fords
FX30-002.arms: a white ford-stone between two black mountains, on rust red
FX30-002.words: We were here before the road.

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the Tiravi Fords
military.unit: the Girvan Shields, 200 spearmen and 60 crossbows
military.ties: Girvan men hold the second road fort above Tiravi for the Nagora Road Wardens and fight under Nagar banners.

FX30-002.power: The rice terraces and fords of the upper Chanpur at Tiravi, one road fort of the Nagora road, and 260 sworn men.
FX30-002.history: The Girvan were hill chiefs of the upper Chanpur who sold salt and honey to the delta long before they bowed to the Pratap rajas. The battle of 12 April 1083 was fought on their terraces: dwarven pits and caltrops broke the Raja's elephants in Girvan rice, and Girvan villagers buried about 3,000 Ranpuri dead. When Raja Devraj gave the Nagar the road forts in 1077, the Girvan got one fort and no share of the tolls, and they have hated the Warden's clerks since. A Girvan child lost a foot to a buried caltrop in 1101, and the house still pays boys a pice for every iron spike they dig up.
FX30-002.reputation: Proud, poor hill lords who know every goat path round the Nagora Gate.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Tiravi Fords
members.note: Watched the elephants trample his terraces in 1083 and has billed the crown for the rice every year since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Girvan road fort
members.note: Honest to a fault and the only Girvan the Nagar trust.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Sells road news to Mahesh Scarback, hoping a dwarf raid will shame the Nagar.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Rebuilt the terrace walls stone by stone after the battle and keeps a jar of dwarven caltrops on her table.

famousDead: Uday's brother; guided the Miners of Tirpur to the gate by a goat path and died in the first gallery.
FX30-002.secret: Tarun Girvan sells the movements of the Road Wardens to the rebel Mahesh Scarback, who sells them on to Stonehold's Old Toll.
hooks: The Old Toll marches in spring, and a Girvan son drew their map.
Lord Uday demands the toll share the Nagar never paid.

FX30-003.name: House Mandapi
FX30-003.title: Lady of the Pepper Terraces
FX30-003.arms: a black pepper vine climbing a green tree, on gold

military.office: Lords of the Dasali hill garrison
military.unit: the Mandapi bows, 300 archers in the Dasali garrison
military.ties: Mandapi archers make up a sixth of the 2,000 men who hold the Pepper Hills for the Raja.

FX30-003.power: The pepper gardens of the Madora hills, about a fifth of Ranpur's pepper crop, and a seat in the Dasali hill garrison.
FX30-003.history: The Mandapi were the first pepper chiefs to sell their hills to Raja Aditya Pratap in 338, and he made them Lords for opening the gate of Dasali. For seven centuries they have sold pepper down to Madora and out by sea, and since the Nagora road opened in 1081 their pepper has undercut Kesh's in the north. Lord Govind Mandapi died of fever in 1099, and his widow Padma has run the house since, because her son is a scholar who cannot tell a vine from a creeper. Keshi agents have twice tried to buy her harvest before it reaches the Raja's scales.
FX30-003.reputation: Old, sharp-tongued pepper lords; Kesh thinks them the enemy and Madora thinks them stingy.

members.role: Head of the house in her son's name; Lady of the Pepper Terraces
members.note: Weighs every basket herself and has outlived two Keshi bribes and one poisoned sweet.

members.role: Heir; Lord in name
members.note: Would rather copy palm-leaf hymns than ride the terraces, and owes a bookseller 200 lotus.

members.role: Nephew; captain of the Mandapi bows
members.note: Runs night baskets of pepper down to Keshi captains and keeps the silver in a hollow drum.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: The only one who has noticed her cousin's new silver rings.

famousDead: Opened Dasali's gate to Aditya the Hill-Taker and was made Lord.
FX30-003.secret: Naveen Mandapi sells about 40 baskets a year past the Raja's scales to Keshi smugglers through the Kalapani pirates.
hooks: A Keshi factor offers Lady Padma double for the whole crop.
Ishan's bookseller wants payment in pepper.

FX30-004.name: House Devkar
FX30-004.title: Dyke-Lord of the Western Arm
FX30-004.arms: three blue waves under a brown dyke, on pale ochre
FX30-004.power: The dykes, sluices and 60 villages of the western arm of the Chanpur delta, and the labor of every man there for 20 days a year.
FX30-004.history: Raja Jaidev Sagar the Dyke-Raiser gave the Devkar the western arm of the delta in 590 to raise its dykes and keep them, and for five centuries they have. The cyclone of October 1071 broke the dykes in 40 places, 12 of them Devkar dykes, and Lord Chetan Devkar drowned trying to close a sluice. His son rebuilt them on money borrowed from the temple banks at 12%, and the house now owes House Bhaskar about 9,000 lotus. Half its villages are bound to temple fields until the debt is paid, and the temples still refuse to pay a pice for the outer dykes. Lord Hemant Devkar has begun, very quietly, to listen to the One Face.
FX30-004.reputation: Muddy, hard-working and drowning in temple debt.

members.role: Head of the house; Dyke-Lord of the Western Arm
members.note: Rebuilt his drowned father's dykes on temple loans and now hates every temple bell he hears.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Feeds the bound debtors from her own kitchen and is quietly bankrupting the house doing it.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Goes to Meera Jalan's sermons in a fisherman's cloak.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Draws dyke plans on the walls in charcoal and wants to study with the Raja's engineers.

famousDead: Drowned closing a sluice in the cyclone of 1071; the villagers still leave rice on the sluice gate.
FX30-004.secret: Lord Hemant has given 400 lotus to the One Face preachers and lets Dev the Unbound's men hide in his reed beds.
hooks: The monsoon will test a dyke Hemant could not afford to finish.
The temple court calls in the debt in the spring.

FX30-005.name: House Purkar
FX30-005.title: Lord of the Charcoal Hills
FX30-005.arms: a red flame rising from a black charcoal mound, on dark grey

military.office: Lords of the Charcoal Hills levy
military.unit: 200 hill spears and the charcoal-burners' levy
military.ties: Purkar spears join the Smiths' Wall Guard of Chanari whenever the Steel-Warden calls.

FX30-005.power: Teak and sal forests above Chanari and the charcoal that feeds every Chanari forge, sold by the cartload to the Steel-Warden.
FX30-005.history: The Purkar were hill chiefs who bowed to Aditya Pratap after the five-month siege of Chanari in 338, and his son made them Lords of the forest. Since the Chanari Compact of about 950 their charcoal has fed the crucible furnaces, and the Varma pay them well and watch them closely. The man-eating tiger called the Striped Death killed about 200 people around Chanari before the Raja shot it in 1098, and 60 of them were Purkar villagers. Lord Sameer Purkar beat the drive that day and still says his huntsman's arrow struck first. The house's charcoal tally is kept beside the Varma steel tally, and in 1104 the numbers stopped matching.
FX30-005.reputation: Sooty, stubborn foresters who think Chanari owes them its fame.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Charcoal Hills
members.note: Swears his huntsman shot the Striped Death first and that the Raja only finished it.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the charcoal tally
members.note: Sells 30 extra cartloads a year to a hidden mill above Chanari and writes them down as rain-spoiled.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Hunts, sleeps and lets his sister do the sums.

members.role: Dowager; Sameer's mother
members.note: Lost two sons to the Striped Death and keeps a tiger skull by her bed to remind the gods.

famousDead: Sameer's father; kept the forges burning through the drought of 1064 by cutting the temple grove.
FX30-005.secret: Leela Purkar sells charcoal to Ravi Lohar's hidden water-bellows mill, which makes blades that never enter the Varma tally.
hooks: The Steel-Warden's clerk finds the charcoal and steel tallies do not match.
A dwarf woman buys charcoal at night with Ranpuri silver.

FX30-006.name: House Jaldhar
FX30-006.title: Warden of the Madora Mouth
FX30-006.arms: a white tower standing in teal water, on teal

military.office: Wardens of the Madora river-mouth fort
military.unit: the Madora Mouth garrison, 300 men and four galleys
military.ties: Jaldhar galleys fight the river pirates every dry season beside the Fleet Marines and send their sons to the Raja's galleys.

FX30-006.power: The brick fort at the mouth of the Madora river, its harbor dues, four galleys, and a chain across the channel.
FX30-006.history: Raja Mahendra II Sagar built a fort at the Madora river mouth in 706, when the Neck road closed and Ranpur took to the sea, and gave it to his galley captain Jayant Jaldhar. The Jaldhar have held it since and fought the Amber harbor chiefs for the cotton ships more than once. Pirates of the delta mouths raid cotton barges every dry season, and every dry season the Jaldhar hang a few of them on the fort's water gate. Since 1085 Amber ships have undercut Madora's cotton freight, and the harbor dues have halved. The warden's brother has found another way to make up the difference.
FX30-006.reputation: Brave river wardens with a famously soft spot in their chain.

members.role: Head of the house; Warden of the Madora Mouth
members.note: Has hanged 31 pirates on the water gate and never wondered why the biggest crews always slip past.

members.role: Brother; master of the harbor chain
members.note: Lowers the chain for the Kalapani boats for a tenth of the cargo.

members.role: Heir; galley captain
members.note: Wants a war with the Amber Isles badly enough to start one.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Writes the fort's letters to the Chief Minister and reads the ones her brother-in-law burns.

famousDead: Galley captain of Mahendra II Sagar; first Warden of the Madora Mouth.
FX30-006.secret: Dinesh Jaldhar takes a tenth of the Kalapani pirates' cargo to lower the Madora chain at night.
hooks: A captured pirate swears the warden's own brother let him through.
Hari Jaldhar boards an Amber spice ship without orders.

FX30-007.name: House Ravikar
FX30-007.title: Knight of the Royal Horse
FX30-007.arms: a silver horse rearing under a gold sun-disc, on crimson
FX30-007.words: Swift where the elephants are slow.

military.office: Hereditary captains in the Royal Horse
military.unit: a squadron of 100 Royal Horse at Jalari
military.ties: In a kingdom of elephants the Ravikar have ridden in the Royal Horse for four generations and buy their mounts from Morhaven traders.

FX30-007.power: A knight's fief of rice villages in the Ekapur hills and the captaincy of a Royal Horse squadron.
FX30-007.history: Raja Vikram the Unpoisoned knighted the first Ravikar in 1001, a horse-trader's son who rode the news of the poisoned feast to Tirpur in three days. In a land where horses die of the wet and must all be bought abroad, the house has made riding its pride: Ravikar sons can sit a Morhaven horse at a gallop and shoot from it. They rode at Tiravi in 1083 and were the only Ranpuri horse not scattered by their own elephants. The heir now wants to ride north with the Warden's Northern Road party and join the race for the upper Tirana gold. The house spends half its rice on horses that cost 80 suns each and die in four monsoons.
FX30-007.reputation: Dashing, poor and horse-mad; the elephant men laugh at them.

members.role: Head of the house; captain of a Royal Horse squadron
members.note: Rode round the Tiravi rout and pulled the Warden's wounded son out of the river.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Has asked the Warden for 200 riders and a road north to the gold.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: The best horse doctor in Ekapur, and she rides astride when her mother is not looking.

famousDead: Rode the news of the poisoned feast to Tirpur in three days and was knighted for it.
hooks: A shipment of Morhaven horses arrives with fever.
Pranav rides north without leave to find the gold.

FX30-008.name: House Gajapal
FX30-008.title: Lord of the Pearl Grazing
FX30-008.arms: a white crescent moon over a grey hill, on slate blue
FX30-008.words: We guard what the gods sent.
FX30-008.power: Grazing lands and herd-villages near Nagita that pasture the Pearl Herd on the temple estate, and the right to catch wild elephants on the southern slopes.
FX30-008.history: The Gajapal were elephant catchers of the southern slopes when the Pratap took the hills, and they bowed to the Mallik as Masters of Elephants in the 4th century. For six hundred years their herd-boys have grazed the Pearl Herd, the grey elephants of the white line, on the temple estate near Nagita, while the Chandar keep the herd book. They have watched the herd grow old and inbred and no white calf come since Moon-Pearl in 1046. In 1101 Gajapal herd-boys were told to feed a pale young cow in a hidden valley and ask nothing. Lord Kanchan Gajapal asked nothing, and was paid for it.
FX30-008.reputation: Quiet herders of holy beasts, trusted by the temples because they never ask questions.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of the Pearl Grazing
members.note: Took 300 lotus from Keeper Anand's agent in 1101 and has not slept well since.

members.role: Heir; master of the herd-boys
members.note: Saw the pale cow up close and knows she has the wrong ears for the white line.

members.role: Herd-boy; grandson
members.note: Feeds the hidden cow sugar cakes every evening and has given her a name.

famousDead: Midwife of elephants who delivered Moon-Pearl in 1046.
FX30-008.secret: Gajapal herd-boys feed the pale cow hidden near Nagita, and Girish knows she is not of the white line.
hooks: A stranger asks a herd-boy what the hidden cow eats.
Girish wants to tell the High Priest the truth.

FX30-009.name: House Nadikar
FX30-009.title: Knight of the Chanpur Ferries
FX30-009.arms: a silver river fish leaping, on blue and green split
FX30-009.power: The ferries and three river gates of Ranpur, with a pice on every boat that passes them.
FX30-009.history: After the cyclone of 812 washed away the Chanpur bridges, Raja Tej II Sagar gave the ferries of the capital to his boatman Kavi Nadikar and knighted him. The house has taken a pice on every boat at three river gates since. The Kotwal captains of the Red Walls say the gates are theirs to shut, and the two families have quarrelled over keys for a century. In 1102 the knight's daughter ran off with an Amber sailor, and the house paid 50 lotus to keep it from the court. Every Elephant Day the Nadikar ferry the sacred river fish to the Great Tank in silver bowls.
FX30-009.reputation: Rich in pice and small in honor; the river folk like them.

members.role: Head of the house; Knight of the Chanpur Ferries
members.note: Knows every boatman on the Chanpur by name and what each one smuggles.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Lives on an Amber spice ship as a sailor's wife and writes home once a year.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Broke a Kotwal sergeant's arm over a gate key and is proud of it.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Feeds the Mud Ward in flood season from the ferry money.

famousDead: Ferried the court across the flooded Chanpur in 812 and was knighted for it.
FX30-009.secret: Neela Nadikar's husband sails for the Amber Grand Vizier and she passes him Ranpur's galley news.
hooks: The Kotwal seize a river gate during a flood.
Neela comes home pregnant on an Amber ship.

FX30-010.name: House Ganjwala
FX30-010.title: Lord of the Sugar Mills
FX30-010.arms: a brown mill-wheel on white, a gold border
FX30-010.power: Eleven cane mills and boiling houses in the Ekapur hills and the contract to supply sugar to the Steel Guard and the Elephant Corps.
FX30-010.history: The Ganjwala were sugar boilers of Ekapur who grew rich when the Nagora road began to carry sugar north. In 1079 Raja Devraj made old Hari Ganjwala a Lord for feeding the road laborers for two years at cost, and the old rice lords have never stopped sneering. The house supplies the sugar ration of the Steel Guard and the sugar cakes the elephants are trained with, including those of the White Stable. Lord Sunil's son married a Tirwala daughter in 1100, and the two houses now vote together in everything. Their mills run on debtors bought out of temple fields, which the temples call theft.
FX30-010.reputation: New money with sticky hands; useful to everyone and loved by no one.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Sugar Mills
members.note: Can taste the cane and name the field it came from.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Married a Tirwala to buy respect and found only a louder wife.

members.role: Kavi's wife, born Tirwala
members.note: Calls her husband's family 'the boilers' and runs their household better than they ever did.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Teaches debtors' children to count in the mill yards.

famousDead: Fed 12,000 road laborers at cost and was made Lord in 1079.
FX30-010.secret: The sugar cakes used to train the pale cow near Nagita came from Ganjwala mills, ordered by Keeper Anand's man in 1101.
hooks: A temple court rules that the house's bought debtors must go back to the fields.
A mill clerk remembers a strange sugar order for Nagita.

FX30-011.name: House Sodhi
FX30-011.title: Captain of the Steel Guard
FX30-011.arms: a silver curved blade point up, on red

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Steel Guard
military.unit: the Steel Guard, 1,000 heavy foot with Chanari blades
military.ties: A Sodhi has stood behind every Ranavir raja's chair since Raja Devraj raised the Guard with Chanari steel in 1046.

FX30-011.power: The captaincy of the 1,000 blades of the Steel Guard and a house inside the palace courts.
FX30-011.history: Raja Devraj raised the Steel Guard in 1046 with blades bought from Warden Kamala Varma, and gave its captaincy to Arun Sodhi, a hill soldier who had tasted his father's cup for twenty years. Sodhi captains have stood behind the Raja's chair ever since, and every Sodhi son is trained at the Blade Hall of Chanari. Captain Veer Sodhi held the palace gate during the riots of 1104. Now Kavi Rane, Master of the Blade Hall, has promised the Steel Guard to Lord Kiran, and Veer's own son trains under Rane. If the succession breaks, the house must choose between the chair and the man in it.
FX30-011.reputation: Grim, loyal and very hard to bribe; the court fears them more than the army.

members.role: Head of the house; Captain of the Steel Guard
members.note: Tastes the Raja's water himself when the tasters are not watching.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Steel Guard, pupil of the Blade Hall
members.note: Worships Kavi Rane, who tells him the Guard serves the blood, not the boy.

members.role: Veer's wife
members.note: Sits with the palace women and hears what the Raja's nurse says when she is drunk.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Wants to be a priest and dares not say so.

famousDead: First Captain of the Steel Guard; tasted Raja Vikram's cup for twenty years and lived.
FX30-011.secret: Veer's son has sworn privately to Kavi Rane that he will follow the blood if the Raja's son is proved unfit.
hooks: Divya hears that Prince Vikram failed his test.
Kiran's men offer Sanjay the captaincy now.

FX30-012.name: the Mahavat family
FX30-012.title: Herd-Leader of the Elephant Corps
FX30-012.arms: a bronze elephant bell on green

military.office: Hereditary Herd-Leaders of the Elephant Corps
military.unit: three herds, 30 tusks and about 480 men
military.ties: Mahavat drivers have ridden the Raja's war elephants since Aditya the Hill-Taker, and six of the 40 drivers flogged after Tiravi were theirs.

FX30-012.power: Thirty war elephants that will obey no other driver, and the training secrets of the Elephant School of Nagita.
FX30-012.history: The Mahavat came down from the hills with Bala Mallik's 40 elephants in 338 and have driven the Raja's war elephants ever since. A Mahavat boy is put on an elephant's neck at five and given his own calf at ten, and the beast and the man grow old together. At Tiravi in April 1083 they led the second wave into the staked pits against Bala Mallik's advice and their own, because Prince Indrajit ordered it. Afterwards the prince had 40 drivers flogged, six of them Mahavat, and old Govind still carries the scars. Since 1086 they have helped Bala Mallik retrain the herds to noise, fire and hidden ground.
FX30-012.reputation: The best drivers alive, and the Raja's most quietly bitter servants.

members.role: Head of the family; herd-leader of the first herd
members.note: Was flogged before his own elephant after Tiravi; the beast wept, and so did he.

members.role: Heir; herd-leader of the second herd
members.note: Rode a howdah elephant out of a pit at Tiravi and has trained pit-probers ever since.

members.role: Ravi's wife; keeper of the herd's medicines
members.note: Can stop an elephant's bleeding with salt, ash and a song.

members.role: Boy driver
members.note: Rode his own calf in the Elephant Day parade at eleven.

famousDead: Drove the lead elephant of the second wave at Tiravi; crushed when it fell into a staked pit.
FX30-012.secret: Govind Mahavat has sworn that his herds will stand still if the Raja ever orders them to charge again on his own whim.
hooks: The Raja orders the elephants into a narrow valley.
A Spice Coast buyer asks about the 30 elephants sold in 1103.

FX30-013.name: the Khandari family
FX30-013.title: Gallery-Master of the Miners of Tirpur
FX30-013.arms: a black mining hammer on yellow

military.office: Gallery-Masters of the Miners of Tirpur
military.unit: two companies of the Miners of Tirpur, about 300 sappers
military.ties: Khandari miners brought down a tower of the Dwarf's Gate in 1084 and now keep the listening galleries under the Nagora Gate.

FX30-013.power: Command of two mining companies and the maps of every gallery dug under the Nagora Gate since 1084.
FX30-013.history: The Khandari dug yellow stone in the Devesh mines for the Ranavir for three generations, men who could work arsenic ore and live. When the Nagora War began in 1082, Prince Indrajit took them to Tirpur to dig. In August 1084, after three races against dwarven counter-mines, Khandari sappers fired the props under a tower of the Dwarf's Gate and brought it down. The Treaty of Tirpur followed, and the family was raised to gentry. Since then they have kept the listening galleries under the Gate for Bhola the Mole. In 1103 old Mohan Khandari heard tapping deep under the Gate, and a Nagar clerk told him to forget it.
FX30-013.reputation: Yellow-stained, deaf in one ear and fearless underground.

members.role: Head of the family; gallery-master
members.note: Heard dwarven picks under the Gate in 1103 and was told to keep it to himself.

members.role: Heir; captain of a mining company
members.note: Fired the props under the Dwarf's Gate tower and was dug out alive two days later.

members.role: Gallery-mapper
members.note: Keeps the gallery maps on cotton in her own hand and has found three passages that are not on them.

members.role: Boy sapper
members.note: Crawls where grown men cannot and has dared his friends to go past the old dwarf seal.

famousDead: Died in the second counter-mine race under the Dwarf's Gate.
FX30-013.secret: The Khandari have found signs of three dwarven galleries still running under the Nagora Gate, and the Warden's clerk buried the report.
hooks: Sunita's maps show a passage that runs toward Stonehold.
The tapping under the Gate starts again in March.

FX30-014.name: House Senapat
FX30-014.title: Bearer of the Lotus Banner
FX30-014.arms: a white lotus on deep pink

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of the Lotus Banner and captains of the Lotus Bows of the capital
military.unit: the Lotus Bows of Ranpur, 5,000 royal archers
military.ties: A Senapat has carried the Raja's Lotus Banner into every battle for 500 years and commands the archers who guard it.

FX30-014.power: The Lotus Banner itself, the command of 5,000 royal archers at Ranpur, and the respect of every soldier who has fought under it.
FX30-014.history: Raja Jaidev Sagar gave the Lotus Banner to the archer Deepak Senapat in 590, and his sons have carried it for three dynasties. In March 998 Ganesh Senapat lowered it to Devendra Ranavir in the palace courtyard, and the Sagar guard laid down their arms; the new house has trusted the Senapat since. At Tiravi in 1083 the banner stood while the elephants broke around it, and Lord Bhanu Tirwala's Shields left the field behind it, which the Senapat have never forgotten. Old Hemant Senapat carried it at Tiravi; his son carries it now. The family keeps the banner's 500-year-old silk in a cedar box and flies a copy.
FX30-014.reputation: Proud as the banner and twice as stiff; the army loves them.

members.role: Head of the house; Bearer of the Lotus Banner
members.note: Took the banner from his wounded father at Tiravi and walked it backward out of the rout.

members.role: Old bearer
members.note: Lost an eye at Tiravi and still calls Lord Tirwala a deserter in public.

members.role: Daughter; archer
members.note: Outshoots her brothers and wants to carry the banner herself one day.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Would rather play the conch than carry anything.

famousDead: Lowered the Lotus Banner to Devendra Ranavir in 998 and ended the Sagar guard's resistance.
FX30-014.secret: The banner the Senapat carried at Tiravi was the copy; the real silk was lost in the river in 1083 and the cedar box is empty.
hooks: The Raja wants the true banner shown on Elephant Day.
Anjali challenges her brother for the right to carry it.

FX30-015.name: the Kotwal family
FX30-015.title: Keeper of the Six Gates
FX30-015.arms: a red gate with a black portcullis, on red-brown
FX30-015.words: Open at six, shut at nine.

military.office: Keepers of the Six Gates of the Red Walls
military.unit: the gate companies of the Red Walls, about 1,200 of the 4,000-man garrison
military.ties: Kotwal captains have held the keys of the Red Walls since the last brick was laid in 118 and serve as the royal watch of the city.

FX30-015.power: The keys and companies of the six gates of Ranpur, and the royal watch of every street outside the Temple City.
FX30-015.history: When Vijay Mitra finished the Red Walls in 118, he gave the keys to the overseer of the debt-laborers who built them, and the Kotwal have kept the six gates since. They are the royal watch of the city everywhere but the Temple City, where the temple guards rule, and each side refuses the other's arrests. When temple guards dragged Meera Jalan from the Great Temple steps in 1104, Kotwal men stood by and let 3,000 people follow her home. The Nadikar knights claim the three river gates as theirs, and the quarrel over keys is a hundred years old. The family's men are poorly paid and well bribed.
FX30-015.reputation: Hard men on the gates; the Mud Ward hates them and the merchants pay them.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Six Gates
members.note: Let the temple guards fail in 1104 because they never return his prisoners.

members.role: Heir; captain of the North Gate
members.note: Refuses bribes, which makes the other gate captains nervous.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Walks behind Meera Jalan every god-day with a knife under her shawl.

members.role: Brother; captain of the River Gate
members.note: Lets the Lotus Knives' boats through after nine for a share of the gold leaf.

famousDead: Overseer of the Red Walls' debt-laborers and first Keeper of the Six Gates.
FX30-015.secret: Amar Kotwal opens the River Gate at night for the Lotus Knives and takes a share of the stolen temple gold.
hooks: Temple guards demand a Kotwal prisoner.
Sarita is arrested at a One Face meeting by her own brother.

FX30-016.name: the Purohan family
FX30-016.title: Hymn-Keeper of the White Stable
FX30-016.arms: a gold key on indigo, under a white rain cloud
FX30-016.power: Two temple estates near Ranpur, a share in the temple banks, and the right to sing the hymn of the white elephant at every crowning.
FX30-016.history: The Purohan were one of the seven temple families that crowned Arun Mitra in the Sleeper's Dim, and they wrote down the hymn of the white elephant beside the Bhaskar in 5 BR. Their singers have chanted it at every crowning since, including the words that frighten the city: when the white elephant dies without a calf, the dream will end. In 1101 Head-Singer Jayant Purohan was one of the three temple heads who joined Keeper Anand to buy a pale cow at Amberport. The family's bank put up a third of the price. His granddaughter, who keeps the family ledgers, found the entry in 1104 and has not slept since.
FX30-016.reputation: Holy, rich and very old; they sing beautifully and lend at 12%.

members.role: Head of the family; Hymn-Keeper of the White Stable
members.note: Believes the false calf will save the faith, and that anyone who says otherwise wants it to die.

members.role: Granddaughter; keeper of the ledgers
members.note: Found the entry 'one pale cow, Amberport, 1,400 lotus' in her grandfather's hand.

members.role: Heir; singer of the Great Temple
members.note: Sings the prophecy hymn and privately thinks the gods do not need help.

members.role: Hari's wife
members.note: Wants her son made High Priest after Govind and counts every vote among the temple families.

famousDead: Wrote down the hymn of the white elephant in 5 BR.
FX30-016.secret: The Purohan bank paid a third of the 1,400 lotus for the pale cow bought at Amberport in 1101.
hooks: Leela must choose between her grandfather and the truth.
Moon-Pearl falls sick on Elephant Day.

FX30-017.name: the Tirathi family
FX30-017.title: Keeper of the Pilgrims' Shrine
FX30-017.arms: a silver star over a white road, on saffron
FX30-017.words: Every road ends at the gods.
FX30-017.power: The Pilgrims' Shrine and rest-house at the foot of the Nagora road, its offerings, and a temple bank counting room that lends to caravans.
FX30-017.history: When Raja Devraj opened the Nagora cart road in 1081, he called it a road for pilgrims bound for the Roof, and the temple banks that paid for it built a shrine at its foot. A junior branch of a Ranpur temple family took it, renamed itself Tirathi, and has kept it since. Pilgrims are few; caravan masters, spies and salt traders from Skyhold are many, and all of them pay for lodging and blessings. The Tirathi lend to caravans at 12% and hear everything said in the rest-house courtyard. They have sold news to the temples, to the Warden, and once to a dwarf.
FX30-017.reputation: Kindly hosts who listen too well.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Pilgrims' Shrine
members.note: Blesses caravans for a lotus and listens to their drivers for free.

members.role: Daughter; mistress of the rest-house
members.note: Keeps a book of every guest's name, cargo and loose talk.

members.role: Heir; temple-bank clerk
members.note: Has lent the Warden's clerks money against their share of the toll book.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: Sings for the pilgrims and believes every word of the hymns.

FX30-017.secret: In 1103 Girish Tirathi sold a dwarf traveller a description of the road forts' garrisons for 40 hold-marks.
hooks: The Amberport toll farmer lodges at the shrine on his way to Tirpur.
Meera's guest book is stolen.

FX30-018.name: the Kumhar family
FX30-018.title: Master of the Crucible Kilns
FX30-018.arms: a grey anvil within a red clay ring, on ochre
FX30-018.power: The secret clay mixture of the sealed crucibles in which Chanari steel is made, and the kilns inside the Smiths' Wall.
FX30-018.history: When the twelve Chanari smiths learned crucible steel from the Emberhand dwarves in about 950, they learned that the steel is only as good as the sealed clay pot it is melted in. A potter named Hari Kumhar learned the clay with them, and his sons have made every crucible in Chanari since. The Varma tally counts blades; it does not count pots, and the Kumhar have always been sworn to the Steel-Warden without being of the smiths. Half the secret is in their clay, and they know it. In 1102 the master's younger son went to work for Ravi Lohar's Steel-Smiths, and crucibles that look very like Kumhar work have turned up in a hidden mill above the town.
FX30-018.reputation: Clay-handed, closed-mouthed craftsmen whom the smiths treat as servants.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Crucible Kilns
members.note: Can tell a cracked crucible by the sound it makes on a fingernail.

members.role: Wife; mixer of the clay
members.note: Knows the whole clay mixture; her husband only thinks he does.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Works for the Steel-Smiths' guild and swears he never took the clay with him.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Has not spoken to his brother in two years.

famousDead: Learned the crucible clay from the Emberhand smiths with the first twelve.
FX30-018.secret: Bhavna Kumhar taught her younger son the full clay mixture before he left, and he sold it to the Steel-Smiths.
hooks: The Steel-Warden asks whose crucibles are in the hidden mill.
Stonehold's Carvers want a Kumhar crucible as proof.

FX30-019.name: the Tantri family
FX30-019.title: Master of the Indigo Vats of Madora
FX30-019.arms: a chequy of indigo and white
FX30-019.power: Forty indigo vats and two hundred looms in Madora, and the dyers' and weavers' guild of the town.
FX30-019.history: The Tantri have woven and dyed Madora cotton since the Sagar rajas sent it to Kesh by sea. Their checked indigo cloth is known in every port of the Eastern Gulf, and the Cotton Brokers of Ranpur sell it. In the cyclone of 1071 their vats flooded and the town ran blue for a week. The family borrowed from a temple bank to rebuild, and a temple court took two of their looms for debt in 1098, the same year Amar Sethi began to preach the One Face. Since then the Tantri have been the One Face's loudest voice in Madora, and their weavers sing its songs at the looms.
FX30-019.reputation: Blue-handed, loud and pious in the new way; the temples call them heretics.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Indigo Vats
members.note: Preaches the One Face from the dye-yard wall with blue arms raised.

members.role: Wife; mistress of the looms
members.note: Runs 200 looms and wishes her husband would preach less loudly.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Carries messages for Dev the Unbound's debtor band.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Secretly betrothed to a temple guard's son.

famousDead: Drowned saving the vat-masters' children in the flood of 1071.
FX30-019.secret: Ravi Tantri carries messages between Amar Sethi's factor and Dev the Unbound's band.
hooks: A temple court summons Kavi for heresy.
Yamini's betrothed is ordered to arrest her father.

FX30-020.name: the Patwar family
FX30-020.title: Keeper of the Rice Rolls of Ekapur
FX30-020.arms: a gold rice sheaf on brown, a white palm leaf beneath
FX30-020.power: The rolls of the Raja's sixth for the Ekapur and Madora hills, and the say over which field is called good and which bad.
FX30-020.history: Raja Tej I Sagar made the Patwar keepers of the rice rolls of Ekapur in 640, and they have measured every field and written down the Raja's sixth since. Chief Minister Sanjay Dhar depends on their rolls to pay the Hold Bank and the temple banks on time. The rolls are copied on palm leaf and kept in a brick vault in Ekapur, and the Patwar are the only ones who can read their old shorthand. Since 1100 the head of the family has called the best Tirwala fields 'flood-poor' and halved their tax, in return for a share of the saved rice.
FX30-020.reputation: Dull clerks with power over every rice field in the hills.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Rice Rolls
members.note: Writes 'flood-poor' beside Tirwala fields that have not flooded in fifty years.

members.role: Daughter; copyist of the rolls
members.note: Copies the old rolls into the new and has seen the numbers change.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Owes a Ranpur dice house 120 lotus.

FX30-020.secret: Since 1100 the Patwar have halved the tax on Tirwala fields for a share of the saved rice, robbing the crown of about 2,000 lotus a year.
hooks: The Chief Minister orders a recount of the Ekapur rolls.
Sameer's creditors offer to forget his debt for a copy of the rolls.

FX30-021.name: the Vaidya family
FX30-021.title: Physician of the Lamps
FX30-021.arms: a green serpent coiled round a gold cup, on white
FX30-021.power: The palace dispensary, the tasters' roster, and the duty of measuring the Ranavir children's arsenic cups at every Festival of Lamps.
FX30-021.history: When Raja Vikram made the arsenic test the law of his house in 1003, he needed a physician to measure the cups, and he chose Mohan Vaidya, who had saved him with milk and charcoal after the feast of 1001. The Vaidya have measured every Ranavir child's dose since and written the results in a book only the Raja may read. They also keep the tasters' roster and treat the palace with poppy, willow bark and silence. In October 1102 Physician Ila Vaidya saw Prince Vikram sicken at his cup, and the nurse Tara Moti swore it was a fever. Ila wrote 'fever' in the book, and has regretted it every day since.
FX30-021.reputation: Discreet, learned and close to the throne; nobody eats with them for fun.

members.role: Head of the family; Physician of the Lamps
members.note: Wrote 'fever' beside Prince Vikram's name in 1102 and knows it was arsenic.

members.role: Heir; taster-master
members.note: Has tasted three poisoned dishes and lived because he spat each time.

members.role: Daughter; apothecary
members.note: Weighs the arsenic for this year's cups and has noticed the nurse watching her scales.

members.role: Old physician; Ila's father-in-law
members.note: Paid the tasters of 1015 and 1026 himself, and laughs when people call Raja Vikram blessed.

famousDead: Saved Vikram after the poisoned feast of 1001 and measured the first arsenic cups.
FX30-021.secret: Ila Vaidya knows Prince Vikram failed his arsenic test in 1102 and wrote 'fever' in the Raja's book.
hooks: The nurse Tara Moti asks Chandra to weigh this year's cup lighter.
Lord Kiran's men ask to see the Raja's book.

FX30-022.name: the Navik family
FX30-022.title: Galley-Captain of Ranpur Light
FX30-022.arms: a white galley with a red sail, on sea blue
FX30-022.words: Out at Opening, home before the rains.

military.office: Hereditary galley captains of the Monsoon Coast fleet
military.unit: three war galleys and 180 Fleet Marines
military.ties: Navik captains have commanded Raja's galleys since Mahendra II built the first 40, and serve under Admiral Jaiwant Sagar.

FX30-022.power: Three war galleys in the Raja's fleet and two armed cotton ships of their own sailing to Kesh and Amberport.
FX30-022.history: The Navik were among the first captains of the 40 galleys Mahendra II Sagar built in 706, and they have commanded Raja's galleys ever since. They fought the Amber harbor chiefs for the cotton ships in the 8th and 10th centuries and pirates every dry season. Since 1085 Amber ships have undercut Ranpur's cotton freight and the family's merchant ships lose money each year. Captain Hema Navik lost her husband and a galley in the cyclone of 1071 and has captained in his place since. The house laughs at the Amber secret needle and drowns too often for it.
FX30-022.reputation: Tough sea people who hate the Amber Isles more than any family in Ranpur.

members.role: Head of the family; galley captain
members.note: Took her drowned husband's galley out the week after the cyclone and has never laid it up early since.

members.role: Heir; captain of an armed cotton ship
members.note: Has bribed an Amber pilot's boy to describe the needle bowl.

members.role: Daughter; marine archer
members.note: Shot a pirate chief through the throat at 200 paces in 1103.

members.role: Ship's boy
members.note: Wants to sail past the Amber Isles to the Isle of Pearls.

famousDead: Hema's husband; lost with his galley in the cyclone of 1071.
FX30-022.secret: Vinod Navik has paid for a description of the Amber pilots' needle and means to build one.
hooks: An Amber pilot's boy is found drowned with Navik silver on him.
The Amber fleet sails for the Isle of Pearls in April.

FX30-023.name: the Kalapani family
FX30-023.title: Lord of the Black Water (river-mouth name)
FX30-023.arms: a white skull on a black oar blade (a mark painted on their boats)
FX30-023.power: Twelve fast reed-boats, about 80 knives, and hiding places in the mangroves of the Madora delta mouths.
FX30-023.history: The Kalapani were fishers of the Madora mouths until a temple court bound the family to the fields for debt in 1012. They took their boats into the mangroves instead and have lived off cotton barges ever since. Each dry season they strike barges at night, strip them and sell the cotton and pepper to Keshi and Amber captains waiting off the coast. The Jaldhar wardens hang a few of them every year, and every year the chain somehow drops when the big boats come through. Their head, an old woman called Mother Jaya, has never been caught.
FX30-023.reputation: Mangrove ghosts; the river folk fear and feed them.

members.role: Head of the clan; called Mother Jaya
members.note: Has run the black water for 30 years and keeps the Jaldhar chain-master on a silver lead.

members.role: Son; captain of the boats
members.note: Swims under barges at night and cuts their anchor ropes with his teeth, they say.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: Wants to leave the river and marry a fisher who knows nothing.

members.role: Son; fence in Madora market
members.note: Sells stolen pepper to Keshi factors in a respectable shop.

famousDead: Took the family into the mangroves rather than work the temple fields.
FX30-023.secret: The clan buys its way past the Madora chain from the warden's own brother and carries Lady Mandapi's nephew's pepper to the Keshi.
hooks: A barge the Kalapani strip carries temple gold.
Neela wants out, and her grandmother does not let anyone out.

FX30-024.name: the Chakor family
FX30-024.title: Master of the Lotus Knives
FX30-024.arms: a gold hand holding a small knife (the Lotus Knives' sign scratched on robbed shrines)
FX30-024.words: The gods do not count their gold.
FX30-024.power: About 40 temple-thieves of the Lotus Knives, a goldsmith's back room in the Cotton Bazaar, and a gate captain who looks away.
FX30-024.history: The Chakor lost everything in the cyclone of 1071 and were bound to temple fields for the price of a new hut. Their eldest son, Kunal, ran away to the Mud Ward and found that the gold leaf on small shrines comes off with a thumbnail. The band he built, the Lotus Knives, strips gold leaf and offerings from shrines across the delta and sells the gold through a Cotton Bazaar goldsmith. They never rob the Great Temple and never hurt a priest, and the poor think them half holy. Kunal's sister runs the melting room; his son wants to rob the White Stable.
FX30-024.reputation: Gutter heroes to the debtors and devils to the temples.

members.role: Head of the band; Master of the Lotus Knives
members.note: Has stripped 300 shrines and never taken a pice from a beggar's bowl.

members.role: Sister; mistress of the melting room
members.note: Melts gold leaf into plain beads and knows which goldsmith cheats.

members.role: Son
members.note: Wants to steal the gold bells of the White Stable and become a legend.

members.role: Daughter; lookout
members.note: Sells flowers on the Temple City steps and counts the guards.

FX30-024.secret: The River Gate captain Amar Kotwal takes a share of every night's gold, and the band could hang him whenever it likes.
hooks: Arun plans a night raid on the White Stable.
A shrine the Knives robbed belonged to Keeper Anand's own family.

FX30-025.name: the Hundiwal family
FX30-025.title: Bill-Broker of the River Steps
FX30-025.arms: three silver bars on dark green
FX30-025.power: A counting house on the River Steps that writes bills of exchange to Amberport, Kesh and Tharmund, and carries the crown's payments to the Hold Bank.
FX30-025.history: After Ranpuri brokers lost about 90,000 lotus in Tessarian bills in the Debt War, the Hundiwal set up a counting house in 1048 that trusted no king's paper and wrote its own bills, backed by silver in its vault. Chief Minister Sanjay Dhar uses them to carry the crown's yearly payment to the Hold Bank of Stonehold. In November 1104 they wrote the bills by which Amberport merchants paid 60,000 lotus for three years of the Nagora tolls. In 1103 they also carried Lord Kiran Ranavir's 30,000-lotus Hold Bank loan, though they wrote it in a dead cousin's name. Two secrets that could each shake the throne pass through one family's ledger.
FX30-025.reputation: Quiet, rich and trusted by everyone who has anything to hide.

members.role: Head of the family; Bill-Broker of the River Steps
members.note: Wrote Lord Kiran's Hold Bank loan in a dead cousin's name and keeps the true copy in his sandal box.

members.role: Daughter; factor at Amberport
members.note: Married into a Well-faith broker house of Amberport and thinks Ranpur is finished.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Wants to stop carrying secrets and fears his father's ledger more than any army.

members.role: Granddaughter
members.note: Can already count lotus faster than her tutor.

famousDead: Founded the counting house after the Debt War and wrote the first silver-backed bill in Ranpur.
FX30-025.secret: The Hundiwal carried Lord Kiran's 30,000-lotus Hold Bank loan under a false name.
hooks: The Chief Minister asks who really borrowed in 1103.
An Amberport toll farmer's bills bounce at the River Steps.

FX30-026.name: the Baghmar family
FX30-026.title: Chief Beater of Chanari
FX30-026.arms: a black bow over a gold tiger stripe, on orange

military.office: Chief Beaters of the Forest Beaters at Chanari
military.unit: the Chanari company of Forest Beaters, 400 scouts with drums and bows
military.ties: Baghmar drummers turned the tiger beat into army drill and lead the Forest Beaters who sweep for pits since 1083.

FX30-026.power: The tiger drives of the Chanari hills, a royal bounty on man-eaters, and 400 Forest Beaters who answer to their drum.
FX30-026.history: The Baghmar have hunted tigers in the Chanari hills for five centuries and drove the beats for every Raja who wanted a skin. Their drums and gongs became army drill when the Forest Beaters were raised, and since Tiravi in 1083 their scouts walk ahead of the elephants with long poles to find pits. In 1098 old Kalu Baghmar beat the drive that brought the Striped Death to the Raja's elephant, and the Raja shot it. The Purkar say their huntsman hit it first; the Baghmar say nobody hit it but the Raja, because that is what a beater says. Kalu's grandson has his eye on the Raja's bounty for a new man-eater on the Nagora road.
FX30-026.reputation: Brave, scarred hill hunters whom every village wants and pays late.

members.role: Head of the family; Chief Beater of Chanari
members.note: Drove the Striped Death to the Raja in 1098 and swears the Raja's arrow was the only one.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Chanari Forest Beaters
members.note: Lost two fingers to a tiger and taught the pit-probe drill to the army.

members.role: Yash's wife; drum-mistress
members.note: Her drum can tell a whole valley of beaters where to turn.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Wants to kill the new man-eater on the Nagora road alone and take the bounty.

famousDead: Killed eleven man-eaters in the Chanari hills.
FX30-026.secret: Kalu's own arrow hit the Striped Death first, and he let the Raja take the glory for a lifetime pension.
hooks: A man-eater stalks the Nagora road forts.
Lord Purkar wants Kalu to swear whose arrow struck first.

FX31-001.name: House Ardisi
FX31-001.title: Lord of the Dry Hills
FX31-001.arms: a black bull on copper red, a gold border

military.office: Lords of the southern lords' horse
military.unit: the Ardisi lances, 90 heavy horse of the southern lords' 1,600
military.ties: Ardisi lances have ridden behind Asterio banners since Albina in 711 and fought for Queen Livia in every battle of the civil war.

FX31-001.power: Dry-hill grazing and copper-cart rights south of Tessar, about 90 Temple-faith lances, and a voice in the queen's war council.
FX31-001.history: The first Ardisi was a centurion who went over to Leo Tessaran with Captain Justin Asterio at Albina in 711, and Leo gave him the dry hills south of Tessar in 712. The house has ridden behind the Asterio ever since and stayed with the Temple when the north went over to the Dawn. Ardisi lances charged at Vitella in 1068 and Felina in 1096, and at Coreria in October 1104 Lord Valerio Ardisi's heir died under the prince's Dawn Lances. The old lord's younger son is now heir and wants peace at any price. The house's grain steward has found a buyer who pays in Ostran suns, not the queen's Leontines: the prince's camp at Coreria.
FX31-001.reputation: The queen's oldest friends in the south; brave, bled white, and tired.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Dry Hills
members.note: Has buried two sons in the queen's war and will not bury a third without asking why.

members.role: Heir since Coreria
members.note: Writes in secret to the queen's envoy at Ostra urging partition.

members.role: Widow of the heir who died at Coreria
members.note: Wants the Dawn Lance who killed her husband found and does not care who pays.

members.role: Grain steward; Valerio's cousin
members.note: Sells Ardisi grain to the prince's quartermasters through a Feleria merchant for good silver.

famousDead: Heir of the house; killed by the Dawn Lances at Coreria.
FX31-001.secret: The Ardisi grain steward sells the house's wheat to Prince Andros's camp at Coreria through the Ramello merchants.
hooks: Sabina learns which Dawn Lance killed her husband.
The queen's quartermaster finds Ardisi sacks at Coreria.

FX31-002.name: House Rosiano
FX31-002.title: Lord of Rosia
FX31-002.arms: a red rose on gold, a green branch beneath

military.office: Lords of the Rosia forward post
military.unit: the Rosia levy, 150 spears, and the hired Tirana Free Company quartered on them
military.ties: Rosia is the queen's forward post in the Coreria woods, and the Rosiano feed 1,800 hired men who have not been paid since October.

FX31-002.power: The manor and woods of Rosia on the road to Coreria, now the queen's forward post.
FX31-002.history: Emperor Leontius I gave the Rosia woods to a road captain named Ugo Rosiano in 948 for clearing bandits off the Neck road. The family's manor now stands at the edge of the war. Since the Battle of Coreria in October 1104 the queen's Tirana Free Company of 1,800 men has wintered at Rosia, eating the house's grain, cutting its woods and owing it everything. The Dawn camp at Coreria is two days' march away. Lady Flavia Rosiano writes weekly to the queen asking for the company's pay; the company's captain writes weekly asking for more.
FX31-002.reputation: A small house that the war has turned into a front line.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of Rosia
members.note: Feeds 1,800 unpaid soldiers and keeps them from burning her village with sharp words and sweet wine.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Rosia levy
members.note: Scouts the Coreria woods by night and has seen the prince's raiders pass.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Has caught the eye of the Free Company's captain, which worries her mother more than the war.

members.role: Old lord; Flavia's father-in-law
members.note: Fought at Vitella and would rather burn Rosia himself than give it to the Dawn.

famousDead: Road captain who cleared the Coreria woods of bandits and was given Rosia.
FX31-002.secret: If the queen's pay does not come by the quarter day, the Free Company's captain has promised Rosia's granary to his men and Ornella to himself.
hooks: The quarter day of 20 March passes without pay.
Remo finds Prince Nikos's raiders camped in the Rosia woods.

FX31-003.name: House Cedrano
FX31-003.title: Knight of the Queen's Household
FX31-003.arms: a silver sword point down between two cedar cones, on green

military.office: Knights of the Queen's Six-Fingers
military.unit: two lances of the Queen's Six-Fingers
military.ties: Cedrano knights have guarded the royal household since Empress Callista and now serve in the Six-Fingers under Dame Helena Tessaran.

FX31-003.power: A knight's house on Crown Hill, two places in the Queen's Six-Fingers, and the queen's gratitude.
FX31-003.history: The Cedrano came to Tessar in 1021 in the household of Empress Callista Asterio and were knighted for guarding her through the Debt War riots. At Vitella in 1068 Sir Bastian Cedrano rode beside Marcus Corvane into the red dawn banners, mistaking them for the queen's gold as the prince-consort did, and died with him. His grandson Sir Ilario now serves in the Queen's Six-Fingers under Dame Helena Tessaran. In 1104 Ilario caught Dame Helena when she fainted on the palace stair, and she made him swear to say nothing. He has kept his word.
FX31-003.reputation: A gallant household family; the queen's tears for Vitella keep them in favor.

members.role: Head of the house; knight of the Six-Fingers
members.note: Caught Dame Helena when she fainted on the stair and swore to tell no one.

members.role: Grandmother; widow of the knight killed at Vitella
members.note: Still wears Bastian's ring and says the prince-consort was blind in more than colors.

members.role: Sister; lady-in-waiting
members.note: Hears palace gossip and knows the queen has written to Prince Nikos.

members.role: Brother; page
members.note: Dreams of the Six-Fingers and practises with a broom.

famousDead: Rode with Marcus Corvane into the Dawn banners at Vitella and died with him.
FX31-003.secret: Sir Ilario knows that Dame Helena Tessaran has the weak heart of the six-fingered line.
hooks: Helena faints again, in front of the war council.
Lucia overhears the name of the queen's chosen heir.

FX31-004.name: House Santicci
FX31-004.title: Lord of Santice
FX31-004.arms: a gold star over a blue stream, on white

military.office: Lords of the Santice forward post
military.unit: the Santice levy, 100 spears, and the Abaran Spears quartered on them
military.ties: Santice is the queen's second forward post toward Coreria, where Prince Tekle's 600 Abaran exiles winter in the Santicci barns.

FX31-004.power: The manor and stream-mill of Santice on the Coreria road, now a forward post of the queen's army.
FX31-004.history: King Anselm gave Santice to a loyal toll clerk named Matteo Santicci in 1048, when the shrunken kingdom paid its servants in land because it had no silver. Since the Battle of Coreria the 600 Abaran Spears of Prince Tekle Asfari have wintered in the Santicci barns. They pay for what they eat, which the Free Company at Rosia does not, and the house has grown fond of them. Lord Pello Santicci's daughter is fonder still of one of them. Prince Tekle wants his release by May Fair, and if he goes, Santice is open to the Dawn.
FX31-004.reputation: A young, poor house that likes its foreign guests too well.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Santice
members.note: Plays draughts with Prince Tekle and loses on purpose.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Has promised to go with an Abaran spear-captain when the exiles leave.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Trusts no foreigner and counts the Abaran spears every night.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Nursed thirty wounded Abarans after Coreria and learned their songs.

FX31-004.secret: Giulia Santicci has promised to leave with the Abaran exiles, and the spear-captain has promised to take Santice's horses with them.
hooks: Prince Tekle is released on May Fair and Santice is left open.
Aldo catches his sister saddling a horse at midnight.

FX31-005.name: House Vellano
FX31-005.title: Lord of the Feleria Cedars
FX31-005.arms: a green cedar on silver, a red dawn rising behind it

military.office: Lords of the Feleria garrison
military.unit: the Feleria garrison, 400 of the 700 men of Feleria and Felina
military.ties: Vellano men hold Feleria for Prince Andros and fought at Felina in 1096, where the prince held the town.

FX31-005.power: The cedar hills of Feleria once held by the Tessarans of Feleria, the cedar trade, and the hall where the Truce of the Cedars was signed.
FX31-005.history: When the last Tessaran lord of Feleria died at Calella in 1046, King Anselm gave the cedar hills to his steward Lucan Vellano, who had kept the cedar books for the six-fingered cousins for twenty years. The Vellano took the Dawn faith with the north in 1061 and have held Feleria for Prince Andros since. The Truce of the Cedars was signed in their hall on 11 November 1087. What the house hides is older: Lucan's wife was the natural daughter of the last Tessaran lord of Feleria. In 1103 a grandson was born with six working fingers on each hand, and the midwife was paid not to cut them.
FX31-005.reputation: Rich cedar lords of the Dawn north, proud of their peace-hall and close-mouthed about their blood.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Feleria Cedars
members.note: Hosted both claimants' envoys in 1087 and keeps the table they signed on under a cloth.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Feleria garrison
members.note: Fought at Felina and saw Lord Lukas Tessaran die for the queen.

members.role: Stefano's wife
members.note: Keeps her son's hands wrapped in mittens even in summer.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Born with six working fingers on each hand; the midwife was paid not to cut them.

famousDead: Steward of the Tessarans of Feleria, made lord of the cedars in 1047.
FX31-005.secret: The Vellano carry the blood of the Tessarans of Feleria, and a grandson born in 1103 has six working fingers.
hooks: A Velgradan envoy asks to see the baby's hands.
If the claimants make peace, a third six-fingered child is a claim.

FX31-006.name: House Marzolo
FX31-006.title: Lord of the Upper Vales
FX31-006.arms: a brown bear standing, on red

military.office: Bannerets of the northern lords' levies
military.unit: 400 of the northern lords' levies at the Coreria camp
military.ties: Marzolo levies have marched for Prince Andros since 1061 and dig in at Coreria this winter.

FX31-006.power: Hill farms of the upper Feleria vales, Temple estates seized in 1061, and 400 levies at Coreria.
FX31-006.history: The Marzolo were hill lords of the upper vales who took the Dawn faith with Calossa in 734 and married Eastfolk wives. In 1061 Lord Gregor Marzolo marched with Teodor Ordane to proclaim the boy Andros, and the house seized two Temple estates to pay its levies. They have fought at Vitella, Felina and Coreria since. To keep the levies fed after 1096 the house borrowed from Velgradan lenders through the Ordane, and it now owes 8,000 marks. If the partition being drafted at Ostra hands the seized estates back to the Temple, the Marzolo are ruined.
FX31-006.reputation: Tough northern fighters, deep in debt and deep in the Dawn.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Upper Vales
members.note: Proclaimed Andros king in 1061 and will hear no word of partition.

members.role: Heir; captain of the levy at Coreria
members.note: Killed a queen's knight at Coreria and wears his gold spurs.

members.role: Lady of the house, born in Velgrad
members.note: Runs the vales alone and has written to her Velgradan kin for another loan.

members.role: Daughter; Dawn novice
members.note: Teaches reading in Eastfolk at the monastery school and wants peace more than God.

FX31-006.secret: The Marzolo have pledged their seized Temple estates as security for 8,000 marks borrowed in Velgrad, which makes them worthless if returned.
hooks: News of partition talks at Ostra reaches Coreria.
A Velgradan lender arrives to inspect the pledged estates.

FX31-007.name: House Lorenzane
FX31-007.title: Knight of the Felina Road
FX31-007.arms: a bend of gold and green across black

military.office: Knights of the Felina road
military.unit: 6 lances, half with the prince and half with the queen
military.ties: The house has sons in both armies: the elder in Andros's northern horse, the younger in the queen's Calella Horse.

FX31-007.power: A knight's fief on the road between Feleria and Felina, held for Prince Andros by a family that is half the queen's.
FX31-007.history: The Lorenzane have been road knights on the Felina road since the empire was proclaimed in 930. In 1061 the house split as the kingdom did. The elder son, Sir Nerio, stayed with the Dawn and rides with the prince's northern horse. The younger, Sir Matteo, had married a southern wife and rode south to the queen; he now commands a squadron of the Calella Horse. At Felina in 1096 the brothers saw each other across the field. Their mother still lives on the fief and writes to both, and the letters cross the lines through a carter of Hektor Wain's guild.
FX31-007.reputation: A family torn in two, whom both sides suspect.

members.role: Head of the house; knight in the prince's northern horse
members.note: Saw his brother across the field at Felina and turned his horse aside.

members.role: Younger brother; captain in the queen's Calella Horse
members.note: Rides patrols toward Coreria and knows his brother's camp from his banner.

members.role: Mother; holds the fief
members.note: Sends both sons the same honey cakes and the same prayers.

members.role: Nerio's daughter
members.note: Named for the queen before the war, and teased for it in the Dawn north.

FX31-007.secret: Lady Agnese's letters carry each son's camp news to the other, and both sons know it.
hooks: The brothers are ordered to meet in battle in May.
The Vellano accuse Lady Agnese of spying for the queen.

FX31-008.name: House Galvane
FX31-008.title: Lord of the Doria Fields
FX31-008.arms: a silver key on black, a red border

military.office: Former castellans of Doria
military.unit: 120 house spears, now attached to the bought Doria garrison
military.ties: The Galvane held Doria for the queen until July 1103, when their unpaid garrison sold the town to Prince Andros.

FX31-008.power: The grain fields around Doria, a ruined name, and a garrison that took the prince's silver.
FX31-008.history: The Galvane held the fields and keys of Doria from 989 and stayed with the queen when the north rose in 1061. In July 1103 Prince Andros besieged Doria for ten weeks and took it without a breach by paying its unpaid garrison, and the garrison captain who took the money was Lord Fabio Galvane's own cousin. The prince let the house keep its fields if it swore to him, and it swore. The words of the house now make men laugh in Feleria. Lord Fabio sends the queen's spymaster news through a refugee priest and waits for the queen to come back.
FX31-008.reputation: Turncoats in the north and traitors in the south; nobody trusts them.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Doria Fields
members.note: Swore to the prince with his lips and sends the queen's spymaster word of every Dawn cart through Doria.

members.role: Cousin; captain of the bought Doria garrison
members.note: Sold Doria for the prince's silver and says fourteen months unpaid was reason enough.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: Thinks both her father and her cousin are fools and runs the fields while they scheme.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Hosts the Dawn priests and the refugee priest who carries her husband's letters.

FX31-008.secret: Lord Fabio sends the queen's spymaster news of Doria through a refugee priest, though he has sworn to Andros.
hooks: The refugee priest is taken by Dawn soldiers.
Orso is offered double to sell Doria back to the queen.

FX31-009.name: the Fennaro family
FX31-009.title: Captain of the Southern Road Stations
FX31-009.arms: a white post-wheel on green and gold

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Neck road stations
military.unit: the queen's Road Riders, 1,000 light horse on the Neck road south of Coreria
military.ties: Fennaro captains have kept the Neck road's stations since Leo the Free turned the old post houses into forts, and now lead the queen's Road Riders.

FX31-009.power: Five road-station forts south of Coreria, a copy of the Toll Book of 845, and 1,000 light horse.
FX31-009.history: The Fennaro were post-riders of the Imperial Post beside the Tessarans themselves, and when Leo the Free turned the post stations into small forts in 712 he gave them five. They have kept the Neck road ever since and can quote the Toll Book of 845 line by line. Since the toll pledge ran out in 1077 both claimants have set toll-keepers on the same road, and carters pay twice. Captain Basil Fennaro commands the queen's Road Riders south of Coreria; his cousins keep two stations for the prince to the north. Every quarter the cousins meet at a ruined station between the lines to compare tolls.
FX31-009.reputation: Road soldiers who know every carter and every bandit of the Neck.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain of the Road Riders
members.note: Can ride from Tessar to Coreria in two days and knows which station has fresh horses.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the toll books
members.note: Keeps the queen's toll book and the cousins' figures side by side.

members.role: Heir; station captain at Ostara
members.note: Chased Prince Nikos's raiders off the road in December and lost three men doing it.

members.role: Cousin; station captain for Prince Andros
members.note: Keeps two stations for the prince and shares the toll news with his southern cousins.

famousDead: Post-rider who rode with Leo the Free and was given the first five stations.
FX31-009.secret: The Fennaro cousins on both sides share their toll books every quarter, so each claimant's road income is known to the other.
hooks: A carter is made to pay three times and riots.
Prince Nikos's raiders strike the Ostara station.

FX31-010.name: House Corradi
FX31-010.title: Sergeant of the Crown Spearmen
FX31-010.arms: a black spear upright on grey stone, a white wall below

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Crown Spearmen of Tessar
military.unit: two hundreds of the Crown Spearmen, 200 spears
military.ties: A Corradi sergeant held the North Gate breach through the siege of 1064 and 1065, and the queen made the post hereditary.

FX31-010.power: Two hundreds of the Crown Spearmen and the defence of the North Gate of Tessar.
FX31-010.history: In the winter of 1064 Prince Andros's 9,000 men besieged Tessar with two siege towers, and 3,000 men held the old walls. Sergeant Aldo Corradi held the North Gate breach for nine days until Silas Vane's new engine smashed both towers on 4 June 1065. Queen Livia made his post hereditary. His son now sergeants the Crown Spearmen at the gate, and his grandson is a file-leader. The family is paid in the queen's Leontine, which nobody takes at face, and fed by the garrison kitchen, which is the only reason they stay.
FX31-010.reputation: Plain, hungry, unbreakable spearmen of the walls.

members.role: Head of the family; sergeant of the North Gate
members.note: Carried water up to his father in the breach of 1065 at seven years old.

members.role: Old sergeant
members.note: Held the North Gate breach nine days and has a bad leg and a good story.

members.role: Heir; file-leader
members.note: Has sold his spear twice to the Leontine Men for bread and bought it back.

members.role: Tullio's wife
members.note: Feeds half the gate company's children from a pot that is never full.

FX31-010.secret: Tullio has told his men they will open the North Gate to whoever feeds them if the queen's pay fails past spring.
hooks: Patriarch Bogdan's men offer bread for a gate.
Nino's spear turns up in the Refugee Field.

FX31-011.name: the Varisco family
FX31-011.title: Bearer of the Dawn Banner
FX31-011.arms: a red sun rising on white

military.office: Hereditary Bearers of the Dawn Banner of the Dawn Lances
military.unit: the banner troop of the Dawn Lances, 60 heavy horse
military.ties: A Varisco has carried the red dawn banner at the head of the Dawn Lances since Andros was crowned at Calossa in 1062.

FX31-011.power: The red dawn banner, the banner troop of the Dawn Lances, and the trust of Prince Nikos.
FX31-011.history: When the priest Kirill crowned Andros at Calossa on 25 March 1062, the boy king gave the new red dawn banner to Dmitar Varisco, a hill knight's son who had carried the first proclamation through the north. At Vitella in 1068 Dmitar's banner was the red that the color-blind Marcus Corvane took for the queen's gold; Marcus rode into it and died, and so did 1,500 of the queen's men. The banner troop rides at the head of the Dawn Lances under Prince Nikos. Dmitar's son carried it at Coreria in 1104. The family is honored in the north and hated in the south, where Vitella widows still curse the red.
FX31-011.reputation: The prince's banner family; heroes in the north, butchers in the south.

members.role: Old bearer; head of the family
members.note: Carried the banner at Vitella and swears God blinded the prince-consort that day.

members.role: Heir; Bearer of the Dawn Banner
members.note: Carried the banner through the queen's crossbow fire at Coreria and has three bolt scars to prove it.

members.role: Andrei's wife
members.note: Sews the red silk of every new banner and prays over each stitch.

members.role: Son; squire of Prince Nikos
members.note: Squires for Prince Nikos and has seen him read a letter from the queen and burn it.

FX31-011.secret: Pavel Varisco saw Prince Nikos burn a letter from Queen Livia offering him her crown.
hooks: A Vitella widow tries to burn the banner in camp.
Prince Nikos asks Pavel to carry a reply to Tessar.

FX31-012.name: the Tirabelli family
FX31-012.title: Captain of the Calossa Crossbows
FX31-012.arms: a black crossbow bolt bendwise on gold

military.office: Hereditary captains in the Calossa Crossbows
military.unit: two companies of the Calossa Crossbows, 400 crossbowmen
military.ties: Tirabelli captains have trained the northern crossbows since the border war of 957 and lead the only men Prince Andros pays in coin.

FX31-012.power: Two companies of the Calossa Crossbows, the only troops of the prince's army paid in silver, and a workshop that makes their bows.
FX31-012.history: The Tirabelli were crossbow sergeants on the northern border after Radoslav the Bear stopped Cassian Reed at Lake Ostec in 957, and they have trained the crossbows of Calossa since. They make their own bows in a Feleria workshop and teach their sons to span them at ten. Prince Andros pays the Calossa Crossbows in coin, struck at his Calossa mint, and Captain Ilaria Tirabelli has noticed that the coin is made of very good copper. She has also noticed the Albina mark on a slag cake at the mint. She has told no one, because her men are paid.
FX31-012.reputation: Hard, well-paid professionals; the rest of the northern army envies them.

members.role: Head of the family; captain of the Calossa Crossbows
members.note: Saw the Albina mark on a slag cake at the Calossa mint and decided her men's pay mattered more.

members.role: Heir; file-leader
members.note: Thinks his mother serves the prince for silver rather than God and tells her so.

members.role: Husband; bowyer
