members.note: Makes 200 crossbows a year and cannot make enough.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Spans a light bow already and wants to fight in May.

famousDead: Crossbow sergeant at Lake Ostec in 957; founded the family's company.
FX31-012.secret: Captain Ilaria knows the prince's coin is struck from Albina copper bought from the queen's own Lord Marshal.
hooks: A queen's spy asks Ilaria about the mint.
The prince's pay chest is late for the first time.

FX31-013.name: the Belcaro family
FX31-013.title: Castellan of Fort Pavella
FX31-013.arms: a gold castle on a green mount, on copper
FX31-013.words: The South Road Is Shut to Thieves

military.office: Castellans of Fort Pavella on the southern road
military.unit: the Fort Pavella garrison, 240 of the 700 men of the southern forts
military.ties: Belcaro castellans have held Fort Pavella for the Asterio lords of Albina since 889 and guard the copper road south.

FX31-013.power: Fort Pavella and its garrison on the dry road south from Albina, and a cut of the copper carts that pass it.
FX31-013.history: The Asterio lords of Albina gave Fort Pavella to their sergeant Ugo Belcaro in 889, to guard the dry road where the copper carts go. The Belcaro have held it since, through the empire, the Debt War and the civil war. Since 1101 the castellan has waved through copper carts that turn north instead of west, carried by Hektor Wain's carters on Lord Marshal Corvin Asterio's own pass. He has guessed where the copper goes. His wife's brother died at Coreria under the prince's lances, and she has not guessed yet.
FX31-013.reputation: Quiet desert castellans who see every cart and say nothing.

members.role: Head of the family; Castellan of Fort Pavella
members.note: Waves the Lord Marshal's copper carts north and has stopped asking why.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Lost her brother at Coreria and would hang anyone who helped the prince.

members.role: Heir; gate sergeant
members.note: Keeps the cart tally and has written 'north' beside forty loads.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Rides patrol on the dry road with her brother and is the better shot.

FX31-013.secret: The Fort Pavella cart tally shows forty copper loads turned north to the prince's mint on the Lord Marshal's pass.
hooks: Serena finds her son's cart tally.
A queen's auditor asks for the Pavella books.

FX31-014.name: the Morello family
FX31-014.title: Master Wright of the Engine Yard
FX31-014.arms: a black hammer over a gold counterweight, on blue
FX31-014.power: The carpenters and wrights of the Engine Yard, and half of the aiming tables of the counterweight engine.
FX31-014.history: The Morello were ship carpenters of Tessar harbor until 1063, when Master Silas Vane hired Bruno Morello to build the frame of an engine nobody had built before. On 4 June 1065 that engine threw 90 kg stones 250 metres and smashed both of Prince Andros's siege towers. Bruno's son is now Master Wright of the Engine Yard. Silas Vane is 68 and keeps the aiming tables in his head; the Morello have the frames, the timbers and, they think, half the tables. Since Coreria, Prince Andros's engineers have offered good silver for a Morello at Coreria.
FX31-014.reputation: The best wrights in the Neck; both armies want them.

members.role: Old master; builder of the first engine
members.note: Built the frame that broke the siege of 1065 and has not been thanked since.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Wright of the Engine Yard
members.note: Has worked out half of Silas Vane's aiming tables by watching where the stones fall.

members.role: Daughter; tally-keeper of the Yard
members.note: Writes down every shot the engines throw and is closer to the tables than her father.

members.role: Son
members.note: Has met the prince's engineers' agent twice in the Bent Leontine.

FX31-014.secret: Paolo Morello is selling his sister's shot tallies to Prince Andros's siege engineers.
hooks: Silas Vane falls ill and the Yard needs a new master.
Elena finds pages missing from her tally book.

FX31-015.name: the Benedane family
FX31-015.title: Canon of the Luminary's Chapter
FX31-015.arms: a white lily under a gold sun, on Temple blue
FX31-015.power: Canonries in the Luminary of Tessar's chapter, Temple lands near the city, and a voice at every Temple crowning.
FX31-015.history: The Benedane have served the Temple at Tessar since the Edict of the Two Altars in 741, and a Benedane canon has stood in the chapter at the noon crowning of every Tessarian king. In February 1061 Canon Tomas Benedane was one of the six witnesses who heard the dying King Anselm name Livia, as the Temple says. Tomas died in 1080. His son was a boy in the next room that night and has never believed his father heard anything. The royal physician's wax tablets, which say the king died without a word, are being copied at Solenne and carried east.
FX31-015.reputation: Solemn, loyal Temple folk whose word helped crown a queen.

members.role: Head of the family; Canon of the Luminary's Chapter
members.note: Was in the next room when King Anselm died and heard no voice at all.

members.role: Widow of the witness
members.note: Will swear on any altar that her husband heard the king name Livia.

members.role: Heir; Temple priest
members.note: Wants to be the next Luminary and needs the queen alive to get it.

members.role: Daughter; Temple teacher
members.note: Teaches refugee children their letters in the Refugee Field.

famousDead: One of the six witnesses of King Anselm's deathbed words.
FX31-015.secret: Canon Amadeo believes his father lied when he witnessed the king's deathbed words in 1061.
hooks: The physician's tablets reach Tessar.
Patriarch Bogdan's people ask Amadeo what he heard.

FX31-016.name: the Medrano family
FX31-016.title: Physician of Feleria
FX31-016.arms: a silver owl on a black wax tablet, on green
FX31-016.power: A physicians' house at Feleria, the trust of the northern lords, and the memory of what the royal physician wrote in 1061.
FX31-016.history: Doctor Simon Medrano was royal physician to King Anselm and sat by him on the night of his death in February 1061. On his wax tablets he wrote that the king died 'without a word or a sign'. When the Temple crowned Livia on the six witnesses' word, Simon took his family north and set up as a physician in Feleria; the tablets went to Solenne, where a friend kept them. Simon died in 1079. His daughter Doctor Lucia Medrano treats the northern lords and the wounded of Coreria. She knows a copy of her father's tablets is coming east, and that both claimants will kill for it or because of it.
FX31-016.reputation: The best physicians in the north, with a past nobody mentions.

members.role: Head of the family; Physician of Feleria
members.note: Remembers her father coming home white-faced the night the king died and burning his own notes.

members.role: Son; army surgeon at Coreria
members.note: Sawed off forty limbs after Coreria and stopped believing in either crown.

members.role: Daughter; apothecary
members.note: Has written to Solenne asking for her grandfather's tablets back.

members.role: Lucia's husband; scribe
members.note: Copies prayer books for the Dawn monasteries and fears every knock at the door.

famousDead: Royal physician who wrote that King Anselm died without a word.
FX31-016.secret: Sara Medrano has asked Solenne for the original wax tablets, and the copy now moving east was sent because of her letter.
hooks: A Temple agent arrives at Feleria asking for Doctor Medrano.
Prince Andros wants Lucia to swear to the tablets in public.

FX31-017.name: the Ramello family
FX31-017.title: Master of the Cedar Yards
FX31-017.arms: three copper bars on cedar green
FX31-017.power: Cedar yards at Feleria, copper and grain brokerage between the two halves of the realm, and partnerships with the Neck Road Carters' Guild.
FX31-017.history: The Ramello were grain merchants of Lorino until 9 October 1071, when the queen's unpaid Grey Hand sacked the town after it had surrendered and killed about 800 people, among them old Dario Ramello and two of his sons. The survivors moved to Feleria and rebuilt in cedar. They trade with both sides now: cedar south, grain north, copper wherever it pays, carried by Hektor Wain's carters, and they pay the double tolls without complaint because they price them in. Mistress Ottavia Ramello brokers the Albina copper that goes north to the prince's mint and the Ardisi grain that goes to his camp. She hates the queen and sells to her anyway.
FX31-017.reputation: Rich survivors of Lorino who sell to everyone and forgive no one.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Cedar Yards
members.note: Hid in a grain bin through the sack of Lorino and has priced her revenge to the last sun.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Rides with the carters and knows every toll-keeper's price.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Has found the soldier Oren Vask, who carries the queen's written leave for the sack, and is bargaining for it.

members.role: Brother-in-law; yard master
members.note: Cuts cedar for both armies' siege engines and asks no questions.

famousDead: Grain merchant of Lorino, killed in the sack of 1071.
FX31-017.secret: The Ramello broker both the Lord Marshal's copper to the prince's mint and the Ardisi grain to his camp, and Chiara is buying the queen's leave for the sack of Lorino.
hooks: Chiara meets Oren Vask in Soldiers' Town.
A queen's auditor follows a copper cart to Feleria.

FX31-018.name: the Salvane family
FX31-018.title: Galley-Master of Tessar
FX31-018.arms: a white galley on blue waves, a gold sun above

military.office: Galley captains of the queen's squadron
military.unit: three of the queen's 12 galleys and 100 galley marines
military.ties: Salvane captains have commanded Tessar galleys since King Marcian built the harbor mole and now keep the queen's grain run open.

FX31-018.power: Three of the queen's 12 galleys, two grain cogs of their own, and the grain runs that feed Tessar.
FX31-018.history: King Marcian built the harbor mole of Tessar in the 780s and gave the first royal galley to a Salvane. The family has captained the kings' galleys since and fought the Tamari and Blackreef on the Middle Sea. Since the Neck road closed, the Salvane grain runs feed the city: Tessar imports its bread by sea and the queen's galleys guard the cogs. Captain Lucan Salvane has run grain from Morhaven and Ostra all winter. He also carries what the queen's quartermaster calls lamp oil, unloaded at night into her cellars, and he knows it is not.
FX31-018.reputation: Hard-working sea captains who keep the city fed.

members.role: Head of the family; Galley-Master of Tessar
members.note: Brought 40 cogs of grain into Tessar this winter and lost only one to the weather.

members.role: Daughter; galley captain
members.note: Rammed a Tamari smuggler in 1103 and took its cargo of figs as prize.

members.role: Heir; master of the grain cogs
members.note: Sells a tenth of the queen's grain to the Refugee Field's bakers at triple price.

members.role: Lucan's wife
members.note: Keeps the house's books and suspects her son.

famousDead: First captain of a royal galley of Tessar.
FX31-018.secret: The Salvane galleys unload the Nine Winds fire-oil into the queen's cellars, and Fausto sells royal grain on the side.
hooks: A grain cog is lost and the city riots.
Prince Nikos's raiders look for the ships that carry the oil.

FX31-019.name: the Coyle family
FX31-019.title: Mother of the Leontine Men
FX31-019.arms: a bent crown stamped on a lead coin (the Leontine Men's mark)
FX31-019.power: A forging den in the Refugee Field, about 30 forgers and passers, and dies stolen from the queen's mint in 1083.
FX31-019.history: When Queen Livia's mint cut the Leontine to two parts silver in five in 1083, a mint striker named Agna Coyle, a Marchwoman by birth, walked out with two old dies in her apron. She set up in the shacks outside the South Gate, and her family has struck the queen's coin in lead and copper since. The Leontine Men pass it to unpaid soldiers, refugees and country carters. Tessar boils coin forgers in oil, an old imperial law the queen revived, and the Coyle have lost two of their own to the pot. Mother Agna is now old and wants out; her grandson wants to strike the prince's coin as well.
FX31-019.reputation: The queen's own forgers; the Refugee Field protects them.

members.role: Head of the clan; Mother of the Leontine Men
members.note: Walked out of the mint with two dies in 1083 and says her coin is more honest than the queen's.

members.role: Grandson; striker
members.note: Has bought a mould of Prince Andros's coin and wants to strike for both sides.

members.role: Daughter; passer
members.note: Pays soldiers in the Bent Leontine with her mother's coin and drinks with the ones who notice.

members.role: Son-in-law; lookout
members.note: Watched his brother boiled in oil in 1099 and sleeps with a knife.

famousDead: Agna's son; boiled in oil at the treasury gate for forging.
FX31-019.secret: The Coyle still hold two genuine dies from the queen's mint, which means their coin can pass even Lady Cassia's assay.
hooks: Lady Cassia Mentis finds a forged coin that passes her scales.
Tobin strikes the prince's coin and draws Dawn spies to the Refugee Field.

FX31-020.name: the Pradane family
FX31-020.title: Horse-Master of the Feleria Hills
FX31-020.arms: a white horse's head on red
FX31-020.power: Horse runs in the Feleria hills, remounts for the Dawn Lances, and a share in the 400 Morhaven horses coming this spring.
FX31-020.history: The Pradane bred horses in the Feleria hills for the Tessarans of Feleria and kept breeding after the cedar lords died out in 1046. Since 1062 they have supplied remounts to the Dawn Lances, and Coreria cost the Lances about 300 horses. This spring the Pradane are to receive 400 Morhaven-bred horses from the Sabine runs, sold against the King of Morhaven's word to Queen Livia, and drive them to Coreria. The head of the house has dealt with Morhaven horse-copers for twenty years. His daughter-in-law is a southerner and has a cousin in the queen's Road Riders.
FX31-020.reputation: Honest breeders, the prince's horse-suppliers, and Morhaven's quiet partners.

members.role: Head of the family; Horse-Master of the Feleria Hills
members.note: Will pay for the Morhaven horses in Ostran suns he has hoarded for ten years.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Will drive the 400 horses past the queen's Road Riders in May.

members.role: Nerio's wife, born in the south
members.note: Has written to her cousin in the queen's Road Riders about the horse drive.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Wants a horse of his own from the Morhaven herd.

FX31-020.secret: Marta Pradane has told the queen's Road Riders the route of the spring horse drive.
hooks: The 400 horses are ambushed on the Neck road.
A Morhaven horse-coper arrives with half the herd and a story.

FX32-001.name: House Teluk
FX32-001.title: Lord of Ruhu Bay
FX32-001.arms: a silver crescent moon over a blue bay, on sea green
FX32-001.words: The bay keeps what it takes.

military.office: Lords of the Ruhu spice squadron
military.unit: four armed spice ships and 300 rowers on the Rowing Hall rolls
military.ties: Teluk ships and rowers sail with the sultan's fleet every war season, and four of them are named for the Isle of Pearls in April.

FX32-001.power: The harbor of Ruhu, its clove and coconut gardens, four armed spice ships, and the harbor dues of a small market town.
FX32-001.history: The Teluk were harbor chiefs of Ruhu who lost half their boats in the Great Cyclone of 858 and swore to Bima Maruang in 859. They have held the bay under the sultans since and sent ships to every war. Teluk ships burned Keshi pepper ships at Kioya in 1068 and lost two hulls off Tekook in 1070. Lord Kamil Teluk died of marsh fever in 1102, and his widow Suria rules for their son, who is thirteen. Her brother-in-law Zainal captains the Ruhu ships and thinks the bay should be his.
FX32-001.reputation: An old harbor house with a boy lord and an uncle who smiles too much.

members.role: Head of the house in her son's name; Lady of Ruhu Bay
members.note: Keeps her son's food tasted and his uncle's ships counted.

members.role: Lord of Ruhu Bay; a boy
members.note: Wants to sail to the Isle of Pearls with his uncle and does not see why his mother says no.

members.role: Uncle; captain of the Ruhu ships
members.note: Keeps 120 dead rowers on the Ruhu roll and their pay in his sea chest.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Plays with her cousins and remembers everything her uncle says over dinner.

famousDead: Lord of Ruhu Bay; burned Keshi ships at Kioya in 1068; died of marsh fever.
FX32-001.secret: Zainal Teluk keeps 120 dead rowers on the Ruhu roll and pockets their pay.
hooks: The fleet sails on 1 April and the Ruhu ships are short of rowers.
Zainal invites his nephew on a voyage.

FX32-002.name: House Tanjung
FX32-002.title: Lord of the Nutmeg Point
FX32-002.arms: a green nutmeg tree with red fruit, on gold
FX32-002.power: Nutmeg gardens on the point of the Nutmeg Bays, perhaps a sixth of all nutmeg, and a warehouse in Paamu.
FX32-002.history: Sultan Yusuf gave the nutmeg point of Paamu to his scale-master Arif Tanjung in 946, a year after the Law of the Scales, to set a loyal house beside the clove lords. The Tanjung have grown nutmeg there since and quarrelled with the Merah's Paamu cousins over every boundary tree. Lord Jalil Tanjung now proposes his younger son as Lady Dewi Merah's adopted heir, since she has no child. The Merah cousins wait for her to die. In 1103 Jalil's elder son sold a sack of nutmeg seedlings to a Spice Coast agent, and smuggling seedlings off the isles is death.
FX32-002.reputation: Rich, loyal nutmeg lords; the clove lords call them the sultan's dogs.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Nutmeg Point
members.note: Wants his younger son made heir of House Merah and the Merah clove gardens with him.

members.role: Elder son and heir
members.note: Sold 200 nutmeg seedlings to a Keshi agent in 1103 to pay a gambling debt.

members.role: Younger son
members.note: Is being offered to Lady Dewi Merah as an heir and would rather marry a diver's daughter.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Prays at the Paamu well-house and knows what her elder son did.

famousDead: Scale-master of Sultan Yusuf, given the nutmeg point in 946.
FX32-002.secret: The heir Faizal sold nutmeg seedlings to a Keshi agent in 1103, a crime that carries death.
hooks: Nutmeg trees are found growing on the Spice Coast.
Lady Dewi Merah agrees to meet Johan.

FX32-003.name: House Pantai
FX32-003.title: Lady of the Shore Gardens
FX32-003.arms: a red clove-flower rose on white, a green border
FX32-003.words: The flower pays for the fleet.
FX32-003.power: Clove gardens along the shore of Great Amber, about 800 bales in a good year, and a seat among the Clove Lords.
FX32-003.history: The Pantai fenced the wild clove groves of the Great Amber shore in 812 and sold their buds through Amberport long before it had a sultan. They joined Lord Anwar Merah's rising of 1009 with six ships, lost them on the Tekook shoals, and paid 1,000 dinars to be forgiven. They have voted with the Clove Lords since. In 1101 the Vizier's men burned 400 Pantai bales beside the Merah cloves to hold the price. Lady Intan Pantai stands with Lady Dewi Merah against paying the spice fifth for the Pearl war. Her son has gone over to the Vizier, who buys toll farms and young men.
FX32-003.reputation: Old clove gentry, bitter about the Scales and split down the middle.

members.role: Head of the house; Lady of the Shore Gardens
members.note: Watched her cloves burn in 1101 and swore not to pay a dinar for the sultan's war.

members.role: Heir; clerk of the Vizier's toll farms
members.note: Works for the Grand Vizier and tells his mother the Clove Lords are finished.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Runs the gardens while her brother counts other men's tolls.

members.role: Old lord; Intan's father
members.note: Was a boy on the ships that sank at Tekook in 1009 and still swims every morning to prove he lived.

famousDead: Sailed six ships in the clove lords' rising of 1009 and lost them all.
FX32-003.secret: Haris Pantai has told the Vizier which Clove Lords will refuse the fifth, and his mother's name is first.
hooks: The sultan's men come for the 1105 fifth.
Haris is offered his mother's gardens if she falls.

FX32-004.name: House Selat
FX32-004.title: Lord of the Outer Roads
FX32-004.arms: a black gate between two blue waves, on silver

military.office: Lords of the harbor-fee galleys
military.unit: three fast galleys and 150 men of the outer roads
military.ties: Selat galleys stop foreign ships in the outer roads and serve with the sultan's fleet in war.

FX32-004.power: The office of collecting the harbor fee in the outer roads of Amberport, three fast galleys, and the Grand Vizier's favor.
FX32-004.history: When Sultan Idris set the harbor fee of one part in twenty in 1046, he gave the collecting of it in the outer roads to Daud Selat, a harbor clerk who could count a cargo by its waterline. The Selat have collected it since, and in 1063 they brought every passing Keshi ship in to pay, cheating as they did. The thief Nuru Keshari proved it in 1068 and started the Spice War. The Treaty of Madamo of 1072 left the Selat collecting only from ships that dock. They have found ways to make ships dock. Since 1093 they have worked hand in glove with the Grand Vizier.
FX32-004.reputation: Hated toll-takers; the Keshi say the Spice War was their fault, and it was.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Outer Roads
members.note: Collected the fees that Nuru Keshari stole the ledgers of in 1068, and has hated Kesh since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the fee galleys
members.note: Rams Keshi fishing boats 'by accident' so they must dock for repairs.

members.role: Daughter; keeper of the fee ledgers
members.note: Keeps two fee ledgers, just as her grandfather did.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Swims out to the Keshi ships to trade shells and has friends among their boys.

famousDead: First Lord of the Outer Roads; his cheating fees began the Spice War.
FX32-004.secret: The Selat keep two fee ledgers and take about 2,000 dinars a year more than they report.
hooks: A Keshi captain refuses to dock and Daud rams him in front of the allied fleet.
Ratna's second ledger goes missing.

FX32-005.name: House Awan
FX32-005.title: Lord of the Gum Forests
FX32-005.arms: a white mountain under a grey cloud, on amber

military.office: Lords of the tapper guards
military.unit: 120 spearmen guarding the Awan tapping camps
military.ties: Awan spearmen fight beside the Highland Spears against the Cloudfolk every dry season, and the house pays its own wyrm bounty on top of the sultan's.

FX32-005.power: Amber-gum tapping camps on the forest edge above Ruhu and the right to sell gum at the Scales.
FX32-005.history: After the first hill war ended at the Moss Line in 968, Sultan Yusuf gave the forest edge above Ruhu to a tapper chief named Bayu Awan to work amber-gum on the coast side of the cairns. The Awan have tapped it since, and since the Highland March was founded in 1034 they have pushed their camps over the line. The Cloud Ridge clan raids them every season. It spares the camps of House Batu, which the Awan have noticed. In 1103 the Cloudfolk killed Lord Haris Awan's eldest son and eleven tappers at a camp the Warden had promised to guard.
FX32-005.reputation: Hardy forest-edge lords with a grievance against the Warden.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of the Gum Forests
members.note: Buried his son in 1103 and asks at court every month why the Batu camps are never raided.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: Has followed Cloud Ridge raiders to within sight of a Batu camp, where they traded.

members.role: Lady of the house
members.note: Boils the gum herself and knows its price better than the Scales.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Son of the dead heir; the house's hope.

famousDead: Heir of the house; killed by the Cloud Ridge clan at a tapping camp.
FX32-005.secret: Kemala Awan has seen Cloud Ridge raiders trading with Batu tappers and means to prove the Warden's truce.
hooks: Kemala brings proof to court.
The Cloud Ridge clan raids the Awan camps the week before the fleet sails.

FX32-006.name: House Kilat
FX32-006.title: Galley-Lord of the Sultan
FX32-006.arms: a gold arrow like a lightning stroke, on black

military.office: Hereditary galley captains of the war fleet
military.unit: two war galleys and 220 men
military.ties: Kilat captains have commanded war galleys since the Tekook yard was founded in 1031 and serve under the Rawang admirals.

FX32-006.power: The captaincy of two war galleys and the Admiral's trust.
FX32-006.history: When Sultan Idris built the naval yard at Tekook in 1031, he gave two of its first galleys to the brothers Megat and Saiful Kilat, sons of a harbor boatman, and the house has captained galleys since. A Kilat galley was beside Prince Adil's when the fire ship took it off Tekook in 1070, and the Kilat pulled out eleven men but not the prince. In 1104 Captain Megat Kilat rowed Admiral Jaya Rawang to a night meeting with the Keshi admiral Jabari Tide and stood guard outside the cabin. He heard the promise of a third of the pearl banks, and he has said nothing.
FX32-006.reputation: Fast, daring galley captains; the Admiral's own men.

members.role: Head of the house; galley captain
members.note: Stood guard outside the Admiral's cabin when he promised the Keshi a third of the pearl banks.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Wants her husband made sea lord if the Rawang fall, and knows how to make them fall.

members.role: Heir; galley officer
members.note: Will lead the boarding party on the Isle of Pearls and dreams of the roc's nest.

members.role: Old captain; Megat's father
members.note: Pulled eleven men from Prince Adil's burning galley in 1070 and still dreams of the twelfth.

famousDead: First Kilat galley captain of the Tekook yard.
FX32-006.secret: Captain Megat Kilat witnessed Admiral Rawang's secret promise to the Keshi admiral.
hooks: Cempaka offers the secret to the Grand Vizier.
The Keshi admiral asks Megat for the written promise.

FX32-007.name: House Gelora
FX32-007.title: Lord of Paamu Harbor
FX32-007.arms: a grey whale breaching, on deep blue

military.office: Lords of the Nutmeg Bays garrison
military.unit: the Nutmeg Bays garrison, 600 men, quartered at Paamu
military.ties: The sultan's garrison of the Nutmeg Bays lives in Gelora barracks, and Gelora sons serve as its officers.

FX32-007.power: The harbor of Paamu, its fish and nutmeg markets, and the barracks of the Nutmeg Bays garrison.
FX32-007.history: The Gelora were harbor chiefs of Paamu on the Isle of Cloves who swore to Bima Maruang with the Merah in 859. They took the Path of the Well with the sultans in 890 and have been the most pious house of the isles since. When the clove lords rose in 1009 the Gelora stayed loyal, and Sultan Harun put his garrison of the Nutmeg Bays in their barracks to watch the Merah cousins. Lady Ratna Gelora is the sister of the Chief Well-Keeper Hamid Sari, who was born in Paamu. Like her brother, she says the sultan must name an heir who has the storm-sense before the fleet sails.
FX32-007.reputation: Pious, loyal and close to the Well-Keepers; the clove lords think them spies.

members.role: Head of the house; Lord of Paamu Harbor
members.note: Feeds the sultan's garrison and reports on the Merah cousins every month.

members.role: Lady of the house; sister of the Chief Well-Keeper
members.note: Writes to her brother every week about the storm-sense in the sultan's children.

members.role: Heir; officer of the garrison
members.note: Likes the Merah cousins he is meant to watch and drinks with them.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Sings the Well verses beautifully and is in love with a Merah cousin.

famousDead: Stayed loyal in the clove lords' rising of 1009 and hosted the sultan's garrison.
FX32-007.secret: Lady Ratna has told her brother that the sultan's elder son has no storm-sense, which the court has tried to hide.
hooks: The Chief Well-Keeper demands the Storm Watch before the fleet sails.
Delima elopes with a Merah cousin.

FX32-008.name: House Ombak
FX32-008.title: Captain of the Sultan's Marines
FX32-008.arms: a white wave breaking over a black spear, on blue
FX32-008.words: From the surf, up the beach.

military.office: Hereditary Captains of the Sultan's Marines
military.unit: the Sultan's Marines, 2,400 men at Amberport and Tekook
military.ties: An Ombak has led the marines who land on beaches since the Tekook yard was founded, and they will lead the first boats onto the Isle of Pearls on 1 April.

FX32-008.power: Command of the 2,400 Sultan's Marines and the first boats of every landing.
FX32-008.history: When Sultan Idris founded the Tekook yard in 1031, he raised a company of marines to board ships and land on beaches and gave it to Ismail Ombak, a pearl diver's son who could swim in mail. The Ombak have led the Sultan's Marines since. They boarded the Keshi pepper ships at Kioya in 1068 and lost a third of their men when the fire ship struck off Tekook in 1070. Captain Hasyim Ombak will take the first boats onto the Isle of Pearls in April. He has counted his boats and the rowers who will row them, and knows the rolls lie.
FX32-008.reputation: The sultan's beach-stormers; brave, loud and very proud of it.

members.role: Head of the house; Captain of the Sultan's Marines
members.note: Will lead the first boats onto the Isle of Pearls and has told his men to row themselves if they must.

members.role: Heir; marine officer
members.note: Swims ashore with a rope in his teeth on every exercise and is cheered for it.

members.role: Hasyim's wife
members.note: Runs the marines' widows' fund and knows every family the war will hurt.

members.role: Brother; marine sergeant
members.note: Lost an arm at Kioya and still teaches boarding drill with the other.

famousDead: Captain of the Marines; died when the fire ship burned Prince Adil's galley off Tekook.
FX32-008.secret: Captain Hasyim knows the Rowing Hall rolls are 1,100 men short and has not told the sultan, because the Admiral asked him not to.
hooks: The landing on the Isle of Pearls goes in short of boats.
Nuri finds the roc's nest.

FX32-009.name: the Dayung family
FX32-009.title: Keeper of the Rowing Rolls
FX32-009.arms: a bronze drum-bell on red, crossed oars behind

military.office: Hereditary drum-masters and roll-keepers of the Rowing Hall of Tekook
military.unit: the drum-masters of the fleet, about 60 men, and the rolls of 9,000 rowers
military.ties: Dayung drummers have set the stroke for the war galleys since 1031 and keep the rolls of the Rowing Hall under its master.

FX32-009.power: The rolls and pay-chests of the Rowing Hall, and the drum that sets the stroke on every war galley.
FX32-009.history: The first Dayung was the drummer of Sultan Idris's flagship, and since the Rowing Hall was founded at Tekook in 1031 the family has kept its drums and its rolls. They set the stroke at Kioya in 1068 and off Tekook in 1070. After the cyclone of 1071 drowned 2,500 men, the dead were slow to come off the rolls, and somehow they never quite did. In 1105 the rolls carry about 1,100 rowers who are dead or gone, and their pay goes somewhere. Master Fikri Laut of the Rowing Hall trains the rowers who exist; the Dayung count the ones who do not.
FX32-009.reputation: Drum-masters and clerks; the rowers call them the Counters.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Rowing Rolls
members.note: Has kept dead men on the rolls since 1071 and shares their pay with three captains.

members.role: Daughter; pay-clerk
members.note: Pays the rowers by hand and has started writing down the names nobody collects.

members.role: Heir; drum-master of the flagship
members.note: Can hold a stroke for six hours and has no idea what his father does with the rolls.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Buys clove gardens with money she says came from her father.

famousDead: Drummer of the flagship at Kioya; beat the stroke until an arrow stopped him.
FX32-009.secret: The Dayung have kept about 1,100 dead and runaway rowers on the rolls since 1071 and share the pay with the captains who sign for them.
hooks: Juwita takes her list of names to the Grand Vizier.
The fleet sails and the galleys are rowed by marines.

FX32-010.name: the Lumut family
FX32-010.title: Keeper of the Harbor Chain
FX32-010.arms: a black key across a grey chain, on moss green
FX32-010.words: Up at the drum, down at the word.

military.office: Hereditary Keepers of the Harbor Chain and captains of the Sea Fort towers
military.unit: the harbor towers company, 400 of the Sea Fort's 1,600 men
military.ties: A Lumut has raised Amberport's harbor chain since Sultan Ismail finished the Sea Fort in 928.

FX32-010.power: The harbor chain of Amberport, the winches of the two chain towers, and 400 men of the Sea Fort.
FX32-010.history: When Sultan Ismail finished the Sea Fort in 928, he gave the harbor chain to Kasim Lumut, the smith who forged it. Lumut keepers have raised it at every alarm since. In June 1069 the Keshi thief Nuru Keshari burned twelve Amber ships in the harbor by night and escaped through a drain of the Sea Fort; the Lumut keeper was flogged, and the drains were sealed. The family has spent 36 years living it down. What the sultan does not know is that one drain under the west chain tower was never truly sealed, and the Lumut use it.
FX32-010.reputation: Steady, rust-handed chain men with a stain they cannot scrub out.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Harbor Chain
members.note: Was flogged as a young keeper in 1069 and has never let the chain be slow since.

members.role: Heir; captain of the west chain tower
members.note: Lets the Creek Boys use the old west drain for a fee.

members.role: Daughter; smith
members.note: Mends the chain links and wonders why the west drain grate is oiled.

members.role: Grandson
members.note: Plays in the drains and knows them better than his grandfather.

famousDead: Forged Amberport's harbor chain and became its first keeper.
FX32-010.secret: The west drain of the Sea Fort was never sealed, and Shukri Lumut lets smugglers use it.
hooks: A Keshi spy escapes the Sea Fort the way Nuru did.
Indah follows the oil trail into the drain.

FX32-011.name: the Penyu family
FX32-011.title: Sergeant of the Highland Spears
FX32-011.arms: a green turtle under a black spear, on amber
FX32-011.words: Slow up the hill, fast down it.

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Highland Spears
military.unit: two hundreds of the Highland Spears at the Aming Stockade
military.ties: Penyu men climbed to Aming with Hasan Batu in 1034 and have fought the Cloudfolk every dry season since.

FX32-011.power: Two hundreds of the Highland Spears, a house inside the Aming Stockade, and the Warden's trust.
FX32-011.history: The first Penyu was a coast fisherman who carried Hasan Batu's supplies up to Aming in 1034 and stayed to fight. Penyu sergeants have led Highland Spears against the Cloudfolk every dry season since, and four Penyu men have died of wyrm bites. In 1086 Sergeant Ali Penyu's spears killed the Cloud Ridge chief and eleven of his men. In 1100 his son carried Warden Hamzah Batu's water skin to Amtiuan Falls and waited out of earshot while the Warden met the dead chief's son alone. He saw them clasp arms. He has said nothing, because the Warden is the Warden.
FX32-011.reputation: Tough highland sergeants, more loyal to the Batu than to the sultan.

members.role: Head of the family; sergeant of the Highland Spears
members.note: Saw the Warden clasp arms with Lintang Cloudwalker at Amtiuan Falls in 1100.

members.role: Old sergeant
members.note: Killed the Cloud Ridge chief in 1086 and would kill his son too if he knew where he slept.

members.role: Jalil's wife; stockade healer
members.note: Has saved six men from wyrm venom with a knife, a fire and no fear.

members.role: Heir; spearman of the Wyrm Spears
members.note: Trains under Bakar the Wyrm-Killer and has taken two wyrm heads already.

famousDead: Carried Hasan Batu's supplies to Aming in 1034 and fought there until a wyrm took him.
FX32-011.secret: Jalil Penyu witnessed Warden Batu's secret bargain with Lintang Cloudwalker, and his father would kill the Warden if he learned of it.
hooks: Old Ali hears a Cloudfolk song about the falls.
Lady Kemala Awan asks Jalil to swear what he saw.

FX32-012.name: the Siput family
FX32-012.title: Head Diver of the Ruhu Banks
FX32-012.arms: a white fish over a pearl-shell, on deep teal
FX32-012.power: Eleven diving boats, the best lungs of the eastern gulf, and the secret marks of the Isle of Pearls banks.
FX32-012.history: The Siput dived the pearl banks long before Sultan Yusuf brought the divers under his fifth in 956, and they have paid it, grumbling, ever since. In 1095 a storm blew a Siput boat onto the reefs of the Isle of Pearls, and the crew found banks richer than any in the south. The family has worked them in secret since and sold the pearls at Madamo without paying the sultan's fifth. In 1100 a Siput diver brought back the roc egg that the sultan's treasury bought. Now the sultan's fleet will sail to take the island, and the first thing it will find is Siput marker stones on the reef.
FX32-012.reputation: Deep-lunged, close-mouthed divers; the best on the banks.

members.role: Head of the clan; Head Diver
members.note: Can stay under for the count of three hundred and has never told the sultan's men a true number.

members.role: Son; boat captain
members.note: Brought the roc egg out of the Isle of Pearls in 1100 and still has the scars of the bird's claws.

members.role: Granddaughter; diver
members.note: Wants to see the roc's nest and has been to the island six times.

members.role: Son; pearl seller at Madamo
members.note: Sells untaxed pearls to Keshi buyers and keeps a wife in Madamo.

famousDead: Diver lost in the cyclone of 1071 with three boats.
FX32-012.secret: The Siput have worked the Isle of Pearls banks since 1095 and sold the pearls at Madamo without paying the sultan's fifth.
hooks: The fleet finds Siput marker stones on the reef.
The admiral wants Siput divers as guides.

FX32-013.name: the Layar family
FX32-013.title: Master of the Layar Ships
FX32-013.arms: a white sailing ship on red

military.office: Owners of armed spice ships pressed into the fleet
military.unit: six armed spice ships and 90 spice-ship guards
military.ties: Layar ships are among the 140 armed spice ships that sail with the war fleet, and six of them are named for the Pearl war.

FX32-013.power: Six armed spice ships on the runs to Kesh, Ranpur and Qadir, and warehouses on the Amberport harbor front.
FX32-013.history: The Layar bought their first spice ship in 990 and have carried cloves and nutmeg to Kesh, Ranpur and Qadir since. They lost three ships in the cyclone of 1071 and rebuilt with House Doravelli's loans, which they are still paying. Since 1085 they have fought Ranpur's cotton ships with low prices. In 1101 Captain Dahlan Layar carried a pale young elephant cow from Amberport to the Ranpur delta for a party of temple agents, and was paid three times the usual freight to forget it. He has not forgotten.
FX32-013.reputation: Rich, cheerful sea traders who will carry anything for a price.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Layar Ships
members.note: Shipped a pale elephant cow to Ranpur in 1101 and knows exactly which river landing she went ashore at.

members.role: Wife; keeper of the house's books
members.note: Wrote the elephant down as 'livestock, temple cargo' and wishes she had not written it at all.

members.role: Heir; captain
members.note: Will sail a Layar ship in the Pearl fleet and hopes for prize money.

members.role: Daughter
members.note: Haggles with Ranpuri cotton brokers in their own tongue and wins.

famousDead: Bought the house's first spice ship in 990.
FX32-013.secret: Captain Dahlan Layar carried the pale elephant cow to Ranpur in 1101 and can name the landing.
hooks: A Ranpuri spy offers Dahlan silver to name the landing.
A Ranpuri galley captain stops a Layar ship off the delta.

FX32-014.name: the Rumpai family
FX32-014.title: Broker of the Scales
FX32-014.arms: a gold sun over a pair of scales, on Well green
FX32-014.power: Two benches on the Scales, a fleet of hired cargo, a share in the Nagora toll farm of Ranpur, and ties by marriage to Ranpur's greatest cotton brokers.
FX32-014.history: The Rumpai were Well-faith spice brokers from Qadira who settled in Amberport's Well Quarter and took an island house name in 1012. They weigh and buy on the Scales and have prospered under the monopoly. In 1090 a Rumpai daughter married Amar Sethi, head of the Cotton Brokers of Ranpur, and in 1099 a Rumpai son married the daughter of a Ranpuri bill-broker. In November 1104 the house joined the Grand Vizier's merchants in buying three years of Ranpur's Nagora tolls for 60,000 lotus. Its younger son is the toll farmer now on his way to Tirpur, and he will find the Warden's two toll books.
FX32-014.reputation: The richest brokers on the Scales; pious, polite and everywhere.

members.role: Head of the family; Broker of the Scales
members.note: Married one daughter to Ranpur's cotton king and bought Ranpur's mountain road with the dowry's profits.

members.role: Younger son; toll farmer bound for Tirpur
members.note: Goes to Tirpur to count the Nagora tolls, and has no idea how dangerous honest counting can be.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Married a Ranpuri bill-broker's daughter and reads her father's letters before she does.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Pays for the Well caravanserai's free water and counts every cup.

famousDead: Came from Qadira and took the house name Rumpai in 1012.
FX32-014.secret: The Rumpai hold a copy of the Amberport market roll entry for the pale calf, sent by their son-in-law Amar Sethi's factor.
hooks: Kamil Rumpai arrives at Tirpur and opens the toll books.
Keeper Anand's agent offers Rahim a fortune for the copy.

FX32-015.name: the Pasir family
FX32-015.title: Auditor of the Market Roll
FX32-015.arms: a white star over a blue well, on sand
FX32-015.power: Seats in the Well-Keepers' court, the yearly audit of Amberport's market roll, and the respect of the Well Quarter.
FX32-015.history: When Sultan Yusuf made the Law of the Scales in 945, the Well-Keepers were given the audit of the market roll, and the Pasir, a family of Well scholars, have done the counting since. Every January a Pasir clerk reads the whole year's roll aloud to the Chief Well-Keeper. In January 1105 the clerk is young Fikri Pasir, and he has found that a page of the 1101 roll has been cut. He has the stub in his sleeve. The family serves Chief Well-Keeper Hamid Sari, who calls himself the sultan's conscience, and the Pasir mean to be his eyes.
FX32-015.reputation: Dry, honest Well scholars; merchants dread their January.

members.role: Head of the family; Auditor of the Market Roll
members.note: Has read forty years of market rolls aloud and never once skipped a line.

members.role: Grandson; audit clerk
members.note: Found a page cut from the 1101 roll and carries the stub in his sleeve.

members.role: Daughter; teacher at the Well-house
members.note: Teaches the Book to merchants' daughters and hears what their fathers say at home.

members.role: Son; judge of the Well court
members.note: Judges debt cases and has never bound a debtor for a day past seven years.

famousDead: First auditor of the market roll under the Law of the Scales.
FX32-015.secret: Fikri Pasir holds the stub of the page cut from the 1101 market roll.
hooks: A Ranpuri agent follows Fikri home.
Fikri must get the stub to the Chief Well-Keeper past the Vizier's watchers.

FX32-016.name: the Camar family
FX32-016.title: Keeper of the Gull Shrine
FX32-016.arms: a white gull flying, on sea blue (painted on the shrine's boat-prows)
FX32-016.power: The Gull Shrine of Paamu and its beach, where the commoners burn their dead and bless their boats, and the trust of the fishing villages.
FX32-016.history: Ranpuri traders brought the Thousand Names to the islands from the 5th century, and the Camar have kept a shrine of the Names and the sea spirits on the Paamu beach since about 640. They bless boats, read the gulls before a voyage and burn the dead on the beach so the ashes go to the sea. The Well-Keepers tolerate them and disapprove of them. The family keeps up old ties with a temple family of Ranpur, and Ranpuri travellers lodge at the shrine. One of them, a quiet man named Nikhil Das, lodged there in December 1104 and asked a lot about the Amberport market roll.
FX32-016.reputation: Kindly beach priests whom the fishers trust more than any Well-Keeper.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Gull Shrine
members.note: Read the gulls for the Pearl fleet and saw a bad sign he has told no one.

members.role: Daughter; burner of the dead
members.note: Has burned 2,000 dead on the beach and sings each one out to sea.

members.role: Grandson; novice
members.note: Showed the Ranpuri lodger the way to the Pasir house in Amberport.

members.role: Awang's wife
members.note: Brews fever tea for half of Paamu and gossip for the other half.

FX32-016.secret: The Camar shrine shelters agents of Ranpur's temple families, and young Bayu guided one to the market-roll auditor's door.
hooks: The Pearl fleet asks for a blessing and Awang must decide whether to speak of the bad sign.
Well-Keepers accuse the shrine of harboring spies.

FX32-017.name: the Angin family
FX32-017.title: Head Hunter of the Ruhu Highlands
FX32-017.arms: a black serpent coiled, a white spear through it, on green
FX32-017.power: The wyrm bounty, a dozen hunting camps in the highlands above Ruhu, and the best trackers on Great Amber.
FX32-017.history: The Angin turned to wyrm hunting when Sultan Harun set the bounty after an Amber Wyrm killed his heir in 1022, and they have taken more than 600 heads since at 5 dinars each. They hunt on cold mornings with heavy spears to the neck, the way the Spear Yard of Aming teaches, and they trap thunderbirds for their feathers. In 1100 Angin hunters caught a pale young elephant cow in the highland forests and sold her in Amberport's market to Ranpuri temple agents. She is a highland cow, pale from birth, and no kin to any white elephant. They thought nothing of it until men started asking.
FX32-017.reputation: Scarred, fearless highland hunters; every village pays them and fears their tempers.

members.role: Head of the family; Head Hunter of the Ruhu Highlands
members.note: Has 140 wyrm heads to his name and a bite scar on each leg.

members.role: Daughter; trapper
members.note: Caught the pale elephant cow in 1100 and raised her on bananas for a month before the sale.

members.role: Heir
members.note: Took a thunderbird alive in 1103 and sold it to a Keshi prince's agent.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Cuts wyrm venom out of hunters and keeps the bounty money buried.

famousDead: Took 200 wyrm heads before a wyrm took his.
FX32-017.secret: The Angin know the pale cow sold to Ranpur in 1100 was a wild highland elephant, not of any white line.
hooks: A Ranpuri cotton broker's agent asks Lestari where the cow was caught.
A huge wyrm is seen near the Awan camps.

FX32-018.name: the Perahu creek line
FX32-018.title: Elder of the Creek Boys
FX32-018.arms: a white open hand on black (the Creek Boys' sign, painted on night boats)
FX32-018.words: What the Scales do not see, the sea forgets.
FX32-018.power: About 40 boatmen of the back channels, fast canoes, and a way past the harbor chain.
FX32-018.history: The Perahu were boatmen of the Stilt Town who were ruined by Sultan Idris's harbor fee in 1046, and the next year they began running sacks of cloves out of the Scales by night. The Creek Boys have done it since, paddling through the back channels to Keshi captains waiting beyond the chain. They carry spice, pearls and, once, a fugitive. They never carry seedlings, because seedlings mean death for everyone aboard. Old Daud Perahu runs the boats; his granddaughter has found that the Sea Fort's west drain is the fastest way past the chain.
FX32-018.reputation: The Stilt Town's darlings and the Scales' worst nightmare.

members.role: Elder of the Creek Boys
members.note: Has run spice past the Scales for forty years and has never been caught with a sack.

members.role: Granddaughter; captain of the canoes
members.note: Found the unsealed drain under the west chain tower and pays its keeper in pepper.

members.role: Son; fence
members.note: Sells to Keshi captains and buys them drink at the Keshi House.

members.role: Great-granddaughter; lookout
members.note: Sits on the stilts and whistles when the Selat galleys move.

famousDead: Founded the Creek Boys after the harbor fee ruined his boats.
FX32-018.secret: The Creek Boys pass the harbor chain through the Sea Fort's unsealed west drain.
hooks: A Keshi captain asks the Creek Boys to carry a man, not a sack.
Dewi Merah's steward offers them the surplus cloves before the burning.

FX32-019.name: the Pulau family
FX32-019.title: Master of the Kris-Smiths
FX32-019.arms: a silver wavy blade on black
FX32-019.power: The kris-smiths' street of Amberport, the contract for the marines' blades, and the folded-steel secrets of the islands.
FX32-019.history: The Pulau forged the first kris for Sultan Daud's court in 891, and they have made the wavy island blades of every Maruang sultan since. They fold island iron with meteor nickel and forge the boarding blades of the Sultan's Marines. In 1099 the master held a Chanari blade in his hands for the first time and understood that island steel is not the best in the world. Since 1102 the family has bought smuggled Chanari blades through Ranpuri sailors to study them, which is illegal in Ranpur and frowned on in Amberport. The master's son wants to go to Chanari and steal the secret.
FX32-019.reputation: Proud island smiths whose blades are prized and whose tempers are short.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Kris-Smiths
members.note: Broke a Chanari blade in his vice to see its grain and wept at what he saw.

members.role: Son
members.note: Plans to sail to Ranpur in a Layar ship and find his way into Chanari.

members.role: Daughter and heir
members.note: Forges the marines' blades and thinks island steel is fine as it is.

members.role: Wife
members.note: Polishes every blade the house sells and names each one.

famousDead: Forged the first kris of the sultans in 891.
FX32-019.secret: The Pulau have bought a dozen smuggled Chanari blades since 1102, and one came from a mill that is not in any Ranpuri tally.
hooks: Saiful sails for Ranpur.
A Chanari blade in the Pulau shop carries a mark the Steel-Warden would recognise.

FX33-001.name: The Cinderwakes
FX33-001.title: Raft-Master of the Ratrock Raft Yard
FX33-001.arms: a black raft trailing red fire across dark water
FX33-001.words: We were there. We say nothing.

military.office: Sworn fire-men of the Forty and raft-masters of the Ratrock Raft Yard
military.unit: one raft-crew of the Forty and 60 of the Raft Yard guard
military.ties: They build and burn the fire-rafts that make the dragon, and every grown Cinderwake is sworn to the Forty under the Oil-Keeper.

FX33-001.power: A sworn place among the Forty, the raft yard's tools and timber, and a double share of every toll for their silence.
FX33-001.history: On the night of 12 July 1051 Mag Brine burned three Lucernan ships in the Strait, and a raft-builder named Gil towed the burning rafts out into the current. He was one of the 40 who knew the truth, and the crews called him Cinderwake for the ash that floated behind him. His family has been of the Forty ever since. In May 1053 Cinderwake rafts were towed through the reef on the fourth night of the Gull Isle Landing and burned 11 galleys at anchor. Every Dragon Night they stage the dragon again in the harbor, and every child of the family learns to tar a raft before it learns to read. On Dragon Night 1104 a sealed jar with Sabra's well-mark went missing from the Ratrock caves, and a Cinderwake had the watch.
FX33-001.reputation: Smoky, silent and paid double; the crews think they are fire-priests of the dragon and buy them drinks to hear about it.

members.role: Head of the family; Raft-Master of the Ratrock Raft Yard; one of the Forty
members.note: Has burned 30 dragons in the harbor and lost the eyebrows of his youth to the first one.

members.role: Jago's wife; pitch-boiler of the raft yard
members.note: Mixes the sulfur and pitch that make the dragon's smoke and swears it is a cure for coughs.

members.role: Heir; cave-watch of the Forty
members.note: Was dicing in the harbor on Dragon Night 1104 instead of at his post in the caves.

members.role: Jago's daughter; raft-tower
members.note: Swims the fire-rafts out through the reef at night and wants to be the first woman sworn to the Forty.

famousDead: Towed the burning rafts out into the Strait on Dragon Night, 12 July 1051.
FX33-001.secret: Dace left the Ratrock caves unwatched on Dragon Night 1104 to dice in the harbor, and the stamped jar went missing in that hour; the Oil-Keeper has not yet asked who had the watch.
hooks: Sten the Quiet starts asking who stood the cave-watch on Dragon Night.
Wren asks to be sworn to the Forty in her brother's place.
Qadir's agents offer the Cinderwakes a fortune to burn a dragon somewhere else.

FX33-002.name: The Chainmen
FX33-002.title: Warden of the Harbor Chain
FX33-002.arms: a black chain of anchor links across a silver harbor mouth

military.office: Hereditary wardens of the Blackreef harbor chain
military.unit: the harbor chain garrison, 400 crossbowmen of the channel towers
military.ties: They raise the Solen chain of anchor links across the reef channel and hold its two towers with crossbows, the last wall of the Brotherhood.

FX33-002.power: The old Solen chain and its windlass towers, 400 crossbowmen, and the say over which ship enters the harbor at night.
FX33-002.history: The harbor chain was forged by Solen marines in the centuries of the galley station, from anchor links as thick as a man's arm, and it still closes the reef channel. When Harl Gannet swore the captains to the Articles in 990 the chain was rusted shut, and a Tessarian smith named Kell freed it in 992 and was made its warden. His family has kept it since. The Chainmen raise it at the first sight of a strange sail and lower it for the Brotherhood's own. In the Corsair War the chain held for the whole winter blockade of 1054 to 1055, and Varenna's galleys never got inside. Varenna's Lion Fleet sails after Sea Opening this year, and the chain has a cracked link that no one outside the family knows of.
FX33-002.reputation: Heavy, careful folk who smell of grease and iron; nobody gets into Blackreef without passing their towers.

members.role: Head of the family; Warden of the Harbor Chain
members.note: Greases every link of the chain himself each spring and counts them twice.

members.role: Kell's wife; captain of the east tower
members.note: Put a bolt through a Varennan galley-master's hand at 200 paces in 1092 and has the man's ring.

members.role: Heir; master of the windlass crews
members.note: Found the crack in the eleventh link after the storm of 1094 and has been patching it with lead ever since.

members.role: Kell's daughter; smith's apprentice
members.note: Says she can recast the eleventh link if someone will buy her a ton of good iron from Varenna, of all places.

famousDead: Tessarian smith who freed the rusted Solen chain in 992.
Held the chain through the winter blockade of 1054 to 1055.
FX33-002.secret: The eleventh link of the harbor chain has been cracked since the storm of October 1094 and is held with lead; a heavy galley driven at it under oars could break it.
hooks: Varenna's Lion Fleet is sighted, and the eleventh link must hold.
Etta needs a ton of iron that only an enemy port sells.
A Redsail captain asks the Chainmen to lower the chain for him at night without the Captain-General's word.

FX33-003.name: The Windlasses
FX33-003.title: Sergeant of the Reef Crossbows
FX33-003.arms: a crossbow windlass over a white wave, on blue-black

military.office: Hereditary sergeants of the Reef Crossbows
military.unit: a company of the Reef Crossbows, 100 crossbowmen hired to Queen Livia at Tessar
military.ties: They train every crossbowman of the Brotherhood and serve in the 800 Reef Crossbows under Brann Hollow, now on hire at Tessar.

FX33-003.power: The training of the Brotherhood's crossbowmen, a company at Tessar, and a sergeant's share of every hire.
FX33-003.history: After the Peace of Ratrock in 1056 the Brotherhood needed fighters it could hire out when it could no longer raid, and a toll-boat crossbowman named Penn taught 30 men to shoot from a pitching deck and stand behind pavises ashore. His family has trained the Brotherhood's crossbowmen since. The Reef Crossbows are their pride. In April 1104 Nell Brine hired the 800 to Queen Livia, and at Coreria on 26 October they held Livia's line and turned the battle into a draw, and three Windlasses died there. Half the company's pay is now owed. Prince Andros has offered double, and the Windlass sergeant at Tessar has listened.
FX33-003.reputation: Steady, tough sell-swords who hold a line; the Brotherhood's best export after fear.

members.role: Head of the family; Sergeant of the Reef Crossbows at Tessar
members.note: Held the pavise line at Coreria with a broken wrist and wound his crossbow with his teeth.

members.role: Penn's wife; keeper of the company's pay-chest at Blackreef
members.note: Counts the queen's missing silver every week and curses Tessar by name each time.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Reef Crossbows
members.note: Has met Prince Andros's agent twice in a Tessar wine shop and told his father only once.

members.role: Penn's daughter; trainer of the harbor recruits
members.note: Teaches 14-year-old galley boys to shoot and has turned out better marksmen than her brother.

famousDead: Taught the first 30 Brotherhood crossbowmen to shoot from a pitching deck.
FX33-003.secret: Rudd has promised Prince Andros's agent that his company of 100 will change sides if the queen's pay is not paid by May, and has taken 200 suns on account.
hooks: The queen's pay does not arrive by May.
Penn learns what his son promised Andros.
Ima Redsail offers the Windlasses a share of open raiding if they come home and vote with her.

FX33-004.name: The Oakums
FX33-004.title: Master of the Caulkers of Ratrock
FX33-004.arms: a caulking iron and mallet crossed over a black hull seam
FX33-004.power: The Caulkers of Ratrock, about 60 caulkers and tarrers who seal every hull in the port, and the debts of half the captains who sail from it.
FX33-004.history: The Oakums came to Ratrock with Hob Redsail's crews in 1031, when a ship's caulker named Ord found that pirates paid better than navies and paid in advance. His family has sealed hulls at Ratrock since, picking oakum from old rope and driving it into seams with pitch. The Caulkers of Ratrock work on credit, and the captains who cannot pay give the Oakums a share of the next prize. When the dragon toll of 1056 cut the prizes, the debts grew. The Redsails owe the Caulkers 300 marks. If Ima Redsail wins her vote and goes back to open raiding, the Oakums will be paid; if Nell Brine keeps the Table, the Redsails' debt may never be paid at all.
FX33-004.reputation: Black-handed, sharp-eyed and owed by everyone; no captain in Ratrock dares quarrel with the Oakums before a voyage.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Caulkers of Ratrock
members.note: Keeps a debt-tally of every captain in Ratrock notched into the doorframe of his shed.

members.role: Ord's wife; oakum-picker and pitch-seller
members.note: Picks oakum with the galley slaves' wives and pays them, which no one else in Ratrock does.

members.role: Heir; hull-sealer of the Redsail galleys
members.note: Has sealed all nine Redsail galleys for a long voyage and knows Ima is not planning to stay in the Strait.

members.role: Ord's daughter; half-orc foster-child and tarrer
members.note: Was left on the Oakums' step as a baby and can lift a pitch-pot two men can't.

famousDead: Ship's caulker who came to Ratrock with Hob Redsail's crews in 1031.
FX33-004.secret: Nell Brine's Quartermaster has offered Ord 300 marks for the Redsails' debt-marker, which under the Articles would let him call Ima's ships into the yard before Share Day.
hooks: Ord must choose between the Quartermaster's silver and Ima's prizes.
Cal tells the Table what the Redsail galleys are sealed for.
A strange half-orc sailor comes asking about a baby left on a caulker's step in 1087.

FX33-005.name: The Ribbands
FX33-005.title: Master Shipwright of the Blackreef slips
FX33-005.arms: a ship's rib-frame on the slip, white on sea green
FX33-005.power: The three building slips of Blackreef harbor, 200 shipwrights and slave-sawyers, and the skill of cutting a captured cog down into a fast galley.
FX33-005.history: When Brask Ninefingers' fleet was beaten at Morhaven in 1011, Sabel Gannet had to rebuild it from nothing, and she gave the Blackreef slips to a Tessarian shipwright called Haskel Ribband who had sailed with Brask and come back alive. His family has built the Brotherhood's galleys since. The isles have little good timber, so the Ribbands rebuild captured ships: they cut down merchant cogs into light galleys and break the rest for planks. Their slave-sawyers come from the galley benches, and the Ribbands have freed more of them than any other masters, in return for seven years of sawing. Twelve captured cogs lie in the harbor now, and the Ribbands can turn four of them into galleys by summer. Nell Brine has asked them for a fifth, smaller and faster, and told them not to put it on the Table's list.
FX33-005.reputation: Proud craftsmen of the slips; the only family in Blackreef that the crews salute without being paid to.

members.role: Head of the family; Master Shipwright of the Blackreef slips
members.note: Can tell a ship's home port by the smell of her timbers and has never been wrong about a Lucernan.

members.role: Haskel's wife; mistress of the timber stores
members.note: Buys timber from Sabran ships and pays in toll crowns that she pretends are hers.

members.role: Heir; master of the secret slip
members.note: Builds the Captain-General's small galley by night in a cave slip behind the shrine.

members.role: Haskel's son; freed sawyer's foster-brother
members.note: Drinks with the Freed Oars and repeats what his family should not say.

famousDead: Tessarian shipwright who rebuilt Sabel Gannet's fleet after 1011.
FX33-005.secret: The Ribbands are building Nell Brine a small, fast galley in a hidden cave slip, off the Table's list, so that she and her son can carry the Captain-General's chest away if the Table votes her out.
hooks: Fitch lets slip the hidden slip to the Freed Oars.
The Gannets demand an accounting of the timber bought with toll crowns.
The secret galley is ready, and Nell has not yet lost the vote.

FX33-006.name: The Lanterns
FX33-006.title: Lamp-Keeper of Wreck Isle
FX33-006.arms: no arms: a shuttered lantern scratched on a door means a Lantern will buy what you have
FX33-006.words: A light on the wrong headland feeds a village.
FX33-006.power: The goat-camps and coves of Wreck Isle, a fleet of small boats no one counts, and the only fence-ring that sells Brotherhood plunder in every Southland port.
FX33-006.history: The Lanterns were wreckers before there was a Brotherhood, before the Solen station closed, in the long centuries when a lantern on the wrong headland on a winter night could feed a village for a year. They lived on Wreck Isle among the goats and the lookouts and swore the Articles in 990 because everyone else did. The Articles maroon crew-thieves on Wreck Isle, and the Lanterns have fed them, sold them water and, for a price, sold them a boat. They are fences now more than wreckers, selling Brotherhood plunder in the Southland ports through cousins who pretend to be fishmongers. They still keep their lanterns trimmed, and when a winter storm blows a ship that has not paid onto the reef, no one asks who lit the headland. In 1102 they took a marooned man off Wreck Isle for 50 marks, and he was one of the Forty.
FX33-006.reputation: Goat-folk, fences and worse; the crews spit when they pass Wreck Isle and still buy their brandy there.

members.role: Head of the clan; Lamp-Keeper of Wreck Isle
members.note: Has a lantern for every headland of Wreck Isle and claims to have lit none of them.

members.role: Ruff's sister; fence of the Southland ports
members.note: Sells stolen Lucernan silks to Lucernan merchants in a Sunland port and makes them haggle.

members.role: Heir; boatman of the marooned
members.note: Rowed the marooned man off Wreck Isle in 1102 and liked him, which was the trouble.

members.role: Moll's daughter; goatherd and lookout
members.note: Saw a burning boat drift past Wreck Isle on Dragon Night and the man in it was still moving.

famousDead: Lit the headland that wrecked a Qadiri salt ship in 1040 and fed Wreck Isle for two winters.
FX33-006.secret: In 1102 the Lanterns sold a boat off Wreck Isle to a marooned man of the Forty who had been cast out for theft, and he sailed east knowing what the dragon really is.
hooks: The marooned man of the Forty is seen in Varenna's port.
The Captain-General's men come to Wreck Isle asking who sold boats to the marooned.
A winter storm drives a toll-paid ship toward the Lanterns' headland.

FX33-007.name: The Dateships
FX33-007.title: Master of the Sabra grain run
FX33-007.arms: a cog with a full hold of gold grain, on sea blue
FX33-007.power: Four round-ships that bring grain, dates and oil from Sabra and the Southland coast, the Brotherhood's grain contract, and a warehouse on the Blackreef quay.
FX33-007.history: The isles cannot feed themselves, and every bad harvest on the Southland shore has meant a hungry winter. In the winter of 1049 to 1050 Mag Brine sailed to Sabra and back through the storms with 2,000 bushels of grain and dates, and the man at his steering oar was a salt-boat master named Lew. When Mag was elected, he gave Lew the Brotherhood's grain contract, and the Dateships have fed the isles since. They buy at Sabra and along the Southland shore and pay in toll crowns. In the Corsair War their ships slipped through the winter blockade of 1054 to 1055 with Sabran supply ships. Their round-ships come home low in the water every spring, and not all of the weight is grain.
FX33-007.reputation: Rich and well liked; when a Dateship sail is sighted in March, the whole town comes down to the quay.

members.role: Head of the family; Master of the Sabra grain run
members.note: Grandson of Mag Brine's steersman, and has sailed to Sabra 50 times without once being asked what he carries back.

members.role: Lew's wife; keeper of the quay warehouse
members.note: Gives a sack of dates to every widow on the quay at Sea Closing, and the widows vote.

members.role: Heir; master of the round-ship Fat Sabel
members.note: Has seen the stamped jars under the grain and has started asking his father why there are more each year.

members.role: Lew's daughter; purser in the Sabra trade
members.note: Speaks Sabran like a Sabran and is courted by a young man of the emir's oil-master's household.

famousDead: Held Mag Brine's steering oar on the winter grain run of 1049 to 1050.
FX33-007.secret: The Sabran fire-oil jars come to Blackreef under the grain in Dateship holds, and the family has carried every jar since 1051.
hooks: A Qadiri galley stops a Dateship ship at sea and wants to see under the grain.
Jinny's suitor asks her about the empty jars that go back to Sabra to be counted.
A bad Southland harvest means the Dateships must buy grain from Varenna, the enemy.

FX33-008.name: The Bonedice
FX33-008.title: Keeper of the Shrine of the Dice
FX33-008.arms: three white bone dice showing six, on dark red
FX33-008.words: The luck-gods do not lie. Often.
FX33-008.power: The keeping of the painted sea cave of the Shrine of the Dice, the throwing of the dice before every raid and every Share Day, and the guardianship of the share-out book.
FX33-008.history: When Harl Gannet swore the captains to the Articles in the painted sea cave in 990, he needed someone the luck-gods would listen to, and he chose a one-eyed dice-player called Sim who had never lost a throw he cared about. Sim's family has kept the Shrine of the Dice since. They throw the dice before every raid and every vote, they feed the Drowned Queen with wine and coin, and they keep the share-out book in which every captain's share is written. On Share Day 1098 a galley slave named Tam won his freedom on a single throw, and the Freed Oars have grown from that throw. The Bonedice say the luck-gods chose him. They have also kept the share-out book for 50 years, and they can read.
FX33-008.reputation: Holy, sly and very lucky at dice; even captains who believe in nothing touch a Bonedice for luck.

members.role: Head of the family; Keeper of the Shrine of the Dice
members.note: Has thrown the dice for 30 Share Days and can roll a six blindfold, which he says is the gods' doing.

members.role: Sim's wife; feeder of the Drowned Queen
members.note: Rows out at every dawn to pour wine for the Drowned Queen and truly believes she answers.

members.role: Heir; keeper of the share-out book
members.note: Has read every page of the share-out book and found a fifth of every toll going somewhere no captain is told.

members.role: Sim's daughter; dice-maker
members.note: Carves the shrine's dice from drowned sailors' bones and knows which ones are weighted.

famousDead: Dice-player chosen by Harl Gannet in 990 to keep the Shrine of the Dice.
FX33-008.secret: The dice of Share Day 1098 that freed Tam Oarsman were weighted by Sim at Nell Brine's request, to give the galley benches a hope; and Mace has read Lucerna's secret fifth in the share-out book.
hooks: Ima Redsail offers Mace a captain's share for one page of the share-out book.
Kit is asked to make weighted dice for this Share Day's vote.
The Freed Oars learn their freedom was thrown with weighted dice.

FX33-009.name: The Ninefathoms
FX33-009.title: Eldest Pilot of the Ratrock shoals
FX33-009.arms: a white sounding-lead on a knotted line, on dark sea blue
FX33-009.power: The night-lore of the reef channel and the Ratrock shoals, which only pilots born on the isles know, and four places among the 60 Shoal Pilots.
FX33-009.history: The Brotherhood exists where it does because its reef harbor and the shoals around it can be entered safely at night only by the pilots born there. The Ninefathoms were reef-fishers before 990 and have piloted ever since, and their founder Jory is said to have sounded the channel at nine fathoms on a moonless night with a lead and a song. In May 1053 Ninefathom pilots towed the fire-rafts through the reef on the fourth night of the Gull Isle Landing. They do not raid and they do not vote; they guide whoever the Captain-General sends. They know every pilot on the isles, and they know which one stole a stamped jar from the Ratrock caves on Dragon Night 1104. The pilot is a friend, and the Ninefathoms' daughter loves him.
FX33-009.reputation: Proud, close-mouthed pilots who are worth more than any galley, and know it.

members.role: Head of the family; Eldest Pilot of the Ratrock shoals
members.note: Can bring a galley through the reef on a moonless night by the sound the water makes on the rocks.

members.role: Jory's wife; reef-fisher and lead-maker
members.note: Casts the pilots' sounding-leads and puts a fishbone in each for luck.

members.role: Heir; Shoal Pilot
members.note: Piloted Nell Brine's galley home through the October storm that drowned her father's.

members.role: Jory's daughter; Shoal Pilot
members.note: Is in love with Lark Shoalwise and knows where he hid the jar, because she helped him.

famousDead: Sounded the reef channel at nine fathoms on a moonless night in the year of the Articles.
FX33-009.secret: Briar helped Lark Shoalwise carry the stolen stamped jar out of the Ratrock caves and hide it in a shoal cave only pilots can reach.
hooks: Lark asks Briar to pilot him to a Qadiri ship when the sea opens.
The Oil-Keeper asks the Eldest Pilot which pilot was near the caves on Dragon Night.
Gage is offered a captain's share by Ima Redsail to guide her galleys at night.

FX33-010.name: The Copperhulls
FX33-010.title: Captain with a share-book of the galleys Copper Gull and Hungry Wren
FX33-010.arms: a copper-sheathed prow breaking a white wave, on grey

military.office: Captains of two galleys and their boarders
military.unit: two light galleys and about 160 sworn boarders
military.ties: Their boarders train at the Dice Yard and sail with the Redsails' nine; their two votes sit with the Old Articles at the Captains' Table.

FX33-010.power: Two galleys, about 160 sworn crew, a share-book and two votes at the Captains' Table, which place their captain as a baron by courtesy abroad.
FX33-010.history: The Copperhulls were a Ratrock crew that took a Lucernan cog in 1033 with copper sheathing on her hull and stripped it to sheathe their own galley's prow, which they rammed through three more ships before the copper wore out. They voted for Mag Brine in 1050 and sailed on Dragon Night. They have raided less every year since the toll of 1056 and hated it more. Their captain sailed with Cob Redsail to Felano in July 1096 and brought one galley home of the two he took out. The Copperhulls are the Redsails' closest friends at the Table and the hardest voices of the Old Articles. Their captain's younger son sails on the Captain-General's flagship and hears everything said there.
FX33-010.reputation: Raiders of the old school who think the toll has made the Brotherhood into a counting-house.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain with a share-book
members.note: Watched Cob Redsail die of a tower bolt on the way home from Felano and swore on his body to raid again.

members.role: Dunk's wife; quartermaster of the Copper Gull
members.note: Keeps the crew's share-book and knows exactly how much less they make under the toll.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Hungry Wren
members.note: Wants his own share-book and thinks the Old Articles will give him one.

members.role: Dunk's younger son; oarsman on the Captain-General's flagship
members.note: Rows on the Drowned Queen and carries everything said at Nell's table to Ima Redsail.

famousDead: Stripped a Lucernan cog's copper to sheathe her galley's prow in 1033.
FX33-010.secret: Fen is Ima Redsail's spy on the Captain-General's flagship, and he has heard Nell speak of selling the 1011 contract to Morhaven without the Table's vote.
hooks: Fen is caught listening at the Captain-General's door.
Dunk's votes decide Share Day.
Pike is offered his own share-book by Nell if he breaks with his father.

FX33-011.name: The Tidecutters
FX33-011.title: Captain with a share-book of the galley Sea Widow
FX33-011.arms: a white galley cutting a black wave, under a gull, on sea green
FX33-011.words: With the Brines, through the weather.

military.office: Captains of the Sea Widow and the Brine Sworn's second boarding company
military.unit: one light galley and about 120 of the Brine Sworn
military.ties: They sail beside the Drowned Queen and lead a boarding company of the 500 Brine Sworn in Blackreef Harbor.

FX33-011.power: One galley, about 120 sworn crew, a share-book and a vote at the Captains' Table, and the Brine line's trust.
FX33-011.history: The Tidecutters were the first captains to stand up for Mag Brine at the Table in January 1050, when he came back from Sabra through the storms, and they have stood with the Brine line at every vote since. Their founder Jem Tidecutter steered the second galley on the winter run and kept it alive in seas no one sails in. They sailed on Dragon Night, fought through the Gull Isle Landing and broke the blockade of 1055 beside Mag's galley. In October 1094 the captain's eldest son drowned with Rook Brine and all 90 aboard off Wreck Isle, and the family's galley was renamed the Sea Widow. They want Nell kept in her seat and her son after her. Their captain, though, has a weakness for dice, and he owes the wrong man.
FX33-011.reputation: The Brines' oldest friends; steady in a storm, dangerous at a dice table.

members.role: Head of the family; Captain with a share-book of the Sea Widow
members.note: Has never lost a ship and never won a dice game he needed to win.

members.role: Hamm's wife; widow-mother of the harbor
members.note: Lost her eldest with Rook Brine and now feeds every sailor's widow in Blackreef at her own table.

members.role: Heir; captain of the Brine Sworn's second company
members.note: Has sworn to Nell's son as his father swore to Nell's father, and means it.

members.role: Hamm's daughter; mate of the Sea Widow
members.note: Wants the Sea Widow's share-book for herself and says her brother will be killed too young being honorable.

famousDead: Steered the second galley on Mag Brine's winter grain run of 1049 to 1050.
Drowned with Rook Brine, for whom he was named, off Wreck Isle in October 1094.
FX33-011.secret: Hamm has pledged his share-book to Wystan Coyle against 900 marks of dice debts, and under the Articles the Toll-Master can claim his vote on Share Day.
hooks: Wystan Coyle calls in the share-book before Share Day.
Ottie learns what her father pledged and offers to pay it with a prize.
Wat is asked to guard Nell's son on a voyage the Table does not know about.

FX33-012.name: The Saltmarrows
FX33-012.title: Salt-Master of the Redreef pans
FX33-012.arms: a white salt-heap on a gull's wing, on pale blue
FX33-012.words: Blood of the isle, salt of the sea.
FX33-012.power: The salt pans of Redreef and Scurvycreek on Gull Isle, about 400 salters and fish-salters, and the blood-tie to the Captain-General.
FX33-012.history: The Saltmarrows were salters of Gull Isle, working the old Solen pans at Redreef, when Rook Brine handfasted with their daughter in 1059. She bore Nell in 1061. The family has been Nell's mother's kin ever since, and Gull Isle salters have crewed Brine galleys for 40 years. They salt the Brotherhood's fish and sell salt to the Southland coast, and they quarrel with the Coyles, the other salters of Gull Isle, over fishing grounds off the Bone Coast. Nell has no grown kin of her father's blood but her son, and her mother's family is her only family. The Saltmarrows know better than anyone how sick the land makes her, because she stays in their house when she must come ashore. They have begun to plan for the day she cannot.
FX33-012.reputation: Salt-crusted, plain-spoken and close to the Captain-General; the Coyles call them 'Nell's pickles'.

members.role: Head of the family; Salt-Master of the Redreef pans; Nell Brine's uncle
members.note: Carried his niece ashore after her last voyage when she could not stand, and told the harbor she was drunk.

members.role: Abel's wife; fish-salter of Scurvycreek
members.note: Sleeps with a knife under the pillow since a Coyle boat was seen off Scurvycreek at night.

members.role: Heir; salt-trader to the Southland coast
