members.note: Wants her cousin Nell's son elected after Nell, and has started counting votes she cannot buy.

members.role: Abel's son; oarsman of the Drowned Queen
members.note: Rows beside the Copperhull boy on the flagship and has noticed how often he goes below.

famousDead: Rook Brine's handfast wife and Nell's mother; salted fish at Redreef until she died.
FX33-012.secret: Nell Brine has fainted twice ashore in the Saltmarrows' house since 1103, and the family has promised to hide her son on Gull Isle with the Captain-General's chest key if the Table turns on her.
hooks: Sal tells Nell's Quartermaster who goes below on the flagship.
The Coyles' toll boats start stopping Saltmarrow salt boats for the toll.
Nell faints ashore where the whole harbor can see.

FX34-001.name: The Paleflank line
FX34-001.title: Chief of the Yagrog camps
FX34-001.arms: a white rhino spear across a pale-flanked horse, on red-brown hide
FX34-001.words: First at the rhino, first at the plough.

military.office: Spear-captains of the Plough-Burners
military.unit: the Yagrog spears, 300 riders of the Whitehorn war-band at Thardush
military.ties: Their riders have burned every Drevnan plough east of the cairns since 1098, and they winter at Thardush with Hrok Whitehorn's 5,000.

FX34-001.power: Three Whitehorn kin-bands of the Yagrog camp, about 5,000 horses of the Otsai blood, and the first places at the Tuknak rhino trials after the Whitehorn chief's own.
FX34-001.history: The Paleflanks are the Whitehorn kin of the Yagrog camp, named for the pale-flanked Otsai stallion their founder Mokh took when the Whitehorns burned the Wind camp in August 916. When the Whitehorns swore to Grakka in 1062, last of the 31 clans, the Paleflank chief stood beside Ruk Whitehorn and helped name the price: the first right to the Tuknak rhinos. Ruk died at Zorek in 1064 with three Paleflank riders around him. Their youths face a rhino at 13 and every spring after until they kill one, and the line has buried more sons in the trials than any other camp. Since 1098 they have been the hardest of Hrok's Plough-Burners. In November 1104 Paleflank riders burned the two farms past the Thardush line where a family of six died.
FX34-001.reputation: Brave to the edge of madness, and proud of it; the Drevnan settlers' mothers frighten children with their name.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Yagrog camps
members.note: Killed his rhino at 13 on his first spring and has never let anyone forget it.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Paleflank kin
members.note: Speaks for war in the council of clan-mothers and against Mother Krasha every time.

members.role: Heir; rider of the Yagrog spears
members.note: Was at the burning farm in November, heard the children inside, and has not slept a full night since.

members.role: Varg's daughter; rhino-trial youth
members.note: Has faced three rhinos and killed none, and will face her fourth this spring.

famousDead: Took the pale-flanked Otsai stallion when the Wind camp burned in 916.
Died beside Ruk Whitehorn leading the Whitehorn wave at Zorek.
FX34-001.secret: Thurl told his father the settlers had not fled before the farm was fired, and Varg told Hrok Whitehorn they had; the lie is now the War-Captain's too.
hooks: Thurl wants to confess the burning to the council of clan-mothers.
Kazha faces her fourth rhino, and a Bluetusk hunter offers to make the kill for her as Garn did for the heir.
Drevna names the Paleflanks in its demand for blood-price.

FX34-002.name: The Guidefire line
FX34-002.title: Chief of the Gharhul guide-camps
FX34-002.arms: two fires side by side, one red and one gold, on green felt

military.office: Captains of the Gharhul guides and light riders
military.unit: about 150 guides and light riders of the Dushdush band
military.ties: They scout the Silk Road wells for the War-Mother's Toll Riders and lead the light riders of the Dushdush clans.

FX34-002.power: Guide-rights to six Silk Road wells, about 3,000 horses on the Gharhul grass, and kin in every caravan town from Lubany to Velgrad.
FX34-002.history: The Guidefires were the richest guides of the Dushdush clans before 1067, when Grakka's single toll at Kraoth ended the camp gifts and half their trade with them. Their founder Ulbash married a Velgradan carter's daughter who came west with a caravan, and lit two fires at the wedding, one for each people, which every Dushdush wedding has done since. A fifth of the line are half-orcs, mocked as two-bloods in their youth and full kin all the same. At the Winter Count of 1103 at Dushdush, the half-orc spear-fighter Uzka Twoblood called the half-orcs of the league to follow Tarn Halfblood, and the chief's own daughter stood up first. In the autumn of 1104 she rode west with the 120 on Horde silver. The chief has not decided whether to follow Uzka or the War-Mother, and the clan-mothers have noticed.
FX34-002.reputation: Guides who know every well and two tongues; half the league trusts them with its silk and the other half with nothing.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Gharhul guide-camps
members.note: Half-orc, named for his grandfather, and has never once in his life given a straight answer to a clan-mother.

members.role: Ulbash's wife; keeper of the guide-tallies
members.note: Wants the War-Mother's favor back more than she wants her daughter home.

members.role: Ulbash's daughter; rider of the Seekers of the Rider
members.note: Saw Tarn Halfblood at Gashmar in October and came home sure the Mare had sent him.

members.role: Heir; guide of the Gharhul wells
members.note: Would rather guide caravans than choose between his sister and his War-Mother.

famousDead: Married a Velgradan carter's daughter and lit the first two fires at a Dushdush wedding.
FX34-002.secret: Ulbash took 60 suns of the Horde silver Brak Longwind sent east, and promised the Horde's runner that his camps would feed Tarn if he came to the Tusk Great Ride.
hooks: Uzka Twoblood asks the Guidefires to host Tarn's escort at the Great Ride.
The War-Mother's agent asks Ulbash where the Horde silver went.
Drezka is challenged to face a rhino to prove a two-blood may speak at council.

FX34-003.name: The Snowpine line
FX34-003.title: Chief of the Dushgar winter camps
FX34-003.arms: a snow-laden pine over a running grey horse, on white felt

military.office: Captains of the Drukgar stockade riders
military.unit: about 300 snow-riders of the Gorak war-band
military.ties: They hold the Drukgar ring-fort on the forest edge and ride in the Gorak war-band, which fights best in snow.

FX34-003.power: Four Gorak kin-bands at Dushgar, about 9,000 sheep and 4,000 horses, winter hay stores in every camp, and the favor of House Lubec of Lubany since 1103.
FX34-003.history: The Snowpines are Gorak kin-band chiefs of the forest edge, sworn to Grakmar since Grakka's son Garm married into the Gorak clans in 1061. They paid tribute to the Wind camp at Darbash from 889, and their winter-count shows the Black Cough emptying it in 916. In the three-day blizzard of February 1081 they lost a third of their sheep, and the regency council's hay law saved their horses; they have kept a hay store in every camp ever since and sneer at clans that do not. In February 1103 the chief's son led a lost Lubany silk caravan of 40 people through two nights of snow to the Snowpine tents. House Lubec has sent them gifts each year since, and Lubany's fur buyers pay them first. They want neither Hrok Whitehorn's war nor Uzka's holy rider.
FX34-003.reputation: Cold, steady and dull, say the southern clans; alive, say the Snowpines.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Dushgar winter camps
members.note: Has outlasted four blizzards and three War-Mothers' councils and expects to outlast Hrok.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Snowpine kin
members.note: Keeps a guest-tent warm all winter for anyone caught in a blizzard, as the old custom says.

members.role: Heir; the herder who saved the Lubany caravan
members.note: Is courted by a Lubany banker's daughter in letters he has someone else read to him.

members.role: Hrul's daughter; fur-trader to the Velgradan buyers
members.note: Has learned Velgradan from the buyers and uses it to cheat them politely.

famousDead: Died in the blizzard of 1081 driving the kin's horses to the hay stores.
FX34-003.secret: House Lubec's gifts include a yearly purse of 200 suns for word of Whitehorn movements on the Thardush line, and Hrul has been sending it.
hooks: A Lubany banker asks Krog to guide a caravan by the hidden track south of Kraoth.
A blizzard catches the Whitehorn riders on Snowpine grass and they demand the guest-tent.
The clan-mothers learn whose purse buys Gorak furs first.

FX34-004.name: The Sunsetter line
FX34-004.title: Clan-Mother of the Lughul camps
FX34-004.arms: a hill and a setting sun, gold on brown felt

military.office: Captains of the Lughul border riders
military.unit: about 250 riders of the March clans' war-band at the Thardush cairns
military.ties: Their riders know every ford of the Thardush line and stand at the cairns with Hrok's host this winter.

FX34-004.power: The Lughul camp on the thinnest grass of the league, about 2,000 horses, a share of Drevna's rye at Thardush, and a ploughed field beside the cairns since 1104.
FX34-004.history: The Sunsetters came east in June 887 with the 25,000 March orcs who fled the Wind riders along the edge of the Lakeland, and they still sing the March at every Winter Count and name the hills of the Free Marches they have never seen. Redhand riders of the Grass Sea rode with the Wind columns that pushed them, and no Sunsetter will share a fire with a Redhand. Their spring grazing near Sevmir was the grass Drevnan settlers ploughed in 1062, which started the Tusk War. In the hungry winter of 1075 a Sunsetter cousin sold the labor of a boy named Hodd to a House Zorac farm for seven winters, and that boy is Hodd Ryeseed, who grows barley in hidden gullies near Thardush. In 1104 the clan-mother was the first of twelve March families to agree to plough a field beside the cairns. Her brother rides with Hrok's Plough-Burners.
FX34-004.reputation: The poorest kin on the steppe, with the longest songs and a field nobody else will touch.

members.role: Head of the line; Clan-Mother of the Lughul camps
members.note: Pushed the first plough beside the cairns herself so no young rider could say a clan-mother had not.

members.role: Hogga's brother; captain of the Lughul riders
members.note: Rides with the Plough-Burners and has sworn to burn his sister's field if she does not burn it first.

members.role: Heir; singer of the March
members.note: Knows all 211 verses of the March and has started making a new one about the field.

members.role: Hogga's son; ploughboy and rider
members.note: Follows Hodd Ryeseed around the gullies and wants to learn rye.

famousDead: Led the Lughul kin east in 887 and named every hill they left behind.
Killed defending the spring grass near Sevmir when the settlers' ploughs came.
FX34-004.secret: It was Hogga's own mother who sold the boy Hodd to the Zorac farm in 1075, and Hodd does not know it.
hooks: Torvag rides to burn the field beside the cairns.
Hodd Ryeseed asks Hogga for seed-rye that came from the stolen tribute.
A Redhand rider of the Horde comes east with Uzka's Seekers and asks the Sunsetters for a fire.

FX34-005.name: The Bluetusk line
FX34-005.title: Chief of the Throkbad diggers
FX34-005.arms: a turquoise stone between two rhino spears, on sandy hide

military.office: Spear-captains of the Turquoise Hills foot
military.unit: about 200 heavy spearmen who fight with the Rhino Spears of Krarog
military.ties: They give the Rhino Spear Lodge one youth in five and stand in the 800 Rhino Spears of Krarog when the league calls.

FX34-005.power: Digging-rights to three galleries of the Throkbad turquoise mine, the turquoise trade to the silk caravans and Skyfolk yak-drivers, and the palm springs of Oggoth.
FX34-005.history: The Bluetusks have dug turquoise at Throkbad since before the winter-counts and set it in their tusk-caps, as every grown orc of the hills does. The Wind camps never climbed into the hills, so the Bluetusks paid nothing to the Khan and still boast of it. They swore to Grakka in 1062 after her son Olg was promised to the hill clans. Their youths train at the Rhino Spear Lodge at Krarog under Grel Rhinospear, and the line dispute the Whitehorns' first right to the Tuknak rhinos at every council. Turquoise has made them rich in silver and silk, and the young Bluetusks dress like caravan merchants. Grel's own count shows only about 70 woolly rhinos left in the far valleys, and the Bluetusks have helped empty them.
FX34-005.reputation: Rich hill-folk with blue tusks and soft boots; fine spearmen, sharp traders, poor losers.

members.role: Head of the line; Chief of the Throkbad diggers
members.note: Wears so much turquoise in his tusk-caps that he lisps.

members.role: Clan-mother of the Bluetusk kin
members.note: Votes with Mother Krasha in council and with the highest bidder in the caravan camps.

members.role: Heir; spearman of the Rhino Spears
members.note: Has killed two rhinos on foot and is ashamed of what his father does with the horns.

members.role: Zhok's daughter; turquoise-cutter
members.note: Cuts stones for the caravans and keeps the best blue ones for a tusk-cap she will not show anyone.

famousDead: Opened the third Throkbad gallery and welcomed Grakka's son Olg into the hills in 1063.
FX34-005.secret: Zhok has sold rhino horn to the silk caravans for twelve years, packed in turquoise bales, though the Lodge forbids it and the Whitehorns would call it a blood crime.
hooks: A caravan master opens the wrong bale at Kraoth.
Grel Rhinospear asks the Bluetusks to stop the spring trials in the far valleys.
Gholl offers to make Kazha Paleflank's rhino kill, and both lines would rather die than accept it.

FX34-006.name: The Thunderskin line
FX34-006.title: First Drum-Captain of the Drum Band
FX34-006.arms: a drum struck by a white lightning bolt, on black felt

military.office: Hereditary drum-captains of the Drum Band of Grakmar
military.unit: the Thunderskin drum, 100 drummers of the 400 of the Drum Band
military.ties: Their drums set the pace of every relay and the turn of every wave, and the league's war-songs say they broke the Dravic princes at Zorek.

FX34-006.power: The great war-drums of the Drum Ground at Grakmar, 100 drummers, and the beats that only they and Bolg the Drummer know.
FX34-006.history: The Thunderskins were drummers of Clan Harrak, freed-thrall stock, when Grakka took them to war in 1062. At Zorek on 11 May 1064 their drums began the charge, and the elder Dravic prince, who had his house's sharp ears, fell from his saddle in pain and the Drevnan charge broke around him. The league keeps 11 May with drumming, and the Thunderskins lead it. Their captain has stood at Bolg the Drummer's side since the Drum Band was made, and they teach every drummer in it. Bolg is now nearly deaf, and the Dravic heir still collapses at war-drums. Drevna would pay well to know how many drummers can still play the Zorek beat.
FX34-006.reputation: Loud, holy and a little deaf; the clans love their drums and fear their tempers.

members.role: Head of the line; First Drum-Captain of the Drum Band
members.note: Plays the signals behind Bolg's tent while the old man lifts his sticks in front of the band.

members.role: Grokk's wife; maker of drum-heads from rhino hide
members.note: Stretches the great drums on rhino hide and blames the Bluetusks when hides grow scarce.

members.role: Heir; drum-leader of the Thardush drummers
members.note: Wants to play the Zorek beat at the Sevmir line in spring and see if it still works.

members.role: Grokk's daughter; drum-girl
members.note: Has made a little drum that can be heard a kilometer off and lost her father's temper for it.

famousDead: Beat the opening of the charge at Zorek in 1064.
FX34-006.secret: Bolg the Drummer can no longer hear the signal beats, and since 1102 Grokk has played them for him so that the War-Mother's chief shaman keeps his place.
hooks: A Drevnan agent offers silver for the Zorek beat.
Bolg's deafness shows at the Great Ride and the Thunderskins must choose between him and the truth.
Rogh takes the drums to the Sevmir line without the War-Mother's word.

FX34-007.name: The Beaconhand line
FX34-007.title: Captain of the Thardush cairn watch
FX34-007.arms: a red flame on a stone cairn, on grey

military.office: Hereditary captains of the Thardush cairn watch and its signal fires
military.unit: the cairn watch, 200 scouts of the Thardush line
military.ties: Their fires carry word from the cairns of 1066 to Grakmar in a day, and every scout of the line is trained by them.

FX34-007.power: The signal fires of the Thardush line, the Tukgar stockade, 200 scouts and the knowledge of every Drevnan patrol on the cairns.
FX34-007.history: When the Treaty of Thardush set the grazing line in July 1066, Grakka built stone cairns along it with a signal fire that reaches Grakmar in a day by rider, and she gave the watch to Krazh, a March rider who had lost a hand at Zorek and could still light a fire one-handed. His line has kept the cairns since, from the Tukgar stockade. They count Drevnan cattle that cross the line each summer and Drevnan soldiers that cross it each winter. They train every scout of the March clans. In 1097 the outcast Zagra of Clan Harrak, cast out two years before, came to them before she crossed the line, and the captain's son guided her across. Since 1102 she has been Drevna's scout-captain against the clans.
FX34-007.reputation: Watchers who see everything on the line and say only what the War-Mother asks.

members.role: Head of the line; Captain of the Thardush cairn watch
members.note: Named for his one-handed grandfather and lights the first fire every Winter Count with one hand behind his back.

members.role: Krazh's wife; fire-keeper of the Tukgar stockade
members.note: Keeps the dry wood of 40 cairns counted on one cord.

members.role: Krazh's son; scout of the cairns
members.note: Guided the outcast Zagra across the line in 1097 and still meets her at a cairn nobody watches.

members.role: Heir; captain of the western cairns
members.note: Has noticed that one cairn's fire is always late, and that her brother always has that watch.

famousDead: Lost a hand at Zorek and lit the first cairn fire of the Thardush line in 1066.
FX34-007.secret: Thurgash is Zagra Grassless's lover, and the cairn he watches is where she crosses; what she knows of the Whitehorn camp at Thardush she learned partly from him.
hooks: Zagra offers to guide the Zorin crossbows to Hrok's camp, by the cairn Thurgash watches.
Zoshka must decide whether to report her brother.
The signal fire is lit at night and nobody knows who lit it.

FX34-008.name: The Ironbit line
FX34-008.title: Hundred-Leader of the Roktuk Toll Riders
FX34-008.arms: an iron horse-bit on a silver chain, on undyed felt

military.office: Hereditary hundred-leaders of the Toll Riders of Kraoth
military.unit: the Roktuk hundred, 100 horse-archers of the Toll Riders
military.ties: They escort the silk caravans from Kraoth west and run down any that dodge the toll, under the captain of the Toll Riders.

FX34-008.power: The toll post at the Roktuk springs on the caravan road, a hundred riders, and a share of the fifth of the toll kept at Kraoth for the counters and the Toll Riders.
FX34-008.history: When Grakka made the Toll of Kraoth in June 1067 she raised the Toll Riders from the Kraoth clans, and the Ironbits were among the first hundred. Their founder Urbash took the name when he ran down a caravan that tried to slip the toll and brought its lead camel back by an iron bit through the nose. The line has held the Roktuk springs ever since, a tiny palm oasis that every caravan from Kraoth must water at. Under the Law of the Fire they feed every caravan master before the count, and under Grakka's law they kill anyone who robs a caravan that has paid. In 1098 Gurz the Toll-Keeper made Toruk Chainsilver captain over them, and the Ironbits have obeyed him since, even in the thing they least wanted to do. Velgrad's caravans now dodge the toll on a hidden track south of Kraoth, and the Ironbits are blamed for not finding it.
FX34-008.reputation: Hard, honest riders of the silk road, as the caravan masters see them; Gurz's dogs, as the Whitehorns say.

members.role: Head of the line; Hundred-Leader of the Roktuk Toll Riders
members.note: Named for the founder, and has run down eleven toll-dodgers without losing one.

members.role: Urbash's wife; keeper of the Roktuk toll-fire
members.note: Feeds every caravan master at the toll fire and hears more news than the Tallyhands.

members.role: Heir; file-leader of the Roktuk hundred
members.note: Dug the grave under the Kraoth horse pens in 1103 on Toruk's order and has not eaten meat since.

members.role: Urbash's daughter; rider of the hundred
members.note: Has found camel dung on a track south of the oasis where no caravan is supposed to go.

famousDead: Brought back a toll-dodging caravan's lead camel by an iron bit through its nose in 1067.
FX34-008.secret: Mokh helped Toruk Chainsilver bury the young guide he killed in 1103 under the Kraoth horse pens, and the guide was a Wellfinder.
hooks: Vrenna follows the hidden track south and finds Wellfinder guides on it.
The Wellfinders come asking where their missing son went.
Mokh is ready to confess, and Toruk knows it.

FX34-009.name: The Blackbristle kin
FX34-009.title: Chief of the Blackbristle rustlers
FX34-009.arms: no arms: a boar's black bristle tied to a gate-post is their mark and their warning
FX34-009.words: What crosses the line is ours.
FX34-009.power: About 50 riders and cattle-drivers who know the Thardush line better than the watch, hidden folds in the gullies, and buyers for stolen cattle at Velgrad's border markets.
FX34-009.history: The Blackbristles began on the day the Treaty of Thardush drew the line in 1066, when a March kin-band found that Drevnan cattle grazing across it were easier to steal than to chase off. They have rustled Drevnan herds across the cairns every summer since and sold them to Velgradan drovers who do not ask whose brand they bear. Grakka's law forbids robbing a caravan that has paid, so they have never touched the silk, and they say this makes them honest. They also buy and sell whatever else crosses the line: Drevnan iron, Velgradan ale, and orc horses sold to men who should not have them. In the winter of 1104, when Drevna's Lord Marshal held the rye at Sevmir, a Blackbristle crew took 40 bushels from a Zorac barn by night. Those bushels are now the seed Hodd Ryeseed means to sow at the cairns.
FX34-009.reputation: Thieves of the line; the March clans curse them in council and buy their cattle at dusk.

members.role: Chief of the Blackbristle rustlers
members.note: Can move 200 stolen cattle across a river at night without one of them lowing.

members.role: Borag's sister; seller at the Velgradan border markets
members.note: Speaks Velgradan like a Velgradan and has a Velgradan husband in a town she will not name.

members.role: Borag's son; leader of the rye raid
members.note: Took the 40 bushels from a Zorac barn and left a black bristle on its door.

members.role: Urgha's daughter; half-orc lookout
members.note: Is half Velgradan and wants to see her father's town before she is told who he is.

famousDead: Stole a Drevnan lord's prize bull the night the cairns were raised and named the kin.
FX34-009.secret: The rye Hodd Ryeseed is sowing at the cairns is Drevna's own tribute rye, stolen by Zogan from a Zorac barn, and the black bristle on the door tells Drevna exactly who to blame.
hooks: Drevna's Lord Marshal names the Blackbristles as the reason the rye was held.
Hrok Whitehorn wants the stolen rye for his riders, not for Hodd's field.
A Velgradan drover offers silver for orc horses with the War-Mother's brand.

FX34-010.name: The Longmane herd-mothers
FX34-010.title: Herd-Mother of the Gashoth snow horses
FX34-010.arms: a grey horse with a long white mane, on dark green
FX34-010.words: A thick mane, a full belly, a long winter.
FX34-010.power: About 7,000 shaggy snow horses on the Gashoth river grass, bred to dig through snow for grass, and sales to Velgradan fur buyers and the Gorak war-band.
FX34-010.history: In the blizzard of February 1081 most of the Gorak clans' horses lived only because of the regency council's hay. The Longmane mares lived without it, digging for grass under the snow, and the herd-mother who owned them, Agha Longmane, saw what she had. She bred them for twenty years, and the Longmane horses are now the snow-mounts of the Gorak war-band, small, shaggy and slow in summer, unbeatable in January. The herd-mothers trade them to Velgradan fur buyers who need horses that can work the taiga roads. Clan Ironhide buys their mares for the War-Mother's winter string. The line is run by its women, as horse-herds should be, say the Longmanes, and its men drive.
FX34-010.reputation: Breeders of ugly horses that never die in winter, and proud of every one.

members.role: Head of the line; Herd-Mother of the Gashoth snow horses
members.note: Daughter of the founder, and swears she can hear a mare thinking about snow.

members.role: Agha's husband; horse-driver to the Velgradan markets
members.note: Drives the herds west each autumn and comes back with more silver than he admits.

members.role: Heir; foaling-mistress
members.note: Has bred a mare that throws snow-colored foals and refuses all offers for her.

members.role: Agha's son; rider of the Gorak war-band
members.note: Rides a Longmane in the war-band and loses every summer race and wins every winter one.

famousDead: Saw her mares dig through the blizzard of 1081 and bred the snow horses from them.
FX34-010.secret: In the autumn of 1104 Torvash sold 200 snow horses to a Velgradan buyer who was buying for Drevna's Lord Marshal, and the Zorin crossbows will ride them in a winter raid.
hooks: Longmane horses are seen under Drevnan riders on the Sevmir line.
The War-Mother asks for the snow-colored mare as a gift.
A Velgradan buyer offers a fortune for 1,000 horses before the thaw.

FX34-011.name: The Sablecoat kin
FX34-011.title: Master of the Drukgar trap-lines
FX34-011.arms: a black sable on white, between two fir trees
FX34-011.power: Trap-lines through 3,000 km² of the Drukgar firs, about 2,000 sable and marten skins a year, and the elk-hunting rights of the stockade.
FX34-011.history: The Sablecoats are Gorak hunters who moved into the firs north of the Drukgar stockade in the hungry years around 1040 and never moved out. They trap sable, marten and fox in winter and hunt elk in the autumn, and they sell the furs west with the silk caravans and to Velgradan and Drevnan buyers. They live closer to the Eastfolk forests than any other orcs, and the line has married Eastfolk hunters more than once. Their furs go west with the silk, so a war on the Thardush line or a new road over the Roof would hurt them as much as it would the toll clans. In 1103 the sable came back thin and fewer, and the Sablecoats blame Velgradan trappers working the same firs from the other side.
FX34-011.reputation: Silent forest people who smell of smoke and grease; the steppe clans barely count them as riders.

members.role: Head of the kin; Master of the Drukgar trap-lines
members.note: Has walked every trap-line of the firs on snowshoes and never once ridden a horse in winter.

members.role: Zhorg's wife; Eastfolk-born skinner
members.note: Came out of a Velgradan trapper's camp in 1084 and will not say why she never went back.

members.role: Heir; elk-hunter
members.note: Killed a bull elk with a single arrow at 80 paces and the Gorak war-band wants her as a scout.

members.role: Zhorg's son; half-orc trap-boy
members.note: Has found a Velgradan trap-line on Sablecoat ground and pulled up all its snares.

famousDead: Led the kin into the Drukgar firs and cut the first trap-lines.
FX34-011.secret: Marta fled the Velgradan camp after killing a trapper who beat her, and his brothers have been working the firs on the other side for years looking for her.
hooks: Velgradan trappers cross into Sablecoat firs and someone is found dead in a snare.
Ghela is asked to scout for the Gorak war-band in a winter war.
Marta's past rides in with a fur buyer from Velgrad.

FX34-012.name: The Milkstone line
FX34-012.title: Keeper of the Mare Shrine of Kagmar
FX34-012.arms: a white stone bowl of mare's milk under a storm cloud, on blue-grey
FX34-012.power: The Mare Shrine of Kagmar in the southern hills, the blessing of the spears before every rhino trial of the Turquoise Hills, and a voice the clan-mothers listen to on what is holy.
FX34-012.history: The Milkstones have kept the Mare Shrine of Kagmar since about 962, when a shaman of the hill clans set a stone bowl on the peak and filled it with mare's milk every dawn. The line blesses the spears before every rhino trial in the hills, and they say no orc who skips the blessing has ever killed a rhino. They hold the eastern faith in its hardest form: no living chief is holy, and the Storm-Father has no sons on the grass. Their great-grandmother stood beside Kesha Ironhide in 1042 when she sent Gorath's envoys home, and the line has preached against the Son of the Storm ever since. Uzka Twoblood's holy rider of two peoples is to them the same lie in a new coat. But the keeper's own son has gone to hear Uzka speak.
FX34-012.reputation: Stern hill-shamans who will bless your spear and curse your chief in the same breath.

members.role: Head of the line; Keeper of the Mare Shrine of Kagmar
members.note: Has climbed to the shrine every dawn for 30 years and says the Storm has never once told her a chief's name.

members.role: Mazra's husband; bone-setter of the trial grounds
members.note: Has set the bones of 300 rhino-trial youths and buried 20 whose bones were past setting.

members.role: Mazra's son; shaman of the shrine
members.note: Rode to hear Uzka Twoblood at Dushdush and came back quiet, which frightens his mother more than shouting.

members.role: Heir; spear-blesser of the trials
members.note: Blessed the heir Shara's spear in 1104 and knows Shara's hands shook too much to have thrown it.

famousDead: Stood beside Kesha Ironhide in 1042 and told Gorath's envoys that the Storm has no sons.
FX34-012.secret: Tukzha knows the heir Shara did not make her own rhino kill in 1104, and has told only her mother.
hooks: Mazra is asked to curse Uzka Twoblood at the Great Ride, and her son stands with Uzka.
Mother Krasha asks Tukzha what she saw at the heir's trial.
A Horde shaman comes east to argue the Thunder Horse at the shrine.

FX34-013.name: The Wellfinder kin
FX34-013.title: Elder of the Vashuk guides
FX34-013.arms: a blue water-drop in a ring of camels' feet, on dun
FX34-013.words: Every well has a second way to it.
FX34-013.power: Knowledge of every well, spring and dry cut from Kraoth to the High Wastes, about 40 guides with adopted human and half-orc kin, and fees from every caravan that hires them.
FX34-013.history: The Wellfinders were adopted into the Kraoth camp about 845, when Mother Zelga Tallyhand took in a family of human guides from the east who knew the wells better than her own riders. Their children married orcs, and their grandchildren were full kin, as everywhere on the steppe. For two centuries they guided caravans from well to well and lived on the gifts. When Grakka made the single toll in 1067, the Wellfinders lost half their trade and moved to the Vashuk springs in the southern hills. Since 1101 some of their guides, with the human guide Anvar, have led Velgradan caravans by a hidden track south of Kraoth that pays no toll. In 1103 their youngest guide did not come home from Kraoth.
FX34-013.reputation: The best guides of the eastern steppe, say the caravans; toll-thieves and half-men, say the Toll Riders.

members.role: Head of the kin; Elder of the Vashuk guides
members.note: Half-orc, three-quarters human by blood, and the only one of the kin who has walked the whole hidden track.

members.role: Drogan's wife; keeper of the well-cords
members.note: Keeps a knotted cord for every well on the steppe, with a red knot where the water goes bad in August.

members.role: Heir; guide of the hidden track
members.note: Is sure the Toll Riders killed his younger brother and wants to know which one.

members.role: Drogan's daughter; trade-speech interpreter
members.note: Speaks four tongues and is courted by a Velgradan caravan master who would take her west.

famousDead: Human guide from the east adopted at Kraoth by Mother Zelga.
Youngest guide of the kin; went to Kraoth in 1103 and never came home.
FX34-013.secret: The Wellfinders have guided Velgradan caravans around the Kraoth toll since 1101, splitting the saving with Anvar, which under the War-Mother's law could cost every guide of the kin his head.
hooks: Tovash learns where his brother is buried.
Gurz the Toll-Keeper offers the kin a pardon for the name of the hidden track.
A Velgradan agent asks Drogan to scout a road over the Roof that would empty the steppe road.
